ekegusii: Ase omwaka o ikomi nomo bw’okogamba kwa Yoramu, mosinto bw’Ahabu, Ahasia, konya ochakire kogambera Abayuda.
english: (In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king of Judah.)

ekegusii: Ase amatuko aria Omonene agachaka gotoma Resini, omoruoti bw’Abasiiria, na Peka, mosinto o Remalia, bakagenda korwania Abayuda.
english: (In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.)

ekegusii: Abanto b’Ebisaku batari namachiko, ekero bagokora buna engencho ya mwanyabanto ere aya amachiko are korigia, nonya abwo tibari namachiko, babeire amachiko boka abanyene.
english: (Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature things required by the law, they are a law for themselves, even though they do not have the law,

ekegusii: Orogendo korwa Horebu goetera ase ense y’ebitunwa bia Seiri goika Kadeshi‐Barinea nigo rwarenge orw’amatuko ikomi na rimo.)
english: (It takes eleven days to go from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea by the Mount Seir road.)

ekegusii: Naboigo Yoabu na Abisai omwabo baitete Abineri, ekiagera ere aitete Asaeli omwabo ase esegi eria barwanete aaria Gibeoni.
english: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)

ekegusii: Yonathani, mosinto o Saulo, nabwate omwana oremarete amagoro. Omwana oyio konya okoorire emiaka etano ekero amang’ana ’ogokwa gwa Saulo na okwa Yonathani arentetwe korwa Yesireeli. Omoreri akaimokia omwana oria, na ekero arenge gotama, omwana oria agaakera inse, na igo akaba ekerema. Omwana oria nigo are korokwa Mefiboseti.
english: (Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she hurried to leave, he fell and became crippled. His name was Mephibosheth.)

ekegusii: (Ense ya Tapua neya Manase yarenge, korende omochie o Tapua, ase orobebe rwa Manase, okaegwa Efraimu.)
english: (Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself, on the boundary of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.)

ekegusii: Ekero Abiatari, mosinto o Ahimeleki, atamete gochia ase Daudi agwo Keila, nigo arentete egesibao ki’obokuani.
english: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod down with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)

ekegusii: Ase amatuko a kare ase Abaisraeli, ekero enibo yare koboorigwa, gose koonchorerigwa, engencho yabo nigo yarenge ng’a oyomo bw’abwo nigo arenge gosomora egekoroto kiaye ekemo omoa oria onde. Ayio nigo are kogera aria agambwa takoonchoranwa, na ogokora okwo kwaba kirori.
english: (Now in earlier times in Israel, for the redemption and transfer of property to become final, one party took off his sandal and gave it to the other. This was the method of legalizing transactions in Israel.)

ekegusii: Naki Yeso omonyene aorogetie ng’a omobani tari gosikwa ase ense yaye omonyene.
english: (Now Jesus himself had pointed out that a prophet has no honor in his own country.)

ekegusii: Omonto oyio Musa nigo arenge omoitongo mono kobua abanto bonsi barenge ase ense.
english: (Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth.)

ekegusii: Narenge omonto oyomo korwa Kiriati‐Yearimu orenge korokwa Uria, mosinto o Semaya. Oyio nere akabana ase erieta ri’Omonene mamincha y’omochie oyo na ense eye, agakwana amang’ana buna aria a Yeremia.
english: (Now Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim was another man who prophesied in the name of the LORD; he prophesied the same things against this city and this land as Jeremiah did.

ekegusii: (Ogi, omoruoti o Basani, nere bweka otigarete ase Abarefai. Esanduku yaye y’ogotindekerwa eyaroiseirie ebioma, nao ere agwo Raba, omochie bw’Abaamori, goika rero iga. Obotambe bwaye nigo bware obw’amaboko kianda, na obogare bwaye amaboko aane.)
english: (Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaites. His bed was made of iron and was more than thirteen feet long and six feet wide. It is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.)

ekegusii: (Farao, omoruoti o Misiri, konya ochire korwania Geseri na koyosakora, naende akayosamba nomorero. Agaita abanto ba Kanani baria bamenyete aroro, na koyorua buna ekeegwa ki’ogosokia omoiseke oye abe moga Sulemani.
english: (Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire. He killed its Canaanite inhabitants and then gave it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

ekegusii: Nigo arenge omonyariogi otari kogoma nyomba mwaye.
english: (She is loud and defiant, her feet never stay at home;

ekegusii: Orogongo orwo nigo naende rwamanyekanete buna ense y’Abarefai. Abarefai nabwo bamenyeteo agwo kare, korende Abaamoni bakabaroka Abasamusumi.
english: (That too was considered a land of the Rephaites, who used to live there; but the Ammonites called them Zamzummites.

ekegusii: Bono abanto b’egesaku kia Benjamin bakaigwa ng’a Abaisraeli batiirire gochia Misipa. Abaisraeli bakabora, “Totebie, naki obonyaka obo bwakorete bokaba!”
english: (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, "Tell us how this awful thing happened."

ekegusii: Omwana oria tamanyete ng’a ninki engencho y’amang’ana ayio, korende Yonathani na Daudi mbayamanyete.
english: (The boy knew nothing of all this; only Jonathan and David knew.)

ekegusii: “Ase chingaki chia kare, Abaemi nabwo bamenyete agwo. Abanto abwo nigo barenge abanene, naende abange mono, na abatambe bareng’aine n’Abaanaki.)
english: (The Emites used to live there-- a people strong and numerous, and as tall as the Anakites.

ekegusii: (The flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley had headed and the flax was in bloom.
english: Egatani na esairi bigaakwa, bigasarigwa, naki esairi konya yabekire ebigara, na egatani ngosomoria yare.

ekegusii: Etahabu y’ense eyio nengiya. Naende amagena e rigori rinene nareo, ayakorokwa bedola na berulo.
english: (The gold of that land is good; aromatic resin and onyx are also there.)

ekegusii: (Abaisraeli bakaimoka bakagenda orogendo rwabo korwa Beeroti‐Bene‐Yakani, bagaika Mosera. Haroni agakwera aroro na agatindekwao. Eleazari, omomura oye, akaba omokuani ribaga riaye.
english: (The Israelites traveled from the wells of the Jaakanites to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest.

ekegusii: Omonene akaa abanto baye ogwancherwa ase amasio ’Abamisiri; kobua ayio Musa nigo arenge omonto omonene mono ase ense ya Misiri ase amasio ’abasomba ba Farao, na ase abanto baye.
english: (The LORD made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh's officials and by the people.)

ekegusii: Abasomba ba Huramu na abasomba ba Sulemani, baria barentete chitahabu korwa Ofiri, bakarenta boigo korwa aroro chibao chi’emete ekorokwa alugumu, amo namagena e rigori rinene.
english: (The men of Hiram and the men of Solomon brought gold from Ophir; they also brought algumwood and precious stones.

ekegusii: Ching’iti chiria chinde chiatigarete chikaurwa chinguru chiabo chi’okogamba, korende chigatigwa chigendendererete koba moyo goika ase ebiro ne chingaki chiachikeretwe.
english: (The other beasts had been stripped of their authority, but were allowed to live for a period of time.)

ekegusii: (Naki Abafarisai na Abayahudi bonsi tibakoragera ritang’ani bataraisaba amaboko. Igo babwatetie engencho y’abagaaka babo.
english: (The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they give their hands a ceremonial washing, holding to the tradition of the elders.

ekegusii: Ebisona nigo biarenge ase chinsemo chionsi; obotambe bwabo nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko emerongo ebere na atano, na obogare bwabo obw’amaboko atano.
english: (The porticoes of the gateways around the inner court were twenty-five cubits wide and five cubits deep.)

ekegusii: Abakure abwo batigarete tibaba moyo goika emiaka eria elifu eyemo, ekaera. Okwo nakwo okobokigwa kwe ritang’ani.
english: (The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were ended.) This is the first resurrection.

ekegusii: Naki Abasadukai nigo bagokana ng’a kobokigwa tikori, nonya nabamalaika, nonya nemeika, korende Abafarisai nigo bagwancha onsi.
english: (The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, and that there are neither angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.)

ekegusii: Omonto tari nonya noyomo orenge buna Ahabu, ere oyio bweoonetie ere omonyene gokora amabe ase obosio bw’Omonene, ekero Yesebeli mokaye amoseegetete.
english: (There was never a man like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the eyes of the LORD, urged on by Jezebel his wife.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio akagera Amatuko ayio Amanene arendwe, ayio akorokwa Purimu kobwatekana nerieta ri’obomera boria bokorokwa Puri. Ase engencho y’amang’ana onsi ay’amarube ayio, na ase aria baroche abanyene, na ayio onsi abanyorete,
english: (Therefore these days were called Purim, from the word pur.) Because of everything written in this letter and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,

ekegusii: Obomera bwe ritang’ani bokagwera abanto b’ororeria rwa Haroni, eamate eyemo y’Abakohati, abarenge Abalawi.
english: (these towns were assigned to the descendants of Aaron who were from the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot fell to them):

ekegusii: Abwo bakaria eira goseria abakungu baria babo na barue kera oyomo emingichi eyemo korwa ase riicho riaye ebe ekeng’wanso gi’okomocha kwabo.
english: (They all gave their hands in pledge to put away their wives, and for their guilt they each presented a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.)

ekegusii: Ekiagera baroche Torofimo Omoefeso amo nere ase omochie, bagakaga ng’a Paulo namosoirie ase Hekalu ime.
english: (They had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with Paul and assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple area.)

ekegusii: Naki konya tibaramanya ririko, ng’a nemogwenerete koboka korwa ase abakure.
english: (They still did not understand from Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.)

ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana e rirube riria riarigetwe: “Ase Aritasasita omoruoti. Intwe abasomba bao aba tomenyete aiga bosongo y’orooche rw’Eufarati, twagokwanirie.
english: (This is a copy of the letter they sent him.) To King Artaxerxes, From your servants, the men of Trans-Euphrates:

ekegusii: Erio nigo riarigetwe nyuma y’omoruoti Yekonia, na ng’ina, na abasomba b’enyomba y’oboruoti abagombaetigwe, na abanene b’oboruoti bw’Abayuda na aba Yerusalemu, na abaroisia b’ebinto, na abaturi b’ebioma, kobarure Yerusalemu.
english: (This was after King Jehoiachin and the queen mother, the court officials and the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen and the artisans had gone into exile from Jerusalem.)

ekegusii: (This was before John was put in prison.)
english: Naki Yohana konya tarabekwa echela.

ekegusii: (This was the first census that took place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.)
english: Oyo noro orenge omobaro bwe ritang’ani origetwe ekero Kurenio arenge gavuna o Siiria.

ekegusii: ise omonyene atakorete, korende arie ebing’wanso bikoruegwa ase ebitunwa igoro, naende akore obonyaka nomokungu bw’omonto onde.
english: (though the father has done none of them): "He eats at the mountain shrines. He defiles his neighbor's wife.

ekegusii: (Musa konya oeire ekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase orogongo agwo Basani, na ekeng’ese kende Yoshua agakea orogongo ang’e nabamwabo, bosongo ya Yorodan.) Na ekero Yoshua abaete ribaga bagende chinka chiabo akabasesenia,
english: (To the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half of the tribe Joshua gave land on the west side of the Jordan with their brothers.) When Joshua sent them home, he blessed them,

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaegwa ense eria, na abanto b’ense engeni tibaetete aroro.
english: (to whom alone the land was given when no alien passed among them):

ekegusii: (Under the wings of the cherubim could be seen what looked like the hands of a man.)
english: Nkarora inse ye chimbaba chi’abakerubi baria egento gekororekana buna okoboko kw’omonto.

ekegusii: (Gaki, ringana eri, “Agendete igoro”, engencho yaye inki otatiga naboigo aigete nonya ngoika ensemo y’ense inse?
english: (What does "he ascended" mean except that he also descended to the lower, earthly regions?

ekegusii: (Naboigo, omonto oyo agorete omogondo ase eng’eria y’obobe bwaye. Akagwa maumama, akooreka, amara aye onsi agasoka.
english: (With the reward he got for his wickedness, Judas bought a field; there he fell headlong, his body burst open and all his intestines spilled out.

ekegusii: (Naende nkabatisa abanto ba nyomba mwa Stefana. Kobua ase abwo, tinkomanya gose nabatisete monto onde.)
english: (Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I don't remember if I baptized anyone else.)

ekegusii: Selofehadi, mosinto o Heferi, tabwate abana abamura, korende nabana abaiseke boka abwate, na amarieta ’abaiseke abwo naro aya: Mala, na Noa, na Hogila, na Milka, na Tirisa.
english: (Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons; he had only daughters, whose names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.)

ekegusii: ["You said,] 'Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you shall answer me.'
english: Koranche, ontegerere nkwane, nkoborie, naye ontebie buna are.

ekegusii: “Inwe nigo mogoteba ng’a Nyasae nigo akogachera abana ebibe bi’abaise. Tiga Omonene aakane abanto abanyene ebibe biabo, erio nario baranyare kobimanya.
english: [It is said,] 'God stores up a man's punishment for his sons.' Let him repay the man himself, so that he will know it!

ekegusii: Ekerecha keria ekebe gekabairaneria, “Yeso nimomanyete, na Paulo namomanyire, korende inwe mbarabi?”
english: [One day] the evil spirit answered them, "Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?"

ekegusii: Amagena amaterere are ase chindooche, ayio naro egetari kiao; ayio naro agotungetie. Ayio naro kwabeire gokoumorera okoruegwa kw’ebinyugwa, na koyaruera okoruegwa kw’endagera. Inee! Nindemererie ogokora buna okwo?
english: [The idols] among the smooth stones of the ravines are your portion; they, they are your lot. Yes, to them you have poured out drink offerings and offered grain offerings. In the light of these things, should I relent?

ekegusii: “Amang’ana aya naro aye Yeremia oramotebie: Aya naro Omonene agoteba: Naama! Egento naagachete nagetagore, na eki nasimegete nagesimore, engencho yaye nense engima.
english: [The LORD said,] "Say this to him: 'This is what the LORD says: I will overthrow what I have built and uproot what I have planted, throughout the land.

ekegusii: Amauga aito nigo asiareire ase omogo bw’embeera, buna ebisamunye bie chinko, gose ebi’amagena bigosiarerwa ase riroba igoro.
english: [They will say,] "As one plows and breaks up the earth, so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of the grave."

ekegusii: Aya nigo aganetigwe nabaminto b’oborimo, abasoetigwe bobisi, banyare kounia obosibore bwaito tore nabwo ase Kristo Yeso, erinde batobeke ase obosibwa.
english: [This matter arose] because some false brothers had infiltrated our ranks to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus and to make us slaves.

ekegusii: Ninche ng’o mbwate ogosemia gotari nobong’aini? Ase ayio nakwanire aya ntamanyeti, amang’ana ’ogokumia ansinyire komanya.
english: [You asked,] 'Who is this that obscures my counsel without knowledge?' Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.

ekegusii: Abaiseke abekungi baetwe nigo barenge chilifu ikomi na isano nemo (16,000) na aba Omonene nigo barenge emerongo etato, na babere (32).
english: 16,000 people, of which the tribute for the LORD was 32.

ekegusii: ne chibakuri emerongo ebere chiaroisirie korwa ase chitahabu chire chie rigori buna erie chidariki elifu eyemo, na ebikorero bibere biaroisirie korwa ase chitaai chichenire bire bie rigori buna erie chitahabu.
english: 20 bowls of gold valued at 1,000 darics, and two fine articles of polished bronze, as precious as gold.

ekegusii: 30,500 donkeys
english: ne chitigere chilifu emerongo etato, na amagana atano (30,500),

ekegusii: Chitigere baetwe nigo chiarenge chilifu emerongo etato, na amagana atano (30,500), na echi’Omonene nigo chiarenge emerongo etano nomo, na eyemo (61).
english: 30,500 donkeys, of which the tribute for the LORD was 61;

ekegusii: 36,000 cattle,
english: ne chiombe chilifu emerongo etato na isano nemo (36,000),

ekegusii: Chiombe baetwe nigo chiarenge chilifu emerongo etato na isano nemo (36,000), na echi’Omonene nigo chiarenge emerongo etano na ebere, na ibere (72).
english: 36,000 cattle, of which the tribute for the LORD was 72;

ekegusii: na kasia chikiro ikomi. (Bionsi bibe bi’ekerengo kegokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu). Oimokie na amaguta ’emezeutini ebituba bine.
english: 500 shekels of cassia-- all according to the sanctuary shekel-- and a hin of olive oil.

ekegusii: 61,000 donkeys
english: ne chitigere chilifu emerongo etano nomo na eyemo (61,000)

ekegusii: 72,000 cattle,
english: ne chiombe chilifu emerongo etano na ebere na ibere (72,000),

ekegusii: Barabwo nabana b’abanto abariri na ab’abakayayu; nigo baseretigwe nemecharichi barue ase ense.
english: A base and nameless brood, they were driven out of the land.

ekegusii: Abaelamu amo nemeganda yabo yonsi banyorire amarere abo ase egati y’abwo baitetwe nemioro, ne chimbeera chi’emeganda yabo nigo chibaetanaine. Abwo bonsi bagaitwa nemioro ekero konya batararoka. Agwo kare nigo barentete obwoba ase ense y’abare moyo. Bono babogoirie obosooku amo nabwo bagendire ase chimbeera, ee, nigo babekire ase egati y’abwo baitetwe nemioro.
english: A bed is made for her among the slain, with all her hordes around her grave. All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword. Because their terror had spread in the land of the living, they bear their shame with those who go down to the pit; they are laid among the slain.

ekegusii: Riaaki nigo ringa buna rigena rikomeka‐meka ase amaiso ’omonto oria okoriegwa, ekiagera nigo akorengereria ng’a kende gionsi ararikorere nigo riramorentere ebisio.
english: A bribe is a charm to the one who gives it; wherever he turns, he succeeds.

ekegusii: Egetonto giatachetwe tagokebuna, gose orotambe rw’etaya rokoimoka erioki, takororimia, goika arete oboronge ase okobua;
english: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out, till he leads justice to victory.

ekegusii: Egetonto giatachetwe tagokebuna, gose orotambe rw’etaya rokoimoka erioki takororimia. Ase obwegenwa bwaye narente oboronge.
english: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. In faithfulness he will bring forth justice;

ekegusii: Na rora, omokungu o Kanani korwa ase ensemo eria akaoroka, agakaa eriogi, akabora, “Omonene, omwana o Daudi, indorera amabera; enyaroka yane yachandirwe mono nekerecha.”
english: A Canaanite woman from that vicinity came to him, crying out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is suffering terribly from demon-possession."

ekegusii: Bakabetereria omonto orenge goeta, Simion Omokurene, ore korwa borabu, ise Aleksanderi na Rufo, abogorie omosalaba o Yeso.
english: A certain man from Cyrene, Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and they forced him to carry the cross.

ekegusii: Narenge omonto oyomo korwa Maoni obwate amaicho aye agwo Karimeli. Ere nigo arenge omonda mono; nabwate ching’ondi chilifu isato ne chimbori elifu eyemo. Igo arenge koba okonacha ching’ondi chiaye amarionya agwo Karimeli.
english: A certain man in Maon, who had property there at Carmel, was very wealthy. He had a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.

ekegusii: Ase engaki eria narengeo omonto ore korokwa Manoa. Nigo arenge korwa omochie ore korokwa Sora, omonto bw’egesaku kia Dani. Omokungu oye nigo arenge omogomba, taiborete bana.
english: A certain man of Zorah, named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites, had a wife who was sterile and remained childless.

ekegusii: Na omogambi gete akamoboria, “Omworokia omuya, ninki ndakore inyare koba nomwando bw’obogima bwa kare na kare?”
english: A certain ruler asked him, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"

ekegusii: Erio agwo omonto ore korokwa Goliato, omonto bw’omochie o Gati, akaoroka korwa ase egetwori ki’Abafilisti. Ere nigo arenge etuoni y’esegi; obotambe bwaye nigo bwarenge bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko atano na rimo na ekeng’ese.
english: A champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out of the Philistine camp. He was over nine feet tall.

ekegusii: Enkoro ere nomogoko nigo ekogwenia buna eriogo, korende omoichano ore ase enkoro nigo okwomia emeseto y’amauga.
english: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

ekegusii: Amaiso are nomosasoko nigo akogokia enkoro, na amang’ana amaya akorentwa nigo akogokia amauga.
english: A cheerful look brings joy to the heart, and good news gives health to the bones.

ekegusii: Chinungu nigo chinga buna amasakwe asere; ekero amatimo akwoga gocha nigo egoseka.
english: A club seems to him but a piece of straw; he laughs at the rattling of the lance.

ekegusii: Nigo arikire ng’a ase kera orogongo ogochika okwo kw’omoruoti korarigwe maiso marore ase abanto bonsi ng’a, Abayahudi bebeke ang’e ase rituko erio erio korusia egesiomba ase ababisa babo.
english: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ’amarube ayio achikirwe airwe isiko ase chingongo chionsi ase obogambi boria korareria abanto bonsi bebeke ang’e goika rituko riria riike.
english: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so they would be ready for that day.

ekegusii: Kirori omobe nigo agochecheria oboronge, na omonwa bw’omokori amabe nigo ogworerete ebibe.
english: A corrupt witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down evil.

ekegusii: Na omoganda nigo orenge oikaransete omoetanaine, okamotebia, “Rora nyoko na bamura bamino isiko bare, mbakorigetie.”
english: A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, "Your mother and brothers are outside looking for you."

ekegusii: Eriogi riaigurwe igoro ase ebitunwa bire bosa, eriogi ri’Abaisraeli ri’okorera na ogosorora, ekiagera barubanirie chinchera chiabo, banyebire inche Omonene, Nyasae obo.
english: A cry is heard on the barren heights, the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel, because they have perverted their ways and have forgotten the LORD their God.

ekegusii: Nigo rirabe rituko ri’omosunte na eri’amataturi, rituko ri’amare na omosunte ekerima. Omoganda omonene bwe chinguru nochiche, nigo orarande igoro ase ebitunwa buna ogokiamoka kwa mambia. Omogwekano bw’amang’ana ayio tana koba korwa kare, gose takoba nonya ng’ake ase ebigori bigochi‐gocha.
english: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like dawn spreading across the mountains a large and mighty army comes, such as never was of old nor ever will be in ages to come.

ekegusii: Rora, rituko ri’Omonene ngocha rire, ekero ebinto biaino birasakorwe biatananerwe agwo ase egati yaino.
english: A day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided among you.

ekegusii: Rituko riria neri’okobugigwa kw’ebitureri na okorera gw’esegi igoro y’emechie egiteire chindwaki, na igoro y’emerobiri emetambe mono.
english: a day of trumpet and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the corner towers.

ekegusii: Omokonyi bw’ekanisa abe omonto ore nomokungu oyomo, omanyete kogambera abana baye buya, na ab’enyomba yaye omonyene.
english: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife and must manage his children and his household well.

ekegusii: Abagosiria bachire gosiria Babeli; abarwani baye chituoni bairirwe, amata abo abunirwe. Inche Omonene Nyasae nigo inde Nyasae bw’ogoakana egesiomba, ekeene goika ngeakane kegima.
english: A destroyer will come against Babylon; her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will repay in full.

ekegusii: Inche norokigwe okorora kore ogokong’u mono; abaurereria nigo bagendererete kourereria, na abasaria bagendererete gosaria. Inwe Abaelamu, genda morwane! Inwe Abamedia, genda moboere! Ninsirie obororo bwonsi bwarentirwe n’Abababeli.
english: A dire vision has been shown to me: The traitor betrays, the looter takes loot. Elam, attack! Media, lay siege! I will bring to an end all the groaning she caused.

ekegusii: Omonto ore nokomanya nigo akorigereria gochia ase obong’aini, korende omonto omoriri nigo akorigereria gochia ase chinsinyo chi’ense.
english: A discerning man keeps wisdom in view, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.

ekegusii: Egurugura nebe igoro ase chindooche chiaye, erinde chikame amache! Ense eyio nigo eichire nemegwekano y’ogosasimwa, na abanto mbabe buna chibarimo ase ogosasima emegwekano eyio!
english: A drought on her waters! They will dry up. For it is a land of idols, idols that will go mad with terror.

ekegusii: ase ogosemeria kw’obogima bwa kare na kare. Obogima obo Nyasae ariete eira korwa kare na kare; ere tagokwana oborimo.
english: a faith and knowledge resting on the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the beginning of time,

ekegusii: Omonto ore nenkoro endonge nanyore ogosesenigwa okonge, korende oyo okoayerera ase okoba omonda takomocha konyora egesusuro.
english: A faithful man will be richly blessed, but one eager to get rich will not go unpunished.

ekegusii: kirori bw’oborimo, ogokwana oborimo, na omonto ogosimeka chimbusuro chi’ogoitania ase egati y’abanto abamo.
english: a false witness who pours out lies and a man who stirs up dissension among brothers.

ekegusii: A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who pours out lies will not go free.
english: Kirori bw’oborimo takomocha konyora egesusuro, na omonto ogokwana oborimo takomocha konyora egesusuro kiaye.

ekegusii: A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who pours out lies will perish.
english: Kirori bw’oborimo takomocha konyora egesusuro, na oyo ogokwana oborimo goika asire.

ekegusii: Kirori bw’oborimo nasire, korende omonto ogotegerera nagenderere gokwana.
english: A false witness will perish, and whoever listens to him will be destroyed forever.

ekegusii: Nyasae oria omenyete aase aye aachenu, nere ise bwe chintakana, na omorendi bw’ababoraka.
english: A father to the fatherless, a defender of widows, is God in his holy dwelling.

ekegusii: Emeyega ye chindagera nigo ekorenta omogoko, na edivai nigo egokora omonto bweigwa buya, na ase chibesa nonyare kogora ebinto bionsi.
english: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.

ekegusii: Amatuko atai make gaetire, Agripa omoruoti na Bereniki bagaika Kaisaria gokwania Festo.
english: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

ekegusii: Agasoa Kapernaumu naende nyuma y’amatuko amake; ekaigugwa ng’a nao are nyomba.
english: A few days later, when Jesus again entered Capernaum, the people heard that he had come home.

ekegusii: Abasacha bande bakabwatana nere, bakeegena, na ase abwo narengeo Dionuso, oyomo bw’ekegambero ki’Areopago, naende omokungu oyomo ore korokwa Damari, na abande amo nabarabwo.
english: A few men became followers of Paul and believed. Among them was Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, also a woman named Damaris, and a number of others.

ekegusii: Abanto b’egesaku eke babwate amasio obotindi; babe batari koraara omonto omogotu gose kororera abanto abake amabera.
english: a fierce-looking nation without respect for the old or pity for the young.

ekegusii: Ebinto asangereretie ase enyomba yaye mbiirwe; bionsi nigo birairwe ase rituko ri’endamwamu ya Nyasae.
english: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God's wrath.

ekegusii: Omoriri tari kogokigwa nay’obong’aini, korende nigo anchete gokwana ayare ase enkoro yaye omonyene.
english: A fool finds no pleasure in understanding but delights in airing his own opinions.

ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agokora ebibe buna egosori, korende omonto ore nokomanya nigo agokora ayare ay’obong’aini.
english: A fool finds pleasure in evil conduct, but a man of understanding delights in wisdom.

ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agosokia endamwamu yaye yonsi, korende oyore omong’aini nigo akoyetanga otoerera.
english: A fool gives full vent to his anger, but a wise man keeps himself under control.

ekegusii: Okobeea kw’omonto omoriri nigo gokomanyekana rimo rioka, korende omonto omong’aini nigo akoombia otuba obobe.
english: A fool shows his annoyance at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.

ekegusii: Omoriri nigo agochaya amorokererio a ise akomorongeyia, korende oyokoigwera ogokurerwa nigo akong’ainia.
english: A fool spurns his father's discipline, but whoever heeds correction shows prudence.

ekegusii: Omwana omomura omoriri nigo agoichania ise, naende nigo akorenta obororo ase ngina omoiborete.
english: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to the one who bore him.

ekegusii: Omwana omomura omoriri nigo akorentera ise amabe, na omokungu okona‐kwomana nigo anga buna amatoima ’embura akona‐gotonya.
english: A foolish son is his father's ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.

ekegusii: Chinkwana chi’omoriri nigo chikorenta eriomana, na omonwa oye nigo okorangeria ogoakwa.
english: A fool's lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.

ekegusii: Omonwa bw’omoriri nigo okomorentera ogosirigwa, ne chinkwana chiaye nigo chikoba omoeto asare.
english: A fool's mouth is his undoing, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

ekegusii: Aya omoriri agokwana nigo are enyimbo y’oboenenu, korende aya abang’aini bagokwana nigo akobarenda.
english: A fool's talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.

ekegusii: Emeremo y’omoriri nigo ekomorosia, goika osinywa komanya enchera ekogenda ase omochie.
english: A fool's work wearies him; he does not know the way to town.

ekegusii: Chinibo chikonyorwa ase oromeme rw’obong’ainereria, nigo chire buna omooki okoera bwango, na buna amareba akorenta amakweri.
english: A fortune made by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor and a deadly snare.

ekegusii: Omosani nigo akoba nobwanchani ase chingaki chionsi, na oyomino nigo aiboire akonye ase engaki y’emechando.
english: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

ekegusii: Ekembugu‐mbugu ekenene ki’omwaga gekaoroka, emerindo egaaka‐aka obwato goika amache agachaka goichora obwato ime.
english: A furious squall came up, and the waves broke over the boat, so that it was nearly swamped.

ekegusii: Omonto obwate eriso ri’amabera nasesenigwe, ekiagera bwatananeire omotaka endagera.
english: A generous man will himself be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

ekegusii: Omonto okorua nomoyo bw’ogwancha natenenkigwe; nere oyokorua amache agokendia erang’o, nere naegwe amache agokendia erang’o yaye.
english: A generous man will prosper; he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

ekegusii: Okoiraneria kw’obwororo nigo kogokendia endamwamu, korende amang’ana ’obotindi nigo agoseegeta endamwamu.
english: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

ekegusii: Ekeegwa gekoruegwa bobisi nigo kegokendia endamwamu, ne riaaki ribisire ase eanga ime nigo rigokendia ekeririanda.
english: A gift given in secret soothes anger, and a bribe concealed in the cloak pacifies great wrath.

ekegusii: Ebiegwa bi’omonto nigo bikomoigorera enchera na komobeka amo nabanto abanene.
english: A gift opens the way for the giver and ushers him into the presence of the great.

ekegusii: Aase Hekalu yaito Enchenu ere, nao agwo ekerogo ki’obonene kiabegetwe korwa omochakano.
english: A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.

ekegusii: Omonto omuya nigo agotiga omwando ase abana baye, na ase abachokoro baye, korende obotenenku bw’abanyene ebibe nigo bogacheire abanyene oboronge.
english: A good man leaves an inheritance for his children's children, but a sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.

ekegusii: Omonto omuya nigo akonyora ogwancherwa korwa ase Omonene, korende oyogokora emeroberio y’obobe nigo akonacherwa ekina n’Omonene.
english: A good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a crafty man.

ekegusii: Erieta rigiya nigo ribuete amaguta amaya akweakwa, ne rituko ri’ogokwa nigo rire rigiya kobua eri’okoiborwa.
english: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth.

ekegusii: Erieta rigiya nigo rigwenerete gochorwa kobua chinibo chinyinge, na okomanyekana okuya nigo kobuete efeta na etahabu.
english: A good name is more desirable than great riches; to be esteemed is better than silver or gold.

ekegusii: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
english: Omote omuya tokonyara kwama amatunda amabe, na omote omobe tokonyara kwama amatunda amaya.

ekegusii: Omonto okona‐goeta‐etia obogenki nigo akoorokia obobisi, korende oyobwate omoika bw’obwegenwa tari koorokia obobisi.
english: A gossip betrays a confidence, but a trustworthy man keeps a secret.

ekegusii: Omonto okona‐goeta‐etia obogenki nigo akoorokia obobisi, ase ayio tobaisa kobwatana nomonto otari kwerita ase amang’ana aye.
english: A gossip betrays a confidence; so avoid a man who talks too much.

ekegusii: Na egekone ekenene gekarorekana igoro: Omokungu oboirie erioba, na omotienyi nigo orenge inse y’amagoro aye. Ase omotwe oye nigo arenge negutwa ye ching’enang’eni ikomi na ibere.
english: A great and wondrous sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head.

ekegusii: Omonto ore ne ribero ase okorigia ebitoki ase enchera etari endonge nigo akorenta emechando ase enyomba yaye, korende oyo ogechete riaaki nabe moyo.
english: A greedy man brings trouble to his family, but he who hates bribes will live.

ekegusii: Omonto ore ne ribero nigo agoseegeta eriomana, korende oyosemeretie Omonene natenenkigwe.
english: A greedy man stirs up dissension, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.

ekegusii: Abande abanyasemi b’Abaepikurio na Abastoiki bakaamererania nere. Abande bagateba, “Omonto oyo nomonyamang’ana mange, inki arigetie goteba?” Na abande, “Ororekanire ng’a nigo are buna omorandia bw’amang’ana e chinyasae chingeni”, ekiagera nigo arenge korandia amang’ana a Yeso na okobokigwa kw’abakure.
english: A group of Epicurean and Stoic philosophers began to dispute with him. Some of them asked, "What is this babbler trying to say?" Others remarked, "He seems to be advocating foreign gods." They said this because Paul was preaching the good news about Jesus and the resurrection.

ekegusii: A hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
english: Nkarora okoboko kogonkuna, gokanyimokia, ngatung’ama namaru, ngasigamera inse nebisanyi bi’amaboko nkoiguswa.

ekegusii: Enkoro ere nomosasoko nigo ekorenta omogoko ase obosio, korende onye enkoro ere nomoichano, omoyo nigo okoba nobororo.
english: A happy heart makes the face cheerful, but heartache crushes the spirit.

ekegusii: Enkoro y’omogoko nigo ere obogima bw’omobere, korende ribero nigo rire obogundo bw’amauga.
english: A heart at peace gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

ekegusii: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are quick to rush into evil,
english: enkoro ekoroberia ebirengererio bi’amabe, na amagoro akominyoka gochia gokora amabe;

ekegusii: A horse is a vain hope for deliverance; despite all its great strength it cannot save.
english: Gosemeria chibarasi chi’esegi, ayio mbosa, tichikonyara kobua, chinguru chiabo chinyinge tichigotooria omonto.

ekegusii: Omonto ore nekeririanda, ekeene goika anyore egesusuro; oise komotanga kagokora bobe nigo okomoseegeta.
english: A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.

ekegusii: Omonto ore nenkoro ekoberoroka bwango nigo agoseegeta eriomana, korende oyore omwororo nigo agokanya eriomana.
english: A hot-tempered man stirs up dissension, but a patient man calms a quarrel.

ekegusii: Nkiarenge aroro egetaabo giaichire chinkama, erio bakabeka esifunchi eichire chinkama igoro ase egetonto, bakamobekera monwa.
english: A jar of wine vinegar was there, so they soaked a sponge in it, put the sponge on a stalk of the hyssop plant, and lifted it to Jesus' lips.

ekegusii: Omonto ore namabera nigo akwerentera amaya, korende omonto omotindi nigo agwechanda ere omonyene.
english: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.

ekegusii: Omokungu omwesiki nigo akogenderera gosikwa botambe, korende abanto abaurereria abatindi nigo bakonyora chinibo ase chinguru.
english: A kindhearted woman gains respect, but ruthless men gain only wealth.

ekegusii: Omosomba ogokora emeremo nobong’aini nigo agwancherwa nomoruoti, korende endamwamu y’omoruoti nigo ekoba igoro ase oria okomorentera obosooku.
english: A king delights in a wise servant, but a shameful servant incurs his wrath.

ekegusii: Ekero omoruoti abeire nekeririanda nigo anga buna endo ekoruma, korende ogwancherwa kwaye nigo konga buna riime rire ase obonyansi.
english: A king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.

ekegusii: Endamwamu y’omoruoti nigo enga buna abatomwa bakorenta amakweri, korende omonto omong’aini nigo akoyekanya.
english: A king's wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it.

ekegusii: Okogosa kw’omoruoti nigo konga buna okoruma kw’endo, na oyo okomogechia oba nendamwamu, oyio nigo akogera obogima bwaye bosirigwe.
english: A king's wrath is like the roar of a lion; he who angers him forfeits his life.

ekegusii: Ase ense eyio inamorie endagera enyinge etari kobaerera; aroro timokoremerwa gento kende gionsi. Amagena areo nigo are nebioma, naende namoremere chitaai korwa ase ebitunwa biaye.
english: a land where bread will not be scarce and you will lack nothing; a land where the rocks are iron and you can dig copper out of the hills.

ekegusii: Ense eyio ere nengano na esairi, na emesabibu, na emeko, na emekomomanga, na emezeituni, boigo namooke.
english: a land with wheat and barley, vines and fig trees, pomegranates, olive oil and honey;

ekegusii: Abanto abange bagasangererekana, bagatanga amache e chinsoko chionsi na ay’akarooche karenge ase orogongo roria rwonsi, bagateba, “Nase ki abaruoti b’Abaasuri barache banyore amache ekero bagocha aiga?”
english: A large force of men assembled, and they blocked all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?" they said.

ekegusii: Aria ase egetunwa ndiarengeo riicho rinene rie chimbeche riare korisia.
english: A large herd of pigs was feeding on the nearby hillside.

ekegusii: Ndiarengeo riicho rinene rie chimbeche, chiare korisia ase egetunwa, bikamosorora abie ribaga bichisoe. Akabia ribaga.
english: A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. The demons begged Jesus to let them go into them, and he gave them permission.

ekegusii: Omoganda bw’abanto okamotunyana, na abakungu baare kweaka‐aka, na komweng’erereria.
english: A large number of people followed him, including women who mourned and wailed for him.

ekegusii: Obonge bw’abanto nabwo bore obonene bw’omoruoti, korende ase abanto bare abake omogambi obo nigo agosirigwa.
english: A large population is a king's glory, but without subjects a prince is ruined.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ororeria rw’Eleazari bakanyorekana bare nabateneneri abange kobua abwo b’ororeria rwa Itamari. Ase ayio bakabeka abanto ikomi na batano nomo b’ororeria rw’Eleazari babe abateneneri be chiamate chiabo, na batano na batato b’ororeria rwa Itamari babe abateneneri be chiamate chiabo.
english: A larger number of leaders were found among Eleazar's descendants than among Ithamar's, and they were divided accordingly: sixteen heads of families from Eleazar's descendants and eight heads of families from Ithamar's descendants.

ekegusii: A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with the responsibility for baking the offering bread.
english: Matitia, oyomo bw’Abalawi, omomura omotangi o Salumu, omonto bw’eamate ya Kora, agatenenera emeremo y’okoroisia emegati ekoruegwa.

ekegusii: omobaso okomorekera abanto b’Ebisaku, na obonene bw’abanto bao Abaisraeli.”
english: a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel."

ekegusii: Endo yaimokire korwa ase riraro riaye; oria ogosiria ebisaku oimokire, orure aase aye, akore ense yaino ebe bosa; emechie yaino nesarigwe ebe amaturi, atamenyiri nabanto.
english: A lion has come out of his lair; a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his place to lay waste your land. Your towns will lie in ruins without inhabitant.

ekegusii: a lion, mighty among beasts, who retreats before nothing;
english: Endo ere ne chinguru chinyinge kobua ching’iti chinde, na teri kwoboigwa na ng’iti ende,

ekegusii: Naende ake omonto onde akamorora, akabora, “Aye noyomo obo ore.” Petero akabora, “Omonto oyo, tai inche.”
english: A little later someone else saw him and said, "You also are one of them." "Man, I am not!" Peter replied.

ekegusii: Orare ake igo, bwegondie ake igo; oringanie amaboko otimoke,
english: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest--

ekegusii: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest--
english: Okorara ake, na ogosundoka ake, na okoringania amaboko ake,

ekegusii: Netigarete engaki ensinini, na omokori amabe asirigwe; nobe gokorigereria mono aase aye, takonyorekana oreo.
english: A little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found.

ekegusii: Esagara nabo erabogorigwe nokoboko kw’omonto, korende nabo ekomenya ase chinyomba chi’abaruoti.
english: a lizard can be caught with the hand, yet it is found in kings' palaces.

ekegusii: Okogania gwaikeranigwe nigo kore ogwansu ase omoyo, korende okoonchoka gotiga amabe, okwo nigo kore okogechigwa ase abariri.
english: A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.

ekegusii: oyore buna ensune eyanchire na buna engabi ensiani. Tiga obosiani bwaye bokong’use, na ogokigwe nere chingaki chionsi. Obwanchani bwaye tiga bokogokie kogenderera.
english: A loving doe, a graceful deer-- may her breasts satisfy you always, may you ever be captivated by her love.

ekegusii: Omonto ore noromeme rogokwana oborimo, nigo akogecha abanto abwo amang’ana aye achandire bobe, na omonwa ogokwana amang’ana ay’okweansia nigo okorenta ogosirigwa.
english: A lying tongue hates those it hurts, and a flattering mouth works ruin.

ekegusii: Omonto omogechi nigo akobisa ase ebikoba biaye, obong’ainereria bore ase enkoro yaye.
english: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but in his heart he harbors deceit.

ekegusii: Narengeo omonto ore korokwa Baraba, osibetwe amo nabanto abakorete eriomana, na gokora oboiti ase eriomana.
english: A man called Barabbas was in prison with the insurrectionists who had committed murder in the uprising.

ekegusii: Omonto agacha korwa Baali‐Salisa, akarentera omonto oria o Nyasae emegati emerongo ebere y’esairi y’okwama ogotang’ani, na ebigara ebibese bire egunia ime. Elisha agateba, “Kae abanto barie!”
english: A man came from Baal Shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread baked from the first ripe grain, along with some heads of new grain. "Give it to the people to eat," Elisha said.

ekegusii: Egento ekiya omonto aranyare gokora nokoria na konywa, na kogokera ebinto ebio echandeire kobinyora. Nkamanya ng’a nonya nayio nigo akorwa ase okoboko kwa Nyasae.
english: A man can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in his work. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,

ekegusii: Ogotamoiroka Nyasae tigokoagacha omonto na komokong’ia, korende omori bw’omonyaboronge tokonyegerigwa.
english: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.

ekegusii: Omonto nigo akogokera okoiraneria okuya gokorua ase omonwa oye, ne ring’ana rigokwanwa ase engaki egwenerete, nigo rire rigiya mono.
english: A man finds joy in giving an apt reply-- and how good is a timely word!

ekegusii: Omonto oyomo akamonyora, ekero arenge kona‐goetanana ase erooro, na omonto oyio akamoboria, “Inki okorigia?”
english: a man found him wandering around in the fields and asked him, "What are you looking for?"

ekegusii: Omonto oyomo ase omoganda akamoiraneria, “Omworokia, namorenta omomura one asore, obwatire nekerecha kemokorete rimama;
english: A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought you my son, who is possessed by a spirit that has robbed him of speech.

ekegusii: Naende rora, omonto oyomo ase omoganda oria agaaka egeturi, okobora, “Omworokia, nagosabire, origererie omomura one, ekiagera ere nomwana one omomoima.
english: A man in the crowd called out, "Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.

ekegusii: Naki ere oyore Omoyahudi ase isiko oka, tari Omoyahudi bw’ekeene, gose okwaroka koria gokorire isiko ase omobere, tikori okwaroka gw’ekeene.
english: A man is not a Jew if he is only one outwardly, nor is circumcision merely outward and physical.

ekegusii: A man is not to marry his father's wife; he must not dishonor his father's bed.
english: “Omonto tabaisa korara na moga ise, abaise korentera ise obosooku.

ekegusii: Omonto nigo agotogigwa buna obong’aini bwaye bore, korende oyore nebirengererio ebikorekanu nigo agochaywa.
english: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but men with warped minds are despised.

ekegusii: Omonto oremeire chisemi nigo akobwatana amaboko na kwerua koba intenenera ase omonto onde.
english: A man lacking in judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.

ekegusii: Onye omonto oiboire abana rigana erimo, na abe moyo ase engaki y’emiaka emenge, ee, nonya amatuko ’obogima bwaye abeire amange, korende tegogetie ase ebinto ebiya bi’obogima obwo, na tatindekwa ase amasikani, nigo ngoteba ng’a omwana okwerete enda ya ng’ina nigo are buya kobua omonto oyio.
english: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo akwerita ase amang’ana agokwana, na omonto ore nokomanya nigo abwate omoika bw’oboremereria.
english: A man of knowledge uses words with restraint, and a man of understanding is even-tempered.

ekegusii: Omonto obwate abasani abange nigo akwerentera emechando, korende nare omosani bw’ekeene baigwanaine kobua oyomwabo.
english: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omokorekanu ase enkoro yaye tari goseseneka, na oyobwate oromeme rw’ogosiria nigo akonyorwa nemechando.
english: A man of perverse heart does not prosper; he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.

ekegusii: Naki tegwenereti omosacha gotuba omotwe oye, ekiagera nomogwekano bw’obonene bwa Nyasae; korende omokungu nobonene bw’omosacha.
english: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

ekegusii: Tiga omonto erenge omonyene, erio arie omogati na konywera egekombe.
english: A man ought to examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omotaka otabwati ebinge akorua nigo agochora omote otari kogunda, origia omoroisia omong’aini omanyete kobaacha, ere omobaachera omogwekano otari gosuka.
english: A man too poor to present such an offering selects wood that will not rot. He looks for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.

ekegusii: Onye omonto oritoeirwe nokomocha kw’ogoitera amanyinga ’omonto onde, tiga abe okona‐gotama goika akwe, na onde tagokonya omonto oyio.
english: A man tormented by the guilt of murder will be a fugitive till death; let no one support him.

ekegusii: Narenge aroro omonto oyomo ore korokwa Zakayo, omonene bw’abarusia ebango; ere nomonda orenge.
english: A man was there by the name of Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was wealthy.

ekegusii: Mwanyabanto oyio osikire otabwati obong’aini, nigo anga buna ching’iti chigokwa chiasira.
english: A man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish.

ekegusii: Omonto ogochaya omonto onde, oyio nigo aborire obong’aini, korende omonto omong’aini nigo agokira‐kiri.
english: A man who lacks judgment derides his neighbor, but a man of understanding holds his tongue.

ekegusii: Omonto omenyete aase aria akaboria, “Ise nere ng’o?” Ase engencho eyio amang’ana akaba agokwanwa iga: “Inee! Saulo nere nabeire oyomo bw’ababani?”
english: A man who lived there answered, "And who is their father?" So it became a saying: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

ekegusii: Oyo bwanchete obong’aini nigo akomogokia ise, korende oyogotaara amo nabakungu abatayayi nigo agosiria chinibo chiaye.
english: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.

ekegusii: Omonto okona‐gokurerwa botambe ase okorongeigwa, korende okong’ia ebigoti, oyio nasirigwe mobosokano, tagokonywa.
english: A man who remains stiff-necked after many rebukes will suddenly be destroyed-- without remedy.

ekegusii: Omonto ogotiga enchera y’obomanyi, oyio nabeere ase omosangererekano bw’abanto bakwete.
english: A man who strays from the path of understanding comes to rest in the company of the dead.

ekegusii: Engaki eyio omonto nabwate oyomwabo baiboire komo amotebie, “Aye nobwate chianga okobeka, ase ayio kabe omogambi oito, otenenere obogambi obo bwanyegerigwe.”
english: A man will seize one of his brothers at his father's home, and say, "You have a cloak, you be our leader; take charge of this heap of ruins!"

ekegusii: Rora, omonto orenge noborwaire bwa ukoma akamochiera, akamotung’amera, akamotebia, “Omonene, onye ngwancha nonyare gonsibia.”
english: A man with leprosy came and knelt before him and said, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."

ekegusii: Omonto oyomo orenge noborwaire bwa ukoma agacha asare, akamosorora na komotung’amera, akamotebia, “Onye ngwancha, nonyare gonsibia.”
english: A man with leprosy came to him and begged him on his knees, "If you are willing, you can make me clean."

ekegusii: Na abanto b’enyomba y’omonto inababe ababisa baye.
english: a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.'

ekegusii: Oboriri bw’omonto nigo bokomosiria ase enchera yaye, erio enkoro y’omonto oyio yagechigwa ase Omonene.
english: A man's own folly ruins his life, yet his heart rages against the LORD.

ekegusii: Oboenenu bw’omonto nigo bokomokeeyia, korende oyore nomoika bw’oboitongo nigo akonyora ogosikwa okonene.
english: A man's pride brings him low, but a man of lowly spirit gains honor.

ekegusii: Embooria y’obogima bw’omonto omonda nechinibo chiaye, korende omonto omotaka tari kogoswa nonde.
english: A man's riches may ransom his life, but a poor man hears no threat.

ekegusii: Omoika bw’oboremu nigo okogera omonto oremereria ogochandeka, korende omoika ore nomoichano ning’o orayoremererie.
english: A man's spirit sustains him in sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?

ekegusii: Omonene nere okoraa chinchera chi’omonto, ase ayio naki omonto aranyare komanya chinchera chiaye?
english: A man's steps are directed by the LORD. How then can anyone understand his own way?

ekegusii: Obong’aini bw’omonto nigo bokogera oremereria okogechigwa, na okoombia okomocha nigo kore obonene bwaye.
english: A man's wisdom gives him patience; it is to his glory to overlook an offense.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Inwe abanto baane, igwa amang’ana nkoborokereria, tegerera moigwe amang’ana ’omonwa one.
english: A maskil of Asaph. O my people, hear my teaching; listen to the words of my mouth.

ekegusii: (Ototera gw’Asafu) Nyasae, nase ki gwatotigire kegima? Ninki gekogera endamwamu yao yokire igoro ye ching’ondi chi’oborisia bwao?
english: A maskil of Asaph. Why have you rejected us forever, O God? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?

ekegusii: (Ogosaba gwa Daudi ekero arenge ase rikuruma) Nigo nkorera neriogi ase okorangeria Omonene, naaka eriogi ase okomosaba amabera.
english: A maskil of David. When he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift up my voice to the LORD for mercy.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Etani Omoezara) Aye Omonene, goika kare na kare ninterere obwanchani bwao bogendererete botambe, nindarie obwegenwa bwao ase ebiaare bionsi.
english: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the LORD's great love forever; with my mouth I will make your faithfulness known through all generations.

ekegusii: Oyore omobwatania tari omobwatania ase oyomo, korende Nyasae noyomo.
english: A mediator, however, does not represent just one party; but God is one.

ekegusii: Abanto bakairera Daudi amang’ana, bakamotebia, “Abaisraeli babwatanire n’Abisalomu bamoigwereire.”
english: A messenger came and told David, "The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom."

ekegusii: omonto obwate amang’ana akaminyoka gochia ase Ayubu, akamotebia, “Chiombe nigo chiarenge korema, ne chitigere nigo chiarenge korisia ang’e ase chiombe chiria.
english: a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,

ekegusii: Erio omonto agacha ase Saulo akamotebia, “Irana, ayerera bwango, ekiagera Abafilisti bachire mobosokano korwania ense yaito.”
english: a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land."

ekegusii: A miktam of David. Keep me safe, O God, for in you I take refuge.
english: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Aye Nyasae, ondende, ekiagera naye ngotamera.

ekegusii: Omonyacheche tancheti omonto okomokurera, tagwancha kogenda ase abang’aini.
english: A mocker resents correction; he will not consult the wise.

ekegusii: “Egesaku kiarure sugusu gocha korwania Babeli. Nagesarie ense eyio ebe buna erooro, na monto onde takomenya aroro; abanto nabatame ne ching’iti boigo.”
english: A nation from the north will attack her and lay waste her land. No one will live in it; both men and animals will flee away.

ekegusii: Egesaku kere ne chinguru getari kobareka kiaumokeire ense yane nigo kebwate amaino anga buna ay’endo, na amagegu aye nigo anga buna ay’endo eaberi.
english: A nation has invaded my land, powerful and without number; it has the teeth of a lion, the fangs of a lioness.

ekegusii: Kera egesure igoro ye chisiiro nigo giachabeire nebichanga bitano na bibere biasisire goetanana.
english: A network of interwoven chains festooned the capitals on top of the pillars, seven for each capital.

ekegusii: Engori y’ogotegerwa nebiswe ase riroba ase agotacha, na oboreba botegwe ase enchera agoeta.
english: A noose is hidden for him on the ground; a trap lies in his path.

ekegusii: Abange ase baria abaare gokora chingencho chi’oboragori, bagasangereria ebitabu biabo, bakabisamba ase amasio ’abanto bonsi. Kobakorire omobaro bwe rigori ri’ebitabu ebio, bakanyora ng’a mbiisanete chiropia chie chifeta chilifu emerongo etano.
english: A number who had practiced sorcery brought their scrolls together and burned them publicly. When they calculated the value of the scrolls, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.

ekegusii: Omonto otari kogechigwa bwango nigo abwate okomanya okonene, korende oyo okoberoroka bwango nigo agokinia oboriri bwaye.
english: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man displays folly.

ekegusii: abanto bachire korwa ase ense ya Misiri, na barabwo nigo bare abange, batubete orogongo rwonsi. Ere nigo aganetie imbaragererie, erinde abarwanie, ababue na kobaseria.”
english: 'A people that has come out of Egypt covers the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I will be able to fight them and drive them away.'"

ekegusii: Abanto b’egesaku motamanyeti nabarie okwama kwe riroba riaino, na baire ebinto mwabeire mogochandekera; barabwo mbabakorere bobe, babachande botambe.
english: A people that you do not know will eat what your land and labor produce, and you will have nothing but cruel oppression all your days.

ekegusii: Abanto aba nigo bakongechia na gokora bobe ase obosio bwane botambe; nigo bakoruera ebing’wanso ase emegondo ime na basambera ubani igoro ase ebisasimero bi’amatabori.
english: a people who continually provoke me to my very face, offering sacrifices in gardens and burning incense on altars of brick;

ekegusii: Omonto omonyaborimo nigo akona‐gotaara‐taaria amang’ana akorenta eriomana, na omogenki nigo akorenta obobisa ase abanto banchaine.
english: A perverse man stirs up dissension, and a gossip separates close friends.

ekegusii: Omonto omotaka nigo akogechwa nabanto bamwabo bonsi, gose tikori ogokumia ng’a abasani baye bamotigire. Nigo egenete amang’ana abo, ko aba bosa asare.
english: A poor man is shunned by all his relatives-- how much more do his friends avoid him! Though he pursues them with pleading, they are nowhere to be found.

ekegusii: Ekero omonto omotaka agokwana nigo agosorora, korende omonda nigo akoiraneria ase obotindi.
english: A poor man pleads for mercy, but a rich man answers harshly.

ekegusii: Oboremo oboyia bw’omonto omotaka nigo bokwama endagera enyinge, korende enyinge nigo egosiara‐siarerwa yasira ase engencho y’obobe.
english: A poor man's field may produce abundant food, but injustice sweeps it away.

ekegusii: (Omonto ochandegete okorera ase Omonene) Aye Omonene, igwa ogosaba kwane; ekerero kiane tiga geike asore.
english: A prayer of an afflicted man. When he is faint and pours out his lament before the LORD. Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come to you.

ekegusii: (Ogosaba gwa Daudi) Aye Omonene, integerera, onyigwe na ong’iranerie, ekiagera nigo inde omotaka na omoremerwa.
english: A prayer of David. Hear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Aye Omonene, tegerera oigwe okogania kwane kw’ogokorerwa oboronge, igwa okorera kwane na ogosaba kwane, omonwa one tori gokwana obong’ainereria.
english: A prayer of David. Hear, O LORD, my righteous plea; listen to my cry. Give ear to my prayer-- it does not rise from deceitful lips.

ekegusii: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. On shigionoth.
english: Oko nogosaba kw’omobani Habakuki.

ekegusii: (Ogosaba kwa Musa, omonto o Nyasae) Omonene, aye nigo ore obotamero bwaito ebiaare ase ebiaare.
english: A prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place throughout all generations.

ekegusii: Ekero Abalawi bakorenterwa chinsemo echio chia ikomi, omokuani, omonto bw’ororeria rwa Haroni, goika abe amo nabarabwo. Abalawi abwo mbarusie ensemo ya ikomi ye chinsemo echio chia ikomi, bayeire ase ebinyomba bi’enyomba ya Nyasae.
english: A priest descended from Aaron is to accompany the Levites when they receive the tithes, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of the tithes up to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.

ekegusii: Ekaba agwo omokuani oyomo akaoroka, ogoeta ase enchera eria, akamorora, agaeta ensemo.
english: A priest happened to be going down the same road, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.

ekegusii: Abayuda na abanto ba Yerusalemu bakararerigwa barente ase Omonene ebango eria Musa, omosomba o Nyasae, abekerete Abaisraeli agwo ase erooro.
english: A proclamation was then issued in Judah and Jerusalem that they should bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God had required of Israel in the desert.

ekegusii: Erio amang’ana akararigwa ase ense yonsi y’Abayuda, na ase Yerusalemu, ng’a abanto abwo bairanete korwa ase obosomba basangererekane agwo Yerusalemu.
english: A proclamation was then issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem for all the exiles to assemble in Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo akobisa aya amanyete, korende abariri nigo bakoraria oboriri korwa ase chinkoro chiabo.
english: A prudent man keeps his knowledge to himself, but the heart of fools blurts out folly.

ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo akororera emechando korwa aare, bwebisa, korende oyotamanyeti amange nigo akogenderera gochia bosio, oumerana nero, erio ochandeka.
english: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge, but the simple keep going and suffer for it.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Nyasae nigo agotenena ase omosangererekano oye omochenu, ase egati ye chinyasae nigo akonacha ekina.
english: A psalm of Asaph. God presides in the great assembly; he gives judgment among the "gods":

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Aye Nyasae, abanto batakomanyeti bachire basoire ase omwando oo, barabwo bakorire Hekalu yao Enchenu yabeire eyetachenegeti, bakorire Yerusalemu obeire chitui chi’amagena.
english: A psalm of Asaph. O God, the nations have invaded your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple, they have reduced Jerusalem to rubble.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Ekeene, Nyasae nigo are omuya mono ase Abaisraeli, ee, ase abwo bare ne chinkoro chichenegete.
english: A psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Nyasae omonguru, Nyasae Omonene, nigo agokwana, nigo agokwana na korangeria ense yonsi korwa moocha goika bosongo.
english: A psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to the place where it sets.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, tontogonyera ekero ore nendamwamu, tong’a egesusuro gi’okondongeyia ekero ore nekeririanda.
english: A psalm of David. A petition. O LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger or discipline me in your wrath.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Inwe abana ba Nyasae, motogie Omonene, atora obonene bw’Omonene ne chinguru chiaye.
english: A psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD, O mighty ones, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, monto ki oranyare komenya ase obomenyo bwao? Ning’o oranyare komenya ase egetunwa kiao egechenu?
english: A psalm of David. LORD, who may dwell in your sanctuary? Who may live on your holy hill?

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Aye Omonene, oigwe ogosaba kwane; ase engencho y’oboronge bwao otegerere ogosorora kwane, ong’iranerie ase engencho y’obwegenwa bwao.
english: A psalm of David. O LORD, hear my prayer, listen to my cry for mercy; in your faithfulness and righteousness come to my relief.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, nigo ngokorangeria, ayerera oche bwango! Tegerera oigwe eriogi riane ekero ngokorangeria.
english: A psalm of David. O LORD, I call to you; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to you.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene nomorisia one, tinkoremerwa kende,
english: A psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not be in want.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi ekero arenge gotama Abisalomu, omwana oye) Aye Omonene, ababisa baane nigo bare abange; abange mono banyimokeire gonkora bobe.
english: A psalm of David. When he fled from his son Absalom. O LORD, how many are my foes! How many rise up against me!

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi ekero arenge ase erooro ya Yuda) Aye Nyasae, Nyasae one, naye ngotang’ana korigia. Omoyo one nigo ore nerang’o asore, na omobere one nigo okoganetie, ase ense y’eguru‐gura enyomo pa etari namache.
english: A psalm of David. When he was in the Desert of Judah. O God, you are my God, earnestly I seek you; my soul thirsts for you, my body longs for you, in a dry and weary land where there is no water.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Aye Nyasae one na omoruoti one, ninkobake, nimbe ngotogia erieta riao goika kare na kare.
english: A psalm of praise. Of David. I will exalt you, my God the King; I will praise your name for ever and ever.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi ekero aatananete hekalu ekaba enchenu) Aye Omonene, ningotogie, ekiagera kwanyimokirie korwa inse, tigwatigete ababisa baane betogie igoro yane.
english: A psalm. A song. For the dedication of the temple. Of David. I will exalt you, O LORD, for you lifted me out of the depths and did not let my enemies gloat over me.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gw’Esabato) Nigo ere buya gokoakera aye Omonene ng’a mbuya mono, na gotera ase ogotogia erieta riao, aye Omonene Ore Igoro Mono.
english: A psalm. A song. For the Sabbath day. It is good to praise the LORD and make music to your name, O Most High,

ekegusii: (Ogotera kw’ogoaka ng’a mbuya mono) Inwe abanto b’ense yonsi, moterere Omonene more nomochengo!
english: A psalm. For giving thanks. Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth.

ekegusii: Moterere Omonene ogotera okoyia, ekiagera okorire amang’ana ay’ogokumia; obuire nokoboko kwaye gw’okorio, ee, nokoboko kwaye ogochenu.
english: A psalm. Sing to the LORD a new song, for he has done marvelous things; his right hand and his holy arm have worked salvation for him.

ekegusii: Omokungu omonyariomana nigo anga buna amatoima ’embura akona‐gotonya.
english: A quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping on a rainy day;

ekegusii: Omonto okogechigwa bwango nigo agokora ay’oboriri, na omonto okoroberia ay’obobe nigo akogechwa.
english: A quick-tempered man does foolish things, and a crafty man is hated.

ekegusii: Omonto ore nobomanyi nigo akweorokereria korwa ase ogotogonyerwa okomo, kobua omonto omoriri otari kweorokereria korwa ase ogoakwa ebiranya rigana erimo.
english: A rebuke impresses a man of discernment more than a hundred lashes a fool.

ekegusii: A record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ the son of David, the son of Abraham:
english: Oyo noro omoroberio bw’ororeria rwaye Yeso Kristo, omwana o Daudi, omwana o Ibrahimu.

ekegusii: Abatigari, abwo bare b’ororeria rwa Yakobo, mbamoiranere Nyasae Omobui.
english: A remnant will return, a remnant of Jacob will return to the Mighty God.

ekegusii: Omonto omonda nigo akwerengereria ng’a nomong’aini are, korende omonto omotaka ore nokomanya nigo aramotuke amomanye.
english: A rich man may be wise in his own eyes, but a poor man who has discernment sees through him.

ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge nigo agochandekera obogima bwe chitugo chiaye, korende enkoro y’omokori amabe nigo ere entindi.
english: A righteous man cares for the needs of his animal, but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel.

ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge nigo are omoraai omuya bw’omogisangio oye, korende chinchera chi’abakori amabe nigo chikobatang’ana chiabasiria.
english: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge nigo akonyora emechando emenge, korende Omonene namotoorie korwa ase eyio yonsi;
english: A righteous man may have many troubles, but the LORD delivers him from them all;

ekegusii: Orooche rw’omorero rogasoka korwa asare. Chilifu ne chilifu bakamokorera; ne chilifu ikomi ara chilifu ikomi bagatenena ase obosio bwaye. Ab’ekegambero bagaikaransa kogamba, ne chibuku chikamaanorwa.
english: A river of fire was flowing, coming out from before him. Thousands upon thousands attended him; ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court was seated, and the books were opened.

ekegusii: Orooche rogasoka korwa ase Edeni na kobekera omogondo oria amache. Korwa agwo rogaatananeka, rokaba chindooche inye.
english: A river watering the garden flowed from Eden; from there it was separated into four headwaters.

ekegusii: Ebinyomba mbiarengeo amo nebisieri biabo ang’e ne chisiiro agwo ase amaagacho onsi arenge nebiita; agwo nao ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa biarenge gosiberigwa.
english: A room with a doorway was by the portico in each of the inner gateways, where the burnt offerings were washed.

ekegusii: Ning’onchorane oboruoti obo, ee, nimboonchorane, nimboonchorane; tibobao nonya ng’ake goika oyio oboruoti obo bore obwaye achiche, oyio nere ndaboe.
english: A ruin! A ruin! I will make it a ruin! It will not be restored until he comes to whom it rightfully belongs; to him I will give it.'

ekegusii: Omonto omotaka ore nokobua ogokorera abataka bande bobe ase okobaurereria, nigo anga buna embura enyinge egosaria chindagera.
english: A ruler who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no crops.

ekegusii: Omogambi naoroke korwa ase egati y’abanto ba Yakobo asirie abanto batameire emechie banyore oborendi.”
english: A ruler will come out of Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city."

ekegusii: Omonto otagwenereti kende ore omokori amabe nigo agoeta‐eta, ogokwana oborimo korwa ase omonwa oye.
english: A scoundrel and villain, who goes about with a corrupt mouth,

ekegusii: Omonto otagwenereti kende nigo akona‐koremora amabe, ne chinkwana chiaye nigo chinga omorero ogosamba.
english: A scoundrel plots evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.

ekegusii: Na agwo Ekibatana, omochie omonene ase orogongo rw’Abamedia, ebuku ekanyorekana erikire amang’ana aya:
english: A scroll was found in the citadel of Ecbatana in the province of Media, and this was written on it: Memorandum:

ekegusii: Omomalaika onde, oyo o kabere, akamotunyana, ogoteba, “Babeli ogure! Babeli, omochie oria omonene, ogure, oyo onyoisirie abanto b’ebisaku bionsi edivai y’endamwamu y’obotomani bwaye!”
english: A second angel followed and said, "Fallen! Fallen is Babylon the Great, which made all the nations drink the maddening wine of her adulteries."

ekegusii: A second time they summoned the man who had been blind. "Give glory to God," they said. "We know this man is a sinner."
english: Erio eria kabere bakarangeria omonto oria orenge omouko, bakamotebia, “Moe Nyasae ogotogia; intwe twamanyire ng’a omonto oyio nomonyene ebibe.”

ekegusii: A servant cannot be corrected by mere words; though he understands, he will not respond.
english: Amang’ana oka amasa takorongeyia omosomba, ekiagera naba oyamanyete, takoyaigwera.

ekegusii: A servant girl saw him seated there in the firelight. She looked closely at him and said, "This man was with him."
english: Erio omoiseke oyomo akamorora oikaransete ang’e nomorero, akamobeta amaiso akabora, “Oyo nere igo arenge amo nere.”

ekegusii: Ekero omosomba akoba omoruoti, na omonto omoriri akoigota endagera,
english: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is full of food,

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, Nyasae one, naye ngotamera, intoorie korwa ase abachandi baane, nkonye!
english: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjamite. O LORD my God, I take refuge in you; save and deliver me from all who pursue me,

ekegusii: Omoseboka norue ase ritina ria Yese riabutoretwe, na egesebo keramere korwa ase emeri yaye, nkiame amatunda.
english: A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; from his roots a Branch will bear fruit.

ekegusii: Ekiagera omonto oyomo ore korokwa Demeterio, omoturi bwe chifeta, oyorenge gokora ebihekalu bie chifeta bi’Aritemi, nigo arenge konyorera abaroisia enibo enyinge.
english: A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought in no little business for the craftsmen.

ekegusii: Amaakwa amabe buna ayio nache boigo ase chibarasi, ne chiyombo, ne chingamia, ne chitigere, ne ching’iti chinde chionsi chire ase ebitwori biabo.
english: A similar plague will strike the horses and mules, the camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.

ekegusii: Oyotamanyeti amange nigo akwegena kera ring’ana, korende oyomanyete nigo akorigereria aase agochia.
english: A simple man believes anything, but a prudent man gives thought to his steps.

ekegusii: Omonto omworo tari korema ase engaki egwenerete, na ekero rigesa riaikire, nigo akogenda gosuma, takonyora gento.
english: A sluggard does not plow in season; so at harvest time he looks but finds nothing.

ekegusii: Nasesenirie kera omonto omoirogete Omonene, naende obwatete chinchera chiaye.
english: A song of ascents. Blessed are all who fear the LORD, who walk in his ways.

ekegusii: Ekero inde nemechando nigo nkorera ase Omonene, ere nigo akonyigwa.
english: A song of ascents. I call on the LORD in my distress, and he answers me.

ekegusii: Ninyimokererie amaiso aane gochia ase ebitunwa. Ogokonywa kwane, ng’ai korarwe?
english: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to the hills-- where does my help come from?

ekegusii: Ninyimokererie amaiso aane gocha asore, agwo igoro ase omenyete.
english: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to you, to you whose throne is in heaven.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, oinyore Daudi, ase engencho y’obokong’u bwonsi bwamonyorete.
english: A song of ascents. O LORD, remember David and all the hardships he endured.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Rora buna ere buya na okogokia okonene ekero abanto abamo bakomenya amo, baigwanaine.
english: A song of ascents. Of David. How good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity!

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Nigo nabete nomogoko ekero abanto bantebetie, “Inchuo, togende ase enyomba y’Omonene!”
english: A song of ascents. Of David. I rejoiced with those who said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD."

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Inee! Naki yare gocha koba onye Omonene atabete ase ensemo yaito? Tiga Abaisraeli bairanerie.
english: A song of ascents. Of David. If the LORD had not been on our side-- let Israel say--

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Omonene, ase enkoro yane tindi kweimokereria igoro, gose tindi omwerori. Inche tinyechandeti kwerigeria amang’ana amanene, gose ayare amakong’u mono asende.
english: A song of ascents. Of David. My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty; I do not concern myself with great matters or things too wonderful for me.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Sulemani) Onye Omonene takoagacha enyomba, abwo bakoyeagacha nigo bagokora emeremo ya bosa. Onye Omonene takorenda omochie omonto oyio okoyorenda nigo akorenda bosa.
english: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchmen stand guard in vain.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, nigo nkorera asore, korwa ase chindiba ime.
english: A song of ascents. Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD;

ekegusii: Inchuo motogie Omonene, inwe abasomba baye mwensi, inwe abamokomokorera ase enyomba yaye botuko.
english: A song of ascents. Praise the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who minister by night in the house of the LORD.

ekegusii: “Ababisa nigo batochandete korwa oboke bwaito.” Nabo Abaisraeli bagoteba.
english: A song of ascents. They have greatly oppressed me from my youth-- let Israel say--

ekegusii: Abwo bamosemeretie Omonene nigo banga buna egetunwa gia Sayoni getari konyegerigwa, korende nigo kegendererete kobao botambe.
english: A song of ascents. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but endures forever.

ekegusii: Ekero Omonene atoiraneretie intwe aba Sayoni amaya aito, nigo twabete buna nkorota tore.
english: A song of ascents. When the LORD brought back the captives to Zion, we were like men who dreamed.

ekegusii: A song. A psalm of Asaph. O God, do not keep silent; be not quiet, O God, be not still.
english: (Ogotera gw’Asafu) Aye Nyasae, tokira‐kiri! Nyasae, totoerera na gotimoka.

ekegusii: (Ogotera gwa Daudi) Aye Nyasae, enkoro yane nigo ere noboremu! Nintere na gochenga! Omoyo one bwonsi, boka!
english: A song. A psalm of David. My heart is steadfast, O God; I will sing and make music with all my soul.

ekegusii: (Ogotera kwa basinto ba Kora; okworokereria kwa Hamani Omoezara) Aye Omonene, Nyasae bw’ogotooreka kwane, omobaso na obotuko nigo nkorera asore ng’a onkonye.
english: A song. A psalm of the Sons of Korah. For the director of music. According to mahalath leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God who saves me, day and night I cry out before you.

ekegusii: (Ogotera kwa basinto ba Kora) Omonene nigo are omonene mono, goika atogigwe; ere goika atogigwe agwo ase omochie o Nyasae oito, ase egetunwa kiaye egechenu.
english: A song. A psalm of the Sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and most worthy of praise, in the city of our God, his holy mountain.

ekegusii: Embeo egaeta ase obosio bwane, na amarionya ’omobere one agatenena.
english: A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.

ekegusii: Na rora ekerecha nigo gekomobwata, na ere bwango nigo akorera, naende kemogaragaria, erinde asokia amasombogoku, korende tikeri komorua otatiga ase okomosionora mono.
english: A spirit seizes him and he suddenly screams; it throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It scarcely ever leaves him and is destroying him.

ekegusii: Ensoko gose aase amache akogachwa nabigenderere koba ebichenegete, korende ebinto binde bionsi ebiaao biise gokuna ching’iti echio chikwete mbibe ebitachenegeti.
english: A spring, however, or a cistern for collecting water remains clean, but anyone who touches one of these carcasses is unclean.

ekegusii: Omonto obwate ribero nigo akoayerera koba omonda, gose tari korengereria ng’a obotaka mbomonyore.
english: A stingy man is eager to get rich and is unaware that poverty awaits him.

ekegusii: Rigena rikarentwa rigakuneka ase omonwa bw’engoro eria, erio omoruoti akabeka ekemanyererio kiaye omonyene amo nebi’abanene b’oboruoti bwaye, erinde amang’ana ande onsi Danieli akoreretwe taonchorwa.
english: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that Daniel's situation might not be changed.

ekegusii: Enyancha egachaka koimoka ase engencho y’omwaga omonge orenge kogusa.
english: A strong wind was blowing and the waters grew rough.

ekegusii: na etuoni egwesigoria, na egoree, na omoruoti okoraa abarwani baye b’esegi.
english: a strutting rooster, a he-goat, and a king with his army around him.

ekegusii: Omworokigwa tari omonene kobua omworokia oye, korende kera oyomo gakoorire kworokererigwa nabe buna omworokia oye.
english: A student is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

ekegusii: Omoro obe igoro ase abaringoria, erinde babe abariri! Omoro obe igoro ase abarwani baye bare chituoni, erinde basirigwe!
english: A sword against her false prophets! They will become fools. A sword against her warriors! They will be filled with terror.

ekegusii: Omoro obe igoro ase chibarasi ne chigari chia Babeli! Omoro obe igoro ase abarwani esegi b’ense eng’ao, abare ase egati yabo, erinde obakore babe buna abakungu! Omoro obe igoro ase chinibo chiabo erinde chisakorwe!
english: A sword against her horses and chariots and all the foreigners in her ranks! They will become women. A sword against her treasures! They will be plundered.

ekegusii: Omoro nochiche igoro ya Misiri, na emechando emenene nebe aaria Etiopia, ekero abanto ba Misiri baraitwe, na obotenenku bwabo boirwe, na amaroso ’ense eria naiyerigwe inse.”
english: A sword will come against Egypt, and anguish will come upon Cush. When the slain fall in Egypt, her wealth will be carried away and her foundations torn down.

ekegusii: Naki eema eria ye ritang’ani yaroisetigwe. Ime ase eema eria mbiarengeo ekebekerero gie chitaya, na emesa amo nemegati yarenge koruegwa ase Nyasae. Aase aria are korokwa Aase Aachenu.
