ekegusii: Riko riaye nigo riarenge ase chianga chiaye, torengereretie igoro y’omoerio oye. Ase ayio okogwa kwaye gokaba ogw’okoondokia, torenge nonde okoyoremia. “Aye Omonene, rigereria emechando yane, ekiagera omobisa one ngwetogia are!”
english: Her filthiness clung to her skirts; she did not consider her future. Her fall was astounding; there was none to comfort her. "Look, O LORD, on my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed."

ekegusii: Ababisa baye babeire abanene baye, ee, ababisa baye nigo bagendererete goseseneka. Omonene oyotomeire emechando ase engencho y’ogosaria kwaye okonge, na ababisa baye bairire abana baye ase obosomba.
english: Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. The LORD has brought her grief because of her many sins. Her children have gone into exile, captive before the foe.

ekegusii: Ebiita biaye biarimeire ase riroba, emekorogoto yaye yabunirwe na gosarigwa. Omoruoti oye, na abagambi baye, nigo bamenyete ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku bitabwati amachiko, na ababani baye tibari konyora amaroro korwa ase Omonene.
english: Her gates have sunk into the ground; their bars he has broken and destroyed. Her king and her princes are exiled among the nations, the law is no more, and her prophets no longer find visions from the LORD.

ekegusii: Akarambora okoboko kwaye, akaimokia ekerochi ki’eema, na ase okoboko kwaye gw’okorio akaimokia ekegogi, agaakera Sisera nakerokio, agakong’onta omotwe oye, akabeta chintakunero chiaye gochia ime.
english: Her hand reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman's hammer. She struck Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.

ekegusii: Enyomba yaye nero enchera ekogenda aase abakure; ee, enchera eyio nigo ekogenda ase chiero chi’amakweri.
english: Her house is a highway to the grave, leading down to the chambers of death.

ekegusii: Enkoro y’omosacha oye nigo emwegenete, gose omosacha oyio takoremerwa konyora ebitoki.
english: Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value.

ekegusii: Omosacha bw’omokungu oyio nigo amanyekanete ase ebiita bi’omochie, agwo ase agoikaransa ogamba ebina amo nabagaaka b’ense eyio.
english: Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he takes his seat among the elders of the land.

ekegusii: Eira ende yonsi, gose ogotiana konde gwonsi kw’ogwetanga korwa ase egento gete, omokungu oria arakore, omosacha oye nabo aranyare koyianchera, gose kwanga.
english: Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow she makes or any sworn pledge to deny herself.

ekegusii: Omosacha oria akaimoka ore nomosomba oyomo ne chitigere ibere, akagenda kogamba nere ase obwororo, agateema komoebereria airane nere. Omokungu oria akamosoyia nyomba mwa ise, na ise akamoroisia ase omogoko.
english: her husband went to her to persuade her to return. He had with him his servant and two donkeys. She took him into her father's house, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.

ekegusii: Korende omosacha oye akamotunyana goika Bahurimu okona‐korera. Erio Abineri akamotebia, “Irana!” Ere akairana.
english: Her husband, however, went with her, weeping behind her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back home!" So he went back.

ekegusii: Omoruoti amo nabagambi b’oboruoti bwaye mbooswe bairwe ase obosomba.” Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: Her king will go into exile, he and his officials together," says the LORD.

ekegusii: Abatang’ani b’omochie oyio nigo bakogamba ebina ase okoegwa riaaki, na abakuani baye nigo bakworokereria ase ogoakanerwa, na ababani baye nigo bagokora oboringoria ase okoegwa chibesa. Nonya naboigo nigo bakweegeka ase Omonene, bateba, “Inee! Omonene tari ase egati yaito? Amang’ana amabe tagotonyora.”
english: Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD and say, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come upon us."

ekegusii: Naomi akamoboria, “Ng’ai kware gochora ebigara rero? Nase omogondo o ng’o kware gokora emeremo? Nyasae asesenie omonto oyio ogwechandera kogokonya!” Rutu agatebia Naomi ng’a nigo arenge gokora emeremo ase omogondo bw’omonto ore korokwa Boazi.
english: Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the one at whose place she had been working. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said.

ekegusii: Abatureti baye na eamate yaye bakaigwa ng’a Omonene omororeire amabera amange, bakagoka amo nere.
english: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they shared her joy.

ekegusii: Abanto abasike tibagotokao baranyare kobekwa bagambe; abagambi babo bonsi nigo barasire.
english: Her nobles will have nothing there to be called a kingdom, all her princes will vanish away.

ekegusii: Abagambi bare ime yaye nigo banga buna chindo chikoronya, na abagambi ebina baye nigo banga buna chisese chi’orosana chikoria mogoroba, tichiri gotigaria kende goika mambia.
english: Her officials are roaring lions, her rulers are evening wolves, who leave nothing for the morning.

ekegusii: Abagambi baye nigo banga buna chisese chi’orosana chigotandorana ebi chiaitire. Baitire abanto abange ase okwenyorera ebitoki ase enchera etari ey’obwegenwa.
english: Her officials within her are like wolves tearing their prey; they shed blood and kill people to make unjust gain.

ekegusii: Abaibori baye bagakumia, mono, korende akabachika tibatebia monto ayakoreka.
english: Her parents were astonished, but he ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Babeli nabaronye amo buna chindo chikoronya; nabarere buna chindo chinsae.
english: Her people all roar like young lions, they growl like lion cubs.

ekegusii: Abakuani baye basaririe ogochika kwane, na bakorire ebinto biane ebichenu biabeire ebitachenegeti. Tibakoreti ogwatananekana ase egati y’egento kere egechenu, na egetari egechenu, gose tiborokerereti abanto baatanane ebinto bitachenegeti korwa ase ebichenegete, naende bamiamirie amaiso abo ng’a tibasika Chisabato chiane, na ase enchera eyio bankorire koba buna oyo otachenegeti ase egati yabo.
english: Her priests do violence to my law and profane my holy things; they do not distinguish between the holy and the common; they teach that there is no difference between the unclean and the clean; and they shut their eyes to the keeping of my Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.

ekegusii: Ababani baye nigo bagwetogia ase amang’ana abo abanyene; nigo bare abanto abang’ainereria; abakuani baye bakorire ekere egechenu koba egetachenegeti, na basaririe amachiko.
english: Her prophets are arrogant; they are treacherous men. Her priests profane the sanctuary and do violence to the law.

ekegusii: Ababani babo babaakire echooka etochoganiri buya; nigo bakobarorera amaroro ’oborimo na kobaringoreria oborimo, bateba: Aya naro Omonene Nyasae agoteba, na Omonene takwaneti bo.
english: Her prophets whitewash these deeds for them by false visions and lying divinations. They say, 'This is what the Sovereign LORD says'-- when the LORD has not spoken.

ekegusii: Abanto abanda bare ase egati yaino baichire nobourereria, na abwo bamenyete agwo nigo bagokwana oborimo, ne chimeme chiabo nigo chire echi’obong’ainereria.
english: Her rich men are violent; her people are liars and their tongues speak deceitfully.

ekegusii: Omoika oye okairana, agatenena erio kegima. Yeso akabachika bamoe endagera arie.
english: Her spirit returned, and at once she stood up. Then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.

ekegusii: Emechie y’ense eyio yasirigwe yabeire ey’okoondokia, yabeire enyomo na erooro, ense etamenyiri na monto onde, na mwanyabanto onde tagoeta aroro.
english: Her towns will be desolate, a dry and desert land, a land where no one lives, through which no man travels.

ekegusii: Chinchera chiaye nigo chire echi’omogoko, na oboeto bwaye bwonsi nigo bore obw’omorembe.
english: Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peace.

ekegusii: “Amaicho amange e chingamia amo ne chimori chiabo narentwe asore korwa Midiani na Efa. Abanto bonsi ba Seba mbache asore, mbarente chitahabu na ubani, bararie ogotogigwa kw’Omonene.
english: Herds of camels will cover your land, young camels of Midian and Ephah. And all from Sheba will come, bearing gold and incense and proclaiming the praise of the LORD.

ekegusii: Bakamoroiseria endagera aria. Martha ere agakora emeremo eyio, korende Lazaro nigo arenge oyomo bwa baria baikaransete ase endagera amo nere.
english: Here a dinner was given in Jesus' honor. Martha served, while Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with him.

ekegusii: Ime ase ebio mbarenge abanto abange abarwaire baare korara, emeuko, ebirema, na amagata, [baganyete amache aturubanigwe.
english: Here a great number of disabled people used to lie-- the blind, the lame, the paralyzed.

ekegusii: Naama! Inche amo nabana aba Omonene ang’eire nigo tore ebimanyererio na emegwekano ase egati y’Abaisraeli, ebio bikorwa ase Omonene bw’Emeganda, oyio omenyete ase Egetunwa gia Sayoni.
english: Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me. We are signs and symbols in Israel from the LORD Almighty, who dwells on Mount Zion.

ekegusii: Aba nabwo abanto bakorete emeremo amo nororeria rwabo: Korwa ase ororeria rwa Kohati: Hemani, omonene bw’abateri, mosinto o Yoeli o Samweli,
english: Here are the men who served, together with their sons: From the Kohathites: Heman, the musician, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,

ekegusii: Aya naro amarieta ’ebitwori bi’Abaisraeli, ekero baare ase orogendo korwa ase ense ya Misiri, baare ase emeganda yabo inse y’oboraai bwa Musa na Haroni.
english: Here are the stages in the journey of the Israelites when they came out of Egypt by divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.

ekegusii: Here he is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying a word to him. Have the authorities really concluded that he is the Christ?
english: Nao are aa gokwana maiso marore gose tibari komotebia ing’ana? Aande gose abanene bamanyire bori ng’a nere Kristo?

ekegusii: Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with him, and he with me.
english: Rigereria, ninteneine gesieri gotura; omonto karaigwe eriogi riane na koigora egesieri, ninsoe asare, nindagere amo nere, na ere amo nainche.

ekegusii: Bono inche nao inde aa. Inwe mobe kirori asende ase obosio bw’Omonene na obw’omoakwa amaguta oye. Inee! Neng’ombe ya ng’o nairete? Gose netigere ya ng’o nairete? Ning’o naureretie, gose nakorerete bobe? Gose nkorwa ase okoboko kwa ng’o naetwe riaaki rikang’ukoria amaiso aane? Onye nakorete ayio, nimbairanerie ebio nairete.”
english: Here I stand. Testify against me in the presence of the LORD and his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe to make me shut my eyes? If I have done any of these, I will make it right."

ekegusii: Ring’ana eri neri’ekeene, rigwenerete gwancherwa kegima, ng’a Kristo Yeso nigo achete ase ense gotooria abanyene ebibe, na ase abwo inche noyo bwe ritang’ani.
english: Here is a trustworthy saying that deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners-- of whom I am the worst.

ekegusii: Here is a trustworthy saying: If anyone sets his heart on being an overseer, he desires a noble task.
english: Ring’ana eri neri’ekeene, onye omonto origetie koba omotang’ani bw’ekanisa, igo aganetie emeremo emiya.

ekegusii: Here is a trustworthy saying: If we died with him, we will also live with him;
english: Ring’ana eri neri’ekeene: Onye twakwete amo nere, natobe moyo amo nere boigo.

ekegusii: Rora, Rebeka oyio ore ase obosio bwao, moire, mogende komo, achie koba omokungu bw’omwana bw’omonene oo, buna Omonene konya atebire.”
english: Here is Rebekah; take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has directed."

ekegusii: Aya naro agerete Yeroboamu akaba mamincha y’omoruoti. Sulemani nigo aagachete Milo, na agaticha egetongo kiarenge ase Omochie o Daudi ise.
english: Here is the account of how he rebelled against the king: Solomon had built the supporting terraces and had filled in the gap in the wall of the city of David his father.

ekegusii: Oyo noro omoroberio bw’emeremo Sulemani abetereretie abanto bakore: Akababeka koagacha enyomba y’Omonene, na enyomba yaye omonyene, na Milo, na orwaki rwaetanaine Yerusalemu, na emechie ya Hasori, na Megido, na Geseri,
english: Here is the account of the forced labor King Solomon conscripted to build the LORD's temple, his own palace, the supporting terraces, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

ekegusii: (agwo omokuani abeke omokungu oyio inse y’okoragererigwa gw’okomotiania) rirorio Omonene nagere abanto bao bakoragererie na kogochaya, karakore enda yao egombae na kobimba.
english: here the priest is to put the woman under this curse of the oath-- "may the LORD cause your people to curse and denounce you when he causes your thigh to waste away and your abdomen to swell.

ekegusii: Agwo takoba Omogiriki gose Omoyahudi, oyobwarogete gose oyotarogeti, oyotari Omogiriki gose oyore Omosikuti, omosomba gose omosibore, korende Kristo nere onsi, na ase bonsi.
english: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free, but Christ is all, and is in all.

ekegusii: Bakamobamba aroro amo nabanto bande babere, oyonde ensemo, na oyonde ensemo, na Yeso gati‐gati.
english: Here they crucified him, and with him two others-- one on each side and Jesus in the middle.

ekegusii: akamenta neri igoro ase onsi, agasiba Yohana echela.
english: Herod added this to them all: He locked John up in prison.

ekegusii: Goika akarigia komoita, korende akairoka abanto, ekiagera konya banchire ng’a Yohana nomobani orenge.
english: Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the people, because they considered him a prophet.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Hesiboni na Eleale nigo bakorera neriogi rinene. Eriogi riabo nigo rikoigweka goikera Yahasi. Ase ayio abarwani esegi ba Moabu bakorera neriogi rinene; chinkoro chiabo chiaondokire.
english: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out, their voices are heard all the way to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out, and their hearts are faint.

ekegusii: Heshbon and Jazer, together with their pasturelands-- four towns in all.
english: na Hesiboni, na Yaeseri, emechie ene, amo namarisio arengeo.

ekegusii: Heshbon and Jazer, together with their pasturelands.
english: na Hesiboni, na Yaeseri amo namarisio aetanaine emechie eyio.

ekegusii: Hesiboni noro orenge omochie omonene o Sihoni, omoruoti bw’Abaamori, oria konya orwanirie omoruoti orenge kogambera Abaamori agwo ritang’ani. Sihoni konya oirire ense yonsi y’omoruoti oyio goikera Arinoni.
english: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and had taken from him all his land as far as the Arnon.

ekegusii: Hezekia amo nabanto bonsi bakaba nomogoko ase ayio Nyasae akorerete abanto, ekiagera nigo abairanerete ase obwango.
english: Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had brought about for his people, because it was done so quickly.

ekegusii: Hezekia akaboria abakuani na Abalawi igoro ye chitui chiria,
english: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps;

ekegusii: Hezekia akairania abakuani na Abalawi, akabaroberia ase ebiombe. Kera oyomo obo akabekwa ase ekeombe kiaye koreng’ana nemeremo yaye arenge gokora. Bakabekwa korua ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa na ebi’omorembe, na gokora emeremo agwo ase ebiita bi’egetwori ki’Omonene, naende ase ogoaka ng’a mbuya mono ase Omonene na komotogia namatera.
english: Hezekiah assigned the priests and Levites to divisions-- each of them according to their duties as priests or Levites-- to offer burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, to minister, to give thanks and to sing praises at the gates of the LORD's dwelling.

ekegusii: Erio Hezekia agachika abanto baagache ebigachero ase enyomba y’Omonene. Na ekero babiaagachete,
english: Hezekiah gave orders to prepare storerooms in the temple of the LORD, and this was done.

ekegusii: Erio Hezekia agachika ng’a ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa keruegwe ase egesasimero. Ekero ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa giachagete koruegwa, abanto bagachaka goterera Omonene; na ababugia ebirombeta bakabibugia bakoraagwa nebinto bi’okobugigwa bia Daudi, omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli.
english: Hezekiah gave the order to sacrifice the burnt offering on the altar. As the offering began, singing to the LORD began also, accompanied by trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.

ekegusii: Hezekia akaboria Isaya, “Nkemanyererio ki ndaegwe ng’a Omonene nangwenie, naende ng’a nintiire ngende ase enyomba yaye rituko ria gatato?”
english: Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the temple of the LORD on the third day from now?"

ekegusii: Boigo Hezekia konya oboririe iga: “Nkemanyererio ki gekonyorokia ng’a ningende ase enyomba y’Omonene?”
english: Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the temple of the LORD?"

ekegusii: Hezekia nigo abwate obotenenku obonge, na abanto abange nigo bamosigete. Akeagachera ebigachero ase arenge kobeka chifeta, ne chitahabu, na amagena e rigori rinene, na ebinsari, ne chinguba, na ebinto ao ao bie rigori rinene.
english: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor, and he made treasuries for his silver and gold and for his precious stones, spices, shields and all kinds of valuables.

ekegusii: Hezekia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, akaa omosangererekano chieri elifu eyemo, ne ching’ondi chikoruegwa ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa chilifu isano na ibere; na abagambi b’oboruoti bwaye bakayoa chieri elifu eyemo, ne ching’ondi chilifu ikomi. Erio abakuani abange bagechena.
english: Hezekiah king of Judah provided a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep and goats for the assembly, and the officials provided them with a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep and goats. A great number of priests consecrated themselves.

ekegusii: Hezekia akabaroisia buya, erio akaborokia chimonga chiaye chionsi, ne chifeta, ne chitahabu, na ebinsari, na amaguta e rigori rinene, na ebirwanero biaye bionsi, na ebinto bionsi biagachire ase chinyomba chiaye. Tatigete gento kende gionsi ase enyomba yaye, gose ase chikungo chi’oboruoti bwaye, ataborogetie.
english: Hezekiah received the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his storehouses-- the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his entire armory and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.

ekegusii: Hezekia akaegwa rirube korwa ase abanto baria batometwe, akarisoma, erio akagenda ase enyomba y’Omonene, akarirambora ase obosio bw’Omonene.
english: Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the temple of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.

ekegusii: Hezekia akabaroisia buya, erio akaboorokia ebinto bionsi biarenge ase chikungo chiaye chionsi: Chifeta, ne chitahabu, na ebinsari, na amaguta e rigori rinene, na ebirwanero biaye, na ebinto bionsi biagachire ase chinyomba chiaye. Tatigete gento kende gionsi ase enyomba yaye gose ase chimonga chi’oboruoti ataborogetie.
english: Hezekiah received the messengers and showed them all that was in his storehouses-- the silver, the gold, the spices and the fine oil-- his armory and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.

ekegusii: Hezekia akarara ase chisokoro chiaye chiararete, agatindekwa ase egetirimboko ase chimbeera chi’ororeria rwa Daudi chiarenge. Abayuda bonsi na abanto ba Yerusalemu bakaorokia amasikani ase ogokwa kwaye. Na Manase, omomura oye, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: Hezekiah rested with his fathers and was buried on the hill where the tombs of David's descendants are. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him when he died. And Manasseh his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Hezekia akarara ase chisokoro chiaye chiararete, na Manase, omwana oye omomura, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: Hezekiah rested with his fathers. And Manasseh his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Hezekia agatoma amang’ana ase Abaisraeli na ase Abayuda bonsi, naende akarika amarube ase Abaefraimu na ase Abamanase ng’a bachiche ase enyomba y’Omonene agwo Yerusalemu korenda Rituko Rinene ri’Epasaka ase Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli.
english: Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah and also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.

ekegusii: Hezekia akagokia Abalawi, akababeka chinguru ase ogokwana amang’ana ’oboremu asebare, ase engencho y’emeremo emiya bakorete ase Omonene. Abanto bakaria endagera y’omoyega oria ase engaki y’amatuko atano na abere, bakarua ebing’wanso bi’omorembe, bagaakera Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiabo, ng’a mbuya mono.
english: Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites, who showed good understanding of the service of the LORD. For the seven days they ate their assigned portion and offered fellowship offerings and praised the LORD, the God of their fathers.

ekegusii: na Hezekia akaibora Manase, na Manase akaibora Amoni, na Amoni akaibora Yosia,
english: Hezekiah the father of Manasseh, Manasseh the father of Amon, Amon the father of Josiah,

ekegusii: Hezekia akaba ogosemeria Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli. Onde tabete buna ere ase egati y’abaruoti bonsi b’Abayuda baria bamobwatetie gose baria bamotang’anerete.
english: Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, either before him or after him.

ekegusii: Hezekia akaonchora obosio bwaye gochia ase enyasi, erio agasaba Omonene, akabora,
english: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,

ekegusii: Hezekia akaonchora obosio bwaye gochia ase enyasi, agasaba Omonene,
english: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,

ekegusii: Hezekia agachaka kogamba ekero arenge nemiaka emerongo ebere, na etano, na akagamba emiaka emerongo ebere, na kianda, agwo Yerusalemu. Ng’ina nigo arenge korokwa Abiya, omosubati o Zakaria,
english: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.

ekegusii: Hesero korwa Karimeli, na Naara, mosinto bw’Esibai;
english: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,

ekegusii: Hesiro korwa Karimeli na Paarai korwa Ariba;
english: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

ekegusii: Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,
english: Hezironi akaibora Ramu, na Ramu akaibora Aminadabu;

ekegusii: Imbise korwa ase emeroberio ya bobisi y’abakori amabe, korwa ase eburu‐buru y’abakori ebibe.
english: Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked, from that noisy crowd of evildoers.

ekegusii: Onchora obosio bwao, torora ebibe biane; otinyie obobe bwane bwonsi.
english: Hide your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquity.

ekegusii: Hilen, Debir,
english: Hileni na Debiri amo namarisio aetanaineo;

ekegusii: Hilikia amo nabanto omoruoti atomete bakagenda ase Hulda, omokungu omobani moka Salumu, mosinto o Tokihati o Hasira. Salumu nere orenge omorendi bwe rigachero rie chianga agwo Hekalu. (Ase ekero ekio Hulda nigo amenyete agwo Yerusalemu ase ensemo enyia.) Abanto abwo bagatebia omokungu oria amang’ana aria aria.
english: Hilkiah and those the king had sent with him went to speak to the prophetess Huldah, who was the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second District.

ekegusii: Erio Hilikia agatebia Safani omoriki, “Nanyorire Ebuku y’Amachiko ime ase enyomba y’Omonene,” akaa Safani ebuku eria.
english: Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the temple of the LORD." He gave it to Shaphan.

ekegusii: Hilikia, omokuani omonene, agatebia Safani omoriki, “Nanyorire ebuku y’Amachiko ase enyomba y’Omonene.” Hilikia akaa Safani ebuku eria, nere akayesoma.
english: Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the temple of the LORD." He gave it to Shaphan, who read it.

ekegusii: Ase igo Hilikia omokuani, na Ahikamu, na Akibori, na Safani, na Asaia bakagenda koboria Hulda, omobani omokungu, mokaa Salumu, mosinto o Tikiwa, o Harasi. Salumu oyio nigo arenge omorendi bwe rigachero rie chianga. Ase ekero ekio Hulda nigo amenyete agwo Yerusalemu ase ensemo enyia.
english: Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Acbor, Shaphan and Asaiah went to speak to the prophetess Huldah, who was the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second District.

ekegusii: Hilikia nigo arenge oyo o kabere, na Tebalia oyo o gatato, na Zakaria oyo o kane. Aba na abamura ba Hosa amo nabamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na batato.
english: Hilkiah the second, Tabaliah the third and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and relatives of Hosah were 13 in all.

ekegusii: Ere oyorabue nimobeke abe esiiro ase Hekalu ya Nyasae one, ere tagosoka korwao nonya ng’ake, na inche nindike asare erieta ria Nyasae one, na erieta ri’omochie o Nyasae one, Yerusalemu omoyia, oyogoika korwa igoro, korwa ase Nyasae one, na erieta riane riyia.
english: Him who overcomes I will make a pillar in the temple of my God. Never again will he leave it. I will write on him the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which is coming down out of heaven from my God; and I will also write on him my new name.

ekegusii: Huramu, omoruoti o Turo, akairaneria ase rirube atomete ase Sulemani, rigoteba: “Ekiagera Omonene anchete abanto baye, okobekire aye koba omoruoti igoro asebare,”
english: Hiram king of Tyre replied by letter to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king."

ekegusii: Obeire nekeririanda ekenene asende, na ombarire ng’a nomobisa oye inde.
english: His anger burns against me; he counts me among his enemies.

ekegusii: Ekieni kiaye nigo kiarenge buna okomesa kw’embura, na eanga yaye nendabu buna amagena ’embura.
english: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow.

ekegusii: Abaruti emegwe baye bang’etananire aande onsi, ombetire chinyigo chiane, tandorereti amabera; oumoire amache ’endorwe yane igoro ase riroba.
english: his archers surround me. Without pity, he pierces my kidneys and spills my gall on the ground.

ekegusii: Amaboko aye nigo anga buna etahabu ebombire buya, echabeire amagena akomeka‐meka. Omobere oye nigo onga buna amaino e chinchogu aroisirie buya, na gochaberwa namagena e rigori rinene akorokwa safiro.
english: His arms are rods of gold set with chrysolite. His body is like polished ivory decorated with sapphires.

ekegusii: Ase ayio abasomba bagatebia omoruoti, “Hamani oteneine ase egoora.” Omoruoti akabatebia, “Motebie asoe.”
english: His attendants answered, "Haman is standing in the court." "Bring him in," the king ordered.

ekegusii: Obonene bwaye namagonko aye anga buna chinguba, achokaine chindwaro; nigo abwataine amo amo, buna ayanantirie.
english: His back has rows of shields tightly sealed together;

ekegusii: Omobere oye nigo orenge komeka‐meka buna berulo, rigena rie rigori rinene; obosio bwaye nigo bwarenge kororekana buna okomesa kw’embura, na amaiso aye nigo arenge gwoka buna ebieri bi’omorero. Amaboko na amagoro aye nigo arenge komeka‐meka buna etaai yasenigwe. Eriogi ri’amang’ana aye nigo riarenge kwoga buna eri’omoganda omonene bw’abanto.
english: His body was like chrysolite, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.

ekegusii: his body well nourished, his bones rich with marrow.
english: ebirandi biaye biichire namabeere, na amauga ’omobere oye aichire nemeseto.

ekegusii: Amauga aye nigo are amakong’u buna emebirangwa eroisirie korwa ase etaai; ee, amauga ’omobere oye nigo anga buna emeriibo y’ebioma.
english: His bones are tubes of bronze, his limbs like rods of iron.

ekegusii: Omoika bw’Omonene oye nigo onga orooche roichire goika ebigoti. Nasonge abanto b’ebisaku negesongero ki’ogosiria; ase emenwa yabo nigo arabeke ebinto ase emenwa yabo bi’okobatantania.
english: His breath is like a rushing torrent, rising up to the neck. He shakes the nations in the sieve of destruction; he places in the jaws of the peoples a bit that leads them astray.

ekegusii: Omoika bw’omonwa oye nigo ogosoka buna ekebemberi ki’omorero, na omorero nigo ogosoka korwa ase omonwa oye,
english: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames dart from his mouth.

ekegusii: Na momura omwabo nigo are korokwa Yubali; oyio nere sokoro bw’abaare kobugia amakano na ebiroria.
english: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.

ekegusii: Abamwabo bakamoboria, “Inee! Aye nigo orengereretie ng’a nigo orabe omogambi oito, otogambere?” Ase igo barabwo bakamenta komogecha mono ase engencho y’okorota kwaye, na ase engencho y’amang’ana aye.
english: His brothers said to him, "Do you intend to reign over us? Will you actually rule us?" And they hated him all the more because of his dream and what he had said.

ekegusii: Erio abamwabo bagacha, bagatung’ama inse ase obosio bwaye, bakabora, “Intwe iga nabasomba bao tore.”
english: His brothers then came and threw themselves down before him. "We are your slaves," they said.

ekegusii: Abamwabo bakamobwaterwa ribero, korende ise ere akagacha ogokwana okwo ase enkoro yaye, takweba.
english: His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.

ekegusii: erio omokungu oria omoboraka aike ang’e ase omomura oria omwabo omosacha oye, asomore egekoroto korwa ase okogoro kw’omonto oria agwo ase amasio ’abagaaka, naende amotwere amate ase obosio bwaye, akwane: Nabo arakorwe omonto onde bwensi okwanga goteneneria omomura omwabo egesaku.
english: his brother's widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, take off one of his sandals, spit in his face and say, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's family line."

ekegusii: Chinsea chiaye nigo chinga buna ebigondo bi’ebimeri bi’ebinsari, bigotioka rimisu rigiya. Ebikoba biaye nigo binga buna ebisicha ebiya, nigo bigotonyia manemane.
english: His cheeks are like beds of spice yielding perfume. His lips are like lilies dripping with myrrh.

ekegusii: Enkoro yaye nenkong’u buna rigena, ee, nenkong’u buna orogena rogosia.
english: His chest is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone.

ekegusii: Abana baye tibakonyora ogokonywa, nigo bakomionogorerwa geita, gose monto onde tari okobatooria.
english: His children are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.

ekegusii: Abana baye mbabe bagosaberera korwa ase abataka, na amaboko aye nairanie obotenenku bwaye bwonsi.
english: His children must make amends to the poor; his own hands must give back his wealth.

ekegusii: Oroiboro rwaye ndobe nokobua ase ense; ekiaare ki’abare ne chinkoro chindonge ngesesenigwe.
english: His children will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.

ekegusii: Chianga chiaye chikameka‐meka, chikaba chindabu mono, buna omoroisia bw’ense atanyare gochikora chibe chindabu.
english: His clothes became dazzling white, whiter than anyone in the world could bleach them.

ekegusii: Naboigo nabwate omokungu o sere‐sere, oyomenyete Sekemu; nere akamoiborera omwana omomura, na Gidioni akamoroka Abimeleki.
english: His concubine, who lived in Shechem, also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelech.

ekegusii: Naende omokungu oye o sere‐sere, ore korokwa Reuma, akamoiborera Teba, na Gahamu, na Tahasi, na Maaka.
english: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also had sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

ekegusii: Omwana oye omoiseke nigo arenge korokwa Seera, oria oagachete Beti‐Horoni ya rogoro na eya maate, na Useni‐Seera.
english: His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon as well as Uzzen Sheerah.

ekegusii: Bono moga Finehasi, omomura o Eli, nigo arenge morito; engaki yaye y’okogonkia konya yabereire ang’e. Ekero aigwete amang’ana ng’a ise biara amo nomosacha oye bakure, obororo bw’okobina bokamochera, agatung’ama inse, akagonkia.
english: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near the time of delivery. When she heard the news that the ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went into labor and gave birth, but was overcome by her labor pains.

ekegusii: Abana ba Isumaeli nigo bamenyete bagachakera Havila, bagaika Suri moocha ya Misiri, ase enchera ekogenda Asuri; bakamenya bosio bw’abamwabo bonsi.
english: His descendants settled in the area from Havilah to Shur, near the border of Egypt, as you go toward Asshur. And they lived in hostility toward all their brothers.

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakamoiraneria, “Naki omonto aranyare koigotia abanto aba, na aiga nerooro?”
english: His disciples answered, "But where in this remote place can anyone get enough bread to feed them?"

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakamotebia, “Aa nerooro, ng’ai toranyore emegati emenge eraisane abanto abange buna aba baigote?”
english: His disciples answered, "Where could we get enough bread in this remote place to feed such a crowd?"

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakamoboria, “Omoreng’anio oyio ninki ogoteba?”
english: His disciples asked him what this parable meant.

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakamoboria, “Rabii, ning’o okorete ebibe, nomonto oyo, gose nabaibori baye, goika akaiborwa ore omouko?”
english: His disciples asked him, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?"

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakainyora ng’a nerikire, “Risemi ri’enyomba yao riandire.”
english: His disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for your house will consume me."

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakamotebia, “Omonene, onye orarire, nagwene.”
english: His disciples replied, "Lord, if he sleeps, he will get better."

ekegusii: Aborokigwa baye bakarigererania, bagasinywa komanya gose ning’o atora.
english: His disciples stared at one another, at a loss to know which of them he meant.

ekegusii: Okobua kw’obonyasae bwaye gwatoeire ebinto bionsi ebire nobogima na ebie chingencho chi’obonyasae ase okomomanya ere oyotorangeretie ase obonene bwaye obonyene, na okobua kwaye.
english: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through our knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and goodness.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etato na ibere, na amagana abere (32,200).
english: His division numbers 32,200.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etato na isano, na amagana ane (35,400).
english: His division numbers 35,400.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo ene, na amagana atano (40,500).
english: His division numbers 40,500.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo ene na eyemo, na amagana atano (41,500).
english: His division numbers 41,500.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo ene na isano, na amagana atano na rimo, na emerongo etano (45,650).
english: His division numbers 45,650.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo ene na isano nemo, na amagana atano (46,500).
english: His division numbers 46,500.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano na isato, na amagana ane (53,400).
english: His division numbers 53,400.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano na inye, na amagana ane (54,400).
english: His division numbers 54,400.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano na isano na ibere, na amagana ane (57,400).
english: His division numbers 57,400.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano na kianda, na amagana atato (59,300).
english: His division numbers 59,300.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano nomo na ibere, na amagana atano na abere (62,700).
english: His division numbers 62,700.

ekegusii: na omoganda oye nigo ore nabanto chilifu emerongo etano na ebere na inye, na amagana atano na rimo (74,600).
english: His division numbers 74,600.

ekegusii: Amaiso aye nigo arenge buna ekebemberi ki’omorero, na igoro ase omotwe oye nchiarengeo chigutwa chinyinge. Narenge nerieta riarikire asare ritamanyiri na onde, otatiga ere omonyene.
english: His eyes are like blazing fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has a name written on him that no one knows but he himself.

ekegusii: Amaiso aye nigo agwekaine amaruma are ase chindooche, ee, nigo anga amaruma asibigwe namabeere, naende nigo anga amagena akomeka‐meka achokire buya.
english: His eyes are like doves by the water streams, washed in milk, mounted like jewels.

ekegusii: Amaiso aye nigo arabe amabariri ase okonywa edivai, na amaino aye abe amarabu ase okonywa amabeere.
english: His eyes will be darker than wine, his teeth whiter than milk.

ekegusii: Erio agwo obosio bw’omoruoti bokaonchoka bokarachoka, na ebirengererio biaye bikamochanda; ebiimo bi’omobere oye bikororoba, na amaru aye agaakana.
english: His face turned pale and he was so frightened that his knees knocked together and his legs gave way.

ekegusii: Korende ise na ng’ina bakamoboria, “Inee! Moiseke tari, nonya noyomo, ase abanto b’egesaku giaito, gose ase eamate yaito yonsi? Nase ki okogenda konyuoma omokungu korwa ase Abafilisti abwo batarogeti?” Korende Samison akairaneria ise, “Monyorere ere oyio, ekiagera ere ongweneire.”
english: His father and mother replied, "Isn't there an acceptable woman among your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She's the right one for me."

ekegusii: Ise na ng’ina omwana oyio bamobwate, bamoire ase abagaaka b’omochie agwo ase bakogambera ebina geita ki’omochie.
english: his father and mother shall take hold of him and bring him to the elders at the gate of his town.

ekegusii: Erio Isaka ise akamoiraneria, akamotebia, “Rora, obomenyo bwao inabobe aare korwa ase obonoru bwe riroba, na aare korwa ase riime rikorwa igoro.
english: His father Isaac answered him, "Your dwelling will be away from the earth's richness, away from the dew of heaven above.

ekegusii: Isaka ise akamoboria, “Naye ng’o?” Ere akamoiraneria, “Ninche Esau omwana oo omotangi.”
english: His father Isaac asked him, "Who are you?" "I am your son," he answered, "your firstborn, Esau."

ekegusii: Ekaba ng’a ise Publio narenge omonyareku ase esosera na gosaa amanyinga. Paulo agasoa asare akamosabera, akabeka amaboko aye igoro yaye, akamogwenia.
english: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.

ekegusii: Zakaria ise agaichorwa n’Omoika Omochenu, akabana, okobora,
english: His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied:

ekegusii: Ise biara akamoboria abeere aroro; erio akaba amo nere amatuko atato, bakaria na konywa, bakarara aroro.
english: His father-in-law, the girl's father, prevailed upon him to stay; so he remained with him three days, eating and drinking, and sleeping there.

ekegusii: Amagoro aye nabwatwe noboreba, abe ogotaara ase egati ye chiirima.
english: His feet thrust him into a net and he wanders into its mesh.

ekegusii: Na amagoro aye nigo arenge buna etaai esenirie koyasibigwe ase eriko ri’omorero, na eriogi riaye buna eriogi ri’amache amange akoeera.
english: His feet were like bronze glowing in a furnace, and his voice was like the sound of rushing waters.

ekegusii: Chinyama chi’omobere oye nigo chikoera, tichikororekana, na amauga aye atongorora.
english: His flesh wastes away to nothing, and his bones, once hidden, now stick out.

ekegusii: Omogisangio bw’omonto oria akairaneria, “Oyio nomoro o Gidioni, oria Omoisraeli, mosinto o Yoashi. Tigekonyara koba gento kende ekeao. Nyasae otobekire intwe Abamidiani, amo nemeganda yaito yonsi y’abarwani, ase amaboko aye.”
english: His friend responded, "This can be nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given the Midianites and the whole camp into his hands."

ekegusii: Nyasae oye nigo akomworokereria enchera engiya y’ogokora emeremo eyio.
english: His God instructs him and teaches him the right way.

ekegusii: Omotwe oye na etukia yaye nigo biarenge ebirabu se buna amarionya amarabu, ebirabu se buna amagena ’embura; na amaiso aye nigo arenge buna ekebemberi ki’omorero.
english: His head and hair were white like wool, as white as snow, and his eyes were like blazing fire.

ekegusii: Omotwe oye nigo ore omuya onga etahabu echenire, etukia yaye nigo ere omosamugoku bw’obwari; nigo ere emwamu ti buna amarionya ’ekegonkoru.
english: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.

ekegusii: Omotwe oye okarentwa ase esani, okaegwa omoiseke oria, na ere akayoira ase ng’ina.
english: His head was brought in on a platter and given to the girl, who carried it to her mother.

ekegusii: Enkoro yaye teri koirianyeka gose kwoboa, ere nigo akoremereria goika abamochandi babugwe.
english: His heart is secure, he will have no fear; in the end he will look in triumph on his foes.

ekegusii: Akaba omoremu ase chinchera chi’Omonene, agasaria aase aimokererete igoro agosasimerwa, na akarusia emete y’Asera, enyasae eria enkungu, korwa ase Abayuda.
english: His heart was devoted to the ways of the LORD; furthermore, he removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.

ekegusii: Korende nyuma y’ayio agakorera Dina, omoiseke oyio o Yakobo, buya, akamwancha na gokwana nere amang’ana amaya.
english: His heart was drawn to Dinah daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.

ekegusii: Chibarasi chi’omoruoti oyio nigo chire chinyinge mono, nachiimokie ebuse enyinge egotube kegima. Ekero arabe ogosoa ase ebiita biao buna abanto bagosoa ase omochie otagoirwe, chindwaki chiao nigo chiratengeche ase okwoga kw’abariini chibarasi ne chigari ao ao.
english: His horses will be so many that they will cover you with dust. Your walls will tremble at the noise of the war horses, wagons and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city whose walls have been broken through.

ekegusii: erinde bono, ase enchera y’ekanisa, obong’aini bwa Nyasae, obore ne chingencho chinyinge, bomanyekane nabagambi na abare nokobua kwa igoro.
english: His intent was that now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God should be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms,

ekegusii: Okoboko kwaye kwa bomosi nigo kore inse y’omotwe one, na okwa borio komboanetie.
english: His left arm is under my head and his right arm embraces me.

ekegusii: Okoboko kwaye kwa bomosi nigo kore inse y’omotwe one, na okwa borio nigo komboanetie.
english: His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

ekegusii: Amagoro aye nigo anga chisiiro chi’amagena amarabu se akomeka‐meka, abekire ase chinterekerero chie chitaabu chingiya. Okororekana kwaye nigo konga buna okwa Lebanoni, ekieni kiaye nigo kere ekiya buna eki’emecharake,
english: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as its cedars.

ekegusii: Okomesa kwaye gwe chinkoba nigo gokomoreka ense eye; ense nigo ekorora okomesa okwo yatengechigwa.
english: His lightning lights up the world; the earth sees and trembles.

ekegusii: Naisa gotuba okogecha kwaye nobong’ainereria, obokayayu bwaye goika bomanyekane nomosangererekano bwonsi.
english: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

ekegusii: Omonene bw’omosomba oria akabora, “Titokogobera kogenda korara ase omochie bw’abanto batari Abaisraeli, korende tobaetanie togende Gibea.”
english: His master replied, "No. We won't go into an alien city, whose people are not Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah."

ekegusii: Amabera aye nigo are ase abwo bamoirogete korwa ebigori goika ebigori.
english: His mercy extends to those who fear him, from generation to generation.

ekegusii: Ng’ina akamotebia, “Okoragererigwa kwao tiga kobe igoro yane; igwa aya nkogotebia rioka, genda ondetere chimanwa echio chie chimbori.”
english: His mother said to him, "My son, let the curse fall on me. Just do what I say; go and get them for me."

ekegusii: His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
english: Ng’ina agatebia abasomba, “Rinde rionsi arabatebie, morikore.”

ekegusii: Aya agokwana nigo aichire okoragereria, na obong’ainereria, na ogokorera abande bobe; oromeme rwaye nigo robwate amang’ana ’obobe na ogosaria.
english: His mouth is full of curses and lies and threats; trouble and evil are under his tongue.

ekegusii: Chinkwana chiaye nigo chire chinyansu mono, chingencho chiaye chionsi nigo chire echi’ogosanerwa mono. Inwe abakungu ba Yerusalemu, naboigo omwanchi one are, oyio ore omosani one.
english: His mouth is sweetness itself; he is altogether lovely. This is my lover, this my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Omonto oyio noyo bw’ororeria rwa Kalebu, nigo arenge korokwa Nabali, na mokaye Abigaeli. Omokungu oyio nigo arenge omong’aini mono na omonyakieni, korende omosacha oria nigo arenge omonto omotindi na omonyandamwamu.
english: His name was Nabal and his wife's name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was surly and mean in his dealings.

ekegusii: His neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging asked, "Isn't this the same man who used to sit and beg?"
english: Nabo abagisangio baye, na baria bamoroche ekero arenge omosabereri bakabora, “Inee! Oyo tari ere oria orenge oikaransete gosaba?”

ekegusii: Ere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obuya bwochoganirie namaguta, bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo, na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta, bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo, na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Abagambi abarenge amo nomoruoti bagancha koa abanto, na abakuani, na Abalawi, ching’iti chi’ebing’wanso. Hilikia na Zakaria, na Yehieli, abateneneri b’enyomba ya Nyasae, bakaa abakuani chimanwa chie ching’ondi chilifu ibere, na amagana atano na rimo (2,600), ne chiombe amagana atato (300), chibe ebing’wanso bi’Epasaka.
english: His officials also contributed voluntarily to the people and the priests and Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the administrators of God's temple, gave the priests twenty-six hundred Passover offerings and three hundred cattle.

ekegusii: Abasomba baye bagakora omoroberio bw’okomoita, bakamoitera ime ase enyomba yaye agwo Milo, agwo ase enchera ekogenda Sila.
english: His officials conspired against him and assassinated him at Beth Millo, on the road down to Silla.

ekegusii: Abasomba baye bakamotebia, “Bono twaigure ng’a abaruoti b’enyomba y’Abaisraeli nigo bare namabera, tiga tweboyie chianga chie chigunia, na tonaarie chingori ase amagoti aito, erio tosoke, togende ase omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli; ande nabo arabaise gototiga tobe moyo.”
english: His officials said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Let us go to the king of Israel with sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads. Perhaps he will spare your life."

ekegusii: Abaibori baye nigo bakwanete aya ase okoiroka Abayahudi, ekiagera Abayahudi konya babwatanire, ng’a monto onde bwensi oramoorokie ng’a nere Kristo aserigwe korwa ase esinagogi.
english: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews, for already the Jews had decided that anyone who acknowledged that Jesus was the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.

ekegusii: Omonene tagokiri ne chinguru chie chibarasi, gose ase omoayerero bw’omonto,
english: His pleasure is not in the strength of the horse, nor his delight in the legs of a man;

ekegusii: Amang’ana ’ogosaba kwaye, na buna Nyasae anchete ogosaba okwo kw’ogosorora, na igoro y’ebibe biaye bionsi, na ogotegenwa kwaye, na aase onsi aagachete aase aimokererete igoro agosasimerwa, na buna atenenetie emete y’Asera, na emegwekano, ritang’ani konya atarekeyia omonyene, amang’ana aya onsi nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’Abarori.
english: His prayer and how God was moved by his entreaty, as well as all his sins and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself-- all are written in the records of the seers.

ekegusii: Abanto bamwabo korwa ase Eliezeri nigo barenge Rehabia, omomura oye, na Yesaia omomura oye, na Yoramu omomura oye, na Sikiri omomura oye, na Selomiti omomura oye.
english: His relatives through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zicri his son and Shelomith his son.

ekegusii: Emeri yaye iyome inse ye riroba, ne chinsagia chiaye nachisusane.
english: His roots dry up below and his branches wither above.

ekegusii: Oyo o kabere Kileabu, omwana bw’Abigaeli, oyotigetwe omoboraka, orenge moka Nabali o Karimeli; na oyo o gatato Abisalomu o Maaka, mosubati o Talimai, omoruoti o Gesuri.
english: his second, Kileab the son of Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

ekegusii: Abasomba baye bakamotebia, “Ing’ana ki eri gwakora? Ekero omwana arenge moyo okeng’ata na korera korende bono omwana gakure, kwaimokire kwarageire.”
english: His servants asked him, "Why are you acting this way? While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but now that the child is dead, you get up and eat!"

ekegusii: Abasomba baye bakamobogoria ase egari, bakamoira Yerusalemu, bakamotindeka ase embeera yaye ase chisokoro chiaye chiatindegetwe, agwo ase Omochie o Daudi.
english: His servants took him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him with his fathers in his tomb in the City of David.

ekegusii: Ekero abasomba ba Daudi baigete ase Abigaeli agwo Karimeli, bakamotebia, “Daudi nigo atotomire asore, erinde tokoire obe mokaye.”
english: His servants went to Carmel and said to Abigail, "David has sent us to you to take you to become his wife."

ekegusii: His sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.
english: Hamoleketi omosubati omwabo Gileadi, akaibora Isi‐Hodi na Abieseri, na Mahala.

ekegusii: His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
english: Omoiseke omwabo omwana oria agatenena aare ake amanye egekonyora omwana.

ekegusii: Ekero egwasimora, chinsase nigo chigosoka chiamoreka, amaiso aye nigo anga buna amasase agosakia mambia.
english: His snorting throws out flashes of light; his eyes are like the rays of dawn.

ekegusii: Korende omwana oria bw’omokungu omosomba akaiborwa buna monto onde bwensi; na oria bw’omokungu omonyuome, oyotarenge omosomba, akaiborwa ase eira.
english: His son by the slave woman was born in the ordinary way; but his son by the free woman was born as the result of a promise.

ekegusii: Semaya, omomura oye, akaiborerwa abana abamura bakaba abateneneri be chiamate chiabo; abwo nigo barenge abanto abakong’u ase emeremo yabo.
english: His son Shemaiah also had sons, who were leaders in their father's family because they were very capable men.

ekegusii: na abamura baye bakamorentera amanyinga ekeng’wanso ekio, ere agatobeka ekiara kiaye ase amanyinga aria, erio akayagindia ase emegwekano ye chingunchara ere ase chikoona chi’egesasimero, na amanyinga atigarete akayaumora ase egesasimero inse.
english: His sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and put it on the horns of the altar; the rest of the blood he poured out at the base of the altar.

ekegusii: Isaka na Isumaeli bakamotindeka ase rikuruma agwo Makipela ase oboremo bwa Efuroni, omwana o Sohari, Omohiti, moocha ya Mamure,
english: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite,

ekegusii: Abamura b’Ayubu nigo banarete gokora emeyega ase chibisi, kera oyomo ase rituko riaye. Nigo barenge korangeria abaiseke bamwabo baria batato bacha koragera na konywa amo nabarabwo.
english: His sons used to take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

ekegusii: “Abamura b’omoruoti o sugusu mbebeke ang’e, basangererie abarwani esegi abange mono, oyomo agende aumokere ense eria nomoganda oye omonene oresiarere aande onsi, naende bairane eria kabere barwane gochia bosio bw’eburi yaye.
english: His sons will prepare for war and assemble a great army, which will sweep on like an irresistible flood and carry the battle as far as his fortress.

ekegusii: Ere omonyene nigo agosuka gochia ang’e noboina, na obogima bwaye gochia ase abagosiria obogima.”
english: His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the messengers of death.

ekegusii: Orotanga rwe ritimo riaye nigo rware buna omwaro omonene na oborito bw’ensonga ye ritimo riaye nigo bwarenge koreng’ana chikiro isano na ibere. Omonto ore komobogoreria enguba nigo arenge komotang’ana.
english: His spear shaft was like a weaver's rod, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. His shield bearer went ahead of him.

ekegusii: Chinkwana chiaye nigo chiarenge chinyororo kobua amaguta atundire, korende ebirengererio biaye nebi’esegi; amang’ana aye nigo arenge amororo kobua amaguta, nonya naboigo nigo akonachanacha buna emioro.
english: His speech is smooth as butter, yet war is in his heart; his words are more soothing than oil, yet they are drawn swords.

ekegusii: Bagancha amang’ana aye, na ekero barangeretie abatomwa, bakabaaka, bakabachika tibakwana ase erieta ria Yeso. Erio bakabatiga bagende.
english: His speech persuaded them. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

ekegusii: Okobara kwaye nigo konga buna okw’erioba, gokomoreka korwa ase okoboko kwaye, aroro agwo obobui bwaye nao bobisire.
english: His splendor was like the sunrise; rays flashed from his hand, where his power was hidden.

ekegusii: Ekemincha kiaye nigo kere egekong’u pa buna omocharake, na emeki y’amariagati aye nigo esisekaine amo.
english: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are close-knit.

ekegusii: Ekemincha kiaye kegakurura ensemo ya gatato ye ching’enang’eni chia igoro na gochiyeria ase ense. Na enchoka eria egatenena ase obosio bw’omokungu oria orenge ang’e koibora, erinde ekero aiboire erie omwana oye.
english: His tail swept a third of the stars out of the sky and flung them to the earth. The dragon stood in front of the woman who was about to give birth, so that he might devour her child the moment it was born.

ekegusii: Obomenyo bwaye Obochenu nigo bore agwo Salemu, ere nigo amenyete agwo Sayoni.
english: His tent is in Salem, his dwelling place in Zion.

ekegusii: Ekerundo gi’okomesa nigo gekoraria igoro ya Nyasae, nonya ne ching’iti nigo chikomanya ng’a ekerundo ngocha kere.”
english: His thunder announces the coming storm; even the cattle make known its approach.

ekegusii: Ebiombe bi’abarwani baye b’esegi nigo bigocha bire amo, biabekire eburi ase ngoetera; biatoorire biang’etananire ase chinsemo chionsi chi’obomenyo bwane.
english: His troops advance in force; they build a siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

ekegusii: Ase enda yaye nigo ebwate ebigionkorio ebioge; nigo egotiga ebimanyerererio buna ebi’egari y’okoorera egokurura ase etintira.
english: His undersides are jagged potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

ekegusii: Nigo akoramama buna endo kobaboera, erio obwata namaboko aye omonto otari na gokonywa konde.
english: His victims are crushed, they collapse; they fall under his strength.

ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo akogenderera gokina ase chinchera chiaye. Ebina biao okonacha nigo bire igoro mono, takobimanya; nigo agochaya ababisa baye bonsi.
english: His ways are always prosperous; he is haughty and your laws are far from him; he sneers at all his enemies.

ekegusii: Korende Yesebeli mokaye agacha asare, akamoboria, “Nase ki enkoro yao ere nomoichano goika nonya nendagera otari koria?”
english: His wife Jezebel came in and asked him, "Why are you so sullen? Why won't you eat?"

ekegusii: Erio mokaye akamoboria, “Inee, nonya ngoika bono nigo ogendererete koba omwegenwa ase Omonene? Ragereria Nyasae, erio okwe!”
english: His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"

ekegusii: na omokungu bw’omonto oria akaimokia egekuneko, akayekuneka, akanekera endagera yaye igoro aroro; gose omonto onde tamanyete amang’ana ayio.
english: His wife took a covering and spread it out over the opening of the well and scattered grain over it. No one knew anything about it.

ekegusii: Erio Seresi mokaye, na abasani baye bonsi bakamotebia, “Tiga orobambo rore nobotambe bw’amaboko emerongo etano rosimisigwe. Ankio mambia oborie omoruoti ng’a Moredekai atongwe igoro ase orobambo orwo, erinde ogende ase omoyega kore nomogoko.” Ring’ana erio rikagokia Hamani; ere agasimisia orobambo orwo.
english: His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built, seventy-five feet high, and ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the dinner and be happy." This suggestion delighted Haman, and he had the gallows built.

ekegusii: Moga Saulo nigo arenge korokwa Ahinoamu omosubati bw’Ahimasi. Omochiki bw’abarwani b’esegi nigo arenge korokwa Abineri, mosinto o Neri, oyorenge ise moke Saulo.
english: His wife's name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of Saul's army was Abner son of Ner, and Ner was Saul's uncle.

ekegusii: Oroteru rwaye nigo rore koboko kwaye, ere naabuse ekeooreri kiaye, nasangererie engano ase ekiage kiaye, korende omoiriro nayosambe ase omorero otakorimeka.”
english: His winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."

ekegusii: Oroteru rwaye nigo rore koboko kwaye, ere naabuse ekeooreri kiaye, nasangererie engano ase ekiage kiaye, korende omoiriro nayosambe ase omorero otakorimeka.”
english: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor, gathering his wheat into the barn and burning up the chaff with unquenchable fire."

ekegusii: Omonene nigo are nobong’aini ase enkoro yaye, na omonyene chinguru, monto ki oratoorigwe onye takomoigwera?
english: His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed?

ekegusii: emeremo ya kera omonto ing’eorokigwe maiso marore. Naki Rituko erio inariyeorokie, ekiagera narioroke nomorero; na omorero oyio noteeme emeremo ya kera omonto ng’a naki ere.
english: his work will be shown for what it is, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will test the quality of each man's work.

ekegusii: Amage aye nigo akonywa amanyinga, na aase emebere ekwete ere, nao ekeongo kere.”
english: His young ones feast on blood, and where the slain are, there is he."

ekegusii: Ebisebo biabo mbirande, na obwari bwabo nabobe buna obw’emezeituni, ne rimisu riabo ndiesiarere buna eri’emete ya Lebanoni.
english: his young shoots will grow. His splendor will be like an olive tree, his fragrance like a cedar of Lebanon.

ekegusii: na Abahiti, na Abaperisi, na Abarefai,
english: Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,

ekegusii: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,
english: na Abahivi, na Abaarikiti, na Abasini,

ekegusii: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,
english: Abahivi na Abaariki, na Abasini;

ekegusii: Hodiah, Bani and Beninu.
english: Hodia, na Bani, na Beninu.

ekegusii: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
english: Hodia, na Hasumu, na Besai;

ekegusii: “Chinyimbo echio orabe kwarikire ochibwate ase okoboko kwao agwo ase amaiso ’abanto.
english: Hold before their eyes the sticks you have written on

ekegusii: Bwata amorokererio bokong’u, toyatiga arue asore; yarende, ekiagera naro obogima bwao.
english: Hold on to instruction, do not let it go; guard it well, for it is your life.

ekegusii: Mobasike mono ase obwanchani, ase engencho y ’emeremo yabo. Mobe nomorembe inwe ase inwe.
english: Hold them in the highest regard in love because of their work. Live in peace with each other.

ekegusii: Obe nokwegena na enkoro etari gokogambia, ebio abande babisereirie are, na ase amang’ana ’okwegena basirire.
english: holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have rejected these and so have shipwrecked their faith.

ekegusii: Holon, Debir,
english: na Holoni, na Debiri,

ekegusii: Ekerengero ki’oborito gi’ekeene nigo gekorwa ase Omonene, na ebirengero bionsi bire ase chisaro nigo bire ogokora kwaye.
english: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are of his making.

ekegusii: na obooke, na amaguta, ne ching’ondi, na amabomba ’amabeere e chiombe abwatanirie bibe endagera ase Daudi amo nabanto barenge komo. Abwo babirentete nigo batebete, “Abanto aba enchara yabanyarire, naende barang’ire na barosire aiga ase erooro.”
english: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from cows' milk for David and his people to eat. For they said, "The people have become hungry and tired and thirsty in the desert."

ekegusii: Osike Omonene ne chinibo chiao chionsi na ogotongora kwao gwonsi kw’endagera.
english: Honor the LORD with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops;

ekegusii: sika iso na nyoko; naende: Ancha omogisangio oo buna bweanchete.”
english: honor your father and mother,' and 'love your neighbor as yourself.'"

ekegusii: Egesemeirie kogiatebanire nigo gekogera enkoro yarwara, korende ogosemeria kogwaikeranigwe nigo kore omote bw’obogima.
english: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.

ekegusii: Agwo kare Abahori boigo mbamenyete Seiri, korende abanto b’ororeria rw’Esau bakabaseria na kobaita, bakamenya ase ense eria ribaga riabo. Bagakora buna Abaisraeli bakorete ase ense eria Omonene abaete ebe eyabo.”
english: Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed the Horites from before them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them as their possession.)

ekegusii: Abana abamura ba Hosa b’ororeria rwa Merari nabwo aba: Simuri, omoteneneri obo, nonya tarenge omotangi, ise akamobeka akaba omoteneneri.
english: Hosah the Merarite had sons: Shimri the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him the first),

ekegusii: Abanto babwatetie ekeombe ekio nabwo aba: Hosaya, na ekeng’ese ki’abanene b’Abayuda,
english: Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed them,

ekegusii: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
english: Hosea, na Hanania, na Hasubu;

ekegusii: Chinyomba ne chinibo nigo chire omwando abana bakonyora korwa ase abaise korende omokungu omong’aini nigo are ekeegwa korwa ase Omonene.
english: Houses and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.

ekegusii: Chinyomba nigo chirabe chiichire nebinto ebiya, ebio inwe motabegeteo, ne chinsoko chi’amache echio motakunyete, na emegondo y’emesabibu na ey’emezeituni, eyio motasimegete.
english: houses filled with all kinds of good things you did not provide, wells you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves you did not plant-- then when you eat and are satisfied,

ekegusii: Ee, naki obuya bwaye na obosiani bwaye bore bw’ogokumia! Endagera yaye nenorie abamura baye bagirigente, na edivai yaye enyia nenorie abaiseke baye bagirigente.
english: How attractive and beautiful they will be! Grain will make the young men thrive, and new wine the young women.

ekegusii: Omonene ore Igoro Mono nigo are oyo bw’okoirokia, ere nomoruoti omonene bw’ense yonsi.
english: How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!

ekegusii: Obee! Naki rituko riria rire rinene! Rinde tiriri ringa buna rirorio. Eyio nengaki y’emechando y’abanto ba Yakobo, korende nonya naboigo mbatoorigwe korwa ase emechando eyio.”
english: How awful that day will be! None will be like it. It will be a time of trouble for Jacob, but he will be saved out of it.

ekegusii: Naki amagoro abo are amaseera, abwo bakorenta amang’ana amaya, bagoeta igoro ase ebitunwa, abwo bakoraria omorembe, na barenta obotomwa obore namang’ana amaya. Nigo bakoraria ogotooreka, batebia Sayoni: “Nyasae oo nere okogamba.”
english: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, "Your God reigns!"

ekegusii: Naki aye ore omoseera naende oyo bw’okogokia mono! Aye omwanchi bw’okogokia!
english: How beautiful you are and how pleasing, O love, with your delights!

ekegusii: Naama! Aye omwanchi one, naki ore omoseera mono! Ee, nabo ore omoseera mono. Ekieni ki’amaiso ao nigo kenga eki’amaruma.
english: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes are doves.

ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, naki ore omoseera! Naama! Nigo ore omoseera! Korwa ime y’egietubo kiao ekieni ki’amaiso ao nigo kenga eki’amaruma; etukia yao nigo enga buna riicho rie chimbori, nigo chigotirimboka ase ebitirimboko bia Gileadi.
english: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes behind your veil are doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead.

ekegusii: Aye omoiseke bw’omogambi, naki ebisanyi bi’amagoro ao bire ebiya ase ebikoroto ime! Naki amariagati ao amerete buya, are buna emeremo y’omoroisia omong’aini.
english: How beautiful your sandaled feet, O prince's daughter! Your graceful legs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman's hands.

ekegusii: Imosesenirie inwe aba mogosimeka chimbusuro mbarabare ase amache onsi, mogotiga chiombe ne chitigere chiagenda aande onsi.
english: how blessed you will be, sowing your seed by every stream, and letting your cattle and donkeys range free.

ekegusii: Naki enturago eria yaagete ense engima yaakirwe na gwateka! Naki Babeli osirigwe, na abanto baichanigwe ase okoyorora igo!
english: How broken and shattered is the hammer of the whole earth! How desolate is Babylon among the nations!

ekegusii: Naki omonto omosae arakore arende orogendo rwaye robe orochenu? Nase okoigwera ring’ana riao.
english: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.

ekegusii: Naki ndakore ndagererie oyo Nyasae ataragerereti? Naki ndakore ngambie oyo Omonene atagambeti?
english: How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?

ekegusii: Naki ndakore ing’irane ase tata, omosae oyo atari amo nainche? Tinkoremereria korora emechando enga buna eyio ekomonyora tata.”
english: How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? No! Do not let me see the misery that would come upon my father."

ekegusii: Ngento ki ndarue ing’iranerie Omonene ase engencho y’amaya aya ankoreire?
english: How can I repay the LORD for all his goodness to me?

ekegusii: Naki inche omosomba oo ndanyare gokwana naye, Omonene one? Chinguru chionsi chiarure asende, na tindi nomoika ime yane.”
english: How can I, your servant, talk with you, my lord? My strength is gone and I can hardly breathe."

ekegusii: Naki torakore totere ogotera kw’Omonene ase ense engeni?
english: How can we sing the songs of the LORD while in a foreign land?

ekegusii: Nase nchera ki toranyare koiraneria Nyasae ng’a mbuya mono ase engencho yaino, ase omogoko bwonsi oyotokoigwa ase engencho yaino ase obosio bwa Nyasae oito?
english: How can we thank God enough for you in return for all the joy we have in the presence of our God because of you?

ekegusii: Naki moranyare kwegena, inwe abamokoenana obonene inwe ase inwe, na obonene boria bokorwa ase Nyasae ore bweka, timori koborigia?
english: How can you believe if you accept praise from one another, yet make no effort to obtain the praise that comes from the only God?

ekegusii: Naki oranyare kobua omoteneneri oyomo ore omoke ase egati y’abasomba b’omonene one, ekero osemeretie ense ya Misiri ase okonyora korwa aroro chigari na abariini chibarasi?
english: How can you repulse one officer of the least of my master's officials, even though you are depending on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

ekegusii: Gose naki oratebie oyomino: Oyominto, ntige nkorusie ekeogoto kere ase eriso riao ime, na aye omonyene torochi omoribo ore ase eriso riao? Aye omong’ainereria, rusia ritang’ani omoribo ore ase eriso riao, nario orarore buya omanye korusia ekeogoto kere ase eriso ri’oyomino.
english: How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.

ekegusii: Gose naki oratebie oyomino: Ntige nkorusie ekeogoto kere ase eriso riao, na rora omoribo nore ase eriso riao?
english: How can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when all the time there is a plank in your own eye?

ekegusii: Naki omonto oyomo arakore aserie abanto elifu eyemo, na abanto babere baserie abanto chilifu ikomi, onye oria ore egetare kiabo atabaoonetie na kobarua, naende onye Omonene tabatigete?
english: How could one man chase a thousand, or two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?

ekegusii: Aye moiseke ominto, omoriakari one, obwanchani bwao naki bore obuya mono! Naki bore obuya mono kobua edivai! Ne rimisu ri’amaguta ao ogweaka nigo ribuete ebinsari bionsi!
english: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much more pleasing is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than any spice!

ekegusii: Naki omochie oyo otigaire bosa, oyio orenge oichire nabanto! Naki otigaire buna omoboraka, oyio orenge omonene ase egati y’ebisaku! Oyio orenge buna eting’ana ase egati y’emechie, bono obeire omosomba.
english: How deserted lies the city, once so full of people! How like a widow is she, who once was great among the nations! She who was queen among the provinces has now become a slave.

ekegusii: Aye omokungu, ng’ai oramanyere gose notoorie omosacha oo? Gose aye omosacha, ng’ai oramanyere gose notoorie omokungu oo?
english: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or, how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

ekegusii: Korende nabe aakong’u ase abare barito na abakogonkia ase amatuko aria.
english: How dreadful it will be in those days for pregnant women and nursing mothers!

ekegusii: Nabe aakong’u ase abare barito na barabwo abakogonkia ase amatuko aria.
english: How dreadful it will be in those days for pregnant women and nursing mothers!

ekegusii: Nabe aakong’u ase abare barito na abakogonkia ase amatuko aria, ekiagera nebe emechando emenene igoro ase ense, na endamwamu ase egesaku eke.
english: How dreadful it will be in those days for pregnant women and nursing mothers! There will be great distress in the land and wrath against this people.

ekegusii: How foolish! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
english: Omoriri oyo, eke ogosimeka aye, tikeri komera getakweti.

ekegusii: igoro ya Yeso o Nazareti, buna Nyasae amoete Omoika Omochenu ne chinguru, na buna ataarete na gokora emeremo emiya, na kogwenia bonsi abaregetwe na Saitani, ekiagera Nyasae nigo arenge amo nere.
english: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and how he went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with him.

ekegusii: “Naki ebimanyererio biaye bire ebinene, na amakumia aye are nokobua okonene! Oboruoti bwaye nigo bore obwa kare na kare, na obogambi bwaye nigo bogendererete ekiaare ase ekiaare.
english: How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; his dominion endures from generation to generation.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, emeremo yao nigo ere emenene mono, na ebirengererio biao nigo bire ebia ime mono.
english: How great are your works, O LORD, how profound your thoughts!

ekegusii: Rora, Nyasae nigo are omonene mono, na intwe titomomanyeti; omobaro bw’emiaka yaye tomanyekaneti.”
english: How great is God-- beyond our understanding! The number of his years is past finding out.

ekegusii: Rora, nobwanchani bore naki, obwo Tata atoeire, ng’a torokwe abana ba Nyasae, na naboigo tore! Naki ekegerete ense etatomanyeti neke, ng’a temomanyeti ere.
english: How great is the love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.

ekegusii: Naki obuya bwao bore obonge na obw’ogokumigwa, obwo kwagacheire abanto abakoirogete, ase amasio a mwanyabanto nigo okoboorokia ase abakogotamera.
english: How great is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you, which you bestow in the sight of men on those who take refuge in you.

ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, nigo ore omoseera. Ee, aye nigo ore oyo bw’okogokia, oborere bwaito togotimokera nigo bonga obonyansi obwororo.
english: How handsome you are, my lover! Oh, how charming! And our bed is verdant.

ekegusii: Abanto bao na abasomba bao aba bagotenena botambe ase obosio bwao na obong’aini bwao, mbare negesio ekenene.
english: How happy your men must be! How happy your officials, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!

ekegusii: Abanto bao, na abasomba bao, abagotenena botambe ase obosio bwao, na koigwa obong’aini bwao, mbare negesio ekenene.
english: How happy your men must be! How happy your officials, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!

ekegusii: Rora, inche nigo nganetie koigwera amachiko ao; ing’a obogima oboyia goetera ase oboronge bwao.
english: How I long for your precepts! Preserve my life in your righteousness.

ekegusii: Ee, anga nancha koba amo nainwe bono, na koonchora eriogi riane, ekiagera timanyeti inki ngokora asemore.
english: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you!

ekegusii: Naki inwe motari komanya ng’a tindi gokwana igoro y’emegati? Mwerende nememera y’Abafarisai na Abasadukai.”
english: How is it you don't understand that I was not talking to you about bread? But be on your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

ekegusii: Morigererie gose riroba ndire nobotobu gose neritaka, naende gose emete nereo, gose teiyo. Mobe abaremu, morentane okwama kw’amatunda gw’ense eria.” (Engaki eria nigo yarenge ekero emesabibu konya yamire ase ogotongorwa.)
english: How is the soil? Is it fertile or poor? Are there trees on it or not? Do your best to bring back some of the fruit of the land." (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)

ekegusii: How is your beloved better than others, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than others, that you charge us so?
english: Aye ore omoseera kobua abakungu bonsi, inee, omwanchi oyio oo, naki abuete abanchi bande? Ee, omwanchi oyio oo, naki abuete abanchi bande, goika gwatosoroire iga?

ekegusii: How long must I see the battle standard and hear the sound of the trumpet?
english: Ngoika ririri ndagenderere korora ekemanyererio gi’esegi, na koigwa eriogi ri’egetureri rikobugigwa?

ekegusii: Ngoika ririri ndabe ndemereretie emechando ase omoyo one, imbe nobororo ase enkoro yane rituko ase rituko? Ngoika ririri omobisa one arabe okogokera emechando yane?
english: How long must I wrestle with my thoughts and every day have sorrow in my heart? How long will my enemy triumph over me?

ekegusii: Ngoika ririri inche omosomba oo ndagenderere koremereria? Ndiriri oranache ekina ase abanto abwo bagonchanda?
english: How long must your servant wait? When will you punish my persecutors?

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, ngoika ririri ababisa barabe bakona‐gochecheria? Inee! Ababisa aba nigo bagochia kona‐korama erieta riao kogenderera botambe?
english: How long will the enemy mock you, O God? Will the foe revile your name forever?
