ekegusii: Erieta ri’Omonene ritogigwe korwa bono goika kare na kare!
english: Let the name of the LORD be praised, both now and forevermore.

ekegusii: “Tiga abanto b’ebisaku baseegetane, bache ase Rikura ria Yehosafati. “Aroro agwo nao ndanachere abanto b’ebisaku bionsi babaetanaine ekina.
english: 'Let the nations be roused; let them advance into the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations on every side.

ekegusii: Tiga omorembe o Kristo ogambere chinkoro chiaino, noro mwarangererigwe ase omobere oyomo, na mobe abakoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono.
english: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, since as members of one body you were called to peace. And be thankful.

ekegusii: Abakuani abwo bakomokorera Omonene tiga barere ase egati y’egesona na egesasimero, bakwane iga, “Aye Omonene, rorera abanto bao amabera; totiga abanto abwo bare omwando oo bachecherigwe, bakwanwe bobe ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku. Nase ki abanto baraborie: Ng’ai Nyasae obo are”?
english: Let the priests, who minister before the LORD, weep between the temple porch and the altar. Let them say, 'Spare your people, O LORD. Do not make your inheritance an object of scorn, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?''

ekegusii: Omobani oria obwate chindoto, tiga achikwane, korende oyobwate ring’ana riane, tiga arikwane ase obwegenwa. Inee! Omoiriro, ninki oisaine ekero okoreng’anigwa nengano? Nabo inche Omonene natebire.
english: Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let the one who has my word speak it faithfully. For what has straw to do with grain?" declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo Omonene abooretie tiga bakwane igo, abwo abooririe korwa ase okoboko kw’omochandi.
english: Let the redeemed of the LORD say this-- those he redeemed from the hand of the foe,

ekegusii: Abanyene oboronge mbabe nomogoko ase Omonene na komotamera. Abwo bare ne chinkoro chindonge mbabe bagwetogia.
english: Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in him; let all the upright in heart praise him!

ekegusii: Chindooche tiga chiake chinkobi, na ebitunwa tiga bitere nomogoko amo,
english: Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains sing together for joy;

ekegusii: Tiga abegenwa bachenge ase obonene, babe bagotera nomogoko kobare ase amarere abo.
english: Let the saints rejoice in this honor and sing for joy on their beds.

ekegusii: Tiga enyancha echenge ase okoeera, amo nebinto bionsi bire ime yaye, na emegondo echenge amo nebinto bionsi bireo.
english: Let the sea resound, and all that is in it; let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them!

ekegusii: Tiga enyancha ebe ekoruma amo nebinto bionsi bire ime yaye, boigo nense na abanto bonsi bamenyeteo.
english: Let the sea resound, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.

ekegusii: Tiga abakori amabe abwo bagwe ase ebichanga biabo abanyene, korende inche ntooreke.
english: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.

ekegusii: Tiga omokori amabe atige chinchera chiaye, na oyo otari omoronge atige ebirengererio biaye. Omonto oyio tiga airane ase Omonene, nere amororere amabera, ee, ase Nyasae oito, ere namwabere kegima.
english: Let the wicked forsake his way and the evil man his thoughts. Let him turn to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he will freely pardon.

ekegusii: Ase okoigwa emereng’anio eyio omonto omong’aini nigo akong’aiinia goetania, na oyore nokomanya bwenyorera ogosemigwa okuya.
english: let the wise listen and add to their learning, and let the discerning get guidance--

ekegusii: Ring’ana ria Kristo rimenye ase obonge ime yaino, mobe mokworokererania na gotebererania ase obong’aini bwonsi, mogotera ase chizaburi, na amatera, ne chingero chi’omoika, ase ogoakera Nyasae ng’a mbuya mono ase chinkoro chiaino ime.
english: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.

ekegusii: Kiria emenwa y’abwo bagokwana amang’ana ’oborimo, abwo bagokwana amang’ana amabe igoro y’oyore omoronge, na gokwana amang’ana ’oboenenu na ay’ogochaya.
english: Let their lying lips be silenced, for with pride and contempt they speak arrogantly against the righteous.

ekegusii: Tiga chinsoko echio chibe echiao aye bweka na tari echi’abanto abaao.
english: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.

ekegusii: Abakungu abwo tiga baayerere gocha barere na kobokia amagombo asetore, erinde amariga aiteke korwa ase amaiso aito, na amaiso aito aichorwe naro.
english: Let them come quickly and wail over us till our eyes overflow with tears and water streams from our eyelids.

ekegusii: Tiga banywe, erinde beebe obotaka bwabo, na tibabaisa kona‐koinyora emechando yabo.
english: let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more.

ekegusii: Tiga babake Omonene agwo ase omosangererekano bw’abanto, bamotogie nase abagaaka bagoikaransa kogamba.
english: Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people and praise him in the council of the elders.

ekegusii: Abwo bonsi batogie Omonene na koraria obonene bwaye ase ebisinka na ase chinse chire ang’e nenyancha.
english: Let them give glory to the LORD and proclaim his praise in the islands.

ekegusii: Tiga abanto baakere Omonene ng’a mbuya mono ase engencho y’obwanchani bwaye bwa botambe na ase emeremo y’ogokumia akobakorera mwanyabanto.
english: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his unfailing love and his wonderful deeds for men,

ekegusii: Tiga baakere Omonene ng’a mbuya mono ase engencho y’obwanchani bwaye bwa botambe, na ase emeremo y’ogokumia akoreire mwanyabanto.
english: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his unfailing love and his wonderful deeds for men,

ekegusii: Tiga baakere Omonene ng’a mbuya mono ase engencho y’obwanchani bwaye bwa botambe, na ase emeremo y’ogokumia akoreire mwanyabanto.
english: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his unfailing love and his wonderful deeds for men.

ekegusii: Tiga baakere Omonene ng’a mbuya mono, ase engencho y’obwanchani bwaye bwa botambe, na ase emeremo y’ogokumia akoreire mwanyabanto.
english: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his unfailing love and his wonderful deeds for men.

ekegusii: Tiga abansoeri abwo bamanye ng’a aya nigo arure ase okoboko kwao. Aye Omonene, naye gwakorire aya.
english: Let them know that it is your hand, that you, O LORD, have done it.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo tiga bamanye ng’a naye bweka okorokwa Omonene, nigo ore Oyore Igoro Mono igoro y’ense yonsi.
english: Let them know that you, whose name is the LORD-- that you alone are the Most High over all the earth.

ekegusii: Batogie erieta riaye ase ogotenga, babe bakobugia chinchigiri na amakano.
english: Let them praise his name with dancing and make music to him with tambourine and harp.

ekegusii: Ebinto ebio bionsi tiga bitogie erieta ri’Omonene, ekiagera nere ochigete, na ebio bigatongwa,
english: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for he commanded and they were created.

ekegusii: Inwe mwensi, togia erieta ri’Omonene, ekiagera erieta riaye nario rioka rire rinene rikobakwa; obonene bwaye nigo boetanaine ense na igoro.
english: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his splendor is above the earth and the heavens.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi tiga batogie erieta riaye rinene na eri’okoirokia. Ere nigo are omochenu.
english: Let them praise your great and awesome name-- he is holy.

ekegusii: Tiga barue ebing’wanso bi’ogoaka ng’a mbuya mono, naende bararie ogokora kwaye ase ogotera nomogoko.
english: Let them sacrifice thank offerings and tell of his works with songs of joy.

ekegusii: ase obosio bw’Omonene, ekiagera ngocha are konachera ense ekina. Ere nanachere ense ekina ase oboronge, na abanto nabanachere ekina atari gwanchereria.
english: let them sing before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples with equity.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo tiga basirigwe kegima buna amache omogoko agoeta asira; ekero bakoruta emegwe yabo, eburoke.
english: Let them vanish like water that flows away; when they draw the bow, let their arrows be blunted.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio tiga arikwe agachwe ase engencho y’ekiaare kegochi‐gocha, erinde abanto abwo bataraiborwa, nabarabwo bache gotogia Omonene.
english: Let this be written for a future generation, that a people not yet created may praise the LORD:

ekegusii: Tiga Kristo, Omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, aike bono korwa ase omosalaba, tonyare korora na kwegena.” Na barabwo ababambetwe amo nere bakamorama.
english: Let this Christ, this King of Israel, come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe." Those crucified with him also heaped insults on him.

ekegusii: Tiga abanto abwo bairogete Omonene batebe, “Obwanchani bwaye nigo bogendererete goika kare na kare.”
english: Let those who fear the LORD say: "His love endures forever."

ekegusii: Inwe abamwanchete Omonene, gecha obobe! Ere nigo akorenda emioyo y’abachenu baye; nigo akobatooria korwa ase amaboko ’abakori amabe.
english: Let those who love the LORD hate evil, for he guards the lives of his faithful ones and delivers them from the hand of the wicked.

ekegusii: Intwe tiga tomomanye Omonene, ee, tiga tokore omokia tomomanye. Okooroka kwaye nigo korabe ogw’ekeene buna ogosoka kw’erioba; natochere buna embura, ee, buna embura ekwamia endagera na konyiyia riroba.
english: Let us acknowledge the LORD; let us press on to acknowledge him. As surely as the sun rises, he will appear; he will come to us like the winter rains, like the spring rains that water the earth."

ekegusii: Totaare buna egwenerete ase omobaso; tari ase okoria bobe na gotinda, tari ase obotomani aa ase obonyaka, tari ase eriomana ne ribero.
english: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in orgies and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

ekegusii: Erio torente naende Esanduku ya Nyasae oito ebeere amo naintwe, ekiagera ntwayetigete ase amatuko aria Saulo arenge kogamba.”
english: Let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we did not inquire of it during the reign of Saul."

ekegusii: Inchuo, togende ase obosio bwaye ase okomoakera ng’a mbuya mono, tomochengere namatera ay’ogotogia!
english: Let us come before him with thanksgiving and extol him with music and song.

ekegusii: Tochore ayare amaronge; intwe amo toteeme komanya ayare amaronge.
english: Let us discern for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, toike ang’e ne chinkoro chire nekeene, tobe nobomaene oboikeranu ase okwegena, ne chinkoro chiaito chianyororokerigwe oborabu, tichigotogambia, twasibigwe ase emebere yaito namache amaya.
english: let us draw near to God with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and having our bodies washed with pure water.

ekegusii: Tiga twetuke intwe abanyene na toteeme chinchera chiaito, erio tomoiranere Omonene!
english: Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the LORD.

ekegusii: na korigereria Yeso, omochaki na omoikerania bw’okwegena gwaito. Ribaga ri’omogoko oyobegetwe bosio bwaye, akaremereria omosalaba na gochaya obosooku, ere nigo aikaransete ensemo ya borio y’ekerogo ki’obonene kia Nyasae.
english: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

ekegusii: toimoke mambia chuni togende ase emegondo y’emesabibu, torore gose yachakire goseboka, naende gose amasabibu amanokire na gosicha, boigo gose amakomomanga asichire. Aroro agwo ninkoboanie nobwanchani bwane.
english: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vines have budded, if their blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates are in bloom-- there I will give you my love.

ekegusii: Tiga togende goika Yorodan, na kera oyomo ageche omote oyomo aroro, erinde toagachere enyomba aroro tokomenya.” Elisha akairaneria, “Genda!”
english: Let us go to the Jordan, where each of us can get a pole; and let us build a place there for us to live." And he said, "Go."

ekegusii: Tiga tobwate mono okoorokia kw’ogosemeria gwaito, totari konyegerigwa; ekiagera ere oyoriete eira nomwegenwa.
english: Let us hold unswervingly to the hope we profess, for he who promised is faithful.

ekegusii: Tiga torare inse tobe nobosooku, na echayo ebe asetore, ekiagera twasaririe ase Omonene, Nyasae oito, korwa obwana bwaito goika rero iga, intwe amo ne chisokoro chiaito. Titwamoigwerete Omonene, Nyasae oito.”
english: Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. We have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers; from our youth till this day we have not obeyed the LORD our God."

ekegusii: Tiga toimokererie chinkoro chiaito igoro, na amaboko aito, gochia ase Nyasae ore igoro, totebe:
english: Let us lift up our hearts and our hands to God in heaven, and say:

ekegusii: Titoba nokogania kw’ogwetogia abanyene, titochegania, gose koba nemoko intwe ase intwe.
english: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying each other.

ekegusii: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
english: Titorosa gokora amaya, ekiagera natogese ekero engaki eraike, totakweti emioyo.

ekegusii: Titotiga gosangererekana amo, buna engencho y’abande ere, korende toremanie intwe ase intwe, kobua mono ekiagera moroche ng’a Rituko riria riaikire ang’e.
english: Let us not give up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but let us encourage one another-- and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

ekegusii: Togoke na gochenga, tomotogie ase obonene bwaye, ekiagera rituko ri’enyangi y’Emanwa y’Eng’ondi riaikire, na omoriakari oye bwebekire ang’e.
english: Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.

ekegusii: Gaki, toike ang’e ase ekerogo ki’obonene aase obuya bore, erinde tonyore amabera na obuya bw’ogotokonya ase engaki y’okoremerwa.
english: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

ekegusii: Ase igo, tiga torigie chingencho chi’omorembe ne chingencho chigwenerete ase okoagachana.
english: Let us therefore make every effort to do what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, togende asare isiko y’omochie, tobwatane nere ase okoramwa kwaye,
english: Let us, then, go to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore.

ekegusii: Gaki, tokore omokia gosoa ase ogotimoka koria, erinde onde tacha kogwa ase ogotaigwera kogwekaine koria koria.
english: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following their example of disobedience.

ekegusii: Ondorere amabera, erinde imbe moyo; inche nigo ngokerete amachiko ao.
english: Let your compassion come to me that I may live, for your law is my delight.

ekegusii: Botambe chinkwana chiaino chibe chinyororo, chinywere buna omonyo, erinde momanye buna mogwenerete koiraneria kera omonto.
english: Let your conversation be always full of grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.

ekegusii: Ndigererie oigwe ogosaba kwane, inche omosomba oo. Nigo ngosaba ase obosio bwao omobaso na obotuko, ase engencho y’abasomba bao Abaisraeli, na koorokia ebibe intwe Abaisraeli twakorire asore. Ee, ekeene, nonya ninche amo nabanto b’eamate ya tata twakorire ebibe.
english: let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer your servant is praying before you day and night for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites, including myself and my father's house, have committed against you.

ekegusii: Tiga amaiso ao arigererie gochia bosio, na ebioge bi’amaiso ao biramokigwe boronge.
english: Let your eyes look straight ahead, fix your gaze directly before you.

ekegusii: Ing’onchorere obosio bwao, inche omosomba oo, ontoorie ase engencho y’obwanchani bwao bogendererete botambe.
english: Let your face shine on your servant; save me in your unfailing love.

ekegusii: Obwororo bwaino bomanyekane ase abanto bonsi. Omonene ng’ang’e are.
english: Let your gentleness be evident to all. The Lord is near.

ekegusii: Orende nokoboko kwao omonto oyio gwachorire nokoboko kwao gw’okorio, mwanyabanto abwo aye gwechoreire.
english: Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you have raised up for yourself.

ekegusii: Nagosabire ontige inche, omosomba oo, ing’irane, erinde nkwere ase omochie one, ang’e nembeera ya tata na baba. Korende omosomba oo Kimuhamu, nao are aa, tiga amboke amo naye, omonene one, na omokorere aya orarore are amaya.”
english: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever pleases you."

ekegusii: Emegwe yao nigo ere emioge, nigo ekobeta chinkoro chi’ababisa bao aye omoruoti abanto nigo bakogwa inse yao.
english: Let your sharp arrows pierce the hearts of the king's enemies; let the nations fall beneath your feet.

ekegusii: Bono, tiga toe tata edivai anywe, atinde, torare nere, erinde tomotenenerie egesaku kiaye, tigesira.”
english: Let's get our father to drink wine and then lie with him and preserve our family line through our father."

ekegusii: Tiga tomoroiserie akanyomba igoro ase ekerama, tomobekere oborere aroro, na emesa, na ekerogo, na etaya, erinde engaki ende yonsi agocha asetore, osoa orarao.”
english: Let's make a small room on the roof and put in it a bed and a table, a chair and a lamp for him. Then he can stay there whenever he comes to us."

ekegusii: Inchuo tobamere kobare moyo, buna aase abakure akomera, bagende abagima ase embeera.
english: let's swallow them alive, like the grave, and whole, like those who go down to the pit;

ekegusii: Naende yarengeo Libuna, na Eteri, na Asani,
english: Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

ekegusii: Ekiagera obogima nobonene kobua endagera, na omobere nomonene kobua chianga.
english: Life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.

ekegusii: Na obogima bwao nigo borarabe se kobua erioba ria mobaso gati; omosunte oye nigo oraonchoke obe buna ekero bogokia mambia.
english: Life will be brighter than noonday, and darkness will become like morning.

ekegusii: Imoka, oimokie omwana, omobwate koboko kwao; naki nimokore abe egesaku ekenene.”
english: Lift the boy up and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."

ekegusii: Tenenia ebendera ase chindwaki chia Babeli! Kora oborendi bobe obokong’u ase okobeka abarendi. Beka abanto bebise na koboa, ekiagera Omonene orobeirie na goikerania amang’ana aria akwanete ase abanto bamenyete Babeli.
english: Lift up a banner against the walls of Babylon! Reinforce the guard, station the watchmen, prepare an ambush! The LORD will carry out his purpose, his decree against the people of Babylon.

ekegusii: Ramokia amaiso ao, origererie orore; bonsi mbasangererekane amo bachiche asore. Omonene otebire ng’a ekeene, buna Ere are moyo, abwo bonsi babe buna ogwechabera kwao, nigo oreboyie buna omoriakari akweboyia.
english: Lift up your eyes and look around; all your sons gather and come to you. As surely as I live," declares the LORD, "you will wear them all as ornaments; you will put them on, like a bride.

ekegusii: Imokereria amaiso aino igoro, rora abanto baria bagocha korwa sugusu. Inee! Ng’ai rire riicho riria rigiya kwaetwe?
english: Lift up your eyes and see those who are coming from the north. Where is the flock that was entrusted to you, the sheep of which you boasted?

ekegusii: “Imokia amaiso aino morigererie igoro, naende morigererie ense inse aa. Igoro chionsi nchisire buna erioki, na ense negote buna eanga. Abanto bamenyeteo nigo barakwe buna ebichuni, korende ogotooreka kwane nkogenderere kobao kare na kare, na oboronge bwane tibokoera nonya ng’ake.
english: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, look at the earth beneath; the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment and its inhabitants die like flies. But my salvation will last forever, my righteousness will never fail.

ekegusii: Rambora amaboko aino gochia Aase Aachenu, motogie Omonene!
english: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary and praise the LORD.

ekegusii: Inwe ebiita, imokereria emekorogoto yaino igoro! Inwe ebiita bia kare, igoka, erinde Omoruoti bw’obonene asoe ime!
english: Lift up your heads, O you gates; be lifted up, you ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.

ekegusii: Inwe ebiita, imokereria emetwe yaino igoro! Inwe ebiita bia kare, igoka, erinde Omoruoti bw’obonene asoe ime!
english: Lift up your heads, O you gates; lift them up, you ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in.

ekegusii: Rigereria gochia igoro morore! Ning’o otongete ebinto ebio bionsi? Nere oria okoraa emeganda y’ebitongwa ebio ase omobaro obo, na koroka kera ekemo erieta riaye. Okobua kwaye nokonene mono, ne chinguru chiaye nigo chire nokobua, ase ayio kende tikeremeti nonya nekemo.
english: Lift your eyes and look to the heavens: Who created all these? He who brings out the starry host one by one, and calls them each by name. Because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.

ekegusii: Oborabu nigo bokomochera oyore omoronge, na omogoko obachera abare ne chinkoro chindonge.
english: Light is shed upon the righteous and joy on the upright in heart.

ekegusii: Omobaso nigo ore omwansu, na amaiso nigo akogokigwa korora erioba.
english: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

ekegusii: Motogie, inwe omorero na amagena ’embura, na obokeng’entu, na amare, na aye omwaga omotindi ogoikerania aya achigete!
english: lightning and hail, snow and clouds, stormy winds that do his bidding,

ekegusii: Ogosemeria omonto otari omwegenwa ase engaki y’emechando, nigo enga buna erino ribunegete gose okogoro goteng’eretie.
english: Like a bad tooth or a lame foot is reliance on the unfaithful in times of trouble.

ekegusii: Ee, omokungu oyio nigo akoboera buna omouri, nigo akomentekania abasaria ase egati ya mwanyabanto.
english: Like a bandit she lies in wait, and multiplies the unfaithful among men.

ekegusii: Nigo amboerete buna edubu, enyang’au entindi, ekoboera, na buna endo eboerete eite.
english: Like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in hiding,

ekegusii: Nimbaumokere buna edubu yaurirwe chimanwa chiaye, mbatandore ebikuba biabo, erinde mbaite mbarie buna endo ekoria, ee, nimbe buna eng’iti y’orosana mbatandorane.
english: Like a bear robbed of her cubs, I will attack them and rip them open. Like a lion I will devour them; a wild animal will tear them apart.

ekegusii: Omonto ogotama korwa bwoye nigo anga buna enyoni ekong’anya korwa ase egeswa kiaye.
english: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.

ekegusii: Omonto otamanyeti kwegambera omonyene nigo anga buna omochie chindwaki chiaye chiatagoirwe.
english: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who lacks self-control.

ekegusii: Omonto okoba kirori bw’oborimo ase omonto onde nigo anga buna enungu y’esegi, gose omoro, gose ensara enyonge.
english: Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow is the man who gives false testimony against his neighbor.

ekegusii: Omonto obwate amang’ana amansu ase ebikoba biaye, korende ore nobobe ase enkoro yaye, nigo anga buna egekorero ki’amaroba giatekire keoomire nefeta.
english: Like a coating of glaze over earthenware are fervent lips with an evil heart.

ekegusii: Nigo arasire buna chindoto, takonyorekana, ee, nigo aragikerigwe buna chindoto.
english: Like a dream he flies away, no more to be found, banished like a vision of the night.

ekegusii: Buna enchiro ekona‐koong’anya, na buna egesingororo gekoiruruka, naboigo na okoragereria gotari nengencho gotaikerere oria oragererigwe.
english: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.

ekegusii: Omokungu omonyakieni tari na semi nigo anga buna ebonyi y’etahabu ere ase chimioro chi’embeche.
english: Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who shows no discretion.

ekegusii: Kera omonto nabe buna engabi egoserigwa, na buna ching’ondi chitari nomorisia; kera oyomo nairane ase abanto baye, na kera oyomo natame gochia ase ense yaye.
english: Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep without a shepherd, each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land.

ekegusii: Omoreng’anio ogokwanwa nomonwa bw’omoriri nigo onga buna omonto egesegora, okogoro kwaye gotari gokora emeremo.
english: Like a lame man's legs that hang limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

ekegusii: Ee, koreng’ana buna egesicha ekiya kere ase egati y’amagwa, naboigo omwanchi one are ase egati y’abaiseke.
english: Like a lily among thorns is my darling among the maidens.

ekegusii: “Rora, buna koreng’ana endo egosoka korwa ase rinani rinoru ria Yorodan, erinde yagenda goita ching’ondi chire ime ase obweri obokong’u, naboigo na inche ndachiere abanto ba Babeli mobosokano, mbaserie batame korwa aroro. Onde bwensi ndachore nimobeke abe omorisia igoro asebare. Ning’o oranyare koreng’anigwa nainche? Ning’o orambekere rituko indue omobaro? Morisia ki oranyare kweegera ase obosio bwane?
english: Like a lion coming up from Jordan's thickets to a rich pastureland, I will chase Babylon from its land in an instant. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? Who is like me and who can challenge me? And what shepherd can stand against me?"

ekegusii: Omonene otigire abanto baye, buna endo egotiga riraro riaye. Ense yabo yasarigwe na gotigwa bosa, ase engencho y’obotindi bw’abachandi, na ase engencho y’endamwamu entindi y’Omonene.”
english: Like a lion he will leave his lair, and their land will become desolate because of the sword of the oppressor and because of the LORD's fierce anger.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli nigo batung’aime inse buna endo, buna endo eaberi, ning’o orabe noboremu abature? Asesenigwe omonto oria okobasesenia inwe, na aragererigwe omonto oria okobaragereria inwe.”
english: Like a lion they crouch and lie down, like a lioness-- who dares to rouse them? "May those who bless you be blessed and those who curse you be cursed!"

ekegusii: Omonto okong’aina omonto onde, na nyuma yaye omotebia, “Negosori yoka nare gokora asore,” oyio nigo anga buna ebarimo ekoruta ebigenga bi’omorero, ne chinsara, na amakweri.
english: Like a madman shooting firebrands or deadly arrows

ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge okorua ribaga ase omokori amabe nigo anga buna orooche rore netintira na buna ensoko yasarekire.
english: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.

ekegusii: Omonto okonyora obotenenku ase enchera y’obong’ainereria, nigo anga buna enkware ekorarera amagena etabiareti. Obotenenku obwo nigo bogosira korwa asare gaikire obogima bwaye gati, ase omoerio oye nigo agotigara ore omoriri.
english: Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is the man who gains riches by unjust means. When his life is half gone, they will desert him, and in the end he will prove to be a fool.

ekegusii: Omogambi omokayayu okogambera abanto abataka nigo anga buna endo ekoruma, gose edubu yagechigwe.
english: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked man ruling over a helpless people.

ekegusii: Emegwekano eyio yabo nigo enga buna ebinto bikogosa chinyoni chire ase emegondo y’amasosa. Emegwekano eyio tekonyara gokwana; nigo ekobogorigwa, ekiagera teri gotaara. Timobaisa koyeiroka, ekiagera tegokora bobe bonde bwensi, gose tekonyara gokora gento kende ekiya.”
english: Like a scarecrow in a melon patch, their idols cannot speak; they must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not fear them; they can do no harm nor can they do any good."

ekegusii: Obomenyo bwane bwatagoirwe na korusigwa asende buna eema y’omorisia, naringire obogima bwane buna omoroisia ebitambaa akobiringa; nabutoirwe korwa ase egekorero; ekero botaraira, aye nigo okoeria obogima bwane.
english: Like a shepherd's tent my house has been pulled down and taken from me. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life, and he has cut me off from the loom; day and night you made an end of me.

ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana omosomba akogania anyore aase agokenderera, na buna koreng’ana omonto orikire emeremo akogania aegwe eng’eria yaye,
english: Like a slave longing for the evening shadows, or a hired man waiting eagerly for his wages,

ekegusii: Barabwo tiga babe buna amakorominyo akonyititoka amarenda aera, na buna oborito bw’omokungu bokogwa botaraika engaki yaye.
english: Like a slug melting away as it moves along, like a stillborn child, may they not see the sun.

ekegusii: Omoreng’anio okorwa ase omonwa bw’omonto omoriri nigo onga buna rigwa rikobeta okoboko kw’omonto otindire amarwa.
english: Like a thornbush in a drunkard's hand is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

ekegusii: Nimbaserebanie ase obosio bw’ababisa babo, buna omwaga o moocha ogoserebania. Ning’onchoke imbae omogongo, gose tinkoborokia obosio bwane ase rituko ri’emechando yabo.”
english: Like a wind from the east, I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them my back and not my face in the day of their disaster."

ekegusii: “Abanto aba basaririe okobwatana kwane kw’ogotianania, buna Adamu agosaretie. Ase amang’ana ayio babeire abatari abegenwa asende.
english: Like Adam, they have broken the covenant-- they were unfaithful to me there.

ekegusii: Koreng’ana buna omote bw’amapera osimekire ase egati y’emete y’orosana, naboigo omwanchi one are ase egati y’abamura. Nigo naikaransete ase ekiriri kiaye inde nomogoko, na amatunda aye akanyansera.
english: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my lover among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

ekegusii: Omonto omanyete emeremo nigo agwekorera emeremo emiya, korende oyore omoriri nigo akorika onde bwensi ogoeta, na emeremo yasareka.
english: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or any passer-by.

ekegusii: Buna ekeongo gekorangeria amage aye na kiayorokereria koiruruka, kiarambora chimbaba chiaye koyabogoria, naboigo Omonene akobogoria abanto baye ase chimbaba chiaye ime.
english: like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, that spreads its wings to catch them and carries them on its pinions.

ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini ogokurera oyokoigwera nigo are buna ebonyi ne chisonoi biroseirie chitahabu.
english: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man's rebuke to a listening ear.

ekegusii: Ere otingire obota bwaye buna omobisa agotinga, otenenire na kobong’usa nokoboko kwaye gw’okorio buna omochandi; agaita bonsi aba twetogeretie. Igoro y’obomenyo bw’abanto ba Sayoni, oumoire ekeririanda kiaye kere buna omorero.
english: Like an enemy he has strung his bow; his right hand is ready. Like a foe he has slain all who were pleasing to the eye; he has poured out his wrath like fire on the tent of the Daughter of Zion.

ekegusii: Abana omonto akonyora kare ne chinguru chi’oboke bwaye, nigo banga buna chinsara chire koboko kw’omorwani etuoni.
english: Like arrows in the hands of a warrior are sons born in one's youth.

ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana chinyoni chikorambora chimbaba chiabo, naboigo inche Omonene bw’Emeganda ndaegere Yerusalemu; ninyorende na koyobooria; ninyororere amabera na koyotooria.”
english: Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD Almighty will shield Jerusalem; he will shield it and deliver it, he will 'pass over' it and will rescue it."

ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana egesera geichire ne chinyoni, naboigo ne chinyomba chiabo chiaichoire nebinto bisakoire; ase engencho eyio babeire ne chinguru, na abanda mono.
english: Like cages full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; they have become rich and powerful

ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana chiombe chikoirwa ase rikura korisigwa, naboigo Omoika bw’Omonene oete abanto baria ogotimoka. Ee, nigo kwaraaete abanto bao, erinde okenyorera erieta ri’obonene.
english: like cattle that go down to the plain, they were given rest by the Spirit of the LORD. This is how you guided your people to make for yourself a glorious name.

ekegusii: Omonto ogwetogia ng’a nare nomoyo omorabu, ko tari korua ebiegwa, nigo anga amare na omwaga bitari korenta embura.
english: Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of gifts he does not give.

ekegusii: Amang’ana amaya akorentwa korwa ase ense y’aare nigo anga buna amache amakendu ase omonto ore nerang’o.
english: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.

ekegusii: Omonto ogotoma amang’ana ase okoboko kw’omonto omoriri, oyio nigo akobutora amaboko aye omonyene bwerentera emechando.
english: Like cutting off one's feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.

ekegusii: Abanto b’emechie ya Moabu mbabe bakonakoong’anya gochia ase chingegu chi’orooche rw’Arinoni, babe buna chinyoni chikoiruruka chiaserigwe korwa ase ebiswa biabo.
english: Like fluttering birds pushed from the nest, so are the women of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.

ekegusii: na inwe mobe buna abanto baganyete omonene obo, gakoirana korwa ase omoyega bw’enyangi, erinde kagocha na gotura, erio kegima bamoigorere.
english: like men waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks they can immediately open the door for him.

ekegusii: Buna abana ebing’werere baiborwa rero iga, moganie amabeere ’ekeene ay’omoika, erinde monyare gokina ase aro, na goikera ogotooreka,
english: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation,

ekegusii: Omonto orenge goeta na gwesoyia ase eriomana ritarenge eriaye nigo anga buna oyo okobwata amato ’esese.
english: Like one who seizes a dog by the ears is a passer-by who meddles in a quarrel not his own.

ekegusii: Omonto ogotera amatera ’omogoko ase omonto obwate enkoro ere nobororo nigo anga buna okorusia eanga ase engaki y’obokendu gose kobeka egento ekeroro ase eriote.
english: Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day, or like vinegar poured on soda, is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.

ekegusii: buna Sara aigwerete Ibrahimu, akamoroka omonene. Na inwe bono mwabeire abana baye komorakore amaya, gose timokwoboigwa ase kogoswa konde gwonsi.
english: like Sarah, who obeyed Abraham and called him her master. You are her daughters if you do what is right and do not give way to fear.

ekegusii: Buna riicho rie ching’ondi nigo bakoirwa gochia aase abakure, amakweri naro arabe omorisia obo. Abwo bare abaronge mbabagambera kobogokiamoka, na ebieni biabo mbisirere agwo aase abakure aase are obomenyo bwabo.
english: Like sheep they are destined for the grave, and death will feed on them. The upright will rule over them in the morning; their forms will decay in the grave, far from their princely mansions.

ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana obokendu bogocha ase engaki y’egurugura, gose embura egotwa ase engaki ye rigesa, naboigo ere bobe omonto omoriri konyora amasikani.
english: Like snow in summer or rain in harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool.

ekegusii: Na buna Abaanaki abwo nigo barenge korokwa Abarefai, korende Abamoabu nigo barenge kobaroka Abaemi.
english: Like the Anakites, they too were considered Rephaites, but the Moabites called them Emites.

ekegusii: Oborabu boria bwarenge komoreka chinsemo chiaye chionsi, nigo bwagwekaine nomokubinyongo ase engaki y’embura. Okororekana okwo nakw’obonene bw’Omonene. Ekero naroche ayio ngatung’ama inse nkaumama; erio nkaigwa eriogi ri’oyomo ogokwana.
english: Like the appearance of a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the radiance around him. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard the voice of one speaking.

ekegusii: Nigo tokona‐gotaba‐taba ase enyasi y’enyomba buna abanto emeuko, nigo tokona‐kouna‐una buna abatabwati amaiso; intwe nigo tokogochwa mobaso gati buna mbwamura‐murire. Ase egati y’abare ne chinguru nigo tonga buna abakwete.
english: Like the blind we grope along the wall, feeling our way like men without eyes. At midday we stumble as if it were twilight; among the strong, we are like the dead.

ekegusii: Omotomwa ore omwegenwa nigo are ase abwo bakomotoma buna amache amakendu ase engaki ye rigesa, ekiagera nigo akogera emioyo yabo yaba emeyia.
english: Like the coolness of snow at harvest time is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the spirit of his masters.

ekegusii: Ogoseka kw’abariri nigo konga amagwa akoyia atoreka inse y’enyongo ere riko. Ayio boigo mbosa.
english: Like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.

ekegusii: Buna ebisaku biria, Omonene arasirie korwa ase amasio aino, naboigo nainwe morasirigwe, ekiagera motaigwerete eriogi ri’Omonene, Nyasae oino.”
english: Like the nations the LORD destroyed before you, so you will be destroyed for not obeying the LORD your God.

ekegusii: Abatamoirogeti Omonene nigo banchayete na gonchecheria, bakangecha bakaba bakondiananeria amaino.
english: Like the ungodly they maliciously mocked; they gnashed their teeth at me.

ekegusii: Nigo baonchogete tibaba abegenwa, buna chisokoro chiabo chitabete abegenwa, bakaba abasaria buna obota bosaregete.
english: Like their fathers they were disloyal and faithless, as unreliable as a faulty bow.

ekegusii: Omonto okoa omoriri amasikani, nigo anga buna oyokoruta omobuko ore nebinto bie rigori rinene ase etui y’amagena.
english: Like tying a stone in a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.

ekegusii: Intwe twensi goika tokwe; nigo tore buna amache aitekire inse atanyare kobuuchwa naende. Nyasae tari gosiria obogima. Nigo akoroberia ng’a oria otamete taserigwa na gwatananwa korwa asare.
english: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But God does not take away life; instead, he devises ways so that a banished person may not remain estranged from him.

ekegusii: “Rora, abataka abwo babeire buna chitigere chi’orosana chire ase erooro; nigo bagokora emeremo emekong’u ase okonyora ebi bakoria. Ase ekerubo ekiomo nao bakorigeria abana babo endagera.
english: Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of foraging food; the wasteland provides food for their children.

ekegusii: Nyasae, buna koreng’ana erieta riao rikumete, naboigo nogotogigwa kwao gokumete goikera chinsinyo chi’ense. Okoboko kwao gw’okorio nigo goichire noboronge.
english: Like your name, O God, your praise reaches to the ends of the earth; your right hand is filled with righteousness.

ekegusii: Naboigo kera omote omuya nigo okwama amatunda amaya, na omote omobe nigo okwama amatunda amabe.
english: Likewise every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

ekegusii: Naboigo na oromeme nekiimo egeke, na rororwo nigo rokweenenia ase amang’ana amanene. Rigereria buna ensase enke egosamba rinani rinene mono.
english: Likewise the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.

ekegusii: Naboigo naye nore nabanto babwatete okworokereria kw’Abanikolaiti.
english: Likewise you also have those who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.

ekegusii: Naboigo nabakungu abagotu babe norogendo rw’obochenu, tibaba abang’achi, gose abasomba ase okonywa edivai enyinge, korende babe aborokia b’ayare amaya,
english: Likewise, teach the older women to be reverent in the way they live, not to be slanderers or addicted to much wine, but to teach what is good.

ekegusii: Chindo chiarumire asebare, chiarumire namariogi amanene; chirochio chiasaririe ense yabo yabeire erooro; emechie yabo yabeire amaturi atamenyiri nabanto.
english: Lions have roared; they have growled at him. They have laid waste his land; his towns are burned and deserted.

ekegusii: Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
english: Tegerera moigwe eriogi riane; igwera amang’ana aane ngokwana!

ekegusii: Tegerera onyigwe, tiga ogotebereria kwane gosoe ase amato aino.
english: Listen carefully to my words; let your ears take in what I say.

ekegusii: Bono ntegerera, ngotebie chisemi chingiya orakore, na Nyasae nabe amo naye. Aye kabe oyo ogotenenera abanto ase obosio bwa Nyasae, na komoirera amang’ana abo.
english: Listen now to me and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people's representative before God and bring their disputes to him.

ekegusii: Igwera ogosemigwa naende bwanche okworokererigwa, igo nario oranyore obong’aini boragokonye ase chingaki chire bosio.
english: Listen to advice and accept instruction, and in the end you will be wise.

ekegusii: “Aye Omonene, inyigwe, tegerera amang’ana aya ababisa baane bagokwana.
english: Listen to me, O LORD; hear what my accusers are saying!

ekegusii: Inwe abanto momenyete ase ebisinka, na ase chinse chionsi chire aare, tegerera monyigwe! Omonene nigo andangeretie konde ase enda ya baba, nigo andogete erieta konde enda ime.
english: Listen to me, you islands; hear this, you distant nations: Before I was born the LORD called me; from my birth he has made mention of my name.

ekegusii: “Inwe abamore abanyabigoti bikong’u, inwe abamore aare korwa ase oboronge, inyigwera!
english: Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, you who are far from righteousness.

ekegusii: Aye omoruoti one, Nyasae one, tegerera oigwe amang’ana ’okorera kwane, ekiagera naye ngosaba.
english: Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God, for to you I pray.

ekegusii: Tegerera oigwe ekerero kiane, ekiagera nachandekire mono! Ntoorie korwa ase abanto abwo bagonchanda, ekiagera nigo babwate chinguru kombua.
english: Listen to my cry, for I am in desperate need; rescue me from those who pursue me, for they are too strong for me.

ekegusii: Igwera amorokererio! Ancha obong’aini, timobwanga!
english: Listen to my instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’okorera nariigugwe korwa Horonaimu, rigoteba: Ogotigara bosa na ogosirigwa okonene.
english: Listen to the cries from Horonaim, cries of great havoc and destruction.

ekegusii: Tegerera! Abanto baane nkorera bare korwa ase chinsemo chionsi chi’ense, bakoboria: “Inee! Omonene tari ase Sayoni? Omoruoti o Sayoni tari aroro?” Omonene nigo agoteba; “Nase ki abanto bangechirie nabeire nendamwamu ase ogosasima emegwekano yabo ebombire amo ne chinyasae chiabo chingeni?”
english: Listen to the cry of my people from a land far away: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King no longer there?" "Why have they provoked me to anger with their images, with their worthless foreign idols?"

ekegusii: “Igwa eriogi ri’abanto bagotama korwa ase ense ya Babeli, bakoraria ase Sayoni igoro y’Omonene, Nyasae oito, buna akoruseria Hekalu yaye egesiomba.
english: Listen to the fugitives and refugees from Babylon declaring in Zion how the LORD our God has taken vengeance, vengeance for his temple.

ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe buna abarisia bakorera bono ekero obonene na obuya bwabo bwasirigwe! Tegerera moigwe buna chindo chinsae chikoruma bono ekero rinani rinoru ria Yorodan riasirigwe!
english: Listen to the wail of the shepherds; their rich pastures are destroyed! Listen to the roar of the lions; the lush thicket of the Jordan is ruined!

ekegusii: Bono inwe tegerera moigwe aya Omonene agoteba: Imoka, mwekwanere agwo bosio bw’ebitunwa, na motige ebigoro biigwe amariogi aino.
english: Listen to what the LORD says: "Stand up, plead your case before the mountains; let the hills hear what you have to say.

ekegusii: Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
english: Igwera iso okoiborete, na tobaisa gochaya nyoko ekero agotire.

ekegusii: Rora, nimbeke omoika gete ime yaye, erio ekero araigwe chinkuma nairoke, airane gochia ase ense yaye; nimorue aitwe nomoro, agwo ase ense yaye omonyene.”
english: Listen! I am going to put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down with the sword.'"

ekegusii: Rora nimbeke omoika gete ime yaye, erio ekero araigwe chinkuma airoke, airane gochia ase ense yaye; nimoiyerie aitwe nomoro agwo ase ense yaye omonyene.”
english: Listen! I am going to put such a spirit in him that when he hears a certain report, he will return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down with the sword.'"

ekegusii: Tegerera oigwe okogukura kw’eriogi riaye, na okoruma gokorwa ase omonwa oye.
english: Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice, to the rumbling that comes from his mouth.

ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe eriogi ri’omwanchi one! Rora oyio ogocha! Nigo agocharoka‐charoka igoro ase ebitunwa, na gocharara ase ebigoro.
english: Listen! My lover! Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

ekegusii: Omonene nigo akorangeria abare ase omochie, na omonto oirogete erieta riaye nere omong’aini. Eriogi riaye nigo rigoteba: “Igwa igoro y’egesusuro na ning’o ogechikire.
english: Listen! The LORD is calling to the city-- and to fear your name is wisdom-- "Heed the rod and the One who appointed it.

ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe! Ebirage bigocha. Riroroche ri’omoganda omonene riaigurwe rigocha korwa sugusu, gocha gosaria emechie y’Abayuda ebe amaturi, ase chisese chi’orosana chiramenye.”
english: Listen! The report is coming-- a great commotion from the land of the north! It will make the towns of Judah desolate, a haunt of jackals.

ekegusii: Igwa, abarendi baino ngoaka bare eriogi, bonsi amo nigo bagotera nomogoko, barorire namaiso abo buna Omonene akoirana gocha Sayoni.
english: Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices; together they shout for joy. When the LORD returns to Zion, they will see it with their own eyes.

ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe amariogi ’emeganda y’abanto bakwoga igoro ase ebitunwa! Tegerera moigwe amariogi ay’okomumura kw’amaruoti ’ebisaku asangererekanire amo. Omonene bw’Emeganda nkoroberia are emeganda y’esegi.
english: Listen, a noise on the mountains, like that of a great multitude! Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations massing together! The LORD Almighty is mustering an army for war.

ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe, ekiagera nigo ndakwane amang’ana amaya mono; amang’ana akorwa ase omonwa one nay’oboronge.
english: Listen, for I have worthy things to say; I open my lips to speak what is right.

ekegusii: Rigereria, aya nkobatebia nobobisi. Titogokwa intwe twensi, korende twensi natoonchorwe,
english: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed--

ekegusii: Abaminto abanchani, tegerera! Inee! Nyasae tachorete abataka b’ense eye babe abanda ase okwegena, naende babe abanyamwando b’oboruoti obo abarierete eira, abwo bamwanchete?
english: Listen, my dear brothers: Has not God chosen those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom he promised those who love him?

ekegusii: Aye omwana one, igwa amang’ana aane, oyaanche, igo nario emiaka y’obogima bwao erabe emenge.
english: Listen, my son, accept what I say, and the years of your life will be many.

ekegusii: Aye omwana one, igwa na obe nobong’aini, naende orende enkoro yao ebwatie enchera endonge.
english: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path.

ekegusii: Omwana one, igwera amorokererio a iso, na tobaisa gotiga aya nyoko akogochika.
english: Listen, my son, to your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching.

ekegusii: Inwe abana baane, igwa amorokererio aane inche iso; tegerera mono, erinde monyare koba nokomanya.
english: Listen, my sons, to a father's instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.

ekegusii: Aye omoiseke, igwa! Ntegerera mono! Eba bono abanto baino na ab’enyomba ya iso.
english: Listen, O daughter, consider and give ear: Forget your people and your father's house.

ekegusii: “Inwe igoro, ntegerera moigwe, nkwane, naye ense, igwa amang’ana akorwa ase omonwa one.
english: Listen, O heavens, and I will speak; hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.

ekegusii: Omonto kare namato akoigwera, tiga aigwe.]”
english: Listen, then, if you have ears! [* Verse originally omitted in Good News version. See Mark 4.23.]

ekegusii: Bono agatongia omorero ase ebieri biria, agatiga ebibwe bikominyoka ase emegondo y’Abafilisti, na birobio bigasamba engano yagesire ebekire amo, amo neye konya etarageswa, na emegondo y’emezeituni egasambwa boigo.
english: lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned up the shocks and standing grain, together with the vineyards and olive groves.

ekegusii: Nigo ndabaserie ng’ora ng’ora goika momenteke moisane komenya ense eyio.
english: Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased enough to take possession of the land.

ekegusii: Mobe abanto abasibore, korende timokorera obosibore bwaino ase okobiserera obobe, korende mobe norogendo rogwenerete abasomba ba Nyasae.
english: Live as free men, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

ekegusii: Abanto bonsi abare ababiare b’Abaisraeli nabamenye ase ebigutu ase engaki y’amatuko atano na abere.
english: Live in booths for seven days: All native-born Israelites are to live in booths

ekegusii: Mobe nomoyo oyomo inwe ase inwe. Timorengereria ayare amanene, korende mosange nabare noboitongo. Timoba abanto bakoenenera obong’aini.
english: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people of low position. Do not be conceited.

ekegusii: Mobe norogendo oruya ase egati y’abanto b’Ebisaku, erinde nonya bakobang’acha ng’a nabakori amabe more, banyare korora ogokora kwaino okuya na gotogia Nyasae rituko riria agocha kobachera.
english: Live such good lives among the pagans that, though they accuse you of doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day he visits us.

ekegusii: Chingige tichibwati omoruoti, korende nigo chikogendera amo emeganda emeganda.
english: locusts have no king, yet they advance together in ranks;

ekegusii: Korwa kare nimanyete korwa ase oborori bwao ng’a naye kwabobegete bobeo goika kare na kare.
english: Long ago I learned from your statutes that you established them to last forever.

ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bobwate obogima bw’amatuko amange ase okoboko kwaye gw’okorio, na ase okoboko kwaye gw’okobee nigo bobwate obonda obonge amo nogosikwa.
english: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.

ekegusii: Tiga omoruoti agenderere koba moyo. Chitahabu chi’ense ya Seba chirentwe asare, tiga abanto babe bakomosabera botambe, boigo tiga abe okona‐gosesenigwa kera rituko.
english: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him and bless him all day long.

ekegusii: Ee, rigereria oyio ore omoenenu, omokeyie, na abakori amabe obatindachere inse agwo ase bateneine.
english: look at every proud man and humble him, crush the wicked where they stand.

ekegusii: Look at me and be astonished; clap your hand over your mouth.
english: Indigererie na moichanigwe; erio motube emenwa yaino namaboko, mokire.

ekegusii: Rora amaboko aane na amagoro aane, ng’a ninche omonyene; mbwata‐bwate, morore, ekiagera rirengari tiriri nomobere na amauga buna mondoche inche inde naro.” [
english: Look at my hands and my feet. It is I myself! Touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have."

ekegusii: Morigererie chinyoni chia igoro! Chirochio tichiri gosimeka, tichiri kogesa, tichiri gosangereria gochia biage, na Iso oino ore igoro nigo agochirageria. Inee! Inwe timobueti rigori riabo?
english: Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

ekegusii: Rigereria ense y’Abakalidayo! Abanto aba tibarenge egesaku. Abaasuri nabwo barentete ching’iti chi’orosana komenya aroro. Abwo bakaagacha chindwaki chi’okoboera, bakaonchorana chinyomba chi’obogambi chi’omochie oyio, bakayotagora okaba etui.
english: Look at the land of the Babylonians, this people that is now of no account! The Assyrians have made it a place for desert creatures; they raised up their siege towers, they stripped its fortresses bare and turned it into a ruin.

ekegusii: Look at them! Sitting or standing, they mock me in their songs.
english: Rora, ekero abwo baikaransete, na ekero bakoimoka, ninche engeero yabo bagochaya.

ekegusii: Rora, abarwani bao b’esegi nigo banga abakungu, na ebiita bi’ense yao nigo biigoire biasie ase ababisa bao. Omorero osambire emekorogoto y’ebiita biao.
english: Look at your troops-- they are all women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed their bars.

ekegusii: Intige, inyore chinguru chinyia ntararua ase ense, na ntabeo naende.
english: Look away from me, that I may rejoice again before I depart and am no more."

ekegusii: Omonene, rigereria inse aa, korwa agwo igoro ase obomenyo bwao obochenu bore, na obonene bwao bore. Ng’ai risemi riao, ne chinguru chiao, bire? Okonyechandera kwao, na amabera ao asende, ng’ai bire? Ekeene, biatangirwe korwa asende.
english: Look down from heaven and see from your lofty throne, holy and glorious. Where are your zeal and your might? Your tenderness and compassion are withheld from us.

ekegusii: Korwa agwo igoro, ase Obomenyo bwao Obochenu bore, origererie, erinde otorore inse aa; osesenie abanto bao Abaisraeli, osesenie na ense eye gwatoeire buna kwarierete chisokoro chiaito eira, ense entenenku ere namabeere na amooke.
english: Look down from heaven, your holy dwelling place, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us as you promised on oath to our forefathers, a land flowing with milk and honey."

ekegusii: Rigia korwa ase ebuku y’Omonene, mosome: Nonya nekemo ki’ebitongwa ebio tigekobora kobeera aroro, kera ekemo goika kebe nekiamwabo. Omonene ochikire amang’ana ayio, na Omoika oye nobisangererieo.
english: Look in the scroll of the LORD and read: None of these will be missing, not one will lack her mate. For it is his mouth that has given the order, and his Spirit will gather them together.

ekegusii: Rora bono, aye nigo osemeretie ense y’Abamisiri, eyio enga buna egetonto kebunegete. Omonto onde bwensi okogiesiirera nigo keramokebe okoboko. Naboigo Farao o Misiri are ase abanto bonsi bamosemeretie.
english: Look now, you are depending on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces a man's hand and wounds him if he leans on it! Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who depend on him.

ekegusii: Rora bono, aye nigo osemeretie ense y’Abamisiri, eyio enga buna egetonto kebunegete. Omonto onde bwensi okogiesiirera, ekio nigo keramokebe okoboko. Naboigo Farao omoruoti o Misiri are ase abanto bonsi abwo bamosemeretie.
english: Look now, you are depending on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces a man's hand and wounds him if he leans on it! Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who depend on him.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, Nyasae one, ondigererie, ong’iranerie ase ogosaba kwane! Ondamokie amaiso aane, timbaisa korara chitoro chi’amakweri.
english: Look on me and answer, O LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, or I will sleep in death;

ekegusii: ee, rigereria Ibrahimu, sokoro yaino, na engoro ase mwakunyetwe korwa, na Sara oyo obaiborete. Ekero Ibrahimu arenge bweka, nigo namorangeretie, nkamosesenia, nkamomentekania.
english: look to Abraham, your father, and to Sarah, who gave you birth. When I called him he was but one, and I blessed him and made him many.

ekegusii: Ekero nkorigereria ase ensemo yane y’okorio, tindi korora monto aroro ogonkonya; gose tindi korora aase ndatamere, monto onde tari okonyechandera.
english: Look to my right and see; no one is concerned for me. I have no refuge; no one cares for my life.

ekegusii: Rigia Omonene amo ne chinguru chiaye, morigie mobe ase obosio bwaye botambe.
english: Look to the LORD and his strength; seek his face always.

ekegusii: Rigia Omonene amo ne chinguru chiaye, morigie obosio bwaye botambe.
english: Look to the LORD and his strength; seek his face always.

ekegusii: “Rigereria gochia igoro, orore; rora amare buna are igoro mono kogoetania.
english: Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds so high above you.

ekegusii: ndigererie orore obororo bwane na ogochandwa kwane, na onyabere ebibe biane bionsi.
english: Look upon my affliction and my distress and take away all my sins.

ekegusii: Look upon my suffering and deliver me, for I have not forgotten your law.
english: Rigereria emechando yane, ontoorie, ekiagera tinyebeti amachiko ao.

ekegusii: Look upon our shield, O God; look with favor on your anointed one.
english: Aye Nyasae ore enguba yaito, origererie obosio bw’omoakwa amaguta oo.

ekegusii: Rigereria Sayoni, omochie oyio ase togosangererekana ase Amatuko aito Amanene! Erio amaiso ao narore Yerusalemu, obomenyo bw’obotoereru, eema etari kona‐kong’anya‐ng’anyigwa; eyio ebirochi biaye bitari gosimorwa, gose chingori chiaye chitari kobutoka.
english: Look upon Zion, the city of our festivals; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful abode, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up, nor any of its ropes broken.

ekegusii: Naama! Egesaku gete nkeimokerere igoro keiruruke bwango buna ekeongo, kerambore chimbaba chiaye igoro y’omochie o Bosira. Ase rituko erio chinkoro chi’abarwani esegi b’Edomu bare chituoni nachiondoke, na barabwo babe buna omokungu okobina ase okoibora.”
english: Look! An eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

ekegusii: Rora, omobisa nigo agotochera buna amare, nigo abwate chigari chi’esegi chinga buna ekerambauti; chibarasi chiaye nigo chikominyoka chimbero kobua ekeongo. Obobe nobwaito! Ee, twasirigwe.
english: Look! He advances like the clouds, his chariots come like a whirlwind, his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us! We are ruined!

ekegusii: Rora aaria, ekerogo gi’okobogoreria Sulemani, geetananire nabanto emerongo etano nomo, abare chituoni chi’Abaisraeli.
english: Look! It is Solomon's carriage, escorted by sixty warriors, the noblest of Israel,

ekegusii: Rora, Omonene ngosoka are korwa aase aye; ere ngoika are gocha aa, atache ebitunwa bi’ense.
english: Look! The LORD is coming from his dwelling place; he comes down and treads the high places of the earth.

ekegusii: Rigereria, mwabarinire abakoreri, abagesire emegondo yaino, eng’eria yabo. Bono eng’eria eria ekorera, na okorera kw’abagesi baria gwaikire ase amato ’Omonene bw’Emeganda.
english: Look! The wages you failed to pay the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord Almighty.

ekegusii: Rigereria, ngocha are namare, na kera eriso narimorore, nonya nabwo bamoitete, na abanto b’ebisaku bionsi bi’ense nabeng’ererie ase engencho yaye. Ee, nabo. Amina.
english: Look, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him; and all the peoples of the earth will mourn because of him. So shall it be! Amen.

ekegusii: “Bono abariini chibarasi ngocha bare babere babere.” Na omotengeri oria agaaka eriogi riaye naende, agateba, “Babeli ogure! Ogure kegima! Emegwekano yaye yonsi y’ogosasimwa yasenyentirwe na gotiringerwa inse.”
english: Look, here comes a man in a chariot with a team of horses. And he gives back the answer: 'Babylon has fallen, has fallen! All the images of its gods lie shattered on the ground!'"

ekegusii: Rora omochie oyo ore ang’e aiga, omochie omoke, noro ndaike bwango. Tiga ntame gochia ase omochie oria, ore omoke iga, ntoorie obogima bwane.”
english: Look, here is a town near enough to run to, and it is small. Let me flee to it-- it is very small, isn't it? Then my life will be spared."

ekegusii: Rora, nimbwate omoiseke one omwekungi, na omonto oyo nabwate omokungu oye o sere‐sere, tiga mbasokie asemore bono. Mobakorere obonyaka buna moganetie, korende timobaisa gokorera omonto oyo egento buna ekio gi’okogechia.”
english: Look, here is my virgin daughter, and his concubine. I will bring them out to you now, and you can use them and do to them whatever you wish. But to this man, don't do such a disgraceful thing."

ekegusii: Rora, nimbwate abaiseke baane babere abekungi; tiga mbabarentere, na mobakorere buna moranche, korende abanto aba iga timobakorera ing’ana riibe, ekiagera basoire nyomba mwane ime.”
english: Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you like with them. But don't do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof."

ekegusii: rora, nkobeka nde risankwa rire namarionya e ching’ondi ase ekeooreri gekoorerwa; obotooru bokoba ase risankwa riria rire namarionya oka, korende riroba ribe eriomo, erio nario ndamanye ng’a aye notoorie Abaisraeli goetera ase okoboko kwane, buna gwatebire.”
english: look, I will place a wool fleece on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you said."

ekegusii: Igwa, abanto abwo bare chituoni nigo bakorera mono agwo isiko, na abwo batomirwe bare namang’ana ’omorembe nigo bakorera bare nobororo.
english: Look, their brave men cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.

ekegusii: Rigereria ase ebitunwa, orore amagoro ay’oyio okorenta amang’ana amaya ay’omogoko na koraria amang’ana ’omorembe! Inwe Abayuda, renda Amatuko aino Amanene, moikeranie chiira chiria mwariete. Abakori amabe tibagocha kobarwania naende, ekiagera basirigwe kegima.
english: Look, there on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your festivals, O Judah, and fulfill your vows. No more will the wicked invade you; they will be completely destroyed.

ekegusii: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
english: Rora, enyomba yaino mwatigeirwe ritombe.

ekegusii: Rora, enyomba yaino mwatigeirwe ere ritombe; na inche nabatebirie ng’a timokondora nonya ng’ake, goika ekero keria morache goteba: Nasesenirie oyogocha ase erieta ri ’Omonene.”
english: Look, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

ekegusii: Yeso akaimokia amaiso aye ase aborokigwa baye, akabora, “Imosesenirie inwe abamore abataka, ekiagera oboruoti bwa Nyasae nobwaino.”
english: Looking at his disciples, he said: "Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, ase okoba namang’ana buna ayio, abanto nigo bakoba moyo, na obogima bw’omoika one nao bore ase ayio, na bono ingwenie kegima na onkore imbe moyo.
english: Lord, by such things men live; and my spirit finds life in them too. You restored me to health and let me live.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, naigure chinkuma chiao, nairokire. Omonene, ogokora kwao tiga kobe okoyia ase emiaka eye, tiga komanyekane ase emiaka eye. Ekero ore nendamwamu oinyore amabera.
english: LORD, I have heard of your fame; I stand in awe of your deeds, O LORD. Renew them in our day, in our time make them known; in wrath remember mercy.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, ekero barenge nemechando nigo bakorigetie, ekero kwabaete egesusuro, nigo bagosabete mono.
english: LORD, they came to you in their distress; when you disciplined them, they could barely whisper a prayer.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, notorentere omorembe, ekiagera emeremo twabeire togokora, naye kwabeire gokoyetokorera.
english: LORD, you establish peace for us; all that we have accomplished you have done for us.

ekegusii: Omonene nere egetare kiane; nere akong’a onsi aya ngwenerete konyora; ere igo arendete aya antungetie.
english: LORD, you have assigned me my portion and my cup; you have made my lot secure.

ekegusii: Loti agatiira korwa Soari, agacha akamenya ase ebitunwa amo nabaiseke baye babere, ekiagera nigo oboete komenya Soari; akamenya ase rikuruma amo nabaiseke baye babere.
english: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains, for he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.

ekegusii: Loti akaimokia amaiso aye akarigereria, akarora ense omweya ya Yorodan ng’a nigo yare namache amange kera aase; goika Soari nigo yare buna omogondo bw’Omonene, buna ense ya Misiri. Nabo yarenge ritang’ani Omonene atarasaria Sodomu na Gomora.
english: Lot looked up and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, toward Zoar. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)

ekegusii: Loti agasoka isiko ase abanto baria, agasieka egesieri korwa nyuma yaye,
english: Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him

ekegusii: Abanto ba kera eamate, enke na enene, bagaaka obomera bamanye ngeita ki bararende.
english: Lots were cast for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.

ekegusii: Obuya na obwegenwa, nabio bikorenda omoruoti, na ekerogo kiaye ki’obogambi nigo kegokong’igwa namabera.
english: Love and faithfulness keep a king safe; through love his throne is made secure.

ekegusii: Aase agwo obwanchani bogendererete botambe na ekeene mbiumerane, boigo oboronge na omorembe mbinyunyuntane.
english: Love and faithfulness meet together; righteousness and peace kiss each other.

ekegusii: Obwanchani tibogokorera omogisangio oo bobe; naboigo, obwanchani nabwo bogoikerania amachiko.
english: Love does no harm to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

ekegusii: tibokogokera obobe, korende bogokera ekeene.
english: Love does not delight in evil but rejoices with the truth.

ekegusii: Obwanchani nigo bokoremereria, naende nigo bokoba nobwororo. Obwanchani tibori koba ne ribero, tibori koenena, tibori gwetogia,
english: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

ekegusii: Obwanchani bobe botari nobong’ainereria. Gecha erire riibe, bwatana nerire rigiya.
english: Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil; cling to what is good.

ekegusii: Obwanchani tibori nomoerio; korende koborabeo obobani, nabosire; kerabe emenwa, neere; gochirabe chisemi, nachisire.
english: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be stilled; where there is knowledge, it will pass away.

ekegusii: “Ase igo bono mwanche Omonene, Nyasae oino, botambe mobwate aya achikire, na emeroberio yaye echikire, na amachiko aye onsi.
english: Love the LORD your God and keep his requirements, his decrees, his laws and his commands always.

ekegusii: naye mwanche Omonene Nyasae oo nenkoro yao yonsi, na omoyo oo bwonsi, na obong’aini bwao bwonsi, ne chinguru chiao chionsi.
english: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.'

ekegusii: Mwanche Omonene, Nyasae oo, nenkoro yao yonsi, na omoyo oo bwonsi, ne chinguru chiao chionsi.
english: Love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.

ekegusii: Mwanche Omonene, inwe abachenu baye mwensi! Omonene nigo akobarenda buya abanto bare abegenwa, korende nigo akorua egesusuro ase oyore omomwenu.
english: Love the LORD, all his saints! The LORD preserves the faithful, but the proud he pays back in full.

ekegusii: Ekeene, mwanyabanto nigo bare buna omooki rioka, abanto baeire obonene nigo bare bosa; ekero bakorengwa nigo bare abagusu; bonsi nigo bare abagusu kobua omooki.
english: Lowborn men are but a breath, the highborn are but a lie; if weighed on a balance, they are nothing; together they are only a breath.

ekegusii: Ekiagera Lida nigo orenge ang’e na Yopa, na aborokigwa konya baigure ng’a Petero nao are aria, bagatoma abanto babere asare komosorora na komotebia, “Koranche, totebana gocha asetore.”
english: Lydda was near Joppa; so when the disciples heard that Peter was in Lydda, they sent two men to him and urged him, "Please come at once!"

ekegusii: Maarath, Beth Anoth and Eltekon-- six towns and their villages.
english: na Maarati, na Beti‐Anoti, na Elitekoni, emechie etano nomo, amo nebichie biabo.

ekegusii: Maasia, na Biligai, na Semaya. Aba nabwo barenge abakuani.
english: Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.

ekegusii: Macnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
english: Makinadebai na Sasai, Sarai

ekegusii: nonya nekero keria twarenge tokwete ase ogosaria gwaito, agatoa obogima amo na Kristo; naki mwatoorigwe ase obuya.
english: made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in transgressions-- it is by grace you have been saved.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Madimena nigo bagendererete gotama, na abamenyete Gebimu ngotama bare ase ogwetooria.
english: Madmenah is in flight; the people of Gebim take cover.

ekegusii: na omogambi Magadieli, na omogambi Iramu. Aba nabwo abagambi barwete ase ororeria rw’Edomu, koreng’ana buna bamenyete chinsemo chiabo ase ense eria bairete ekaba eyabo. (Esau nere sokoro bw’Abaedomu).
english: Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they occupied. This was Esau the father of the Edomites.

ekegusii: Magadieli na Iramu. Abwo nabwo barenge abagambi b’Abaedomu.
english: Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

ekegusii: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
english: Magipiasi, na Mesulamu, na Hesiri;

ekegusii: Maharai korwa Netofa, na Heledi, mosinto o Baana korwa Netofa;
english: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,

ekegusii: Nigo agokorera abanto chilifu obwanchani botari koera; ere nigo akwabera amamocho, na ogosaria, na ebibe, korende tagotiga koa abana na abachokoro egesusuro goika ekiaare kia gatato na egia kane ase engencho y’amabe ’abaibori babo.”
english: maintaining love to thousands, and forgiving wickedness, rebellion and sin. Yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he punishes the children and their children for the sin of the fathers to the third and fourth generation."

ekegusii: Okore boigo egechungi gi’etaai na obeke chibonyi inye chie chitaai ase chikoona chiaye inye.
english: Make a grating for it, a bronze network, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the network.

ekegusii: Ase chikoona inye chi’egesasimero oroisie emegwekano ye chingunchara inye. Chingunchara echio nigo chirabe egento ekemo negesasimero; oome gionsi netaai.
english: Make a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar are of one piece, and overlay the altar with bronze.

ekegusii: Inse y’ekerama otige ribaga ri’okorenta oborabu ase obwato obwo, orikore obotambe gochia igoro obw’ekerengo gi’okoboko okomo, obeke egesieri rikere ensemo. Onachane obwato obwo amarongo atato.
english: Make a roof for it and finish the ark to within 18 inches of the top. Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks.

ekegusii: Okore chindogio chi’okobuucha ribu korwa ase egesasimero. Naende okore ebichiko, na ebitaabo, ne chigami, ne chindogio chi’okorenta omorero. Ebinto ebi bionsi biroisigwe korwa ase chitaai.
english: Make all its utensils of bronze-- its pots to remove the ashes, and its shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.

ekegusii: Mokore omokia konyora obomo bw’Omoika ase egesibo ki’omorembe.
english: Make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

ekegusii: Kora omokia koba nomorembe nabanto bonsi, na rigia obochenu, ekiagera onde tari orarore Omonene, atari naborobwo.
english: Make every effort to live in peace with all men and to be holy; without holiness no one will see the Lord.

ekegusii: Okore ebioro emerongo etano, obibeke ase ensinyo ye rirondia rinene rie ritang’ani, na emerongo etano ase rirondia rinene ria kabere rigochakera.
english: Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and also along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.

ekegusii: Okore ebioro emerongo etano, obibeke ase egetambaa kegochakera rirondia rie ritang’ani, na emerongo etano ase egetambaa kegokoorera rirondia ria kabere. Ebioro bia kera rirondia bibe bichikaine.
english: Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other.

ekegusii: “Oroisie rirondia ri’amasankwa e chimingichi aakire etaago, ribe rigotuba eema, ne rirondia rinde ri’amasankwa amaterere e ching’iti chia rooche, ribe rikobekwa igoro ye rirondia rie ritang’ani.
english: Make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of hides of sea cows.

ekegusii: Okore chibonyi inye chie chitahabu ase emesa eria, ochibeke ase chikoona inye ase amagoro aye,
english: Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners, where the four legs are.

ekegusii: Make gold filigree settings
english: Oture ebikonde bibere bi’etahabu,

ekegusii: Naende obaache chisiiro isano chi’emekonge ase ogosunga egetambaa ekio, ochioome netahabu; oture ebigobanio bie chitaai. Okore chinterekerero inye chie chitaai chinyititoire, chibe ase chisiiro echio.”
english: Make gold hooks for this curtain and five posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold. And cast five bronze bases for them.

ekegusii: Naende kora omokia komenya ase obotoereru, na kwenaria ogokora kwaino, na gokora emeremo namaboko aino, buna twabachigete.
english: Make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, to mind your own business and to work with your hands, just as we told you,

ekegusii: Rongeyia oboeto bw’amagoro ao, ne chinchera chiao chionsi chibe chindonge.
english: Make level paths for your feet and take only ways that are firm.

ekegusii: Okore ebioro bie chiusi chiburu, obibeke ase ensinyo y’egetambaa eke kere ensinyo y’ensemo eyemo ya kera rirondia.
english: Make loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and do the same with the end curtain in the other set.

ekegusii: Goika moroisie emegwekano y’amagumba, na eye chimbeba, ebio bigosaria ense yaino; erio motogie Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli. Ande nabo arakore emechando yaino ebe emegusu asemore, na ase chinyasae chiaino, na ase ense yaino.
english: Make models of the tumors and of the rats that are destroying the country, and pay honor to Israel's god. Perhaps he will lift his hand from you and your gods and your land.

ekegusii: Terera Omonene ase okobugia amakano, ee, ase okobugia amakano tera namariogi amaya.
english: make music to the LORD with the harp, with the harp and the sound of singing,

ekegusii: oyomo ase kera ensinyo. Oyekore ebe egento ekemo n’Oboikaranso bw’Amabera.
english: Make one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other; make the cherubim of one piece with the cover, at the two ends.

ekegusii: Emeroberio nigo egoikeranigwa goetera ase ogosemia okuya na gokorwana esegi, oyerwanie nogosemania okuya.
english: Make plans by seeking advice; if you wage war, obtain guidance.

ekegusii: Obaache emiaro y’emekonge ase egesasimero ekio, oyeoome netaai.
english: Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.

ekegusii: Okore emegwekano y’amatunda e rikomomanga korwa ase chiusi chi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, oyebeke eetanane omoringero o inse. Ase egati ya kera omogwekano bwe rikomomanga obeke chindege chie chitahabu.
english: Make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn around the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.

ekegusii: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
english: Toigorere chinkoro chiaino; titokorereti monto onde bobe, titosareti monto, titorieti monto kiaboama.

ekegusii: Oroiserie Haroni, momura omino, chianga chinchenu chi’obonene na echi’oboseera.
english: Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron, to give him dignity and honor.

ekegusii: Ase ensemo ya nyuma y’Obomenyo eyerochie bosongo, oroisie chibao isano nemo,
english: Make six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle,

ekegusii: Rigereria ng’a onde taakana oyomwabo obobe ase obobe, korende botambe morigie gokorerana ayare amaya inwe ase inwe, na ase abanto bonsi.
english: Make sure that nobody pays back wrong for wrong, but always try to be kind to each other and to everyone else.

ekegusii: Mwerende, tabaisa koba ase egati yaino omonto omosacha gose omokungu, gose eamate, gose egesaku, oraonchoke ase rituko ria rero, atige Omonene, Nyasae oito, na gosasima chinyasae chi’abanto b’ebisaku ebio. Toba ase egati yaino omori okomera ekemeri kere nobosongo gekwama okwama okororo.
english: Make sure there is no man or woman, clan or tribe among you today whose heart turns away from the LORD our God to go and worship the gods of those nations; make sure there is no root among you that produces such bitter poison.

ekegusii: “Okore amasugunia, oyabeke ase emego ene y’eganchwa yao entambe, eria okwambara.
english: Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.

ekegusii: Egesasimero keagachwe ne chibao, ime getigwe giasaime. Okeroisie buna kworogetigwe ase egetunwa.”
english: Make the altar hollow, out of boards. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.

ekegusii: Okore chinkoro chi’abanto aba chibe chinkong’u, na amato abo abe amarito ase okoigwa, na amaiso abo aukore, erinde tibabaisa korora namaiso abo, gose koigwa namato abo, gose komanya ne chinkoro chiabo, baonchoke, bagwenigwe.”
english: Make the heart of this people calloused; make their ears dull and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed."

ekegusii: Obaache emiaro eria korwa ase emekonge, oyeoome netahabu.
english: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

ekegusii: Obaache emiaro eria korwa ase emekonge, oyeoome netahabu, nero emesa erabogorerigwe.
english: Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold and carry the table with them.

ekegusii: Make the price for the bride and the gift I am to bring as great as you like, and I'll pay whatever you ask me. Only give me the girl as my wife."
english: Mborie enibo ende yonsi na ebiegwa boigo, nimbae buna moraganie, kogicha mong’e omoiseke oyo abe mokane.”

ekegusii: Bae abanto abwo emeremo emerito mono, baisaneke nero, na tibabaisa gotegerera amang’ana ’oborimo.”
english: Make the work harder for the men so that they keep working and pay no attention to lies."

ekegusii: naende ng’a asiarere abanto b’ororeria rwabo, bagende komenya ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku ase chinse ao ao.
english: make their descendants fall among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.

ekegusii: Okore abanto babo basikire buna gwakorete Orebu na Seebu, na abanene babo babe buna Seba na Salimuna,
english: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae one, tiga abanto abwo bairurukigwe buna orotu, ee, buna omoiriro okoirurukigwa nomwaga.
english: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.

ekegusii: Ase ebinto ebio oroisie amaguta akweakwa ase chisemi chi’omoroisia omong’aini, abe amaguta amachenu akweakwa.
english: Make these into a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It will be the sacred anointing oil.

ekegusii: Mondoiserie Obomenyo na ebinto bionsi ebirabeo, buna ndakworokie.”
