english: Make this tabernacle and all its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.

ekegusii: “Erio oroiserie abamura ba Haroni chiganchwa, ne chinkini; naende obaroiserie ebigogwa emechoro bi’ogosika na ebi’oboseera:
english: Make tunics, sashes and headbands for Aaron's sons, to give them dignity and honor.

ekegusii: Koraroisie chibao echio, oroisie emerongo ebere ase ensemo ya irianyi.
english: Make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle

ekegusii: Okore chibonyi chinde ibere chie chitahabu, ochibeke ase egesembe keria ase emego ebere ya inse korwa nyuma, echigete egesibao.
english: Make two gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod.

ekegusii: Okore boigo chibonyi ibere chi’etahabu, ochibeke ase emego ya igoro y’egesembe keria.
english: Make two gold rings for it and fasten them to two corners of the breastpiece.

ekegusii: Make two gold rings for the altar below the molding-- two on opposite sides-- to hold the poles used to carry it.
english: Okore chibonyi ibere chie chitahabu ochibeke inse y’omong’ororia chinsemo ibere, na emiaro esoigwe imeo, erinde egesasimero kenyare kobogorerigwa.

ekegusii: Naende okore chibonyi chinde ibere chie chitahabu, ochibwateranie ase ebitwanga biria bibere bi’amareko bi’egesibao bire bosio, ang’e nomobarero, igoro y’orokini rw’egesibao.
english: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod.

ekegusii: Otogokie amatuko ang’ana buna ayio twachandegete, na emiaka eng’ana buna eria twanyorete amabe.
english: Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.

ekegusii: Inwe karie chiira ase Omonene, Nyasae oino, na mochiikeranie. Abanto bonsi bamoetanaine, tiga bamorentere ebiegwa, ere oria ogwenerete koirokwa.
english: Make vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them; let all the neighboring lands bring gifts to the One to be feared.

ekegusii: Mbarerie inche omosomba oo obosio bwao, na onyorokererie emeroberio yao echikire.
english: Make your face shine upon your servant and teach me your decrees.

ekegusii: Renda engaki yaino, ekiagera amatuko aya namabe.
english: making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil.

ekegusii: Makiri akanyuomeria Hupimu omokungu, boigo akanyuomeria Supimu omokungu. Omoiseke omwabo nigo arenge korokwa Maaka. Omwana omomura o kabere o Manase nigo arenge korokwa Selofehadi. Selofehadi nigo abwate abana abaiseke boka.
english: Makir took a wife from among the Huppites and Shuppites. His sister's name was Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, who had only daughters.

ekegusii: Maaka, moka Makiri, akaibora omwana omomura, akamoroka Peresi; na momura omwabo Peresi akarokwa Seresi. Abana abamura babere ba Peresi nabwo Ulamu na Rakemu.
english: Makir's wife Maacah gave birth to a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.

ekegusii: chigasoa ase obwato amo na Nuhu ibere ibere, chinsacha ne chinkungu, buna Nyasae achigete Nuhu.
english: male and female, came to Noah and entered the ark, as God had commanded Noah.

ekegusii: Malikia, mosinto o Harimu, na Hasubu, mosinto o Pahati-Moabu, bakaagacha ensemo ende; boigo bakaagacha Omorobiri bw’Eriko.
english: Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.

ekegusii: Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
english: na Malikiramu, Pedaya na Senasari, Yekamia na Hosama, na Nedabia.

ekegusii: Malluch, Harim and Baanah.
english: Maluku, na Harimu, na Baana.

ekegusii: “Mwanyabanto tamanyeti rigori ri’obong’aini; borobwo tibori konyorekana ase ense emenyire nabare moyo.
english: Man does not comprehend its worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living.

ekegusii: Amaene, mwanyabanto nigo agotaara ore buna omogwekano okorora ase okorota; nigo agwechanda bosa; asangereria enibo, korende tamanyeti gose ning’o orache koyeria.
english: Man is a mere phantom as he goes to and fro: He bustles about, but only in vain; he heaps up wealth, not knowing who will get it.

ekegusii: Omonto nigo are buna omooki, amatuko aye nigo anga buna omorengari ogoeta.
english: Man is like a breath; his days are like a fleeting shadow.

ekegusii: Abanto nigo bagotongia chitaya ime aaria, basiria omosunte; erio baba bakoriga‐rigia amagena ase ebinunchi bire ase omosunte ekerima.
english: Man puts an end to the darkness; he searches the farthest recesses for ore in the blackest darkness.

ekegusii: Manase akarara ase chisokoro chiaye chiararete, agatindekwa ase omogondo bw’enyomba yaye oria orenge o Usa; na Amoni, omwana oye omomura, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried in his palace garden, the garden of Uzza. And Amon his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Manase akarara ase chisokoro chiaye chiararete, na abanto bakamotindeka ime ase enyomba yaye. Amoni, omomura oye, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried in his palace. And Amon his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Manase nigo arenge nemiaka ikomi na ebere, ekero achagete kogamba; akagamba emiaka emerongo etano, na etano, agwo Yerusalemu.
english: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years.

ekegusii: Manase nigo arenge nemiaka ikomi na ebere, ekero achagete kogamba, na akagamba emiaka emerongo etano, na etano, agwo Yerusalemu. Ng’ina nigo arenge korokwa Hebisiba.
english: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years. His mother's name was Hephzibah.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Manase mbarie aba Efraimu, na aba Efraimu mbarie aba Manase, na abwo amo mbaonchokere Abayuda. Ase engencho y’ayio Omonene taratiga endamwamu yaye; nigo agendererete korambora okoboko kwaye kobaa egesusuro.
english: Manasseh will feed on Ephraim, and Ephraim on Manasseh; together they will turn against Judah. Yet for all this, his anger is not turned away, his hand is still upraised.

ekegusii: Ase igo abanto ba Manase bakaegwa chinsemo ikomi, amo nense eria ya Gileadi, na Basani, ng’umbu ya Yorodan,
english: Manasseh's share consisted of ten tracts of land besides Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan,

ekegusii: Manoa akaimoka, agatunyana mokaye. Erio agacha ase omonto oria, akamoboria, “Inee! Naye omonto oria okwana nomorugi one?” Omomalaika oria akamoiraneria, “Ee, ninche.”
english: Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he said, "Are you the one who talked to my wife?" "I am," he said.

ekegusii: Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "We would like you to stay until we prepare a young goat for you."
english: Manoa agatebia omomalaika oria, “Koranche twagotangire, obeere aa, tokonyenyere emanwa y’embori, tokoyeroiserie orie.”

ekegusii: Omonto nigo abareire amatuko aye, na omobaro bw’emetienyi yaye naye kwayochikire, naende kwamobekeire chimbebe atanyare goetania.
english: Man's days are determined; you have decreed the number of his months and have set limits he cannot exceed.

ekegusii: Amang’ana akonyora ching’iti naro ayio akobanyora mwanyabanto; buna ching’iti chigokwa, naboigo na mwanyabanto bagokwa. Omoika noyomo ore ase ching’iti na ase mwanyabanto; mwanyabanto tabueti ching’iti kende. Amang’ana onsi mbosa.
english: Man's fate is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath; man has no advantage over the animal. Everything is meaningless.

ekegusii: “Mwanyabanto nigo agokunya egetare ekiomo pa, erio osensema ebitunwa korwa inse obionchorana.
english: Man's hand assaults the flinty rock and lays bare the roots of the mountains.

ekegusii: Abanto abange nigo bakweraria ng’a nabaya bare, korende ning’o oranyare konyora omonto omwegenwa bori?
english: Many a man claims to have unfailing love, but a faithful man who can find?

ekegusii: Nkabasusura ebiro ebinge ase chisinagogi chionsi, naende mbabetereria korama, nkababwaterwa endamwamu enene mono, nkabatunya na kobachanda goika emechie y’ense engeni.
english: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. In my obsession against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

ekegusii: Mbare abanto abange bagokwana: “Naki yare koba buya onye ntwanyora ayare amaya.” Aye Omonene, tiga omobaso bw’obosio bwao otomorekere.
english: Many are asking, "Who can show us any good?" Let the light of your face shine upon us, O LORD.

ekegusii: Abange nigo bagokwana igoro yane, bateba: Nyasae tancheti komotooria.
english: Many are saying of me, "God will not deliver him." Selah

ekegusii: Abagonchanda na abare ababisa baane nigo bare abange, korende tinkogobera korwa ase oborori bwao.
english: Many are the foes who persecute me, but I have not turned from your statutes.

ekegusii: Emeroberio emenge nere ase enkoro y’omonto, korende nonya naboigo emeroberio y’Omonene nero eratenene.
english: Many are the plans in a man's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that prevails.

ekegusii: Omokungu oyio oiyeirie abanto abange, ee, oitire omoganda omonene.
english: Many are the victims she has brought down; her slain are a mighty throng.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nare namaakwa amange, korende oyomosemeretie Omonene, Omonene nigo amoetananeretie nobwanchani botari koera.
english: Many are the woes of the wicked, but the LORD's unfailing love surrounds the man who trusts in him.

ekegusii: Ababisa baane nigo bare abagima, naende bare ne chinguru, abwo bangechete bosa nabange bare.
english: Many are those who are my vigorous enemies; those who hate me without reason are numerous.

ekegusii: Abanto abange bakarentera Omonene ebiegwa agwo Yerusalemu, bakarentera na Hezekia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, ebinto bie rigori rinene. Korwa ase engaki eria na kogenderera Hezekia akaba okoegwa amasikani amanene nabanto b’ebisaku bionsi.
english: Many brought offerings to Jerusalem for the LORD and valuable gifts for Hezekiah king of Judah. From then on he was highly regarded by all the nations.

ekegusii: Chieri chinyinge nching’etanaine, ee, chieri chiria chia Basani chire ne chinguru nigo ching’etanaine.
english: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.

ekegusii: Abanto abange nigo bakorigia ogwancherwa korwa ase abanene b’obogambi, na abange nigo bakoba abasani b’omonto okorua ebiegwa nomoyo omorabu.
english: Many curry favor with a ruler, and everyone is the friend of a man who gives gifts.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’amatuko amange gaetire Omonene agantebia, “Imoka ogende goika Eufarati, orusie orokini roria nagochigete ng’a orobise aroro, ororente aa.”
english: Many days later the LORD said to me, "Go now to Perath and get the belt I told you to hide there."

ekegusii: Naki abang’ainereria abange basokire gochia ase ense, abatari koorokia Yeso Kristo ng’a ochire ase omobere. Oyore buna abwo, nere oria omong’ainereria, naende nomobisa o Kristo.
english: Many deceivers, who do not acknowledge Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh, have gone out into the world. Any such person is the deceiver and the antichrist.

ekegusii: Abanto abange beruete korika ebirage bi’amang’ana aria aikeranetigwe egati yaito.
english: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku ebinge mbabe bakogendao bagoteba: “Inchuo totiire gochia ase egetunwa ki’Omonene, gochia ase enyomba ya Nyasae o Yakobo, erinde atworokererie chinchera chiaye, na intwe tochibwatie.” Amachiko narue Sayoni, ne ring’ana ri’Omonene ndiiche korwa Yerusalemu.
english: Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, so that we may walk in his paths." The law will go out from Zion, the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Abanto abange korwa asebare bakeegena amo nabakungu Abagiriki abaare abasike, na abasacha batai bake.
english: Many of the Jews believed, as did also a number of prominent Greek women and many Greek men.

ekegusii: Nabo amariko ayio abange b’Abayahudi mbayasomete, ekiagera aase aria Yeso abamberetwe nigo arenge ang’e nomochie; naro nigo arigetwe ase Ekeibirania, na Ekerumi, na Ekegiriki.
english: Many of the Jews read this sign, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and the sign was written in Aramaic, Latin and Greek.

ekegusii: Naonchore abange b’Abaisraeli gocha ase Omonene, Nyasae obo.
english: Many of the people of Israel will he bring back to the Lord their God.

ekegusii: Naende ase omochie oria Abasamaria abange bakamwegena ase engencho y’oborori bw’omokungu oria ekero abatebetie ng’a, “Ontebirie amang’ana onsi aya nakorire.”
english: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the woman's testimony, "He told me everything I ever did."

ekegusii: Abange babo bakabora, “Nigo abwatire nekerecha, naende nigo are ebarimo; nase ki mokomotegerera?”
english: Many of them said, "He is demon-possessed and raving mad. Why listen to him?"

ekegusii: Abanto abange mbagochwe na kogwa, mbasenyentwe, mbategwe na kobwatwa.”
english: Many of them will stumble; they will fall and be broken, they will be snared and captured."

ekegusii: Many of those who believed now came and openly confessed their evil deeds.
english: Abange babo, abachagete kwegena, bagacha, bakaorokia chingencho chiabo chimbe baare gokora.

ekegusii: Na omoganda omonene mono bw’abanto b’ebisaku ao ao bakagenda komo, bakairana ching’ondi, ne chiombe, ne chitugo chinde chinyinge mono.
english: Many other people went up with them, as well as large droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.

ekegusii: Abanto abange bakaara chianga chiabo inchera; abande bakanacha chinsagia chi’emete na gochiaara inchera.
english: Many people spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut in the fields.

ekegusii: Many people, because they had heard that he had given this miraculous sign, went out to meet him.
english: Ekio nakio kiagerete omoganda okagenda komorotota, ekiagera baigwete ng’a okorire egekone eke.

ekegusii: Ee, abanto abange mbagendeo batebanie: “Inchuo, totiire gochia ase egetunwa ki’Omonene, togende ase enyomba ya Nyasae o Yakobo, erinde atworokererie chinchera chiaye, na intwe tonyare kobwatia oboeto bwaye.” Amachiko ’Omonene nasoke korwa Sayoni, ne ring’ana riaye ndirue Yerusalemu.
english: Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, so that we may walk in his paths." The law will go out from Zion, the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Abanto abange bakamotogonyera, bakamotebia ng’a anyare gokira, korende akamenta goaka eriogi kobua, ogoteba “Omwana o Daudi, indorera amabera!”
english: Many rebuked him and told him to be quiet, but he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"

ekegusii: Abanto abange nigo bakorigia ogwancherwa gokorwa ase omogambi, korende kera omonto nigo akonyora oboronge korwa ase Omonene.
english: Many seek an audience with a ruler, but it is from the LORD that man gets justice.

ekegusii: Abarisia abange basaririe omogondo one bw’emesabibu, batiringeire inse omogondo one. Bakorire omogondo one oyorenge kongokia ogwekanire buna erooro ere bosa.
english: Many shepherds will ruin my vineyard and trample down my field; they will turn my pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.

ekegusii: ekiagera abange bakamotebera oborimo, na oborori bwabo tibwabwatana.
english: Many testified falsely against him, but their statements did not agree.

ekegusii: Ase chingaki chinyinge Omonene nigo arenge kobatooria, korende ase ogosemania kwabo bagachora gosaria asare: ase igo bakaba bagochandeka mono ase engencho y’ebibe biabo.
english: Many times he delivered them, but they were bent on rebellion and they wasted away in their sin.

ekegusii: Amache are amange mono takonyara gokendia obwanchani, gose chindooche tichikonyara koboiranana. Omonto naisa korua obotenenku bwonsi bw’enyomba yaye konyora obwanchani, oyio nigo arachaywe.
english: Many waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot wash it away. If one were to give all the wealth of his house for love, it would be utterly scorned.

ekegusii: Abanto abange mbacheneke na koraba, babe basibekire, korende abakori amabe mbagenderere gokora amabe, onde tagotoka ase abakori amabe orabe nokomanya, korende abare nobong’aini mbamanye.
english: Many will be purified, made spotless and refined, but the wicked will continue to be wicked. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.

ekegusii: ekiagera abange nabache ase erieta riane, babore: Inche ninche ere; naraae abange na kobasiria.
english: Many will come in my name, claiming, 'I am he,' and will deceive many.

ekegusii: Abange nabatunyane ogokora kwabo kw’obonyaka, na ase engencho y’abwo enchera y’ekeene neramwe.
english: Many will follow their shameful ways and will bring the way of truth into disrepute.

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria nabange barantebie: Omonene, Omonene, titware kobana ase erieta riao, na ase erieta riao goseria ebirecha, na ase erieta riao gokora ebikone bie chinguru ebinge?
english: Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?'

ekegusii: Mbarengeo boigo abakungu abange, barigereretie korwa are, abatunyanete Yeso korwa Galili, bakomokorera.
english: Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to care for his needs.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, Nyasae one, ogokora kwao na ebirengererio biao asetore nebi’ogokumia; onde tari orareng’anigwe naye. Ninganetie koraria ayio na koyakwana, korende namange mono, takobareka.
english: Many, O LORD my God, are the wonders you have done. The things you planned for us no one can recount to you; were I to speak and tell of them, they would be too many to declare.

ekegusii: Naende yarengeo Maoni, na Karimeli, na Sifu, na Yuta,
english: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

ekegusii: Aye amo nabarwani bao goika motaare moetanane omochie oyio ara rimo kera rituko ase engaki y’amatuko atano na rimo.
english: March around the city once with all the armed men. Do this for six days.

ekegusii: Igwa, inche Paulo nkobatebia nde inwe, ng’a moise kwarokigwa, rirorio Kristo takoba nengencho ende asemore.
english: Mark my words! I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.

ekegusii: Bworokie enchera ase omoro oraetere, eyemo gochia ase Raba ase ense y’Abaamoni, na eyende ase Yerusalemu, omochie ogiteire chindwaki, ase ense y’Abayuda.
english: Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites and another against Judah and fortified Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Okonyuomana gosikwe nabanto bonsi, na ebirarero bibe bitari nobosooku, naki abanyaka na abatomani Nyasae nabagambie ekina.
english: Marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept pure, for God will judge the adulterer and all the sexually immoral.

ekegusii: Monyuome abakungu babaiborere abana, abamura na abaiseke. Nyuomeria abamura baino abakungu, na abaiseke baino mobasokie, erinde baibore abana, abamura na abaiseke. Momentekane mobuche agwo, gose omobaro oino tobaisa gokea.
english: Marry and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Increase in number there; do not decrease.

ekegusii: Marshal your troops, O city of troops, for a siege is laid against us. They will strike Israel's ruler on the cheek with a rod.
english: Aye Omochie bw’emeganda, sangereria emeganda yao y’esegi. Ababisa banaaririe omochie oito bayorwanie esegi. Barabwo mbaake omogambi bw’Abaisraeli orosea rwaye nenyimbo.

ekegusii: Martha akamotebia, “Namanyire ng’a nache kobokigwa ase okobokigwa rituko ri’omoerio.”
english: Martha answered, "I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day."

ekegusii: Mariamu Magidalena na Mariamu ng’ina Yose bakarigereria aase abegetwe.
english: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid.

ekegusii: Mbarengeo Mariamu Magidalena na Mariamu onde, baikaransete bosio bw’oboina.
english: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there opposite the tomb.

ekegusii: Mariamu Magidalena akagenda, agatebia aborokigwa amang’ana ng’a, “Narorire Omonene”, naende ng’a omotebirie aya.
english: Mary Magdalene went to the disciples with the news: "I have seen the Lord!" And she told them that he had said these things to her.

ekegusii: Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months and then returned home.
english: Mariamu akamenya nere emetienyi etato, akairana sobo.

ekegusii: Mariamu agaichana mono ase ring’ana eri, akarota‐rotia omoyo oye ime, “Ngokwania ki oko?”
english: Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.

ekegusii: Inwe abanene, kae abasomba baino ekere kia boronge, mokomanya ng’a nainwe more n’Omonene igoro.
english: Masters, provide your slaves with what is right and fair, because you know that you also have a Master in heaven.

ekegusii: Matania, mosinto o Mika o Sabudi bw’ororeria rw’Asafu, oyorenge omoraai bw’amatera ase okoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono amo nogosaba; Bakibukia, nere orenge oyo o kabere ase Matania; Abuda, mosinto o Samua o Galali bw’ororeria rwa Yedutuni.
english: Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, the director who led in thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his associates; and Abda son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.

ekegusii: Matania, na Bakibukia, na Obadia, na Mesulamu, na Talimoni, na Akubu, abarendi b’ebiita, nigo barenge korenda ebigachero agwo ase ebiita.
english: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.

ekegusii: Mattaniah, Mattenai and Jaasu.
english: na Matania, Matenai na Yaasu;

ekegusii: Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called the Zealot,
english: na Matayo na Tomas, Yakobo bw’Alufayo, na Simion oyomo bw’Abazelote,

ekegusii: Tiga abamoete ebinto singo bache baire ebinto biaye bionsi; abanto abaao bache basakore ebi bakorerete emeremo emekong’u.
english: May a creditor seize all he has; may strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, abaruoti bonsi b’ense mbagotogie, ekero baraigwe amang’ana akorwa ase omonwa oo;
english: May all the kings of the earth praise you, O LORD, when they hear the words of your mouth.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakogokera emechando yane, tiga basookigwe na batantanigwe; abwo bagwetogia igoro yane, tiga baboigwe obosooku na ogochaywa.
english: May all who gloat over my distress be put to shame and confusion; may all who exalt themselves over me be clothed with shame and disgrace.

ekegusii: Abwo bonsi bagechete Sayoni, tiga basookigwe na koonchorwa gochia nyuma.
english: May all who hate Zion be turned back in shame.

ekegusii: Abwo bonsi barigetie kong’ita, tiga basookigwe na batantanigwe bonsi amo, na abwo baganetie obobe banyore, tiga bairanigwe nyuma barore obosooku.
english: May all who seek to take my life be put to shame and confusion; may all who desire my ruin be turned back in disgrace.

ekegusii: Tiga omosunte na ekiriri ekemwamu biritube. Tiga amare aritube, na kende gionsi egekorenta obomwamu ase rituko kerioboyie.
english: May darkness and deep shadow claim it once more; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm its light.

ekegusii: Na Nyasae Omobui nagosesenie, agokinie, na oroiboro rwao naromente robe omoganda omonene bw’ebisaku.
english: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and increase your numbers until you become a community of peoples.

ekegusii: Nyasae ang’e egesusuro ekenene onye tingoikeraneria Daudi aya Omonene amorierete eira amokore:
english: May God deal with Abner, be it ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD promised him on oath

ekegusii: Ekeene, Nyasae ang’e egesusuro bono na kogenderera onye mambia kobogokia tekonyora naitire na gosiria abanto abasacha bonsi bare amo na Nabali.”
english: May God deal with David, be it ever so severely, if by morning I leave alive one male of all who belong to him!"

ekegusii: Nyasae agareerie Yafeti obomenyo, tiga amenye ase chiema chia Shemu, na Kanani abe omosomba oye.”
english: May God extend the territory of Japheth; may Japheth live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave."

ekegusii: Nyasae akoe ebie riime rikorwa igoro na obonoru bwe riroba, ne rigesa riao ribe eringe, na edivai boigo.
english: May God give you of heaven's dew and of earth's richness-- an abundance of grain and new wine.

ekegusii: Nyasae omonyene omorembe abachene kegima, na inwe abanyene morendwe ase emeika, na emioyo, na emebere, na mobe motari na komocha ekero ki’ogocha kw’Omonene oito Yeso Kristo.
english: May God himself, the God of peace, sanctify you through and through. May your whole spirit, soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ekegusii: Tiga Nyasae, oyo obekire erieta riaye ribeere aroro, aonchore na koiyeria inse omoruoti onde bwensi, gose abanto, barateeme koonchora ogochika oko, gose gosaria enyomba eye ya Nyasae ere Yerusalemu. Inche Dario narure ogochika okwo, tiga koigwerwe kegima.”
english: May God, who has caused his Name to dwell there, overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to change this decree or to destroy this temple in Jerusalem. I Darius have decreed it. Let it be carried out with diligence.

ekegusii: monyare koba ne chinguru ase okomanya amo nabachenu bonsi obogare na obotambe, na gochia igoro, na gochia inse,
english: may have power, together with all the saints, to grasp how wide and long and high and deep is the love of Christ,

ekegusii: Tiga agenderere botambe koba omoruoti ase obosio bwao aye Nyasae; obwanchani bwao bogendererete botambe, na obwegenwa bwao, bimorende,
english: May he be enthroned in God's presence forever; appoint your love and faithfulness to protect him.

ekegusii: Ere nakoe ogosesenigwa kwa Ibrahimu, aye amo nororeria rwao, erinde onyare koira ense eye ore omomenyi bono, eye Nyasae aete Ibrahimu!”
english: May he give you and your descendants the blessing given to Abraham, so that you may take possession of the land where you now live as an alien, the land God gave to Abraham."

ekegusii: Tiga akoe ogokania gw’enkoro yao, na aikeranie emeroberio yao yonsi.
english: May he give you the desire of your heart and make all your plans succeed.

ekegusii: Tiga ainyore okorua kwao gwonsi, anche na kogokera ebing’wanso biao bionsi bi’ogosambwa.
english: May he remember all your sacrifices and accept your burnt offerings. Selah

ekegusii: Ere nagotomere ogokonywa korwa ase obomenyo bwaye obochenu, na akoe chinguru korwa ase Sayoni.
english: May he send you help from the sanctuary and grant you support from Zion.

ekegusii: Ase igo anyare gokong’ia chinkoro chiaino chibe chitari na komocha, ase obochenu ase obosio bwa Nyasae, Tata oito ekero ki’ogocha kw’Omonene oito Yeso Kristo amo nabachenu baye bonsi.
english: May he strengthen your hearts so that you will be blameless and holy in the presence of our God and Father when our Lord Jesus comes with all his holy ones.

ekegusii: korende aonchore chinkoro chiaito gochia asare, tonyare kobwatia chinchera chiaye, na kobwata amachiko aye na emeroberio yaye echikire, na onsi aya achigete chisokoro chiaito.
english: May he turn our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep the commands, decrees and regulations he gave our fathers.

ekegusii: Tiga okomocha kw’ogoiterwa kw’amanyinga aye kobe igoro ya Yoabu, na igoro ase abanto b’eamate yaye: naende enyomba ya Yoabu teborwa omonto ogoiteka amache anga buna chimengere, gose oyore noborwaire bwa ukoma, gose oyo ogwesiirera enyimbo, gose oyo oraitwe nemioro, gose oyore omoremerwa bw’endagera.”
english: May his blood fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house! May Joab's house never be without someone who has a running sore or leprosy or who leans on a crutch or who falls by the sword or who lacks food."

ekegusii: Tiga abana baye batigwe bare chintakana, na omokungu oye atigwe ore omoboraka.
english: May his children be fatherless and his wife a widow.

ekegusii: Abana baye babe bakoombogana na kona‐gosaberera, bagende kona‐korigia endagera aare korwa ase amaturi bamenyete.
english: May his children be wandering beggars; may they be driven from their ruined homes.

ekegusii: Amatuko aye tiga abe amake, na oboteneneri bwaye omoao aboire.
english: May his days be few; may another take his place of leadership.

ekegusii: Tiga ororeria rwaye rosirigwe, na erieta riaye riebwe kegima ase ekiare gia kabere.
english: May his descendants be cut off, their names blotted out from the next generation.

ekegusii: Erieta riaye tiga rigenderere kobao botambe, rikume koreng’ana buna erioba rigendererete kobao. Abanto mbabe bagosesenigwa ime yaye; abanto b’ebisaku bionsi tiga bamoroke oyosesenirie.
english: May his name endure forever; may it continue as long as the sun. All nations will be blessed through him, and they will call him blessed.

ekegusii: Ogwetogia kobe are nainche, otatiga inyetogerie omosalaba bw’Omonene oito Yeso Kristo, ase oro ense yabambirwe asende, na inche ase ense.
english: May I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

ekegusii: Tiga obwegenwa na oboronge bindende, ekiagera naye nsemeretie.
english: May integrity and uprightness protect me, because my hope is in you.

ekegusii: Tiga okoragererigwa okwo kobe buna egetambaa akwambara, naende kobe buna orokini akweboeria botambe.
english: May it be like a cloak wrapped about him, like a belt tied forever around him.

ekegusii: Tiga ebe iga; Kondaborie oyomo obo: Koranche obeke enyongo yao inse, inche inywe amache, na ere karang’iranerie: Ee, kanywe aye, na nimbuuchere chingamia chiao nachirochio; otige oyio abe nere gwachoreire omosomba oo Isaka, na inche erio nimanye ng’a gwakoreire omonene one obuya.”
english: May it be that when I say to a girl, 'Please let down your jar that I may have a drink,' and she says, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too'-- let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master."

ekegusii: Ching’enang’eni chiaye chia ituko ria mambia chibe omosunte; obotuko tiga bochie koganya ng’a bokie, korende tibokia rinde, gose tibobaisa korora ogokiamoka kwa mambia,
english: May its morning stars become dark; may it wait for daylight in vain and not see the first rays of dawn,

ekegusii: Ababisa abwo bakorigia obogima bwane, tiga basookigwe na gosirigwa kegima; abwo bakorigia gonkora bobe, tiga bachaywe na gochecherigwa mono.
english: May my accusers perish in shame; may those who want to harm me be covered with scorn and disgrace.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, tiga okorera kwane goike ase obosio bwao; ing’a obong’aini koreng’ana ne ring’ana riao!
english: May my cry come before you, O LORD; give me understanding according to your word.

ekegusii: Tiga enkoro yane ebe etari na komocha ase emeroberio yao echikire, erinde timbaisa konyora obosooku.
english: May my heart be blameless toward your decrees, that I may not be put to shame.

ekegusii: May my lips overflow with praise, for you teach me your decrees.
english: Nimbe nkona‐kogotogia nebikoba biane, ekiagera aye kwanyorokereirie imanye emeroberio yao echikire.

ekegusii: Omonene one, tobaisa kobara Nabali, omonto oyo omobe, ng’a nomonto ogwenerete. Nere okorokwa Nabali, na engencho y’erieta eri noboriri. Naboigo are omonto omoriri. Bono inche, omosomba oo omokungu, tinaroche abanto aba aye, omonene one, gwatomete.
english: May my lord pay no attention to that wicked man Nabal. He is just like his name-- his name is Fool, and folly goes with him. But as for me, your servant, I did not see the men my master sent.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene agokigwe nebirengererio ebio biane, ekiagera inche nigo ngogete asare.
english: May my meditation be pleasing to him, as I rejoice in the LORD.

ekegusii: Bwanchere ogosaba kwane buna ubani, na amaboko aane aimokereirie igoro oyanchere buna ekeng’wanso kia mogoroba!
english: May my prayer be set before you like incense; may the lifting up of my hands be like the evening sacrifice.

ekegusii: Ogosaba kwane tiga goike ase obosio bwao, tegerera oigwe okorera kwane.
english: May my prayer come before you; turn your ear to my cry.

ekegusii: Tiga ogosaba kwane goike asore; ontoorie koreng’ana ne ring’ana riao!
english: May my supplication come before you; deliver me according to your promise.

ekegusii: Onye tingokoinyora aye Yerusalemu, erinde obe omogoko one omonene mono, rirorio tiga oromeme rwane robwatane namang’ang’ura.
english: May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not consider Jerusalem my highest joy.

ekegusii: Oromeme rwane ndotere ring’ana riao, ekiagera amachiko ao onsi nigo are amaronge.
english: May my tongue sing of your word, for all your commands are righteous.

ekegusii: Aye omonyene onachere ekina gi’okong’a oboronge, amaiso ao nigo akorora ayare ay’ekeene.
english: May my vindication come from you; may your eyes see what is right.

ekegusii: Abanto bagokorere, na ebisaku bigotung’amere. Obe omonene ase abamino, abana ba nyoko bagotung’amere; oyorakoragererie, nere naragererigwe, na oyoragosesenie, nere nasesenigwe!”
english: May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed and those who bless you be blessed."

ekegusii: Monto onde tabaisa koba omuya asare, gose onde taba namabera ase abana baye bare chintakana.
english: May no one extend kindness to him or take pity on his fatherless children.

ekegusii: Bono Omonene oito Yeso Kristo omonyene, na Nyasae Tata oito, oyotwanchete na otoete okoremia gwa kare na kare, na ogosemeria okuya ase obuya bwaye,
english: May our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father, who loved us and by his grace gave us eternal encouragement and good hope,

ekegusii: Ogosirigwa tiga kobanyore mobosokano; oboreba obwo bantegeire tiga bobabwate barabwo abanyene, tiga bagwe imeo abanyene na gosirigwa.
english: may ruin overtake them by surprise-- may the net they hid entangle them, may they fall into the pit, to their ruin.

ekegusii: Omonto oyio, tiga abe buna emechie eria Omonene asiretie atari namabera. Oyio tiga aigwe ebirero bi’obororo mambia, na amariogi’okogoswa mobaso gati,
english: May that man be like the towns the LORD overthrew without pity. May he hear wailing in the morning, a battle cry at noon.

ekegusii: Ee, obotuko boria tiga bogombae; eriogi ri’omogoko tiribaisa koigugwa ase borobwo.
english: May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it.

ekegusii: Tiga abanto abamwenu barore obosooku, ekiagera bankoreire bobe engencho ende etaiyo, korende inche nigo nkona koiranerera amachiko ao.
english: May the arrogant be put to shame for wronging me without cause; but I will meditate on your precepts.

ekegusii: Obosiani bw’Omonene, Nyasae oito, bobe igoro yaito, na emeremo y’amaboko aito oyesesenie asetore, ee, osesenie emeremo y’amaboko aito!
english: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish the work of our hands for us-- yes, establish the work of our hands.

ekegusii: Totiga amagoro ’abaenenu ang’ike ang’e kondwania, gose amaboko ’abakori amabe anserie.
english: May the foot of the proud not come against me, nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.

ekegusii: Tiga obonene bw’Omonene bogenderere kobao kare na kare; Omonene tiga agokere emeremo yaye.
english: May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in his works--

ekegusii: Nyasae o Ibrahimu, Nyasae o Nahori, oyorenge Nyasae o ise obo, agambe ase egati yaito.” Ase igo Yakobo agatiana ase Oyio Isaka ise airogete.
english: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." So Jacob took an oath in the name of the Fear of his father Isaac.

ekegusii: Naboigo Nyasae bw’ogosemerigwa abaichorie nomogoko bwonsi na omorembe ase okwegena, monyare komenta mono ase ogosemeria ase chinguru chi’Omoika Omochenu.
english: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

ekegusii: Bono Nyasae bw’omorembe oyomorentete naende korwa ase amakweri Omonene oito Yeso, oyore omorisia omonene bwe ching’ondi goetera ase amanyinga ’okobwatana gwa kare na kare,
english: May the God of peace, who through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep,

ekegusii: Na Nyasae bw’oboremereria na bw’okoremia abakonye mobe nomoyo oyomo inwe ase inwe ase omogwekano o Kristo Yeso;
english: May the God who gives endurance and encouragement give you a spirit of unity among yourselves as you follow Christ Jesus,

ekegusii: Obuya bw’Omonene Yeso Kristo, na obwanchani bwa Nyasae na okobwatana kw’Omoika Omochenu bibe amo nainwe mwensi.
english: May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

ekegusii: Tiga ekerero ki’abasibire geike ase obosio bwao; tooria abanto abwo banacheirwe ekina bakwe, ekiagera aye nobwate okobua okonene.
english: May the groans of the prisoners come before you; by the strength of your arm preserve those condemned to die.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, egesusuro gi’okomocha kw’ogoitera amanyinga nkebe igoro ase Yoabu, naende kebe igoro ase ororeria rwaye goika kare na kare. Korende ase Daudi, na ororeria rwaye, na enyomba yaye, na ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene, omorembe okorwa ase Omonene nobeo kare na kare.”
english: May the guilt of their blood rest on the head of Joab and his descendants forever. But on David and his descendants, his house and his throne, may there be the LORD's peace forever."

ekegusii: Ebibe bie chisokoro chiaye biinyorwe ase obosio bw’Omonene, na ebibe bia ng’ina tibibaisa gotinyigwa.
english: May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before the LORD; may the sin of his mother never be blotted out.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene anache ekina ase egati yane naye, erio andwanerere na gontooria korwa ase okoboko kwao.”
english: May the LORD be our judge and decide between us. May he consider my cause and uphold it; may he vindicate me by delivering me from your hand."

ekegusii: Omonene agosesenie korwa Sayoni! Erio orore obuya bwa Yerusalemu ase amatuko onsi ore moyo,
english: May the LORD bless you from Zion all the days of your life; may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem,

ekegusii: Omonene okirie emenwa y’abwo bagokwana amang’ana ’okweansia, ne chimeme chi’abwo bagwetogia ase amang’ana ’oboenenu.
english: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and every boastful tongue

ekegusii: Omonene atang’ane chinkoro chiaino, erinde momanye obwanchani bwa Nyasae, na oboremereria bwa Kristo.
english: May the Lord direct your hearts into God's love and Christ's perseverance.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene akoe obong’aini na okomanya, erio ekero orabe gokogambera Abaisraeli obwate amachiko ’Omonene, Nyasae oo.
english: May the LORD give you discretion and understanding when he puts you in command over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.

ekegusii: Omonene abanchere kera oyomo oino anyuomwe naende, na anyore mwaye.” Erio Naomi akabanyunyunta ase okobatiga. Korende barabwo bagachaka korera mono,
english: May the LORD grant that each of you will find rest in the home of another husband." Then she kissed them and they wept aloud

ekegusii: Omonene namwanchere anyore amabera korwa ase Omonene Rituko riria. Aye kwamanyire buya buna are gokora emeremo emenge aaria Efeso.
english: May the Lord grant that he will find mercy from the Lord on that day! You know very well in how many ways he helped me in Ephesus.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene arore oyore nokomocha, ninche gose naye. Omonene anduserie egesiomba, korende okoboko kwane tikogokora bobe.
english: May the LORD judge between you and me. And may the LORD avenge the wrongs you have done to me, but my hand will not touch you.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene abamentekanie, inwe amo ne chinderia chiaino.
english: May the LORD make you increase, both you and your children.

ekegusii: Omonene abakore momenteke na gokina ase ogwanchana inwe ase inwe, na ase ogwancha abanto bonsi, buna intwe tobanchete inwe.
english: May the Lord make your love increase and overflow for each other and for everyone else, just as ours does for you.

ekegusii: Omonene abaorokerie obwanchani bwaye botari koera, na obwegenwa bwaye. Nainche boigo nimbakorere amaya, ekiagera mwakora ring’ana erio.
english: May the LORD now show you kindness and faithfulness, and I too will show you the same favor because you have done this.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oito, abe naintwe buna abete ne chisokoro chiaito; tabaisa gototiga gose gotwanga,
english: May the LORD our God be with us as he was with our fathers; may he never leave us nor forsake us.

ekegusii: Omonene agoakane ase aya gwakorire; ee, Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, oyo gwatameire, erinde orendwe inse ye chimbaba chiaye akoe eng’eria eng’ikeranu.”
english: May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

ekegusii: Omonene abarorere amabera abwo bare ab’enyomba y’Onesiforo, ekiagera ekero ase ekero nigo are gontimokia, gose tare korora obosooku ase engencho y’ebinyuri biane.
english: May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiaino, abamentekanie ara elifu, mobe abange goetania buna more bono, naende abasesenie buna abarierete eira.
english: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times and bless you as he has promised!

ekegusii: Omonene, oria otongete igoro na ense, agosesenie korwa Sayoni!
english: May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.

ekegusii: Tiga abanto b’ebisaku bagoke na gotera nomochengo; ekiagera aye nigo okonachera abanto ebina ase oboronge. Aye naye okoraa ebisaku bire ase ense.
english: May the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you rule the peoples justly and guide the nations of the earth. Selah

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, tiga abanto bagotogie; ee, abanto bonsi tiga bagotogie!
english: May the peoples praise you, O God; may all the peoples praise you.

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, tiga abanto bagotogie, ee, abanto bonsi tiga bagotogie!
english: May the peoples praise you, O God; may all the peoples praise you.

ekegusii: Tiga ogotogigwa okonene kwa Nyasae kobe ase emenwa yabo, na ase amaboko abo babogorie emeyio ya birende ere nobwoge chinsemo ibere,
english: May the praise of God be in their mouths and a double-edged sword in their hands,

ekegusii: Tiga endagera ere ase amasio abo, ebe egesugunia asebare, na oboreba ase abwo bekagete ng’a mbuya bare.
english: May the table set before them become a snare; may it become retribution and a trap.

ekegusii: Obobe bw’obotindi bwakoretwe asende na ase abaminto nabobekwe igoro ya Babeli. Tiga abanto ba Sayoni batebe: Okomocha kw’ogoiterwa kw’amanyinga aito, tiga kobe igoro ase Abakalidayo.”
english: May the violence done to our flesh be upon Babylon," say the inhabitants of Zion. "May our blood be on those who live in Babylonia," says Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, Egetare kiane na Omobooria one, anchera amang’ana aane na ebirengererio bire ase enkoro yane.
english: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.

ekegusii: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.
english: Oukorie amaiso abo: otengechie chibachwa chiabo kogenderera.

ekegusii: Tiga amaiso abo abekwe omosunte tibarora. Obakumbe emegongo yabo botambe!”
english: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever."

ekegusii: Omosunte na oboterere bibe ase enchera bagoetera, na omomalaika bw’Omonene abe okobabwata abasirie.
english: may their path be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.

ekegusii: Tiga omochie obo otigare bosa, monto onde tamenya ase chiema chiabo.
english: May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents.

ekegusii: Ebibe biabo tiga bigenderere kobeera ase obosio bw’Omonene botambe; na barabwo tibabaisa koinyorwa ase ense nonya ng’ake.
english: May their sins always remain before the LORD, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth.

ekegusii: Omorembe obe ase chindwaki chiao ime, na ogosesenigwa kobe ase chinyomba chiao chi’oboruoti.
english: May there be peace within your walls and security within your citadels."

ekegusii: Tiga amarieta abo atinyigwe korwa ase ebuku y’abare moyo, tarikwa amo nay’abanyene oboronge.
english: May they be blotted out of the book of life and not be listed with the righteous.

ekegusii: Barabwo tiga babe buna omoiriro okoirurukigwa nomwaga, na omomalaika bw’Omonene abe okobaiyeria.
english: May they be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them away;

ekegusii: Barabwo tiga babe buna obonyansi bore kerama igoro, bogosusana botarakina;
english: May they be like grass on the roof, which withers before it can grow;

ekegusii: Abanto abwo tiga babe nobosooku na omoichano goika kare na kare; ee, tiga basookigwe na basire kegima.
english: May they ever be ashamed and dismayed; may they perish in disgrace.

ekegusii: mbabe bagotera igoro y’ogokora kwao, aye Omonene, ekiagera obonene bwao nigo bore obonene mono.
english: May they sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.

ekegusii: Tiga Omonene abaakane igo abwo bagonsoera, abwo bagokwana bobe igoro y’obogima bwane.
english: May this be the LORD's payment to my accusers, to those who speak evil of me.

ekegusii: Tiga amache aya akorenta okoragereria kagosoa enda yao, ayekore ebimbe na kogombaa.” Omokungu oria airanerie: Ee, ekeene, amina.
english: May this water that brings a curse enter your body so that your abdomen swells and your thigh wastes away." "'Then the woman is to say, "Amen. So be it."

ekegusii: Boragererigwe nabwo bamanyete koragereria amatuko, abwo baganyete korenta Leviatani eng’iti enene y’okwoboyia.
english: May those who curse days curse that day, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo banchete ng’a ng’egwe oboronge bwane, tiga baake eriogi ri’omogoko na omochengo, bagenderere goteba, “Omonene noyo bw’obonene! Ee, nigo agokirie namaya omosomba oye akonyora!”
english: May those who delight in my vindication shout for joy and gladness; may they always say, "The LORD be exalted, who delights in the well-being of his servant."

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakoirogete mbandore bagoke, ekiagera nsemeretie ring’ana riao.
english: May those who fear you rejoice when they see me, for I have put my hope in your word.

ekegusii: Tiga abanto abwo bakoirogete bache asende. Abwo bamanyete oborori bwao.
english: May those who fear you turn to me, those who understand your statutes.

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae bw’Emeganda, totiga abanto abwo bagosemeretie, bare ime yane, barore obosooku. Aye Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, totiga abanto abwo bagokorigia, bare ime yane, bachaywe.
english: May those who hope in you not be disgraced because of me, O Lord, the LORD Almighty; may those who seek you not be put to shame because of me, O God of Israel.

ekegusii: Abanto bagoeta inchera tibakonyara goteba, “Omonene abasesenie!” Gose goteba, “Nkobasesenia tore inwe ase erieta ri’Omonene!”
english: May those who pass by not say, "The blessing of the LORD be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD."

ekegusii: Abwo bagonsiereria bagoteba, “Kiamonyorire!” Tiga bakirigwe‐kiri ase obosooku bwabo.
english: May those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!" be appalled at their own shame.

ekegusii: Abwo bagonchaya na goteba: “Kiamonyorire!” Tiga bakirigwe‐kiri ase obosooku bwabo.
english: May those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!" turn back because of their shame.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakorigia gosiria obogima bwane, tiga babugwe na gosookigwa. Abwo bagokora emeroberio emebe y’okong’ita, tiga bairanigwe babe nobosooku.
english: May those who seek my life be disgraced and put to shame; may those who plot my ruin be turned back in dismay.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo barigetie gosiria obogima bwane, tiga basookigwe na gotantanigwa, na abwo baganetie ng’a obobe bonyore inche, tiga bairanigwe nyuma na gochaywa.
english: May those who seek my life be put to shame and confusion; may all who desire my ruin be turned back in disgrace.

ekegusii: Mosesenigwe n’Omonene, oria otongete igoro na ense.
english: May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

ekegusii: Obong’aini bwao botogigwe, naye boigo otogigwe, ekiagera rituko ria rero gwantangire ting’itera amanyinga na imbe nokomocha gose kweruseria egesiomba inche omonyene.
english: May you be blessed for your good judgment and for keeping me from bloodshed this day and from avenging myself with my own hands.

ekegusii: Tworokie intwe, abasomba bao, ogokora kwao, na abana baito oborokie obonene bwao.
english: May your deeds be shown to your servants, your splendor to their children.

ekegusii: Tiga amaiso ao abe akorigereria enyomba eye omobaso na obotuko, arigererie aase aiga aye kwarire eira kobeka erieta riao, erinde oigwe ogosaba oko inche omosomba oo ngosaba ndigereretie aase aiga.
english: May your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, this place of which you said you would put your Name there. May you hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.

ekegusii: Tiga amaiso ao arigererie enyomba eye obotuko na omobaso aase aiga aye gwatebete igoro yaye: Erieta riane naribeere aroro. Ase ayio oigwe ogosaba oko inche, omosomba oo, ngosaba ndigereretie aase aiga.
english: May your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, this place of which you said, 'My Name shall be there,' so that you will hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.

ekegusii: Bagokie iso na nyoko, tiga oria okoiborete akogokere.
english: May your father and mother be glad; may she who gave you birth rejoice!

ekegusii: Tiga ensoko yao esesenigwe, naye ogokere omokungu bw’oboke bwao,
english: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth.

ekegusii: Okoboko kwao, tiga kobe ang’e gonkonya, ekiagera nachorire kobwatia amachiko ao.
english: May your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.

ekegusii: Tiga abakuani bao beboyie oboronge, na abanto bao abachenu babe bagoaka amariogi ’omogoko.
english: May your priests be clothed with righteousness; may your saints sing for joy."

ekegusii: Tiga obwanchani bwao bogendererete botambe bondemie, koreng’ana buna kwarire eira asende, inche omosomba oo.
english: May your unfailing love be my comfort, according to your promise to your servant.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, oorokia asende obwanchani bwao bogendererete botambe, naende ontoorie buna kwandierete eira.
english: May your unfailing love come to me, O LORD, your salvation according to your promise;

ekegusii: Omonene, obwanchani bwao botari koera bobe amo naintwe, ekiagera naye togosemeretie.
english: May your unfailing love rest upon us, O LORD, even as we put our hope in you.

ekegusii: na Me‐Yarikoni, na Rakoni, amo nense erochie Yafo.
english: Me Jarkon and Rakkon, with the area facing Joppa.

ekegusii: Nabo Omoyahudi oyomo, ore korokwa Apolo, omobiare bw’Aleksanderia, agaika Efeso. Ere nigo arenge omonto omanyete gokwana buya, naende nigo arenge omonto omanyete amariko buya kegima.
english: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was a learned man, with a thorough knowledge of the Scriptures.

ekegusii: Nabo omoganda omonene bw’Abayahudi bakamanya ng’a ere nao are aria; bagacha, tari ase engencho ya Yeso yoka, korende barore Lazaro, oyio Yeso abogetie korwa ase abakure.
english: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews found out that Jesus was there and came, not only because of him but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

ekegusii: Na rora, omobani agacha ase Ahabu, omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, akamotebia, “Aya naro Omonene agoteba: Inee! Kwarorire omoganda oyo omonene bw’esegi? Rora, ninyobeke ase okoboko kwao ase rituko ria rero; naye nomanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene.”
english: Meanwhile a prophet came to Ahab king of Israel and announced, "This is what the LORD says: 'Do you see this vast army? I will give it into your hand today, and then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

ekegusii: Boazi akagenda agaikaransa ase etureti agwo ase egeita ki’omochie. Ekaba ng’a omonto oria omonyamwando bw’Elimeleki ore ang’e kobua Boazi, oria Boazi akwanete igoro yaye, ngoeta arenge. Boazi akamorangeria, akamotebia, “Oyominto, gobera gocha aa, oikaranse!” Omonto oria akagobera, agaikaransa.
english: Meanwhile Boaz went up to the town gate and sat there. When the kinsman-redeemer he had mentioned came along, Boaz said, "Come over here, my friend, and sit down." So he went over and sat down.

ekegusii: Meanwhile his disciples urged him, "Rabbi, eat something."
english: Agwo ekero bataracha, aborokigwa bakamosorora bakabora, “Rabii, ragera?”

ekegusii: Nere Yeso agatenena ase gavuna; na gavuna akamoboria, “Naye Omoruoti bw’Abayahudi?” Yeso akamotebia, “Naboigo. Aye gwatebire.”
english: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" "Yes, it is as you say," Jesus replied.

ekegusii: Yoabu akarwania Raba bw’Abaamoni, akaira ensemo y’omochie eyarenge y’omoruoti.
english: Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal citadel.

ekegusii: Yuda akaa omosani oye Omoadulamu emanwa egoree airere omokungu oria, erinde ere airanie ebinto biria amoete bibe intenenera, korende tamonyora.
english: Meanwhile Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite in order to get his pledge back from the woman, but he did not find her.

ekegusii: Abarwani esegi baria Amasia atancherete bagende nabarabwo korwana esegi, bakarwania emechie y’Abayuda, gochakera Samaria goikeera Beti‐Horoni, bagaita abanto chilifu isato (3,000), bagasakora ebinto ebinge.
english: Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had sent back and had not allowed to take part in the war raided Judean towns from Samaria to Beth Horon. They killed three thousand people and carried off great quantities of plunder.

ekegusii: Naki intwe ase eye iga togwechanda, ntore namaiga koboyigwa obomenyo bwaito bokorwa igoro.
english: Meanwhile we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,

ekegusii: Erio Abimeleki akarua Gerari, amo n’Ahusati, omosemia oye ase obogambi, na Pikoli, oria omochiki omonene bw’abarwani baye, bagachiera Isaka.
english: Meanwhile, Abimelech had come to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his personal adviser and Phicol the commander of his forces.

ekegusii: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Ish-Bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim.
english: Bono Abineri, mosinto o Neri, orenge omotang’ani bw’abarwani ba Saulo. Ere konya oirire Isi‐Boseti, mosinto o Saulo, gochia Mahanaimu,

ekegusii: Abisalomu na abanto abwo bonsi b’Abaisraeli bagaika Yerusalemu, na Ahitofeli nigo arenge amo nere.
english: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

ekegusii: Bono Abisalomu konya otamire. Omomura omorendi orenge otengerete agachia korigereria, akarora abanto abange mono bagotirimboka korwa ekegoro ensemo, magega yaye.
english: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. Now the man standing watch looked up and saw many people on the road west of him, coming down the side of the hill. The watchman went and told the king, "I see men in the direction of Horonaim, on the side of the hill."

ekegusii: Na abanto bonsi nigo barenge komoreera, bakweng’ereria, korende Yeso akabora, “Timoreera, ekiagera takweti, korende nigo araire.”
english: Meanwhile, all the people were wailing and mourning for her. "Stop wailing," Jesus said. "She is not dead but asleep."

ekegusii: Erio Horamu, omoruoti o Geseri, agatiira gokonya Lakisi, korende Yoshua akamoita ere amo nabarwani baye; onde tatigarete ore moyo.
english: Meanwhile, Horam king of Gezer had come up to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army-- until no survivors were left.

ekegusii: Korende Saulo akamenta kobagosa na korengereria goita aborokigwa b’Omonene. Akagenda ase omokuani omonene,
english: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the Lord's disciples. He went to the high priest

ekegusii: Erio omokuani omonene akaboria Yeso amang’ana igoro y’aborokigwa baye, na amang’ana ’okworokereria kwaye.
english: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.

ekegusii: Na Abamidiani baria bakamoonia aaria Misiri ase Potifari, omoteneneri bw’enka ya Farao na omotang’ani bw’abarendi baye bande.
english: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the captain of the guard.

ekegusii: Abasomba b’omoruoti bw’Abasiiria bakamotebia, “Chinyasae chiabo nigo chire chinyasae chi’ebitunwa, na ase ayio nigo chiaba ne chinguru gotobua; korende togende torwane nabanto abwo ase ense omweya, ekeene, goika tobe ne chinguru kobabua.
english: Meanwhile, the officials of the king of Aram advised him, "Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they were too strong for us. But if we fight them on the plains, surely we will be stronger than they.

ekegusii: Erio Abayahudi bagateba, “Chinguru chi’abakobogoria chigurube chiorobire, na amaoomo namange mono ase okogokomora, goika twasinyirwe gokora emeremo y’okoagacha orwaki.”
english: Meanwhile, the people in Judah said, "The strength of the laborers is giving out, and there is so much rubble that we cannot rebuild the wall."

ekegusii: Na abanto baria baganyete Zakaria, bagakumia ase ogotebana kwaye aroro Hekalu ime.
english: Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he stayed so long in the temple.

ekegusii: Omofilisti oria agacha bosio, akamoika Daudi ang’e, na omobogoreria bw’enguba yaye omotang’aine.
english: Meanwhile, the Philistine, with his shield bearer in front of him, kept coming closer to David.

ekegusii: Abayahudi bande abarenge ase chingongo chinde chi’obogambi obwo bagasangerereka amo ase okoegera obogima bwabo, ase okwenyorera obotoereru na gwetooria korwa ase ababisa babo. Bagaita abanto chilifu emerongo etano na ebere na isano (75,000), korende tibakuneti ebinto biabo kobisakora.
english: Meanwhile, the remainder of the Jews who were in the king's provinces also assembled to protect themselves and get relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of them but did not lay their hands on the plunder.

ekegusii: Engaki enke egaeta, na amare akamwamia igoro, na omwaga okagusa; embura egatwa enyinge mono. Ahabu akariina egari yaye, akagenda Yesireeli.
english: Meanwhile, the sky grew black with clouds, the wind rose, a heavy rain came on and Ahab rode off to Jezreel.

ekegusii: Ekero ekio omosangererekano bw’abanto chilifu chinyinge bagachia gosangerereka goika bagatachana. Yeso agachaka gotebia aborokigwa baye ritang’ani, “Mwerende nememera y’Abafarisai, engencho yaye nobong’ainereria.
english: Meanwhile, when a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling on one another, Jesus began to speak first to his disciples, saying: "Be on your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

ekegusii: Omonto otari na mechando ende, nigo agochaya emechando, nigo are ang’e gotachera inse abwo batererigwe.
english: Men at ease have contempt for misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, mwanyabanto bakaria endagera y’abamalaika; Omonene akabatomera endagera enyinge mono.
english: Men ate the bread of angels; he sent them all the food they could eat.

ekegusii: Abanto tibari gochaya omoibi onye ore koiba endagera ekiagera are nenchara.
english: Men do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger when he is starving.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Turo, abamenyete ase omochie oria, nigo barenge korenta chinswe, na ebinto binde bionsi, na kobiooneria Abayuda na abanto ba Yerusalemu, ase rituko ri’Esabato.
english: Men from Tyre who lived in Jerusalem were bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them in Jerusalem on the Sabbath to the people of Judah.

ekegusii: “Abanto nigo bagotigeria chimbebe, baira amaicho e chitugo nechinguru, bachia koyarisia aba ayabo.
english: Men move boundary stones; they pasture flocks they have stolen.

ekegusii: Abanto bakarwa ase chinse chionsi, bagacha koigwa obong’aini bwa Sulemani, na abaruoti bonsi b’ense bagatoma abanto bagachia komoigwa.
english: Men of all nations came to listen to Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the world, who had heard of his wisdom.

ekegusii: Abarwani esegi b’Ariwadi, amo nabarwani bao b’esegi, bakarenda chindwaki chiao ase chinsemo chionsi, na abanto ba Gamadi nabwo bateneine ase emerobiri yao y’ogotengerera. Barabwo bagasunga ching’aya chiabo ase chinyasi chiao chinsemo chionsi; boigo bagakora oboseera bwao bokaba oboikeranu.
english: Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls on every side; men of Gammad were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls; they brought your beauty to perfection.

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abaaseri: abanto abakong’u baisanerete ase okorwana esegi, chilifu emerongo ene (40,000).
english: men of Asher, experienced soldiers prepared for battle-- 40,000;

ekegusii: Ababenjamin, abanto b’eamate ya Saulo, nigo barenge chilifu isato (3,000), nonya nase ekero ekio abange mono kobua b’abwo bagendererete kobwatana nenyomba ya Saulo.
english: men of Benjamin, Saul's kinsmen-- 3,000, most of whom had remained loyal to Saul's house until then;

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abadani: abanto baisanerete ase okorwana esegi, chilifu emerongo ebere na isano na isato, na amagana atano na rimo (28,600).
english: men of Dan, ready for battle-- 28,600;

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abaefraimu: chilifu emerongo ebere, na amagana atano na atato (20,800), abanto chituoni ase esegi bamanyekanete ase chiamate chiabo.
english: men of Ephraim, brave warriors, famous in their own clans-- 20,800;

ekegusii: Abanto b’egesaku ekeng’ese kia Manase: chilifu ikomi na isano na isato (18,000), baria batoretwe amarieta abo bache kobeka Daudi abe omoruoti.
english: men of half the tribe of Manasseh, designated by name to come and make David king-- 18,000;

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abaisakaru: abanto abang’aini abamanyi ebimanyererio bie chingaki, bamanyete egento Abaisraeli bagwenerete gokora, abateneneri amagana abere (200), amo nabamwabo abarenge inse ase obochiki bwabo.
english: men of Issachar, who understood the times and knew what Israel should do-- 200 chiefs, with all their relatives under their command;

ekegusii: Abayuda ababogoretie chinguba na amatimo nigo barenge chilifu isano nemo, na amagana atano na atato (6,800), baisanerete ase okorwana esegi.
english: men of Judah, carrying shield and spear-- 6,800 armed for battle;

ekegusii: Abalawi nigo barenge chilifu inye, na amagana atano na rimo (4,600),
english: men of Levi-- 4,600,

ekegusii: Korwa Abanafutali: abachiki elifu eyemo (1,000), amo nabanto chilifu emerongo etato na isano na ibere (37,000), babwate chinguba na amatimo.
english: men of Naphtali-- 1,000 officers, together with 37,000 men carrying shields and spears;

ekegusii: Nimbeere aare korwa ase abwo bare ne chinkoro chi’obokorekanu, ring’ana rinde rionsi ri’obobe ribe aare nainche.
english: Men of perverse heart shall be far from me; I will have nothing to do with evil.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Sidoni na ab’Ariwadi nabwo barenge bagosukia amaato ao nemegango. Aye Turo, abanto abang’aini nigo bamenyete ime yao, barabwo nigo barenge abagendia be chimeeri chiao.
english: Men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen; your skilled men, O Tyre, were aboard as your seamen.

ekegusii: Abasimeoni nigo barenge chilifu isano na ibere, ne rigana erimo (7,100), abanto chituoni abakong’u ase esegi.
english: men of Simeon, warriors ready for battle-- 7,100;

ekegusii: Abanto bamenyete bosongo mbakumie igoro ye rituko ri’ogosirigwa kwaye, na abamenyete moocha mbaondokigwe namang’ana ayio.
english: Men of the west are appalled at his fate; men of the east are seized with horror.

ekegusii: Korwa ase Abasabuloni: abarwani abakong’u baare nomoyo oyomo, baisanerete ase okorwana esegi, babwate ebirwanero biisaine, abanto chilifu emerongo etano (50,000).
english: men of Zebulun, experienced soldiers prepared for battle with every type of weapon, to help David with undivided loyalty-- 50,000;

ekegusii: Abanto nigo banyasameretie emenwa yabo, bang’akire chindoe ase chinsea, bakondama; nigo bagosangererekana amo ng’a bankore bobe.
english: Men open their mouths to jeer at me; they strike my cheek in scorn and unite together against me.

ekegusii: Ababisa baito nigo batoboerete, titwarenge konyara gotaara ase chinchera chiaito. Engaki yaito nigo ere ang’e koera; amatuko aito abarirwe; ee, omoerio oito oikire.
english: Men stalked us at every step, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near, our days were numbered, for our end had come.

ekegusii: Naki abanto nigo bagotiana ase oyore omonene kobabua, na omoerio bw’okoamererania nemuma egokoora.
english: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and the oath confirms what is said and puts an end to all argument.

ekegusii: abanto ababekire obogima bwabo ase engencho y’erieta ri’Omonene oito Yeso Kristo.
english: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ekegusii: Abwo baramenye inse ase ekiriri kiabo bairane, bagenderere koreereta buna ebimeri bia mogondo mbasiche, na obonene bwabo bobe buna obw’emesabibu ya Lebanoni.
english: Men will dwell again in his shade. He will flourish like the grain. He will blossom like a vine, and his fame will be like the wine from Lebanon.

ekegusii: Abanto mbakwe ekeondogo na okoiroka kobaganyete ayagochera ense, ekiagera chinguru chia igoro nachitengechigwe.
english: Men will faint from terror, apprehensive of what is coming on the world, for the heavenly bodies will be shaken.

ekegusii: Abanto mbasoe ase amakuruma ’ebitare, na ase chingoro chire ase riroba; mbatame korwa ase okoirokia kw’Omonene, na korwa ase obonene bwaye bore obonene, ekero araimoke kwoboyia ense.
english: Men will flee to caves in the rocks and to holes in the ground from dread of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.

ekegusii: Abanto mbache agwo babwate amata ne chinsara, ekiagera orogongo orwo rwonsi rwamerire amageri na amagwa.
english: Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the land will be covered with briers and thorns.

ekegusii: Abanto mbatayaye korwa ase enyancha goika ase enyancha ende, na korwa sugusu goika moocha; mbaminyoke gochia aaria na aaria, babe bakorigia ring’ana ri’Omonene, korende tibakorinyora.
english: Men will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, searching for the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.

ekegusii: Naende nababatebie: Rora aaria, gose: Rora aiga! Timogenda, gose timobatunyana.
english: Men will tell you, 'There he is!' or 'Here he is!' Do not go running off after them.

ekegusii: Abanto bagasasima enchoka eria, ekiagera yaete eng’iti eria okobua. Naende bagasasima eng’iti eria bagoteba, “Ning’o oreng’aine neng’iti eye? Ning’o oranyare koyerwania?”
english: Men worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast, and they also worshiped the beast and asked, "Who is like the beast? Who can make war against him?"

ekegusii: Menahemu akarusia chibesa echio buna ebango korwa ase Abaisraeli abarenge abanda; kera oyomo obo akarua chisekeli chie chifeta emerongo etano. Chibesa echi akaa omoruoti bw’Abaasuri. Ase ayio omoruoti bw’Abaasuri akairana tamenya ase ense eria.
english: Menahem exacted this money from Israel. Every wealthy man had to contribute fifty shekels of silver to be given to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria withdrew and stayed in the land no longer.

ekegusii: Menahemu akarara ase chisokoro chiaye chiararete, na Pekahia, omwana oye omomura, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: Menahem rested with his fathers. And Pekahiah his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Meonotai akaibora Ofura. Seraya akaibora Yoabu ise Abageharasimu. Barabwo nigo barogetwe igo, ekiagera barenge abaroisia ebinto.
english: Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, the father of Ge Harashim. It was called this because its people were craftsmen.

ekegusii: Mefiboseti agatung’ama inse naende, akabora, “Inche inde buna esese ekwete. Ninki ing’isaine orankorere amaya buna ayio?”
english: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?"

ekegusii: Mefiboseti nabwate omwana omomura ore korokwa Mika. Abanto bonsi abarenge o Siba bakaba abasomba ba Mefiboseti.
english: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all the members of Ziba's household were servants of Mephibosheth.

ekegusii: Mefiboseti akamoiraneria, “Omoruoti, tiga Siba ayaire onsi, inche naisanekire ng’a aye, omonene one, kwairanire inka buya.”
english: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has arrived home safely."

ekegusii: Erio Mefiboseti, omochokoro o Saulo, agatirimboka gochia korotota omoruoti. Korwa ekero keria omoruoti aruete Yerusalemu, Mefiboseti konya tana gwesibia amagoro aye, gose konacha chinderu, gose gosibia chianga chiaye, goika rituko riria omoruoti airanete nomorembe.
english: Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.

ekegusii: Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
english: na Merayoti omomura oye, na Amaria omomura oye, na Ahitubu omomura oye,

ekegusii: Meraioth the father of Amariah, Amariah the father of Ahitub,
english: Merayoti akaibora Amaria, na Amaria akaibora Ahitubu;

ekegusii: Amabera, na omorembe, na obwanchani, bimenteke asemore.
english: Mercy, peace and love be yours in abundance.

ekegusii: Oyobwatetie abwo koagacha, i’Meremoti, mosinto o Uria o Hakosi. Oyobwatetie ere koagacha, i’Mesulamu, mosinto o Berekia o Meshesabeli. Oyo obwatetie ere n’Zadoki, mosinto o Baana.
english: Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, repaired the next section. Next to him Meshullam son of Berekiah, the son of Meshezabel, made repairs, and next to him Zadok son of Baana also made repairs.

ekegusii: Abana abamura ba Meselemia amo nabanto bamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na batano, abamanyete buya gokora emeremo yabo.
english: Meshelemiah had sons and relatives, who were able men-- 18 in all.

ekegusii: Abana abamura ba Meselemia nabwo aba: Zakaria omwana oye omotangi; Yediaeli oyo o kabere; Zebadia oyo o gatato; Yatinieli oyo o kane.
english: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,

ekegusii: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
english: Meshesabeli, na Zadoki na Yadua;

ekegusii: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
english: Mesobabu, na Yamuleki, na Yosha, mosinto bw’Amasia;

ekegusii: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
english: Mesulamu, na Abiya, na Miyamini;

ekegusii: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
english: Mika, na Rehobu, na Hasabia;

ekegusii: Mika akamoboria, “Ng’ai okorwa?” Ere akairaneria, “Inche n’Omolawi o Bethlehemu o Yuda, naende nigo nkogenda korigia aase nkomenya.”
english: Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" "I'm a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah," he said, "and I'm looking for a place to stay."

ekegusii: Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
english: Simei akaibora Mika, na Mika akaibora Reaya, na Reaya akaibora Baali.

ekegusii: Naende Mikaya akagenderera gokwana, agateba, “Ase ayio, igwa ring’ana ri’Omonene. Inarora Omonene oikaransete ase ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene, na emeganda yonsi y’abamalaika eteneine ensemo yaye y’okorio na ey’okobee.
english: Micaiah continued, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne with all the host of heaven standing around him on his right and on his left.

ekegusii: Naende Mikaya akagenderera gokwana, agateba, “Ase ayio, igwa ring’ana ri’Omonene. Inarora Omonene oikaransete ase ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene, na emeganda yonsi y’abamalaika eteneine ensemo yaye y’okorio na ey’okobee.
english: Micaiah continued, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne with all the host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.

ekegusii: Mikaya akamoiraneria, “Onye gokoirana kore nomorembe, rirorio Omonene takwanete goetera asende,” Naende agateba, “Inwe abanto bonsi, igwa amang’ana aya.”
english: Micaiah declared, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Mark my words, all you people!"

ekegusii: Mikaya akamoiraneria, “Onye kogochia koirana kore nomorembe, rirorio Omonene takwaneti goetera asende.” Naende agateba, “Inwe abanto bonsi, igwa amang’ana ayio.”
english: Micaiah declared, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Mark my words, all you people!"

ekegusii: Mikaya akamoiraneria, “Aye norore rituko riria oratame na gosoa ase ekenunchi bwebisa.”
english: Micaiah replied, "You will find out on the day you go to hide in an inner room."

ekegusii: Mikaya akamoiraneria, “Aye norore ayio rituko riria oratame na gosoa ase ekenunchi bwebise.”
english: Micaiah replied, "You will find out on the day you go to hide in an inner room."

ekegusii: Mikaeli, na Isipa, na Yoha; aba nigo barenge abana abamura ba Beria.
english: Michael, Ishpah and Joha were the sons of Beriah.

ekegusii: Korigochia kogoroba bakaba bakobaboka goikera omogoroba oyio ekero okoruegwa kw’endagera kware koruegwa, korende riogi tiriaigwetwe, onde tabairaneretie gose kobaigwa.
english: Midday passed, and they continued their frantic prophesying until the time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no response, no one answered, no one paid attention.

ekegusii: Ase ayio Abaisraeli bagachandeka mono ase engencho y’Abamidiani; erio bakarera ase Omonene ng’a abakonye.
english: Midian so impoverished the Israelites that they cried out to the LORD for help.

ekegusii: Omonene nere obwate okobua okonene aria igoro; okobua kwaye nigo kobuete okoruma kw’amache, ee, okw’amache amange na okw’emerindo y’enyancha.
english: Mightier than the thunder of the great waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea-- the LORD on high is mighty.

ekegusii: Mijamin, Moadiah, Bilgah,
english: Miyamini, na Maadia, na Biliga;

ekegusii: Mikiloti nere orenge ise Simeamu. Aba boigo nigo bamenyete bakabebekana nabamwabo agwo Yerusalemu.
english: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.

ekegusii: oria okorete ogokora kw’ogokumia ase ense ya Hamu, naende agakora amang’ana ay’okoondokia aaria ase Enyancha Embariri.
english: miracles in the land of Ham and awesome deeds by the Red Sea.

ekegusii: Miriamu na Haroni bagakwana amang’ana arenge mamincha ya Musa, ekiagera Musa konya onyuomire omokungu korwa ase Abaetiopia.
english: Miriam and Aaron began to talk against Moses because of his Cushite wife, for he had married a Cushite.

ekegusii: Miriamu akabaitaberia, na gotera, “Moterere Omonene, ekiagera ere obuire ase okobua okonene, chibarasi amo nabachiriinete obarimeirie ase enyancha ime.”
english: Miriam sang to them: "Sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. The horse and its rider he has hurled into the sea."

ekegusii: Amang’ana amabe nigo agotunyana abanyene ebibe, korende abanyene oboronge nabaegwe amaya.
english: Misfortune pursues the sinner, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.

ekegusii: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
english: na Misima, na Duma, na Masa,

ekegusii: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
english: Misima na Duma, Masa na Hadadi, na Tema,

ekegusii: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
english: na Misimana oyo o kane, na Yeremia oyo o gatano,

ekegusii: Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah,
english: na Misipa, na Kefira, na Mosa,

ekegusii: Misiri nere oiborete Abaludi, na Abaanami, na Abalehabi, na Abanafutu,
english: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

ekegusii: Misiri nere oiborete Abaludi na Abaanami, Abalehabi na Abanafutu,
english: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

ekegusii: Ense ya Moabu yasookigwe, ekiagera yasirigwe; rera na kweumia! Tebia abamenyete ase chinsemo chi’orooche rw’Arinoni ng’a ense ya Moabu yasirigwe kegima.
english: Moab is disgraced, for she is shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.

ekegusii: Moabu negetaabo kiane ngoisabera; nindute egekoroto kiane igoro ase Edomu, ning’ake eriogi ri’okobua igoro y’ense y’Abafilisti.”
english: Moab is my washbasin, upon Edom I toss my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph."

ekegusii: Moabu negetaabo kiane ngoisabera, nindute egekoroto kiane igoro ase Edomu, ning’ake eriogi ri’okobua igoro y’ense y’Abafilisti.”
english: Moab is my washbasin, upon Edom I toss my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph."

ekegusii: “Ense ya Moabu yasarigwe, abana baye nigo bakorera mono.
english: Moab will be broken; her little ones will cry out.

ekegusii: Oyogosaria na gosiria ense ya Moabu na emechie yaye ochire; abamura baye bare abaya mono baitirwe. Nabo omoruoti, oyore Omonene bw’Emeganda, otebire.
english: Moab will be destroyed and her towns invaded; her finest young men will go down in the slaughter," declares the King, whose name is the LORD Almighty.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Moabu nabasirigwe kegima tibagenderera koba egesaku, ekiagera beimokereretie igoro mamincha y’Omonene.
english: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because she defied the LORD.

ekegusii: ogotogigwa kw’Abamoabu gwasirire. Ababisa bare Hesiboni barobeirie gokora ense eria bobe. Nigo bagotebania: Inchuo tosirie abanto baye tibabaisa koba egesaku naende. Aye omochie o Madimena boigo nokirigwe‐kiri, omoro nokobwatie korwa nyuma.
english: Moab will be praised no more; in Heshbon men will plot her downfall: 'Come, let us put an end to that nation.' You too, O Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.

ekegusii: Chingunchara chi’Abamoabu chiabutoirwe, na amaboko abo abunirwe.” Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: Moab's horn is cut off; her arm is broken," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Abanyacheche nigo bakoburukania omochie, korende abanto abang’aini nigo bagokendia endamwamu.
english: Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.

ekegusii: Moredekai natugete omoiseke oyomo, omwana o ise moke. Omoiseke oyio nigo arenge korokwa Hadasa, na erieta rinde n’Esteri. Nigo abwate omobere omuya, naende nigo arenge omonyakieni mono. Ekero abaibori baye bonsi bakwete, Moredekai akaba okomotuga buna omwana oye.
english: Mordecai had a cousin named Hadassah, whom he had brought up because she had neither father nor mother. This girl, who was also known as Esther, was lovely in form and features, and Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter when her father and mother died.
