ekegusii: “Abamenyi bamenyete ase egati yaino mbabe abanene kobabua, korende inwe mogenderere gokea mobe inse asebare.
english: The alien who lives among you will rise above you higher and higher, but you will sink lower and lower.

ekegusii: Orobebe rw’orogongo roria obomera bwagwerete ororeria rwa Yusufu rogachakera orooche rwa Yorodan, ang’e na Yeriko, moocha ye chinsoko chi’aroro goika erooro, rogatiira korwa Yeriko goetera ase erooro gochia ase ense y’ebitunwa ya Beteli.
english: The allotment for Joseph began at the Jordan of Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, and went up from there through the desert into the hill country of Bethel.

ekegusii: Chiamate chi’egesaku kia Yuda nigo chiaetwe orogongo rwabo ase ensemo ya irianyi, ang’e norobebe rwa Edomu, ase erooro ya Sini ere irianyi kegima.
english: The allotment for the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, extended down to the territory of Edom, to the Desert of Zin in the extreme south.

ekegusii: Oyio Omonguru, intwe titokonyara komorora buna are; nigo abwate okobua okonene, naende nigo are omonyene ekeene, ere nigo are omonyene oboronge mono, takorega onde.
english: The Almighty is beyond our reach and exalted in power; in his justice and great righteousness, he does not oppress.

ekegusii: Aase bagoutera omorero na gosambera ebing’wanso igoro y’egesasimero nigo arenge ay’ekerengo ki’amaboko ane gochia igoro, na korwa aroro emegwekano ene ye chingunchara yaroisirie yarochie igoro.
english: The altar hearth is four cubits high, and four horns project upward from the hearth.

ekegusii: Na eriko riria nigo riarenge eri’ekerengo ki’amaboko ikomi na abere, obotambe na obogare nigo biareng’aine.
english: The altar hearth is square, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.

ekegusii: na egesasimero ase ebing’wanso bigosamberwa amo nebikorero biaye, na egetuba amo nenterekerero yaye.
english: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.

ekegusii: egesasimero ase ebing’wanso birasamberwe na ebikorero biaye, na egetuba amo nenterekerero yaye,
english: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin with its stand--

ekegusii: na egesasimero aase ebing’wanso bigosamberwa amo negechungi kiaye gi’etaai, na emiaro yaye, na ebikorero biaye bionsi, na egetuba amo nenterekerero yaye;
english: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the bronze basin with its stand;

ekegusii: na egesasimero ase ubani egosamberwa amo nemiaro yaye, na amaguta akweakwa, na amanukato are ne rimisu rigiya, na ebitambaa bigosungwa ase egesoero ki’Obomenyo obwo;
english: the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense; the curtain for the doorway at the entrance to the tabernacle;

ekegusii: Abaameleki bakaoroka korwania Abaisraeli aaria Refidimu.
english: The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.

ekegusii: Abaameleki nigo bamenyete ase ense ya Negebu, ensemo ya irianyi y’ense eria; Abahiti, na Abayebusi, na Abaamori, nigo bamenyete ase ense y’ebitunwa. Abakanani barabwo nigo bamenyete ase enyancha enene mbarabare, naende ang’e norooche rwa Yorodan.”
english: The Amalekites live in the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan."

ekegusii: Abaamoni bakaboria Hanuni, omonene obo, “Inee! Igo okagete ng’a Daudi nigo asigete iso ase ogotoma abanto gocha gokoremia? Taibo. Nigo abatomire bache koroota omochie na koyosaria.”
english: the Ammonite nobles said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending men to you to express sympathy? Hasn't David sent them to you to explore the city and spy it out and overthrow it?"

ekegusii: Korende abatang’ani b’Abaamoni bagatebia Hanuni, “Inee! Igo okagete ng’a Daudi nigo asigete iso ase ogotoma abanto gocha gokoremia? Taibo. Abasomba baye nigo bachire koroota ense eye bayesarie.”
english: the Ammonite nobles said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending men to you to express sympathy? Haven't his men come to you to explore and spy out the country and overthrow it?"

ekegusii: Amo nayio Abaamori bakaamboka Yorodan gochia korwania Abayuda, na Ababenjamin, na Abaefraimu, goika Abaisraeli bagachandwa bobe mono.
english: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim; and Israel was in great distress.

ekegusii: Abaamoni bakarua ebango ase Usia; ere nigo abete nokobua okonene, ne chinkuma chiaye chigasarera gochia ase ense ya Misiri.
english: The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, because he had become very powerful.

ekegusii: Abaamoni bakagenda bakarobera ase egeita ki’omochie; Abasiiria ba Soba, na abwo ba Rehobu, amo nabanto korwa Tobu na Maaka, barabwo bakarobera ao boka ase egetii.
english: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to their city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.

ekegusii: Abaamori bagacha bakarobera agwo ase egesoero ki’omochie, na abaruoti baria konya bachire bakabeera boka aase aarabu.
english: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to their city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.

ekegusii: Abaamori bakamiga abanto b’egesaku kia Dani gochia ense y’ebigoro gose tibabatigerete ribaga batirimboke gochia ase ense omweya,
english: The Amorites confined the Danites to the hill country, not allowing them to come down into the plain.

ekegusii: Abaamori abamenyete ase ense eria bagacha kobarwania, bakabaseria buna chinchoke chigoseria abanto, bakababua agwo Seiri, bakabasiarera, bakababwatia gochia Horima.
english: The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you; they chased you like a swarm of bees and beat you down from Seir all the way to Hormah.

ekegusii: Naende omomalaika bw’Omonene akamotebia, “Nimentekanie ororeria rwao, na omobaro obo tokonyarwa kobareka, ekiagera barabe abange mono.”
english: The angel added, "I will so increase your descendants that they will be too numerous to count."

ekegusii: Ere akairaneria, agantebia, “Echi nechimbeo inye chia igoro chikogenda korwa ase konya chiteneine agwo ase obosio bw’Omonene bw’ense yonsi.
english: The angel answered me, "These are the four spirits of heaven, going out from standing in the presence of the Lord of the whole world.

ekegusii: Omomalaika akamoiraneria, “Ninche Gabirieli, ngotenena ase obosio bwa Nyasae; ninche natomwa nkwane naye, ngotebie amang’ana aya amaya.
english: The angel answered, "I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to tell you this good news.

ekegusii: Omomalaika akamotebia, “Omoika Omochenu nogochere, ne chinguru chiaye Oyore Igoro Mono nachikobekere ekiriri. Ase ayio, oyoraiborwe narokwe Omochenu, Omwana o Nyasae.
english: The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God.

ekegusii: Omomalaika oria o Nyasae akamotebia, “Imokia chinyama echi na emegati eye etabekiri memera, obibeke igoro ase egetare eke, naende obiumorere omosori oyio.” Gidioni agakora bo.
english: The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, place them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And Gideon did so.

ekegusii: Erio omomalaika bw’Omonene akandangeria ase chindoto: Yakobo! Inche ngaitaba: Nao inde aa!
english: The angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob.' I answered, 'Here I am.'

ekegusii: Naende Omomalaika bw’Omonene akamotebia, “Rora, morito ore, noibore omwana omoisia; nomoroke Isumaeli, ekiagera Omonene oigure ekerero ki’emechando yao.
english: The angel of the LORD also said to her: "You are now with child and you will have a son. You shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard of your misery.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene akamoiraneria, “Ayio onsi natebia omorugi oo, goika ayakore.
english: The angel of the LORD answered, "Your wife must do all that I have told her.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene akamoorokera, akamotebia, “Aye nigo ore omogomba, tobwati bana, korende nobe morito, erio oibore omwana omomura.
english: The angel of the LORD appeared to her and said, "You are sterile and childless, but you are going to conceive and have a son.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene akaboria Baalamu, “Nase ki gwaakire etigere yao chintunda echi isato? Rora, inche nigo nacha kogotanga, ekiagera orogendo oro okogenda norw’ogosaria rore mamincha yane.
english: The angel of the LORD asked him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I have come here to oppose you because your path is a reckless one before me.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene akarangeria Ibrahimu korwa igoro eria kabere, akamotebia,
english: The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time

ekegusii: Erio omomalaika bw’Omonene agacha, agaikaransa inse y’omote onga buna omotontera agwo Ofura, oyio orenge o Yoashi, omonto bw’eamate y’Abieseri. Gidioni, omomura oye, nigo arenge koora engano ase ekemitero ki’edivai, erinde Abamidiani tibayenyora.
english: The angel of the LORD came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to keep it from the Midianites.

ekegusii: Naende omomalaika oria bw’Omonene agacha eria kabere, akamokuna, akamotebia, “Imoka orie, ekiagera orogendo norotambe okogenda.”
english: The angel of the LORD came back a second time and touched him and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene nigo akorenda na goetanana abwo bamoirogete Omonene na kobatooria.
english: The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and he delivers them.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene akarora Hagari ase erooro ase ensoko y’amache yarenge ase enchera ekogenda Suri.
english: The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring in the desert; it was the spring that is beside the road to Shur.

ekegusii: Erio omomalaika oria bw’Omonene akamoenekeria Yoshua, akamotebia,
english: The angel of the LORD gave this charge to Joshua:

ekegusii: Omomalaika oria bw’Omonene akamoiraneria, “Nonya gwantanga ng’a mbeere aiga, tinkoria endagera yao, korende koraroisie ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa, okerue ase Omonene.” (Manoa tamanyete ng’a oria nigo arenge omomalaika bw’Omonene.)
english: The angel of the LORD replied, "Even though you detain me, I will not eat any of your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." (Manoah did not realize that it was the angel of the LORD.)

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene agatebia Baalamu, “Genda amo nabanto abwo, korende amang’ana aria ndagochike, naro oka ogochia gokwana.” Bono Baalamu akagenda amo nabanene baria ba Balaki.
english: The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but speak only what I tell you." So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.

ekegusii: Erio omomalaika bw’Omonene agatebia Elija, “Tirimboka, ogende amo nere; tobaisa komwoboa.” Erio Elija akaimoka, agatirimboka, akagenda amo nere ase omoruoti.
english: The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

ekegusii: Omomalaika bw’Omonene agatiira korwa Giligali, agaika Bokimu, agatebia Abaisraeli, “Inche nigo nabang’anyetie korwa Misiri, nkabarenta ase ense eye nabarierete chisokoro chiaino eira ng’a nimbayee. Ngateba: Tingosaria okobwatana kw’ogotianania okwo nakorete nainwe,
english: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land that I swore to give to your forefathers. I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you,

ekegusii: Erio agantebia, “Aya namang’ana ’obwegeni na ay’ekeene, na Omonene Nyasae, oyogotang’ana ababani n’Omoika oye, agatoma omomalaika oye, erinde aorokerie abasomba baye ayagwenerete gokoreka bwango.
english: The angel said to me, "These words are trustworthy and true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent his angel to show his servants the things that must soon take place."

ekegusii: Korende omomalaika agatebia abakungu baria, “Timoiroka inwe, ekiagera namanyire ng’a Yeso mokorigia, oria obambetwe.
english: The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.

ekegusii: Erio omomalaika oria agachika abwo bateneineo ase okomokorera, akabatebia, “Morusie chianga echio chire ne riko.” Nyuma y’ayio omomalaika oria agatebia Yoshua, “Naama! Narusirie ebibe biao korwa asore, ninkobekere chianga chingiya chi’omoyega.”
english: The angel said to those who were standing before him, "Take off his filthy clothes." Then he said to Joshua, "See, I have taken away your sin, and I will put rich garments on you."

ekegusii: Omomalaika oria akabutora, agasangereria amasabibu ’emesabibu y’ense, na akayaruta ase ekemitero ekenene ki’endamwamu ya Nyasae.
english: The angel swung his sickle on the earth, gathered its grapes and threw them into the great winepress of God's wrath.

ekegusii: Agacha asare, akabora, “Mbuya ore aye, oyokwaeirwe obuya. Omonene nigo are amo naye.”
english: The angel went to her and said, "Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you."

ekegusii: omomalaika oria ontooretie korwa ase amabe onsi, asesenie abamura aba. Abana aba babe bagwatorwa ase erieta riane, na ase erieta ria sokoro yane Ibrahimu, na eria Isaka tata; tiga bakine babe abanto abange ase ense.”
english: the Angel who has delivered me from all harm--may he bless these boys. May they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they increase greatly upon the earth."

ekegusii: Omomalaika oria okwanete nainche nigo arenge nemoti y’okorenga y’etahabu, anyare korenga omochie na ebiita biaye, na orwaki rwaye.
english: The angel who talked with me had a measuring rod of gold to measure the city, its gates and its walls.

ekegusii: Omonene akaba nendamwamu asare, akamotomera omobani komoboria, “Nase ki kwarigirie chinyasae chi’abanto, chiria chitabakonyete korwa ase okoboko kwao?”
english: The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why do you consult this people's gods, which could not save their own people from your hand?"

ekegusii: Ase igo Omonene akaba nendamwamu entindi ase Abaisraeli, akabatiga bakabugwa na Kusani‐Risataimu, omoruoti o Mesopotamia; na Abaisraeli bakaba bakomokorera ase engaki y’emiaka etano na etato.
english: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel so that he sold them into the hands of Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram Naharaim, to whom the Israelites were subject for eight years.

ekegusii: Endamwamu y’Omonene ekaba enene asebare, akarua aroro agwo, akagenda.
english: The anger of the LORD burned against them, and he left them.

ekegusii: Omonene takoonchoka atige endamwamu yaye, goika aikeranie okogania kw’ebirengererio biaye ase okonacha ekina. Nigo morache komanya buya amang’ana ayio ase amatuko agocha.
english: The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he fully accomplishes the purposes of his heart. In days to come you will understand it clearly.

ekegusii: Ebing’wanso biatananetwe nigo biarenge chieri amagana atano na rimo, ne ching’ondi chilifu isano.
english: The animals consecrated as sacrifices amounted to six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep and goats.

ekegusii: Echi chionsi chiasoete, chinsacha ne chinkungu chire moyo chia kera egesaku, chigasoa buna Nyasae achigete Nuhu, na Omonene akamosiekera egesieri.
english: The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.

ekegusii: Erio ching’iti chi’orosana chiagenda kwebisa, chiagenderera kobeera ase amakuruma abo.
english: The animals take cover; they remain in their dens.

ekegusii: Mochore emanwa y’omwaka oyomo etari na kemocho ase omobere oye, ebe emingichi gose egoree.
english: The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take them from the sheep or the goats.

ekegusii: Abatomwa na abagaaka bagasangererekana amo, erinde banyare korengereria igoro ye ring’ana erio.
english: The apostles and elders met to consider this question.

ekegusii: Naende abatomwa na abaminto abarenge Boyahudi bakaigwa ng’a abanto b’Ebisaku nabarabwo banyorire ring’ana ria Nyasae.
english: The apostles and the brothers throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

ekegusii: Abatomwa bakairana ase Yeso, bakamotebia onsi ayabakorete, na amang’ana onsi ayaborokereretie.
english: The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to him all they had done and taught.

ekegusii: Na barabwo bakarua ase ekegambero keria, bagogete ekiagera konya babarirwe ng’a bagweneire korenterwa obosooku ase engencho y’Erieta eri.
english: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing because they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

ekegusii: Ase amaboko ’abatomwa ebikone ebinge na amakumia amange bigakoreka ase abanto. Na barabwo bonsi nigo barenge amo ase omoyo oyomo ase Egesona gia Sulemani.
english: The apostles performed many miraculous signs and wonders among the people. And all the believers used to meet together in Solomon's Colonnade.

ekegusii: Abatomwa bakamotebia, “Omonene, tomentere okwegena gwaito.”
english: The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith!"

ekegusii: Okororekana kw’ebitongwa ebio nigo kwarenge buna omorero bw’amakara ogwoka buna ebimore bigoetanana ase egati yabo. Omorero oria nigo orenge komoreka mono, na korwa ase omorero oyio okomesa gw’enkoba gokaruao.
english: The appearance of the living creatures was like burning coals of fire or like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures; it was bright, and lightning flashed out of it.

ekegusii: The archer will not stand his ground, the fleet-footed soldier will not get away, and the horseman will not save his life.
english: Omonto omanyete koruta chinsara, tagotenena arwane, gose oyomanyete kominyoka chimbero, tagwetooria, na omoriini ebarasi tagwetooria.

ekegusii: ense y’Abagebali amo na Lebanoni yonsi gochia moocha, na korwa Baali‐Gadi inse y’egetunwa kia Herimoni goika enchera ekogenda Hamati.
english: the area of the Gebalites; and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo Hamath.

ekegusii: Esanduku eria ya Nyasae ekabeera ase enka y’Obedi‐Edomu nyomba ime ase engaki y’emetienyi etato; na Omonene agasesenia enka y’Obedi‐Edomu na ebinto bionsi abwate.
english: The ark of God remained with the family of Obed-Edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he had.

ekegusii: The ark of God was captured, and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
english: Esanduku ya Nyasae ekairwa, na Hofini na Finehasi, abamura babere ba Eli, bagaitwa.

ekegusii: Ekabeera ase enyomba y’Obedi‐Edomu ase engaki y’emetienyi etato, na Omonene agasesenia Obedi‐Edomu na abanto bonsi b’enyomba yaye.
english: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and his entire household.

ekegusii: na Esanduku eria ere ne chibao chirikire oborori, amo nemiaro yaye, na Oboikaranso bw’Amabera,
english: the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the atonement cover;

ekegusii: Esanduku na emiaro yaye, na Oboikaranso bw’Amabera, na etoto eria erabekwe ebokenge;
english: the ark with its poles and the atonement cover and the curtain that shields it;

ekegusii: Abarwani abarenge nebirwanero bagatang’ana abakuani abarenge kobugia ebitureri biria, na abarwani bande bakabwatia Esanduku eria ebitureri kobigendererete kobugigwa.
english: The armed guard marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark. All this time the trumpets were sounding.

ekegusii: Na emeganda y’esegi ere igoro ekamotunyana, na abwo bariinete chibarasi chindabu, babekeire chianga chi’egatani engiya endabu.
english: The armies of heaven were following him, riding on white horses and dressed in fine linen, white and clean.

ekegusii: Abarwani ba Daudi bakagenda orosana korwania Abaisraeli, na esegi ekarwanerwa ase rinani ri’Efraimu.
english: The army marched into the field to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

ekegusii: na Abayuda bakabwata abanto bande chilifu ikomi bare moyo, bakabaira ase egechuria, ki’egetare igoro, bakabatuguta gochia inse, goika bakabunanekana bakaba ebing’ese.
english: The army of Judah also captured ten thousand men alive, took them to the top of a cliff and threw them down so that all were dashed to pieces.

ekegusii: Ase engaki eyio abarwani b’esegi b’omoruoti o Babeli nigo baboerete Yerusalemu, na Yeremia omobani agasiekerwa ase egoora y’echela yarenge ase enyomba y’omoruoti bw’Abayuda.
english: The army of the king of Babylon was then besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the royal palace of Judah.

ekegusii: Obomwenu bwa mwanyabanto mbokeeigwe, na oboenenu bwabo mboiranigwe inse, na ase rituko erio Omonene bweka naimokererigwe igoro.
english: The arrogance of man will be brought low and the pride of men humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,

ekegusii: Nyasae, abanto abaenenu banyimokeire kondwania esegi; ekeombe ki’abanto abatindi nigo bakorigia basirie obogima bwane, abwo tibakoirogeti nonya ng’ake.
english: The arrogant are attacking me, O God; a band of ruthless men seeks my life-- men without regard for you.

ekegusii: Abanto abaenenu tibakonyara gotenena ase obosio bwao, nigo ogechete abakori amabe bonsi.
english: The arrogant cannot stand in your presence; you hate all who do wrong.

ekegusii: Abanto abamwenu batabwateti amachiko ao nigo bankunyeire chiirima.
english: The arrogant dig pitfalls for me, contrary to your law.

ekegusii: Abanto abamwenu nigo bagonchecheria mono, nonya naboigo tindi gotiga amachiko ao.
english: The arrogant mock me without restraint, but I do not turn from your law.

ekegusii: Oyio ore omoenenu nagochwe na kogwa, gose monto onde takomogororokia. Nintongie omorero ase emechie y’ense eyio noro nosambe chinsemo chiaye chionsi.
english: The arrogant one will stumble and fall and no one will help her up; I will kindle a fire in her towns that will consume all who are around her."

ekegusii: Nyasae Omonguru ombetire emegwe yaye, na omoika one ong’usire obosongo bwabo; okogosa kwa Nyasae kwarobeire kondwania.
english: The arrows of the Almighty are in me, my spirit drinks in their poison; God's terrors are marshaled against me.

ekegusii: Onye ekoba bo, omosangererekano bw’abanto noro oragambe ekina ase egati y’omonto oria oita omonto onde mosiabano na oria oganetie korusia egesiomba ki’oyomwabo oitetwe, na onache ekina koreng’ana nemeroberio echikire.
english: the assembly must judge between him and the avenger of blood according to these regulations.

ekegusii: Omosangererekano bw’abanto notoorie omoiti oria korwa ase oria oganetie korusia egesiomba. Bamotige airane abeere ase omochie oria bw’obotamero atamerete, amenye aroro goika omokuani omonene bw’engaki eyio, oyoakire amagutwa, akwe.
english: The assembly must protect the one accused of murder from the avenger of blood and send him back to the city of refuge to which he fled. He must stay there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.

ekegusii: Bono abande nigo barenge korera iga, na abande iga, ekiagera omosangererekano oria konya obeire neburu‐buru. Abange asebare tibamanyete nase ki basangererekanete amo.
english: The assembly was in confusion: Some were shouting one thing, some another. Most of the people did not even know why they were there.

ekegusii: Abakalidayo baria bakairaneria omoruoti, bakamotebia, “Monto onde tari ase ense eye oranyare koorokia ring’ana erio aye omoruoti oganetie komanya, ekiagera omoruoti onde tari, nonya ore omonene mono, gose ore nokobua kore naki, oboririe egento kenga buna ekio korwa ase abaringoria, gose abaragori, gose korwa ase Abakalidayo bamanyete oborogi.
english: The astrologers answered the king, "There is not a man on earth who can do what the king asks! No king, however great and mighty, has ever asked such a thing of any magician or enchanter or astrologer.

ekegusii: Omonto oria okorigia korusia egesiomba ki’oyomwabo oitetwe, nere oraite omoiti oria aande onsi ase araumerane nere.
english: The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.

ekegusii: na abanto ba Awa oyo o Nibuhasi, na Taritaki, na abanto ba Sefariwaimu, bagasamba abana babo bakaba ebing’wanso ase Adirameleki na Anameleki, chinyasae chia Sefariwaimu.
english: the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

ekegusii: Nonya mbono egesire kiabekirwe ase emeri y’emete; nabo kera omote otameti okwama okuya nonachwe, otugutwe ase omorero.
english: The ax is already at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

ekegusii: Nonya mbono egesire kiabekirwe ase emeri y’emete; nabo kera omote otameti okwama okuya nonachwe, otugutwe ase omorero.”
english: The ax is already at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."

ekegusii: Abana bakaba bakomigana enda yaye ime. Ere akabora, “Onye nabo iga, okoba moyo kwane ninki korangwenere?” Akagenda koboria Omonene.
english: The babies jostled each other within her, and she said, "Why is this happening to me?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.

ekegusii: Ee, nindete abanto ba Babeli, na Abakalidayo bonsi, na abanto ba Pekodi, na aba Soa, na aba Koa, na Abaasuri bonsi mbache amo nabwo; bonsi nigo barenge abamura abaya b’ogosanerwa, na abagambi, na abarwani abanene, bonsi nabariini chibarasi barenge.
english: the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, handsome young men, all of them governors and commanders, chariot officers and men of high rank, all mounted on horses.

ekegusii: Abakalidayo bakabuna chisiiro chie chitaai chiria chiarenge ime ase enyomba y’Omonene, na ebibekerero bi’ebituba, na egetuba keria ekenene mono kiaroisirie korwa ase etaai ebiarenge ase enyomba y’Omonene. Kobabibunire bikaba ebing’ese, bakaira etaai eria yonsi Babeli.
english: The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands and the bronze Sea that were at the temple of the LORD and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.

ekegusii: Abakalidayo bakabuna chisiiro chi’etaai chiria chiarenge ime ase enyomba y’Omonene, na ebibekerero bi’ebituba, na egetuba keria ekenene keroisirie korwa ase etaai, ebiarenge ase enyomba y’Omonene, Kobabibunire, bikaba ebing’ese, bakaira chitaai chiria chionsi Babeli.
english: The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands and the bronze Sea that were at the temple of the LORD and they carried the bronze to Babylon.

ekegusii: Naende Abakalidayo bagasamba enyomba y’omoruoti oyio amo ne chinyomba chi’abanto, naende bagatagora chindwaki chia Yerusalemu, bagachiiyeria inse.
english: The Babylonians set fire to the royal palace and the houses of the people and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Abakalidayo abwo bayonaaretie nabache bayotongie omorero, bayosambe amo ne chinyomba echio igoro ase ebirama biabo mware gosambera ubani ase enyasae Baali, naende mokarua okoruegwa kw’ebinyugwa ase chinyasae ching’ao, na igo mokangechia nkaba nendamwamu.
english: The Babylonians who are attacking this city will come in and set it on fire; they will burn it down, along with the houses where the people provoked me to anger by burning incense on the roofs to Baal and by pouring out drink offerings to other gods.

ekegusii: Chinterekerero chie chisiiro chiaye nigo chiarenge chie chitaai, korende ebigobanio ne chinuga chiabo nigo chiarenge chie chifeta, na ebisure biabo bikaoomwa nefeta.
english: The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver; so all the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

ekegusii: the bases for the surrounding courtyard and those for its entrance and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and those for the surrounding courtyard.
english: ne chinterekerero chie chisiiro chi’eraaro chibe chinsemo chionsi, na echi’egesoero ki’eraaro, na ebirochi bionsi bi’eema y’Obomenyo, na ebi’eraaro chinsemo chionsi.

ekegusii: Esegi nigo yesiarerete ase orosana rwonsi rw’aase aria, na ase rituko riria abanto abange bagakwera ase rinani ime kobua abwo baitetwe nemioro.
english: The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest claimed more lives that day than the sword.

ekegusii: Esegi ekaba entindi mono ase rituko erio, na Abineri na Abaisraeli bakabugwa nabanto ba Daudi.
english: The battle that day was very fierce, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by David's men.

ekegusii: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are firs.
english: Ebisigisa bi’enyomba yaito nebi’emecharake, ne chindote nechi’emetarakwa.

ekegusii: Ne chingunchara chiria ikomi kwaroche, echio amo neng’iti nachigeche omotayayi oria; nachimokore abe bosa na getirianda, nachimorie chinyama chiaye, naende nachimosambe kegima nomorero.
english: The beast and the ten horns you saw will hate the prostitute. They will bring her to ruin and leave her naked; they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire.

ekegusii: Na eng’iti eria naroche nigo yagwekaine engo. Amagoro aye nigo arenge buna ay’edubu, na omonwa oye buna oyo bw’endo. Enchoka ekaa eng’iti eria chinguru chiaye, na ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene, na okobua okonene.
english: The beast I saw resembled a leopard, but had feet like those of a bear and a mouth like that of a lion. The dragon gave the beast his power and his throne and great authority.

ekegusii: Eng’iti eria ekaegwa ribaga ri’ogokwana amang’ana amanene na ay’okorama, naende ekaegwa okobua gw’okogamba ase engaki y’emetienyi emerongo ene na ebere.
english: The beast was given a mouth to utter proud words and blasphemies and to exercise his authority for forty-two months.

ekegusii: Na eng’iti eria yarengeo, korende bono teiyo, ero neya gatano na gatato ere, Ero neyemo ya chiria isano na ibere, na nkogenda ere ase ogosirigwa kwaye.
english: The beast who once was, and now is not, is an eighth king. He belongs to the seven and is going to his destruction.

ekegusii: Eng’iti eria kwaroche yarengeo, korende bono teiyo, ng’ang’e ere gotiira korwa ase eora y’abakure na kogenda gosirigwa. Na abwo bamenyete ase ense, abwo amarieta abo atarikiri ase ebuku y’obogima korwa omochakano, ekero oboroso bw’ense bwabegetwe, nabakumie ase eng’iti eria, ekiagera yarengeo, na bono teiyo, naende neche kobao.
english: The beast, which you saw, once was, now is not, and will come up out of the Abyss and go to his destruction. The inhabitants of the earth whose names have not been written in the book of life from the creation of the world will be astonished when they see the beast, because he once was, now is not, and yet will come.

ekegusii: Oborere nigo bore obweng’e omonto agosinywa kwerambora igoro ase borobwo, na ekiebisio nigo kere ekenyerere mono omonto atanyare kwebisia.
english: The bed is too short to stretch out on, the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.

ekegusii: The beginning of the gospel about Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
english: Oyo noro omochakano bw’enchili ya Yesu Kristo, Omwana o Nyasae,

ekegusii: Omoguba ogouta omorero nigo ogouterera mono, korende ribiria tiriri gwatananwa. Ogochenwa okwo nigo kore okwa bosa, ekiagera obobe tibori korusigwao.
english: The bellows blow fiercely to burn away the lead with fire, but the refining goes on in vain; the wicked are not purged out.

ekegusii: Ase igo omong’ororia bw’emegwekano ye rikomomanga bwateranirie ne chindege orenge ase omoringero o inse ase eganchwa eria ekobekwa ase obokoreri bw’obokuani. Naboigo buna Omonene konya achikire Musa.
english: The bells and pomegranates alternated around the hem of the robe to be worn for ministering, as the LORD commanded Moses.

ekegusii: Naende bagateba, “Ababenjamin abatooregete goika banyorerwe abanyamwando, erinde egesaku ekemo korwa ase Abaisraeli tigesirigwa kegima.
english: The Benjamite survivors must have heirs," they said, "so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.

ekegusii: korende Ababenjamin bagasoka korwa Gibea, bagaita Abaisraeli chilifu fu emerongo ebere na ibere, ase rituko erio.
english: The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and cut down twenty-two thousand Israelites on the battlefield that day.

ekegusii: Ababenjamin bagasoka, bakagenda korwana nabanto abwo, bakang’uswa gochia aare korwa ase omochie oria, na buna chingaki chiria chinde bagachaka goita Abaisraeli ase enchera enene egotiira gochia Beteli, na ase eyende ekogenda Gibea, naboigo naase aarabu. Bagaita Abaisraeli ang’e emerongo etato.
english: The Benjamites came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to inflict casualties on the Israelites as before, so that about thirty men fell in the open field and on the roads-- the one leading to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.

ekegusii: Korende abanto b’egesaku kia Benjamin tibaseretie Abayebusi, abanto bamenyete Yerusalemu. Ase ayio Abayebusi nigo bagendererete komenya Yerusalemu amo n’Ababenjamin nonya ngoika rero iga.
english: The Benjamites, however, failed to dislodge the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem; to this day the Jebusites live there with the Benjamites.

ekegusii: Moe abakuani okwama kwaino ogotang’ani gwa kera egento; boigo mobae okorua kwaino, na obosie bw’ogotongora kwaino. Erio nario ogosesenigwa koragenderere koba ase chinyomba chiaino.
english: The best of all the firstfruits and of all your special gifts will belong to the priests. You are to give them the first portion of your ground meal so that a blessing may rest on your household.

ekegusii: Oyore omuya goetania abande ase egati yabo nigo anga buna egetutu kere namagwa, na oyore nenkoro endonge nigo are nobobe kobua orobago rogiteire amagwa. Ekero rituko ri’abarendi bao, riria ri’egesusuro kiao riraike, abanto mbabe nomoichano.
english: The best of them is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen has come, the day God visits you. Now is the time of their confusion.

ekegusii: Chinyoni nigo chikomenya ang’e na chirochio, nigo chikoba chigotera ekero chigwete ase chinsagia chi’emete.
english: The birds of the air nest by the waters; they sing among the branches.

ekegusii: ne chinyoni chikoiruruka amo ne chinswe chi’enyancha, na kende gionsi kegoetanana ase chindiba chie chinyancha.
english: the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas.

ekegusii: Omoturi ebioma nigo akobogoria enturago yaye otura ekioma. Nigo agokebeka igoro ase omorero bw’amakara, ogesamba, erio okebomba ase ogokebaraga nokoboko kwaye kore ne chinguru. Ekero agendererete koroisia omogwekano oyio, nigo akoba nenchara na erang’o ogoya.
english: The blacksmith takes a tool and works with it in the coals; he shapes an idol with hammers, he forges it with the might of his arm. He gets hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.

ekegusii: Nigo moranyore ogosesenigwa komoraigwere amachiko ’Omonene, Nyasae oino, aya nkobachika rituko ria rero,
english: the blessing if you obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today;

ekegusii: Ogosesenigwa kw’Omonene nigo gokorenta obotenenku, na ere tari komenta obororo ase ogosesenigwa okwo.
english: The blessing of the LORD brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.

ekegusii: Emeuko na amagata bakamochiera aria ase Hekalu, na ere akabagwenia.
english: The blind and the lame came to him at the temple, and he healed them.

ekegusii: Abarenge emeuko nkorora bare, abarenge amagata ngotaara bare, abarenge noborwaire bwa ukoma basibekire, abarenge emetino nkoigwa bare, abare ebitondo nkobokigwa bare, na abataka nkoranderigwa bare amang’ana amaya.
english: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, those who have leprosy are cured, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

ekegusii: Naki onye amanyinga e chimbori na aye chieri, ne ribu ri’amatororo biare konyororokerigwa ase abatachenegeti mbinyare gochena ase ogosibigwa kw’omobere,
english: The blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that they are outwardly clean.

ekegusii: Amanyinga ayio abe ekemanyererio ase chinyomba chiria morabe momenyete. Ekero ndarore amanyinga aria ning’ete mbatige inwe, na amaakwa aria takobanyora inwe abasirie, ekero ndaake ense ya Misiri.
english: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are; and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destructive plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.

ekegusii: Naki buna omobere ore oyomo, oro nore nebiimo ebinge, na ebiimo bionsi bi’omobere oria, nonya bire ebinge, nigo bire omobere oyomo; naboigo na Kristo are.
english: The body is a unit, though it is made up of many parts; and though all its parts are many, they form one body. So it is with Christ.

ekegusii: Emekorogoto y’ebiita biaino ebe ey’ebioma ne chitaai, na buna amatuko aino arabe, naboigo ne chinguru chiaino chirabe.
english: The bolts of your gates will be iron and bronze, and your strength will equal your days.

ekegusii: Ebintungetie biangwereire agwo aase are aagiya, ee, omwando one nigo ore omuya mono.
english: The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; surely I have a delightful inheritance.

ekegusii: The boundary of the Amorites was from Scorpion Pass to Sela and beyond.
english: Sugusu ya Sera orobebe rw’Abaamori rokagenda goetera egetirimboko ki’Egetunwa ki’Ebiuge.

ekegusii: Orooche rwa Yorodan nigo rwarenge orobebe rwa bosongo rw’orogongo rw’egesaku kia Reuben. Emechie eyio amo nebichie biabo nigo yaatananetwe ase kera eamate y’egesaku kia Reuben, ekaba omwando obo.
english: The boundary of the Reubenites was the bank of the Jordan. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Reubenites, clan by clan.

ekegusii: Erio orobebe rokaonchoka gochia bosongo goika Asinoti‐Tabori, na korwa agwo rokagenderera goika Hukoki, rogatwomera orogongo rw’egesaku gia Sabuloni ensemo ya sugusu, na orw’egia Aseri ensemo ya bosongo, na orw’ekia Yuda ensemo ya moocha ase Yorodan.
english: The boundary ran west through Aznoth Tabor and came out at Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west and the Jordan on the east.

ekegusii: Erio orobebe rokaonchoka gochia Rama, rogaika omochie omonene o Turo, oyogiteire chindwaki, rokaonchoka gochia Hosa, na rokanucha Enyancha Enene. Naende orogongo orwo rokabwaterania engegu y’ensemo y’Akisibu,
english: The boundary then turned back toward Ramah and went to the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah and came out at the sea in the region of Aczib,

ekegusii: na rokagenda korwa ebate eria y’Akori goika Debiri, naende rokaonehoka sugusu gochia Giligali kororia Adumini, irianyi y’ebate eria. Naende rokagenderera goika chinsoko chia Eni‐Semesi rogaika ase ensoko ya Eni‐Rogeli. Erio rokagenderera goika chinsoko chia Eni‐Semesi, na goika ensoko ya Eni‐Rogeli.
english: The boundary then went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor and turned north to Gilgal, which faces the Pass of Adummim south of the gorge. It continued along to the waters of En Shemesh and came out at En Rogel.

ekegusii: Orobebe rwabo rogatwomera boigo Tabori na Sahasuma, na Beti‐Semesi, rokanucha Yorodan. Orogongo oro rokabwaterania emechie ikomi, na etano nomo, amo nebichie biabo.
english: The boundary touched Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth Shemesh, and ended at the Jordan. There were sixteen towns and their villages.

ekegusii: Korwa agwo rogatirimboka rogaika ensinyo y’egetunwa kerochie Rikura ria Beni‐Hinomu, rire ensemo ya sugusu y’ense omweremo ya Refaimu. Erio rokagenda gochia irianyi goetera Rikura ria Hinomu, irianyi y’esagamo y’Abayebusi gochia Eni‐Rogeli.
english: The boundary went down to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom, north of the Valley of Rephaim. It continued down the Hinnom Valley along the southern slope of the Jebusite city and so to En Rogel.

ekegusii: Ase ayio ribebe erio richakere korwa ase enyancha rigenderere goika Hasari‐Enoni, omochie ore ase ribebe ria Damesiki, naende rigenderere gochia sugusu goika ase orogongo rwa Hamati. Nario rirabe ribebe ria sugusu.
english: The boundary will extend from the sea to Hazar Enan, along the northern border of Damascus, with the border of Hamath to the north. This will be the north boundary.

ekegusii: naende rotirimboke gochia Ribula, moocha y’Aini, rotirimboke gochia moocha y’engegu y’enyancha ya Kinereti.
english: The boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain and continue along the slopes east of the Sea of Kinnereth.

ekegusii: Omwana oria Samweli akaba ogokora emeremo ase obosio bw’Omonene inse y’oboteneneri bwa Eli. Ase amatuko aria ring’ana ri’Omonene tiriarenge gokwanwa mono na amaroro ’obobani tarenge konyorekana otatiga okomo okomo.
english: The boy Samuel ministered before the LORD under Eli. In those days the word of the LORD was rare; there were not many visions.

ekegusii: Ekero abana abwo bakinire, Esau akaba omotwari bwe ching’iti, korende Yakobo nigo arenge omonto omotoereru, ore kobeera ase chiema.
english: The boys grew up, and Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man, staying among the tents.

ekegusii: Nyasae nigo akorua omoika bw’obokeng’entu obwatania amache, na amache oyarenta abwatana oma pa.
english: The breath of God produces ice, and the broad waters become frozen.

ekegusii: Oyore nomoriakari nere omonyuomi, korende omong’wansi oye nigo agotenena na komoigwa, ogokera eriogi ri’omonyuomi; naboigo omogoko one oikeranire bono.”
english: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend who attends the bridegroom waits and listens for him, and is full of joy when he hears the bridegroom's voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.

ekegusii: The bridegroom was a long time in coming, and they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
english: Ekero omonyuomi atebana gocha, bagasundoka bonsi, bakarara.

ekegusii: Na egesasimero gi’etaai kiarenge ase egati y’egesasimero keria ekeyia na ase enyomba y’Omonene, agakebeka ensemo ya sugusu y’egesasimero keria.
english: The bronze altar that stood before the LORD he brought from the front of the temple-- from between the new altar and the temple of the LORD-- and put it on the north side of the new altar.

ekegusii: na egesasimero gi’etaai amo negechungi gi’etaai, na emiaro yaye, na ebikorero biaye bionsi, na egetuba amo nenterekerero yaye,
english: the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

ekegusii: Na igoro ase kera esiiro, egesure nkiarengeo kiaroiseirie etaai, na obotambe bwaye nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko atano. Egechanga na emegwekano y’amatunda amakomomanga biaroisirie korwa ase chitaai, nigo biaetanaine egesure keria.
english: The bronze capital on top of the one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

ekegusii: Chitaai chie chisiiro chiria ibere, na echi’egetuba keria ekenene, na echi’ebibekerero biria bi’ebituba, ebinto ebio bionsi Sulemani aroisetie ase enyomba y’Omonene, tibiarenge korengeka.
english: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the movable stands, which Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD, was more than could be weighed.

ekegusii: Oborito bwe chitaai chiaroisetie chisiiro chiria ibere, na egetuba keria ekenene mono, na emegwekano ye chieri ikomi na ebere yeroisirie korwa ase chitaai eyio yaimokereretie egetuba keria igoro, amo nebibekerero bionsi biria Sulemani omoruoti aroisetie ase enyomba y’Omonene, nigo bwaetanetie ekerengo.
english: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD, was more than could be weighed.

ekegusii: Chitaai chiatananetwe chibe ekerugwa, nigo chiarenge chikiro chilifu isato, na amagana atano, na emerongo ene, na isano (3,545).
english: The bronze from the wave offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.

ekegusii: Korende oyomino otari nobonene agoke, ekiagera aimokererigwe igoro,
english: The brother in humble circumstances ought to take pride in his high position.

ekegusii: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah.
english: Isia omomura omwabo Mika, na Zakaria bw’ororeria rwa Isia.

ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo arenge gokwanwa buya nabaminto abamenyete Listra na Ikonio.
english: The brothers at Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.

ekegusii: Erio kegima abaminto baria bagatoma Paulo agende goika nyancha, korende Sila na Timotheo bagatigara aroro.
english: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed at Berea.

ekegusii: Abaminto b’aroro, ekero baigwete amang’ana igoro yaito, bagacha goika Apioforo na Tiretaberne gotorototera aroro. Paulo ekero achia kobarora, akamobaka Nyasae, akaremigwa.
english: The brothers there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these men Paul thanked God and was encouraged.

ekegusii: Amamumu ayio amo ne chinsagia biroisigwe bibe egento ekemo ne ritina, bionsi biroisigwe korwa ase ribomba erimo ri’etahabu echenire esunyuntire.
english: The buds and branches shall all be of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

ekegusii: Bionsi bikaroisigwa korwa ase ribomba erimo ri’etahabu echenire esunyuntire.
english: The buds and the branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

ekegusii: Oboagacho obwarenge ao, ensemo ya bosongo, nigo bwarenge nobogare bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko emerongo etano na ebere. Obonetu bw’enyasi yonsi y’enyomba eria nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko atano, na obotambe bwaye amaboko emerongo kianda.
english: The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.

ekegusii: Obotambe bw’enyomba eria nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko rigana erimo, na obogare bwaye amaboko emerongo etano, na egesoero nigo kiarochie sugusu.
english: The building whose door faced north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.

ekegusii: Eeri eria amo nembori eria chiaruetwe chibe ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe, echio amanyinga abo arentwe ime y’Aase Aachenu Mono akore okobwatanigwa, chiirwe isiko y’egetwori. Riiyo ne risankwa, amo ne chinyama ne chisike chiabo, bisamberwe aroro nomorero.
english: The bull and the goat for the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; their hides, flesh and offal are to be burned up.

ekegusii: Ense y’omokenye ogosamba nebe ritibo ri’amache, na ase ense enyomo chinsoko chi’amache nchitubokeo; aase chisese chi’orosana chiamenyete, obonyansi, na ebitonto, na amauncho mbimereo.
english: The burning sand will become a pool, the thirsty ground bubbling springs. In the haunts where jackals once lay, grass and reeds and papyrus will grow.

ekegusii: Ase rituko ri’Esabato omogambi arue ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa ase Omonene, chimanwa chie ching’ondi isano nemo, na emingichi eyemo, chionsi chibe chitari na kemocho ase emebere yabo.
english: The burnt offering the prince brings to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six male lambs and a ram, all without defect.

ekegusii: Na omoruoti orenge kogamba Aradi, ensemo ya irianyi ase ense ya Kanani, akaigwa ng’a Abaisraeli nigo bare inchera gocha.
english: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.

ekegusii: Abakanani na abanto bande bonsi b’ense eye baise koigwa ring’ana eri nigo barache gotoetanana na korusia amarieta aito korwa ase ense, titoinyorwa. Inki rende otagete okore, erinde erieta riao rinene ritogigwe?”
english: The Canaanites and the other people of the country will hear about this and they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. What then will you do for your own great name?"

ekegusii: Chindooche chigochiao nigo chiragunde chitioke, na amache ’emetaro agwo Misiri nakee aere; ebitonto na amauncho mbiome.
english: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up. The reeds and rushes will wither,

ekegusii: Ebisure igoro ye chisiiro chiarenge ime y’enyomba ya bosio, nigo biabombire bigwekaine ebisicha; obotambe bwabo nobw’amaboko ane.
english: The capitals on top of the pillars in the portico were in the shape of lilies, four cubits high.

ekegusii: Ebisure nigo biabombire buna ebisicha nigo biarenge igoro ase chisiiro. Na igo emeremo ye chisiiro ekaera.
english: The capitals on top were in the shape of lilies. And so the work on the pillars was completed.

ekegusii: na abatang’ani b’abarwani emerongo etano, na abanto abasike, na abasemia, na abaroisia abang’aini, na abaragori bamanyete oborogi mono.
english: the captain of fifty and man of rank, the counselor, skilled craftsman and clever enchanter.

ekegusii: Omotang’ani bw’abarendi akabeka Yusufu abe okobarigereria na kobakorera, na barabwo bakabeera ase egesibo ase engaki enke.
english: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he attended them. After they had been in custody for some time,

ekegusii: Omochiki bw’emeeri akagenda asare akamoboria, “Naki oraire chitoro iga okirete‐kiri? Imoka orangerie Nyasae oo! Ande Nyasae oyio nabo arabaise gotorengereria atokonye titosira.”
english: The captain went to him and said, "How can you sleep? Get up and call on your god! Maybe he will take notice of us, and we will not perish."

ekegusii: Abagendi ba Tema nigo bakoriga‐rigia amache, naboigo abaonchoreria ba Seba basemeria koyanyora.
english: The caravans of Tema look for water, the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.

ekegusii: Omosenia chibao nigo akorambora ekerengo, bwata omong’ororia nekaramu ase ebao. Erio oyesenia neranda, oyeng’ororia ekeringerera, naende oyebaacha yaba omogwekano bw’omonto omonyakieni, oyobeka nyomba ime.
english: The carpenter measures with a line and makes an outline with a marker; he roughs it out with chisels and marks it with compasses. He shapes it in the form of man, of man in all his glory, that it may dwell in a shrine.

ekegusii: na abasenia be chibao, na abaagachi, na abaagachi b’amagena. Naende chibesa chiria chigorwe chibao, na amagena abaachire ase okoagachera enyomba.
english: the carpenters, the builders and the masons. Also have them purchase timber and dressed stone to repair the temple.

ekegusii: Ekero egari eria yaigete ase omogondo o Yoshua o Beti‐Semesi egatenenao, ase rigena rinene riarenge. Abanto bagaatia chibao chi’egari eria, erio bakarua chiombe chiria chikaba ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa ase Omonene.
english: The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and there it stopped beside a large rock. The people chopped up the wood of the cart and sacrificed the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

ekegusii: rikuruma eri rire ase oboremo agwo Makipela, moocha ya Mamure, ase ense ya Kanani. Oboremo boria Ibrahimu agorete korwa ase Efuroni Omohiti bobe aase ogotindeka.
english: the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre in Canaan, which Abraham bought as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, along with the field.

ekegusii: The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it, nor could the pine trees equal its boughs, nor could the plane trees compare with its branches-- no tree in the garden of God could match its beauty.
english: Emecharake ende ey’omogondo o Nyasae tiyayoetaneti, gose emebunduki tiyarenge ne chinsagia buna echiaye; na emeuru tiyarenge nebisagia buna ebiaye. Ee, omote onde bw’omogondo o Nyasae torenge omosiani buna oro.

ekegusii: Chindogio echio chi’abanto baria basirete ekiagera bakorete ebibe, tiga chisunyuntwe chiroisigwe, chibe ekemumeko gekomumeka egesasimero, ekiagera abanto baria nigo bachiruete ase obosio bw’Omonene; ase ayio chindogio echio konya chiabeire chinchenu. Echio nachio ekemanyererio ki’ogokurera.”
english: the censers of the men who sinned at the cost of their lives. Hammer the censers into sheets to overlay the altar, for they were presented before the LORD and have become holy. Let them be a sign to the Israelites."

ekegusii: Omoriibo o gati‐gati obekwe omogima, oriibe korwa ensinyo eyemo goika eyende.
english: The center crossbar is to extend from end to end at the middle of the frames.

ekegusii: Agachia koigwa amang’ana igoro ya Yeso, agatoma asare abagaaka b’Abayahudi komoboria ache agwenie omosomba oye.
english: The centurion heard of Jesus and sent some elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and heal his servant.

ekegusii: Oria omotang’ani bw’abarwani rigana akamoiraneria, “Omonene, inche tinyisaini aye orasoe inse y’ekerama kiane; korende kwana ring’ana rioka, na omosomba one nagwene.
english: The centurion replied, "Lord, I do not deserve to have you come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

ekegusii: Omotang’ani bw’abarwani rigana agachia korora aya, agatogia Nyasae, akabora, “Ekeene, omonto oyo nigo arenge omonyene oboronge.”
english: The centurion, seeing what had happened, praised God and said, "Surely this was a righteous man."

ekegusii: Na ekero abateneneri be chigari baroche ng’a ere tarenge omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, bakaonchoka, bagatiga komobwatia.
english: the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel and stopped pursuing him.

ekegusii: Chigari chia Nyasae nigo chire chilifu chinyinge mono, Omonene nigo are ase egati yabo buna nase Sinai, aase aye aachenu.
english: The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands; the Lord [has come] from Sinai into his sanctuary.

ekegusii: Chigari chi’esegi nigo chigotitiria ase chinchera; nigo chikobagachana ase chiraaro chi’omochie; nigo chikomesa buna ebieri bi’omorero, na kominyoka buna okomesa kw’embura.
english: The chariots storm through the streets, rushing back and forth through the squares. They look like flaming torches; they dart about like lightning.

ekegusii: Abakerubi abwo barambore chimbaba chiabo igoro y’Oboikaranso bw’Amabera, babobekere ekiriri, na amasio abo abe achikaine, na barabwo barigererie Oboikaranso bw’Amabera.
english: The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the cover.

ekegusii: Abakerubi abwo bakarambora chimbaba chiabo igoro y’Oboikaranso bw’Amabera, bakabobekera ekiriri, na amasio abo agachikana; na barabwo bakarigereria Oboikaranso bw’Amabera.
english: The cherubim had their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the cover.

ekegusii: Abakerubi nigo baramborete chimbaba chiabo igoro y’aase aria Esanduku eria yarenge, bagatuba Esanduku eria amo nemiaro yaye yare kobogorerigwa.
english: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and covered the ark and its carrying poles.

ekegusii: Abakerubi abwo nigo baramborete chimbaba chiabo igoro y’aase aria Esanduku eria yarenge, bagatuba Esanduku eria amo nemiaro yaye yare kobogorerigwa.
english: The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its carrying poles.

ekegusii: Nonya nabo oyio omoteneneri bw’ebinyugwa taba okoinyora Yusufu, korende akamweba.
english: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.

ekegusii: Eleazari, omomura o Haroni omokuani, nere orabe omonene igoro ase abaraai b’Abalawi, naende omoteneneri bw’abanto barabe bagokora emeremo ase Obomenyo Obochenu.
english: The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest. He was appointed over those who were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.

ekegusii: Abagambi b’abanto nigo baare gokira tibagokwana, batuba emenwa yabo namaboko.
english: the chief men refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands;

ekegusii: Oyorenge omoteneneri bw’Abalawi abamenyete Yerusalemu, nere Usi, mosinto o Bani, o Hasabia, o Matania, o Mika. Usi nigo arenge oyomo bw’ororeria rw’Asafu, abanto abarenge abateneneri b’amatera ase enyomba ya Nyasae.
english: The chief officer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. Uzzi was one of Asaph's descendants, who were the singers responsible for the service of the house of God.

ekegusii: Omoteneneri oria omonene akabaroka amarieta amayia, akaroka Danieli Beli‐Tesasari, na Hanania Sadaraka, na Mishaeli Meshaka, na Asaria Abedi‐Nego.
english: The chief official gave them new names: to Daniel, the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.

ekegusii: Abakuani abanene bakamosoera ase amang’ana amange.
english: The chief priests accused him of many things.

ekegusii: na buna abakuani na abanene baito bamoruete ase ekina ki’ogokwa, bakamobamba.
english: The chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him;

ekegusii: Abakuani abanene na aborokia b’amariko bakanyora amang’ana, bakarigia enchera y’okomosiria, ekiagera bamoirogete; naki emeganda yonsi egakumia ase okworokereria kwaye.
english: The chief priests and the teachers of the law heard this and began looking for a way to kill him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.

ekegusii: The chief priests and the teachers of the law were standing there, vehemently accusing him.
english: Abakuani abanene na aborokia b’amariko bagatenena, bakomosoera ne chinguru.

ekegusii: Abakuani abanene na ab’ekegambero bonsi bakarigia oborori igoro ase Yeso banyare komoita, korende tibabonyora,
english: The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for evidence against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they did not find any.

ekegusii: The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for false evidence against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
english: Erio abakuani abanene na ab’ekegambero bonsi bakarigia amang’ana ’oborimo ay’ogosoera Yeso, banyare komoita;

ekegusii: Erio abakuani abanene na Abayahudi bagatebia Pilato, “Torika ng’a, n’Omoruoti bw’Abayahudi, korende ng’a nigo arenge kobora: Inche nomoruoti bw’Abayahudi.”
english: The chief priests of the Jews protested to Pilate, "Do not write 'The King of the Jews,' but that this man claimed to be king of the Jews."

ekegusii: Korende abakuani abanene bakaimokia chibesa chiria chie chifeta bakabora, “Tari boronge gochibeka ase ekungo y’esadaka ya Nyasae, ekiagera chirochio nechie rigori ri’amanyinga.”
english: The chief priests picked up the coins and said, "It is against the law to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money."

ekegusii: Abagambi b’Edomu bakaondoka, abanto abanene ba Moabu bakabwatwa nomotengecho, na abanto bonsi ba Kanani bakerusia moyo.
english: The chiefs of Edom will be terrified, the leaders of Moab will be seized with trembling, the people of Canaan will melt away;

ekegusii: Omwana oria agakina, agatiga okogonka. Ase rituko riria Isaka atigete kogonka, Ibrahimu agakora omoyega omonene.
english: The child grew and was weaned, and on the day Isaac was weaned Abraham held a great feast.

ekegusii: Omwana oria gakinire, ekaba rituko erimo akagenda ase ise ase abanto barenge kogesa,
english: The child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the reapers.

ekegusii: Nebe ase engaki eyio abana kwauretwe barakwane ase oigwete, batebe: Aase aiga naagote mono, togareerie tonyore aase tokomenya.
english: The children born during your bereavement will yet say in your hearing, 'This place is too small for us; give us more space to live in.'

ekegusii: Abana nigo bagochora chinko, na abaise bauta omorero, na abakungu bagokonya obosie koroisia emegati ase enyasae enkungu eria ekorokwa Eting’ana ya Igoro. Naende baumora okoruegwa kw’ebinyugwa ase chinyasae ching’ao, bangechia naba nendamwamu.
english: The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead the dough and make cakes of bread for the Queen of Heaven. They pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.

ekegusii: Abana b’Amuramu nabwo aba: Haroni na Musa, na Miriamu omoiseke. Abana abamura ba Haroni nabwo aba: Nadabu na Abihu, Eleazari na Itamari.
english: The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

ekegusii: The children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.
english: Na mosinto o Ana nere Disoni, na omoiseke o Ana nere Oholibama.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ororeria rw’abasomba b’Omonene mbayeire ebe eyabo, boigo nabanto baria banchete erieta ri’Omonene mbamenye aroro.
english: the children of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell there.

ekegusii: Abana ba mosubati omino omochore bagokwanirie.
english: The children of your chosen sister send their greetings.

ekegusii: Abana b’abasomba bao mbamenye ase oborendi obuya, ne chinderia chiabo chigenderere komenya ase obosio bwao.”
english: The children of your servants will live in your presence; their descendants will be established before you."

ekegusii: Ise na ng’ina bagakumia ase aria akwanwa igoro asare.
english: The child's father and mother marveled at what was said about him.

ekegusii: Bagatomwa nekanisa, bagaeta egati ya Foiniki na Samaria, bakararia amang’ana ’okoonchoka kw’abanto b’Ebisaku, bakagokia abaminto bonsi.
english: The church sent them on their way, and as they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the Gentiles had been converted. This news made all the brothers very glad.

ekegusii: Abanto be chikanisa chi’Asia babakwanirie. Akwila na Priskila babakwanirie mono ase Omonene, amo nekanisa ere ime ase enyomba yabo.
english: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.

ekegusii: Enkoro yane nigo ere nemechando mono, teri nobotoereru, amatuko ’emechando anchicheire.
english: The churning inside me never stops; days of suffering confront me.

ekegusii: Abegenete korwa ase abarogete abachete amo na Petero, bagakumia, ekiagera nonya nabanto b’Ebisaku banyorire ekeegwa ki’Omoika Omochenu.
english: The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.

ekegusii: Emechie y’ensemo ya irianyi yasiekirwe ebiita biaye, monto onde takobiigora. Abayuda bonsi boosirwe bairirwe ase obosomba, bairirwe kegima.
english: The cities in the Negev will be shut up, and there will be no one to open them. All Judah will be carried into exile, carried completely away.

ekegusii: Emechie y’Aroeri neng’anywe etigwe ere bosa. Nigo erabe amarisio. Chitugo nchibe chikorara aroro, na onde tari orachioboyie.
english: The cities of Aroer will be deserted and left to flocks, which will lie down, with no one to make them afraid.

ekegusii: Beseri ase erooro, ase ense eraire eimokererete igoro, nigo orenge omochie bw’obotamero ase abanto b’egesaku kia Reuben, na Ramoti ase ense ya Gileadi ase abanto ba Gadi, na Golani ase ense ya Basani ase abanto ba Manase.
english: The cities were these: Bezer in the desert plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.

ekegusii: Omochie oyo oragererigwe, na ebinto bionsi ebire imeo biatananirwe ase Omonene. Rahabu bweka, omokungu oria omotayayi, amo nabanto bare nyomba mwaye nabwo baratigare bare moyo, ekiagera ere abisete abanto baria twatomete koroota ense.
english: The city and all that is in it are to be devoted to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house shall be spared, because she hid the spies we sent.

ekegusii: Omoriki bw’omochie agakiria abanto agateba, “Inwe abasacha b’Efeso, monto ki ore aa otamanyeti ng’a omochie bw’Abaefeso noro omorendi bwe hekalu y’Aritemi eria enene, na obw’omogwekano oria ogwete korwa igoro?
english: The city clerk quieted the crowd and said: "Men of Ephesus, doesn't all the world know that the city of Ephesus is the guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

ekegusii: Na omochie oria toganeiri erioba gose omotienyi biyobarere, ekiagera obonene bwa Nyasae bwabaririe omobaso, na etaya yaye n’Emanwa y’Eng’ondi.
english: The city does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp.

ekegusii: Omochie osarigwe kegima; ebiita biatagoirwe na konacha‐nachanwa.
english: The city is left in ruins, its gate is battered to pieces.

ekegusii: Naende ase chinchera chi’omochie oyio abana abange, abamura na abaiseke, inababe bakogosoreria aroro.
english: The city streets will be filled with boys and girls playing there."

ekegusii: Igo omochie oria okaba onaaririe goika omwaka o ikomi nomo bw’okogamba gwa Zedekia omoruoti.
english: The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

ekegusii: Na omochie oria nigo ore ne chinsanganio inye, obotambe na obogare bwaye nigo biareng’aine. Akarenga omochie nemoti eria. Nigo orenge chimaeli elifu eyemo, na amagana atano; obotambe na obogare bwaye, na gochia igoro kwaye nigo biareng’aine.
english: The city was laid out like a square, as long as it was wide. He measured the city with the rod and found it to be 12,000 stadia in length, and as wide and high as it is long.

ekegusii: eamate y’enyomba ya Lawi ensemo yaye, na abakungu babo ensemo yabo; eamate ya Simei ensemo yaye, na abakungu babo ensemo yabo;
english: the clan of the house of Levi and their wives, the clan of Shimei and their wives,

ekegusii: Akarangeria egesaku kia Yuda, na obomera bokagwera eamate ya Zera, Akarangeria eamate ya Zera, enyomba ase enyomba, na obomera bokagwera enyomba ya Sabidi.
english: The clans of Judah came forward, and he took the Zerahites. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward by families, and Zimri was taken.

ekegusii: Enyongo chinyama echio chiraiyekerwe goika yaatwe, korende onye chikoiyekerwa ase esuguria, rirorio ero esisikigwe na gosibigwa namache.
english: The clay pot the meat is cooked in must be broken; but if it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot is to be scoured and rinsed with water.

ekegusii: Ekemoa gokeranyorekane ng’a giasirire ekero eanga, gose egetambaa keria, gose gento kende gionsi keroisirie korwa ase risankwa, giasibigwe, rirorio gesibigwe eria kabere. Bono egento keria nakebe giachenekire.”
english: The clothing, or the woven or knitted material, or any leather article that has been washed and is rid of the mildew, must be washed again, and it will be clean."

ekegusii: ne riire riria ri’Omonene nigo riarenge igoro asebare ekero kia mobaso chingaki chinde chionsi barenge koimoka korwa ase ebitwori kogenda ase orogendo.
english: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

ekegusii: Embura eyio nigo egotwa gocha ase ense, yatwera mwanyabanto ase obonge.
english: the clouds pour down their moisture and abundant showers fall on mankind.

ekegusii: Amare agaitera amache; ne chinkoba chigaaka korwa igoro, chinsara chiao chikamesa ase chinsemo chionsi.
english: The clouds poured down water, the skies resounded with thunder; your arrows flashed back and forth.

ekegusii: Ogocha kw’omosaria oria nigo kore ogokora gwa Saitani, naende nkobe nokobua gwonsi, na ebikone, na amakumia ’oborimo,
english: The coming of the lawless one will be in accordance with the work of Satan displayed in all kinds of counterfeit miracles, signs and wonders,

ekegusii: Na buna amang’ana achigetwe ng’a egesike ki’omote getigwe amo nemeri, oboruoti bwao nabokoiranere ekero keria oramanye ng’a Oyore Igoro Mono nere okogamba.
english: The command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots means that your kingdom will be restored to you when you acknowledge that Heaven rules.

ekegusii: Erio omotang’ani oria omonene agaika aroro, akamobwata, agachika asibwe nebinyuri bibere. Akababoria, “Nere ng’o oyo, naende inki akora?”
english: The commander came up and arrested him and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.

ekegusii: Erio omotang’ani oria omonene agatiga omomura oria agende, akamotebia, “Totebia monto onde ng’a kwamanyirie aya.”
english: The commander dismissed the young man and cautioned him, "Don't tell anyone that you have reported this to me."

ekegusii: Omoteneneri oria bw’abarendi akaira Seraya, omokuani omonene, na Sefania, omokuani o kabere, na abarendi b’egesieri batato.
english: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

ekegusii: Omoteneneri oria bw’abarendi akaira Seraya, omokuani omonene, na Safania, omokuani o kabere, na abarendi b’egesieri batato.
english: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

ekegusii: Bakaira ne chibakuria chinke, ne chindogio chi’okorenta omorero, ne chisani, ne chinyongo, na ebibekerero bie chitaya, na ebitaabo bi’ogosambera ubani, na ebikombe bi’okoruerwa kw’ebinyugwa. Omoteneneri oria bw’abarendi akaira ebinto bionsi bie chitahabu chichenire, na ebie chifeta chichenire.
english: The commander of the imperial guard took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and bowls used for drink offerings-- all that were made of pure gold or silver.

ekegusii: Bakaira ne chindogio chi’okorenta omorero, amo ne chisani. Omoteneneri oria bw’abarendi akaira ebinto bionsi bie chitahabu na ebie chifeta.
english: The commander of the imperial guard took away the censers and sprinkling bowls-- all that were made of pure gold or silver.

ekegusii: Omotang’ani oria bw’omoganda okorwana esegi y’Omonene agatebia Yoshua, “Rusia ebikoroto biao, ekiagera aase agwo oteneine naachenu.” Na Yoshua agakora bo.
english: The commander of the LORD's army replied, "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.

ekegusii: Omotang’ani bw’abarwani elifu agachika arentwe ime ase enyomba enene y’abarwani, agachika aborigwe amang’ana aye ase okong’wanigwa emecharichi, erinde amanye engencho bakomwogerera eriogi buna eri.
english: the commander ordered Paul to be taken into the barracks. He directed that he be flogged and questioned in order to find out why the people were shouting at him like this.

ekegusii: Omotang’ani oria omonene akamobwata okoboko, akagenda nere ensemo, akamoboria bobisi, “Ing’ana ki obwate origetie gontebia?”
english: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside and asked, "What is it you want to tell me?"

ekegusii: Omotang’ani oria omonene agacha, akamotebia, “Ntebia, n’Omorumi ore?” Agateba, “Ee.”
english: The commander went to Paul and asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes, I am," he answered.

ekegusii: Erio abanene baria b’Abafilisti bakaboria, “Ninki Abaibirania aba bagokora aiga?” Akisi akabairaneria, “Oyo n’Daudi, omosomba o Saulo, omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli. Oyio obeire omenyete amo nainche goetania omwaka oyomo, tinana korora komocha asare korwa riria achete asende goika rero iga.”
english: The commanders of the Philistines asked, "What about these Hebrews?" Achish replied, "Is this not David, who was an officer of Saul king of Israel? He has already been with me for over a year, and from the day he left Saul until now, I have found no fault in him."

ekegusii: Abatang’ani baria b’abarendi amagana bagakora onsi koreng’ana buna Yehoyada omokuani abachigete. Kera oyomo akarenta abanto baye, baria barenge gokora emeremo ase rituko ri’Esabato na baria barenge korua ase emeremo ase rituko erio. Igo bakagenda ase Yehoyada omokuani.
english: The commanders of units of a hundred did just as Jehoiada the priest ordered. Each one took his men-- those who were going on duty on the Sabbath and those who were going off duty-- and came to Jehoiada the priest.

ekegusii: Naki amachiko aya, “Totomana, Toita, Toiba, Toba nokogania okobe”, na gakorabeo gochika konde gwonsi, kwabekeranigwe amo ase ring’ana eri, “Ancha omogisangio oo buna bweanchete.”
english: The commandments, "Do not commit adultery," "Do not murder," "Do not steal," "Do not covet," and whatever other commandment there may be, are summed up in this one rule: "Love your neighbor as yourself."

ekegusii: Ase omosangererekano oyio ogochika nokomo korabe asemore na ase omomenyi omenyete ase egati yaino. Okwo nakobe ogochika koragenderere botambe, ebiaare ase ebiaare. Buna inwe more, naboigo omomenyi omenyete ase egati yaino arabe ase obosio bw’Omonene.
english: The community is to have the same rules for you and for the alien living among you; this is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come. You and the alien shall be the same before the LORD:

ekegusii: nigo kiarenge ching’ondi chilifu amagana atato na emerongo etato na isano na ibere, na amagana atano (337,500),
english: the community's half-- was 337,500 sheep,

ekegusii: Na aborokigwa b’ababani, abarenge agwo Beteli, bagacha ase Elisha, bakamoboria, “Inee! Nomanyete ng’a rituko ria rero Omonene nache aire omonene oo arue asore?” Ere akabairaneria, “Ee, namanyire ayio, korende inwe kira‐kiri.”
english: The company of the prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" "Yes, I know," Elisha replied, "but do not speak of it."

ekegusii: Aborokigwa b’ababani, abarenge agwo Yeriko, bagacha ase Elisha, bakamoboria, “Inee! Nomanyete ng’a rituko ria rero Omonene nache aire omonene oo arue asore?” Ere akabairaneria, “Ee, namanyire ayio, korende inwe kira‐kiri.”
english: The company of the prophets at Jericho went up to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" "Yes, I know," he replied, "but do not speak of it."

ekegusii: Ekero aborokigwa b’ababani, baria barenge agwo Yeriko, bamoroche ore egeka egeke korwa asebare, bakabora, “Omoika bw’Elija nigo ore igoro ase Elisha.” Erio bakagenda komorotota, bagatung’ama inse, bakaumama ase obosio bwaye,
english: The company of the prophets from Jericho, who were watching, said, "The spirit of Elijah is resting on Elisha." And they went to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

ekegusii: Aborokigwa b’ababani bagatebia Elisha, “Rora aase aiga tomenyete inse y’oboteneneri bwao igo are aake mono asetore.
english: The company of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we meet with you is too small for us.

ekegusii: Timoria egesengi, ekiagera nigo gekoria eng’ang’ura, korende tikebwati ebitaago biatananegete; ase ayio tigechenegeti.
english: The coney, though it chews the cud, does not have a split hoof; it is unclean for you.

ekegusii: Ebisibo bi’amakweri nigo biang’etananete; ogoichanigwa gw’aase abakure gokambwata; nigo nabete nemechando na omoichano.
english: The cords of death entangled me, the anguish of the grave came upon me; I was overcome by trouble and sorrow.

ekegusii: The cords of death entangled me; the torrents of destruction overwhelmed me.
english: Obororo bw’amakweri bokong’etanana, chiooro chi’obobe chikandetera obwoba.

ekegusii: Obobe bw’amakweri nigo bwang’etananete, emeeto y’amakweri egantega na kombwata.
english: The cords of the grave coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.

ekegusii: Abanto baria abaango bairete amarube bakagenda ase kera omochie ase ense y’Efraimu na eya Manase, na goika eya Sabuloni, korende abanto bakabachecheria na kobachaya.
english: The couriers went from town to town in Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but the people scorned and ridiculed them.

ekegusii: Ase ogochika okwo kw’omoruoti abatomwa bakariina chibarasi chi’omoruoti chiare kominyoka bwango. Ogochika koria gokararigwa boigo agwo Susa, omochie oria omonene bw’eburi.
english: The couriers, riding the royal horses, raced out, spurred on by the king's command. And the edict was also issued in the citadel of Susa.

ekegusii: Obotambe bw’eraaro eyio bobe obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko rigana erimo, na obogare bwaye amaboko emerongo etano. Egetambaa keria geetanaine eraaro kebe nobotambe gochia igoro bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko atano na keroisigwe ne chiusi chi’egatani engiya chisisire. Chinterekerero chi’eraaro chibe echie chitaai.
english: The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.

ekegusii: na okobwatana koria kw’ogotianania akorete na Ibrahimu, na eira yaye y’ogotianania arierete Isaka.
english: the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.

ekegusii: na okobwatana koria gw’ogotianania akorete na Ibrahimu, na eira yaye y’ogotianania amorierete Isaka.
english: the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.

ekegusii: the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of hides of sea cows and the shielding curtain;
english: na egietubo ki’amasankwa e chimingichi, aakire etaago, na egietubo ki’amasankwa e ching’iti chia rooche, na etoto eria ekengete,

ekegusii: Eng’ombe na edubu nchiriserie amo, emori y’eng’ombe na emanwa y’edubu nchirare amo. Endo nebe ekorisia obonyansi buna eng’ombe.
english: The cow will feed with the bear, their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.

ekegusii: Oria bwosetwe na agasibwa nasiborwe bwango; ere tagokwa na koirwa ase embeera, na takoborwa endagera.
english: The cowering prisoners will soon be set free; they will not die in their dungeon, nor will they lack bread.

ekegusii: The crack of whips, the clatter of wheels, galloping horses and jolting chariots!
english: Igwa eriogi ri’emecharichi egoaka, na ogochura kw’amagoro e chigari, na ogw’okominyoka gwe chibarasi, na okorunda kw’amagoro e chigari.

ekegusii: Omosenia bwe chibao nigo akobeka omoturi bw’etahabu omokia, na omoturi ebioma obeka omoturagi chinguru, oteba, “Oborembo bw’okobwatania nobuya.” Erio babwatania omogwekano nemesumari tonyegera.
english: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and he who smooths with the hammer spurs on him who strikes the anvil. He says of the welding, "It is good." He nails down the idol so it will not topple.

ekegusii: Naboigo abaagachi ba Sulemani, na aba Hiramu amo nabanto b’omochie o Gebali bagakora emeremo y’okobaacha na gosenia amagena na koroisia chibao ase oboagacho boria.
english: The craftsmen of Solomon and Hiram and the men of Gebal cut and prepared the timber and stone for the building of the temple.

ekegusii: Nabo ebitongwa bionsi nigo biganyete nokogania okonene mono ase rituko riria abana ba Nyasae bagocha koorokigwa.
english: The creation waits in eager expectation for the sons of God to be revealed.

ekegusii: The creatures sped back and forth like flashes of lightning.
english: Erio ebitongwa biria bire moyo bikaba bikominyoka gochia aaria na aaria, buna okomesa gw’enkoba.

ekegusii: The crowd came up and asked Pilate to do for them what he usually did.
