english: The LORD will march out like a mighty man, like a warrior he will stir up his zeal; with a shout he will raise the battle cry and will triumph over his enemies.

ekegusii: Omonene takonyara kwabera omonto onga buna oyio, korende endamwamu yaye, ne risemi mbibe igoro y’omonto oyio, na okoragereria okwo gwonsi korikire ase ebuku eye nigo korabeere asare, na Omonene natinyie erieta ri’omonto oyio rirue inse y’erioba, tainyorwa.
english: The LORD will never be willing to forgive him; his wrath and zeal will burn against that man. All the curses written in this book will fall upon him, and the LORD will blot out his name from under heaven.

ekegusii: Nabakunorere emonga yaye engiya ere igoro, na abatwerie embura ase ense yaino ase chingaki chiganeirie. Nasesenie emeremo yaino yonsi mogokora, erinde monyare koa abanto b’ebisaku ebinge ebinto singo. Korende inwe timokoremerwa, erinde mochie gosaba singo.
english: The LORD will open the heavens, the storehouse of his bounty, to send rain on your land in season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations but will borrow from none.

ekegusii: Nabarentere amarwaire agoita akobabwatia, na inwe mosire korwa ase ense eria mogochia gosoa na koyeira ebe eyaino.
english: The LORD will plague you with diseases until he has destroyed you from the land you are entering to possess.

ekegusii: Omonene amorende na komokorera agenderere koba moyo, erinde arokwe oyosesenirie ase ense. Omonene tagotiga ababisa bamokorere buna banchete.
english: The LORD will protect him and preserve his life; he will bless him in the land and not surrender him to the desire of his foes.

ekegusii: Omonene nagambe kare na kare.”
english: The LORD will reign for ever and ever."

ekegusii: Omonene naite Yoabu ase okomocha kwaye kw’ogoitera amanyinga, ogokora okwo Daudi tata atamanyete. Yoabu nigo aitete nomoro Abineri mosinto o Neri, omochiki bw’abarwani esegi b’Abaisraeli, na Amasa mosinto o Yeteri, omochiki bw’abarwani esegi b’Abayuda. Abanto abwo babere nigo barenge abaronge, naende abaya komobua.
english: The LORD will repay him for the blood he shed, because without the knowledge of my father David he attacked two men and killed them with the sword. Both of them-- Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army-- were better men and more upright than he.

ekegusii: Omonene akairaneria abanto baye, akabatebia, “Rora, nkobatomera nde endagera, na edivai, na amaguta, na inwe namoisaneke; tinkobatiga mogenderere gochaywa ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku.
english: The LORD will reply to them: 'I am sending you grain, new wine and oil, enough to satisfy you fully; never again will I make you an object of scorn to the nations.

ekegusii: Omonene nansibore korwa ase amabe onsi, na antoorie goika nsoe ase oboruoti bwa igoro. Ogotogigwa nokwaye kare na kare. Amina.
english: The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and will bring me safely to his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

ekegusii: Omonene nkoirania are obonene bw’abanto ba Yakobo, ee, obwo bore obonene bw’Abaisraeli, ekiagera abasakori babasakoire na kobatiga bare bosa, babunire chinsagia chi’emesabibu yabo, bachitugutire inse.
english: The LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and have ruined their vines.

ekegusii: Omonene naimoke akore buna akorete ase egetunwa gia Perasimu; nabe nendamwamu buna abete ase Rikura ria Gibeoni; nakore ogokora kwaye kore okogeni, nakore emeremo yaye ere ey’ogokumia.
english: The LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim, he will rouse himself as in the Valley of Gibeon-- to do his work, his strange work, and perform his task, his alien task.

ekegusii: Omonene narume korwa Sayoni, aake eriogi riaye korwa Yerusalemu; igoro na ense nchitengechigwe. Korende Omonene nabe obotamero bw’abanto baye, na eburi enkong’u y’Abaisraeli.
english: The LORD will roar from Zion and thunder from Jerusalem; the earth and the sky will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.

ekegusii: Omonene nantoorie; ase ayio ntobe togotera amatera, ase okobugia amakano aane, ase obogima bwaito bwonsi, agwo ase enyomba y’Omonene.
english: The LORD will save me, and we will sing with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the temple of the LORD.

ekegusii: Omonene nabasiarere ase egati y’abanto b’ebisaku binde, nainwe abamoratigare nabake ase omobaro, namomenye ase egati y’abanto baria ase Omonene arabaire.
english: The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive among the nations to which the LORD will drive you.

ekegusii: “Omonene nachike ogosesenia kwaye gocha asemore, ase ebiage biaino, na ase emeremo yonsi mogokora; nabasesenie ase ense eyio Omonene, Nyasae oino, agochia kobaa ebe eyaino.
english: The LORD will send a blessing on your barns and on everything you put your hand to. The LORD your God will bless you in the land he is giving you.

ekegusii: rirorio Omonene narente asemore, na igoro ase abana baino, amaakwa are amanene na amatindi aragenderere ase engaki entambe.
english: the LORD will send fearful plagues on you and your descendants, harsh and prolonged disasters, and severe and lingering illnesses.

ekegusii: “Omonene nabarentere okoragererigwa, na obotantanu, na emechando ase emeremo yaino yonsi mogokora, goika mosirigwe na koera bwango ase engencho y’ogokora kwaino okobe, na ekiagera mwantigire inche.
english: The LORD will send on you curses, confusion and rebuke in everything you put your hand to, until you are destroyed and come to sudden ruin because of the evil you have done in forsaking him.

ekegusii: Omonene nabatige moriine chimeeri moirane gochia Misiri, orogendo orwo inche nabatebetie ng’a timokorogenda naende. Ekero morabe mwaikireo, ase okoremerwa kwaino namwerue inwe abanyene, morigie kweoonia ase ababisa baino mobe abasomba babo, abasacha na abakungu, korende ekero morabe mokwerwa igo, omonto tagotoka orabagore.”
english: The LORD will send you back in ships to Egypt on a journey I said you should never make again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.

ekegusii: Omonene namokore abe ekiorokererio ase amasio ’abanto b’ebisaku bionsi bi’Abaisraeli, na amorentere amaakwa onsi koreng’ana nokoragereria gw’okobwatana kw’ogotianania oko korikire ase ebuku eye y’amachiko.
english: The LORD will single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.

ekegusii: Omonene naake ense ya Misiri, nayeake na koyegwenia, na abanto b’aroro mbamoiranere Omonene, ere naigwe ogosaba kwabo abagwenie.
english: The LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; he will strike them and heal them. They will turn to the LORD, and he will respond to their pleas and heal them.

ekegusii: Nabaake noborwaire borakoore obogima, na obw’esosera, na obw’okobimbia omobere; narente riberera ri’egurugura entindi, na oborwaire bw’enyagetabo ase chindagera, na obw’okorigisia chindagera chiaino. Amaakwa ayio nababwatie goika abasirie kegima.
english: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, with blight and mildew, which will plague you until you perish.

ekegusii: “Omonene naremie Sayoni, naremie abatigarete bare ase amaturi. Naroisie aase aye abete erooro, abe buna omogondo o Edeni, na ense enyomo yaye ebe buna omogondo bw’Omonene. Omogoko na omochengo mbibe bikoigweka ime yaye, boigo okoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono, na amatera ay’ogotogia, mbibeo.
english: The LORD will surely comfort Zion and will look with compassion on all her ruins; he will make her deserts like Eden, her wastelands like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.

ekegusii: Omonene namorende ekero are borere arwarete, namogusuerie oborwaire bwaye.
english: The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed and restore him from his bed of illness.

ekegusii: Ribaga ri’embura egotwa ase riroba riaino, Omonene narente ebuse na omokenye bibatwere korwa igoro na kobasiria kegima.
english: The LORD will turn the rain of your country into dust and powder; it will come down from the skies until you are destroyed.

ekegusii: Ase omoika bw’okonacha ekina na gochena, Omonene nasibie obobe bw’abakungu ba Sayoni, naende achene abanto ba Yerusalemu korwa ase okomocha kwabo kw’ogoitera amanyinga.
english: The Lord will wash away the filth of the women of Zion; he will cleanse the bloodstains from Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

ekegusii: Omonene nakorende kogosoka na kogosoa, korwa bono na goika kare na kare.
english: the LORD will watch over your coming and going both now and forevermore.

ekegusii: Ekero Omonene arakore omobaro bw’abanto, nigo ararike, “Oyo na oyo nao baiboreretwe ime aaria.”
english: The LORD will write in the register of the peoples: "This one was born in Zion." Selah

ekegusii: Omonene nigo agendererete gokora ayare ay’oboronge ime y’omochie oria, tari gokora ayare amabe; emambia ase emambia nigo akoorokia oboronge bwaye bwamoreka; ere tari komocha koboorokia, korende abwo batari abanyaboronge tibari korora obosooku.
english: The LORD within her is righteous; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he dispenses his justice, and every new day he does not fail, yet the unrighteous know no shame.

ekegusii: Omonene okorire kera egento ase engencho gete, nonya nabakori amabe ase engencho ye rituko ri’emechando.
english: The LORD works out everything for his own ends-- even the wicked for a day of disaster.

ekegusii: Omonene nere okorua oboronge na ekeene ase abwo bonsi bagokorerwa bobe.
english: The LORD works righteousness and justice for all the oppressed.

ekegusii: Na Omonene aba ogokwana na Musa obosio ase obosio, buna omonto agokwana nomonto onde. Erio Musa aba okoirana gochia ase egetwori, korende Yoshua, omosomba oye omosae, mosinto o Nuni, tare korua ase Eema eria.
english: The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young aide Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.

ekegusii: Omonene akarika ase chibao chiria amang’ana aria aria arigete engaki eria entang’ani, amachiko ikomi aria konya akwanire nainwe agwo ase egetunwa, korwa ase egati‐gati y’omorero, ase rituko riria mwasangererekanete aroro. Erio Omonene akang’a chibao chiria,
english: The LORD wrote on these tablets what he had written before, the Ten Commandments he had proclaimed to you on the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly. And the LORD gave them to me.

ekegusii: “Rituko ria rero Omonene, Nyasae oo, ogochikire oigwere na kobwata amachiko aya na emeroberio echikire. Ase ayio oyarende mono na koyakora nenkoro yao yonsi, na omoyo oo bwonsi.
english: The LORD your God commands you this day to follow these decrees and laws; carefully observe them with all your heart and with all your soul.

ekegusii: “Inyora buna Omonene, Nyasae oino, abasesenirie ase emeremo yaino yonsi mwabeire mogokora. Nigo abeire obarendete ase orogendo rwaino ase erooro eye enene ase emiaka eye emerongo ene. Omonene, Nyasae oino, obeire amo nainwe, na inwe timwaremeretwe gento kende.”
english: The LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast desert. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.

ekegusii: Omonene Nyasae oino, obamentekanirie mono, na bono inwe nigo more abange mono buna ching’enang’eni chia igoro.
english: The LORD your God has increased your numbers so that today you are as many as the stars in the sky.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oino omonyene, nabatang’ane aserie ebisaku bionsi bire ase amasio aino, erinde moire ense yabo, na Yoshua nabe omoraai oino, buna Omonene atebire.
english: The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD said.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oino, nere oraserie abanto abwo babatame, nainwe moire ense yabo moyemenye, buna Omonene, Nyasae oino, abarierete eira.
english: The LORD your God himself will drive them out of your way. He will push them out before you, and you will take possession of their land, as the LORD your God promised you.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oo, oyomenyete ase egati yao, nigo are omorwani etuoni okogotooria. Ere nigo akogokerete nomogoko omonene. Nabe okirete‐kiri ore nobwanchani bwaye; akogokere nogotera kw’omogoko.”
english: The LORD your God is with you, he is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you, he will quiet you with his love, he will rejoice over you with singing."

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oino, narokie chinkoro chiaino, ne chinkoro chi’ororeria rwaino, nabae inwe ne chinderia chiaino chinkoro chi’okoigwera; erio nario moramwanche ne chinkoro chiaino chionsi, na emioyo yaino yonsi, mogenderere koba moyo.
english: The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, so that you may love him with all your heart and with all your soul, and live.

ekegusii: “Omonene, Nyasae oino, naserie korwa ase amasio aino abanto b’ebisaku ebio mogochia koira ense yabo na koyemenya. Nyuma Omonene kabasiririe,
english: The LORD your God will cut off before you the nations you are about to invade and dispossess. But when you have driven them out and settled in their land,

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oino, naserie ebisaku ebio ng’ora ng’ora, birue asemore. Timobaisa kobiseria biere kegima ase ekero ekemo gioka. Moise gokora bo, ching’iti chi’orosana nigo chiramentekane chibachande.
english: The LORD your God will drive out those nations before you, little by little. You will not be allowed to eliminate them all at once, or the wild animals will multiply around you.

ekegusii: Omonene Nyasae oino nabeke okoragereria okwo gwonsi igoro y’ababisa baino, na igoro ya baria babagechete na kobachanda.
english: The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies who hate and persecute you.

ekegusii: Korende ase egati y’abamino, Omonene, Nyasae oino, nabaimokerie omobani onga buna inche. Oyio nere moraigwere.
english: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own brothers. You must listen to him.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae oino, oria okobaraa, nere orabarwanere esegi buna mwaroche aya abakorerete ekero mwarenge Misiri,
english: The LORD your God, who is going before you, will fight for you, as he did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes,

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiabo, akagenderera kobatomera amang’ana ay’okobakurera goetera ase abatomwa baye, ekiagera arorerete abanto baye, na obomenyo bwaye, amabera.
english: The LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to them through his messengers again and again, because he had pity on his people and on his dwelling place.

ekegusii: Ase engaki eyio Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda, nigo abatebetie ng’a morere na kobokia amagombo, na mokigite chitukia chi’emetwe yaino, na kweboyia chigunia.
english: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, called you on that day to weep and to wail, to tear out your hair and put on sackcloth.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda, ochorire engaki ere nobotantanu, na ogotiringerwa inse, na omoichano, na engaki eyio nigo erache igoro ye Rikura ri’Amaroro. Ase engaki eyio chindwaki nchitagorwe chigwe inse, na ebirero mbiigweke gochia ase ebitunwa.
english: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, has a day of tumult and trampling and terror in the Valley of Vision, a day of battering down walls and of crying out to the mountains.

ekegusii: Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda, karakune ense, ero nigo ekonyititoka, na ebitongwa bionsi bireo bibe bikorera. Ense engima neimokererigwe igoro, naende eiranigwe inse, buna orooche rwa Naili rore agwo Misiri.
english: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, he who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live in it mourn-- the whole land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt--

ekegusii: Omonene oyore Omonene bw’Emeganda, narente ogosirigwa ase ense yonsi, buna achikire.
english: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land.

ekegusii: Omonene akaba nendamwamu enene ase Abaisraeli, akabatiga bakana‐goetanana ase erooro ase engaki y’emiaka emerongo ene, goika abanto bonsi b’ekiaare keria, abwo konya bakorire ebibe ase Omonene, bagasirigwa kegima.
english: The LORD's anger burned against Israel and he made them wander in the desert forty years, until the whole generation of those who had done evil in his sight was gone.

ekegusii: Erio Omonene akaba nendamwamu enene ase Usa, akamoaka, ekiagera akunete Esanduku eria ya Nyasae, na Usa agakwera agwo agwo.
english: The LORD's anger burned against Uzzah because of his irreverent act; therefore God struck him down and he died there beside the ark of God.

ekegusii: Erio Omonene akaba nendamwamu enene ase Usa, akamoaka, ekiagera akunete Esanduku eria; na Usa agakwera aroro ase obosio bwa Nyasae.
english: The LORD's anger burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. So he died there before God.

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria Omonene akaba nendamwamu enene, agatiana, akabora:
english: The LORD's anger was aroused that day and he swore this oath:

ekegusii: Omoakwa amaguta bw’Omonene, oyio orenge omoika bw’obogima bwaito, akabwatwa ne chiirima chiabo, oyio nere twatebete ng’a ase ekiriri kiaye nao toramenye ase egati y’ebisaku.
english: The LORD's anointed, our very life breath, was caught in their traps. We thought that under his shadow we would live among the nations.

ekegusii: Okoragereria kw’Omonene nigo kore ase chinyomba chi’abakori amabe, korende nigo agosesenia chinka chi’abanyene oboronge.
english: The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses the home of the righteous.

ekegusii: Okoboko kw’Omonene nigo kwabaagete, gokabarusia ase egetwori, goika bonsi bagasira kegima.”
english: The LORD's hand was against them until he had completely eliminated them from the camp.

ekegusii: Okoboko kw’Omonene gokaritoera abanto b’Asidodi. Ere agachanda na kwoboyia abanto bonsi b’Asidodi amo nab’orogongo orwo rwonsi, akabaaka bakariegwa namagumba.
english: The LORD's hand was heavy upon the people of Ashdod and its vicinity; he brought devastation upon them and afflicted them with tumors.

ekegusii: Okoboko kw’Omonene nigo kwarenge amo nabarabwo; abanto abange bakamwegena Omonene, na komoonchokera.
english: The Lord's hand was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.

ekegusii: Naki korwa asemore ring’ana ri’Omonene riaigurwe, tari ase Makedonia na Akaya oka, korende amang’ana akumire kera aase, ng’a imomwegenete Nyasae. Ase igo titogwenereti gokwana ring’ana rinde rionsi.
english: The Lord's message rang out from you not only in Macedonia and Achaia-- your faith in God has become known everywhere. Therefore we do not need to say anything about it,

ekegusii: “Rituko ria ikomi na kane ri’omotienyi bwe ritang’ani, chinsa chia mogoroba, nario Epasaka y’Omonene.
english: The LORD's Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.

ekegusii: Okoboko gw’okorio kw’Omonene nigo koimokererete igoro, ee, okoboko gw’okorio kw’Omonene nigo kogokora amang’ana ’ogokumia.”
english: The LORD's right hand is lifted high; the LORD's right hand has done mighty things!"

ekegusii: The lot came up for the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan. Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Judah and Joseph:
english: Obomera bwe ritang’ani bokagwera chiamate chi’egesaku kia Benjamin. Orogongo rwabo rokaba egati y’orogongo rw’egesaku kia Yuda na orw’ekia Yusufu.

ekegusii: Obomera bokagwera Selemia ase okorenda egeita kia moocha. Naende bagaakera Zakaria, omomura oye, obomera, bokamochora korenda egeita gia sugusu. Ere nigo arenge omosemia omong’aini.
english: The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him.

ekegusii: The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-Edom, and the lot for the storehouse fell to his sons.
english: Obomera bokagwera Obedi‐Edomu, bokamochora korenda egeita kia irianyi, na abamura baye bakaegwa korenda ebigachero.

ekegusii: Obomera nigo bokorutwa ase esaro ime, korende Omonene nere ogochora oyo bokogwera.
english: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

ekegusii: Supimu na Hosea bagachorwa korenda ensemo ya bosongo, agwo ase Egeita gia Saleketi, ase enchera egotiira, na oborendi obomo bogachikana nobonde.
english: The lots for the West Gate and the Shalleketh Gate on the upper road fell to Shuppim and Hosah. Guard was alongside of guard:

ekegusii: Omote oyio noro ore ekiriri kiaye; ee, emete enga buna emesobeti nigo eyeetanaine.
english: The lotuses conceal him in their shadow; the poplars by the stream surround him.

ekegusii: Inse y’ebinyomba ebio, ensemo ya moocha egesoero nkiarengeo ase omonto aranyare gosoera korwa ase eraaro ya isiko.
english: The lower rooms had an entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court.

ekegusii: Obogare bw’ebinyomba bia inse nigo bwarenge bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko atano, na ebie rirongo ria kabere amaboko atano na rimo, na ebie rirongo ria gatato amaboko atano na abere. Nigo akorete ebitambokero bikabwatana nenyasi ye Hekalu ase kera rirongo, erinde emeriibo egosiira kera rirongo etoorere ase ebitambokero ebio, etari gosoigwa ase enyasi.
english: The lowest floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits and the third floor seven. He made offset ledges around the outside of the temple so that nothing would be inserted into the temple walls.

ekegusii: Ere nigo akoimokereria abanto abaitongo igoro, na abwo bachandegete bakorera, nigo akobabeka ase oborendi obuya.
english: The lowly he sets on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.

ekegusii: Na abaringoria tibanyara gotenena ase obosio bwa Musa, ekiagera amagumba konya abariire barabwo buna Abamisiri bande.
english: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils that were on them and on all the Egyptians.

ekegusii: Abaringoria bagatebia Farao, “Eke nekiara kia Nyasae.” Korende Farao agakong’ia enkoro yaye, na buna Omonene atebete, akaanga kobaigwa.
english: The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." But Pharaoh's heart was hard and he would not listen, just as the LORD had said.

ekegusii: Ensemo y’enyomba yarenge Hekalu enyene nigo yarenge y’ekerengo ki’amaboko emerongo ene.
english: The main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.

ekegusii: Nyasae oria otongete igoro na ense, na enyancha, na ebinto bionsi bire imeo. Ere nigo agendererete koba omwegenwa goika kare na kare.
english: the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them-- the LORD, who remains faithful forever.

ekegusii: Na abwo babere, omonto oyio na mokaye, nigo barenge getirianda, na tibaare kororerana obosooku.
english: The man and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.

ekegusii: Omonto oria akairaneria, “Ring’ana eri neri’ogokumia, ng’a inwe timomanyeti aase arure, na ere ondamokirie amaiso.
english: The man answered, "Now that is remarkable! You don't know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.

ekegusii: Akamoboria, “Naki okorokwa?” Akamoiraneria, “Yakobo.”
english: The man asked him, "What is your name?" "Jacob," he answered.

ekegusii: The man became rich, and his wealth continued to grow until he became very wealthy.
english: Omonto oyio akaba ne chinguru, akagenderera komenteka gokina, goika akaba nokobua okonene.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’ayio omonto oria akang’ira gochia ase egesieri gie Hekalu. Nkarora amache akorwa inse y’egesona gie Hekalu, agotirimboka gochia moocha ase enyomba eria yarochie. Amache aria agaeta korwa inse y’ensemo ya moocha ye Hekalu agwo irianyi y’egesasimero.
english: The man brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water coming out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east). The water was coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.

ekegusii: Omonto oria obegete eanga y’egatani, oria oteneine ase amache a rooche igoro, akarambora okoboko kwaye gw’okorio na ogw’okobee gochia igoro; nkamoigwa ogotiana asare oyore moyo goika kare na kare ng’a aya nigo araikeranigwe ase ekero ekemo, na ebiro bibere, na ekeng’ese gi’ekero, na ekero okobua kw’abanto abachenu korabe gwasirigwe kegima.
english: The man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, lifted his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by him who lives forever, saying, "It will be for a time, times and half a time. When the power of the holy people has been finally broken, all these things will be completed."

ekegusii: Omonto oria agakora buna Yusufu amotebetie, agasoyia abanto abwo nyomba ime.
english: The man did as Joseph told him and took the men to Joseph's house.

ekegusii: Na omonto oria orusetigwe ebirecha akamosorora abe amo nere, korende Yeso akamokania, akabora,
english: The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,

ekegusii: omonto oyio nabwate oborwaire bwa ukoma, ere tachenegeti. Omokuani atebe ng’a omonto oyio tachenegeti; oborwaire nigo bore ase omotwe oye.
english: the man is diseased and is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean because of the sore on his head.

ekegusii: Omonto oria o Nyasae akamoboria, “Ng’ai kiagwera?” Ekero omonto oria amworogetie aase aria, Elisha akanacha egete, agakeruta gochia imeo, akagera egesire keria kegacheng’enena amache igoro.
english: The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, Elisha cut a stick and threw it there, and made the iron float.

ekegusii: Omonto oria o Nyasae agacha ase omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, akamotebia, “Aya naro Omonene atebire: Abasiiria batebire ng’a Omonene nigo are enyasae y’ebitunwa, korende tari enyasae y’ense omweya. Ase ayio, nimbeke omoganda oyo omonene bwonsi ase okoboko kwao, naye nomanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene.”
english: The man of God came up and told the king of Israel, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because the Arameans think the LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys, I will deliver this vast army into your hands, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"

ekegusii: Korende omobani oria orwete ense ya Yuda akamoiraneria, “Tinkoirana amo naye, gose tingwancha ondoisie nyomba mwao; tinkoria endagera amo naye gose konywa amache aase aiga.
english: The man of God said, "I cannot turn back and go with you, nor can I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.

ekegusii: Korende omonto oria o Nyasae agatoma amang’ana ase omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, akamotebia, “Bwerende, tobaisa goetera aase aiga, ekiagera Abasiiria nao bakare.”
english: The man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Beware of passing that place, because the Arameans are going down there."

ekegusii: Omonto oria o Nyasae akaba nendamwamu asare, akamotebia, “Nigo yagwenerete orase inse ara gatano, gose ara gatano na rimo; kware gokora igo nanga nigo kwabua Abasiiria na kobasiria kegima, korende bono nigo orabaake ara gatato rioka”.
english: The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck the ground five or six times; then you would have defeated Aram and completely destroyed it. But now you will defeat it only three times."

ekegusii: Omonto okobwatia chinchera chi’oboronge nigo ararendwe buya, korende oyo okobwatia chinchera chimbe nigo aramanyekane.
english: The man of integrity walks securely, but he who takes crooked paths will be found out.

ekegusii: Ere nigo agotama ekiagera nomorikwa, gose tarengerereti amang’ana e ching’ondi.
english: The man runs away because he is a hired hand and cares nothing for the sheep.

ekegusii: Omonto oria agantebia, “Aye mwanyabanto, rigereria orore namaiso ao, na otegerere oigwe namato ao, naende orengererie mono igoro y’aya onsi ngochia gokworokia, ekiagera aye nigo kwarentirwe aase aiga, erinde nkworokie amang’ana ayio. Amang’ana ayio onsi orarore, oyatebie Abaisraeli.”
english: The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes and hear with your ears and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Tell the house of Israel everything you see."

ekegusii: Omonto oria akamoiraneria, “Omokungu oyo kwang’ete ng’a abe amo nainche, nere ong’ete amatunda ’omote oyio, na inche nkaria.”
english: The man said, "The woman you put here with me-- she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it."

ekegusii: Erio omonto oria agateba, “Bono oyo neriuga korwa ase amauga aane, ne chinyama korwa ase chinyama chiane; ere nigo ararokwe omokungu, ekiagera nigo arusirie ase omosacha.”
english: The man said, "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called 'woman', for she was taken out of man."

ekegusii: Omonto oria akamoiraneria, “Ning’o okobegete koba omoteneneri na omogayani igoro yaito? Inee! Nigo origetie kong’ita buna gwaita Omomisiri oria?” Aya akagera Musa akoboa. Ere agateba ase omoyo oye ime, “Ndoche ng’a amang’ana aya amanyekanire.”
english: The man said, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and thought, "What I did must have become known."

ekegusii: The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
english: Omonto oria akagenda, agatebia Abayahudi amang’ana, ng’a Yeso nere omokorete koba omogima.

ekegusii: Erio oria orentete amang’ana akamoiraneria, “Abaisraeli batamire korwa ase Abafilisti, abanto abange baitirwe; Hofini na Finehasi, abana bao babere, bakure; boigo Esanduku ya Nyasae yairirwe.”
english: The man who brought the news replied, "Israel fled before the Philistines, and the army has suffered heavy losses. Also your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."

ekegusii: The man who burns it must also wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he too will be unclean till evening.
english: Na omonto oria ogosamba eng’ombe eria goika asibie chianga chiaye, esibie nomobere namache, ere nabe oyotachenegeti goika omogoroba oyio.

ekegusii: Omonto oria orasambe ebinto ebio nigo arasibie chianga chiaye, esibie nomobere namache; nyuma y’ayio amanye gosoa ase egetwori.
english: The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may come into the camp.

ekegusii: The man who eats everything must not look down on him who does not, and the man who does not eat everything must not condemn the man who does, for God has accepted him.
english: Oyokoria tachaya oria otari koria, na oria otari koria tagambia oria okoria, ekiagera Nyasae omwancheire.

ekegusii: Korende oyogosoera gesieri oyio nomorisia bwe ching’ondi.
english: The man who enters by the gate is the shepherd of his sheep.

ekegusii: Omonto oria orabuuche ribu riria, asibie chianga chiaye, nere nabe oyotachenegeti goika omogoroba oyio. Oko nakwo ogochika koragenderere botambe ase Abaisraeli na ase omomenyi omenyete ase egati yabo.
english: The man who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he too will be unclean till evening. This will be a lasting ordinance both for the Israelites and for the aliens living among them.

ekegusii: Oria oetwe chitalanta isano agacha ne chitalanta chinde isano, akabora: Omonene, nkwang’ete chitalanta isano, rora nanyorire ebitoki, chitalanta chinde isano.
english: The man who had received the five talents brought the other five. 'Master,' he said, 'you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.'

ekegusii: The man who had received the five talents went at once and put his money to work and gained five more.
english: Oria oetwe chitalanta isano akagenda ara rimo, agachionchoreria, akanyora ebitoki, chitalanta chinde isano.

ekegusii: Oyobwanchire oborori bwaye oorokirie Nyasae maiso marore, ng’a noyo bw’ekeene.
english: The man who has accepted it has certified that God is truthful.

ekegusii: Ase rituko ria gatato, na ase rituko ria gatano na kabere, omonto ochenegete anyororokie amache ase oria otachenegeti. Ase igo ase rituko ria gatano na kabere namochene; ere oria ogochia gochenwa nasibie chianga chiaye, esibie nomobere namache, na ase engaki ya mogoroba nabe ochenekire.
english: The man who is clean is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third and seventh days, and on the seventh day he is to purify him. The person being cleansed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and that evening he will be clean.

ekegusii: Oyoranche obogima bwaye, nabosirie; oyorageche obogima bwaye ase ense eye, nabogache goika obogima bwa kare na kare.
english: The man who loves his life will lose it, while the man who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.

ekegusii: Nere oyio osaretie ense ekaba erooro, naende akaonchorana emechie y’ense, oria otarenge gosibora abasibwa baye bagende ase chinka chiabo?
english: the man who made the world a desert, who overthrew its cities and would not let his captives go home?"

ekegusii: Naboigo oyogosimeka, na oyokobeka amache nigo bareng’anetie; na kera omonto nanyore eng’eria yaye koreng’ana buna emeremo yaye ere.
english: The man who plants and the man who waters have one purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.

ekegusii: Nere oyoyaroche akaba kirori, na oborori bwaye nobw’ekeene, nere omanyire ng’a igo agokwana ekeene, erinde inwe monyare kwegena.
english: The man who saw it has given testimony, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, and he testifies so that you also may believe.

ekegusii: Ere oyogoteba, “Nimomanyete,” na tabwateti amachiko aye, oyio nomonyaborimo, gose ekeene tikeri ime yaye.
english: The man who says, "I know him," but does not do what he commands is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

ekegusii: Omonto onde bwensi ore omomwenu na kwanga koigwera omokuani oyio ogotenena agwo ase obosio bw’Omonene, Nyasae oino, gose aange koigwera omogambi, ere goika aitwe akwe. Goika morusie obobe borue ase Abaisraeli.
english: The man who shows contempt for the judge or for the priest who stands ministering there to the LORD your God must be put to death. You must purge the evil from Israel.

ekegusii: Omonto karekage ng’a namanyete ring’ana rinde rionsi, oyio taramanya nonya mbono buna emogwenerete amanye.
english: The man who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.

ekegusii: Ogosesenigwa kw’omonto konya obeire ang’e gosira nigo gwanchicherete, nkagera ababoraka bagatera nechinkoro chire nomogoko.
english: The man who was dying blessed me; I made the widow's heart sing.

ekegusii: Korende oria ogwenetigwe tamomanyete gose ning’o. Yeso nigo erusananetie, ekiagera abanto abange barenge aase aria.
english: The man who was healed had no idea who it was, for Jesus had slipped away into the crowd that was there.

ekegusii: Nabo mwanyabanto ore ne chingencho chia kare, takonyora ebiegwa bi’Omoika o Nyasae, naki asare ere ebi nebiriri, gose takonyara kobimanya, ekiagera nigo bikomanyekana ase chinguru chi’Omoika.
english: The man without the Spirit does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

ekegusii: Omonto oyio arente emingichi eyemo asende inche Omonene, agwo ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano, ebe ekeng’wanso gi’okomocha kwaye.
english: The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for a guilt offering to the LORD.

ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, amatunda amansu nigo agotioka rimisu rigiya mono, na igoro y’ebisieri biaito nareo amatunda ao ao are amaya mono, amakoro na amayia; ayio nasangereirie ase ogokogachera.
english: The mandrakes send out their fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, both new and old, that I have stored up for you, my lover.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’ayio mana ekaera, tiyagwa, na Abaisraeli tibanyora mana naende. Korwa ase omwaka oria oria, bariete okwama gwa Kanani.
english: The manna stopped the day after they ate this food from the land; there was no longer any manna for the Israelites, but that year they ate of the produce of Canaan.

ekegusii: Mana nigo yarenge kororekana buna chinyeke chi’amaemba enkomba.
english: The manna was like coriander seed and looked like resin.

ekegusii: Omonto oria nigo arenge korokwa Elimeleki, na mokaye Naomi, na abamura baye babere Mahaloni na Kilioni. Barabwo n’Abaefarati barenge. Ekero bamenyete aaria Moabu,
english: The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Kilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem, Judah. And they went to Moab and lived there.

ekegusii: na abaagachi b’amagena na ababaachi amagena. Naende nigo barenge kogora chibao, na amagena asenirie, ase okoroiseria enyomba y’Omonene aase yatagogete. Chibesa echio nigo chiaruetwe ase kera egento kiaganeirie ase okoroiseria enyomba eria.
english: the masons and stonecutters. They purchased timber and dressed stone for the repair of the temple of the LORD, and met all the other expenses of restoring the temple.

ekegusii: omonene bw’omosomba oria nigo arache rituko atakagereti, na ensa atamanyeti;
english: The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he is not aware of.

ekegusii: omonene bw’omosomba oria nachiche rituko atakagereti, na ensa atamanyeti, nigo aramonachane abe ebing’ese, namoe ensemo yaye amo nabategeneti.
english: The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he is not aware of. He will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.

ekegusii: Ring’ana erio tiriamogwenera Ibrahimu nonya ng’ake, ase engencho y’omwana oye.
english: The matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son.

ekegusii: Ebirubo nigo biichire namaicho e ching’ondi, na amakura nigo atubire ne chindagera. Kera egento nigo kegochenga nomogoko.
english: The meadows are covered with flocks and the valleys are mantled with grain; they shout for joy and sing.

ekegusii: Orobebe rwaye rw’okoyorenga narogende aare, rorongee gochia ase ekegoro kia Garebu, naende roonchoke rogende roike Goa.
english: The measuring line will stretch from there straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn to Goah.

ekegusii: Chinyama chi’ekeng’wanso kiaye ki’omorembe ki ogoaka ng’a mbuya mono chiriegwe ase rituko riria gekoruegwa; tichibaisa gotigara nonya ne chinsinini goika rituko ria kabere.
english: The meat of his fellowship offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day it is offered; he must leave none of it till morning.

ekegusii: Oyio takoinyorwa ase ense nonya ng’ake, gose nonya nerieta riaye tirikogenderera koinyorwa agwo ase enchera.
english: The memory of him perishes from the earth; he has no name in the land.

ekegusii: Okoinyorwa kw’omonyene oboronge nigo gokorenta ogosesenigwa, korende erieta ri’omokori amabe nigo riragunde.
english: The memory of the righteous will be a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.

ekegusii: Na abanto abwo nabatugi be chitugo, na bono barentire chitugo chiabo, ching’ondi ne chiombe, na binde bionsi bare nabio.
english: The men are shepherds; they tend livestock, and they have brought along their flocks and herds and everything they own.'

ekegusii: Abanto amarieta abo atoretwe bakaimoka, bakaboyia baria boosetwe barenge gesobono, bakababekera chianga na ebikoroto, bakabaa nendagera na ebinyugwa, bakabaaka namaguta. Naende bakariinia ase chitigere baria batarenge ne chinguru, bakaira baria bonsi boosetwe, amo nebisakorwa bionsi gochia Yeriko, Omochie bw’Emekendo, ase abamwabo bamenyete. Nyuma y’ayio bakairana Samaria.
english: The men designated by name took the prisoners, and from the plunder they clothed all who were naked. They provided them with clothes and sandals, food and drink, and healing balm. All those who were weak they put on donkeys. So they took them back to their fellow countrymen at Jericho, the City of Palms, and returned to Samaria.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bagakora emeremo ase obwegenwa. Aba nabwo abateneneri babegetwe igoro asebare: Yahati na Obadia, Abalawi b’ororeria rwa Merari, na Zakaria, na Mesulamu b’ororeria rwa Kohati, na Abalawi bonsi bamanyete kobugia ebinto bi’amatera.
english: The men did the work faithfully. Over them to direct them were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites descended from Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, descended from Kohath. The Levites-- all who were skilled in playing musical instruments--

ekegusii: Abanto ba Babeli bakaroisia omogwekano bw’enyasae yabo Sukoti‐Benoti, bakayosasima na abanto ba Kuta omogwekano o Nerigali, na abanto ba Hamati oyo bw’Asima,
english: The men from Babylon made Succoth Benoth, the men from Cuthah made Nergal, and the men from Hamath made Ashima;

ekegusii: Abamwabo Yusufu bagaikaransigwa ase obosio bwaye, bakaroberigwa gochakera ase oria omonene kogenderera goika ase oria omoke. Bonsi kobaikaransire, bakarigererania, bagakumia.
english: The men had been seated before him in the order of their ages, from the firstborn to the youngest; and they looked at each other in astonishment.

ekegusii: Baria babegetwe gokora emeremo, bagakora omokia, na emeremo ekagenderera buya goika enyomba eria ekaroisigwa, ekaba buna enyia, naende enkong’u.
english: The men in charge of the work were diligent, and the repairs progressed under them. They rebuilt the temple of God according to its original design and reinforced it.

ekegusii: Aba iga batoire ase amarieta abo nabwo barenge abateneneri be chiamate chiabo. Chiamate echi chikamentekana mono.
english: The men listed above by name were leaders of their clans. Their families increased greatly,

ekegusii: Abanto ba Ai bagachia korigereria nyuma, bakarora erioki korwa ase omochie rikoimoka igoro. Bagasinywa gotama gochia aaria na aaria, ekiagera Abaisraeli abwo konya batamire gochia erooro bakairana kobaumokera.
english: The men of Ai looked back and saw the smoke of the city rising against the sky, but they had no chance to escape in any direction, for the Israelites who had been fleeing toward the desert had turned back against their pursuers.

ekegusii: Abaamoni na Abamoabu bakaumokera korwania abanto b’ebigoro bia Seiri, bakabasiria kegima, na ekero basiretie abanto abwo, Abaamoni na Abamoabu bagaitana, bagakoorana.
english: The men of Ammon and Moab rose up against the men from Mount Seir to destroy and annihilate them. After they finished slaughtering the men from Seir, they helped to destroy one another.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Bethlehemu: rigana erimo, na emerongo ebere, na batato (123);
english: the men of Bethlehem 123

ekegusii: Abanto ba Bethlehemu na Netofa: rigana erimo, na emerongo etano na etato, na batano na batato (188);
english: the men of Bethlehem and Netophah 188

ekegusii: Abanto b’Efraimu bagasangererekana amo, bakaamboka gochia Safoni, bagakwana na Yefta, bakamotebia, “Nase ki kwagendete korwania Abaamoni, ko tigwatorangeria togende komo? Bono ntorigetie gosamba enyomba yao, naye boigo togosamberao.”
english: The men of Ephraim called out their forces, crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you go to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We're going to burn down your house over your head."

ekegusii: Abanto b’Efraimu, abwo babogoretie amata, bakaonchoka bagatama ase rituko ri’esegi.
english: The men of Ephraim, though armed with bows, turned back on the day of battle;

ekegusii: Abaisraeli na Abayuda, baria bamenyete ase emechie y’Abayuda, bakarenta ensemo ya ikomi ye chiombe na eye ching’ondi, ebinto baatananete ase Omonene, Nyasae obo; ebio bakabibeka amo, bikaba chitui.
english: The men of Israel and Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tithe of their herds and flocks and a tithe of the holy things dedicated to the LORD their God, and they piled them in heaps.

ekegusii: Bono ekemanyererio giancheranetwe ase egati y’ekeombe ekenene ki’abarwani b’Abaisraeli na abanto bebisete baboete nakio eke: Ekero barenge korora rikundesi ri’erioki rigochongororoka korwa ase omochie oria,
english: The men of Israel had arranged with the ambush that they should send up a great cloud of smoke from the city,

ekegusii: Bono Abaisraeli konya barire eira na gotiana agwo Misipa ng’a, “Onde tari ase egati yaito oranyare korua omwana oye omoiseke konyuomwa nomonto bw’egesaku kia Benjamin.”
english: The men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: "Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite."

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bakaimoka korwa agwo Misipa, bakabwatia Abafilisti goika Beti‐Kari, bakabaitera inchera.
english: The men of Israel rushed out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, slaughtering them along the way to a point below Beth Car.

ekegusii: Korende Abaisraeli bagatebia Abahivi baria, “Naki rende torakore okobwatana nainwe? Aande gose nigo momenyete ase egati yaito.”
english: The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "But perhaps you live near us. How then can we make a treaty with you?"

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bagancha koigwa endagera yabo, korende tibarigia ogosemia korwa ase Omonene.
english: The men of Israel sampled their provisions but did not inquire of the LORD.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bakairana naende korwania Ababenjamin bakabaita nemioro, bagaita abanto, ne chitugo, bagasiria ebinto bionsi banyorete aroro. Bagasamba nomorero emechie yonsi yarenge ase ensemo eria.
english: The men of Israel went back to Benjamin and put all the towns to the sword, including the animals and everything else they found. All the towns they came across they set on fire.

ekegusii: na abanto babo bagasoka, bakagenda korwania Ababenjamin. Bakaroberia abarwani korwana esegi ase omochie o Gibea,
english: The men of Israel went out to fight the Benjamites and took up battle positions against them at Gibeah.

ekegusii: Igo Abaisraeli bakabugwa bakabekwa inse y’obogambi bw’Abayuda, na Abayuda nigo babuete ekiagera basemeretie Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiabo.
english: The men of Israel were subdued on that occasion, and the men of Judah were victorious because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Yeriko bakamobwatia, bakaagacha ensemo ende; na oyobwatetie abanto aba, n’Sakuri, mosinto o Imuri.
english: The men of Jericho built the adjoining section, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to them.

ekegusii: The men of Judah also took Gaza, Ashkelon and Ekron-- each city with its territory.
english: Abayuda bakaira Gasa, na Asikeloni, na Ekironi, amo ne chinsemo chiaetanaine emechie eyio.

ekegusii: Abayuda bakababoria, “Nase ki mwachire gotorwania?” Barabwo bakairaneria, “Nigo twachire gosiba Samison, tomokorere ere buna atokorera intwe.”
english: The men of Judah asked, "Why have you come to fight us?" "We have come to take Samson prisoner," they answered, "to do to him as he did to us."

ekegusii: Abayuda bakarwania Yerusalemu bakayoira. Bagaita abanto b’aroro nemioro, naende bagasamba omochie nomorero.
english: The men of Judah attacked Jerusalem also and took it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Nineva nabatenene ase rituko ri’ekina amo nabanto b’ekegori eke, na barabwo nabakenachere ekina, ekiagera barabwo nigo baonchogete ase okorandia kwa Yona, na rora, oyobuete Yona naiga are.
english: The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now one greater than Jonah is here.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Nineva nabatenene ase rituko ri’ekina amo nabanto b’ekegori eke, na barabwo nabakenachere ekina, ekiagera baonchogete ase okorandia kwa Yona; na rora, oyobuete Yona naiga are.
english: The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now one greater than Jonah is here.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Reuben, na aba Gadi, na ekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase bagatang’ana Abaisraeli, babogoretie ebirwanero bi’esegi, buna Musa abatebetie,
english: The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over, armed, in front of the Israelites, as Moses had directed them.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli abarenge ase omochie ime bagatirimboka gochiao. Ase igo abanto ba Ai bagaetananwa kegima n’Abaisraeli, na bonsi bagaitwa. Onde tatigarete otooregete,
english: The men of the ambush also came out of the city against them, so that they were caught in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. Israel cut them down, leaving them neither survivors nor fugitives.

ekegusii: Abanto b’omochie oria bagatebia Elisha, “Omochie oyo ore omuya, buna aye omonene oito oyoroche, korende amache areo namabe, ne riroba ri’ense eye tiriri kwama endagera.”
english: The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, our lord, this town is well situated, as you can see, but the water is bad and the land is unproductive."

ekegusii: Erio abarendi babo b’eburi bakarangeria Yonathani amo nomobogoreria bw’ebirwanero biaye, bakabatebia, “Inchuo tiira gocha aa asetore, tobatebie ring’ana.” Yonathani agatebia omomura oria, “Mbwatie, totiire gochia aroro, ekiagera Omonene obabekire ase amaboko ’Abaisraeli.”
english: The men of the outpost shouted to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, "Come up to us and we'll teach you a lesson." So Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Climb up after me; the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."

ekegusii: Erio abanto b’omochie oria bagatebia Yoashi, “Morente omomura oyio oo aiga, ere goika aitwe, ekiagera otagoire egesasimero kia Baali, na otagoire omote oria bw’Asera orenge ensemo yaye.”
english: The men of the town demanded of Joash, "Bring out your son. He must die, because he has broken down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it."

ekegusii: Naende bakabeka ebikoroto ebigotu biatandogete, ne chiganchwa chingotu, na emegati bairete nigo yarenge emeboosu na emegundo.
english: The men put worn and patched sandals on their feet and wore old clothes. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.

ekegusii: Bakamotebia, “Nigo twatomirwe na Kornelio, omotang’ani bw’abarwani rigana, omonto omoronge, omoirogete Nyasae, oyogokwanwa buya negesaku gionsi ki’Abayahudi. Natebigwa nomomalaika omochenu ng’a atome abanto asore gokorangeria ogende bwoye, anyare koigwa amang’ana korwa asore.”
english: The men replied, "We have come from Cornelius the centurion. He is a righteous and God-fearing man, who is respected by all the Jewish people. A holy angel told him to have you come to his house so that he could hear what you have to say."

ekegusii: Abanto baria bakamotebia, “Intwe natosiborwe korwa ase eira twatianete, onye aye togokora aya tokoboria.
english: The men said to her, "This oath you made us swear will not be binding on us

ekegusii: Abanto ba Daudi bakamotebia, “Rituko eri ndiria Omonene agotebetie ng’a nabeke omobisa oo ase okoboko kwao, naye omokore buna oranche.” Erio Daudi agachoba ng’ora‐ng’ora, akabutora omokoba bw’eganchwa ya Saulo bobisi.
english: The men said, "This is the day the LORD spoke of when he said to you, 'I will give your enemy into your hands for you to deal with as you wish.'" Then David crept up unnoticed and cut off a corner of Saul's robe.

ekegusii: Erio bakamobwata, bakamoira.
english: The men seized Jesus and arrested him.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakabeera aroro amo na Daudi ase amatuko atato, bakaba bakoria na konywa, ekiagera abamwabo konya babaariganeirie ebinto bionsi.
english: The men spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, for their families had supplied provisions for them.

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria abanto bakaba bagochoba gosoa ase omochie ime buna abanto bagotama korwa ase esegi bare nobosooku ase engencho y’ayio.
english: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.

ekegusii: Abanto baria nigo barenge barigereretie banyore ekemanyererio, na ekero baigwete ring’ana “Oyominto” bakairaneria bwango, “Ee, momura omino Beni‐Hadadi.” Erio omoruoti akabatebia, “Genda momorente!” Beni‐Hadadi agacha ase omoruoti, na omoruoti akamochika ariine egari yaye.
english: The men took this as a good sign and were quick to pick up his word. "Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad!" they said. "Go and get him," the king said. When Ben-Hadad came out, Ahab had him come up into his chariot.

ekegusii: Abanto abagendete amo nere bagatenena, bagakira‐kiri; bakaigwa eriogi, korende tibarora monto.
english: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless; they heard the sound but did not see anyone.

ekegusii: Erio abanto baria bakarua agwo, bakagenda gochia Sodomu, korende Ibrahimu agatigara oteneine agwo ase obosio bw’Omonene.
english: The men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.

ekegusii: Abanto baria bagakumia, bagateba, “Monto ki oyo, nonya nomwaga na enyancha bikomoigwera?”
english: The men were amazed and asked, "What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the waves obey him!"

ekegusii: Ekero baria baegwa ribaga, bagatirimboka gochia Antiokia, bagasangereria abanto b’ekanisa y’aroro, bakabaa rirube riria.
english: The men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they gathered the church together and delivered the letter.

ekegusii: Baria bakoobete Paulo bakamoikia Atene, na ekero banyorire ogochika koirera Sila na Timotheo ng’a bache asare bwango buna eranyarekane, bakarua aroro.
english: The men who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then left with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagasoka, bakarindokera omochie oria, bagaita abanto bonsi b’omochie nemioro.
english: The men who had been in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah, spread out and put the whole city to the sword.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baria barwarete oborwaire bwa ukoma baigete ase omochakano bw’egetwori bagasoa ase eema eyemo, bakaria endagera na konywa, bakabogoria chifeta, ne chitahabu, ne chianga, bakagenda bagachibisa. Naende bakairana, bagasoa ase eema ende, bakabogoria ebinto korwa aroro, bakagenda nabirobio bakabibisa.
english: The men who had leprosy reached the edge of the camp and entered one of the tents. They ate and drank, and carried away silver, gold and clothes, and went off and hid them. They returned and entered another tent and took some things from it and hid them also.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo basaretie okobwatana kw’ogotianania nakorete nabarabwo, gose tibarendete amang’ana ’okobwatana koria barabwo bakorete ase obosio bwane, inche nimbakorere buna barabwo bakorete ase emori eria y’okobwatana, bayenachanete ebing’ese bibere, erio bagaeta ase egati y’ebing’ese biria.
english: The men who have violated my covenant and have not fulfilled the terms of the covenant they made before me, I will treat like the calf they cut in two and then walked between its pieces.

ekegusii: Abanto baria babwatete Yeso, bakamosekereria, na komoaka.
english: The men who were guarding Jesus began mocking and beating him.

ekegusii: Abanto aba batoire ase amarieta abo bagacha ekero Hezekia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, arenge kogamba. Barabwo bagasaria chiema chi’abanto b’aroro na bagasiria Abameuni, abanto banyorekanete aroro; bakabasiria kegima na tibaiyo nonya goika rero iga. Erio bakamenya agwo ribaga riabo, ekiagera oborisia mbwarengeo ase chitugo chiabo.
english: The men whose names were listed came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites in their dwellings and also the Meunites who were there and completely destroyed them, as is evident to this day. Then they settled in their place, because there was pasture for their flocks.

ekegusii: Korwa ase egesaku gia Sabuloni, Abalawi abatigarete, chiamate chia Merari, bakaegwa emechie ya Yokinamu, na Karita,
english: The Merarite clans (the rest of the Levites) were given: from the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam, Kartah,

ekegusii: Abana ba Merari nabwo Mali na Musi. Abanto abwo nigo barenge chisokoro chie chiamate chi’Abalawi, kera oyomo ase eamate yaye.
english: The Merarite clans: Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, according to their families.

ekegusii: Abamerari abatigarete bakaegwa korwa ase egesaku gia Sabuloni: Rimoni na Tabori amo namarisio aetanaine emechie eyio.
english: The Merarites (the rest of the Levites) received the following: From the tribe of Zebulun they received Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmono and Tabor, together with their pasturelands;

ekegusii: Abamerari nabwo barabe bakorenda ebinto ebi: chibao chi’Obomenyo Obochenu, na emeriibo, ne chisiiro, ne chinterekerero, amo nebikorero biabo bionsi. Bakore emeremo ende yonsi eganeirie gokorwa ase ebinto ebio.
english: The Merarites were appointed to take care of the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, bases, all its equipment, and everything related to their use,

ekegusii: Oyo noro omobaro bw’ororeria rwa Merari, eamate ase eamate, na enyomba ase enyomba.
english: The Merarites were counted by their clans and families.

ekegusii: Abarwani esegi barangeretigwe gokonya nigo banga buna chimori chinoru. Beonchoire batamire bonsi amo, gose tibakonyara gotenena korwana esegi. Naki rituko ri’emechando yabo riabaikeire; eye nengaki bakoegwa egesusuro kiabo.
english: The mercenaries in her ranks are like fattened calves. They too will turn and flee together, they will not stand their ground, for the day of disaster is coming upon them, the time for them to be punished.

ekegusii: Omoonchoreria nigo abwate ebirengero bi’obong’ainereria ase amaboko aye, nigo anchete gokora oborianania.
english: The merchant uses dishonest scales; he loves to defraud.

ekegusii: Abaonchoreria bare ase egati y’abanto, nigo bagokumirie na kobugia emeroria. Aye gwaikeire ogosirigwa gw’okoondokia, tokobao naende nonya ng’ake.”
english: The merchants among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more.'"

ekegusii: Na abaonchoreria b’ebinto ebio, abwo betenenkirie ase engencho yaye ere, nigo baratenenere are, ekiagera bare nokoiroka ase ogoakwa kwaye, bakorera na kweumia,
english: The merchants who sold these things and gained their wealth from her will stand far off, terrified at her torment. They will weep and mourn

ekegusii: Omonto oria agatebia Daudi, “Abanto baria nigo barenge ne chinguru chinyinge gotobua, bagatotubokera agwo ase egetii aarabu. Nonya naboigo ntwababua, tokabairania gochia ase egeita ki’omochie.
english: The messenger said to David, "The men overpowered us and came out against us in the open, but we drove them back to the entrance to the city gate.

ekegusii: The messenger set out, and when he arrived he told David everything Joab had sent him to say.
english: Erio omotomwa oria akagenda, agatebia Daudi amang’ana onsi aya Yoabu amotomete akwane.

ekegusii: Omonto oria otometwe gochia korangeria Mikaya akagenda akamotebia, “Rora, amang’ana ’ababani bande nigo are ayamo, akoria eira y’egesio ekiya ase omoruoti; tiga ring’ana riao ribe erimo namang’ana abo; naye boigo okwane amang’ana okoria eira y’egesio ekiya ase omoruoti.”
english: The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, as one man the other prophets are predicting success for the king. Let your word agree with theirs, and speak favorably."

ekegusii: Omonto oria otometwe gochia korangeria Mikaya akagenda, akamotebia, “Rora, amang’ana ’ababani bande nigo are ayamo, okoria eira y’egesio ekiya ase omoruoti; tiga ring’ana riao ribe erimo namang’ana abo; naye boigo okwane amang’ana okoria eira y’egesio ekiya ase omoruoti.”
english: The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, as one man the other prophets are predicting success for the king. Let your word agree with theirs, and speak favorably."

ekegusii: Abanto baria batometwe bakairana naende, bagateba, “Aya naro Beni‐Hadadi agoteba: Natoma amang’ana asore ng’a ong’e chifeta chiao, ne chitahabu chiao, na abakungu bao, na abana bao.
english: The messengers came again and said, "This is what Ben-Hadad says: 'I sent to demand your silver and gold, your wives and your children.

ekegusii: Abamidiani, na Abaameleki, na abanto ba moocha nigo barenge agwo ase ense omweya abange buna chingige. Nigo barenge ne chingamia chinyinge buna omokenye ore ase engegu y’enyancha chitaare kobareka.
english: The Midianites, the Amalekites and all the other eastern peoples had settled in the valley, thick as locusts. Their camels could no more be counted than the sand on the seashore.

ekegusii: Abaiboria bakairaneria Farao, “Abakungu b’Abaibirania tibari buna aba Abamisiri; barabwo nabaango ase okoibora, nigo bakoibora ritang’ani omoiboria ataraika.”
english: The midwives answered Pharaoh, "Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women; they are vigorous and give birth before the midwives arrive."

ekegusii: Korende abaiboria baria nigo bamoirogete Nyasae. Tibakorete buna omoruoti o Misiri abatebetie, korende bagatiga abana abaisia babe moyo.
english: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do what the king of Egypt had told them to do; they let the boys live.

ekegusii: Abanto bare ne chinguru nababe buna amasakwe amomo, na emeremo yabo ebe buna chinsase chi’omorero, abwo mbasambwe bayiere amo, na onde tari orarimie omorero oyio.
english: The mighty man will become tinder and his work a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the fire."

ekegusii: Abanto chituoni b’abarwani esegi nabwo aba: Asaeli momura omwabo Yoabu, na Elihanani, mosinto o Dodo korwa Bethlehemu.
english: The mighty men were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

ekegusii: Naki okorengereria kw’engencho y’ebibe namakweri, korende okorengereria kw’engencho y’Omoika nobogima na omorembe.
english: The mind of sinful man is death, but the mind controlled by the Spirit is life and peace;

ekegusii: Erio abanto abwo batarenge ne chinkoro chi’oboremereria mbabe nebirengererio bi’okomanya, na abwo barenge gotutura mbamanye gokwana buya na koigugwa buya.
english: The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.

ekegusii: Abamoabu bagatebia abagaaka ba Midiani, “Omoganda oyo omonene nigo ogochia koria okoore kera egento getoetanaine aiga, buna chiombe chikorisia obonyansi ase egetii chiabokoora.” Ase engaki eria Balaki, mosinto o Sipori, orenge omoruoti bw’Abamoabu.
english: The Moabites said to the elders of Midian, "This horde is going to lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field." So Balak son of Zippor, who was king of Moab at that time,

ekegusii: Abanto abwo mbabaake amagena, naende mbabaite nemioro yabo. Boigo mbaite abana babo, abamura na abaiseke, basambe chinyomba chiabo nomorero.
english: The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords; they will kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omochecheria narigia obong’aini, takobonyora, korende chisemi nigo chikonyorekana ase omonto ore omwango ase okomanya.
english: The mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.

ekegusii: Korende korwa ase chibesa chiria chiarentetwe ase enyomba y’Omonene tibaroisetie chisani chie chifeta gose ebinachi, gose ebitaabo, gose ebirombeta, gose ebikorero binde bie chitahabu, gose ebie chifeta, ase enyomba y’Omonene,
english: The money brought into the temple was not spent for making silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets or any other articles of gold or silver for the temple of the LORD;

ekegusii: Chibesa chiarenge koruegwa ase okorongeyia okomocha, na echio chiarenge koruegwa ase ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe tichiarentetwe ase enyomba y’Omonene; echio nigo chiabete echi’abakuani.
english: The money from the guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the temple of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.

ekegusii: Akabeka omotienyi ne ching’enang’eni bigambe botuko, ekiagera obwanchani bwaye nigo bogendererete goika kare na kare.
english: the moon and stars to govern the night; His love endures forever.

ekegusii: Aye kwabekire omotienyi obeire ekemanyererio gie chingaki, na erioba nigo rimanyete boronge ekero rigwenerete kogwa.
english: The moon marks off the seasons, and the sun knows when to go down.

ekegusii: Erio omotienyi tokorua oborabu bwaye, na erioba tirikobara, ekiagera Omonene bw’Emeganda nabe okogamba ase egetunwa gia Sayoni, na ase Yerusalemu, na ase abagaaka b’aroro naorokie obonene bwaye.
english: The moon will be abashed, the sun ashamed; for the LORD Almighty will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before its elders, gloriously.

ekegusii: Oborabu bw’omotienyi mborabe se buna omobaso bw’erioba, na omobaso bw’erioba nobare ara gatano na kabere, buna okobara kw’amatuko atano na abere. Amang’ana ayio nigo arakorekane ekero Omonene araboe chingoma na agwenie amaakwa aagete abanto baye.
english: The moon will shine like the sun, and the sunlight will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, when the LORD binds up the bruises of his people and heals the wounds he inflicted.

ekegusii: “Buna abakuani bagendererete kobucha, naboigo bagendererete gokora ebibe asende. Ase ayio ning’onchore obonene bwabo bobe obosooku.
english: The more the priests increased, the more they sinned against me; they exchanged their Glory for something disgraceful.

ekegusii: Ogokwana okonge nigo gokorenta amang’ana amange are bosa. Inee! Ayio mbuya ki akorenta ase mwanyabanto?
english: The more the words, the less the meaning, and how does that profit anyone?

ekegusii: Omokungu ore omwereria mono naende ore bw’enyomba y’amasikani ase egati yaino, oria otarenge konyara gotacha inse namagoro aye agende aande, ekiagera igo are omwereria narorere omosacha oye anchete mono ribero, narorere nabana baye, abamura na abaiseke, ribero boigo.
english: The most gentle and sensitive woman among you-- so sensitive and gentle that she would not venture to touch the ground with the sole of her foot-- will begrudge the husband she loves and her own son or daughter

ekegusii: Nonya nomokungu oiborete abana batano na babere, nigo akogireka ase omoichano; erioba ri’obogima bwaye riagure kobore mobaso, osookigwe na goichanigwa. Nindue abatigari baitwe nemioro y’ababisa babo”. Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: The mother of seven will grow faint and breathe her last. Her sun will set while it is still day; she will be disgraced and humiliated. I will put the survivors to the sword before their enemies," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa ebio mbinyititoke inse yaye, na amagoko nabwereke, binyititoke buna obochoe bokonyititoka ase omorero, na bibe buna amache akoba ekero aumoirwe ase egetirimboko.
english: The mountains melt beneath him and the valleys split apart, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa nigo bikonyititoka buna obochoe ase obosio bw’Omonene, ee, ase obosio bw’Omonene bw’ense yonsi.
english: The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.

ekegusii: Aye egetunwa kia Basani, nigo ore egetunwa kia Nyasae, aye egetunwa kia Basani, nigo obwate ebichuria ebinge.
english: The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains; rugged are the mountains of Bashan.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa nigo bigotengechigwa ase obosio bw’Omonene, ebigoro nigo bikonyititoka. Ense nigo ekonyegerigwa ase obosio bwaye, ee, ense amo nebitongwa bionsi bireo.
english: The mountains quake before him and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at his presence, the world and all who live in it.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa bikanyegerigwa ase obosio bw’Omonene, ee, nonya negetunwa keria gia Sinai, ase obosio bwa Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli.
english: The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa nigo biakoroche, bikanyegerigwa, amache e chiooro agaeta; chindiba chigaaka amariogi, chikaimokia amaboko abo gochia igoro.
english: the mountains saw you and writhed. Torrents of water swept by; the deep roared and lifted its waves on high.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa bigachara‐charara buna chimingichi, na ebigoro buna chimanwa chie ching’ondi.
english: the mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs.

ekegusii: Ekiriri ki’omosabibu oyio nigo giatubete ebitunwa, ne chinsagia chiaye chikaranda gochia aase emecharake ya Nyasae ere.
english: The mountains were covered with its shade, the mighty cedars with its branches.

ekegusii: Ebitunwa na ebigoro mbirentere abanto omorembe goetera ase oboronge.
english: The mountains will bring prosperity to the people, the hills the fruit of righteousness.

ekegusii: Omonwa bw’omokungu omotayayi nigo ore eirima entambe, na omonto onde bwensi Omonene agechigwe nere goika agwe ase eirima eyio.
english: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the LORD's wrath will fall into it.

ekegusii: Omonwa bw’omonyene oboronge nigo ogokwana ay’obong’aini, korende oromeme rokong’ainereria ndosirigwe.
english: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.

ekegusii: Omonwa bw’omonyene oboronge nigo onga buna ensoko y’obogima, korende obochege nigo boichire ase emenwa y’abakori amabe.
english: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but violence overwhelms the mouth of the wicked.

ekegusii: Omonwa bw’omonto omoronge nigo agokwana amang’ana ’obong’aini, na oromeme rwaye nigo rogosokia ay’ekeene.
english: The mouth of the righteous man utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks what is just.

ekegusii: Amariogi ’abakobugia amakano na ebiroria, na ebitureri, takoigugwa ime asore naende nonya ng’ake; nonya nomoroisia o gento kende gionsi takororekana ime asore naende nonya ng’ake; nonya neriogi ri’orogena rogosia tirikoigugwa ime asore naende nonya ng’ake;
english: The music of harpists and musicians, flute players and trumpeters, will never be heard in you again. No workman of any trade will ever be found in you again. The sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again.

ekegusii: The musicians Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals;
english: Abateri baria Hemani na Asafu, na Etani babe bakobugia chisani chi’etaai chikobugigwa na kwoga.

ekegusii: Na abateri, abanto b’eamate y’Asafu, nigo babeerete aase abo buna Daudi, na Asafu, na Hemani, na Yedutuni, omorori bw’omoruoti, bachigete. Abarendi b’ebiita bakabeera aase abo ase kera egeita. Tibatigete emeremo yabo, ekiagera Abalawi bamwabo mbabaroiseretie ebing’wanso biabo.
english: The musicians, the descendants of Asaph, were in the places prescribed by David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer. The gatekeepers at each gate did not need to leave their posts, because their fellow Levites made the preparations for them.

ekegusii: Obo nabwo obobisi bwe ching’enang’eni chiria isano na ibere kwarora ase okoboko kwane gw’okorio, na ebibekerero biria bie chitaya bie chitahabu bitano na bibere: Ching’enang’eni chiria isano na ibere nabamalaika be chikanisa isano na ibere, na ebibekerero biria bitano na bibere nechikanisa isano na ibere.”
english: The mystery of the seven stars that you saw in my right hand and of the seven golden lampstands is this: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

ekegusii: Obobisi boria bwabisetwe korwa kare ase ebigori ebinge, korende bono bwaorokigwe ase abachenu baye.
english: the mystery that has been kept hidden for ages and generations, but is now disclosed to the saints.

ekegusii: Moka Amuramu nigo arenge korokwa Yokebedi, mosubati o Lawi, oria oiboreretwe Lawi agwo ase ense ya Misiri. Omokungu oria akamoiborera Amuramu abana aba: Haroni, na Musa, na Miriamu, omoiseke omwabo.
english: the name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, a descendant of Levi, who was born to the Levites in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses and their sister Miriam.

ekegusii: Omomura oye omotangi nigo are korokwa Yoeli, na oyo o kabere Abiya. Barabwo nigo babete abagambi agwo Beeri‐Seba.
english: The name of his firstborn was Joel and the name of his second was Abijah, and they served at Beersheba.

ekegusii: Orooche rwe ritang’ani rokarokwa Pisoni. Orwo narwo roetanaine ense yonsi ya Havila aase etahabu egotoka.
english: The name of the first is the Pishon; it winds through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.

ekegusii: Omoisraeli oria oitetwe amo nomokungu Omomidiani nigo arenge korokwa Simuri, mosinto o Salu, omotang’ani bw’eamate yaye ase egesaku gia Simeoni.
english: The name of the Israelite who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family.

ekegusii: Erieta ri’Omonene nigo rire orwaki orokong’u; omonyene oboronge nigo akorotamera oba orendire buya.
english: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.

ekegusii: Na orooche rwa kabere rokarokwa Gihoni. Orwo narwo roetanaine ense yonsi ya Kusi.
english: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the entire land of Cush.

ekegusii: Erieta ri’eng’enang’eni eria nigo yare korokwa Ekemeri Ekeroro; na ensemo ya gatato y’amache ekaba endoro, na abanto abange bagakwa ase amache ayio, ekiagera abete amaroro.
english: the name of the star is Wormwood. A third of the waters turned bitter, and many people died from the waters that had become bitter.

ekegusii: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Asshur. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
english: Na orooche rwa gatato rokarokwa Tigirisi, orwo rogoeta moocha y’Asuri. Na orooche rwa kane narororwo rokarokwa Eufarati.

ekegusii: The names of the sons of Aaron were Nadab the firstborn and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
english: Aya naro amarieta ’abamura ba Haroni: Nadabu, omomura oye omotangi, na Abihu, na Eleazari, na Itamari.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bagure ase eirima bakunyete, na ase oboreba babisete babwatirwe abanyene.
english: The nations have fallen into the pit they have dug; their feet are caught in the net they have hidden.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bakaigwa chinkuma chiaye; bakayeremera eirima, ero ekagwa imeo, bakayegobania nekegobanio, bakayeira Misiri.
english: The nations heard about him, and he was trapped in their pit. They led him with hooks to the land of Egypt.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bakabea, korende bono endamwamu yao yachire, na engaki y’okogambia abakure, na engaki y’okoa abasomba bao ababani, na abachenu, na abwo bairogete erieta riao, abake na abanene, eng’eria yabo, na gosiria abwo bagosaria ense.”
english: The nations were angry; and your wrath has come. The time has come for judging the dead, and for rewarding your servants the prophets and your saints and those who reverence your name, both small and great-- and for destroying those who destroy the earth."

ekegusii: Ebisaku bionsi mbiiroke erieta ri’Omonene, na abaruoti bonsi b’ense mbairoke obonene bwaye.
english: The nations will fear the name of the LORD, all the kings of the earth will revere your glory.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bakayaigwa, bagatengechigwa ase omoondoko, omoichano na obororo bikabwata abamenyete Bofilisti.
english: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku baigure amang’ana igoro y’obosooku bwaino, na ebirero biaino biaichoire ase ense, ekiagera omorwani etuoni ogochirwe na kogwa igoro ase etuoni ende. Bonsi bagwereranire amo.
english: The nations will hear of your shame; your cries will fill the earth. One warrior will stumble over another; both will fall down together."

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku mbarore oboronge bwao, na abaruoti bonsi barore obonene bwao; erio aye orokwe erieta riyia, rirarue ase omonwa bw’Omonene.
english: The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku nabataare ase omobaso oye, na abaruoti b’ense nabarente obonene bwabo imeo.
english: The nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their splendor into it.

ekegusii: Naende Musa agateba, “Abanto b’ebisaku ebio mogochia goseria nigo bakoigwera abarogi na abariori, korende inwe Omonene, Nyasae oino, obakanirie ng’a timobaisa gokora ebinto ebio.
english: The nations you will dispossess listen to those who practice sorcery or divination. But as for you, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.

ekegusii: na Negebu, na ense omweya ya Yeriko, Omochie bw’Emekendo, na goika Soari.
english: the Negev and the whole region from the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.

ekegusii: Obwoba bogasoa ase abatureti babo bonsi. Amang’ana aya onsi agasarera ase ense yonsi y’ebitunwa bia Boyahudi.
english: The neighbors were all filled with awe, and throughout the hill country of Judea people were talking about all these things.

ekegusii: Ase engaki eyio, na kogenderera, amamonto namenyete ase ense, ekero abana abamura ba Nyasae baare konyuoma abaiseke ba mwanyabanto na konyora abana. Abwo nabwo barenge abanto chituoni, baare gotogigwa agwo kare.
english: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days-- and also afterward-- when the sons of God went to the daughters of men and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown.

ekegusii: Edivai enyia nigo ekobokia amagombo, na emesabibu yasusanire, na abanto bonsi barenge nomogoko bw’enkoro nigo baichanete.
english: The new wine dries up and the vine withers; all the merrymakers groan.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Agripa agacha amo na Bereniki ase obonene obonge, bagasoa ase ekegambero amo nabatang’ani b’abarwani elifu na abanto abanene b’omochie. Festo akarua ogochika ng’a Paulo arentwe ime.
english: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high ranking officers and the leading men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere omoika omobe okorwa ase Nyasae ogacha igoro ase Saulo, na ere akaba okobaboka buna ebarimo agwo nyomba mwaye. Daudi nigo arenge kobugia obokano buna anarete kera rituko, na Saulo nabwate ritimo koboko kwaye.
english: The next day an evil spirit from God came forcefully upon Saul. He was prophesying in his house, while David was playing the harp, as he usually did. Saul had a spear in his hand

ekegusii: Goika mambia yaye kobakorwa Bethania Yeso akaigwa enchara.
english: The next day as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

ekegusii: Goika mambia yaye akarua chisiringi ibere, akaa omonyene enyomba, akamotebia: Morende buya; na kende gionsi orarue kobua, kondairane naende, ningoakane.
english: The next day he took out two silver coins and gave them to the innkeeper. 'Look after him,' he said, 'and when I return, I will reimburse you for any extra expense you may have.'

ekegusii: Naende akagenda rituko ria kabere, akarora Abaibirania babere bakorwana; akamoboria oria ochegetie oyomwabo, “Nase ki ogoaka oyomino?”
english: The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, "Why are you hitting your fellow Hebrew?"

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Yeso akarigia koimoka kogenda Galili. Akanyora Filipo, akamotebia, “Ntunyana.”
english: The next day Jesus decided to leave for Galilee. Finding Philip, he said to him, "Follow me."

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Yohana akarora Yeso ogocha asare, akabora, “Rora, Emanwa y’Eng’ondi ya Nyasae, oyokorusia ebibe bi’ense!
