english: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

ekegusii: Naende rituko ria kabere Yohana nigo arenge oteneine amo na babere b’aborokigwa baye.
english: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere akaorokera Abaisraeli babere ekero baare korwana, akarigia kobatorania agateba: Abaminto, inwe nabamo, nase ki mokorwana?
english: The next day Moses came upon two Israelites who were fighting. He tried to reconcile them by saying, 'Men, you are brothers; why do you want to hurt each other?'

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Musa agasoa ase Eema eria y’Oborori, akarora enyimbo ya Haroni, eyatenenerete egesaku kia Lawi, yasebokire, ne chinsagia echio chiasokirie amamumu na ebisicha, naende chiamire amatunda amalozi atobire.
english: The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron's staff, which represented the house of Levi, had not only sprouted but had budded, blossomed and produced almonds.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Musa agatebia abanto, “Mwakorire ebibe ebinene mono. Na bono ngotiira inde gochia ase Omonene, aande nabo ndabanyorere okobwatanigwa, ekiagera mwakorire ebibe.”
english: The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a great sin. But now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Musa agaikaransa kogamba ebina bi’abanto; na abanto nigo barengeo bamoetanaine korwa mambia goika mogoroba.
english: The next day Moses took his seat to serve as judge for the people, and they stood around him from morning till evening.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Paulo agasoa mwa Yakobo amo naintwe, na abagaaka bonsi nao barenge.
english: The next day Paul and the rest of us went to see James, and all the elders were present.

ekegusii: Erio Paulo akaira abasacha baria, ne rituko ria kabere agakora buna engencho yare y’ogwesibia amo nabarabwo. Erio agasoa Hekalu ime, ase okoraria amang’ana ’ogwesibia na engaki y’okorua esadaka ase engencho ya kera oyomo obo.
english: The next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he went to the temple to give notice of the date when the days of purification would end and the offering would be made for each of them.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere Saulo akaroberia abanto baye ase ebiombe bitato, na barabwo bagacha mambia kobogokiamoka, bagasoa ase egetwori ki’Abaamoni, bakabaita kogenderera goika mobaso gati. Abwo batigarete bagesiarera, gose onde tatigara ore nonde amo.
english: The next day Saul separated his men into three divisions; during the last watch of the night they broke into the camp of the Ammonites and slaughtered them until the heat of the day. Those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

ekegusii: Inkio yaye omoganda oteneine ng’umbu y’enyancha bakarora ng’a obwato bonde tibwarenge aroro, otatiga boria obomo bwoka, naende ng’a Yeso tasoete ase obwato boria amo naborokigwa baye, korende naborokigwa baye bagendete boka.
english: The next day the crowd that had stayed on the opposite shore of the lake realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not entered it with his disciples, but that they had gone away alone.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere abanto abange abachete ase Rituko Rinene, kobachie koigwa ng’a Yeso ngocha are Yerusalemu,
english: The next day the great crowd that had come for the Feast heard that Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere omoiseke oria omotangi agatebia oria omoke omwabo, “Rora, obotuko bwa igoro nigo naraire na Tata; tomonyoisie naende edivai ase obotuko obo, erio naye ochie, orare nere, erinde tomotenenerie egesaku kiaye, tigesira.”
english: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Last night I lay with my father. Let's get him to drink wine again tonight, and you go in and lie with him so we can preserve our family line through our father."

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere abanto bagasoka ase egetii aarabu, na Abimeleki agatebigwa amang’ana ayio.
english: The next day the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and this was reported to Abimelech.

ekegusii: Mambia kobwakia, abanene babo, na abagaaka, na aborokia b’amariko bagasangererekana Yerusalemu,
english: The next day the rulers, elders and teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Korende rituko ria kabere, omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli okemurunganeria Musa na Haroni, okabora, “Ninwe mwaitire abanto b’Omonene.”
english: The next day the whole Israelite community grumbled against Moses and Aaron. "You have killed the LORD's people," they said.

ekegusii: Ekero bwakia mambia bagatiga abarwani be chibarasi bagenderere norogendo na Paulo, na barabwo abanyene bakairana ase enyomba enene y’abarwani.
english: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.

ekegusii: Ne rituko ria kabere barabwo bakaruera Omonene ebing’wanso, bakamoruera nebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa; chieri elifu eyemo, ne chimingichi elifu eyemo, ne chimanwa chie ching’ondi elifu eyemo, amo nokoruegwa kw’ebinyugwa gwachikire amo nabirobio, naende akarua ebing’wanso ebinge ase engencho y’Abaisraeli bonsi.
english: The next day they made sacrifices to the LORD and presented burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams and a thousand male lambs, together with their drink offerings, and other sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere togaika Sidoni. Yulio akarenda Paulo buya, akamoa ribaga agende ase abasani baye akonywe nabarabwo.
english: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.

ekegusii: Tokamanora korwa agwo, ne rituko ria kabere togaika kororia Kio. Rituko ria gatato togaika Samo, tokabeera Torogilo, ne rituko ria kane togaika Mileto.
english: The next day we set sail from there and arrived off Kios. The day after that we crossed over to Samos, and on the following day arrived at Miletus.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere akarengereria komanya boronge nase engencho ki asoeirwe n’Abayahudi, akamosibora, agachika abakuani abanene na abanto b’ekegambero bonsi bache. Agatirimbokia Paulo, akamobeka ase amasio abo.
english: The next day, since the commander wanted to find out exactly why Paul was being accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul and had him stand before them.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere, nario riare rigotunya rituko ri’Okwearigania, abakuani abanene na Abafarisai bagasangererekana ase Pilato,
english: The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees went to Pilate.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere, ekero Pasuri asiborete Yeremia korwa ase rikorogoto, Yeremia akamotebia, “Omonene tagokoroka Pasuri, korende okorokire Omwoboyia ase chinsemo chionsi.
english: The next day, when Pashhur released him from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD's name for you is not Pashhur, but Magor-Missabib.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere, ekero Abafilisti bachete konuura ebinto korwa ase emebere y’abanto bakwete, bakanyora Saulo amo nabamura baye bakwete agwo ase egetunwa kia Giliboa.
english: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere ekero Abafilisti bachete konuura ebinto korwa ase emebere y’abanto bakwete, bakanyora Saulo na abamura baye batato bakwete agwo ase egetunwa kia Giliboa.
english: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere ekero baare gotirimboka korwa ase egetunwa, omoganda omonene okaumerana nere.
english: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.

ekegusii: Ase ayio Baalaamu akaimoka mambia rituko ria kabere, agatebia abanene baria batometwe na Balaki, “Bono inwe irana mogende ase ense yaino, ekiagera Omonene bwangire kong’a ribaga ngende amo nainwe.”
english: The next morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's princes, "Go back to your own country, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere mambia Balaki akaira Baalamu igoro ase Bamoti‐Baali, na korwa igoro agwo Baalamu akarora ensemo eyemo y’omoganda bw’Abaisraeli.
english: The next morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal, and from there he saw part of the people.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere ekero asogete mambia, agatenena agakwana nabanto bonsi, akabora, “Inwe timori na komocha. Ninche nakora omoroberio mamincha y’omonene one, nkamoita, korende ning’o oita abaiga bonsi?
english: The next morning Jehu went out. He stood before all the people and said, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him, but who killed all these?

ekegusii: The next morning the Israelites got up and pitched camp near Gibeah.
english: Erio Abaisraeli bakaimoka bonsi mambia chuni, bagatoora ang’e nomochie o Gibea,

ekegusii: Bogachia gokiamoka, Abayahudi bakabwatana komoboera Paulo, bagatianania ng’a tibakoria gose tibakonywa goika bamoitire.
english: The next morning the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

ekegusii: Rituko ria kabere mambia, ekero ki’engaki y’okorua ekeng’wanso, amache agacha korwa ensemo y’Edomu, goika agaichora orogongo roria.
english: The next morning, about the time for offering the sacrifice, there it was-- water flowing from the direction of Edom! And the land was filled with water.

ekegusii: Ekero nabogete mambia ngonkie omwana one, nkanyora ng’a okure, korende ekero narigereretie omwana oria buya ase emambia eyio, nkarora ng’a oyo tari omwana oria naiborete.”
english: The next morning, I got up to nurse my son-- and he was dead! But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, I saw that it wasn't the son I had borne."

ekegusii: Abanto ba Tekoa bakabwatia abwo koagacha, korende abanene babo abasikire tibakumbete emegongo yabo ase ogokora emeremo y’Omonene obo.
english: The next section was repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their nobles would not put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors.

ekegusii: Ekero ebimeri bigochaka gosomoria, Beni‐Hadadi akaroberia Abasiiria, akagenda Afeki korwania Abaisraeli.
english: The next spring Ben-Hadad mustered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

ekegusii: Ase obotuko boria bwatang’anerete rituko riria Herode arengereretie komoira ase ekegambero, Petero nigo arenge oraire gati y’abarendi babere, osibire nebinyuri bibere, na abarwani nigo barenge gesieri barendete echela.
english: The night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries stood guard at the entrance.

ekegusii: Obotuko bwaisire koera, omobaso obeire ang’e. Torusie ogokora kw’omosunte; tweboyie ebirwanero bi’omobaso.
english: The night is nearly over; the day is almost here. So let us put aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

ekegusii: Orooche rwa Naili naroichorwe nebioto, na birobio nabitiire korwa aroro, nabisoe nyomba mwao, na enyomba yao y’okorara, amo noborere bwao; nabisoe ne chinyomba chi’abasomba bao na echi’abanto bao, ase amariko ao ase okogekera emegati, na ase ebituba biao bi’ogokonyera obosie.
english: The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up into your palace and your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and on your people, and into your ovens and kneading troughs.

ekegusii: Obwa ikomi na kianda bokagwera Maloti; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: obwa ikomi na kianda bokagwera Petahiya, na obwa emerongo ebere Ezekieli;
english: the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,

ekegusii: Abanto ba Nineva bakegena amang’ana a Nyasae, bakararia okweng’ata, na abanto bonsi pi, korwa omonene goika omoke, bakeboyia chigunia.
english: The Ninevites believed God. They declared a fast, and all of them, from the greatest to the least, put on sackcloth.

ekegusii: obwa kianda bokagwera Yesua, na obwa ikomi Sekania;
english: the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,

ekegusii: Obwa kianda bokagwera Matania; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Oyo o kianda, Abieseri korwa Anatoti bw’ororeria rwa Benjamin akaba omoteneneri bw’ekeombe ki’omotienyi o kianda. Ekeombe kiaye nigo kiarenge nabanto chilifu emerongo ebere na inye (24,000).
english: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjamite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

ekegusii: Abagambi b’abanto basangererekanire amo, babe abanto ba Nyasae o Ibrahimu. Chinguba chi’ense nigo chire echia Nyasae; ere oimokererigwe igoro mono kegima.
english: The nobles of the nations assemble as the people of the God of Abraham, for the kings of the earth belong to God; he is greatly exalted.

ekegusii: Abanto abanene nigo bagotoma abasomba babo bagende korenta amache, bagoika ase chinsoko, banyora amache taiyo; bairana ne chinyongo chire bosa. Nigo bagosookigwa na gokwa emioyo, baba batubete emetwe yabo.
english: The nobles send their servants for water; they go to the cisterns but find no water. They return with their jars unfilled; dismayed and despairing, they cover their heads.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’esegi riachire ase ense amo nogosirigwa okonene.
english: The noise of battle is in the land, the noise of great destruction!

ekegusii: Naboigo ase ensemo ya sugusu oroisie ebitambaa bire nobotambe bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko rigana erimo, bisiirwe ne chisiiro emerongo ebere, ne chinterekerero chiabo emerongo ebere chie chitaai. Ebigobanio amo ne chinuga chiabo bibe bie chifeta.
english: The north side shall also be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

ekegusii: Naboigo ase ensemo ya sugusu akaroisia ebitambaa bire nobotambe bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko rigana erimo. Chisiiro emerongo ebere echiare kobibwata nigo chiarenge ne chinterekerero chiabo emerongo ebere chie chitaai, korende ebigobanio ne chinuga chiabo nigo chiarenge chie chifeta.
english: The north side was also a hundred cubits long and had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo ene na eyemo, na amagana atano (41,500).
english: The number from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etato na isano, na amagana ane (35,400).
english: The number from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano nomo na ibere, na amagana atano na abere (62,700).
english: The number from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo ene, na amagana atano (40,500).
english: The number from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo ene na isano, na amagana atano na rimo, na emerongo etano (45,650).
english: The number from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano na inye, na amagana ane (54,400).
english: The number from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano na ebere na inye, na amagana atano na rimo (74,600).
english: The number from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etato na ibere, na amagana abere (32,200).
english: The number from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano na isato, na amagana ane (53,400).
english: The number from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo ene na isano nemo, na amagana atano (46,500).
english: The number from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano na kianda, na amagana atato (59,300).
english: The number from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.

ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu emerongo etano na isano na ibere, na amagana ane (57,400).
english: The number from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

ekegusii: Abanto abasacha, aba konya bakoorire omotienyi oyomo na goetania, nigo barenge chilifu isano na isato, na amagana atano na rimo (8,600). Abanto aba nabwo barabe bakorenda ebinto bire ase Obomenyo Obochenu.
english: The number of all the males a month old or more was 8,600. The Kohathites were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.

ekegusii: Abanto abasacha, aba konya bakoorire omotienyi oyomo na goetania, nigo barenge chilifu isano nemo, na amagana abere (6,200).
english: The number of all the males a month old or more who were counted was 6,200.

ekegusii: Abanto abasacha, aba konya bakoorire omotiengi oyomo na goetania, nigo barenge chilifu isano na ibere, na amagana atano (7,500).
english: The number of all the males a month old or more who were counted was 7,500.

ekegusii: Omobaro bw’ebing’wanso biria omosangererekano orentete nigo orenge chieri emerongo etano na ebere, ne chimingichi rigana erimo, ne chimanwa chie ching’ondi amagana abere. Echio chionsi nigo chiaruetwe chikaba ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa ase Omonene.
english: The number of burnt offerings the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred male lambs-- all of them for burnt offerings to the LORD.

ekegusii: Na abasacha abariete emegati eria nigo barenge chilifu isano.
english: The number of the men who had eaten was five thousand.

ekegusii: Na omobaro bw’emeganda y’abariinete chibarasi nigo orenge chimilion amagana abere. Nkaigwa ng’a omobaro obo nigo orenge buna iga.
english: The number of the mounted troops was two hundred million. I heard their number.

ekegusii: Ase rituko erio erio omoruoti akarenterwa omobaro bw’abaitetwe aria Susa, omochie omonene,
english: The number of those slain in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king that same day.

ekegusii: Na abwo bariete nigo barenge abasacha chilifu isano, otatiga abakungu na abana.
english: The number of those who ate was about five thousand men, besides women and children.

ekegusii: Na abwo bariete nigo barenge abasacha chilifu inye, otatiga abakungu na abana.
english: The number of those who ate was four thousand, besides women and children.

ekegusii: the oath he swore to our father Abraham:
english: Emuma eria arierete sokoro yaito Ibrahimu,

ekegusii: Nere akarua esani eyemo eroisirie korwa ase efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli rigana erimo, na emerongo etato, na egetaabo ekemo gi’efeta y’oborito bwe chisekeli emerongo etano na ebere, ase ekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Bionsi bibere nigo biaichire nobosie obonuke bwochoganirie namaguta bokaba okoruegwa kw’endagera.
english: The offering he brought was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;

ekegusii: Omotang’ani oria bw’abarwani esegi nigo airaneretie omonto oria o Nyasae, agateba, “Nonya Omonene omonyene are koigora ebibao bia igoro, ayio takonyara koba.” Omonto oria o Nyasae nigo amoiraneretie, “Aye noyarore namaiso ao, korende tokoria endagera eyio.”
english: The officer had said to the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD should open the floodgates of the heavens, could this happen?" The man of God had replied, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!"

ekegusii: Erio omotang’ani bw’abarwani esegi, oyio omoruoti egenete, agatebia omonto oria o Nyasae, “Nonya Omonene omonyene are koigora ebibao bia igoro, egento ekio tigekonyara koba.” Korende omonto oria o Nyasae agateba, “Aye noyarore namaiso ao, korende tokoria endagera eyio.”
english: The officer on whose arm the king was leaning said to the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD should open the floodgates of the heavens, could this happen?" "You will see it with your own eyes," answered Elisha, "but you will not eat any of it!"

ekegusii: Aba nabwo barenge abaraai b’ebisaku bi’Abaisraeli: Eliezeri, mosinto o Sikiri, ase Abareuben; Sefatia, mosinto o Maaka, ase Abasimeoni;
english: The officers over the tribes of Israel: over the Reubenites: Eliezer son of Zicri; over the Simeonites: Shephatiah son of Maacah;

ekegusii: Abanyanyimbo bakairera abagambi amang’ana aya, na bar abwo bakoboa ekero baigwa ng’a Paulo na Sila n’Abarumi bare.
english: The officers reported this to the magistrates, and when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they were alarmed.

ekegusii: “Erio abateneneri bakwane nabanto, babatebie: Onye omonto ore aiga oagachire enyomba, korende tarayemenya, tiga airane bwoye, tabaisa gochia gokwera ase esegi, na omonto omoao achie koira enyomba yaye na koyemenya.
english: The officers shall say to the army: "Has anyone built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him go home, or he may die in battle and someone else may dedicate it.

ekegusii: Abanene b’ensemo eria tibamanyete ase nagendete, gose eki narenge gokora, ekiagera konya tindatebia Abayahudi gento, gose abakuani, gose abanto basikire, gose abanene, gose abanto bande bonsi abaare gocha gokora emeremo.
english: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, because as yet I had said nothing to the Jews or the priests or nobles or officials or any others who would be doing the work.

ekegusii: Abagambi ba Soani nigo bare abariri kegima; na abasemia abang’aini ba Farao nigo bagosemia ay’oboriri. Naki moranyare gotebia Farao: “Intwe nabana b’abanto abang’aini, abana b’abaruoti abakoro?”
english: The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools; the wise counselors of Pharaoh give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am one of the wise men, a disciple of the ancient kings"?

ekegusii: Abagambi ba Soani babeire abariri, na aba Memifisi bang’ainirwe. Abwo bare buna amagena e chikoona ase ebisaku biabo batantanirie ense ya Misiri.
english: The officials of Zoan have become fools, the leaders of Memphis are deceived; the cornerstones of her peoples have led Egypt astray.

ekegusii: Abasomba baye, Yosakari, mosinto o Simeati, na Yehosabadi, mosinto o Someri, aba nabwo bamoitete agakwa. Yoashi agatindekwa ase chisokoro chiaye chiatindegetwe agwo ase Omochie o Daudi, na Amasia, omwana oye omomura, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: The officials who murdered him were Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer. He died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. And Amaziah his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Omobani oria omogotu akamotebia, “Nainche igo inde omobani buna aye, na omomalaika nigo achigetwe n’Omonene agantebia: Genda omoiranie ache amo naye goika nyomba mwao, arie endagera na konywa amache.” Korende igo amotebetie oborimo.
english: The old prophet answered, "I too am a prophet, as you are. And an angel said to me by the word of the LORD: 'Bring him back with you to your house so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" (But he was lying to him.)

ekegusii: Oria omotangi akaibora omwana omoisia, akamoroka Moabu; oyio nere sokoro bw’Abamoabu goika rero iga.
english: The older daughter had a son, and she named him Moab; he is the father of the Moabites of today.

ekegusii: Oria omonene nigo arenge korokwa Ohola, na oria omoke Oholiba. Abwo bakaba abaane, bakaibora abana, abamura na abaiseke. Engencho y’amarieta abo nero ere: Ohola nere Samaria, na Oholiba nere Yerusalemu.
english: The older was named Oholah, and her sister was Oholibah. They were mine and gave birth to sons and daughters. Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Omonene oria oikaransete aaria igoro, nigo agoseka na kobakorera echeche.
english: The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord scoffs at them.

ekegusii: Rituko rie ritang’ani Nahasoni, mosinto bw’Aminadabu bw’egesaku kia Yuda, akarenta okoruegwa kwaye.
english: The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah.

ekegusii: The one who calls you is faithful and he will do it.
english: Ere oyobarangeirie nomwegenwa, nakore ayio.

ekegusii: Ere oyotarogeti ase omobere, onye obwatete amachiko, Inee, tagokonachera ekina aye, oyore namachiko na okwaroka, naende osaririe amachiko?
english: The one who is not circumcised physically and yet obeys the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.

ekegusii: Na oyo obusuirwe ase amagwa, oyo nere okoigwa ring’ana; okorengereria gw’ense na obong’ainereria bw’enibo biaba nkomiga bire ring’ana, riaba tirikwama.
english: The one who received the seed that fell among the thorns is the man who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke it, making it unfruitful.

ekegusii: Na oyo obusuirwe ase egetare nere oria okoigwa ring’ana, erio kegima oribwata nomogoko,
english: The one who received the seed that fell on rocky places is the man who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

ekegusii: Ere oyontomete nigo are amo nainche, tantigeti inche bweka, ekiagera botambe nigo ngokora ayakomogwenera.”
english: The one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what pleases him."

ekegusii: Naki ere oyogosimeka ase chingencho chiaye chi’ebibe nache kogesa ogosareka korwa ase chingencho chiaye chi’ebibe, korende ere oyogosimeka ase Omoika nache kogesa obogima bwa kare na kare korwa ase Omoika.
english: The one who sows to please his sinful nature, from that nature will reap destruction; the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.

ekegusii: karabe otimokire, naende asoke isiko gotaara ogwesiirera enyimbo, rirorio oria omoagete nigo aratigwe, otatiga amoakane ase engencho y’eng’eria eria asiririe, na amorende goika agwene kegima.
english: the one who struck the blow will not be held responsible if the other gets up and walks around outside with his staff; however, he must pay the injured man for the loss of his time and see that he is completely healed.

ekegusii: Omokuani onde bwensi orakune egento buna ekio nabe oyotachenegeti goika omogoroba oyio; ere takoria ebinto ebichenu goika ekero arabe bwesibirie omobere oye namache.
english: The one who touches any such thing will be unclean till evening. He must not eat any of the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water.

ekegusii: “Egari eria ekong’uswa ne chibarasi chimwamu nigo ekogenda ase ense ya sugusu, na eria ye chibarasi chindabu eyebwatie, na eria ye chibarasi chire matonto nigo ekogenda gochia ase ense ya irianyi.”
english: The one with the black horses is going toward the north country, the one with the white horses toward the west, and the one with the dappled horses toward the south."

ekegusii: Ase ensemo ya Goseni yoka, ase Abaisraeli bamenyete, nao embura y’amagena etatwete.
english: The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were.

ekegusii: Aya namang’ana ’omonto okoigwa buya aya Nyasae agoteba, naende onyorire okomanya korwa ase oria ore Igoro Mono. Na okorora amaroro akorwa ase oria Omonguru, oyogotung’ama inse na koramokigwa amaiso.
english: the oracle of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate, and whose eyes are opened:

ekegusii: Aya namang’ana ’omonto okoigwa buya aya Nyasae agoteba, oyo okorora amaroro akorwa ase ase oria Omonguru, oyogotung’ama inse na koramokigwa amaiso aye.
english: the oracle of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate, and whose eyes are opened:

ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana amakong’u omobani Habakuki aroche ase okorora.
english: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet received.

ekegusii: Korende aborokigwa bande bagacha ase obwato, bagakurura ekeonga geichire chinswe, ekiagera tibarenge are ase ense enyomo, ang’e chifuti amagana atato.
english: The other disciples followed in the boat, towing the net full of fish, for they were not far from shore, about a hundred yards.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ande onsi Yotamu akorete, ne chisegi chiaye chionsi, ne chinchera chi’obogima bwaye, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli na ab’Abayuda.
english: The other events in Jotham's reign, including all his wars and the other things he did, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ande onsi igoro y’Abiya ne chinchera chiaye, ne chinkwana chiaye, nigo arikire ase omogano bw’omobani Ido.
english: The other events of Abijah's reign, what he did and what he said, are written in the annotations of the prophet Iddo.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi Hezekia akorete, na ogokora kwaye okuya, nigo arikire ase Okorora gwa Isaya omobani, mosinto bw’Amosi, ime ase Ebuku y’Abaruoti b’Abayuda na ab’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Hezekiah's reign and his acts of devotion are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi Ahasi akorete, ne chinchera chiaye chionsi, korwa omochakano goika omoerio, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abayuda na ab’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of his reign and all his ways, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi Yehoyakimu akorete, na okogechia akorete, na okomocha kwanyorekanete asare, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli na ab’Abayuda, na Yehoyakini, omwana oye omomura, akaba okogamba ase ribaga riaye.
english: The other events of Jehoiakim's reign, the detestable things he did and all that was found against him, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son succeeded him as king.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi igoro ya Yehosafati, korwa omochakano goika omoerio, nigo arikire ase amariko a Yehu, mosinto o Hanani, ayio are ime y’Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Jehoshaphat's reign, from beginning to end, are written in the annals of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi Yeroboamu akorete, buna arwanete chisegi, na buna agambete, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Jeroboam's reign, his wars and how he ruled, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi ay’ogokora kwa Yosia, na amaya aya akorete koreng’ana naya arikire ase amachiko ’Omonene,
english: The other events of Josiah's reign and his acts of devotion, according to what is written in the Law of the LORD--

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi igoro ya Manase, na ogosaba kwaye asabete Nyasae oye, na amang’ana abarori bakwanete nere ase erieta ri’Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Manasseh's reign, including his prayer to his God and the words the seers spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are written in the annals of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi igoro ya Pekahia, na aya onsi akorete, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Pekahiah's reign, and all he did, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana onsi igoro ya Salumu, na omoroberio oria bw’ogoita akorete, nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Shallum's reign, and the conspiracy he led, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ande onsi igoro ya Usia, korwa omochakano goika omoerio, nigo arikire na Isaya omobani, mosinto bw’Amosi.
english: The other events of Uzziah's reign, from beginning to end, are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

ekegusii: Bono amang’ana ande onsi igoro ya Zakaria nigo arikire ase Ebuku y’ogokora kw’Abaruoti b’Abaisraeli.
english: The other events of Zechariah's reign are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

ekegusii: Na baria baikaransete amo nere bagachaka goteba ase emioyo yabo ime, “Nere ng’o oyo oranyare kwabera ebibe?”
english: The other guests began to say among themselves, "Who is this who even forgives sins?"

ekegusii: Abanto b’egesaku kia Reuben, na ekia Gadi, amo nekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase, konya bairire ense ere ng’umbu, moocha ya Yorodan ekaba, omwando obo. Eyio nero Musa, omosomba bw’Omonene, konya abaeire.
english: The other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received the inheritance that Moses had given them east of the Jordan, as he, the servant of the LORD, had assigned it to them.

ekegusii: Agwo amo nere Abayahudi bande bagakora obong’ainereria boria, erinde nonya Barnaba agasirigwa nobong’ainereria bwabo.
english: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.

ekegusii: Natebire “enkoro techandeka”, tari eyao, korende eyaye oria onde.) Nase ki obosibore bwane bokogambigwa nenkoro y’omonto onde omoao?
english: the other man's conscience, I mean, not yours. For why should my freedom be judged by another's conscience?

ekegusii: Korende omokungu oria o kabere agakana, “Yaya taibo, omwana oyo ore moyo, nere oyone, na omwana oria okwete nere oyoo.” Omokungu oria omotang’ani akabora, “Yaya, omwana oria okwete, nere oyoo, na omwana oyo ore moyo, nere oyone.” Naboigo bakwanete, bakoamererania ase obosio bw’omoruoti.
english: The other woman said, "No! The living one is my son; the dead one is yours." But the first one insisted, "No! The dead one is yours; the living one is mine." And so they argued before the king.

ekegusii: Emetobwa y’ebisieri nigo yareng’aine obogare na obotambe, boigo na bosio bw’Aase Aachenu Mono.
english: The outer sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe, and the one at the front of the Most Holy Place was similar.

ekegusii: Obonetu bw’enyasi ya isiko y’ebinyomba biria nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko atano, na ensemo y’oboroso boria yasogete isiko yatigetwe nigo yarenge nobogare bw’obotambe bw’amaboko atano.
english: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. The open area between the side rooms of the temple

ekegusii: Aase agwo chinyakweumia nchiagache ebiswa biabo, chibiare amagena na goturagia ebichuchu, na chibisangererie ase ekiriri gie chimbaba chiabo ime; ee agwo amakoru nasangererekaneo, kera erimo neriamwabo.
english: The owl will nest there and lay eggs, she will hatch them, and care for her young under the shadow of her wings; there also the falcons will gather, each with its mate.

ekegusii: omonto omonyene enyomba eria agende atebie omokuani: Yarorekanire ase enyomba yane ng’a ukoma mboreo.
english: the owner of the house must go and tell the priest, 'I have seen something that looks like mildew in my house.'

ekegusii: Omonto oria, omonyene enyomba, agasoka, akabatebia, “Taibo, abaminto, timobaisa gokora obokayayu buna obwo. Omonto oyio nomogeni one. Timobaisa komokorera obonyaka buna obwo.
english: The owner of the house went outside and said to them, "No, my friends, don't be so vile. Since this man is my guest, don't do this disgraceful thing.

ekegusii: rirorio omonyene engoro goika aakane omonyene etugo chibesa. Erio eng’iti eria yakure ebe eyaye.
english: the owner of the pit must pay for the loss; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.

ekegusii: Eng’ombe nigo emanyete omonyene, na etigere nigo emanyete aase omonene oye akoyeera endagera, korende Abaisraeli tibamanyeti kende, ee, amaene, abanto baane tibamanyeti kende gionsi.”
english: The ox knows his master, the donkey his owner's manger, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand."

ekegusii: Chiombe ne chitigere chiaino, echio mokoremia ase emegondo yaino, nchinyore chindagera chingiya chisongire noroteru na goswagwa, chiochoganirie nomonyo, chirie.
english: The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat fodder and mash, spread out with fork and shovel.

ekegusii: Epasaka enga buna eyio konya tiyana korendwa ase egati y’Abaisraeli korwa amatuko a Samweli omobani. Moruoti onde bw’Abaisraeli konya tana korenda Epasaka buna eria Yosia arendete, ere amo nabakuani, na Abalawi, na Abayuda bonsi, na Abaisraeli abarengeo, na abanto ba Yerusalemu.
english: The Passover had not been observed like this in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel; and none of the kings of Israel had ever celebrated such a Passover as did Josiah, with the priests, the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were there with the people of Jerusalem.

ekegusii: The Passover lambs were slaughtered, and the priests sprinkled the blood handed to them, while the Levites skinned the animals.
english: Bakanyenya chimanwa chie ching’ondi chi’Epasaka, erio abakuani bakaegwa amanyinga e chimanwa chiria, bakayanyororokia ekero Abalawi bagendererete korusia amasankwa.

ekegusii: Omochie oyio nigo orabe namarisio buna iga: Oborisia bwa sugusu nigo borabe obw’ekerengo gie chimoti amagana abere, na emerongo etano (250), na obwa irianyi amagana abere, na emerongo etano (250), na obwa moocha amagana abere, na emerongo etano (250), na obwa bosongo amagana abere, na emerongo etano (250).
english: The pastureland for the city will be 250 cubits on the north, 250 cubits on the south, 250 cubits on the east, and 250 cubits on the west.

ekegusii: Enchera y’omonto omong’aini nigo egotiira gochia ase obogima, erinde omonto oyio tabaisa kogenda inse agwo aase abakure.
english: The path of life leads upward for the wise to keep him from going down to the grave.

ekegusii: The path of the righteous is level; O upright One, you make the way of the righteous smooth.
english: Enchera y’abanyene oboronge nenteremu; naye okoyekora yaba enteremu.

ekegusii: Korende enchera y’abanyene oboronge nigo enga buna amasase a mambia; ayio akogenderera koraba goetania goika bwakia se.
english: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining ever brighter till the full light of day.

ekegusii: Obomenyo bwarenge bw’obotoereru bwasarigwe ase endamwamu entindi y’Omonene.
english: The peaceful meadows will be laid waste because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

ekegusii: Na abanto bonsi amo bakairaneria, bakabora, “Ayio onsi Omonene atebire, inatoyakore.” Musa nere akairera Omonene amang’ana abanto bairaneretie.
english: The people all responded together, "We will do everything the LORD has said." So Moses brought their answer back to the LORD.

ekegusii: Bagatebia Samweli, “Tosabere intwe, abasomba bao, ase Omonene, Nyasae oo, erinde titokwa. Twarorire ng’a amo nebibe biaito bionsi twamentire ebibe binde ebiaao bi’okoboria ng’a toegwe omoruoti.”
english: The people all said to Samuel, "Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die, for we have added to all our other sins the evil of asking for a king."

ekegusii: Abanto bakareo nabanene, naende nabatambe, abanto b’ororeria rw’Anaki mwabeire mokoigwa chinkuma chiabo, bagokwanwa: Ning’o oranyare kobua Abaanaki?
english: The people are strong and tall-- Anakites! You know about them and have heard it said: "Who can stand up against the Anakites?"

ekegusii: Bakaria, bakaigota; bagasangereria ebisamunye ebiatigarete, ebitonga bitano na bibere.
english: The people ate and were satisfied. Afterward the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

ekegusii: Abanto bakagenda ase Musa, bakamotebia, “Twakorire ebibe, ekiagera twakwanire mamincha y’Omonene na asore. Koranche osabe Omonene arusie ching’iti echi asetore.” Ase ayio Musa akabasabera.
english: The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned when we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray that the LORD will take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.

ekegusii: Abanto bagasesenia abwo bonsi beruete kogenda komenya Yerusalemu.
english: The people commended all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Bakamorigereria mono, bagakaga ng’a nabimbe, gose nagwe inse na gokwa bwango, korende ekero baganya engaki entambe, na bobe bonde tibomonyoreti, bakaonchora ebirengererio biabo, bakabora ng’a ere nenyasae.
english: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead, but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

ekegusii: amo nabanto bamwabo ase chinderia chiabo, nigo barenge amagana kianda, na emerongo etano, na batano nomo (956). Aba bonsi nigo barenge abateneneri be chiamate chiabo, kera oyomo ase eamate yaye.
english: The people from Benjamin, as listed in their genealogy, numbered 956. All these men were heads of their families.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bakarorera Ababenjamin amabeebe, ekiagera Omonene aatanenete ebisaku bi’Abaisraeli.
english: The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.

ekegusii: abanto abwo netongeire, erinde bararie ogotogigwa kwane.”
english: the people I formed for myself that they may proclaim my praise.

ekegusii: abanto abamenyete omosunte ime, barorire omobaso omonene, na abamenyete ensemo y’ekiriri ki’amakweri, omobaso obabareire.”
english: the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned."

ekegusii: Abanto ba Beteli konya batomire Sareseri, na Regemu‐Meleki, na abanto bande babo bagende gosaba Omonene, erinde banyore ogwancherwa korwa asare;
english: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech, together with their men, to entreat the LORD

ekegusii: Ekero abanto ba Gasa baigwete ng’a Samison nao are, bagaetanana aase aria, bakamoboera ase egeita ki’omochie obotuko obogima. Bagakira‐kiri obotuko bwonsi, bagateba, “Tiga toganye goika bokie mambia, erio tomoite.”
english: The people of Gaza were told, "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They made no move during the night, saying, "At dawn we'll kill him."

ekegusii: ekiagera Abaisraeli, na Abayuda, amo nabaruoti babo, na abanene b’amaruoti abo, na abakuani babo, na ababani babo, na abanto bonsi ba Yuda, na aba Yerusalemu, bakorete ebibe bikagera nkaba nendamwamu.
english: The people of Israel and Judah have provoked me by all the evil they have done-- they, their kings and officials, their priests and prophets, the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bakaroka endagera eyio mana; ero nigo yare buna chinyeke chi’amaemba enkomba, chindabu, na obwansu bwaye nigo bware buna omogati ore nobooke.
english: The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli na Abalawi mbarente okoruegwa kwabo gwe chindagera, na okw’edivai, na amaguta, ase ebinyomba ebio. Agwo nao ebikorero bi’Aase Aachenu bire; boigo nao abakuani bagokora emeremo, na abarendi b’ebiita, na abateri bare. “Titogotiga enyomba ya Nyasae oito eborwe ebinto.”
english: The people of Israel, including the Levites, are to bring their contributions of grain, new wine and oil to the storerooms where the articles for the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers and the singers stay. "We will not neglect the house of our God."

ekegusii: Barabwo n’Abaisraeli, bakorirwe koba abana ba Nyasae, barorire, obonene, bancheirwe okobwatana, baeirwe amachiko ne ribaga ri’ogosasima Nyasae, baeirwe ne chiira chiaye.
english: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory, the covenants, the receiving of the law, the temple worship and the promises.

ekegusii: Naki abamenyete Yerusalemu, na abanene babo tibamomanyete, ekiagera tibamanyete nonya namang’ana ’ababani. Ase okomogambia baikeranirie ayare gosomwa ase chibuku chi’ababani kera Esabato.
english: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Yerusalemu bakabeka Ahasia, omwana omomura omoke o Yehoramu, akaba omoruoti ase ribaga riaye, ekiagera ekeombe ki’abanto bachete amo n’Abaarabu ase egetwori konya baitire abamura abanene bonsi ba Yehoramu. Ase igo Ahasia, omomura o Yehoramu, akaba omoruoti bw’Abayuda.
english: The people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his place, since the raiders, who came with the Arabs into the camp, had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakairaneria, “Ense eria y’ebitunwa tegotoisana, na Abakanani abamenyete ase ense omweya nigo babwate chigari chi’ebioma, abwo bamenyete Beti‐Sehani na ebichie bire inse yabo, amo nabwo bamenyete ase ense omweremo ya Yesireeli boigo.”
english: The people of Joseph replied, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the plain have iron chariots, both those in Beth Shan and its settlements and those in the Valley of Jezreel."

ekegusii: Abanto b’egesaku kia Yusufu bagakwana na Yoshua, bakamotebia, “Nase ki gwatoeire ensemo eyemo yoka ebe omwando oito? Intwe nigo tore abanto abange, ekiagera Omonene otosesenirie.”
english: The people of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one allotment and one portion for an inheritance? We are a numerous people and the LORD has blessed us abundantly."

ekegusii: Abayuda na Abaisraeli nigo barenge abange mono, buna omokenye o nyancha; barabwo bakaria na konywa, bakaba bakwegokia.
english: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore; they ate, they drank and they were happy.

ekegusii: Abayuda na Abaisraeli mbasangererekane amo, bechorere oyomo abe omotwe obo okobaraa, barue ase ense eye. Ee, rituko erio ria Yesireeli nigo rirabe rinene.
english: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be reunited, and they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

ekegusii: Abayuda bagasangererekana amo, bakarigia ogokonywa korwa ase Omonene. Ee, bagacha korwa ase emechie yonsi y’Abayuda korigia Omonene.
english: The people of Judah came together to seek help from the LORD; indeed, they came from every town in Judah to seek him.

ekegusii: Abanto ba Samaria mbaegwe egesusuro, ekiagera basaririe ase Nyasae obo, mbaitwe nemioro, na abana babo banachanwe ebing’ese. Abakungu babo bare barito mbatandorwe chinda.”
english: The people of Samaria must bear their guilt, because they have rebelled against their God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to the ground, their pregnant women ripped open."

ekegusii: Korende abanto b’omochie oria bagaatananekana. Abande bakabwatana n’Abayahudi na abande nabatomwa.
english: The people of the city were divided; some sided with the Jews, others with the apostles.

ekegusii: Abanto ekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase bakamenya ense eria; bakamentekana mono, bakamenya korwa orobebe rwa Basani goika Baali‐Herimoni, na Seniri, na egetunwa kia Herimoni.
english: The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were numerous; they settled in the land from Bashan to Baal Hermon, that is, to Senir (Mount Hermon).

ekegusii: Abanto b’ense eyio bakorire obobe bw’ogochanda abande, begeire obouri, naende bachandire abataka na abaremeire, boigo bakorire abamenyi bobe, batari noboronge bw’ogokora bo.
english: The people of the land practice extortion and commit robbery; they oppress the poor and needy and mistreat the alien, denying them justice.

ekegusii: Abasabuloni bakerua nonya ngoika ogokwa, na Abanafutali boigo ase okorwana esegi ase ebitunwa.
english: The people of Zebulun risked their very lives; so did Naphtali on the heights of the field.

ekegusii: Na barabwo kobarisomire, bakagoka ase engencho y’okoremigwa okwo.
english: The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.

ekegusii: Erio abanto bakaba nomogoko, ekiagera bonsi nigo baruete ase ogwancha, na ase chinkoro chieruete ase Omonene. Daudi omoruoti boigo akaba nomogoko omonene.
english: The people rejoiced at the willing response of their leaders, for they had given freely and wholeheartedly to the LORD. David the king also rejoiced greatly.

ekegusii: Ase igo abanto bagatenena aare, ekero Musa agendete ang’e ase riire riria rimwamu, ase Nyasae arenge.
english: The people remained at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.

ekegusii: Rigereria abanto abwo nigo banga buna endo eaberi ekoboka, na buna endo ekoimokerera igoro, teri korara goika eraria echi yatwarire, goika eranywa amanyinga ay’echi yaitire.”
english: The people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion that does not rest till he devours his prey and drinks the blood of his victims."

ekegusii: Abanto bakaba bagokorera Omonene ase amatuko a Yoshua, na ase amatuko ’abagaaka abatigarete nyuma y’ogokwa kwaye, abwo baroche ogokora okwo okonene Nyasae akorerete Abaisraeli.
english: The people served the LORD throughout the lifetime of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him and who had seen all the great things the LORD had done for Israel.

ekegusii: Abanto bagatenena, bakarigereria. Na barabwo abanyene bakamokorera echeche, bakabora, “Natooretie abande, tiga etoorie ere omonyene, onye oyo nere Kristo o Nyasae, Omochore oye.”
english: The people stood watching, and the rulers even sneered at him. They said, "He saved others; let him save himself if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One."

ekegusii: Erio Abaisraeli bagatebia Samweli, “Mbarabi baria bakanete ng’a Saulo takobagambera. Renta abanto abwo, tobaite.”
english: The people then said to Samuel, "Who was it that asked, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Bring these men to us and we will put them to death."

ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bakong’etie amasio abo ne chinkoro chiabo. Asebare nao nkogotoma gochia, goika obatebie iga: Aya naro Omonene Nyasae agoteba.
english: The people to whom I am sending you are obstinate and stubborn. Say to them, 'This is what the Sovereign LORD says.'

ekegusii: Bakarenta omomura oria, ore moyo, bakaba nokoremigwa okonene.
english: The people took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo barenge gotaara ase omosunte, bono barorire omobaso omonene; abwo bamenyete ase ense y’ekiriri ki’amakweri omobaso obabareire.
english: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned.

ekegusii: Abanto nigo barenge gosoka bayesangereria, naende bayesia ne chingena, gose bayeswaga ase chikonu. Erio baba bakoyeiyekera ase chinyongo na koyeroisia yaba emegati. Igo yarenge gwansa buna amaandasi aroiseirie amaguta.
english: The people went around gathering it, and then ground it in a handmill or crushed it in a mortar. They cooked it in a pot or made it into cakes. And it tasted like something made with olive oil.

ekegusii: Abanto bakagenda Beteli, bagaikaransa aroro ase obosio bwa Nyasae goika mogoroba, bagaaka amariogi, bakarera nobororo,
english: The people went to Bethel, where they sat before God until evening, raising their voices and weeping bitterly.

ekegusii: Bagaichana bonsi, goika bakaborania, bakobora, “Inki eke? Nokworokereria okoyia! Omonto oyo nigo abwate okobua kw’ogochika nonya nebirecha bi’eubi, na birobio bikomoigwera.”
english: The people were all so amazed that they asked each other, "What is this? A new teaching-- and with authority! He even gives orders to evil spirits and they obey him."

ekegusii: Bagakumia ase okworokereria kwaye, ekiagera arenge koborokereria buna oyore nokobua, gose tari buna aborokia b’amariko.
english: The people were amazed at his teaching, because he taught them as one who had authority, not as the teachers of the law.

ekegusii: Goika emeganda egakumia ekero bachia korora abarenge amamama bagokwana, abarenge ebirema babeire buya, abarenge amagata bakogenda, na abarenge emeuko bakorora; bakamobaka Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli.
english: The people were amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled made well, the lame walking and the blind seeing. And they praised the God of Israel.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baganyete na konakorengereria, bonsi bakeboria igoro ya Yohana ng’a, gose nere Kristo.
english: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John might possibly be the Christ.

ekegusii: Abanto bamenyete Samaria mbatengechigwe ase engencho y’omogwekano bw’emori bagosasima agwo Beti‐Aveni. Abwo bakoyosasima mbarere, na abakuani baye mbeng’ererie, ekiagera obonene bwaye bwasirigwe.
english: The people who live in Samaria fear for the calf-idol of Beth Aven. Its people will mourn over it, and so will its idolatrous priests, those who had rejoiced over its splendor, because it is taken from them into exile.

ekegusii: Abanto bakagenderera korua ebing’wanso agwo aase aimokererete igoro agosasimerwa, korende nigo babiruete ase Omonene, Nyasae obo bweka.
english: The people, however, continued to sacrifice at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

ekegusii: Abanto nigo barenge koruera ebing’wanso ase ebisasimero biarenge aase aimokererete igoro, ekiagera nyomba ende yonsi konya teraagachwa ase baranyare gosasima erieta ri’Omonene.
english: The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because a temple had not yet been built for the Name of the LORD.

ekegusii: Abanto mbasambwe bayie babe ribu, na buna amagwa akobutorwa asambwa nomorero.”
english: The peoples will be burned as if to lime; like cut thornbushes they will be set ablaze."

ekegusii: Oria Omofarisai agatenena, agasaba iga ase omoyo oye: Nyasae, nakoiraneirie ng’a mbuya mono, ekiagera inche tindi buna abanto bande, abauri, abatari boronge, abatomani, gose buna oyo omorusia ebango.
english: The Pharisee stood up and prayed about himself: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other men-- robbers, evildoers, adulterers-- or even like this tax collector.

ekegusii: Abafarisai na Abasadukai bagacha ase ogoteema Yeso, bakamosaba aborokie egekone buna ekemanyererio korwa igoro.
english: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus and tested him by asking him to show them a sign from heaven.

ekegusii: Erio Abafarisai na abande ase aborokia b’amariko barwete Yerusalemu, bagasangerereka asare.
english: The Pharisees and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus and

ekegusii: Aborokia baria b’amariko na Abafarisai bagachaka korengereria, bakobora, “Ning’o oyo ogokwana okorama? Ning’o oranyare kwabera ebibe, otatiga oyomo, nere Nyasae?”
english: The Pharisees and the teachers of the law began thinking to themselves, "Who is this fellow who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"

ekegusii: Aborokia b’amariko na Abafarisai bakamotega korora gose namogwenie ase rituko ri’Esabato, banyare komosoera.
english: The Pharisees and the teachers of the law were looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, so they watched him closely to see if he would heal on the Sabbath.

ekegusii: Abafarisai bakaoroka, bagachaka koamererania na Yeso, bakarigia aborokie egekone buna ekemanyererio korwa igoro, bakomoteema.
english: The Pharisees came and began to question Jesus. To test him, they asked him for a sign from heaven.

ekegusii: Erio Abafarisai bakamotebia, “Aye nigo okwebera kirori omonyene, na oborori bwao tibori obw’ekeene.”
english: The Pharisees challenged him, "Here you are, appearing as your own witness; your testimony is not valid."

ekegusii: Nabo Omonene agachia komanya ng’a Abafarisai baigure ng’a Yeso okorire aborokigwa abange kobua Yohana, na kobatisa,
english: The Pharisees heard that Jesus was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John,

ekegusii: Abafarisai bakaigwa omoganda okwemurungania igoro yaye. Erio abakuani abanene na Abafarisai bagatoma abarendi erinde bamobwate.
english: The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering such things about him. Then the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple guards to arrest him.

ekegusii: Abafarisai bakamobcria, “Rora, naki bagokora eritari boronge gokorwa ase rituko ri’Esabato?”
english: The Pharisees said to him, "Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?"

ekegusii: Abafarisai abarenge abanchi enibo bakaigwa amang’ana aya onsi, bakamosekereria.
english: The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and were sneering at Jesus.

ekegusii: Abanene b’Abafilisti bakaba bagocha korwana esegi, korende ase engaki ende yonsi Daudi akaba okonyora obobui kobua abasomba bonsi ba Saulo. Ase igo erieta riaye rigakuma mono na gotogigwa.
english: The Philistine commanders continued to go out to battle, and as often as they did, David met with more success than the rest of Saul's officers, and his name became well known.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bagatiga emegwekano yabo y’ogosasimwa aroro, na Daudi na abanto baye bakayerusiao na koyeira.
english: The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.

ekegusii: Bakaboria, “Inee! Okoruegwa okwo gw’okomocha nkoroki torairanie ase Omonene?” Barabwo bakabairaneria, “Emegwekano etano y’amagumba, na etano ye chimbeba, yonsi eroisirie korwa ase etahabu. Moire emegwekano ereng’aine nomobaro bw’abagambi b’Abafilisti, ekiagera amaakwa ayio nigo abete igoro asemore mwensi, na igoro ase abanene baino boigo.
english: The Philistines asked, "What guilt offering should we send to him?" They replied, "Five gold tumors and five gold rats, according to the number of the Philistine rulers, because the same plague has struck both you and your rulers.

ekegusii: The Philistines assembled and came and set up camp at Shunem, while Saul gathered all the Israelites and set up camp at Gilboa.
english: Abafilisti bagasangererekana, bagatoora agwo Sunemu; Saulo nere agasangereria Abaisraeli bonsi amo, nabarabwo bagatoora agwo Giliboa.

ekegusii: Erio Abafilisti bagasangererekana amo barwanie Abaisraeli. Nigo barenge ne chigari chilifu emerongo etato (30,000), na abariini chibarasi chilifu isano nemo (6,000), na abarwani bande abange buna omokenye ore engegu y’enyancha. Barabwo bagacha, bagatoora agwo Mikimasi, moocha ya Beti‐Aveni.
english: The Philistines assembled to fight Israel, with three thousand chariots, six thousand charioteers, and soldiers as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Micmash, east of Beth Aven.

ekegusii: Erio Abafilisti bakarangeria abakuani babo na abaringoria, bakababoria, “Ninki togokora ase Esanduku eye y’Omonene? Totebie inchera ki torayeiranie aase aye.”
english: the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how we should send it back to its place."

ekegusii: Abafilisti bakeroberia korwania Abaisraeli. Esegi egatindia, na Abafilisti bakabua Abaisraeli, bagaita abanto chilifu inye.
english: The Philistines deployed their forces to meet Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand of them on the battlefield.

ekegusii: The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, and Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.
english: Abafilisti bagasangereria abarwani babo bonsi b’esegi agwo Afeki, na Abaisraeli bagatoora ang’e nensoko yarenge agwo Yesireeli.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bagatiga chinyasae chiabo aroro, na Daudi agachika abanto, bachisambe nomorero.
english: The Philistines had abandoned their gods there, and David gave orders to burn them in the fire.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bagatenena ase egetunwa ekemo, na Abaisraeli ase ekende, ne rikura ndiarenge ase egati yabo.
english: The Philistines occupied one hill and the Israelites another, with the valley between them.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bakabwatia Saulo mono, na abamura baye, bagaita Yonathani, na Aminadabu, na Maliki‐Sua, abamura ba Saulo.
english: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bakabwatia Saulo na abamura baye, bagaita Yonathani, na Abinadabu, na Malikisua, abamura ba Saulo.
english: The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua.

ekegusii: Erio Abafilisti bagatiira, bagatoora ase ense ya Yuda, bakaumokera omochie o Lei.
english: The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi.

ekegusii: bakaondoka mono, bagakwana, “Enyasae yachire ase egetwori keria.” Naende bagateba, “Obobe nobwaito! Egento kenga buna ekio tikiana gokorekana asetore nonya ng’ake.
english: the Philistines were afraid. "A god has come into the camp," they said. "We're in trouble! Nothing like this has happened before.

ekegusii: Timoria embeche; nebwate ebitaago biatananegete, korende teri koria eng’ang’ura. Ase ayio nebe asemore eyetachenegeti. Timoria chinyama chie ching’iti echio gose timokuna emebere yabo ekero chiakure.
english: The pig is also unclean; although it has a split hoof, it does not chew the cud. You are not to eat their meat or touch their carcasses.

ekegusii: Chisiiro chia igoro nigo chigotengecha, chiakumia ase ogotogonyera kwaye.
english: The pillars of the heavens quake, aghast at his rebuke.

ekegusii: Abatigari baye nigo oborwaire borabaite, na abakungu baratigwe bare ababoraka, tibakonyara kobareera.
english: The plague will bury those who survive him, and their widows will not weep for them.

ekegusii: The plan seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his officials.
english: Amang’ana ayio akagwenera Farao amo nabasomba baye bonsi.

ekegusii: Omoroberio oyio okaba omoronge ase omoruoti na ase omosangererekano bwonsi.
english: The plan seemed right both to the king and to the whole assembly.

ekegusii: Emeroberio y’omonto omong’aini nigo ekomorentera ebitoki ebinge, korende omonto okoayerera nigo akogenderera koremerwa.
english: The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.

ekegusii: Ebirengererio bi’omonyene oboronge nigo bire ebi’ekeene, korende ogosemia kw’abakori amabe nigo kore okw’obong’ainereria.
english: The plans of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

ekegusii: Ebisakorwa ebiatigarete ase abarwani b’esegi, ebi barentete ekero babuete, nabio ebi: ching’ondi, amo ne chimbori, chilifu amagana atano na rimo na emerongo etano na ebere na isano (675,000),
english: The plunder remaining from the spoils that the soldiers took was 675,000 sheep,

ekegusii: Gaki, ring’ana rinene ri’ayio togokwana nario eri: Ntore n’Omokuani Omonene buna iga, oikaransete ensemo ya borio y’ekerogo ki’Obonene aria igoro,
english: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

ekegusii: Oyesoyie ase chibonyi echio chie chinsemo ibere chi’egesasimero, ebeo ekero gekobogorigwa.
english: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so they will be on two sides of the altar when it is carried.

ekegusii: Emiaro eyio goika ebe ime ase chibonyi echio, terusigwao.
english: The poles are to remain in the rings of this ark; they are not to be removed.

ekegusii: Akabaacha emiaro eria korwa ase emekonge, akayeooma netahabu.
english: The poles for carrying the table were made of acacia wood and were overlaid with gold.

ekegusii: Omonto omotaka nigo agechire nonya nase abanto bamwabo, korende omonda nigo abwate abasani abange.
english: The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.

ekegusii: Omotaka na omochandi nigo bamenyete amo; Omonene nere okobaa bonsi babere oborabu bw’amaiso.
english: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.

ekegusii: Abwo bare abaitongo mbanyore endagera barie baigote. Abanto bakorigia Omonene mbabe bakomotogia, ne chinkoro chiaino nchigenderere koba moyo goika kare na kare.
english: The poor will eat and be satisfied; they who seek the LORD will praise him-- may your hearts live forever!

ekegusii: Abwo bakoreire bobe mbarore ayio, bagoke; inwe aba mokorigia Nyasae, tiga chinkoro chiaino chikorwe chinyia.
english: The poor will see and be glad-- you who seek God, may your hearts live!

ekegusii: Naki amatuko onsi nigo more nabataka amo nainwe, na kero kende gionsi mwanchete, namonyare kobakorera amaya, korende timori nainche amatuko onsi.
english: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them any time you want. But you will not always have me.

ekegusii: ekiagera amatuko onsi nigo more nabataka amo nainwe, korende timori nainche amatuko onsi.
english: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have me.

ekegusii: Abare abataka mono mbaragerigwe, na abaremeire bamenye nobotoereru. Korende abare ritina riaino mbaite nenchara, na abatigari baino nimbaite.
english: The poorest of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety. But your root I will destroy by famine; it will slay your survivors.

ekegusii: Enyomba eria yaagachetwe bosio bwe Hekalu enyene nigo yarenge iga: Obotambe bwaye gochia ime nobw’ekerengo ki’amaboko ikomi, na obogare bwaye amaboko emerongo ebere, nigo bwareng’aine nobogare bwe Hekalu.
english: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple extended the width of the temple, that is twenty cubits, and projected ten cubits from the front of the temple.

ekegusii: Enyomba eria yaagachetwe bosio bwe Hekalu nigo yarenge iga: obogare bwaye nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko emerongo ebere, na nigo bwareng’aine nobogare bwe Hekalu, na obotambe bwaye gochia igoro nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko rigana erimo na emerongo ebere. Sulemani akayeooma korwa ime ne chitahabu chichenire.
english: The portico at the front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the width of the building and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.

ekegusii: Obogare bw’egesona ekio nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko emerongo ebere, na obotambe bwaye gochia ime obw’amaboko ikomi na rimo. Nkiarengeo ekeriinero kiare koriinerwa gochiao. Ase kera ensemo bosio bw’emetobwa eria, chisiiro nchiarengeo.
english: The portico was twenty cubits wide, and twelve cubits from front to back. It was reached by a flight of stairs, and there were pillars on each side of the jambs.

ekegusii: ne chindogio, na ebichiko, na ebitaabo. Ebinto ebio bionsi biaatoire nigo biare ebibekerero bi’enyomba y’Omonene, Hiramu aroisereretie omoruoti Sulemani. Bionsi nigo biaroisetigwe korwa ase chitaai chisibirie buya.
english: the pots, shovels and sprinkling bowls. All these objects that Huram made for King Solomon for the temple of the LORD were of burnished bronze.

ekegusii: ne chindogio, na ebichiko, ne chiuma, na ebikorero binde bionsi, Ebinto ebio bionsi Huramu‐Abu akabiroisia korwa ase chitaai chikomeka‐meka, buna Sulemani amotebetie akore ase enyomba y’Omonene.
english: the pots, shovels, meat forks and all related articles. All the objects that Huram-Abi made for King Solomon for the temple of the LORD were of polished bronze.

ekegusii: Na okobua gwe chibarasi chiria nigo kware ase emenwa yabo, na ase ebimincha biabo. Ebimincha biabo nigo biagwekaine ching’iti chire nemetwe, na ase ebio nigo chiare koroma.
english: The power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails were like snakes, having heads with which they inflict injury.

ekegusii: Okoboko kw’Omonene gokaba amo n’Elija, ere agesiba ekenema norokini rwaye, akaminyoka agatang’ana bosio bw’Ahabu goika akagenda ase omochie o Yesireeli.
english: The power of the LORD came upon Elijah and, tucking his cloak into his belt, he ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.

ekegusii: Amachiko ’Omonene namaronge, nigo akogokia enkoro; ring’ana Omonene achikire nerironge, nigo rikorenta oborabu ase amaiso.
english: The precepts of the LORD are right, giving joy to the heart. The commands of the LORD are radiant, giving light to the eyes.

ekegusii: Morue amaguta ekerengo gechikire, ebituba bibere korwa ase ekori eyemo. (Ekori eyemo nigo ereng’aine ne homeri eyemo; nigo ebwate chibati ikomi).
english: The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each cor (which consists of ten baths or one homer, for ten baths are equivalent to a homer).

ekegusii: Nigo barenge goakana ekeng’ese gi’esekeli ase ogotiererigwa obokombe na ekoyo, na ebing’ese bibere bi’esekeli, ase ogotiererigwa egesire, na kogechoma ase ogokerambora.
english: The price was two thirds of a shekel for sharpening plowshares and mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening forks and axes and for repointing goads.

ekegusii: Oboenenu bw’enkoro yao bwakong’ainire, aye omenyete ime y’emienya y’ebitare; agwo ase omenyete aimokererete igoro. Nigo ogokwana ase enkoro yao ime, gweteba: Ning’o orang’iyerie gochia inse?”
english: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rocks and make your home on the heights, you who say to yourself, 'Who can bring me down to the ground?'

ekegusii: Omokuani oria akabairaneria, “Genda nomorembe! Orogendo rwaino nigo rore ase oborendi bw’Omonene.”
english: The priest answered them, "Go in peace. Your journey has the LORD's approval."

ekegusii: Naende korwa ase okoruegwa okwo aimokie goke, goichire roe, kobe ekeinyorio ng’a okoruegwa okwo nokw’Omonene, na kogosambera ase egesasimero, na nyuma y’ayio ae omokungu oria amache aria anywe.
english: The priest is then to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial offering and burn it on the altar; after that, he is to have the woman drink the water.

ekegusii: erio omokuani amorenge naende, na kararore ng’a oborwaire boria bwatubire omobere bwonsi bw’omonto oria, rirorio atebe ng’a ochenekire. Onye omobere bwonsi obeire omorabu, omonto oria obeire oyochenegete.
english: the priest is to examine him, and if the disease has covered his whole body, he shall pronounce that person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.

ekegusii: omokuani amorenge naende, na kararore ng’a richoncho riria riesiareire, takorigia korora gose amarionya are monuri nareo, omonto oyio tachenegeti.
english: the priest is to examine him, and if the itch has spread in the skin, the priest does not need to look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.

ekegusii: na ere kararore ng’a egesambo keria giesiareire ase risankwa, erio atebe ng’a omonto oyio tachenegeti. Obwo noborwaire bwa ukoma.
english: The priest is to examine him, and if the rash has spread in the skin, he shall pronounce him unclean; it is an infectious disease.

ekegusii: The priest is to examine him, and if the sores have turned white, the priest shall pronounce the infected person clean; then he will be clean.
english: na ere amorenge buya, na onye egesambo kiaonchokire na koraba, erio omokuani atebe ng’a omonto oyio ochenekire.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, omokuani karamorenge arore ng’a egesambo kebimbete ase risio riria, magega gose bosio, kere nobobariri na oborabu, na nigo gekororekana buna oborwaire bwa ukoma mbore ase risankwa ri’omobere,
english: The priest is to examine him, and if the swollen sore on his head or forehead is reddish-white like an infectious skin disease,

ekegusii: na ere amorenge buya. Kararore egesambo ekerabu ase risankwa, na amarionya aonchokire abeire amarabu, naende onye enyama embariri yachakire gokina imeo,
english: The priest is to examine him, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white and if there is raw flesh in the swelling,

ekegusii: Ere amorenge buya, na kararore ng’a egesambo keria giakorire engoro gochia ime goetania risankwa, na amarionya areo aonchokire na koraba, omokuani atebe ng’a omonto oria tachenegeti. Obwo noborwaire bwa ukoma bwaorokeire ase rigumba riria.
english: The priest is to examine it, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an infectious skin disease that has broken out where the boil was.

ekegusii: Omokuani arenge egento kere na ukoma, erio akebeke ase egesomo ase engaki y’amatuko atano na abere.
english: The priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the affected article for seven days.

ekegusii: Omokuani oyio arenge oborwaire obwo buya. Kararore ng’a amarionya are ase egesambo keria aonchokire abeire amarabu, na oborwaire bwakorire engoro gochia ime goetania risankwa, rirorio oborwaire obwo nobwa ukoma. Ekero omokuani arengire omonto oria buya, atebe ng’a oyio onyorekanire ng’a tachenegeti.
english: The priest is to examine the sore on his skin, and if the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore appears to be more than skin deep, it is an infectious skin disease. When the priest examines him, he shall pronounce him ceremonially unclean.

ekegusii: omokuani arenge egesambo ekio. Onye gekorete engoro gochia ime goetania risankwa, naende onye amarionya areo are monuri na konyererea, erio omokuani atebe ng’a omonto oyio tachenegeti. Erio nerichoncho ri’oborwaire bwa ukoma ase omotwe oye, gose ase ekenyonyobu.
english: the priest is to examine the sore, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest shall pronounce that person unclean; it is an itch, an infectious disease of the head or chin.

ekegusii: omokuani arenge egesambo ekio. Onye amarionya egesambo ekio aonchokire na koraba, naende egesambo kiabeire engoro gochia ime goetania risankwa ri’omobere oye, obwo noborwaire bwa ukoma bwasokire ase risambo ri’omorero riarenge. Omokuani atebe ng’a omonto oyio tachenegeti. Obwo noborwaire bwa ukoma.
english: the priest is to examine the spot, and if the hair in it has turned white, and it appears to be more than skin deep, it is an infectious disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is an infectious skin disease.

ekegusii: omokuani amorenge. Nere kararore ng’a ebisambo bie risankwa ri’omobere nigo bire ebirabu ake, ebisambo ebio tibiri bobe; omonto oyio ochenekire.
english: the priest is to examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; that person is clean.

ekegusii: omokuani agende ayerenge naende. Onye egetamase keria giesiareire ase enyomba eria, obwo noukoma, yabeire eyetachenegeti.
english: the priest is to go and examine it and, if the mildew has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew; the house is unclean.

ekegusii: na omokuani agende isiko y’egetwori amorenge. Kararore ng’a omonto oria ogwenire korwa ase oborwaire bwa ukoma bwamoriete,
english: The priest is to go outside the camp and examine him. If the person has been healed of his infectious skin disease,

ekegusii: Omokuani akore okobwatanigwa ase obosio bw’Omonene ase omonto oria okorire ebibe atancheti, na omonto oria naaberwe.
english: The priest is to make atonement before the LORD for the one who erred by sinning unintentionally, and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.

ekegusii: Omokuani akore okobwatanigwa ase omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli, na barabwo mbaaberwe, ekiagera okomocha okwo nigo gwakoretwe mosiabano ase ogotancha. Barabwo barentire okoruegwa kwabo, ekeng’wanso kegosambwa nomorero ase Omonene, naboigo barentire ekeng’wanso kiabo ki’ebibe ase Omonene ase engencho y’okomocha kwabo gwakoretwe mosiabano ase ogotancha.
english: The priest is to make atonement for the whole Israelite community, and they will be forgiven, for it was not intentional and they have brought to the LORD for their wrong an offering made by fire and a sin offering.

ekegusii: Omokuani arue riruma erimo ribe ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe, na erinde eki’ogosambwa ase ogokora okobwatanigwa ase Omwerwa oria, ekiagera okorire ebibe ase ogoika ang’e negetondo. Ase rituko erio erio omonto oria achene omotwe oye,
english: The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for him because he sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. That same day he is to consecrate his head.

ekegusii: Omokuani achike ng’a ebinto bionsi bire ase enyomba eyio birusigweo ritang’ani atarasoao koborenga. Onye tibagokora bo rirorio ebinto bionsi bire nyomba ime nabibe bitachenegeti. Nyuma y’ayio omokuani asoe ase enyomba eyio koyerenga.
english: The priest is to order the house to be emptied before he goes in to examine the mildew, so that nothing in the house will be pronounced unclean. After this the priest is to go in and inspect the house.

ekegusii: Omokuani ataaere amaguta ase oroe rw’okoboko kwaye gw’okobee.
english: The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand,

ekegusii: Amaguta make ase ayio agotigara ase oroe rwaye ayagindie mesia y’ogoto kwa borio kw’omonto oria ogochia gochenwa, na ekiara ekenene gi’okoboko kwaye kwa borio, na ekiara ekenene gi’okogoro kwaye kwa borio, igoro ase amanyinga ’ekeng’wanso gi’okomocha agindirieo.
english: The priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.

ekegusii: Omokuani arue erimo ribe ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe, na erinde eki’ogosambwa. Ase enchera eyio nakore okobwatanigwa ase omokungu oria ase obosio bwane, ase engencho y’ogotacheneka kwaye kw’ogoiteka kw’amanyinga.
english: The priest is to sacrifice one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement for her before the LORD for the uncleanness of her discharge.

ekegusii: Omokuani arue erimo ribe ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe, na erinde ribe ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa. Ase enchera eyio akore okobwatanigwa ase omonto oria ase obosio bwane, ase engencho y’okorua kwaye kw’amache anga buna chimengere.
english: The priest is to sacrifice them, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement before the LORD for the man because of his discharge.

ekegusii: Na omokuani asiarere amanyinga ase egesasimero kiane agwo ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano, naende asambe ebitinya bibe rimisu rigiya rikongwenera.
english: The priest is to sprinkle the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.

ekegusii: Erio omokuani otenenerete aimokie obosie obonuke boichire roe korwa ase okoruegwa okwo kw’endagera, na amaguta, na ubani yonsi ere igoro yaye, abisambere ase egesasimero, bibe ekemanyererio ng’a okoruegwa okwo nokwane inche Omonene, kore ne rimisu rigiya rikongwenera.
english: The priest is to take a handful of fine flour and oil, together with all the incense on the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.

ekegusii: Omokuani arusie korwa ase okoboko kw’omokungu oria okoruegwa kwe risemi, na kogosungusia ase obosio bw’Omonene. Nyuma y’ayio akorente ase egesasimero.
english: The priest is to take from her hands the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD and bring it to the altar.

ekegusii: Erio omokuani abogorie oroko rw’emecharake na orosagia rwa hisopo, na eusi embariri, erio abirute aseomorero oria ogosamba eng’ombe eria.
english: The priest is to take some cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer.

ekegusii: Omokuani aimokie amanyinga make ay’ekeng’wanso gi’okomocha, na agindie mesia y’ogoto kwa borio kw’omonto oria ogochia gochenwa, naende agindie ekiara ekenene gi’okoboko kwaye kwa borio, na ekiara ekenene gi’okogoro kwaye kwa borio.
