ekegusii: nigo barenge chilifu amagana atano na rimo na isato, na amagana atano, na emerongo etano (603,550).
english: The total number was 603,550.

ekegusii: Obotambe bwe chimbaba chionsi chi’abakerubi baria nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko emerongo ebere. Obotambe bw’orobaba oromo rw’omokerubi oyomo nigo bwarenge obw’amaboko atano. Orwo rwaramboire rogaika enyasi y’enyomba. Na orobaba ronde rw’obotambe buna obwo rogakunana norobaba rw’omokerubi onde.
english: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the temple wall, while its other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.

ekegusii: Emechie yonsi egati y’Ekironi na Gati, eyio Abafilisti konya baurire Abaisraeli, ekairanigwa amo ne chingongo chiaetanaineo. Agwo boigo omorembe okaba ase egati y’Abaisraeli na Abaamori.
english: The towns from Ekron to Gath that the Philistines had captured from Israel were restored to her, and Israel delivered the neighboring territory from the power of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

ekegusii: Engaki eria abanto bare ase emechie y’Abayuda, na aba Yerusalemu nabasambere chinyasae echio ubani na korera ase chirochio ng’a chibakonye, korende tichikonyara kobatooria ekero ogosirigwa korabachere.
english: The towns of Judah and the people of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but they will not help them at all when disaster strikes.

ekegusii: Emechie yonsi y’Abalawi eyarenge ase egati y’omwando bw’Abaisraeli nigo yarenge emerongo ene, na etano na etato, amo namarisio arengeo.
english: The towns of the Levites in the territory held by the Israelites were forty-eight in all, together with their pasturelands.

ekegusii: Emechie eyio morae Abalawi nigo morayerusie korwa ase eria Abaisraeli babwate. Morusie emechie emenge korwa ase egesaku keria kere ekenene kebwate emechie emenge, na korwa ase egesaku kere egeke kebwate emechie emeke morusie emekeo, koreng’ana nomobaro obo.”
english: The towns you give the Levites from the land the Israelites possess are to be given in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: Take many towns from a tribe that has many, but few from one that has few."

ekegusii: Omote oria nigo ogendererete gokina, okaba ne chinguru, ogatambea gochia igoro, okarorekana ase chinsinyo chionsi chi’ense.
english: The tree grew large and strong and its top touched the sky; it was visible to the ends of the earth.

ekegusii: Omote oria kwaroche orenge omonene mono, na omotambe gochia igoro, naende okarorekana ase chinsinyo chionsi chi’ense;
english: The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, with its top touching the sky, visible to the whole earth,

ekegusii: Emete y’emegondo inayame amatunda abo, ne riroba ndiame endagera yaye; barabwo abanyene mbamenye ase ense eyio bare nobotoereru. Ekero ndabune amakorogoto arue ase amagoti abo, mbatoorie korwa ase amaboko ay’abwo babakorete abasomba, erio mbamanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene.
english: The trees of the field will yield their fruit and the ground will yield its crops; the people will be secure in their land. They will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them.

ekegusii: Emete y’Omonene nigo egoisaneka namache, ee, emecharake ya Lebanoni, eyio Omonene asimegete.
english: The trees of the LORD are well watered, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.

ekegusii: Abaratoore ang’e nabarabwo n’Abaaseri. Pagieli, mosinto bw’okirani, nere orabe omotang’ani abo,
english: The tribe of Asher will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.

ekegusii: Naende abaratoore ensemo yabo n’Ababenjamin. Abidani, mosinto o Gidioni, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,
english: The tribe of Benjamin will be next. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.

ekegusii: Emechie ye chiamate chi’egesaku kia Benjamin nigo yarenge: Yeriko, na Beti‐Hogila, na Emeki‐Kesisi,
english: The tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan, had the following cities: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,

ekegusii: Naende abaratoore ensemo yabo n’Abagadi. Eliasafu, mosinto o Reueli, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,
english: The tribe of Gad will be next. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Deuel.

ekegusii: The tribe of Issachar will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
english: Abaratoore ang’e nabarabwo n’Abaisakaru. Netaneli, mosinto o Suari, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,

ekegusii: Abaratoore ang’e nabarabwo n’Abamanase. Gamalieli, mosinto o Pedasuri, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,
english: The tribe of Manasseh will be next to them. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

ekegusii: Naende abaratoore ensemo yabo n’Abanafutali. Ahira, mosinto bw’Enani, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,
english: The tribe of Naphtali will be next. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.

ekegusii: The tribe of Simeon will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
english: Abaratoore ang’e nabarabwo n’Abasimeoni. Selumieli, mosinto o Surisadai, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,

ekegusii: Naende abaratoore ensemo yabo n’Abasabuloni. Eliabu, mosinto o Heloni, nere orabe omotang’ani obo,
english: The tribe of Zebulun will be next. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ebisaku bi’Abaisraeli bagatoma abanto gochia ase chiamate chionsi chia Benjamin, bakabora, “Nobokayayu bore naki, obo bwakorekanire ase egati yaino?
english: The tribes of Israel sent men throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What about this awful crime that was committed among you?

ekegusii: Emechando yaye nigo ekomoiranera; na ogokora kwaye okobe nigo gokomogwera omonyene.
english: The trouble he causes recoils on himself; his violence comes down on his own head.

ekegusii: Omoichano nigo oichire ase enkoro yane, ndusie ase obokong’u bwane,
english: The troubles of my heart have multiplied; free me from my anguish.

ekegusii: Omobaso bw’ekeene, oria okobarera kera omonto, ngocha orenge ase ense.
english: The true light that gives light to every man was coming into the world.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omwegenwa ase oboronge bwaye nabe moyo, korende oyo okorigia obobe na kobobwatia nakwe.
english: The truly righteous man attains life, but he who pursues evil goes to his death.

ekegusii: Nigo yarenge emeremo y’ababugia ebirombeta na abateri baigwekane bagoterera amo ase ogotogia Omonene na komoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono. Na amariogi ’amatera aimokereretigwe igoro, na ay’ebirombeta, na aye chisani chiarenge goakanigwa kwoga, na ay’ebinto binde biare kobugigwa, ekero baare gotogia Omonene, bagoteba, “Omonene nomuya, ekiagera obwanchani bwaye bwa botambe nigo bogendererete kare na kare.” Agwo enyomba y’Omonene egaichorwa ne riire,
english: The trumpeters and singers joined in unison, as with one voice, to give praise and thanks to the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals and other instruments, they raised their voices in praise to the LORD and sang: "He is good; his love endures forever." Then the temple of the LORD was filled with a cloud,

ekegusii: Eriogi riaye nariigweke ase chinsinyo chionsi chi’ense, ekiagera Omonene nabwate ekina nebisaku bionsi. Narente abanto bonsi ase ekina, abakori amabe nabaitwe nemioro. Inche Omonene nakwanire.”
english: The tumult will resound to the ends of the earth, for the LORD will bring charges against the nations; he will bring judgment on all mankind and put the wicked to the sword,'" declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Obwa ikomi na kabere bokagwera Hasabia; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Oyo o ikomi na kabere, Helidai korwa Netofa bw’ororeria rw’Otinieli akaba omoteneneri bw’ekeombe ki’omotienyi o ikomi na kabere. Ekeombe kiaye nigo kiarenge nabanto chilifu emerongo ebere na inye (24,000).
english: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his division.

ekegusii: Ebiita biria ikomi na bibere nechiruru ikomi na ibere, kera egeita neruru eyemo. Na enchera y’omochie netahabu engiya ere buna ekerore getagotanga omobaso.
english: The twelve gates were twelve pearls, each gate made of a single pearl. The great street of the city was of pure gold, like transparent glass.

ekegusii: Na ebitaabo biria ikomi na bibere biaroisirie korwa ase chitahabu biichire na ubani, nigo biarenge kera ekemo noborito bwe chisekeli ikomi koreng’ana nekerengo gi’esekeli yare gokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. Oborito bwe chitahabu chi’ebinto ebio bionsi nigo bwarenge chisekeli rigana erimo na emerongo ebere.
english: The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. Altogether, the gold dishes weighed a hundred and twenty shekels.

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere bokagwera Eliata; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere na rimo bokagwera Hotiri; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere na rimo bokagwera Yakini, na obwa emerongo ebere na kabere Gamuli;
english: the twenty-first to Jakin, the twenty-second to Gamul,

ekegusii: Na abagaaka baria emerongo ebere na bane amo ne ching’iti chiria inye chire moyo bagatung’ama, bagasasima Nyasae oyoikaransete ase ekerogo ki’obonene, bagoteba, “Amina. Haleluya!”
english: The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who was seated on the throne. And they cried: "Amen, Hallelujah!"

ekegusii: abagaaka baria emerongo ebere na bane bagotung’ama ase obosio bwaye oyoikaransete ase ekerogo ki’obonene, na komosasima ere oyore moyo goika kare na kare. Barabwo nigo bakoruta chigutwa chiabo bosio bw’ekerogo keria ki’obonene, bagoteba,
english: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne, and worship him who lives for ever and ever. They lay their crowns before the throne and say:

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere na kane bokagwera Romamuti‐Eseri; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere na kabere bokagwera Gidaliti; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: obwa emerongo ebere na gatato bokagwera Delaya, na obwa emerongo ebere na kane Maasia.
english: the twenty-third to Delaiah and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

ekegusii: Obwa emerongo ebere na gatato bokagwera Mahasioti; ere amo nabana baye abamura na abamwabo nigo barenge ikomi na babere.
english: the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and relatives, 12

ekegusii: Abamalaika baria babere bakagenda, bagaika Sodomu mogoroba, na Loti nigo arenge oikaransete geita gia Sodomu. Ekero Loti abaroche, akaimoka kobarotota, agatung’ama inse, akaumama,
english: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.

ekegusii: Ase ayio ebiombe bi’abateri abarenge gotera amatera ay’okoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono bigatenena ime ase enyomba ya Nyasae, na inche amo nekeng’ese ki’abanene baria togatenena nabarabwo.
english: The two choirs that gave thanks then took their places in the house of God; so did I, together with half the officials,

ekegusii: Abaruoti abwo babere mbabe bakoroberia ng’a bakore amabe, baikaranse ase emesa eyemo babe bagotebania oborimo, korende ayio tagosesenigwa, na omoerio nigo oraike ase engaki eria echikire.
english: The two kings, with their hearts bent on evil, will sit at the same table and lie to each other, but to no avail, because an end will still come at the appointed time.

ekegusii: abanto abwo babere barenge kwomana goika bachiche ase obosio bw’Omonene, ase abakuani na abagambi abwo batenenerete ase amatuko ayio.
english: the two men involved in the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD before the priests and the judges who are in office at the time.

ekegusii: Erio abasacha baria babere bakaboria Loti, “Nore nonde omino aa? Nobwate abana bao banyuomete abaiseke bao, gose abamura na abaiseke bao, gose kobwate bande bamino ase omochie oyo, barusie korwa aase aa.
english: The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here-- sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,

ekegusii: Erio abwo babere bagakora okobwatana kw’ogotianania ase obosio bw’Omonene. Daudi agatigara omenyete agwo Horesi, na Yonathani akairana gochia nka.
english: The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. Then Jonathan went home, but David remained at Horesh.

ekegusii: Abwo babere bagatomwa n’Omoika Omochenu, bagatirimboka gochia Selukia, na korwa agwo bakaamboka nemeeri gochia Kuporo.
english: The two of them, sent on their way by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.

ekegusii: Akaroisia chisiiro ibere, na ebisure bibere biabegetwe igoro ye chisiiro, na ebichanga bisisire biaetanaine, bigatuba chinsemo chi’ebisure echiatambeete gochia isiko,
english: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of network decorating the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;

ekegusii: chisiiro ibere, na ebisure bibere biabegetwe igoro ye chisiiro chiria, na ebichanga bisisire biaetanaine bigatuba ebisure biatambeete gochia isiko, biria biabegetwe igoro ye chisiiro.
english: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of network decorating the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;

ekegusii: “Emingichi eria kwaroche yabwate chingunchara ibere, abwo nabaruoti b’Abamedi na Abaayemi,
english: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.

ekegusii: Ekero amang’ana ao amaanoirwe nigo akorua omobaso na koa oyotamanyeti amange obong’aini.
english: The unfolding of your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.

ekegusii: Egetumo ki’egesasimero nigo kiarenge egi’ekerengo ki’amaboko ikomi na ane, obotambe na obogare nigo biareng’aine. Orosingo rwaetanaine omogo oye nigo rwarenge nobogare bw’ekerengo gi’ekerengo gi’ekeng’ese gi’okoboko okomo. Enterekerero y’egesasimero nigo yarenge ey’ekerengo gi’okoboko okomo ase chinsemo chionsi na ekeriinero kiaye nigo kiarenge ensemo ya moocha.”
english: The upper ledge also is square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, with a rim of half a cubit and a gutter of a cubit all around. The steps of the altar face east."

ekegusii: Abanyaboronge nigo bakorora amang’ana ayio na bagoka mono; korende abakori amabe nigo bagokira‐kiri baumata.
english: The upright see and rejoice, but all the wicked shut their mouths.

ekegusii: Hanuni amo nabanto bamenyete Sanoa bakaroisia Egeita kie Rikura, bagakebekera ebisieri, na ebisiekero, na emekorogoto. Boigo bakaagacha orwaki ase obotambe bw’amaboko elifu eyemo, goika ase Egeita ki’Eubi.
english: The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it and put its doors and bolts and bars in place. They also repaired five hundred yards of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.

ekegusii: Erio ebiambokero bi’enyancha bikarorekana, na oboroso bw’ense bokaorokigwa aarabu, ekero Omonene abatogonyerete ase okwoga kw’omoika bwe chimioro chiaye.”
english: The valleys of the sea were exposed and the foundations of the earth laid bare at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of breath from his nostrils.

ekegusii: Erio ebiambokero bi’enyancha bikarorekana, na amaroso ’ense akaorokigwa aarabu, ekero Omonene abatogonyerete ase ogwoka kw’omoika bwe chimioro chiaye.
english: The valleys of the sea were exposed and the foundations of the earth laid bare at your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of breath from your nostrils.

ekegusii: Amang’ana aya ng’a ngosoerana more inwe ase inwe nigo are ase okobugwa kwaino. Inki motanchereti gokorerwa bobe? Inki motanchereti kourwa ebi mobwate?
english: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means you have been completely defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?

ekegusii: Amatambokero aye are ne chinguru nakeeigwe, na emeroberio yaye emoiyerie inse.
english: The vigor of his step is weakened; his own schemes throw him down.

ekegusii: Emesabibu yomire, na emeko boigo. Emekomomanga, na emekendo, na emete y’amapera, ee, emete ende yonsi y’emegondo yomire. Omogoko bw’abanto oerire.
english: The vine is dried up and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, the palm and the apple tree-- all the trees of the field-- are dried up. Surely the joy of mankind is withered away.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli nabwo omogondo bw’emesabibu bw’Omonene bw’Emeganda, na Abayuda nabwo ekemeri kiaye asimegete na gokegokera. Ekero asemeretie arore ogokora kw’oboronge, akarora abande bagokorerwa bobe, na ekero asemeretie arore oboronge, akaigwa ebirero.
english: The vineyard of the LORD Almighty is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the garden of his delight. And he looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard cries of distress.

ekegusii: The violence of the wicked will drag them away, for they refuse to do what is right.
english: Obourereria bw’abakori amabe mbobasirie barueo, ekiagera bangire gokora ayare ay’oboronge.

ekegusii: Obobe bwakoretwe ase Lebanoni mbogotube, na ogosirigwa gwe ching’iti koria gwachiondogetie; aye noegwe egesusuro, ekiagera gwaiterete amanyinga ’abanto, na ogakora amabe ase ense, na ase emechie, na ase abanto bamenyeteo.
english: The violence you have done to Lebanon will overwhelm you, and your destruction of animals will terrify you. For you have shed man's blood; you have destroyed lands and cities and everyone in them.

ekegusii: Aya namaroro Isaya, mosinto bw’Amosi, aroche igoro y’ense y’Abayuda na omochie o Yerusalemu ekero Usia, na Yotamu, na Ahasi, na Hezekia, barenge abaruoti ase ense y’Abayuda.
english: The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

ekegusii: Obonene obwo naroche ase okorora nigo bwarenge buna boria naroche ekero nachete gosaria omochie o Yerusalemu, na buna okorora koria konya narorire agwo ase orooche rwa Kebari. Erio ngatung’ama inse nkaumama.
english: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the Kebar River, and I fell facedown.

ekegusii: Oko nokorora kw’Obadia. Aya naro Omonene Nyasae agoteba igoro y’egesaku kia Edomu, ee, twaigure amang’ana korwa ase Omonene, na omotomwa otomirwe gochia ase abanto b’ebisaku, ogoteba: “Imoka, togende korwania Abaedomu esegi!”
english: The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Sovereign LORD says about Edom-- We have heard a message from the LORD: An envoy was sent to the nations to say, "Rise, and let us go against her for battle"--

ekegusii: Ababani bao nigo bakobarorera amaroro ’obong’ainereria are bosa, tibakoorokeretie obobe bwao, erinde nario orairanerigwe amaya ao; korende aya amaroro abo ayakworogetie, nigo arenge ay’oborimo, agerete ogatantanigwa.
english: The visions of your prophets were false and worthless; they did not expose your sin to ward off your captivity. The oracles they gave you were false and misleading.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’Omonene nigo rikobuna emete emecharake, ee, nigo rikobuna emecharake ya Lebanoni.
english: The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; the LORD breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’Omonene nigo rikoigweka ase chinyancha igoro; Nyasae bw’obonene nigo agoaka enkoba, Omonene nigo akogukura igoro ye chinyancha chinyinge.
english: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD thunders over the mighty waters.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’Omonene nigo rikoigweka rire nokobua; eriogi ri’Omonene nigo riichire nobonene.
english: The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is majestic.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’Omonene nigo rigotengechia erooro; ee, nigo rigotengechia erooro ya Kadeshi.
english: The voice of the LORD shakes the desert; the LORD shakes the Desert of Kadesh.

ekegusii: Eriogi ri’Omonene nigo rikomesia chinsase chi’omorero.
english: The voice of the LORD strikes with flashes of lightning.

ekegusii: Eriogi erio ri’Omonene nigo rikorekeria chingabi, nigo rigosabora emete y’amanani yaba bosa. Ase Hekalu yaye ebitongwa bionsi biatogia obonene bwaye.
english: The voice of the LORD twists the oaks and strips the forests bare. And in his temple all cry, "Glory!"

ekegusii: Ase eriogi ri’Omonene, na ase ogoaka nenyimbo yaye, Abaasuri mbaondoke mono.
english: The voice of the LORD will shatter Assyria; with his scepter he will strike them down.

ekegusii: Tegerera! Abwo bagoaka amariogi ase bagosangererekana kobuucha amache, nigo bagokwana igoro y’obobui bw’Omonene, ee, igoro y’ogokora kwaye okoronge gokogambera Abaisraeli. Erio abanto b’Omonene bagatirimboka gochia ase ebiita.
english: the voice of the singers at the watering places. They recite the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his warriors in Israel. "Then the people of the LORD went down to the city gates.

ekegusii: Eriogi rikamochera eria kabere, rikamotebia, “Eki Nyasae achenire tokeroka ng’a tikeri egechenu.”
english: The voice spoke to him a second time, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean."

ekegusii: Amariogi ’abagambi nigo arenge gokea, chimeme chiabo chiabwatana namang’ang’ura abo.
english: the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

ekegusii: Ogokora kw’omonyene oboronge nigo gokomoraa gochia ase obogima, korende okonyora kw’omokori amabe nigo gokomoraa gochia ase ebibe.
english: The wages of the righteous bring them life, but the income of the wicked brings them punishment.

ekegusii: Na orwaki rw’omochie oria nigo rwarenge namaroso ikomi na abere, na igoro yabo amarieta ikomi na abere ay’abatomwa ikomi na babere b’Emanwa y’Eng’ondi.
english: The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

ekegusii: Na orwaki rwaye nigo rwaagachire namagena a yasipi, na omochie omonyene nigo orenge bw’etahabu engiya, endabu buna ekerore ekerabu.
english: The wall was made of jasper, and the city of pure gold, as pure as glass.

ekegusii: Esegi ase egati y’eamate ya Saulo na eya Daudi ekaba ekogenderera ase engaki entambe. Daudi akagenderera komenteka chinguru chiaye, korende abanto b’eamate ya Saulo bakagenderera koba aboro goetania.
english: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David lasted a long time. David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

ekegusii: Na omonene oria bw’echela tachia goitaa kende gionsi kiare ase amaboko a Yusufu, ekiagera Omonene nigo arenge amo nere, na ande onsi are gokora, Omonene nigo are koyasesenia.
english: The warden paid no attention to anything under Joseph's care, because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.

ekegusii: Omorendi akarangeria gochia inse, agatebia omoruoti amang’ana ayio. Na omoruoti akamotebia, “Onye ore bweka nigo abwate amang’ana amaya.” Omonto oria akaba ogoika ang’e kobua.
english: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, "If he is alone, he must have good news." And the man came closer and closer.

ekegusii: Omorendi bw’egesieri nigo akomoigorera, ne ching’ondi nigo chikoigwa eriogi riaye; ere nigo akorangeria ching’ondi chiaye ase amarieta abo na gochiira isiko.
english: The watchman opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.

ekegusii: Omorendi nigo akoiraneria: “Emambia yachire, nonya naboigo obotuko nao bore. Onye moganetie koboria erinde momanye, boria; moirane moche naende.”
english: The watchman replies, "Morning is coming, but also the night. If you would ask, then ask; and come back yet again."

ekegusii: Omorendi agateba, “Nigo ndoche ng’a omominyoki oria bwe ritang’ani nigo anga buna Ahimasi, mosinto o Zadoki.” Erio omoruoti agateba, “Ere nomonto omuya, nigo akorenta amang’ana amaya.”
english: The watchman said, "It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He's a good man," the king said. "He comes with good news."

ekegusii: Ekero abarendi barenge goetanana omochie koyorata, bakanyora inche, na inche nkababoria, “Mwarora omwanchi bw’omoyo one?”
english: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. "Have you seen the one my heart loves?"

ekegusii: Ekero abarendi barenge goetanana omochie koyorata, bakanyora inche, bakang’aka chingoma; bakang’ura egetambaa gi’okwambara, abarendi baria barendete chindwaki.
english: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They beat me, they bruised me; they took away my cloak, those watchmen of the walls!

ekegusii: Amache akairanerana, akamera chigari, na abariini chibarasi amo nomoganda bwonsi bw’abarwani ba Farao, abatunyanete Abaisraeli, gochia ase enyancha. Monto onde tatigara nonya noyomo.
english: The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen-- the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.

ekegusii: erio amache ayare gotirimboka korwa rogoro agatenena buna orwaki aare mono, agwo Adamu, omochie orenge ang’e na Saretani. Amache arenge gotirimboka gochia Enyancha y’Ekerubo Ekiomo, nero Enyancha y’Omonyo, akanacheka pi. Erio abanto bakaamboka kororia omochie o Yeriko.
english: the water from upstream stopped flowing. It piled up in a heap a great distance away, at a town called Adam in the vicinity of Zarethan, while the water flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea) was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

ekegusii: The water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.
english: Amache akaminyoka agaetanana egesasimero gionsi, na omotaro bwonsi ogaichora amache.

ekegusii: na amache akagenderera gokea korwa ase ense, na ekero amatuko rigana erimo, na emerongo etano (150) aerete, amache agachaka gokeana.
english: The water receded steadily from the earth. At the end of the hundred and fifty days the water had gone down,

ekegusii: Amache agaichora agaeta ase omotwe one igoro, ngateba: Omoerio one oikire.
english: the waters closed over my head, and I thought I was about to be cut off.

ekegusii: Na amache akagenderera gokea goika omotienyi o ikomi. Ase rituko rie ritang’ani ri’omotienyi o ikomi ebichuria bi’ebitunwa bikarorekana.
english: The waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.

ekegusii: Amache akamera kegima abachandi baria babo; onde tatigarete ore moyo nonya noyomo.
english: The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them survived.

ekegusii: Amache akagenderera goichora igoro ase ense ase engaki y’amatuko rigana erimo, na emerongo etano (150).
english: The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

ekegusii: Omote oyio okaba okonyora amache na gokina; chinsoko chia inse chikayotambeyia. Chindooche nigo chiaetanaine ase osimekire, nyuma yaye chindooche echio chikaba chikonyosia emete yonsi ye rinani amache.
english: The waters nourished it, deep springs made it grow tall; their streams flowed all around its base and sent their channels to all the trees of the field.

ekegusii: The waters of Nimrim are dried up and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone and nothing green is left.
english: Orooche rwa Nimurimu rwakamire amache; obonyansi bwomire, na bonde tibori komera, ekemeri kende ekebese tikeri aroro.

ekegusii: Amache ’orooche rwa Naili nakame pi, na orooche orwo ndokame kegima.
english: The waters of the river will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and dry.

ekegusii: Amache akamenteka goichora, agatiira goika ebirengo bi’amaboko ikomi na atano igoro y’ebitunwa bionsi.
english: The waters rose and covered the mountains to a depth of more than twenty feet.

ekegusii: Amache agaichora, akamenteka mono igoro y’ense, na obwato boria bogacheng’enena ase amache igoro.
english: The waters rose and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water.

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, ekero amache akoroche, ee, ekero akoroche, nigo akwoboete, ne chindiba chikanyegerigwa.
english: The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you and writhed; the very depths were convulsed.

ekegusii: Enchera y’omonto omoriri nigo ekororekana ase amaiso aye ng’a nendonge, korende omonto omong’aini nigo akoigwera ogosemigwa.
english: The way of a fool seems right to him, but a wise man listens to advice.

ekegusii: enchera y’ensoti igoro, na ey’eng’iti igoro ase egetare, na ey’emeeri igoro ase amache ’enyancha, na enchera y’omosacha gochia ase omoiseke.
english: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a maiden.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo tibamanyeti enchera y’omorembe, na oboronge tibori ase bagoeta; nigo bagoeta ase chinchera chinkorekanu, na onde bwensi ogoeterao takomanya amang’ana ’omorembe.
english: The way of peace they do not know; there is no justice in their paths. They have turned them into crooked roads; no one who walks in them will know peace.

ekegusii: Enchera y’omomochi nigo ere enkorekanu, korende ogokora kw’oyore nenkoro endonge nigo kore okoronge.
english: The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

ekegusii: Enchera y’Omonene nigo ere egekengero egekong’u ase abanyene oboronge, korende nigo erasirie abagokora ebibe.
english: The way of the LORD is a refuge for the righteous, but it is the ruin of those who do evil.

ekegusii: Enchera y’omonto omworo nigo enga buna orobago rw’amagwa, korende ey’abanyene oboronge nigo ere enene erongeete.
english: The way of the sluggard is blocked with thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.

ekegusii: Obotenenku bw’omonto omonda nigo bore asare buna omochie ogiteire chindwaki, korende obotaka nabwo ogosirigwa kw’abataka.
english: The wealth of the rich is their fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.

ekegusii: Omonto omonda nigo akorengereria ng’a obotenenku bwaye nigo bonga buna omochie omokong’u, naende buna orwaki orotambe gochia igoro rokomorenda.
english: The wealth of the rich is their fortified city; they imagine it an unscalable wall.

ekegusii: Obonda nigo bore egutwa y’abanto abang’aini, korende oboriri bw’abanto abariri nigo bore oboriri bwoka.
english: The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the folly of fools yields folly.

ekegusii: Naki ebirwanero biaito bi’esegi tibiri ebia mwanyabanto, korende mbire nokobua kwa Nyasae koiyeria chindwaki.
english: The weapons we fight with are not the weapons of the world. On the contrary, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.

ekegusii: na oborito bwe chitahabu chia kera emesa y’emegati ekoruegwa ase Nyasae, na obwe chifeta chikoroiserigwa chimesa chie chifeta.
english: the weight of gold for each table for consecrated bread; the weight of silver for the silver tables;

ekegusii: na oborito bwe chitahabu chi’ebibekerero bie chitaya na echie chitaya chiria, na obwa kera ekebekerero gie chitaya ao ao, na oborito bwe chifeta chia kera ekebekerero gie chitaya, ne chitaya chiria, koreng’ana nemeremo ya kera ekebekerero,
english: the weight of gold for the gold lampstands and their lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of silver for each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;

ekegusii: Akamotebereria igoro ye chigami, ne chisani, na ebitaabo biroisigwe korwa ase chitahabu chichenire na igoro ye chibakuri chie chitahabu, na echie chifeta, na oborito bwa kera eyemo;
english: the weight of pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls and pitchers; the weight of gold for each gold dish; the weight of silver for each silver dish;

ekegusii: Oborito bw’e bigera biria asabete aegwe nigo bwarenge koreng’ana chikiro emerongo ebere. Amo nebio akaira chisonoi, na ebigera, ne chianga chimonyinga, ebinto abaruoti b’Abamidiani barenge kobeka, amo ne chisonoi chiria chiarenge ase amagoti e chingamia chiabo.
english: The weight of the gold rings he asked for came to seventeen hundred shekels, not counting the ornaments, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian or the chains that were on their camels' necks.

ekegusii: Etahabu yare korentwa ase Sulemani kera omwaka nigo yarenge goetania chikiro chilifu emerongo ebere na isato (23,000).
english: The weight of the gold that Solomon received yearly was 666 talents,

ekegusii: Chitahabu chiare korentwa ase Sulemani kera omwaka nigo chiarenge goetania chikiro chilifu emerongo ebere na isano (25,000).
english: The weight of the gold that Solomon received yearly was 666 talents,

ekegusii: Ase ensemo ya bosongo bakaroisia ebitambaa bire nobotambe bw’ekerengo ki’amaboko emerongo etano, ne chisiiro ikomi amo ne chinterekerero chiabo ikomi, korende ebigobanio ne chinuga chiabo nigo chiarenge chie chifeta.
english: The west end was fifty cubits wide and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

ekegusii: eyarenge orobebe rwa bosongo. Abanto be chiamate chia Yuda nabwo bamenyete ase orogongo orwo.
english: The western boundary is the coastline of the Great Sea. These are the boundaries around the people of Judah by their clans.

ekegusii: Korende chingano tichiasaretigwe, ekiagera konya tichirakina.
english: The wheat and spelt, however, were not destroyed, because they ripen later.)

ekegusii: Amagoro ayio nigo aroisetigwe buna aye chigari. Amagoro amagima nigo aroisetigwe korwa ase etaai yanyititoire na kobombwa. Boigo amanyongo, ne chingata, na ebitingiro biaroisetigwe.
english: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; the axles, rims, spokes and hubs were all of cast metal.

ekegusii: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
english: etibibi, na etekere, na ensoti;

ekegusii: Erio abanto bonsi bakairana buya ase Yoshua agwo Makeda ase batoorete. Onde tarenge noboremu gokwana mamincha y’Abaisraeli naende.
english: The whole army then returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah, and no one uttered a word against the Israelites.

ekegusii: Omosangererekano oria bwonsi bw’abanto ogancha gokora amang’ana ayio, ekiagera nigo abete amaronge ase abanto bonsi.
english: The whole assembly agreed to do this, because it seemed right to all the people.

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi ogakira, ogategerera Barnaba na Paulo, ekero baare koraria amang’ana igoro y’ebikone na amakumia Nyasae akorete goetera asebare ase egati y’abanto b’Ebisaku.
english: The whole assembly became silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul telling about the miraculous signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

ekegusii: Erio omosangererekano bwonsi ogasasima, na abateri bagatera, na ababugia ebirombeta bakabibugia ase amariogi amanene; bakagenderera goika okoruegwa gw’ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa kogakoorwa.
english: The whole assembly bowed in worship, while the singers sang and the trumpeters played. All this continued until the sacrifice of the burnt offering was completed.

ekegusii: Omosangererekano bwonsi ogakora okobwatana kw’ogotianania nomoruoti agwo ase enyomba ya Nyasae. Erio Yehoyada akabatebia, “Rora omwana bw’omoruoti! Tiga agambe, buna Omonene akwanete igoro y’ororeria rwa Daudi.
english: the whole assembly made a covenant with the king at the temple of God. Jehoiada said to them, "The king's son shall reign, as the LORD promised concerning the descendants of David.

ekegusii: the whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
english: Ekero Abaisraeli baigwete amang’ana ayio, omoganda obo bwonsi ogasangererekana agwo Silo, erinde ogende kobarwania esegi.

ekegusii: Ekero Abaisraeli babuete ense eria, omoganda obo bwonsi ogasangererekana agwo Silo, na agwo bagatenenia Eema y’Omosangererekano.
english: The whole assembly of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The country was brought under their control,

ekegusii: Erio omosangererekano bwonsi okairaneria ase eriogi rinene, ogateba, “Amang’ana ayio nabo are, goika tokore buna gwatebire.
english: The whole assembly responded with a loud voice: "You are right! We must do as you say.

ekegusii: Omosangererekano bwonsi ogancherana korenda Amatuko Amanene ase amatuko ande atano na abere; ase ayio bakayarenda ase amatuko ande atano na abere, bare nomogoko.
english: The whole assembly then agreed to celebrate the festival seven more days; so for another seven days they celebrated joyfully.

ekegusii: Abarwani esegi bonsi b’Abakalidayo, na baria barenge amo nomoteneneri oria bw’abarendi, bagatagora chindwaki chionsi chiaetanaine Yerusalemu.
english: The whole Babylonian army under the commander of the imperial guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Abarwani esegi bonsi b’Abakalidayo, baria barenge amo nomoteneneri oria bw’abarendi, bagatagora chindwaki chiaetanaine Yerusalemu.
english: The whole Babylonian army, under the commander of the imperial guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Omochie bwonsi ogatitira, na abanto bakaminyoka gocha amo, bakabwata Paulo, bakamokurura, bakamosokia korwa ase Hekalu. Erio ebisieri bigasiekwa.
english: The whole city was aroused, and the people came running from all directions. Seizing Paul, they dragged him from the temple, and immediately the gates were shut.

ekegusii: The whole community of Israel must celebrate it.
english: Omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli goika bakore omoyega oyio.

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi bw’abanto oiranete nigo orenge chilifu emerongo ene na ibere, na amagana atato, na emerongo etano nomo (42,360),
english: The whole company numbered 42,360,

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi bw’abanto nigo orenge chilifu emerongo ene na ibere, na amagana atato, na emerongo etano nomo (42,360),
english: The whole company numbered 42,360,

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi bw’abanto bairanete korwa ase obosomba bakaagacha ebigutu bamenye imeo, ekiagera korwa ase engaki ya Yoshua, mosinto o Nuni, goika ase engaki eyio, Abaisraeli konya tibana gokora bo. Na bono bakaba nomogoko omonene.
english: The whole company that had returned from exile built booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated it like this. And their joy was very great.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ense eria bakarera namariogi amanene ekero abanto bonsi baare goeta, na omoruoti akaamboka akarooche ga Kidironi; abanto bonsi bakaamboka bakagenda ase enchera y’erooro.
english: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the desert.

ekegusii: Enyomba yonsi y’Ahabu goika esire erue aroro; inche ninsirie kera omonto omosacha korwa ase enyomba y’Ahabu, abasibire na abatasibiri ase Abaisraeli.
english: The whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every last male in Israel-- slave or free.

ekegusii: Naboigo omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli amo nomomenyi omenyete ase egati yabo, bonsi nabaaberwe, ekiagera abwo bonsi nigo babareretwe okomocha koria gwakoretwe mosiabano ase ogotancha.
english: The whole Israelite community and the aliens living among them will be forgiven, because all the people were involved in the unintentional wrong.

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli bakamanora na koimoka korwa Elimu, na ase rituko ria ikomi na gatano ri’omotienyi o kabere nyuma kobarure ense ya Misiri, bagaika ase erooro ya Sini, eyio ere egati y’Elimu na Sinai.
english: The whole Israelite community set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of Egypt.

ekegusii: The whole Israelite community set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
english: Omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli okarua Kadeshi, okagenda ogaika egetunwa kia Hori.

ekegusii: Omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli okaimoka korwa erooro ya Sini. Barabwo bakabwatia orogendo rwabo, bakana‐gotoora buna Omonene abachigete, Bagaika Refidimu, bagatoora aroro, korende mache tarengeo abanto baare konyara konywa.
english: The whole Israelite community set out from the Desert of Sin, traveling from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.

ekegusii: Abanto b’ense yonsi ya Boyahudi, na bonsi aba Yerusalemu bakamochiera, bakabatiswa nere ase orooche rwa Yorodan, bakoorokia ebibe biabo.
english: The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

ekegusii: Inche ninkoe aye, na ororeria rwao rorache korwa nyuma yao, ense eye omenyete bono buna omomenyi, ense yonsi ya Kanani, ebe eyaino kare na kare, na inche nimbe Nyasae obo.”
english: The whole land of Canaan, where you are now an alien, I will give as an everlasting possession to you and your descendants after you; and I will be their God."

ekegusii: Ense yonsi inayome pa ebe buna amagena ’omorero akonyititoka, na omonyo, ebe bosa etari kwama, nonya nobonyansi tibokomerao, esirigwe buna emechie ya Sodomu, na Gomora, na Adima, na Seboimu, eria Omonene asiretie ekero abete nendamwamu na okogechigwa.
english: The whole land will be a burning waste of salt and sulfur-- nothing planted, nothing sprouting, no vegetation growing on it. It will be like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in fierce anger.

ekegusii: Ekero ekio ense eye yonsi neonchorwe ebe ense omweya korwa Geba goika Rimoni, irianyi ya Yerusalemu. Korende Yerusalemu oro nogenderere kobeera igoro agwo aase aye, korwa ase Egeita kia Benjamin goika ase Egeita kie Ritang’ani, na goika ase Egeita gi’Ekoona, na korwa ase Omorobiri bwa Hananeli goika ase ebimitero bi’edivai bi’omoruoti.
english: The whole land, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, will become like the Arabah. But Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the royal winepresses.

ekegusii: The whole town gathered at the door,
english: Na omochie bwonsi okaba ngosangererekana ore gesieri.

ekegusii: Rikura rionsi rire nemebere ekwete, ne ribu, amo nemegondo yonsi ere agwo goikera akarooche ga Kidironi, na goika ekoona ekorokwa Egeita gie Chibarasi, gochia ase ensemo ya moocha; chinsemo echio nchibe chinchenu asende inche Omonene. Tichikoonchoranwa gose gosarigwa nonya ng’ake.”
english: The whole valley where dead bodies and ashes are thrown, and all the terraces out to the Kidron Valley on the east as far as the corner of the Horse Gate, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or demolished."

ekegusii: Abanto korwa ase chinse chionsi bagacha ase Sulemani, erinde baigwe obong’aini boria Nyasae abegete ime yaye.
english: The whole world sought audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.

ekegusii: Oborabu nigo bogotangwa korwa ase abakori amabe, ne chinguru chiabo chi’okweenenia nigo chikobunwa chiasirigwa.
english: The wicked are denied their light, and their upraised arm is broken.

ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bakomboera ng’a bansirie, korende nigo inyigwerete oborori bwao.
english: The wicked are waiting to destroy me, but I will ponder your statutes.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo agosoa ase emechando y’omonyene oboronge, oba embooria yaye, na oyo otari omwegenwa oba embooria y’oyore nenkoro endonge.
english: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the unfaithful for the upright.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo akoira egento singo tagokeirania, korende omonto omoronge nigo are namabera na korua ebiegwa,
english: The wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous give generously;

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo akogania ebionga bi’abanto ababe, korende omori bw’omonyene oboronge nigo ogoseboka bwama.
english: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.

ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bagosomora emeyio yabo na batinga amata abo, erinde baite abanto abataka na abaremeire, baite na abakobwatia chinchera chi’oboronge.
english: The wicked draw the sword and bend the bow to bring down the poor and needy, to slay those whose ways are upright.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bakobabwata nebigobanio biabo babakurura nekeonga kiabo na kobasangereria ase ekeonga kiabo bakorubera; erio bagoka na gochenga.
english: The wicked foe pulls all of them up with hooks, he catches them in his net, he gathers them up in his dragnet; and so he rejoices and is glad.

ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bagoetanana chinsemo chionsi, na obonyaka bonde bwonsi bogotogigwa ase egati ya mwanyabanto.
english: The wicked freely strut about when what is vile is honored among men.

ekegusii: Abakori amabe babekire omoeto ase ngoeta, korende tintantaniri korwa ase amachiko ao.
english: The wicked have set a snare for me, but I have not strayed from your precepts.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo agotengera omonto omoronge, erio origia chinchera chi’okomoita.
english: The wicked lie in wait for the righteous, seeking their very lives;

ekegusii: Omoyo bw’omokori amabe nigo okogania gokora ebibe, na omonto oyio tari kororera omonto onde amabera.
english: The wicked man craves evil; his neighbor gets no mercy from him.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo akwenyorera eng’eria y’obong’ainereria, korende oyo ogosimeka oboronge nigo akwenyorera eng’eria y’ekeene.
english: The wicked man earns deceptive wages, but he who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.

ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bagotama nonya onde tari kobabwatia, korende abanyaboronge nigo bare abaremu buna chindo chinsae.
english: The wicked man flees though no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

ekegusii: Ekero omonto omonyabibe akorora ayio, nigo agoichana ogechigwa, oriania amaino aye, orea osira. Okogania kw’omonyabibe nigo kogosira.
english: The wicked man will see and be vexed, he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the longings of the wicked will come to nothing.

ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo agokora omoroberio bw’ogoita oyore omoronge, na komoriananeria amaino.
english: The wicked plot against the righteous and gnash their teeth at them;

ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bakogenda gochia aase abakure, naboigo nabanto bonsi b’ebisaku abwo bebire Nyasae.
english: The wicked return to the grave, all the nations that forget God.

ekegusii: Oyore omoboraka bori, na otigire bweka, oyo nigo amosemeretie Nyasae, na kogenderera ase okoboria na ogosaba obotuko na omobaso.
english: The widow who is really in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day to pray and to ask God for help.

ekegusii: Obogare bwa bosio bwe Hekalu ensemo ya moocha, amo neraaro nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko rigana erimo.
english: The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits.

ekegusii: Omoboraka bw’omworokigwa oyomo bw’ababani akarera ase Elisha, akabora, “Omosacha one, omosomba oo, nakwete; aye nomanyete ng’a omosomba oo nigo amoirogete Omonene. Bono omoriegwa esira oye ochire koira abana abamura baane babere abakore babe abasomba baye.”
english: The wife of a man from the company of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that he revered the LORD. But now his creditor is coming to take my two boys as his slaves."

ekegusii: Omokungu tari nokobua igoro ase omobere oye, korende nomosacha oye; naboigo nomosacha tari nokobua igoro ase omobere oye, korende nomokungu oye.
english: The wife's body does not belong to her alone but also to her husband. In the same way, the husband's body does not belong to him alone but also to his wife.

ekegusii: erinde ching’iti chi’orosana amo nebibwe ne chisagero chinywe chintogie. Ekero ekio nintubokie amache ase erooro, ne chindooche ase ense enyomo, ng’ee abanto baane, abwo nachorire, amache banywe,
english: The wild animals honor me, the jackals and the owls, because I provide water in the desert and streams in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen,

ekegusii: ekero omwaga ogocha, okerusiao giasira pi, aase aye tari komanya ng’a nkiarengeo.
english: the wind blows over it and it is gone, and its place remembers it no more.

ekegusii: Embeo nigo ekogusa gochia irianyi, naende yaonchoka yagusa gochia sugusu; nigo ekona‐goetanana yagenderera kogusa, naende yagenderera goetanana naende naende.
english: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.

ekegusii: Embeo nigo ekogusa aase erigetie, na egeturi kiaye nigo ogokeigwa, korende tomanyeti aase ekorwa gose aase ekogenda; naboigo na kera omonto oiboirwe ase Omoika.”
english: The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit."

ekegusii: Omwaga noirurukie abarisia bao bonsi, na abanchwa bao nabooswe, bairwe ase obosomba, erio aye norore obosooku na gotang’ang’a ase engencho y’ebibe biao bionsi.
english: The wind will drive all your shepherds away, and your allies will go into exile. Then you will be ashamed and disgraced because of all your wickedness.

ekegusii: Chimbaba chi’abakerubi baria nigo chiaramboire chikaba nobotambe bw’amaboko emerongo ebere. Abakerubi abwo nigo bateneine namagoro abo, barigereretie gochia Aase Aachenu.
english: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.

ekegusii: Obong’aini bw’omonto ore nokomanya nigo bokomokonya omanya buna chinchera chiaye chire, korende oboriri bw’abanto abariri nigo bokobang’aina.
english: The wisdom of the prudent is to give thought to their ways, but the folly of fools is deception.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omong’aini ase enkoro yaye nigo anchete amachiko, korende oyogokwana amang’ana atagwenereti nigo arasirigwe,
english: The wise in heart accept commands, but a chattering fool comes to ruin.

ekegusii: Omonto ore omong’aini ase enkoro yaye narokwe omomanyi, ne chinkwana chingiya nigo chikomenta chisemi.
english: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant words promote instruction.

ekegusii: Abanto abang’aini mbanyore omwando bw’obonene, korende abariri mbabogorie obosooku.
english: The wise inherit honor, but fools he holds up to shame.

ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo abwate amaiso ase omotwe oye, korende omonto omoriri nigo agotaara ase omosunte; nonya nabeigo, nkarora ng’a bonsi nigo bakonyorwa negento ekemo.
english: The wise man has eyes in his head, while the fool walks in the darkness; but I came to realize that the same fate overtakes them both.

ekegusii: Bono abanto abang’aini na abarogi mbarentwa ase obosio bwane basome amariko aya, naende bantebie engencho yaye, korende tibanyarete gontebia engencho y’amang’ana aya.
english: The wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and tell me what it means, but they could not explain it.

ekegusii: Abanto abang’aini mbasookigwe mbaichanigwe na gotang’ang’a, ekiagera bangire ring’ana ri’Omonene. Mbong’aini ki bore asebare?
english: The wise will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and trapped. Since they have rejected the word of the LORD, what kind of wisdom do they have?

ekegusii: Omokungu omong’aini nigo akoagacha mwaye, korende oyore omoriri nigo agotagora mwaye na maboko aye.
english: The wise woman builds her house, but with her own hands the foolish one tears hers down.

ekegusii: korende baria abang’aini bakaimokia amaguta ase ebinto biabo amo ne chitaya chiabo.
english: The wise, however, took oil in jars along with their lamps.

ekegusii: Abaiseke abang’aini abarenge amo nere bakamoiraneria, na ere omonyene akaba okoiranerera amang’ana aya:”
english: The wisest of her ladies answer her; indeed, she keeps saying to herself,

ekegusii: Esese y’orosana na emanwa y’eng’ondi nchibe chikoriseria amo, endo nebe ekorisia obonyansi buna eng’ombe, na orotu ndobe endagera y’eng’iti engenda inse. Ogokora bobe na ogosiria konde gwonsi tikogokorwa ase egetunwa kiane egechenu. Nabo Omonene atebire.”
english: The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, but dust will be the serpent's food. They will neither harm nor destroy on all my holy mountain," says the LORD.

ekegusii: Esese y’orosana nemenye amo nemanwa y’eng’ondi, na engo nerare amo nemanwa y’embori; emori, na endo, na eng’ombe enoru nachibe chikogosoria amo, na omwana omoke nabe ogochiraa.
english: The wolf will live with the lamb, the leopard will lie down with the goat, the calf and the lion and the yearling together; and a little child will lead them.

ekegusii: Korende omokungu oria akamochiera akamosasima, akabora, “Omonene, nkonya.”
english: The woman came and knelt before him. "Lord, help me!" she said.

ekegusii: Omokungu oria akaba morito; agatoma amang’ana ase Daudi, akabora, “Nabeire morito.”
english: The woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, "I am pregnant."

ekegusii: Omokungu oria agatama gochia ase erooro agwo aase aroiseretigwe na Nyasae, erinde arendwe aroro ase engaki y’amatuko elifu eyemo, na amagana abere, na emerongo etano nomo (1,260).
english: The woman fled into the desert to a place prepared for her by God, where she might be taken care of for 1,260 days.

ekegusii: Omokungu omoriri nigo are omonyariogi. Ere nigo are bosa, na tamanyeti ring’ana rinde.
english: The woman Folly is loud; she is undisciplined and without knowledge.

ekegusii: Nyuma y’ayio omokungu oria akaibora omwana omoisia, akamoroka Samison. Omwana oyio agakina, na Omonene akamosesenia.
english: The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. He grew and the LORD blessed him,

ekegusii: Omokungu oria nabwate emori enoru nka bwoye, akayenyenya bwango. Boigo akaimokia obosie, akabokonya, agakora emegati etabekiri memera, akayegekera.
english: The woman had a fattened calf at the house, which she butchered at once. She took some flour, kneaded it and baked bread without yeast.

ekegusii: Ase igo omokungu oria akaminyoka bwango akarangeria omosacha oye, akamotebia, “Rora, omonto oria ochicha asende rituko riria ong’orokeire naende.”
english: The woman hurried to tell her husband, "He's here! The man who appeared to me the other day!"

ekegusii: Ase igo omokungu oria akaimoka na agakora buna omonto oria o Nyasae amotebetie; akagenda amo nabanto b’enyomba yaye, akamenya ase ense y’Abafilisti ase engaki y’emiaka etano na ebere.
english: The woman proceeded to do as the man of God said. She and her family went away and stayed in the land of the Philistines seven years.

ekegusii: Omokungu oria akamotebia, “Omonene, ing’a amache ayio tindang’a, gose timbaisa gocha aiga kobuucha.”
english: The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water so that I won't get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water."

ekegusii: Omokungu oria akairaneria eng’iti eria, “Amatunda a kera omote ore ase omogondo natonyare koria,
english: The woman said to the serpent, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden,

ekegusii: Omokungu oria akamotebia, “Namanyire ng’a ngocha are Masihi (oyokorokwa Kristo); karache ere, natoorokerie onsi.”
english: The woman said, "I know that Messiah" (called Christ) "is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us."

ekegusii: Ase igo omokungu oria akabora, “Naki aye kwarobeirie amang’ana buna ayio are mamincha y’abanto ba Nyasae? Ase ogokwana ring’ana eri, aye omoruoti kwegambirie aye omonyene, ekiagera toeti omwana oo, oria otamete, ribaga airane nka.
english: The woman said, "Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?

ekegusii: Omokungu oria n’Omogiriki orenge, egesaku kiaye n’Omosurofenisa. Akamosaba amosererie ekerecha korwa ase enyaroka yaye.
english: The woman was a Greek, born in Syrian Phoenicia. She begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

ekegusii: Na omokungu oria nigo arenge oboirie eanga emonyinga na embariri mono, na ochabeire chitahabu, na amagena e rigori rinene, ne chiruru. Ere nigo arenge negekombe gi’etahabu koboko kwaye, geichire okogechia na eubi y’obotomani bwaye.
english: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and was glittering with gold, precious stones and pearls. She held a golden cup in her hand, filled with abominable things and the filth of her adulteries.

ekegusii: Korende omokungu oria akaegwa chimbaba ibere buna echi’ensoti enene, anyare koiruruka korwa ase eng’iti eria gochia ase erooro aase agochia korendwa ase engaki y’emiaka etato na ekeng’ese.
english: The woman was given the two wings of a great eagle, so that she might fly to the place prepared for her in the desert, where she would be taken care of for a time, times and half a time, out of the serpent's reach.

ekegusii: Erio omokungu oria omwana oye arenge moyo, ekiagera anchete omwana oye mono, agatebia omoruoti, “Aye omoruoti, tobaisa goita omwana, kae omokungu oyo omwana oyo ore moyo.” Korende oria onde agateba, “Omwana takoba oyone, gose oyoo; tiga anachanwe.”
english: The woman whose son was alive was filled with compassion for her son and said to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living baby! Don't kill him!" But the other said, "Neither I nor you shall have him. Cut him in two!"

ekegusii: Na omokungu oria kwaroche nomochie oria omonene oyore noboruoti igoro y’abaruoti b’ense.”
english: The woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."

ekegusii: Chinda chi’abaiborete nchibebe pi; amakonde nabarie baere, tibakoinyorwa nonya ng’ake; igo oyogokora amabe nabunwe buna omote.
english: The womb forgets them, the worm feasts on them; evil men are no longer remembered but are broken like a tree.

ekegusii: Na abakungu bagateba, “Ekero twasambete ubani na koumora okoruegwa gwaito gw’ekenyugwa ase Eting’ana ya Igoro, naende tokayeroiseria emegati yabekire omogwekano oye, abasacha baito nigo bancheranete nayio.”
english: The women added, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did not our husbands know that we were making cakes like her image and pouring out drink offerings to her?"

ekegusii: Abakungu abarenge abagisangio baye bakabora, “Naomi oiboreirwe omwana omochokoro omomura”, bakamoroka Obedi. Obedi oyio nere oiborete Yese, na Yese akaibora Daudi.
english: The women living there said, "Naomi has a son." And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.

ekegusii: Erio abakungu b’omochie oyio bagatebia Naomi, “Omonene atogigwe! Ere tagotigeti; rero okoeire omonyamwando, oyio erieta riaye riramanyekane ase egati y’Abaisraeli!
english: The women said to Naomi: "Praise be to the LORD, who this day has not left you without a kinsman-redeemer. May he become famous throughout Israel!

ekegusii: Abakungu abachete amo nere korwa Galili, nigo batunyanete korwa nyuma, bakarigereria oboina na buna omobere oye bwareretigwe.
english: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph and saw the tomb and how his body was laid in it.

ekegusii: Na rirorio Ring’ana rigakoreka koba omobere, akamenya ase egati yaito. Tokarora obonene bwaye, obonene buna obw’Omwana omomoima orure ase Tata, oichire nobuya na ekeene.
english: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the One and Only, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.

ekegusii: Ase omwaka o kane bw’okogamba kwa Yehoyakimu mosinto o Yosia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yeremia, rikamotebia amang’ana igoro y’Abayuda bonsi. (Oyio noro orenge omwaka omotang’ani bw’okogamba kwa Nebukadinesaro, omoruoti o Babeli.)
english: The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yeremia nyuma Zedekia omoruoti gakoorire gokora okobwatana nabanto bonsi ba Yerusalemu ng’a obosibore borarigwe ase egati yabo.
english: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim freedom for the slaves.

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yeremia nyuma Nebusaradani, omochiki bw’abarendi, kamorusirie korwa ase omochie o Rama, aase arenge osibire ne chingataare amo nabanto ba Yerusalemu na Abayuda baria bairetwe Babeli ase obosomba.
english: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard had released him at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah bound in chains among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.

ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana Omonene arentete ase Yeremia, ekero Zedekia omoruoti amotomerete Pasuri, mosinto o Malikia, na Zefania, mosinto o Maaseya, bakamotebia,
english: The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malkijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They said:

ekegusii: ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende inche Ezekieli omokuani, mosinto o Busi, agwo ang’e norooche rwa Kebari, ase ense y’Abakalidayo, na okoboko kw’Omonene gokang’ikera aroro.
english: the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, by the Kebar River in the land of the Babylonians. There the hand of the LORD was upon him.

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria ri’emerongo ebere na kane, omotienyi oria o kianda, ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Hagai naende, rikamotebia,
english: The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yeremia ase omwaka o ikomi na gatato bw’okogamba kwa Yosia mosinto bw’Amoni, omoruoti bw’Abayuda.
english: The word of the LORD came to him in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah,

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yeremia, rikamotebia,
english: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Yona mosinto bw’Amitai, rikamotebia:
english: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:

ekegusii: Naende ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende eria kabere, rikamboria: “Ngento ki oroche?” Nkairaneria, “Nenyongo indoche, ere namache akobera; omonwa oye nigo orochie gocha aa korwa sugusu.”
english: The word of the LORD came to me again: "What do you see?" "I see a boiling pot, tilting away from the north," I answered.

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende rigantebia:
english: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende, rigantebia:
english: The word of the LORD came to me:

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende, rigantebia,
english: The word of the LORD came to me:

ekegusii: Naende ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende, rigantebia:
english: The word of the LORD came to me:

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende naende, rigantebia:
english: The word of the LORD came to me:

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha asende, rigantebia: “Yeremia, ngento ki oroche?” Nkamoiraneria, “Nigo ndoche enyimbo y’omote okorokwa omolozi.”
english: The word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" "I see the branch of an almond tree," I replied.

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rigacha ase Sulemani, rikamotebia,
english: The word of the LORD came to Solomon:

ekegusii: Eri nering’ana rikong’u riakwanetwe n’Omonene igoro y’ense ya Hadaraki, riikere nonya nomochie o Damesiki. Amaiso ’abanto b’ebisaku amo nay’Abaisraeli nigo arigereretie Omonene.
english: The word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach and will rest upon Damascus-- for the eyes of men and all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD--

ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’Omonene rikaranda ase ense eria yonsi.
english: The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

ekegusii: Eri nario ring’ana ri’Omonene riacherete Hosea, mosinto o Beeri, ase amatuko aria Usia, na Yotamu, na Ahasi, na Hezekia, barenge abaruoti b’Abayuda, na ekero Yeroboamu, mosinto o Yehoasi, arenge omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli.
english: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash king of Israel:

ekegusii: Eri nario ring’ana ri’Omonene riachete ase Yoeli, mosinto o Petueli.
english: The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.

ekegusii: Eri nario ring’ana ri’Omonene riachete ase Mika, oyo omenyete agwo Moreseti, ekero Yotamu, na Ahasi, na Hezekia, barenge abaruoti b’Abayuda. Omonene akamomaanorera ayare gochia koba igoro ya Samaria na Yerusalemu.
english: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah-- the vision he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Eri nario ring’ana ri’Omonene riachete ase Sefania, mosinto o Kusi, o Gedalia bw’Amaria, bw’Hezekia, ekero Yosia, mosinto bw’Amoni, arenge omoruoti bw’Abayuda.
english: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, during the reign of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah:

ekegusii: Korende amang’ana aya “akabarerwa ng’a nare noboronge” tarigetwe ase engencho yaye bweka,
english: The words "it was credited to him" were written not for him alone,

ekegusii: Korende ring’ana eri, “Ara rimo naende”, nigo rikoorokia, ng’a ebinto biria bigotengechigwa nigo birang’anyigwe ekiagera biatongetwe, erinde ebitanyare gotengechigwa bibeo.
english: The words "once more" indicate the removing of what can be shaken-- that is, created things-- so that what cannot be shaken may remain.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ’omogenki nigo are buna endagera enyansu; naro nigo agotirimboka gochia ase enkoro ime.
english: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to a man's inmost parts.

ekegusii: Amang’ana omonto omoitania nigo are buna endagera enyansu egotirimboka gochia ase enda inse.
english: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to a man's inmost parts.

ekegusii: Amang’ana akorua ase omonwa bw’omonto nigo anga buna amache e chindiba, ensoko y’obong’aini nigo enga buna amache ’orooche akominyoka.
english: The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, but the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.

ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana Amosi, oyomo bw’abarisia ba Tekoa, aroche. Ase amaroro nigo orogetigwe amang’ana ayio igoro y’Abaisraeli miaka ebere ekero omotengecho bw’ense konya otaracha. Ekero ekio Usia nere orenge omoruoti bw’Abayuda, na Yeroboamu, mosinto o Yehoasi, nere orenge omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli.
english: The words of Amos, one of the shepherds of Tekoa-- what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.

ekegusii: Amang’ana omonto oyio agokwana nigo are ay’ogosaria na obong’ainereria; ere otigire gokora amang’ana ’obong’aini na ayare amaya.
english: The words of his mouth are wicked and deceitful; he has ceased to be wise and to do good.

ekegusii: Aya namang’ana akwanetwe na Yeremia, mosinto o Hilikia, oyo orenge oyomo bw’abakuani abarenge ase omochie bw’Anatoti, agwo ase orogongo rwa Benjamin.
english: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.

ekegusii: Aya namang’ana a Nehemia, mosinto o Hakalia. Ase omotienyi o Kisilewi, omwaka bw’emerengo ebere, ekero narenge ase eburi agwo Susa, omochie omonene,
english: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah: In the month of Kislev in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa,

ekegusii: Na amang’ana ’ababani nigo abwataine nayio, buna arikire,
english: The words of the prophets are in agreement with this, as it is written:

ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana ’omorandia mosinto o Daudi, omoruoti o Yerusalemu.
english: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:

ekegusii: Amang’ana abakori amabe nigo akoboera na goitera amanyinga, korende aya abanyene oboronge bagokwana nigo agotooria abanto.
english: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.

ekegusii: Amang’ana abanto abang’aini bagokwana nigo anga buna chimbambo chinyoge, na aya basangereirie anga buna emesumari eakeire bokong’u. Ayio onsi nebiegwa korwa ase Omorisia oyomo.
english: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails-- given by one Shepherd.

ekegusii: Ekero agendererete gokwana, eriogi rikarwa igoro, rigoteba “Aye omoruoti Nebukadinesaro, aya naro ogotebigwa: Oboruoti bwarusigwe asore;
english: The words were still on his lips when a voice came from heaven, "This is what is decreed for you, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your royal authority has been taken from you.

ekegusii: The workers from the city who farm it will come from all the tribes of Israel.
english: Abakori emeremo b’omochie oyio ab’ebisaku bi’Abaisraeli mbabe bakorema orogongo orwo.

ekegusii: Abwo bare chisiiro chi’abanto b’ense mbasenyentwe, na bonsi abarikire gokora emeremo mbaichane.
english: The workers in cloth will be dejected, and all the wage earners will be sick at heart.

ekegusii: Ogokora kw’amaboko aye nigo kore okw’obwegenwa na okw’oboronge, na amachiko aye onsi nay’obwegenwa.
english: The works of his hands are faithful and just; all his precepts are trustworthy.

ekegusii: Na ense eye nigo egoeta, na okogania kwaye, korende ere oyogokora ogwancha kwa Nyasae nigo akoba moyo goika kare na kare.
english: The world and its desires pass away, but the man who does the will of God lives forever.

ekegusii: Ense tekonyara kobagecha inwe, korende nigo engechete inche, ekiagera inche nkoyeorokia ng’a emeremo yaye nemebe.
english: The world cannot hate you, but it hates me because I testify that what it does is evil.

ekegusii: abanto ense etagwenere koba nabarabwo. Barabwo nigo barenge goetanana ase chirooro na ase ebitunwa, ase amabwago na amakuruma.
english: the world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.

ekegusii: ne chianga chiria chinseera chigokorerwa ime y’Aase Aachenu, engencho yaye chianga chia Haroni omokuani, amo nechi’abamura baye, barabe bakobeka ekero bagokora emeremo yabo y’obokuani.”
english: the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary-- both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when they serve as priests."

ekegusii: Naki endamwamu ya Nyasae yaorokigwe korwa igoro, igoro ase ogotamoiroka Nyasae gwonsi na obobe bwa mwanyabanto, abagotanga ekeene nobobe bwabo.
english: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness,

ekegusii: Na amariko ’ogosoerwa kwaye nigo arikire igoro, “OMORUOTI BW’ABAYAHUDI.”
english: The written notice of the charge against him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.

ekegusii: Omomura oyio tatebana gokora ring’ana riria, ekiagera omoiseke oria o Yakobo konya omogweneire. Bono Sekemu nigo asikire kobua abande bonsi ase eamate yabo.
english: The young man, who was the most honored of all his father's household, lost no time in doing what they said, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter.

ekegusii: Abamura ba Oni, na aba Pi‐Beseti, mbaitwe nemioro, na abanto bande babo bairwe ase obosomba.
english: The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the cities themselves will go into captivity.

ekegusii: abasae abaare kondora nigo barenge kogobera, na abanto abagotu batenena konyorokia amasikani.
english: the young men saw me and stepped aside and the old men rose to their feet;

ekegusii: Abamura baria b’ekegori kiaye bakamotebia, “Aya naro oratebie abanto abwo bakoboretie ng’a bwororobie rikorogoto riria iso akorete ririto: Ekiara gi’okoboko kwane nigo kere ekenetu kobua ekenema gia tata.
english: The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell the people who have said to you, 'Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but make our yoke lighter'-- tell them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.

ekegusii: Abamura baria bakinete komo bakamotebia, “Aya naro oratebie abanto abwo bakoboretie ng’a bwororobie rikorogoto riria iso akorete ririto: Ekiara gi’okoboko kwane nigo kere ekenetu kobua ekebono gia tata.
english: The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell these people who have said to you, 'Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but make our yoke lighter'-- tell them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.

ekegusii: Korende abasomba baria abamura b’abagambi be chingongo amo nomoganda bw’esegi okobabwatia bakarua ase omochie, bakagenda,
english: The young officers of the provincial commanders marched out of the city with the army behind them

ekegusii: Abasomba baria abamura b’abagambi be chingongo bakagenda ritang’ani, na Beni‐Hadadi agatoma abatuki b’amang’ana; barabwo bakarenta amang’ana, bakamotebia, “Abanto ngocha bare korwa Samaria.”
english: The young officers of the provincial commanders went out first. Now Ben-Hadad had dispatched scouts, who reported, "Men are advancing from Samaria."

ekegusii: Na oria omwabo omoke, nere akaibora omwana omoisia, akamoroka Ben‐Ami; oyio nere sokoro bw’Abaamoni goika rero iga.
english: The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-Ammi; he is the father of the Ammonites of today.

ekegusii: Oria omoke agatebia ise: Tata, ing’a ensemo y’enibo entungetie. Ise akabaatanera ebinto biaye.
english: The younger one said to his father, 'Father, give me my share of the estate.' So he divided his property between them.

ekegusii: neba ng’a omosae oria nigo aruete echela akabekwa oboruoti, gose nigo aiboretwe ore omotaka ase obogambi bw’omoruoti oria.
english: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.

ekegusii: Amauga aye nigo aichire ne chinguru chi’oboke bwaye, korende chinguru echio nigo chirarare nere ase riroba.
english: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie with him in the dust.

ekegusii: Abanto bande ba Sifu bakagenda ase Saulo agwo Gibea, bakamotebia ng’a Daudi igo akebisete ase ekegoro gia Hakila kororia Yesimoni.
english: The Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hakilah, which faces Jeshimon?"

ekegusii: Abanto bande ba Sifu bakagenda ase Saulo agwo Gibea, bakamotebia, “Daudi nigo ebisete ase orogongo rwaito ase amabwago ’ebitunwa bia Horesi, ase ekegoro kia Hakila, irianyi ya Yesimoni.
english: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?

ekegusii: Emegwe yabo nigo ere emioge, na amata abo nigo atingire; ebitaago bie chibarasi chiabo nigo binga buna amagena amakong’u, na amagoro e chigari chiabo nigo akominyoka buna ekerambauti.
english: Their arrows are sharp, all their bows are strung; their horses' hoofs seem like flint, their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.

ekegusii: Ninsibie okomocha kwabo kw’ogoitera amanyinga, okwo ntasibetie ritang’ani. Inche Omonene nigo ngendererete komenya Sayoni.”
english: Their bloodguilt, which I have not pardoned, I will pardon.' The LORD dwells in Zion!

ekegusii: Bakabogorigwa goika Sekemu, bagatindekwa ase embeera eria Ibrahimu agorete ase chifeta korwa ase abana ba Hamori, aaria Sekemu.
english: Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a certain sum of money.

ekegusii: na ebitondo ebio nabibeere ase enchera y’omochie oria omonene aase Omonene obo abambetwe. Ase okobayena omochie oyio erieta riaye nigo okorokwa Sodomu na Misiri.
english: Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city, which is figuratively called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.

ekegusii: Orobebe rwabo rogachaka korwa Helefu ase omote onga buna omotontera orenge, agwo Sananimu, na korwa Adami‐Nekebu, na Yabuneli, rogaika Lakumu, rogatwomera Yorodan.
english: Their boundary went from Heleph and the large tree in Zaanannim, passing Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum and ending at the Jordan.

ekegusii: Barabwo mbaite abamura b’abwo ase okobabeta chinsara, tibakororera abana bare inda, gose abana bande, amabera.
english: Their bows will strike down the young men; they will have no mercy on infants nor will they look with compassion on children.

ekegusii: Abanto bamwabo abarenge ase emechie yabo bakabetererigwa gocha koba amo nabarabwo ase kera rituko ria gatano na kabere ase engaki yachikire.
english: Their brothers in their villages had to come from time to time and share their duties for seven-day periods.

ekegusii: Chiombe chiabo nigo chikonyora amarieme buya, naende chiabiara chitari korekera.
english: Their bulls never fail to breed; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

ekegusii: Abanto bagochigora nigo bagochinyenya, tibari korora ng’a mbare nokomocha, na abwo bagochioonia nigo bagoteba: Omonene atogigwe, ekiagera twenyoreire obonda obonge. Nonya nabarisia babo abanyene tibari gochirorera amabera.
english: Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, 'Praise the LORD, I am rich!' Their own shepherds do not spare them.

ekegusii: “Mosakore, moire chingamia chiabo, ne chiombe chiabo chibe echiaino. Abanto abwo bakogingira chitukia chiabo nimbaserie mbasiarere gochia ase kera ensemo y’ense. Nimbarentere emechando korwa ase kera ensemo. Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: Their camels will become plunder, and their large herds will be booty. I will scatter to the winds those who are in distant places and will bring disaster on them from every side," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: Abana babo mbabe abange buna kare, omoganda obo nonyore chinguru ase obosio bwane, abwo bakobachanda, nimbae egesusuro.
english: Their children will be as in days of old, and their community will be established before me; I will punish all who oppress them.

ekegusii: Erio abana babo konya bataramanya amachiko aya, bayaigwe na kweorokereria komoiroka Omonene, Nyasae oino, ekero morabe mogendererete komenya ase ense eria ng’umbu ya Yorodan, eyio mogochia koira ebe eyaino.”
english: Their children, who do not know this law, must hear it and learn to fear the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

ekegusii: Chiusi chiria bakoroisia ng’a chibe chianga, korende chianga echio tichigotuba emebere y’abanto. Emeremo y’abanto abwo nigo ere ey’ebibe, nigo benaretie gokora ay’obotindi namaboko abo.
english: Their cobwebs are useless for clothing; they cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their deeds are evil deeds, and acts of violence are in their hands.

ekegusii: Abana babo mbamanyekane ase abanto b’ebisaku, na abanto b’ororeria rwabo mbamanyekane ase abanto bonsi. Abanto bonsi barabe bakobarora mbabamanye na baorokie ng’a abwo nabanto Omonene asesenirie.”
