english: They came to appease them and escorted them from the prison, requesting them to leave the city.

ekegusii: Nabarabwo bagacha ase Baalamu, bakamotebia, “Aya naro Balaki, mosinto o Sipori, agoteba: Koranche totiga kende gionsi kegotange tochicha.
english: They came to Balaam and said: "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Do not let anything keep you from coming to me,

ekegusii: They came to Bethsaida, and some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
english: Bagaika Bethisaida. Bakamorentera omonto omouko, bakamosorora amokune.

ekegusii: They came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"
english: Bagaika Kapernaumu. Ekero arenge nyomba ime, akababoria, “Ninki mware koamererania inchera?”

ekegusii: Ase igo Isumaeli, mosinto o Netania, na Yohanani, na Yonathani, basinto ba Karea, na Seraya, mosinto o Tanahumeti, na basinto ba Efai korwa Netofa, na Yesania, mosinto bw’omonto oyomo korwa Maaka, amo nabanto babo, bagachiera Gedalia agwo Misipa.
english: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah-- Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, and their men.

ekegusii: Bagachia goika bakamotebia, “Omworokia, twamanyire ng’a aye nigo ore omonto bw’ekeene, gose tori koyiera monto, naki torengerereti obonene bw’abanto, korende ase ekeene nigo okworokereria enchera ya Nyasae. Inee! Mboronge koa Kaisari ebango, gose taibo?
english: They came to him and said, "Teacher, we know you are a man of integrity. You aren't swayed by men, because you pay no attention to who they are; but you teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?

ekegusii: Bagachiera Yohana, bakamotebia, “Omworokia, ere oyorenge amo naye ng’umbu ya Yorodan, oyio kwaorogetie aye, oyio nao are akobatisa, na abanto bonsi nkomochiera bare.”
english: They came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, that man who was with you on the other side of the Jordan-- the one you testified about-- well, he is baptizing, and everyone is going to him."

ekegusii: Barabwo bagachiera Filipo o Bethisaida bw’ensemo ya Galili, bakamosaba, bakobora, “Omosike, ntorigetie korora Yeso.”
english: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, with a request. "Sir," they said, "we would like to see Jesus."

ekegusii: bakagenda ase Serubabeli, na ase abateneneri be chiamate chiabo, bakabatebia, “Tiga tobaagachisie, naintwe nabo togosasima Nyasae oino buna inwe mogokora, na ase chingaki korwa kare gese Esari‐Hadoni, omoruoti bw’Abaasuri, oria otorentete aiga, twabeire tokorwa ebing’wanso ase Nyasae oyo.”
english: they came to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the families and said, "Let us help you build because, like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to him since the time of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

ekegusii: Barabwo bakabwatana amo, erinde barwanie Yoshua na Abaisraeli.
english: they came together to make war against Joshua and Israel.

ekegusii: Nigo barenge gocha amo ne chitugo chiabo ne chiema chiabo, abange buna chingige. Barabwo abanyene ne chingamia chiabo, omobaro obo torenge kobareka. Bagasoa ase ense eria, bakagania koyesaria kegima.
english: They came up with their livestock and their tents like swarms of locusts. It was impossible to count the men and their camels; they invaded the land to ravage it.

ekegusii: Bakaba bagotoora ase ense y’Abaisraeli, erio basaria chindagera chiabo goika chimbebe chia Gasa. Tibaare gotigareria Abaisraeli ching’ondi, gose chiombe, gose chitigere, nonya ngento kende gionsi Abaisraeli baare koria.
english: They camped on the land and ruined the crops all the way to Gaza and did not spare a living thing for Israel, neither sheep nor cattle nor donkeys.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaira emechie yagiteire chindwaki, na ense entenenku, bakaira ne chinyomba chiaichire nebinto ebiya, ne chinsoko chi’amache chiabaachetwe ase ebitare, na emegondo y’emesabibu na ey’emezeituni, na emete emenge y’amatunda. Bakaria, bakaigota na konora, bakaba nomogoko omonene ase obuya bwao obonge.”
english: They captured fortified cities and fertile land; they took possession of houses filled with all kinds of good things, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves and fruit trees in abundance. They ate to the full and were well-nourished; they reveled in your great goodness.

ekegusii: Rituko erio erio bakayobwata, bagaita nemioro abanto b’aroro, buna bakorete omochie o Lakisi.
english: They captured it that same day and put it to the sword and totally destroyed everyone in it, just as they had done to Lachish.

ekegusii: Bakamoimokia, bakamoira goika ase ense ya Kanani. Erio bakamotindeka ase rikuruma riria riare, ase oboremo agwo Makipela, moocha ya Mamure, oboremo boria Ibrahimu agorete korwa ase Efuroni Omohiti abe aase aye agotindeka abakure.
english: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, along with the field.

ekegusii: Bagasakora enibo yabo yonsi, na abana babo, na abakungu babo, na bionsi ebiarenge ase chinyomba bakabiira.
english: They carried off all their wealth and all their women and children, taking as plunder everything in the houses.

ekegusii: Agakora chibonyi inye, agachibeka ase chikoona inye chi’egechungi ekio gi’etaai, ase emiaro egosoigwa.
english: They cast bronze rings to hold the poles for the four corners of the bronze grating.

ekegusii: Naende agakora chibonyi inye korwa ase chitahabu, ne chibonyi echio agachibeka ase chikoona inye ase amagoro aye ane.
english: They cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners, where the four legs were.

ekegusii: Baakeire abanto baane obomera, baoonirie abana abamura, erinde banyore abakungu abatayayi, na baoonirie abana abaiseke, erinde banyore edivai bakonywa.
english: They cast lots for my people and traded boys for prostitutes; they sold girls for wine that they might drink.

ekegusii: They caused the cry of the poor to come before him, so that he heard the cry of the needy.
english: Abwo bagerire ekerero ki’abataka giaikire asare, nere oigure ekerero ki’abagokorerwa bobe.

ekegusii: Nigo chikominyoka gochia korwana esegi buna abarwani esegi chituoni; nigo chikoriina chindwaki igoro buna abarwani esegi. Kera eyemo nigo eragenderere gochia bosio, ende teri eragobere esire enchera ebwatetie.
english: They charge like warriors; they scale walls like soldiers. They all march in line, not swerving from their course.

ekegusii: Igo bagoteba ng’a mbamomanyete Nyasae, korende ase ogokora kwabo bamokana. Nigo bare abagechigwa, abatari koigwera, na ase ayio tibakonyara gokora ogokora okuya konde gwonsi.
english: They claim to know God, but by their actions they deny him. They are detestable, disobedient and unfit for doing anything good.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bare ne chinkoro chitari namabera nigo bagokwana amang’ana ’oboenenu.
english: They close up their callous hearts, and their mouths speak with arrogance.

ekegusii: Omonene ngocha are amo nebirwanero bi’endamwamu yaye korwa ense y’aare, ase chinsinyo chia igoro, erinde asirie ense yonsi.
english: They come from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens-- the LORD and the weapons of his wrath-- to destroy the whole country.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bakoroberia amabe, barenta ogosaria; okwama kwabo bakorenta nokw’obong’ainereria.”
english: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb fashions deceit."

ekegusii: Barabwo bagakania Usia omoruoti, bakamotebia, “Usia, aye tochikiri gosamba ubani ase Omonene, korende abakuani ab’ororeria rwa Haroni nabwo baatananetwe gosamba ubani. Aye soka korwa aiga Aase Aachenu, kwamochire. Omonene Nyasae tagokoa ogosikwa ekiagera gwakorire ayio.”
english: They confronted him and said, "It is not right for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD. That is for the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who have been consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful; and you will not be honored by the LORD God."

ekegusii: Ekero narenge nemechando bakandwania, korende Omonene akaba egekengero kiane.
english: They confronted me in the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.

ekegusii: Nigo bagosangererekana amo baroberia komboera, barigererie kera egento ngokora; naboigo bagendererete korigia obogima bwane babosirie.
english: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps, eager to take my life.

ekegusii: Abanto bagakora omoroberio agwo Yerusalemu bw’ogoita Amasia, korende ere agatama gochia Lakisi. Abanto bagatomwa gochia Lakisi, bakamoitera aroro.
english: They conspired against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagatenenia omogwekano oria bw’ogosasimwa obaachire, oria Mika aroisetie, na omogwekano oria okabeera aroro ase engaki yonsi obomenyo bwa Nyasae bwatenenete agwo Silo.
english: They continued to use the idols Micah had made, all the time the house of God was in Shiloh.

ekegusii: Naende bakabora, “Tobatige babe moyo, korende babe bagwatia chinko, naende babe bakorentera abanto bonsi amache.”
english: They continued, "Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the entire community." So the leaders' promise to them was kept.

ekegusii: Chingige echio chigatuba ense eria yonsi goika ekamwama ti, chikaria ebimeri bionsi pi ase ense eria, na amatunda onsi ay’emete, ebio bionsi bitasaretigwe nembura y’amagena. Tigiatigarete kemeri kende gionsi ekebese gose amato ’emete ase ense ya Misiri engima.
english: They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail-- everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.

ekegusii: Abwo nigo bakoba ne ribero ri’okonyora emegondo, bayaire ne chinguru, bagania ne chinyomba bachiira. Nigo bakoura omonto enyomba yaye, ee, bamoura na omwando oyo.
english: They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them. They defraud a man of his home, a fellowman of his inheritance.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakarigereria, korende onde tarenge obatooretie; bakarangeria Omonene, korende ere tabaigwa.
english: They cried for help, but there was no one to save them-- to the LORD, but he did not answer.

ekegusii: Abanto aba bakarera ng’a bakonywe, korende onde tarenge obatooretie, bakarangeria Omonene, korende ere tabaigwa.
english: They cried for help, but there was no one to save them-- to the LORD, but he did not answer.

ekegusii: Ase igo bakarera ase Omonene, bakabora; Twakorire ebibe, ekiagera twatigire Omonene; twakoreire chinyasae chiria chikorokwa Baali na Asitaroti. Bono totoorie korwa ase amaboko ’ababisa baito, naintwe ntogokorere aye.
english: They cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned; we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. But now deliver us from the hands of our enemies, and we will serve you.'

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo barerete asore, bakanyora ogotooreka, nigo babete bagosemeretie, na tibasoogetigwe.
english: They cried to you and were saved; in you they trusted and were not disappointed.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaamboka orooche gochia kwambokia abanto b’enka y’omoruoti na gokora ande onsi omoruoti aganetie. Ekero omoruoti abeire ang’e kwamboka Yorodan, Simei, mosinto o Gera, agatung’ama inse ase obosio bwaye,
english: They crossed at the ford to take the king's household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king

ekegusii: Nigo chigwekumba chiabiara chimanwa chiabo, na ekero chiabiarire, obororo bw’okobina bwasira.
english: They crouch down and bring forth their young; their labor pains are ended.

ekegusii: Amo nere bakabamba abauri babere, oyomo ensemo y’okoboko kwaye gw’okorio, na oyomo ensemo y’okoboko kwaye gw’okobee. [
english: They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.

ekegusii: Nigo bakomitera abakori amabe amaguta ’amazeituni, korende nonya naboigo nigo bare nerang’o.
english: They crush olives among the terraces; they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.

ekegusii: Aye Omonene, abwo nigo bagosamunyorana abanto bao, na gochanda abanto bare omwando oo.
english: They crush your people, O LORD; they oppress your inheritance.

ekegusii: Abafilisti bakabutora omotwe o Saulo, bakaira na ebirwanero biaye, erio bagatoma abanto bararie amang’ana ayio ase ense yonsi y’Abafilisti, ase hekalu y’emegwekano yabo bagosasima, na ase abanto.
english: They cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.

ekegusii: Bakararia ase Abaisraeli bonsi korwa Beeri‐Seba goika Dani ng’a, abanto bachiche Yerusalemu barende Rituko Rinene ri’Epasaka ase Omonene, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, ekiagera konya tiriana korendwa nabanto abange buna yachigetwe.
english: They decided to send a proclamation throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling the people to come to Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel. It had not been celebrated in large numbers according to what was written.

ekegusii: Ase ayio abanto abwo bagesoyia ase ogotacheneka ase engencho y’ogokora kwabo, bagakora obonyaka tibaba abegenwa.
english: They defiled themselves by what they did; by their deeds they prostituted themselves.

ekegusii: Bagatagora omogwekano o Baali enyene na enyomba yaye, erio bakaroisia aase aria akaba echoo, naboigo ere nonya ngoika rero iga.
english: They demolished the sacred stone of Baal and tore down the temple of Baal, and people have used it for a latrine to this day.

ekegusii: Nigo bagochecheria abaruoti, na gosekerera abagambi. Nigo bagochaya kera eburi enkong’u, baagacha chiburi chiabo, babua bachiira.
english: They deride kings and scoff at rulers. They laugh at all fortified cities; they build earthen ramps and capture them.

ekegusii: Bakabua na gosaria emechie yonsi yaetanaine Gerari, ekiagera Omonene abegete obwoba ase abanto b’emechie eria. Bagasakora ebinto korwa ase emechie eria yonsi, ekiagera ebinto ebinge bi’ogosakorwa mbiarengeo.
english: They destroyed all the villages around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them. They plundered all these villages, since there was much booty there.

ekegusii: Bagatagora emechie yabo bagasaria kera oboremo obuya. Kera omonto akaruta rigena ase oboremo goika amagena akabotuba kegima. Bagaticha kera ensoko y’amache na bagatema kera omote omuya. Amagena oka agatigara ase omochie o Kiri‐Hariseti, na abanto barenge koruta chinduruche bakayoetanana, bakayoumokera.
english: They destroyed the towns, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up all the springs and cut down every good tree. Only Kir Hareseth was left with its stones in place, but men armed with slings surrounded it and attacked it as well.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bangechete, bantamire; tibetangeti gontwera amate obosio bwane.
english: They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

ekegusii: Bagaita abanto bonsi b’omochie, abasacha na abakungu, abasae na abagotu, nemioro, bagaita boigo chiombe, ne ching’ondi, ne chitigere.
english: They devoted the city to the LORD and destroyed with the sword every living thing in it-- men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakagenderera ase okworokereria kw’abatomwa na ase obomo, ase ogosamunyora omogati na ase ogosaba.
english: They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.

ekegusii: Abwo bakourereria chinyomba chi’ababoraka, na ase obong’ainereria basaba ogosaba ogotambe; aba nabanyore ekina ekere ekenene kobua.”
english: They devour widows' houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. Such men will be punished most severely."

ekegusii: abakourereria chinyomba chi’ababoraka, na ase obong’ainereria basaba ogosaba ogotambe. Abwo nabanyore ekina kere ekenene kobua.”
english: They devour widows' houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. Such men will be punished most severely."

ekegusii: Barabwo tibaboretie: Inee! Omonene oria otorusetie ase ense ya Misiri, ng’ai are? Ere nigo atoraaete ase erooro, ense eria ere enyomo ere namaoromomo, ense y’eguru‐gura enyomo pa ere ekiriri ki’amakweri. Ense eria omonto atarenge konyara goeta ase egati yaye, agwo omonto nonya noyomo atamenyete.
english: They did not ask, 'Where is the LORD, who brought us up out of Egypt and led us through the barren wilderness, through a land of deserts and rifts, a land of drought and darkness, a land where no one travels and no one lives?'

ekegusii: Abaisraeli tibaitete basirie kegima abanto b’ebisaku, buna Omonene konya achikire.
english: They did not destroy the peoples as the LORD had commanded them,

ekegusii: Amang’ana onsi omoruoti achigete abakuani na Abalawi nigo aikeranetigwe kegima ase kera ring’ana rinde rionsi amo nerie chimonga.
english: They did not deviate from the king's commands to the priests or to the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries.

ekegusii: Korende barabwo tibaseretie Abakanani abwo bamenyete Geseri. Ase ayio Abakanani nao bamenyete amo n’Abaefraimu, naboigo nao bare nonya ngoika rero iga. Korende mbakoretwe bakaba abasomba babo b’ogokora emeremo emekong’u.
english: They did not dislodge the Canaanites living in Gezer; to this day the Canaanites live among the people of Ephraim but are required to do forced labor.

ekegusii: Barabwo tibarendete okobwatana kw’ogotianania kwa Nyasae, naende nigo bangete kobwatia amachiko aye.
english: they did not keep God's covenant and refused to live by his law.

ekegusii: Barabwo tibamanya ng’a Yusufu nayaigwete, ekiagera omonogi narengeo ore komoonchorera.
english: They did not realize that Joseph could understand them, since he was using an interpreter.

ekegusii: Tibabete bakoinyora chinguru chi’okoboko kwaye, gose tibabete bakoinyora rituko riria ababooretie korwa ase ababisa babo,
english: They did not remember his power-- the day he redeemed them from the oppressor,

ekegusii: Abanto abwo barenge koegwa chibesa chiria tibarenge koborigwa koorokia omobaro, ekiagera barenge abegenwa.
english: They did not require an accounting from those to whom they gave the money to pay the workers, because they acted with complete honesty.

ekegusii: Ekero Omonene aetetie abanto baye ase erooro, tibabete nerang’o, nigo abatubokeretie amache korwa ase egetare, akabochora egetare, na amache agatimboka gocha isiko.
english: They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he made water flow for them from the rock; he split the rock and water gushed out.

ekegusii: Tibamanya ng’a nigo are gokwana asebare aya Ise.
english: They did not understand that he was telling them about his Father.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagakora bo. Haroni akarambora okoboko kwaye, agaaka riroba nenyimbo yaye, na orotu rokaonchoka rokaba chinsona, na chirochio chikaroma mwanyabanto ne chitugo. Orotu rwonsi rwe riroba rokaonchoka rokaba chinsona.
english: They did this, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the ground, gnats came upon men and animals. All the dust throughout the land of Egypt became gnats.

ekegusii: erinde bakore aya okoboko kwao na omoroberio oo biare goteba korwa kare akoreke.
english: They did what your power and will had decided beforehand should happen.

ekegusii: Abanto nigo bagokwa ara rimo; nigo bakonyegerigwa botuko gati, basira kegima, baria bare nokobua nigo bagosirigwa ko tari namaboko a mwanyabanto.
english: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and they pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bagokwa ekero bare abake, obogima bwabo nigo bogosirigwa buna obw’abanyaka.
english: They die in their youth, among male prostitutes of the shrines.

ekegusii: Ekiagera batabwatanete barabwo ase barabwo, bakagenda ekero Paulo akwanete ring’ana eri erimo ng’a, “Omoika Omochenu nokwanete buya ne chisokoro chiaito goetera ase omonwa bw’omobani Isaya, ogoteba,
english: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your forefathers when he said through Isaiah the prophet:

ekegusii: Bagatebania barabwo ase barabwo, bakabora, “Toise goteba: Nigoro yarwete, nigo aratoborie: Naki rende motamwegenete?
english: They discussed it among themselves and said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why didn't you believe him?'

ekegusii: Bagatebania barabwo ase barabwo, bakobora, “Toise goteba: Nigoro yarwete, nigo aratoborie: Naki motamwegenete rende?
english: They discussed it among themselves and said, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Why didn't you believe him?'

ekegusii: They discussed this among themselves and said, "It is because we didn't bring any bread."
english: Bakaborania, bagoteba, “Titwarentete emegati.”

ekegusii: Bakaamererania barabwo ase barabwo, bakobora, “Titori nemegati.”
english: They discussed this with one another and said, "It is because we have no bread."

ekegusii: Baatananire chianga chiane ase egati yabo; baakeire eganchwa yaane obomera.
english: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.

ekegusii: Igo baatananetwe ase ogoakerwa obomera, bonsi ase enchera eyemo, ekiagera abateneneri abwo b’Aase Aachenu na abwo ba Nyasae nigo bachoretwe korwa ase ororeria rw’Eleazari amo norwa Itamari.
english: They divided them impartially by drawing lots, for there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God among the descendants of both Eleazar and Ithamar.

ekegusii: Tibari korera asende korwa ase chinkoro chiabo, korende nigo bakona‐kwerera ase amarere abo. Nigo bagosangererekana amo bachandekerete endagera na edivai, ekero bagendererete gosaria asende.
english: They do not cry out to me from their hearts but wail upon their beds. They gather together for grain and new wine but turn away from me.

ekegusii: Tichikomigererania, kera eyemo nigo egoeta omong’ororia oye; nigo chigoeta gati‐gati y’ebirwanero, tichigotangeka.
english: They do not jostle each other; each marches straight ahead. They plunge through defenses without breaking ranks.

ekegusii: Barabwo tibari gokwana ase chinkoro chiabo: Tiga tomoiroke Omonene, Nyasae oito, oyogotoa embura ase engaki yaye egwenerete; embura y’omochakano na ey’okwamia endagera, naende nere ogotorendera chichuma chibekire ase rigesa.
english: They do not say to themselves, 'Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives autumn and spring rains in season, who assures us of the regular weeks of harvest.'

ekegusii: Abanto abwo tibari gokwana amang’ana akorenta omorembe; nigo bakona‐korigia amang’ana ’obong’ainereria igoro y’abanto abwo bare abatoereru ase ense.
english: They do not speak peaceably, but devise false accusations against those who live quietly in the land.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bakoonchoka, korende tari gochia ase Oyore Igoro Mono. Nigo banga buna obota bootokanete. Abagambi babo mbaitwe nemioro ase engencho y’obotindi bwe chimeme chiabo. Ring’ana erio ndigere ense ya Misiri ebasekerere na kobachaya.
english: They do not turn to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their insolent words. For this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.

ekegusii: abwo batari gokora amabe, korende nigo bakobwatia chinchera chiaye.
english: They do nothing wrong; they walk in his ways.

ekegusii: Batubire amaote ’abanto baane rioka, bagoteba: Omorembe, omorembe, na omorembe tori aande.
english: They dress the wound of my people as though it were not serious. "Peace, peace," they say, when there is no peace.

ekegusii: Batubire amaote ’abanto baane rioka, bagoteba: Omorembe, omorembe, na omorembe tori aande.
english: They dress the wound of my people as though it were not serious. 'Peace, peace,' they say, when there is no peace.

ekegusii: Abwo nigo bakoira chitigere chie chintakana, baira chiombe chi’ababoraka koba intenenera.
english: They drive away the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox in pledge.

ekegusii: Bagaseria ebirecha ebinge, bagaaka abanto abange amaguta, abwo barenge abarwaire, bakabagwenia.
english: They drove out many demons and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

ekegusii: They eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
english: Endagera yabo bakoria nogokora amabe, na edivai yabo bakonywa nobotindi.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bakobekana chinguru ase ogokora ebibe ebio barobeirie; nigo bagokwana amo igoro y’ogotegera abande oboreba bobisi, bagotebania, “Ning’o otoroche?”
english: They encourage each other in evil plans, they talk about hiding their snares; they say, "Who will see them?"

ekegusii: Ababisa bachire Ayati, baetire ase egati ya Migironi; babekire ebinto biabo Mikimasi.
english: They enter Aiath; they pass through Migron; they store supplies at Micmash.

ekegusii: Bagakora okobwatana kw’ogotianania ng’a bamorigie Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiabo, ne chinkoro chiabo chionsi, na emioyo yabo yonsi.
english: They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul.

ekegusii: Bagacha Yerusalemu bakobugia amakano abo, na amakano abo ay’ebirigisa, na ebirombeta, bakagenda ase enyomba y’Omonene.
english: They entered Jerusalem and went to the temple of the LORD with harps and lutes and trumpets.

ekegusii: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.
english: Ekero bakoorire komboria bakarigia gonsibora, ekiagera tibanyorete engencho ende yonsi yangwenerete ng’itwe.

ekegusii: ekiagera batigete ekeene kia Nyasae, bagachora oborimo, bagasasima na gokorera ebitongwa ribaga ri’Omotongi, oyorabakwe kare na kare! Amina.
english: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator-- who is forever praised. Amen.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaonchoreria oyorenge obonene bwabo, bakaonchokera omogwekano bw’eng’ombe ekorisia obonyansi.
english: They exchanged their Glory for an image of a bull, which eats grass.

ekegusii: Egesembe ki’obokuani bagakeroisia, buna omoroisia omong’aini aranyare gokeroisia, korwa ase egetambaa kere buna eki’egesibao ki’obokuani, nakio keroisirie korwa ase chiusi chi’etahabu na echi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, amo nechi’egatani engiya chisisire.
english: They fashioned the breastpiece-- the work of a skilled craftsman. They made it like the ephod: of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.

ekegusii: Bagasiberania ebichanga ebi bibere bie chitahabu ase chibonyi echi ibere ase emego y’egesembe keria.
english: They fastened the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece,

ekegusii: Nigo bagoisanekigwa nobonoru bokorwa ase enyomba yao, aye nobae banywe korwa ase orooche rwao rw’okogokia.
english: They feast on the abundance of your house; you give them drink from your river of delights.

ekegusii: Nigo bakwerageria ebibe bi’abanto baane, nigo bakogania bakore obobe.
english: They feed on the sins of my people and relish their wickedness.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo batamire korwa ase ogoitwa nemioro, na korwa ase emeyio yasomoirwe, na korwa ase amata atingirwe, na korwa ase emechando y’esegi.
english: They flee from the sword, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow and from the heat of battle.

ekegusii: Agatiira gochia ebitunwa igoro, na agatirimboka gochia ase amakura inse, agaika aase kwayachikerete.
english: they flowed over the mountains, they went down into the valleys, to the place you assigned for them.

ekegusii: Bakamotegerera, ekiagera ase amatuko amange nigo barenge gokumia ase oborogi bwaye.
english: They followed him because he had amazed them for a long time with his magic.

ekegusii: Ase ayio bakababwatia goika Yorodan, bakarora chianga na ebinto binde Abasiiria batugutete inchera ekero barenge gotama. Abanto baria batometwe bakairana, bagatebia omoruoti amang’ana ayio.
english: They followed them as far as the Jordan, and they found the whole road strewn with the clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown away in their headlong flight. So the messengers returned and reported to the king.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bagokania abanto ng’a tibanyuomana, naende tibaria endagera eye Nyasae atongete, erinde baria begenire, na baikire komanya ekeene, bayenyore ase okoiraneria ng’a mbuya mono.
english: They forbid people to marry and order them to abstain from certain foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and who know the truth.

ekegusii: They forgot the God who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt,
english: Bakeba Nyasae, Omotooria obo, oria okorete amang’ana amanene aaria Misiri;

ekegusii: Bakeba amang’ana Omonene konya akorire, na ebikone biria konya aorokirie asebare.
english: They forgot what he had done, the wonders he had shown them.

ekegusii: Bagatiga amachiko onsi ay’Omonene, Nyasae obo, bakabomba emegwekano ebere ye chimori; boigo bakaroisia omote bw’Asera, enyasae eria enkungu, bagasasima erioba na omotienyi ne ching’enang’eni, na gokorera Baali enyasae eria.
english: They forsook all the commands of the LORD their God and made for themselves two idols cast in the shape of calves, and an Asherah pole. They bowed down to all the starry hosts, and they worshiped Baal.

ekegusii: Bagatiga komokorera Omonene, Nyasae bwe chisokoro chiabo, oria obarusetie ase ense ya Misiri, bakaba bakobwatana ne chinyasae chinde ching’ao chinyasae chi’abanto baria bamenyete ase egati yabo. Bagasasima chirochio, na ase ayio bakagechia Omonene.
english: They forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed and worshiped various gods of the peoples around them. They provoked the LORD to anger

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaumokera Abamidiani, bakabarwania buna Omonene achigete Musa, bagaita kera omonto obo omosacha.
english: They fought against Midian, as the LORD commanded Moses, and killed every man.

ekegusii: Bakanyora abaiseke abekungi, abwo konya bataramenyana nomosacha onde bwensi, amagana ane, ase egati y’abanto ba Yabesi o Gileadi, bakabarenta ase batoorete agwo Silo, omochie oria orenge ase ense ya Kanani.
english: They found among the people living in Jabesh Gilead four hundred young women who had never slept with a man, and they took them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.

ekegusii: Abanto baria ba Daudi bakanyora omomura omosae bw’Abamisiri agwo ase arenge aarabu, bakamorenta ase Daudi, bakamoa omogati akaria, na amache akanywa,
english: They found an Egyptian in a field and brought him to David. They gave him water to drink and food to eat--

ekegusii: Aroro agwo ase banyorete oborisia obuya na obonoru, ense nigo yarenge engare, na entoereru, na ey’omorembe. Abanto bamenyete agwo ritang’ani nigo barenge abanto ba Hamu.
english: They found rich, good pasture, and the land was spacious, peaceful and quiet. Some Hamites had lived there formerly.

ekegusii: Bakanyora rigena riria riatigerigwe korwa ase oboina,
english: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

ekegusii: Bakanyora amang’ana arikire ase amachiko ayio Omonene aruete ase Abaisraeli goetera ase Musa, ng’a Abaisraeli goika bamenye ase ebigutu ase Rituko Rinene ri’omotienyi o gatano na kabere,
english: They found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the Israelites were to live in booths during the feast of the seventh month

ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bakoroberia bamoiyerie korwa ase obonene bwaye. Barabwo nigo bakogokigwa mono gokwana oborimo; nigo bagosesenia nebikoba biabo bosa, korende ase chinkoro chiabo ime nigo bakoragereria.
english: They fully intend to topple him from his lofty place; they take delight in lies. With their mouths they bless, but in their hearts they curse. Selah

ekegusii: Abwo nigo bagwasamia emenwa yabo bateba: “Ahaa! Ahaa! Ntwayarora namaiso aito.”
english: They gape at me and say, "Aha! Aha! With our own eyes we have seen it."

ekegusii: Nigo bakogesera omonto onde chindagera chie chitugo chiaye, naende basangereria amasabibu agotigwa ase omogondo bw’omokori amabe.
english: They gather fodder in the fields and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.

ekegusii: They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
english: Bakamoa egesamunye gi’enswe gesambire na obooke boke.

ekegusii: Abanto bakamoa chisekeli chie chifeta emerongo etano na ebere korwa ase enyomba ya Baali‐Beriti, na ase chibesa echio akarikera abanto abatantanu batechigeti: nabarabwo bakamotunyana.
english: They gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith, and Abimelech used it to hire reckless adventurers, who became his followers.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagatebia Musa, “Ntwagenda ase ense eria gwatotomete, ntwayenyora ng’a nentenenku ere namabeere na amooke, rora okwama gw’ense eria.
english: They gave Moses this account: "We went into the land to which you sent us, and it does flow with milk and honey! Here is its fruit.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaegwa Kiriati‐Ariba (noro Heburoni), ase ense y’ebitunwa ya Yuda, amo namarisio aetanaineo. (Ariba nigo arenge sokoro y’Anaki.)
english: They gave them Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), with its surrounding pastureland, in the hill country of Judah. (Arba was the forefather of Anak.)

ekegusii: Barabwo bakarua ase emeremo y’enyomba ya Nyasae chitahabu chitalanta chilifu isano ne chidarikoni chilifu ikomi, ne chifeta chitalanta chilifu ikomi, ne chitaai chitalanta chilifu ikomi na isano na isato, na ebioma chitalanta chilifu rigana erimo.
english: They gave toward the work on the temple of God five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze and a hundred thousand talents of iron.

ekegusii: Chinsoko echio nigo chikoa ching’iti chionsi amache chianywa, ne chitigere chi’orosana nigo chikoyanywa, na erang’o yasira.
english: They give water to all the beasts of the field; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

ekegusii: They go from strength to strength, till each appears before God in Zion.
english: Barabwo mbabe bakomenta koba ne chinguru kogenderera botambe, mbarore Nyasae ayobuete chinyasae agwo Sayoni.

ekegusii: Baeteire ase ekiambokero, batoorire agwo Geba babeere aroro ase obotuko obwo; abanto ba Rama babeire nobwoba, na aba Gibea, omochie o Saulo, batamire.
english: They go over the pass, and say, "We will camp overnight at Geba." Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.

ekegusii: Nigo bagotiira gochia Luhiti bakorera; ekero bagotirimboka korwa Horonaimu, eriogi ri’okorera kw’ogosirigwa nigo rikoigugwa.
english: They go up the way to Luhith, weeping bitterly as they go; on the road down to Horonaim anguished cries over the destruction are heard.

ekegusii: Bakaimoka ensa eria eria, bakairana Yerusalemu, bakanyora baria ikomi nomo basangererekanete, na baria abarenge amo nabarabwo,
english: They got up and returned at once to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, assembled together

ekegusii: Bakaimoka bakamosokia isiko y’omochie, bakamoira goika egemi y’egetunwa keria omochie obo oagachire igoro yaye, banyare komoturunkania.
english: They got up, drove him out of the town, and took him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw him down the cliff.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bagotaba‐taba ase omosunte borabu botaiyo, na ogera baong’anya buna omonto otindire.”
english: They grope in darkness with no light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.

ekegusii: Ekero barenge ase chiema chiabo ime nigo bemurunganetie, tibaigwera eriogi ri’Omonene.
english: They grumbled in their tents and did not obey the LORD.

ekegusii: Igo barenge ne chinswe chinsinini nke igo. Gachisesenirie, akabora, “Nechi baterekere”!
english: They had a few small fish as well; he gave thanks for them also and told the disciples to distribute them.

ekegusii: Nchiarenge nomoruoti obo, omomalaika bw’eora y’abakure, erieta riaye ase Ekeibirania n’Abadoni, na ase Ekegiriki Apolioni.
english: They had as king over them the angel of the Abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek, Apollyon.

ekegusii: Ebikuba biabo nigo biaboirie chingobo chi’ebioma, na egeturi gie chimbaba chiabo nigo kiarenge buna egeturi gie chigari chinyinge chie chibarasi chikominyoka gochia ase esegi.
english: They had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the thundering of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.

ekegusii: Naboigo banyorete Isi‐Boseti oraire borere bwaye agwo ase akanyomba g’okorara bakamoika ang’e bakamoita, bakamobutora omotwe bakayoira; erio bakagenda ase obotuko bwonsi goetera ase enchera y’Ekerubo Ekiomo.
english: They had gone into the house while he was lying on the bed in his bedroom. After they stabbed and killed him, they cut off his head. Taking it with them, they traveled all night by way of the Arabah.

ekegusii: Tibarenge konyara korirenda ase engaki eria yachikire, ekiagera abakuani konya tibarechena baisane omobaro oyoganeirie, gose abanto konya tibarasangererekana agwo Yerusalemu.
english: They had not been able to celebrate it at the regular time because not enough priests had consecrated themselves and the people had not assembled in Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Ekero bagendire egeka geke korwa ase omochie, Yusufu agatebia omoteneneri bw’enka yaye. “Imoka, obwatie abanto baria! Ekero orabanyore obaborie: Nase ki mogoakana amabe ase amaya?
english: They had not gone far from the city when Joseph said to his steward, "Go after those men at once, and when you catch up with them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid good with evil?

ekegusii: Ekero babegete abatomwa gati‐gati, bakababoria, “Inwe nase nguru ki, naende nase erieta ria ng’o mogokora aya?”
english: They had Peter and John brought before them and began to question them: "By what power or what name did you do this?"

ekegusii: Erio eriomana rigatuboka ase egati yabo goika bagaatananekana. Barnaba akaira Mariko, akagenda nemeeri gochia Kuporo,
english: They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,

ekegusii: Naende nigo chiarenge nebimincha bire nemeburera buna ebi’ebiuge, na okobua kwabo kw’ogochanda mwanyabanto ase emetienyi etano nigo kwarenge ase ebimincha biabo.
english: They had tails and stings like scorpions, and in their tails they had power to torment people for five months.

ekegusii: Naboigo abarwani baroberetigwe: Omoganda omonene bw’abarwani okabekwa sugusu y’omochie, na abarwani bande bakabekwa koboa bosongo y’omochie. Yoshua akagenda, akabeera gati‐gati ye rikura obotuko boria.
english: They had the soldiers take up their positions-- all those in the camp to the north of the city and the ambush to the west of it. That night Joshua went into the valley.

ekegusii: Amo nabarabwo chigasoa ching’iti chi’orosana echia kera egesaku, ne ching’iti chigotugwa echia kera egesaku, na echikwagura echia kera egesaku, na kera enyoni y’egesaku kende gionsi.
english: They had with them every wild animal according to its kind, all livestock according to their kinds, every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind and every bird according to its kind, everything with wings.

ekegusii: Bagasunyunta etahabu ekaba eng’oo, naende bakayeninta ekaba chiusi chinyerere, bagachisang’ania ne chiusi chi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, ase okoroisia egetambaa buna omoroisia omong’aini aranyare gokeroisia.
english: They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut strands to be worked into the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen-- the work of a skilled craftsman.

ekegusii: Abamura baye bakamorentera ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa, egetari ase egetari, amo nomotwe, na ere akabisambera ase egesasimero.
english: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burned them on the altar.

ekegusii: Nigo bagoturagia amagena ’amarubi na koroisia chiusi chie chinyambobe. Oyo okoria amagena abo nigo agokwa, na ekero rigena erimo ri’ayio riatirwe rirubi nigo rigosoka korwao.
english: They hatch the eggs of vipers and spin a spider's web. Whoever eats their eggs will die, and when one is broken, an adder is hatched.

ekegusii: Barabwo basaririe ase Omonene, na bono tibagenderereti korokwa abana baye; nigo bare abanto b’obosooku, ekegori egesareku, naende egesiru.
english: They have acted corruptly toward him; to their shame they are no longer his children, but a warped and crooked generation.

ekegusii: Tari ayio oka bakorete asende, korende ase rituko erio nigo bakorete Aase aane Aachenu akaba aatachenegeti, naende bagakora Chisabato chiane chikaba echitachenegeti.
english: They have also done this to me: At that same time they defiled my sanctuary and desecrated my Sabbaths.

ekegusii: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and malice. They are gossips,
english: Bagaichorwa ne chingencho chionsi chitari boronge, na obobe, na okogania okobe, na okorengereria okobe, ne ribero, na oboiti, na eriomana, na obong’ainereria, na okogechana. Bakaba abagenkani,

ekegusii: Na barabwo mbatebetigwe ng’a kworokereirie Abayahudi bonsi abamenyete ase egati y’abanto b’Ebisaku ng’a batige Musa, gokobakania tibarokia abana babo, gose tibabwatia chingencho chiaito.
english: They have been informed that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or live according to our customs.

ekegusii: baonchokire bwango, batigire enchera eria nabachigete gotunyana, bekoreire emori eeri y’etahabu. Bayesasimire na koyeruera ekeng’wanso, bagoteba: Abaisraeli aba, eye nero enyasae yaino, eyabang’anyetie korwa ase ense ya Misiri.”
english: They have been quick to turn away from what I commanded them and have made themselves an idol cast in the shape of a calf. They have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and have said, 'These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'

ekegusii: Barabwo baagachire aase aimokererete igoro ase enyasae Baali, erinde bayesambere abana babo abamura babe ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa asere, amang’ana inche ntachigete gose kobatebia, gose amang’ana atana koba ase ebirengererio biane.
english: They have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as offerings to Baal-- something I did not command or mention, nor did it enter my mind.

ekegusii: Barabwo baroisirie aase aimokererete igoro agosasimerwa agwo ase Tofeti, aaria ase Rikura ria mosinto o Hinomu. Agwo basambire abana babo, abamura na abaiseke, nomorero, amang’ana inche ntachigete gose atana koba ase ebirengererio biane.
english: They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire-- something I did not command, nor did it enter my mind.

ekegusii: nebwate amato, korende teri koigwa, gose tebwati omoika bw’okoeyana.
english: they have ears, but cannot hear, nor is there breath in their mouths.

ekegusii: Nebwate amato, korende teri koigwa, nebwate chimioro, korende teri konyonka eigwe rimisu.
english: they have ears, but cannot hear, noses, but they cannot smell;

ekegusii: Baeire chinyoni emebere y’abasomba bao chiyerie, ee, chinyama chi’emebere y’abachenu bao ase ching’iti chi’orosana.
english: They have given the dead bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the air, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth.

ekegusii: “Ee, barabwo nigo batochandete korwa oboke bwaito, korende tibana‐gotobua.
english: they have greatly oppressed me from my youth, but they have not gained the victory over me.

ekegusii: Nebwate amaboko, korende teri kobwata gento, nebwate amagoro, korende teri gotaara; gose tebwati eriogi ri’ogokwana.
english: they have hands, but cannot feel, feet, but they cannot walk; nor can they utter a sound with their throats.

ekegusii: Ase emeyega yabo nigo bakoba bare namakano ao ao, ne chinchigiri, na ebiroria, na edivai, korende tibari korengereria ogokora kw’Omonene, gose tibari korora emeremo y’amaboko aye.
english: They have harps and lyres at their banquets, tambourines and flutes and wine, but they have no regard for the deeds of the LORD, no respect for the work of his hands.

ekegusii: Mbamanyete korwa ase ekero egetambe, na onye barigetie, banyare koorokia buna narenge oyomo bw’ekeombe keria gi’okobetererigwa bokong’u kobwata engencho yaito y’okomoiroka Nyasae, nakio ekeombe ki’Abafarisai.
english: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that according to the strictest sect of our religion, I lived as a Pharisee.

ekegusii: Basirire ekiagera batigire enchera erambogete na kobwatia enchera ya Baalamu, mosinto o Beori, oyobwanchete eng’eria y’ogokora okobe.
english: They have left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakwanire oborimo igoro ase Omonene, batebire, “Omonene tagokora gento kende. Intwe titokorenterwa amabe; titogocherwa korwanigwa nemioro, gose enchara tegocha asetore.
english: They have lied about the LORD; they said, "He will do nothing! No harm will come to us; we will never see sword or famine.

ekegusii: Bono barabwo nao bamenyete, naende bakoagacheire Obomenyo Obochenu ase engencho y’erieta riao, bagoteba:
english: They have lived in it and have built in it a sanctuary for your Name, saying,

ekegusii: Nigo ebwate emenwa, korende teri gokwana, nebwate amaiso, korende teri korora.
english: They have mouths, but cannot speak, eyes, but they cannot see;

ekegusii: Nigo ebwate emenwa, korende teri gokwana, nebwate amaiso, korende teri korora,
english: They have mouths, but cannot speak, eyes, but they cannot see;

ekegusii: Barabwo tibari konyorwa nobokong’u bonde ase obogima bwabo; emebere yabo nigo ere emiya, naende emenoru.
english: They have no struggles; their bodies are healthy and strong.

ekegusii: Abwo nigo bare nokorengereria okomo ase okoa eng’iti eria chinguru chiabo na okobua kwabo.
english: They have one purpose and will give their power and authority to the beast.

ekegusii: Bairire chibesa chionsi chianyorekanete ase enyomba y’Omonene, na bachibekire ase amaboko ’abateneneri b’emeremo amo nabakori emeremo.”
english: They have paid out the money that was in the temple of the LORD and have entrusted it to the supervisors and workers."

ekegusii: Baiteire amanyinga abo buna amache ase chinsemo chionsi chia Yerusalemu, abakobatindeka baborire.
english: They have poured out blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury the dead.

ekegusii: Abwo baonchokire bairaneire ebibe bie chisokoro chiabo, chiria chiangete koigwera amang’ana aane. Bairaneire gosasima chinyasae ching’ao na gochikorera. Ee, Abaisraeli amo n’Abayuda basaririe okobwatana kw’ogotianania nakorete ne chisokoro chiabo.
english: They have returned to the sins of their forefathers, who refused to listen to my words. They have followed other gods to serve them. Both the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their forefathers.

ekegusii: Besaririe kegima buna yabete ase amatuko aria a kare agwo Gibea. Omonene nainyorete ebibe biabo, abae egesusuro.
english: They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their wickedness and punish them for their sins.

ekegusii: Barabwo banyuomire abaiseke b’abanto abwo, naende banyuomeirie abamura babo abaiseke b’abanto abwo. Bono egesaku eke egechenu giochoganire nabanto be chinse echi. Abagambi na abatang’ani b’abanto nabwo bare abe ritang’ani ase ogokora okwo kw’ogotegenwa.”
english: They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, and have mingled the holy race with the peoples around them. And the leaders and officials have led the way in this unfaithfulness."

ekegusii: Okororekana kwabo nigo konga buna ogwe chibarasi; nigo chikominyoka buna chibarasi chi’okorwana esegi.
english: They have the appearance of horses; they gallop along like cavalry.

ekegusii: batugutire chinyasae chi’abanto abwo ase omorero, ekiagera chirochio tichiri Nyasae, korende nemeremo y’amaboko ’abanto, chiroisirie korwa ase emete na amagena, na ase ayio chigasarigwa.
english: They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods but only wood and stone, fashioned by human hands.

ekegusii: batugutire chinyasae chi’abanto abwo ase omorero, ekiagera chirochio tichiri Nyasae, korende nemeremo y’amaboko ’abanto, chiroisirie korwa ase emete na amagena; ase ayio chigasirigwa.
english: They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods but only wood and stone, fashioned by men's hands.

ekegusii: Barabwo babeire kirori ase ekanisa igoro y’obwanchani bwao. Nokore buya korabakonye ase orogendo rwabo, buna egwenerete ase okomokorera Nyasae.
english: They have told the church about your love. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.

ekegusii: Bono bang’etananire ase chinsemo chionsi; banaaririe, erinde bambwate na konyiyeria inse.
english: They have tracked me down, they now surround me, with eyes alert, to throw me to the ground.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakaba bagokonya Daudi korwania ebiombe bi’abasakori. Abwo bonsi nigo barenge abanto chituoni, bakaba abatang’ani b’abarwani esegi.
english: They helped David against raiding bands, for all of them were brave warriors, and they were commanders in his army.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakarenta abasemia baare goakanerwa, nabwo bakaba bakorua ogosemia okobe gosaria emeroberio yabo, bakaba bagokora igo korwa amatuko ’okogamba gwa Koresi, omoruoti bw’Abaayemi, goikera ay’okogamba kwa Dario, omoruoti bw’Abaayemi.
english: They hired counselors to work against them and frustrate their plans during the entire reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia.

ekegusii: Bagasaba chigari chilifu emerongo etato na ibere (32,000) amo nomoruoti o Maaka na abarwani baye b’esegi. Barabwo bagacha, bagatoora bosio bwa Medeba. Abaamoni bagasangererigwa korwa ase emechie yabo, bagacha korwana esegi.
english: They hired thirty-two thousand chariots and charioteers, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba, while the Ammonites were mustered from their towns and moved out for battle.

ekegusii: Na barabwo bagatosika ase ogosika okonene; naende ekero twachia gosoa emeeri bagatoa ebinto biria twaremeire.
english: They honored us in many ways and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.

ekegusii: Ase obwango obwo kera omonto akarusia eanga yaye akayiaara ase ebiriinero, ayetache. Erio bakabugia ebitureri biabo, bakararia, “Yehu nere omoruoti!”
english: They hurried and took their cloaks and spread them under him on the bare steps. Then they blew the trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"

ekegusii: Kera egari yarenge korentwa korwa Misiri nigo yarenge goakanerwa rigori rie chisekeli chie chifeta amagana atano na rimo, na ebarasi nigo yarenge goakanerwa chisekeli rigana erimo, na emerongo etano. Na goetera ase abaonchoreria b’omoruoti abaruoti bonsi b’Abahiti na ab’Abasiiria nigo barenge kogora chigari ne chibarasi.
english: They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and of the Arameans.

ekegusii: Bakarenta chigari korwa Misiri ase ogoakanera kera eyemo chisekeli amagana atano na rimo chie chifeta, na ebarasi eyemo nigo yare goakanerwa chisekeli rigana erimo, na emerongo etano; boigo abaruoti bonsi b’Abahiti na ab’Abasiiria nigo barenge kogora chigari ne chibarasi goetera ase abaonchoreria ba Sulemani.
english: They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and of the Arameans.

ekegusii: Abakuani nigo barigetwe amo ne chiamate chiabo chionsi, abana babo abake, na abakungu babo, na abana babo abamura na abaiseke, ekiagera nigo baganeirie koba abachenegete na babe bagokora emeremo yabo ase obwegenwa.
english: They included all the little ones, the wives, and the sons and daughters of the whole community listed in these genealogical records. For they were faithful in consecrating themselves.

ekegusii: Agasoyia emiaro eria ase chibonyi chire chinsemo chi’egesasimero, erinde kenyare kobogorerigwa. Agakeagacha ne chibao, akagetiga giasaime.
english: They inserted the poles into the rings so they would be on the sides of the altar for carrying it. They made it hollow, out of boards.

ekegusii: Chingige echio chigacha igoro y’ense yonsi ya Misiri, chikagwa chinsemo chionsi chi’aroro. Chingige chinyinge buna echio chitana gocha ase amatuko aetire, gose tichigochi‐gocha naende nonya ng’ake.
english: they invaded all Egypt and settled down in every area of the country in great numbers. Never before had there been such a plague of locusts, nor will there ever be again.

ekegusii: Bakabwatania amarondia atano amo, akaba rirondia erimo, naende atano na rimo akaba rirondia erimo.
english: They joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another set.

ekegusii: Bakabwatania ebitambaa bitano amo, bikaba rirondia erimo. Naboigo nebitambaa binde bitano.
english: They joined five of the curtains together and did the same with the other five.

ekegusii: Rora, abanto nigo bakomboria: “Ng’ai ring’ana ri’Omonene rire? Tiga riikeranigwe.”
english: They keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it now be fulfilled!"

ekegusii: Abwo nigo bagendererete gotebia abanto baria bachayete ring’ana riane: Omonene otebire ng’a namonyore omorembe. Naende batebia baria bakobwatia obomwenu bwe chinkoro chiabo: Amabe tagocha asemore.”
english: They keep saying to those who despise me, 'The LORD says: You will have peace.' And to all who follow the stubbornness of their hearts they say, 'No harm will come to you.'

ekegusii: They kept asking, "What does he mean by 'a little while'? We don't understand what he is saying."
english: Nabo bagateba, “Ing’ana ki eri agoteba, ng’a nkere ekero egeke? Titomanyeti eri agokwana.”

ekegusii: Nabo bakarigia Yeso, bagatebania barabwo ase barabwo, bagotenena ase Hekalu, “Naki moroche? Tagocha‐gocha ase rituko rinene nonya ng’ake?”
english: They kept looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple area they asked one another, "What do you think? Isn't he coming to the Feast at all?"

ekegusii: Bakabwata ring’ana riria, bakaborania barabwo ase barabwo, ng’a okoboka korwa ase abakure, engencho yaye ninki.
english: They kept the matter to themselves, discussing what "rising from the dead" meant.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagasiria abanto abatigari b’Abaameleki, naende bakamenya aroro, nao bare goika rero iga.
english: They killed the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

ekegusii: Bagaita abana ba Zedekia agwo ase amaiso aye, erio bakamokonora amaiso, bakamosiba ne chingatare, bakamoira Babeli.
english: They killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon.

ekegusii: Abanto bagokora ayio nabariri, tibamanyeti kende. Amaiso abo aukoire, tibakonyara korora, na ebirengererio biabo biasarigwe, tibakonyara komanya.
english: They know nothing, they understand nothing; their eyes are plastered over so they cannot see, and their minds closed so they cannot understand.

ekegusii: They laughed at him, knowing that she was dead.
english: Bakamosekerera, bamanyete ng’a okure.

ekegusii: They left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
english: Bakarua Aburona, bakagenda bagaika Esioni‐Geberi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Alimoni‐Dibulataimu, bagaika ebitunwa bi’Abarimu kororia Nebo bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo.

ekegusii: Bakarua Alusi, bakagenda bagaika Refidimu, aase abanto batanyorete amache bakonywa, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.

ekegusii: They left and found things just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover.
english: Bakagenda, bakanyora buna abatebetie, bakaarigania Epasaka.

ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakagenda gochia ase ense eria y’ebitunwa, bagaika ase ense omweya y’Esikoli, bakaroota ense eria.
english: They left and went up into the hill country, and came to the Valley of Eshcol and explored it.

ekegusii: They left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.
english: Bakarua Bene‐Yakani, bakagenda bagaika Hori‐Hagidigadi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
english: Bakarua Diboni‐Gadi, bakagenda bagaika Alimoni‐Dibulataimu, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
english: Bakarua Dofuka, bakagenda bagaika Alusi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
english: Bakarua Elimu, bakagenda bagaika ang’e n’Enyancha Embariri, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Etham, turned back to Pi Hahiroth, to the east of Baal Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
english: Bakarua Etamu, bakaonchoka bakairana bagaika Pi‐Hahiroti, moocha ya Baali‐Sefoni, bagatoora ang’e na Migidoli.

ekegusii: They left Ezion Geber and camped at Kadesh, in the Desert of Zin.
english: Bakarua Esioni‐Geberi, bakagenda bagaika erooro ya Sini (nao Kadeshi), bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
english: Bakarua Harada, bakagenda bagaika Makeloti, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
english: Bakarua Hasimona, bakagenda bagaika Moseroti, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Haseroti, bakagenda bagaika Ritima, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

ekegusii: They left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
english: Bakarua Hori‐Hagidigadi, bakagenda bagaika Yotibata, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.
english: Bakarua agwo Iyumu, bakagenda bagaika Didoni‐Gadi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
english: Bakarua Yotibata, bakagenda bagaika Aburona, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Kadeshi, bakagenda bagaika egetunwa kia Hori, ang’e norobebe rw’ense ya Edomu, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.

ekegusii: They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
english: Bakarua Kehelata, bakagenda bagaika egetunwa gia Seferi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Kibiroti‐Hatawa, bakagenda bagaika Haseroti, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

ekegusii: They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
english: Bakarua Libuna, bakagenda bagaika Risa, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
english: Bakarua Makeloti bakagenda bagaika Tahati, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Mara, bakagenda bagaika Elimu, aase chinsoko chi’amache ikomi na ibere chiarenge amo nemekendo emerongo etano na ebere, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Marah and went to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

ekegusii: They left Mithcah and camped at Hashmonah.
english: Bakarua Mitika, bakagenda bagaika Hasimona, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
english: Bakarua Moseroti, bakagenda bagaika Bene‐Yakani, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
english: Abaisraeli bakarua egetunwa keria kia Hori, bakagenda bagaika Salimona bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
english: Bakarua egetunwa gia Seferi, bakagenda bagaika Harada, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Oboti, bakagenda bagaika Iye‐Abarimu, bagatoora aroro ase orobebe rwa Moabu.
english: They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab.

ekegusii: Bakarua agwo Pi‐Hahiroti, bakagenda bagaeta egati y’Enyancha Embariri gochia erooro. Erio bakagenda orogendo rw’amatuko atato ase erooro y’Etamu, bagatoora agwo Mara.
english: They left Pi Hahiroth and passed through the sea into the desert, and when they had traveled for three days in the Desert of Etham, they camped at Marah.

ekegusii: They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
english: Bakarua Punoni, bakagenda bagaika Oboti, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Rephidim and camped in the Desert of Sinai.
english: Bakarua Refidimu, bakagenda bagaika erooro ya Sinai, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
english: Bakarua Rimoni‐Peresi, bakagenda bagaika Libuna, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
english: Bakarua Risa, bakagenda bagaika Kehelata, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.
english: Bakarua Ritima, bakagenda bagaika Rimoni‐Peresi, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua Sukoti, bakagenda Etamu, ase ensinyo y’erooro, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the desert.

ekegusii: They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
english: Bakarua Tahati, bakagenda bagaika Tera, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left Terah and camped at Mithcah.
english: Bakarua Tera, bakagenda bagaika Mitika, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left that place and passed through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,
english: Bakarua aria, bagaeta gati‐gati ya Galili; Yeso tancha omonto amanye,

ekegusii: They left the Desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
english: Bakarua erooro ya Sini, bakagenda bagaika Dofuka, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: They left the Desert of Sinai and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
english: Bakarua erooro ya Sinai, bakagenda bagaika Kibiroti‐Hatawa, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Bakarua ebitunwa bi’Abarimu, bakagenda bagaika ase ebirubo ebiomo bia Moabu, ang’e na Yorodan, kororia Yeriko, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.

ekegusii: Bakarua aase aria bagaika erooro ya Sini, bagatoora aroro.
english: They left the Red Sea and camped in the Desert of Sin.

ekegusii: bakagenda are ake, bagatebania, bakabora, “Omonto oyo takoreti ring’ana rigwenerete ogokwa gose ogosibwa.”
english: They left the room, and while talking with one another, they said, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."

ekegusii: They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
english: Bakarua Salimona, bakagenda bagaika Punoni, bagatoora aroro.

ekegusii: Mbarabare ase kera egesasimero barabwo nigo bakorara inse igoro ye chianga chikobekwa kebwaterero. Ase enyomba y’enyasae yabo banywa edivai y’abwo bagambetigwe bakarusigwa chibesa.
english: They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge. In the house of their god they drink wine taken as fines.

ekegusii: Erio bayeimokia bayebeka ase amareko abo, bayebogoria, bayetereka aase aye, yabeera aroro; tekonyara gotigera korwa aase agwo. Omonto naisa korera ase enyasae eria, ero tekonyara komoigwa gose komotooria korwa ase emechando yaye.
english: They lift it to their shoulders and carry it; they set it up in its place, and there it stands. From that spot it cannot move. Though one cries out to it, it does not answer; it cannot save him from his troubles.

ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bamenyete agwo Beeri‐Seba, na Molada, na Hasari‐Suali;
english: They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,

ekegusii: they loaded their grain on their donkeys and left.
english: Erio bakaberekia chitigere chiabo endagera, bakagenda.

ekegusii: Kera endagera ekaba engundo asebare, bakaba ang’e gosoa ase ebiita bi’amakweri.
english: They loathed all food and drew near the gates of death.

ekegusii: Korende ekero bachia korigia komobwata, bakairoka emeganda, ekiagera abanto konya banchire ng’a nomobani are.
english: They looked for a way to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowd because the people held that he was a prophet.

ekegusii: Naende nigo banchete aase e ritang’ani ase emeyega, na goikaransa aase e ritang’ani ase chisinagogi,
english: they love the place of honor at banquets and the most important seats in the synagogues;

ekegusii: na gokwanigwa ase chichiiro, na korokwa omworokia nabanto.
english: they love to be greeted in the marketplaces and to have men call them 'Rabbi.'

ekegusii: Agakora egechungi gi’etaai, agakebeka korwa inse y’orosingo, kegaika gochia igoro gati gati y’egesasimero.
english: They made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, to be under its ledge, halfway up the altar.

ekegusii: Ase chikoona inye chi’egesasimero akaroisia emegwekano ene ye chingunchara, akayeroisia ekaba egento ekemo negesasimero, akaooma gionsi netaai.
english: They made a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar were of one piece, and they overlaid the altar with bronze.

ekegusii: Akaroisia ebikorero bionsi bi’egesasimero nabio ebi: Chindogio chi’okobuucha riibu, na ebichiko, na ebitaabo, ne chigami, ne chindogio chi’okorenta omorero. Ebinto ebi bionsi akabiroisia korwa ase chitaai.
english: They made all its utensils of bronze-- its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.

ekegusii: Chibao chiao chionsi nigo chiaroisetigwe korwa ase emete ekorokwa emebunduki ya Seniri, abanto bakarenta emecharake korwa Lebanoni, bagakoroiseria omoenga.
english: They made all your timbers of pine trees from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.

ekegusii: Erio bakaroisia amarondia ikomi na rimo ay’amanya e chigoree, akaba eema y’ogotuba Obomenyo boria.
english: They made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle-- eleven altogether.

ekegusii: Naende bagakora ebigobanio emerongo etano bie chitaai ase okobwaterania amarondia ayio abere, abe eema engima.
english: They made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together as a unit.

ekegusii: Naende bakabaacha chisiiro inye chi’emekonge, bagachiooma netahabu, na ebigobanio biaye bie chitahabu. Bagakora chinterekerero inye korwa ase efeta enyititoire.
english: They made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold. They made gold hooks for them and cast their four silver bases.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakagera Omonene akaba ne risemi, ekiagera basasimete chinyasae chingeni, bakagera akaba nendamwamu enene, ekiagera akorete okogechia.
english: They made him jealous with their foreign gods and angered him with their detestable idols.

ekegusii: Naende akaroisia chitaya chiaye isano na ibere, na ebinachi, ne chindogio chiaye chie chitahabu chichenire.
english: They made its seven lamps, as well as its wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold.

ekegusii: Bagerire nabeire ne risemi ase engencho y’egetari Nyasae, nagechigwe ase emegwekano yabo ere bosa, eyio bagosasima. Ase ayio inche ninseegete abanto abachorochombu, erinde babagechie nimbatige bagechigwe ase okobarentera egesaku ekeriri.
english: They made me jealous by what is no god and angered me with their worthless idols. I will make them envious by those who are not a people; I will make them angry by a nation that has no understanding.

ekegusii: Bagakora emegwekano y’amatunda e rikomomanga korwa ase chiusi chi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, bakayebeka ase omoringero o inse.
english: They made pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the hem of the robe.

ekegusii: Bakaroisia ebitwanga bi’amareko bi’egesibao keria, bakabibwatania nakerokio, nyuma na bosio; chinsinyo chiaye ibere ibere chikabwatanigwa amo.
english: They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, which were attached to two of its corners, so it could be fastened.

ekegusii: Korende ase ensemo ya nyuma y’Obomenyo, eyerochie bosongo, bakaroisia chibao isano nemo.
english: They made six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle,

ekegusii: Akaroisia egesasimero gie chibao chi’emekonge ase ubani erasamberwe. Obotambe bwaye nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo gi’okoboko okomo, na obotambe bwaye gochia igoro amaboko abere. Emegwekano ye chingunchara ekaroisigwa ekaba egento ekemo negesasimero.
english: They made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high--its horns of one piece with it.

ekegusii: Akaroisia egetuba amo nenterekerero yaye korwa ase ebirore bie chitaai bi’abakungu baare gokorera ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano.
english: They made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

ekegusii: Bakabaacha omoriibo o gati‐gati omogima, ase okoriiba chibao korwa ensinyo eyemo goika eyende.
english: They made the center crossbar so that it extended from end to end at the middle of the frames.

ekegusii: They made the curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
english: Bakaroisia etoto ye chiusi chi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, amo ne chiusi chi’egatani engiya chisisire. Omoroisia omong’aini akayeroisia ekaba emegwekano y’abakerubi.

ekegusii: Bagakora egesibao ki’obokuani korwa ase chiusi chi’etahabu, na echi’amarionya chire buru, ne chimonyinga, ne chimbariri, amo nechi’egatani engiya chisisire.
english: They made the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.

ekegusii: Ekebekerero keria gie chitaya amo nebikorero biaye bionsi bikaroisigwa korwa ase chitahabu chichenire chi’ekerengo gie chikiro emerongo etano.
english: They made the lampstand and all its accessories from one talent of pure gold.

ekegusii: They made the lampstand of pure gold and hammered it out, base and shaft; its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms were of one piece with it.
english: Akaroisia ekebekerero gie chitaya gi’etahabu echenire esunyuntire. Akayeroisia nenterekerero amo ne ritina, na emegwekano y’amamumu na ebisicha; bionsi bikaroisigwa bikaba egento ekemo.

ekegusii: Bagatura ebao y’etahabu echenire, na buna omonto akomang’a ekemanyererio, bakamang’a amang’ana aya: “Achenirwe ase Omonene”.
english: They made the plate, the sacred diadem, out of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.

ekegusii: Akabaacha emiaro eria korwa ase emekonge, akayeooma netaai.
english: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.

ekegusii: Na emiaro eria akabaacha korwa ase emekonge, akayeooma netahabu.
english: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

ekegusii: Bagakora eganchwa korwa ase egetambaa keroisirie ne chiusi chiburu chioka.
english: They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth-- the work of a weaver--

ekegusii: Akaroisia emesa ye chibao chi’emekonge. Obotambe bwaye nigo bwarenge obw’ekerengo ki’amaboko abere, na obogare bwaye okoboko okomo na obotambe bwaye gochia igoro okoboko okomo na ekeng’ese.
english: They made the table of acacia wood-- two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

ekegusii: Bagakong’ia chinkoro chiabo pa buna rigena rikorokwa elimasi ng’a tibabaisa koigwera amachiko na amang’ana ’Omonene bw’Emeganda atomete n’Omoika oye goetera ase ababani ba kare. Ase engencho eyio Omonene bw’Emeganda akaba nendamwamu enene.
english: They made their hearts as hard as flint and would not listen to the law or to the words that the LORD Almighty had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So the LORD Almighty was very angry.

ekegusii: y’ogotiringa esike na gokora amatabori, na emeremo ende ao ao ase emegondo. Ase emeremo ende yonsi Abaisraeli baare gokora nigo baare gokorigwa ase obotindi.
english: They made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar and with all kinds of work in the fields; in all their hard labor the Egyptians used them ruthlessly.

ekegusii: Bakaroisia chibao emerongo ebere ase ensemo ya irianyi.
english: They made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle

ekegusii: Bagakora na ebikonde bibere bie chitahabu, ne chibonyi ibere chie chitahabu, na bakabeka chibonyi echi ibere ase emego ebere ya igoro y’egesembe keria.
english: They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to two of the corners of the breastpiece.

ekegusii: Bagakora chibonyi ibere chie chitahabu bagachibeka ase egesembe keria, ase emego ebere ya inse korwa nyuma, echigete egesibao.
english: They made two gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod.

ekegusii: Agakora chibonyi ibere chie chitahabu, agachibeka inse y’omong’ororia ase chinsemo ibere. Ase chibonyi echio emiaro egasoigwa, erinde egesasimero kenyare kobogorerigwa.
english: They made two gold rings below the molding-- two on opposite sides-- to hold the poles used to carry it.

ekegusii: Naende bakaroisia chibao chi’emekonge ase Obomenyo, bagachitenenia.
english: They made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.

ekegusii: Nigo bagokwana amang’ana atari nengencho, naende betiania ase oborimo ekero bagokora okobwatana kw’ogotianania; ase igo ekina nigo gekobachera buna ekemeri kere nobosongo ase emetaro ya mogondo.
english: They make many promises, take false oaths and make agreements; therefore lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds in a plowed field.

ekegusii: Chimeme chiabo nigo chire chinyoge buna echie ching’iti chingenda inse; obosongo bw’amarubi nigo bore ase ebikoba bi’emenwa yabo.
english: They make their tongues as sharp as a serpent's; the poison of vipers is on their lips. Selah

ekegusii: Abwo bagatiira igoro ase obogare bw’ense, bakanaaria obomenyo bw’abachenu, na omochie oria bwanchire, korende omorero ogaika korwa igoro, okabaria.
english: They marched across the breadth of the earth and surrounded the camp of God's people, the city he loves. But fire came down from heaven and devoured them.

ekegusii: Barabwo bakanyuoma abaiseke b’Abamoabu; oyomo nigo are korokwa Oripa na oyonde Rutu. Nyuma kabamenyire aroro koreng’ana emiaka ikomi,
english: They married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. After they had lived there about ten years,

ekegusii: Barabwo bagasoka ase chiamate chi’egesaku kia Manase, mosinto o Yusufu. Omwando obo ogitigara ore ase egesaku ki’eamate yabo.
english: They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in their father's clan and tribe.

ekegusii: they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.
english: chirochio chikanyora amarieme bosio bw’ebite ebio, chikabiara chimanwa chire chimarera, ne chinkanga, ne chinkororo.

ekegusii: Barabwo mbabe ne ribaga ri’ogokonya baria bamwabo bare abakoreri ase Eema y’Omosangererekano, korende tibabaisa gokora emeremo eyio abanyene. Naboigo oraroberie Abalawi ase emeremo yabo.”
english: They may assist their brothers in performing their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves must not do the work. This, then, is how you are to assign the responsibilities of the Levites."

ekegusii: Barabwo tiga bandagererie, korende aye onsesenie. Tiga abwo bagonkorera bobe barore obosooku, korende inche, omosomba oo, imbe nomogoko.
english: They may curse, but you will bless; when they attack they will be put to shame, but your servant will rejoice.

ekegusii: Nabo baranyare gokora emeremo ase enyomba yane enchenu, naende bagenderere korenda ebiita bi’enyomba yane na gokora emeremo ende ase enyomba eyio; mbabe bakonyenya ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa, na ebing’wanso binde ase engencho y’abanto, mbabe bagotenena ase amasio abo kobakorera.
english: They may serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the temple and serving in it; they may slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before the people and serve them.

ekegusii: Nigo barenge gokora obokoreri bwabo bw’amatera agwo ase Eema y’Omosangererekano goika engaki eria Sulemani aagachete enyomba y’Omonene agwo Yerusalemu; barabwo bagakora emeremo yabo ase omoroberio ochikire.
english: They ministered with music before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem. They performed their duties according to the regulations laid down for them.

ekegusii: Bakabaacha amagena e rigori rinene akorokwa oiniki, bakayabeka ase ebikonde bie chitahabu; na buna omoroisia omong’aini aranyare komanya komang’era ebimanyererio, bakamang’era amarieta ’abamura ba Israeli.
english: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings and engraved them like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.

ekegusii: Emerindo eyio ekaimokerera igoro, naende ekairana inse, na ase ayio abanto bakerusia moyo ase omoichano.
english: They mounted up to the heavens and went down to the depths; in their peril their courage melted away.

ekegusii: Bakarera na kweumia, na kweng’ata goika mogoroba ase engencho ya Saulo na Yonathani, omwana oye, na ase engencho y’abanto b’Omonene na ey’Abaisraeli, ekiagera barabwo konya baitirwe nemioro.
english: They mourned and wept and fasted till evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the army of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

ekegusii: Bakarusia Esanduku eria ya Nyasae korwa ase enyomba y’Abinadabu, bakayebeka igoro ase egari enyia. Usa na Ahiyo nabwo barenge koraa egari eria.
english: They moved the ark of God from Abinadab's house on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding it.

ekegusii: Abakuani mbabe abachenu asende inche Nyasae obo, na tibarentera erieta riane obosooku, ekiagera nabwo bakorua okoruegwa kw’endagera kogosambwa nomorero asende inche Omonene. Ase ayio goika babe abachenu.
english: They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God. Because they present the offerings made to the LORD by fire, the food of their God, they are to be holy.

ekegusii: Abwo mbagwenerete bakirigwe, ekiagera nkoonchorana bare abanto be chinyomba chingima ase okworokereria ayatagwenereti, na igo bakorigia okonyora kw’oborianania.
english: They must be silenced, because they are ruining whole households by teaching things they ought not to teach-- and that for the sake of dishonest gain.

ekegusii: Barabwo boigo barengwe ritang’ani: onye bakonyorekana ng’a tibari ne chingencho chimbe, erio baegwe emeremo y’obokonyi ase ekanisa.
english: They must first be tested; and then if there is nothing against them, let them serve as deacons.

ekegusii: Mbagwenerete babwate obobisi bw’okwegena ase chinkoro chitakobagambia.
english: They must keep hold of the deep truths of the faith with a clear conscience.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli tibabaisa konyenyera ebing’wanso biabo isiko aande na kobirua ase ebirecha, na igo babe abatari abegenwa asende. Oyio nobe omoroberio ochikire oragenderere botambe, ebiaare ase ebiaare.
english: They must no longer offer any of their sacrifices to the goat idols to whom they prostitute themselves. This is to be a lasting ordinance for them and for the generations to come.'

ekegusii: Tebaisa gotigaria nonya nensinini ye chinyama echio goika rituko ria kabere, gose tabuna riuga nonya nerimo ri’emanwa eria. Narende rituko riria rinene ri’Epasaka koreng’ana nemeroberio eria yachigetwe.
