english: We demolish arguments and every pretension that sets itself up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

ekegusii: Naki titokobwatia emegano yarengereretigwe ne chisemi chi’obong’ainereria, ekero twabamanyetie okobua kw’Omonene oito Yeso Kristo na ogocha kwaye, korende intwe abanyene nigo twarenge abarori b’obonene bwaye.
english: We did not follow cleverly invented stories when we told you about the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

ekegusii: Korende titwebegete inse asebare nonya nensa eyemo, erinde ekeene gi’enchili kegenderere amo nainwe.
english: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

ekegusii: Tari ng’a eyio tiyatotungetie, korende igo twekorete abanyene koba ekiorokererio ekiya asemore, erinde motwege.
english: We did this, not because we do not have the right to such help, but in order to make ourselves a model for you to follow.

ekegusii: Gaki titori noboremu kwebara amo nabarabwo abare gwetogia abanyene, gose kwereng’ania nabarabwo. Korende barabwo, ekero bakwerenga abanyene barabwo ase barabwo, na kwereng’ania barabwo ase barabwo, tibari nobong’aini.
english: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are not wise.

ekegusii: Naki baminto, nigo twanchete momanye amang’ana ’emechando eria yatonyorete Asia. Chigurube chiria nigo chiaetanetie chinguru chiaito, goika tokerusia moyo koba moyo.
english: We do not want you to be uninformed, brothers, about the hardships we suffered in the province of Asia. We were under great pressure, far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

ekegusii: Timoba aboro, korende mobe abegi b’abaraire ayabarieretwe chiira, buna omwando, goetera ase okwegena na oboremereria.
english: We do not want you to become lazy, but to imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.

ekegusii: Korende obong’aini mbore togoteba ase egati y’abaikeranu, na borobwo tibori obong’aini bw’ense eye, gose obw’abagambi b’ense eye abagendererete gochia gosira,
english: We do, however, speak a message of wisdom among the mature, but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

ekegusii: Taibo, intwe abasomba bao titware gokora bo. Inee! Chibesa chiria twanyorete igoro y’endagera ase chigunia chiaito ime, titwagochiiraneria naende korwa ase ense ya Kanani? Naki tware gokora toibe efeta gose etahabu korwa ase enyomba y’omonene oo?
english: We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found inside the mouths of our sacks. So why would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?

ekegusii: We found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, went on board and set sail.
english: Tokanyora emeeri eyeranyare kwamboka goika Foiniki, tokariina emeeri eria, tokagenda.

ekegusii: Nigo tokonyora endagera yaito ase okobeka obogima bwaito ase emechando, ekiagera emioro nere ase erooro.
english: We get our bread at the risk of our lives because of the sword in the desert.

ekegusii: Korende, buna momanyete, gatwaikire gochandwa na gochaywa ritang’ani ase Filipi, tokaremigwa na Nyasae oito gokwana enchili ya Nyasae asemore, ase okoumerana nokoamererania okonene mono.
english: We had previously suffered and been insulted in Philippi, as you know, but with the help of our God we dared to tell you his gospel in spite of strong opposition.

ekegusii: Intwe ntobwate omoiseke ominto ore omoke, korende taracha chimbeere; ekero engaki yaye erache akorigigwa anyuomwe, ninki torakorere omoiseke oyio ominto?
english: We have a young sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister for the day she is spoken for?

ekegusii: Twakorire ogosaria okobe mono asore, twatigire kobwata amachiko na emeroberio echikire, ebio gwachigete Musa, omosomba oo.
english: We have acted very wickedly toward you. We have not obeyed the commands, decrees and laws you gave your servant Moses.

ekegusii: Naende ntwarentana chibesa chinde, echi togocha kogora endagera. Titomanyeti gose ning’o ochibegete ase chigunia chiaito ime.”
english: We have also brought additional silver with us to buy food. We don't know who put our silver in our sacks."

ekegusii: Ntore negesasimero aase baria bagokorera Eema batari ne ribaga koria ebinto bikoruegwa aroro.
english: We have an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no right to eat.

ekegusii: Twabeire buna chintakana, chitari nabaise, abababa nigo banga buna ababoraka.
english: We have become orphans and fatherless, our mothers like widows.

ekegusii: Obonyansi obwomo na endagera ende ye chitigere ntobwate. Naboigo ntobwate omogati na edivai bitoisaine inche na omokungu oyo, omosomba oo, na omosae oyo ore amo naintwe, abasomba bao. Titoremeiri gento kende gionsi.”
english: We have both straw and fodder for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves your servants-- me, your maidservant, and the young man with us. We don't need anything."

ekegusii: Naki twabeire ababwatani na Kristo, gatorabwate bokong’u ogosemeria gwaito kwe ritang’ani goika omoerio.
english: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly till the end the confidence we had at first.

ekegusii: Ase Omonene ntore nogosemeria igoro yaino, ng’a ngokora more ayatwabachigete, naende mogenderere koyakora.
english: We have confidence in the Lord that you are doing and will continue to do the things we command.

ekegusii: Nigo tore nebiegwa ao ao koreng’ana ase obuya twaeirwe; onye nobobani tobane koreng’ana ase okwegena gwaito;
english: We have different gifts, according to the grace given us. If a man's gift is prophesying, let him use it in proportion to his faith.

ekegusii: We have endured much ridicule from the proud, much contempt from the arrogant.
english: Twaichoirwe necheche y’abwo beisanekerete, na ogochaywa kw’abamwenu.

ekegusii: Emioyo yaito yatoorekire buna enyoni egotooreka korwa ase egesugunia ki’omotegi. Egesugunia kiabutokire, naintwe twaminchoirie na gotama.
english: We have escaped like a bird out of the fowler's snare; the snare has been broken, and we have escaped.

ekegusii: Twaigure buna Omonene akamogetie amache ’Enyancha Embariri bosio bwaino, ekero mware kong’anya korwa Misiri, naende buna mwasiretie kegima Sihoni na Ogi, abaruoti baria babere b’Abaamori, ng’umbu ya Yorodan.
english: We have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed.

ekegusii: Twaigure buna Abamoabu bare abetogia, barabwo nigo bare aberori mono, na abamwenu, na abaenenu, na abanyandamwamu, korende ogwetogia kwabo nigo kore okw’obong’ainereria.
english: We have heard of Moab's pride-- her overweening pride and conceit, her pride and her insolence-- but her boasts are empty.

ekegusii: Twaigure amang’ana igoro y’esegi eyio, amaboko aito aborirwe chinguru; twasoirwe nomoondoko, na obororo buna obw’omokungu okobina aibore bwatosoire.
english: We have heard reports about them, and our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us, pain like that of a woman in labor.

ekegusii: Twaigure ng’a abanto barure aa asetore ababachandire ase amang’ana abo na koonchorana emioyo yaino, na intwe titwabachigete ng’a bakore bo.
english: We have heard that some went out from us without our authorization and disturbed you, troubling your minds by what they said.

ekegusii: Intwe twabeire tokoigwera na kogenderera komenya ase chiema. Twakorire amang’ana onsi aya Yonadabu, sokoro yaito, atochigete.
english: We have lived in tents and have fully obeyed everything our forefather Jonadab commanded us.

ekegusii: Igoro yaye ntore namang’ana amange tware gokwana korende naakong’u koyorokereria, ekiagera mwabeire aboro ase okoigwa.
english: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain because you are slow to learn.

ekegusii: Titwaigwerete abasomba bao ababani, baria barenge gokwana ase erieta riao ase abaruoti baito, na abanene baito, ne chisokoro chiaito, na ase abanto bonsi b’ense eye.
english: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

ekegusii: Titwaigwerete eriogi riao aye Omonene, Nyasae oito, ase okobwatia amachiko ao, ayio gwatochigete goetera ase abasomba bao ababani.
english: we have not obeyed the LORD our God or kept the laws he gave us through his servants the prophets.

ekegusii: Na intwe titwanyorete omoika bw’ense eye, korende Omoika orwete ase Nyasae, erinde tonyare komanya ebiegwa ebitwaeirwe na Nyasae.
english: We have not received the spirit of the world but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

ekegusii: Ase ayio intwe na abakungu baito, na abana baito, abamura na abaiseke, twabeire toigwerete Yonadabu, mosinto o Rekabu, sokoro yaito, ase amang’ana onsi atochigete ng’a titobaisa konywa edivai ase amatuko aito onsi.
english: We have obeyed everything our forefather Jonadab son of Recab commanded us. Neither we nor our wives nor our sons and daughters have ever drunk wine

ekegusii: Ebikorero bionsi biria Ahasi omoruoti atugutete na akabianga ekero arenge kogamba, ekiagera tabete omwegenwa ase Omonene, twabiroisirie na kobichena. Rora, nao bire agwo bosio bw’egesasimero ki’Omonene.”
english: We have prepared and consecrated all the articles that King Ahaz removed in his unfaithfulness while he was king. They are now in front of the LORD's altar."

ekegusii: we have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have rebelled; we have turned away from your commands and laws.
english: “Intwe twakorire ebibe na ayare amabe, twakorire obokayayu na ogosaria; twaonchokire, twatigire amachiko ao, na emeroberio yao echikire.

ekegusii: We have sinned, even as our fathers did; we have done wrong and acted wickedly.
english: Intwe twakorire ebibe buna chisokoro chiaito chiakorete; twakorire ayare amabe mono, ee, twakorire ayare amabe.

ekegusii: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians, and opened wide our hearts to you.
english: Twakwanire maiso marore nainwe, Abakorinto; chinkoro chiaito chiagareigwe.

ekegusii: We have suffered terror and pitfalls, ruin and destruction."
english: Obwoba ne chiirima biatocheire amo nogosaria na ogosirigwa.

ekegusii: Ogosemeria okwo tore nakorokwo buna ekerochi ki’omoyo, okore ne chinguru, na gotari koonchoka, kogosoa aase are ime moino y’etoto.
english: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,

ekegusii: Naki twaigure ng’a mbare abanto asemore bare aboro, batari gokora emeremo, korende nigo bakona‐gotuka amang’ana ’abanto bande.
english: We hear that some among you are idle. They are not busy; they are busybodies.

ekegusii: Naama! Agwo Efarata tokaigwa amang’ana igoro y’Esanduku y’Okobwatana, tokayenyora aaria ase orosana rwa Yearimu.
english: We heard it in Ephrathah, we came upon it in the fields of Jaar:

ekegusii: Nigo twasemeretie ng’a tonyore omorembe, korende amabe agacha. Tokagania togwenigwe, korende obwoba bogatochera.
english: We hoped for peace but no good has come, for a time of healing but there was only terror.

ekegusii: Intwe nigo togokomanyia, aye omoruoti, ng’a omochie oyo oise koagachwa naende, ne chindwaki chiaye chiagachwe chiere, rirorio orogongo rore bosongo y’orooche rw’Eufarati tirokoba orwao.”
english: We inform the king that if this city is built and its walls are restored, you will be left with nothing in Trans-Euphrates.

ekegusii: Twamanyire ng’a Omwana o Nyasae oikire gocha, na ere otoeire ebirengererio bi’okomanya ere oyore bw’ekeene. Na intwe nigo tore ime asare ere oyore bw’ekeene, ime ase Omwana oye Yeso Kristo. Oyio nere ore Nyasae bw’ekeene, naende obogima bwa kare na kare.
english: We know also that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know him who is true. And we are in him who is true-- even in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.

ekegusii: Twamanyire ng’a kera omonto oiboirwe na Nyasae tagokora ebibe, korende oyoiboirwe na Nyasae nigo akwerenda, na oria omobe takomokuna.
english: We know that anyone born of God does not continue to sin; the one who was born of God keeps him safe, and the evil one cannot harm him.

ekegusii: Twamanyire ng’a Nyasae tari koigwa abanyene ebibe; korende omonto karabe omosasimi Nyasae, na gokora ogwancha kwaye, oyio nere Nyasae akoigwa.
english: We know that God does not listen to sinners. He listens to the godly man who does his will.

ekegusii: Intwe twamanyire ng’a Nyasae nigo arenge gokwana na Musa, korende oyo titomanyeti aase arure.”
english: We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this fellow, we don't even know where he comes from."

ekegusii: Twamanyire ng’a amachiko namaya, onye omonto okoyakorera buna agwenerete gokorerwa,
english: We know that the law is good if one uses it properly.

ekegusii: Naki twamanyire ng’a amachiko nay’Omoika, korende inche nomonto bw’engencho y’ebibe; nigo naoonetigwe inse ase obosomba bw’ebibe.
english: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

ekegusii: Naki twamanyire ng’a ebitongwa bionsi nigo bire nogwechanda, naende nigo bire nobororo nonya ngoika bono,
english: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.

ekegusii: Twamanyire ng’a nigo tore aba Nyasae, na ense yonsi nigo ere inse y’okobua kw’oria omobe.
english: We know that we are children of God, and that the whole world is under the control of the evil one.

ekegusii: Onye tobwatete amachiko aye, ntore nobomaene ng’a ntomomanyete.
english: We know that we have come to know him if we obey his commands.

ekegusii: Intwe twamanyire ng’a twaetire korwa ase amakweri, twasoire ase obogima, ekiagera twanchire abaminto. Oyotancheti nigo amenyete ase amakweri.
english: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. Anyone who does not love remains in death.

ekegusii: Ase eri twamanyire ng’a ntomenyete ime asare, nere ime asetore: Ere otoeire Omoika oye.
english: We know that we live in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.

ekegusii: ekiagera nigo togotaara ase okwegena, tari ase okorora.
english: We live by faith, not by sight.

ekegusii: We love because he first loved us.
english: Intwe twanchire, ekiagera ere natwanchete intwe ritang’ani.

ekegusii: Naboigo naintwe tware namaiga amange asemore, tokaba nomogoko kobaa inwe, tari enchili ya Nyasae yoka, korende nonya nobogima bwaito, ekiagera mwabeire abanchi baito.
english: We loved you so much that we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God but our lives as well, because you had become so dear to us.

ekegusii: Tokagenda ng’ora ase ekero ki’amatuko amange, togaika Kinido ase obokong’u, na ekiagera embeo yatotangete, togaeta ang’e na Kirete maate, erinde tokengane embeo ang’e na Salimone.
english: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

ekegusii: Togaeta ase obokong’u engegu ase engegu, togaika aase akorokwa Ebiambokero Ebiya. Ang’e nagwo norengeo omochie ore korokwa Lasaya.
english: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

ekegusii: Amache tokonywa goika toakane chibesa, ne chinko togwota nigo tokogora.
english: We must buy the water we drink; our wood can be had only at a price.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, netogwenerete gotegerera mono kobua na kobwata ayatwaigure, titocha gosira.
english: We must pay more careful attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

ekegusii: Goika togende orogendo rw’amatuko atato gochia ase erooro, erinde toruere Omonene, Nyasae oito, ekeng’wanso buna atochigete.”
english: We must take a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, as he commands us."

ekegusii: Abaminto, netogwenerete komoakera Nyasae ng’a mbuya mono botambe ase engencho yaino, buna ere boronge, ekiagera okwegena kwaino gwakinire mono, na obwanchani bwa kera oyomo oino ase oyonde nigo bogendererete komentekana.
english: We ought always to thank God for you, brothers, and rightly so, because your faith is growing more and more, and the love every one of you has for each other is increasing.

ekegusii: Nabo etogwenerete intwe koroisia abanto bare buna abwo, erinde tobe abakori emeremo amo nabarabwo ase ekeene.
english: We ought therefore to show hospitality to such men so that we may work together for the truth.

ekegusii: Na eriogi eri nario twaigwete rikorwa igoro, ekero twarenge amo nere ase egetunwa egechenu.
english: We ourselves heard this voice that came from heaven when we were with him on the sacred mountain.

ekegusii: Korende Lisia, omochiki omonene bw’abarwani, agaika, akamorusia ase amaboko aito ne chinguru,
english: We planned to judge him according to our own law, but the commander Lysias came, and with great violence took him from us. Then Lysias gave orders that his accusers should come before you. [* Verse originally omitted in Good News version.]

ekegusii: erinde erieta ri’Omonene oito Yeso ritogigwe ime yaino, na inwe ime yaye, koreng’ana nobuya bwa Nyasae oito, na obw’Omonene Yeso Kristo.
english: We pray this so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ekegusii: Ere nere twararirie, togokurera na kworokereria kera omonto ase obong’aini bwonsi, erinde tonyare korenta kera omonto omoikeranu ime ase Kristo.
english: We proclaim him, admonishing and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ.

ekegusii: Eri twarorire na koigwa, eri naboigo tokobarareria inwe, erinde nainwe monyare kobwatana naintwe. Okobwatana gwaito nigo kore amo na Tata na Omwana oye Yeso Kristo.
english: We proclaim to you what we have seen and heard, so that you also may have fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.

ekegusii: Togaika Sirakusa, tokamenyao amatuko atato.
english: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.

ekegusii: Titobeka ekegocha ase onde bwensi, erinde obosomba bwaito bobaise gokwanwa bobe,
english: We put no stumbling block in anyone's path, so that our ministry will not be discredited.

ekegusii: We questioned the elders and asked them, "Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?"
english: “Agwo ntwakwana nabagaaka baria, tokababoria iga: Ning’o obaa ribaga mokoagacha enyomba eye na gokoora koagacha orwaki oro?

ekegusii: Intwe nigo twasanyorera Negebu aase Abakereti bamenyete, na ensemo ere ey’Abayuda na ey’abanto ba Kalebu. Boigo togasamba Sikilagi nomorero.”
english: We raided the Negev of the Kerethites and the territory belonging to Judah and the Negev of Caleb. And we burned Ziklag."

ekegusii: Twainyoire chinswe twarenge koria ase ense ya Misiri totare goakanera, na endagera ende enga buna emiongo emerandi, na emenyobio, na ebitunguo biare ao ao, ebiororo amo nebiroro.
english: We remember the fish we ate in Egypt at no cost-- also the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic.

ekegusii: Ee, ntwarora amamonto, abanto b’ororeria rw’Anaki. Intwe nigo twerora ng’a nabasinini mono, tore buna ebisase. Naboigo twarorekana asebare.”
english: We saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them."

ekegusii: Togatoma Timotheo oyominto, omokori emeremo amo na Nyasae ase okorandia enchili ya Kristo, erinde abakong’ie na kobaremia ase okwegena kwaino,
english: We sent Timothy, who is our brother and God's fellow worker in spreading the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you in your faith,

ekegusii: Gose titokora obotomani buna abande babo bakorete, na abanto chilifu emerongo ebere na isato bagakwa ase rituko erimo.
english: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did-- and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

ekegusii: Gose titoteema Omonene, buna abande babo bakorete, bagasirigwa ne ching’iti.
english: We should not test the Lord, as some of them did-- and were killed by snakes.

ekegusii: Twaramboreire Abamisiri na Abaasuri amaboko batoe endagera egotoisana.
english: We submitted to Egypt and Assyria to get enough bread.

ekegusii: Tokaira emechie yonsi yarenge ase ense eraire eimokererete igoro na Gileadi yonsi, na Basani yonsi, goikera Saleka na Edirei, emechie y’oboruoti bwa Ogi, oyorenge kogamba agwo Basani.”
english: We took all the towns on the plateau, and all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan.

ekegusii: Ekiagera konya twatwomirwe mono nomwaga oria, rituko ria kabere bagachaka gotuguta chigurube nyancha ime.
english: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.

ekegusii: Tokaira ense yabo, tokayea abanto b’egesaku kia Reuben, na ab’ekia Gadi, na ekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase, na eyio ekaba omwando obo.
english: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

ekegusii: Emioyo yaito nigo emoganyete Omonene, ere nere ogokonywa gwaito, na enguba yaito.
english: We wait in hope for the LORD; he is our help and our shield.

ekegusii: Na intwe ntoganetie mono kera oyomo oino aorokie omokia oria goika omoerio, na igo amanye obomaene oboikeranu bw’ogosemeria kwaino.
english: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

ekegusii: Twerende ne ring’ana eri, omonto tacha gotokwana bobe ase amang’ana ’ekeegwa eke tokogaba intwe.
english: We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this liberal gift.

ekegusii: Korende intwe togatang’ana kogenda nemeeri, tokagenda goika Asosi. Tokarengereria ng’a ntonyore Paulo aria, ekiagera ere nabo achigete. Ere omonyene nigo arengereretie kogenda namagoro.
english: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we were going to take Paul aboard. He had made this arrangement because he was going there on foot.

ekegusii: Nkarora ng’a intwe nigo twarenge mogondo tokoboa emesaima y’endagera, na omosaima one okaimoka ogatenena boronge, na emesaima yaino ekaba ekoyoetanana, egotung’ama inse ase omosaima one.”
english: We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it."

ekegusii: Titwarigetie ogotogigwa korwa ase mwanyabanto, nonya nkorwa asemore, gose korwa ase abanto bande.
english: We were not looking for praise from men, not from you or anyone else. As apostles of Christ we could have been a burden to you,

ekegusii: Naboigo twatindegetwe amo nere ase enchera y’ebatiso ase amakweri, erinde buna Kristo abogetigwe korwa ase abakure ase obonene bwa Ise, naboigo naintwe, totaare ase obogima oboyia.
english: We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.

ekegusii: Nigo tore abamura ikomi na babere, tata noyomo. Oyomo oito takaiyo, na omoke kegima nere okare ase tata inka, ase ense ya Kanani.
english: We were twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is now with our father in Canaan.'

ekegusii: Intwe twabeire tore barito, twabeire tokobina na kweganchorana, korende ekero twaiborete tokaibora embeo bosa. Titorenteti ogotooreka konde ase ense, gose abanto tibaiboretwe ase ense.
english: We were with child, we writhed in pain, but we gave birth to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth; we have not given birth to people of the world.

ekegusii: Intwe abatore ne chinguru netogwenerete kobogoria oboreu bw’abatari ne chinguru, tetogwenereti kwegwenera intwe abanyene.
english: We who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

ekegusii: Korende intwe nigo togochia gokora buna twarire eira gokora. Tosambe ubani ase Eting’ana ya Igoro, naende toumore okoruegwa kw’ebinyugwa asere, buna twakorete intwe amo ne chisokoro chiaito, na abaruoti baito amo nabanene baito. Ayio nigo tware koyakora ase emechie y’Abayuda na ase chinchera chia Yerusalemu. Ekero keria nigo twabwate endagera enyinge, naende tokagenderera gosesenigwa, na titwanyoretwe namabe ande onsi.
english: We will certainly do everything we said we would: We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and will pour out drink offerings to her just as we and our fathers, our kings and our officials did in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. At that time we had plenty of food and were well off and suffered no harm.

ekegusii: Intwe ntobogorie ebirwanero biaito bi’esegi, na twamboke gochia ase ense ya Kanani ase obosio bw’Omonene, erio nario toratware ense eye ere aa moocha ya Yorodan ebe eyaito.”
english: We will cross over before the LORD into Canaan armed, but the property we inherit will be on this side of the Jordan."

ekegusii: Erio tonyore chinibo chionsi chie rigori rinene, toichorie chinyomba chiaito nebisakorwa ebio.
english: we will get all sorts of valuable things and fill our houses with plunder;

ekegusii: Natonyare gwancha okoboria kwaino ase ring’ana erimo rioka, nario eri: Komoranche mobe buna intwe, kera omonto omosacha ore asemore arokigwe.
english: We will give our consent to you on one condition only: that you become like us by circumcising all your males.

ekegusii: We will make you earrings of gold, studded with silver.
english: Intwe ntokoroiserie ebinyuri bie chitahabu bi’ogwechabera, ebitonire ne chifeta.

ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio titokoyabisa ase abana babo; goika totebie ebiaare bigochi‐gocha ogokora kw’obonene bw’Omonene, na amakumia aye ay’okobua akorire.
english: We will not hide them from their children; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD, his power, and the wonders he has done.

ekegusii: We will not receive any inheritance with them on the other side of the Jordan, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan."
english: Intwe titokonyora omwando oito amo nabarabwo agwo ng’umbu ya Yorodan, ekiagera twanyorire omwando oito aiga moocha ya Yorodan.”

ekegusii: Titokoirana ase chinka chiaito goika torore ng’a Abaisraeli baminto banyorire kera omonto orogongo rw’omwando oye.
english: We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.

ekegusii: Erio toake amariogi ’omogoko ase engencho y’obobui bwao, toimokererie igoro ebendera y’erieta ria Nyasae oito! Tiga Omonene aikeranie okoboria kwao kw’oboitongo.
english: We will shout for joy when you are victorious and will lift up our banners in the name of our God. May the LORD grant all your requests.

ekegusii: naende nigo togochandeka gatogokora emeremo namaboko aito abanyene. Ekero tokoramwa, twasesenia; ekero togochandwa, twaremereria;
english: We work hard with our own hands. When we are cursed, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

ekegusii: Nkobarikera tore aya, erinde omogoko oito oikeranigwe.
english: We write this to make our joy complete.

ekegusii: Korende intwe titogwetogia kobua ekerengo giaito, korende ase ekerengo twagabeirwe na Nyasae, nonya nokobaikera inwe.
english: We, however, will not boast beyond proper limits, but will confine our boasting to the field God has assigned to us, a field that reaches even to you.

ekegusii: Obotenenku bwonsi na amasikani nigo bikorwa asore aye, naye okogamba igoro ase bionsi. Ase okoboko kwao chinguru na okobua nao bire; nobwate okobua kw’ogokinia na korua chinguru ase bonsi.
english: Wealth and honor come from you; you are the ruler of all things. In your hands are strength and power to exalt and give strength to all.

ekegusii: Obotenenku na obonda mbibe ase enyomba yaye, na oboronge bwaye mbogenderere kobao botambe.
english: Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.

ekegusii: Omonto omonda nigo akonyora abasani abange, korende omotaka nigo akwangwa nomosani oye.
english: Wealth brings many friends, but a poor man's friend deserts him.

ekegusii: Chinibo tichiri gokonya kende ase rituko ri’endamwamu, korende oboronge nigo boratoorie korwa ase amakweri.
english: Wealth is worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

ekegusii: Korende babeke ebikoroto, go tibeboyia chianga ibere.
english: Wear sandals but not an extra tunic.

ekegusii: Ase ayio bakeboyia chigunia, naende bakanaara chingori ase amagoti abo, erio bakagenda ase omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, bagateba, “Omosomba oo Beni‐Hadadi nigo agosaba ng’a omotige abe moyo.” Ahabu akabora, “Inee! Nonya mbono moyo are? Ere momura ominto.”
english: Wearing sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, they went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says: 'Please let me live.'" The king answered, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

ekegusii: “Inwe abarisia, bokia amagombo morere! Inwe abanene be riicho, egara‐garie ase ribu, ekiagera rituko ri’okonyenywa kwaino na ogoserebanigwa kwaino riachire; namosirigwe mogwe buna chimingichi chiachorirwe chinyenywe.
english: Weep and wail, you shepherds; roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock. For your time to be slaughtered has come; you will fall and be shattered like fine pottery.

ekegusii: Endagera yao orabe gokoria nigo erarengwe, nigo erabe ey’ekerengo gie chisekeli emerongo ebere ase rituko erimo. Eyio nero orabe gokoria rituko ase rituko.
english: Weigh out twenty shekels of food to eat each day and eat it at set times.

ekegusii: Momoroisie gaki ase Omonene ase omogoko bwonsi. Mosike abanto banga buna oyio,
english: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor men like him,

ekegusii: Torusie abanto ikomi korwa ase abanto rigana erimo, na abanto rigana erimo korwa ase abanto elifu eyemo, na abanto elifu eyemo korwa ase abanto chilifu ikomi, korwa ase ebisaku bionsi bi’Abaisraeli. Abanto aba nabasangererie chindagera korwa ase abanto, erinde babarentere baria bagochia korwania Gibea o Benjamin, ekiagera barabwo bakorire ogosaria kw’obosooku ase egati y’Abaisraeli.”
english: We'll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred from a thousand, and a thousand from ten thousand, to get provisions for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can give them what they deserve for all this vileness done in Israel."

ekegusii: Gaki nkwagwenerete kobeka chibesa chiane ase abakorua ebitoki, na inche ngocha, anga nanyora echiane amo nebitoki biane.
english: Well then, you should have put my money on deposit with the bankers, so that when I returned I would have received it back with interest.

ekegusii: abaruoti aba bagakora esegi na Bera, omoruoti o Sodomu, na Birisa, omoruoti o Gomora, na Shinabu, omoruoti o Adima na Shemeberi, omoruoti o Seboimu, na omoruoti o Bela noro Soari.
english: went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).

ekegusii: went up to Beth Hoglah and continued north of Beth Arabah to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
english: rokagenderera gochia Beti‐Hogila, rogaeta sugusu ya Beti‐Araba. Erio rogaika Rigena ria Bohani, mosinto o Reuben,

ekegusii: Emegwekano y’abakerubi na ey’emekendo iyarengeo. Ase kera egati y’abakerubi, omokendo norengeo, na kera omokerubi nigo arenge namasio abere;
english: were carved cherubim and palm trees. Palm trees alternated with cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:

ekegusii: Inse kobibara, nigo bire ebinge goetania omokenye. Ekero nkoboka, nigo ngendererete kobeera amo naye.
english: Were I to count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand. When I awake, I am still with you.

ekegusii: Inee! Abanto b’Etiopia na aba Libia tibarenge omoganda omonene bw’abarwani esegi, naende tibabwate chigari chinyinge, na abariini chibarasi abange? Korende nonya naboigo, ekiagera aye gwasemeretie Omonene, akababeka ase okoboko kwao.
english: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a mighty army with great numbers of chariots and horsemen? Yet when you relied on the LORD, he delivered them into your hand.

ekegusii: Ebisieri biabo nigo biarenge buna ebi’ebinyomba bia sugusu. Egesieri nkiarenge ase omochakano bw’aase aria arenge goeterwa, engencho yaye aase arenge ensemo ya moocha ang’e norwaki ase omonto aranyare goetera.
english: were the doorways of the rooms on the south. There was a doorway at the beginning of the passageway that was parallel to the corresponding wall extending eastward, by which one enters the rooms.

ekegusii: Inee! Igo kwarangeretigwe kore omosomba? Torora ng’a mbobe; korende koranyare gosiborwa, mbuya obe bo.
english: Were you a slave when you were called? Don't let it trouble you-- although if you can gain your freedom, do so.

ekegusii: Inee! Aye Omonene nigo ogechirie ne chindooche, gose endamwamu yao nigo ere igoro ase chirochio? Inee! Nigo ore nekeririanda ase chinyancha, ekiagera nigo gwachete ne chibarasi chiao koriinete chigari chiao chi’obobui?
english: Were you angry with the rivers, O LORD? Was your wrath against the streams? Did you rage against the sea when you rode with your horses and your victorious chariots?

ekegusii: na korwa Ekironi gochia Enyancha Enene emechie yonsi yarengeo ensemo y’Asidodi, amo nebichie biaye.
english: west of Ekron, all that were in the vicinity of Ashdod, together with their villages;

ekegusii: Okogania kw’omonto nigo gokworokia obuya bwaye, na omonto omotaka nigo are omuya mono kobua omonyaborimo.
english: What a man desires is unfailing love; better to be poor than a liar.

ekegusii: Obobe nobwane inche mwanyabanto! Ning’o oransibore korwa ase omobere oyo bw’amakweri?
english: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

ekegusii: Ng’ai ngochia goeta nobosooku obo? Naye nigo orabe buna oyomo, bw’abakayayu bare ase Abaisraeli. Bono, koranche oborie omoruoti akoe ribaga onyuome.”
english: What about me? Where could I get rid of my disgrace? And what about you? You would be like one of the wicked fools in Israel. Please speak to the king; he will not keep me from being married to you."

ekegusii: inee, nigo mogoteba igoro yaye, ere oyo Tata aatananete akamotoma ase ense: Nkorama are, ekiagera nateba: Inche n’Omwana o Nyasae?
english: what about the one whom the Father set apart as his very own and sent into the world? Why then do you accuse me of blasphemy because I said, 'I am God's Son'?

ekegusii: Mbuya ki omonto omong’aini abwate kobua oyore omoriri? Gose ninki omonto omotaka akonyora, oria omanyete buna akwerenda ase abare moyo?
english: What advantage has a wise man over a fool? What does a poor man gain by knowing how to conduct himself before others?

ekegusii: What advantage, then, is there in being a Jew, or what value is there in circumcision?
english: Gaki rende, Omoyahudi inki abuete abande? Na okwaroka inki kogwenerete?

ekegusii: Naki ere buya gwasemirie omonto otari nobong’aini, na gwakwanire amang’ana aichire ne chisemi chingiya!
english: What advice you have offered to one without wisdom! And what great insight you have displayed!

ekegusii: Naende ngosanga ki kore ase egati ye Hekalu ya Nyasae na emegwekano y’ogosasimwa? Naki intwe ne Hekalu ya Nyasae ore moyo, buna Nyasae atebete, “Nimenye ime yabo, na ase egati yabo nintaare, na inche nimbe Nyasae obo, na barabwo nababe abanto baane.
english: What agreement is there between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: "I will live with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people."

ekegusii: Mang’ana ki omonto arabairanerie abatomwa b’egesaku keria? Obairanerie ng’a Omonene obekire oboroso bwa Sayoni, na abanto baye abachandire mbanyore obotamero aroro.
english: What answer shall be given to the envoys of that nation? "The LORD has established Zion, and in her his afflicted people will find refuge."

ekegusii: Aye ninki ogokora aiga, na monto ki obwate aa? Nase ki ogwekunyera oboina aase are igoro mono? Inee! Nigo okwebaachera oboina aiga ase egetare bobe obomenyo bwao?
english: What are you doing here and who gave you permission to cut out a grave for yourself here, hewing your grave on the height and chiseling your resting place in the rock?

ekegusii: Aye oyo gwatigirwe bosa na gwasarigwe, ninki orengereretie ekero okobeka chianga chimonyinga, naende ogwechabera nebinto bie chitahabu, na gosata amaiso ao? Nigo ogwechabera bosa. Abanchi bao bagochayire, na nigo bakorigia gosiria obogima bwao.
english: What are you doing, O devastated one? Why dress yourself in scarlet and put on jewels of gold? Why shade your eyes with paint? You adorn yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.

ekegusii: Nkwama ki rende mwanyorete korwa ase ebinto biria bikobarentera obosooku bono? Naki omoerio bw’ebinto ebi namakweri.
english: What benefit did you reap at that time from the things you are now ashamed of? Those things result in death!

ekegusii: Inee! Ninche ngwenerete kogambia abare isiko? Na inwe timogwenereti kogambia abare ime?
english: What business is it of mine to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?

ekegusii: What can I say for you? With what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may comfort you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? Your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can heal you?
english: Aye omochie o Yerusalemu, ninki ndagotebie? Ninki ndakoreng’anie? Mang’ana ki anga buna ayao ndagotebie, erinde nkoremie, aye Sayoni ore buna omoiseke omwekungi? Ogosarigwa kwao nokonene buna enyancha ere enene, ning’o oranyare gokogwenia?

ekegusii: Esegi na okorwana ebire ase egati yaino, ng’ai bikorwa? Inee! Tibiri korwa agwo ase okogania kwaino okobe, ogokorwana nebiimo biaino?
english: What causes fights and quarrels among you? Don't they come from your desires that battle within you?

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baigwete amang’ana a Daudi, bakagenda bakayatebia Saulo, na Saulo akamorangeria.
english: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.

ekegusii: Ing’ana ki erio akwana: Namondigie, korende timokoonyora, na aase ndabe inche, timokonyara gochao?”
english: What did he mean when he said, 'You will look for me, but you will not find me,' and 'Where I am, you cannot come'?"

ekegusii: Ubani eria bakondetera korwa Seba, ninki erangwenere, gose ebinto bigotioka buya bakorenta korwa ase ense y’aare? Ebing’wanso biaino bi’ogosambwa nabiangire, nonya nebing’wanso biaino binde tibingogeti.
english: What do I care about incense from Sheba or sweet calamus from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please me."

ekegusii: Ninki kiagera aya ndoche akorekire? Baondokire na koirana nyuma; abarwani babo chituoni babuirwe, batamire ase okoayerera batari korigereria nyuma; obwoba nigo bore ase chinsemo chionsi. Nabo Omonene atebire.
english: What do I see? They are terrified, they are retreating, their warriors are defeated. They flee in haste without looking back, and there is terror on every side," declares the LORD.

ekegusii: What do you know that we do not know? What insights do you have that we do not have?
english: Inee! Aye ninki omanyete intwe totamanyeti? Mbong’aini ki omanyete intwe totamanyeti?

ekegusii: Omonene Nyasae bw’Emeganda, nigo akoboria iga: Ninki mokorengereria goika mwasunyuntire abanto baane na gosia amasio ’abataka?”
english: What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord, the LORD Almighty.

ekegusii: Naki morigetie? Inchiche asemore nenyimbo gose nobwanchani ase omoika bw’obwororo?
english: What do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a whip, or in love and with a gentle spirit?

ekegusii: Naki moroche?” Bakairaneria, “Omonto oyo nigo agwenerete akwe.”
english: What do you think?" "He is worthy of death," they answered.

ekegusii: What does a man get for all the toil and anxious striving with which he labors under the sun?
english: Ngento ki omonto aranyore ekero akorire emeremo emekong’u na kwerosia mono inse y’erioba?

ekegusii: Mbitoki ki omonto akonyora ase okwerosia gokora emeremo emekong’u aiga inse y’erioba?
english: What does man gain from all his labor at which he toils under the sun?

ekegusii: Ninki amariko agoteba? “Ibrahimu nigo amwegenete Nyasae, na ase engencho eyio akabarwa koba omonyene oboronge.”
english: What does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness."

ekegusii: Inee! Mbitoki ki omonto akonyora ase emeremo yonsi agwechandera?
english: What does the worker gain from his toil?

ekegusii: Tari ekio kegosoa omonwa gekobekera omonto ogotacheneka, korende egekorwa ase omonwa nakio ekio gekobekera omonto ogotacheneka.”
english: What goes into a man's mouth does not make him 'unclean,' but what comes out of his mouth, that is what makes him 'unclean.'"

ekegusii: Ekiagera inki keragwenere omonto karanyore ense yonsi, ko esirie gose gwesaria ere omonyene?
english: What good is it for a man to gain the whole world, and yet lose or forfeit his very self?

ekegusii: Ninki eragwenere omonto konyora ense yonsi, ko asirie omoyo oye?
english: What good is it for a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?

ekegusii: Abaminto, ngokonywa ki omonto aranyore onye ogoteba ng’a nare nokwegena, na ere tari nogokora? Inee! Okwegena koria nkonyare komotooria?
english: What good is it, my brothers, if a man claims to have faith but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?

ekegusii: Ninki eragwenere omonto konyora ense yonsi, ko asirie omoyo oye? Gose omonto inki ararue ase ribaga ri’omoyo oye?
english: What good will it be for a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

ekegusii: Bagaichana kobua ase engencho ye ring’ana riaye, atebete ng’a, “Timokondora obosio bwane naende.” Bakamokooba goika ase emeeri.
english: What grieved them most was his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

ekegusii: Naende nkobwatana ki kore ase egati ya Kristo na Beliali? Gose oyobwegenete, insemo ki abwate amo noyotegeneti?
english: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? What does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

ekegusii: Buna akorirwe ase rituko ria rero, naboigo Omonene achikire akorwe kogenderera ase ogokora okobwatanigwa asemore, erinde mwaberwe.
english: What has been done today was commanded by the LORD to make atonement for you.

ekegusii: Aya arengeo kare, naro agochia kobao naende. Aya akoregete kare, naro agochia gokoreka naende. Ande tari are amayia inse y’erioba.
english: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

ekegusii: What has happened to all your joy? I can testify that, if you could have done so, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
english: Ng’ai rende omogoko oino ore? Naki nababereire kirori, ng’a onye yanyarekana, anga mwanduseria amaiso aino mong’e.

ekegusii: Inyora naende buna akorete ase abarwani b’esegi ba Misiri, ne chibarasi chiabo, ne chigari chiabo, na buna atigete amache ’Enyancha Embariri akabamera, ekero barenge kobabwatia inwe, na buna basirete tibana kororekana goika rero iga.
english: what he did to the Egyptian army, to its horses and chariots, how he overwhelmed them with the waters of the Red Sea as they were pursuing you, and how the LORD brought lasting ruin on them.

ekegusii: Ayio akorete akaba amabe ase obosio bw’Omonene, nere Omonene akamoita.
english: What he did was wicked in the LORD's sight; so he put him to death also.

ekegusii: what he lays up the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver.
english: nonya ochitumbire igo, nomonto omoronge orachibeke, na abatari na komocha baatanane chifeta chiaye.

ekegusii: Ere aise gotagora, onde tari oraagache naende; aise gosiekera omonto, onde tari oramoigorere.
english: What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man he imprisons cannot be released.

ekegusii: Ebinto akoreire emeremo emekong’u nabiiranie, takobimera, gose takonyara kwegokeria ebitoki biria anyorire.
english: What he toiled for he must give back uneaten; he will not enjoy the profit from his trading.

ekegusii: Aya asemeretie nasirigwe kegima, na aya egenete nigo are buna enyomba y’oronyambobe.
english: What he trusts in is fragile; what he relies on is a spider's web.

ekegusii: Korende nigo ngokwana ng’a omonyamwando, ekero are omwana, tari nogwatananeka nomosomba, nonya ore omonyene enibo yonsi.
english: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he owns the whole estate.

ekegusii: What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has happened to me.
english: Naki ring’ana riria inyoboete rianchicheire, na riria rikoondokia rianyorire.

ekegusii: Engencho yagera nakwana bo neye, ng’a oyomo ore ase egati yaino nigo agoteba, “Inche noyo o Paulo,” na oyonde, “Inche noyo bw’Apolo,” na oyonde, “Inche noyo o Kefa,” na oyonde, “Inche noyo o Kristo.”
english: What I mean is this: One of you says, "I follow Paul"; another, "I follow Apollos"; another, "I follow Cephas"; still another, "I follow Christ."

ekegusii: Aya ngokwana naya: Okobwatana koria gwakoretwe ritang’ani na Nyasae; na amachiko aria akarentwa nyuma y’emiaka amagana ane, na emerongo etato, tagosaria okobwatana koria, erinde eira eria ebe eya bosa.
english: What I mean is this: The law, introduced 430 years later, does not set aside the covenant previously established by God and thus do away with the promise.

ekegusii: Korende baminto, nigo ngoteba iga: Ekero getigarete negeke; gaki korwa bono baria bare nabakungu, tiga babe buna tibabwati;
english: What I mean, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none;

ekegusii: What I say to you, I say to everyone: 'Watch!'"
english: Na erio nabatebirie inwe, nabatebirie bonsi: Renda!”

ekegusii: Amaiso aane agerire nabeire nomoichano ase omoyo one ase engencho y’abaiseke bonsi b’omochie one.
english: What I see brings grief to my soul because of all the women of my city.

ekegusii: Eri nkobatebia ase omosunte ime, ritebe ase omobaso; na eri mokoigwa rikomonyererwa, rirarie igoro ase ebirama.
english: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the roofs.

ekegusii: Naki rende onye Nyasae okorigia koorokia endamwamu yaye, na komanyia abanto okobua kwaye, na ase oboremereria obonge akabogorerania nebinto biria bi’endamwamu biakorirwe ase ogosareka,
english: What if God, choosing to show his wrath and make his power known, bore with great patience the objects of his wrath-- prepared for destruction?

ekegusii: erinde aorokie obonda bw’obonene bwaye, ase ebinto biria bi’amabera ebiaroisetie korwa kare binyore obonene?
english: What if he did this to make the riches of his glory known to the objects of his mercy, whom he prepared in advance for glory--

ekegusii: Aande, tata nigo arantaba‐tabe, na inche imbe ase amaiso aye buna omong’ainereria, inyerentere okoragererigwa ribaga ri’ogosesenigwa.”
english: What if my father touches me? I would appear to be tricking him and would bring down a curse on myself rather than a blessing."

ekegusii: Inki rende onye abande tibari abegenwa? Inee! Ogotegenwa kwabo nakonyare gokora obwegenwa bwa Nyasae bobe bosa?
english: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God's faithfulness?

ekegusii: Aande ase baria emerongo etano baise koba batano tibaiyo, abanyene oboronge, Inee, nosarie omochie ekiagera batano tibaiyo?” Akairaneria, “Tingosaria omochie, kondarore agwo emerongo ene, na batano.”
english: what if the number of the righteous is five less than fifty? Will you destroy the whole city because of five people?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it."

ekegusii: Aande ase omochie oria abanyene oboronge emerongo etano mbakareo, nigo orayosirie, gose noyororere amabera ase engencho y’abwo abanyene oboronge emerongo etano?
english: What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will you really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people in it?

ekegusii: Naki erabe rende, komorarore Omwana‐o‐mwanyabanto okogenda aaria aase arenge ritang’ani?
english: What if you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before!

ekegusii: omonto inki aisaine aye ogendererete komorengereria? Mwanyabanto ninki aisaine aye okomorenda?
english: what is man that you are mindful of him, the son of man that you care for him?

ekegusii: Gose tari ase ayio oka, korende nigo achoretwe ne chikanisa agende amo naintwe ase emeremo eye y’obuya obo togokora ase obonene bw’Omonene, na koorokia ng’a intwe nigo tore ang’e kobakorera.
english: What is more, he was chosen by the churches to accompany us as we carry the offering, which we administer in order to honor the Lord himself and to show our eagerness to help.

ekegusii: Ee, nabarire onsi, ng’a abeire bosa ase engencho y’obuya botari nekerengo, engencho yaye okomomanya Kristo Yeso Omonene one. Ase engencho yaye natigire ebinto bionsi, na kobibara buna eubi, erinde imonyore Kristo,
english: What is more, I consider everything a loss compared to the surpassing greatness of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ

ekegusii: Inchera ki ekogenda aase oborabu bokoruerwa, gose ekogenda aase omwaga okorwa moocha bwesiarera ense yonsi?
english: What is the way to the place where the lightning is dispersed, or the place where the east winds are scattered over the earth?

ekegusii: Egento giachiire bogeka tigekorongeigwa, na ekiaremire tigekobareka.
english: What is twisted cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.

ekegusii: Naende morore gose ense eria abanto bamenyete nengiya gose nembe, naende morore emechie yabo ase bamenyete, onye nigo ere ebitwori gose nigo egiteire chindwaki.
english: What kind of land do they live in? Is it good or bad? What kind of towns do they live in? Are they unwalled or fortified?

ekegusii: Monto ki orabe moyo otakwe? Ning’o oranyare gotooria omoyo oye korwa ase chinguru chi’amakweri?
english: What man can live and not see death, or save himself from the power of the grave? Selah

ekegusii: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water?
english: “Inee! Monto ki onga buna Ayubu, oyio okonywa ogochaywa, ogokomera buna amache?

ekegusii: Aye Omonene ng’ai omonto omong’aini are oyoranyare komanya engencho y’amang’ana aya? Ning’o aye Omonene gwakwanire nere, oyio oranyare goteba egekogera ense yabeire ritongo, na yasarekire buna erooro omonto atanyare goeta ase egati yaye?
english: What man is wise enough to understand this? Who has been instructed by the LORD and can explain it? Why has the land been ruined and laid waste like a desert that no one can cross?

ekegusii: Obobe nobwane, ekiagera nabeire nkororekana buna ekero amatunda ’omorakera agosangererigwa, na ayatigaire ase emesabibu achorirwe. Ebisago bi’amasabibu bikoriegwa tibiyo, na amako amatang’ani, aya nganetie, taiyo.
english: What misery is mine! I am like one who gathers summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster of grapes to eat, none of the early figs that I crave.

ekegusii: Inee! Ngento ki nanga nayokorerete goetania, ekio ntakorete? Ekero nasemeretie ng’a mbwame amasabibu amaya, Inee, nase ki bwamete amasabibu amegarori?
english: What more could have been done for my vineyard than I have done for it? When I looked for good grapes, why did it yield only bad?

ekegusii: Aya abwo bakondwania bagokwana na korengereria, nigo bare mamincha yane omobaso boira.
english: what my enemies whisper and mutter against me all day long.

ekegusii: “Inee! Mbanto ba gesaku ki ekenene babwate enyasae ere ang’e nabarabwo buna Omonene, Nyasae oito, are ang’e naintwe? Nigo agotoigwa kero kende gionsi tokomorangeria atokonye.
english: What other nation is so great as to have their gods near them the way the LORD our God is near us whenever we pray to him?

ekegusii: Inee! Omogoko onde nore ase Omonguru ng’a nomonyaboronge ore? Gose inki aranyore onye aye kogokora chinchera chiao chibe ching’ikeranu?
english: What pleasure would it give the Almighty if you were righteous? What would he gain if your ways were blameless?

ekegusii: Orogongo orwo roratigare robebekaine na roria orochenu, nigo rorabe orw’ekerengo gie chimoti chilifu ikomi (10,000) gochia moocha, na chilifu ikomi (10,000) gochia bosongo. Endagera erame aroro nigo erabe ey’abwo barabe bagokora emeremo ase omochie oyio ime.
english: What remains of the area, bordering on the sacred portion and running the length of it, will be 10,000 cubits on the east side and 10,000 cubits on the west side. Its produce will supply food for the workers of the city.

ekegusii: Ninki rende? Intwe Abayahudi nabaya tore kobua abande? Yaya, nonya ng’ake! Naki twasoeire Abayahudi amo n’Abagiriki ng’a bonsi nigo bare inse y’okobua kw’ebibe;
english: What shall we conclude then? Are we any better? Not at all! We have already made the charge that Jews and Gentiles alike are all under sin.

ekegusii: What shall we do? They will certainly hear that you have come,
english: Inki rende kegwenerete gekorwe? Ekeene, nabo baraigwe ng’a gwachire aiga.

ekegusii: Ninki rende toratebe? Amachiko nebibe? Yaya, taibo! Korende tinare komanya ebibe onye amachiko atarengeo; naki tinare komanya okogania okobe, onye ogochika gotagoteba, “Toba nokogania okobe.”
english: What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed I would not have known what sin was except through the law. For I would not have known what coveting really was if the law had not said, "Do not covet."

ekegusii: Ninki rende toratebe? Togenderere ase ebibe, erinde amabera amenteke abe amange kobua?
english: What shall we say, then? Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase?

ekegusii: Rora, chinguru chiaye nigo chire ase ekenema kiaye, na okobua kwaye nigo kore ase chinyama chi’enda yaye.
english: What strength he has in his loins, what power in the muscles of his belly!

ekegusii: Egento eke aye omoruoti kwaboririe nigo kere egekong’u mono, na onde tari oranyare gokeorokia ase omoruoti otatiga chinyasae, na echio tichimenyeti amo na mwanyabanto.”
english: What the king asks is too difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among men."

ekegusii: Endagera chinyanchaba chiatigaretie, chingige chikayeria, na eye chingige chiatigaretie, ebisase bikayeria, na eye ebisase biatigaretie, chingeeti chikayeria.
english: What the locust swarm has left the great locusts have eaten; what the great locusts have left the young locusts have eaten; what the young locusts have left other locusts have eaten.

ekegusii: Aya omokori amabe airogete namochere, korende aya omonyene oboronge aganetie naikeranigwe.
english: What the wicked dreads will overtake him; what the righteous desire will be granted.

ekegusii: Gaki eng’eria yane ninki? Neye, ng’a ndandie enchili ya Kristo ntari konyora ebintungetie, na tinsaba ebiaboronge biane ase okorandia enchili.
english: What then is my reward? Just this: that in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not make use of my rights in preaching it.

ekegusii: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, discovered in this matter?
english: Inki rende toratebe? Ibrahimu sokoro yaito bw’ororeria inki anyorete?

ekegusii: Naki rende baminto? Komogosangererekana amo, kera oyomo nare nogotera, gose okworokereria, gose okomaanorerwa, gose gokwana ase omonwa, gose koonchora, amang’ana onsi tiga akoreke ase okoagacha ekanisa.
english: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a hymn, or a word of instruction, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation. All of these must be done for the strengthening of the church.

ekegusii: Ninki rende toratebe? Ogotaba boronge nkore ase Nyasae? Yaya, taibo!
english: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Not at all!

ekegusii: Ninki rende toratebe? Ng’a abanto b’Ebisaku, abatarenge korigia oboronge mbanyorete oboronge boria bw’okwegena;
english: What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;

ekegusii: Ninki rende? Tokore ebibe ekiagera totari inse y’amachiko korende inse y’amabera? Yaya taibo!
english: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!

ekegusii: Naki rende abeire? Egento keria Abaisraeli baare korigia tibakenyorete, Baria bachoretwe, mbarabwo bakenyorete, korende abatigarete bagakorwa koba abakong’u ase chinkoro chiabo,
english: What then? What Israel sought so earnestly it did not obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,

ekegusii: amang’ana ayio twaigwete na koyamanya, ayio chisokoro chiaito chiatotebetie.
english: what we have heard and known, what our fathers have told us.

ekegusii: Inwe abamore ne chimeme chi’obong’ainereria, ngento ki moraegwe, na mang’ana ki naende morakorerwe?
english: What will he do to you, and what more besides, O deceitful tongue?

ekegusii: ninki ndakore ekero Nyasae aranyimokere? Ninki ndamoiranerie ekero arabe okorua egesusuro ki’ebibe biane?
english: what will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when called to account?

ekegusii: Ngento ki morakore ase rituko riria egesusuro kegocha? Ninki morakore ekero ekembugu‐mbugu kerache korwa aare? Ning’o moratamere abakonye? Ning’o moratigere obotenenku bwaino?
english: What will you do on the day of reckoning, when disaster comes from afar? To whom will you run for help? Where will you leave your riches?

ekegusii: Ninki morakore ekero Rituko Rinene ri’omoyega bw’Omonene riraike?
english: What will you do on the day of your appointed feasts, on the festival days of the LORD?

ekegusii: Ninki oratebe ekero abanto abwo gwakorire koba abasani bao barabe abatang’ani igoro asore? Inee! Tokoba nobororo obonene buna obw’omokungu okobina aibore?
english: What will you say when [the LORD] sets over you those you cultivated as your special allies? Will not pain grip you like that of a woman in labor?

ekegusii: Ayio abanto abang’aini batebetigwe ne chisokoro chiabo, nabarabwo tibayabisete.
english: what wise men have declared, hiding nothing received from their fathers

ekegusii: Erio ekero orabe gokoroberia gokora gento kende gionsi, ekio nkebe bo, na oborabu mbomoreke chinchera chiao.
english: What you decide on will be done, and light will shine on your ways.

ekegusii: Eke gwakorire nigo kere ekebe. Ekeene, buna Omonene are moyo, nigo mogwenerete goitwa, ekiagera mwasinyirwe korenda omonene oino, oyore omoakwa amaguta bw’Omonene. Bono ritimo ri’omoruoti, na ekerandi keria ki’amache kiarenge ang’e nomotwe oye, ng’ai bikare?”
english: What you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, you and your men deserve to die, because you did not guard your master, the LORD's anointed. Look around you. Where are the king's spear and water jug that were near his head?"

ekegusii: Nabo onsi aya mogokwana ase omosunte, naigugwe ase omobaso; naro aya mokomonyererana ase ebinyomba ime nararigwe igoro ase ebirama.
english: What you have said in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the roofs.

ekegusii: Bwatia amang’ana ayare ay’obogima, ayakwaigwete korwa asende, abe ekiorokererio ogotunyana ase okwegena na obwanchani bire ase Kristo Yeso.
english: What you heard from me, keep as the pattern of sound teaching, with faith and love in Christ Jesus.

ekegusii: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
english: Aya momanyete, nainche ninyamanyete; inwe timombueti kende.

ekegusii: Gaki Apolo inki aisaine? Na Paulo inki aisaine? Intwe nabakori emeremo, ababorokereirie komwegena Omonene, kera oyomo buna Omonene amoeire.
english: What, after all, is Apollos? And what is Paul? Only servants, through whom you came to believe-- as the Lord has assigned to each his task.

ekegusii: Ninki rende toratebe ase ayio? Onye Nyasae ore ensemo yaito, ning’o oranyare gotobua?
english: What, then, shall we say in response to this? If God is for us, who can be against us?

ekegusii: Amachiko rende, inki agwenete? Akamentwa ase engencho y’amamocho, goika omoiborwa oria orieretwe eira anyare gocha. Amachiko aria nigo aruetwe goetera ase abamalaika ase okoboko kw’omobwatania.
english: What, then, was the purpose of the law? It was added because of transgressions until the Seed to whom the promise referred had come. The law was put into effect through angels by a mediator.

ekegusii: erio nebe ng’a onde bwensi orasoke korwa ase egesieri ki’enyomba yane abe omotang’ani kondotota ekero ndairane korwa ase Abaamoni inde nobobui, oyio nabe oyoo, Omonene, na inche nimorue abe ekeng’wanso ki’ogosambwa asore.”
english: whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in triumph from the Ammonites will be the LORD's, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering."

ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi kereo nigo kiarogetwe erieta korwa kare, naende nigo yamanyekanete eki omonto are gocha koba. Mwanyabanto takonyara koamererania noria ore ne chinguru komobua.
english: Whatever exists has already been named, and what man is has been known; no man can contend with one who is stronger than he.

ekegusii: Korende orogendo rwaino robe buna egwenerete enchili ya Kristo, erinde onye ngocha kobarora inwe, gose tinkobao, nyigwe amang’ana aino ng’a moteneine bokong’u ase omoika oyomo, na ase omoyo oyomo mokorwanerera okwegena more nakwo ase enchili amo.
english: Whatever happens, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you in my absence, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, contending as one man for the faith of the gospel

ekegusii: Naende enyomba ende yonsi morasoe, mobeere aroro goika moruo.
english: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that town.

ekegusii: Amang’ana areo bono, nao arenge korwa kare; na ayio agochia koba, boigo nao arenge korwa kare. Nyasae nigo akorigia ayio aetire.
english: Whatever is has already been, and what will be has been before; and God will call the past to account.

ekegusii: Na kende gionsi abakuani bare agwo Yerusalemu baraganie baegwe. Kera rituko nigo baraegwe chieri chinsae, ne chimingichi gose ching’ondi, chibe ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa ase Nyasae o igoro. Boigo baegwe engano, na omonyo, na edivai, na amaguta ’amasabibu. Baegwe ebinto ebio, tibamocha kobiegwa.
english: Whatever is needed-- young bulls, rams, male lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine and oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem-- must be given them daily without fail,

ekegusii: “Ebiegwa bionsi ebichenu Abaisraeli barandetere inche Omonene nakobieire aye amo nabana bao, abamura na abaiseke, bibe ebitari biaino kogenderera botambe. Okwo nokobwatana kw’ogotianania kw’omonyo gwa kare na kare ase obosio bwane inche Omonene, okwo nakorire naye na ororeria rwao.”
english: Whatever is set aside from the holy offerings the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and your sons and daughters as your regular share. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the LORD for both you and your offspring."

ekegusii: Aande onsi ase Saulo arenge gotoma Daudi, Daudi nigo arenge konyora obobui. Ase ayio Saulo akamobeka akaba omotang’ani bw’abarwani. Daudi igo anyorete ogwancherwa kw’abanto bonsi na okw’abasomba ba Saulo.
english: Whatever Saul sent him to do, David did it so successfully that Saul gave him a high rank in the army. This pleased all the people, and Saul's officers as well.

ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi Nyasae o igoro arachike ng’a gekorwe, ekio gekorwe boronge ase engencho y’enyomba ya Nyasae o igoro, erinde endamwamu ya Nyasae tebaisa koba igoro y’oboruoti bwane, na abamura baane.
english: Whatever the God of heaven has prescribed, let it be done with diligence for the temple of the God of heaven. Why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and of his sons?

ekegusii: Echio chiremerie ase omwaka bw’ogotimoka gw’ense eria, nachio chirabe chindagera chibaisaine, aye omonyene, na abasomba bao, abamura na abaiseke, na omokori emeremo oo orikire, na omomenyi omenyete bwoo.
english: Whatever the land yields during the sabbath year will be food for you-- for yourself, your manservant and maidservant, and the hired worker and temporary resident who live among you,

ekegusii: Inki mokoroberia igoro y’Omonene? Ere nabasirie kegima, takorenta egesusuro eria kabere.
english: Whatever they plot against the LORD he will bring to an end; trouble will not come a second time.

ekegusii: Onde bwensi orakune enyama y’ekeng’wanso ekio nabe omochenu; naboigo na kende gionsi kerayekune, na amanyinga ’ekeng’wanso ekio aise gotonyera eanga, eyio esiberigwe agwo aase achenire.
english: Whatever touches any of the flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in a holy place.

ekegusii: Amang’ana aria nigo akare aare mono, naende akare aatambe gochia inse, aatambe mono, ning’o oranyare koyatuka?
english: Whatever wisdom may be, it is far off and most profound-- who can discover it?

ekegusii: Rinde rionsi mogokora rikore ase enkoro y’omogoko, buna mogokorera Omonene, gose tari mwanyabanto,
english: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for men,

ekegusii: Amang’ana aya mweorokereretie na koyanyora, na koyaigwa, na koyarora korwa asende, moyakore, na Nyasae bw’omorembe nabe amo nainwe.
english: Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me-- put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you.

ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi okoboko kwao koranyare gokora, gekore ne chinguru chiao chionsi; ekiagera agwo aase abakure ase oragende, meremo ende tekaiyo, gose okorengereria, gose chisemi, gose obong’aini.
english: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in the grave, where you are going, there is neither working nor planning nor knowledge nor wisdom.

ekegusii: Orende mono, oikeranie egento gwakwanete nomonwa oo, ekiagera nigo kwariete eira y’ogwancha ase Omonene, Nyasae oo.
english: Whatever your lips utter you must be sure to do, because you made your vow freely to the LORD your God with your own mouth.

ekegusii: Ekero ense yasaririe nigo ekoba nabagambi abange, korende eye ebwate abanto bare nobong’aini na okomanya, obogambi nigo bokogenderera gotenena bokong’u.
english: When a country is rebellious, it has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.

ekegusii: Inee! Omonto okorema ng’a asimeke chimbusuro nigo akogenderera kona‐korema rioka? Inee! Omonto oyio nigo akogenderera kona‐koboosa rioka?
english: When a farmer plows for planting, does he plow continually? Does he keep on breaking up and harrowing the soil?

ekegusii: Naende embeo ya irianyi egachia kogusa ake, bagakaga ng’a banyorire eki barigetie konyora, bakang’usa ekerochi, bakagenda ang’e na Kirete, ang’e mono nengegu.
english: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had obtained what they wanted; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.

ekegusii: Omoruoti ogoikaransa ase ekerogo kiaye gi’ekegambero nigo agoserebania amabe onsi namaiso aye.
english: When a king sits on his throne to judge, he winnows out all evil with his eyes.

ekegusii: Omosasoko ore ase obosio bw’omoruoti nigo ore obogima, na ogwancherwa kwaye nigo konga buna amare agotwa embura y’okwamia endagera.
english: When a king's face brightens, it means life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.

ekegusii: Ense nigo ebekire inse y’amaboko ’abakori amabe, Nyasae otubire amasio ’abagambi ebina. Onye tari ere, ning’o rende okorire ayio?
english: When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?

ekegusii: Inee! Onye omonto onyorire omobisa oye, nanyare komotiga ore moyo? Ase ayio Omonene tiga akoe eng’eria yao ase amaya aya gwankoreire ase rituko ria rero.
english: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him get away unharmed? May the LORD reward you well for the way you treated me today.

ekegusii: Omonto onye orarire nomokungu, na omobekeire embusuro y’oroiboro, bonsi babere goika besibie emebere yabo namache, nabarabwo nababe abatachenegeti goika omogoroba oyio.
english: When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

ekegusii: Ekero omonto akoria eira ase Omonene, gose agotiana ng’a netange korwa ase egento gete, tagosaria eira eria yaye. Goika akore na goikerania buna akwanete.
english: When a man makes a vow to the LORD or takes an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word but must do everything he said.

ekegusii: ekero omonto antebetie igoro y’ogokwa gwa Saulo, na okagete ng’a igo andeteire amang’ana amaya, inche nigo namobwatete nkamoita aaria Sikilagi. Oko nakwo ogoakana namoete ase amang’ana aye.
english: when a man told me, 'Saul is dead,' and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and put him to death in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news!

ekegusii: Ekero chinchera chi’omonto chiagokirie Omonene, Omonene nigo agokora nonya nababisa b’omonto oyio babwatana nere.
english: When a man's ways are pleasing to the LORD, he makes even his enemies live at peace with him.

ekegusii: Ekero omonto omonyacheche akonyora egesusuro, oria otamanyeti amange nigo akoba omong’aini; na ekero omonto omong’aini akworokererigwa nigo akonyora chisemi.
english: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; when a wise man is instructed, he gets knowledge.

ekegusii: Nyuma ya kera omoyega koerire, mambia chuni Ayubu nigo arenge koruera kera omwana oye ekeng’wanso ase okomochena. Nigo arenge gokora igo, ekiagera arenge korengereria, oteba, “Ande nebe ng’a onde bw’abana baane okorire ebibe, oramire Nyasae ase enkoro yaye ime.” Naboigo Ayubu arenge gokora botambe.
english: When a period of feasting had run its course, Job would send and have them purified. Early in the morning he would sacrifice a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This was Job's regular custom.

ekegusii: Omokungu o Samaria agacha kobuucha amache. Yeso akamotebia, “Ing’a amache inywe.”
english: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, "Will you give me a drink?"

ekegusii: Ekero ebiku bikorenta amakweri a mobosokano, na abanto batari na komocha banyorwe namaakwa, ere nigo akobachecheria.
english: When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent.

ekegusii: Ekero morabugie ekerombeta ase eriogi ri’ogotabobora, abanto bare ase ebitwori bi’ensemo ya moocha baimoke bachake orogendo rwabo.
english: When a trumpet blast is sounded, the tribes camping on the east are to set out.

ekegusii: Inee! Egetureri gi’esegi nkebugigwe ase omochie, na abanto tibaba nobwoba? Amang’ana amabe nabe ase omochie, Omonene atayatometi?
english: When a trumpet sounds in a city, do not the people tremble? When disaster comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?

ekegusii: Ekero omokori amabe agokwa, ogosemeria kwaye nigo kogokwa amo nere, ee, aya abwo batamoirogeti Nyasae basemeretie nigo agosira.
english: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; all he expected from his power comes to nothing.

ekegusii: Na rora, omokungu oyomo ase omochie oria, oyorenge omonyene ebibe, agachia konyora amang’ana ng’a oikaransire ase enyomba y’Omofarisai oria, akarenta echuba ye rigena rirabu ere namaguta e rimisu rigiya,
english: When a woman who had lived a sinful life in that town learned that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume,

ekegusii: Haroni na abanto bonsi, ekero baroche buna risankwa ri’obosio bwa Musa riare komeka‐meka, bakoboa komoika ang’e.
english: When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.

ekegusii: Ekero Haroni ayeroche, akaagacha egesasimero bosio bw’omogwekano oria. Erio akararia, akabora, “Ankio nigo rirabe Rituko Rinene ri’Omonene.”
english: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, "Tomorrow there will be a festival to the LORD."

ekegusii: Ekero Abigaeli aroche Daudi agaika bwango korwa ase etigere, agekumba inse, akaumama ase obosio bwa Daudi.
english: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off her donkey and bowed down before David with her face to the ground.

ekegusii: Ekero Abigaeli aigete nka, akanyora Nabali obwate omoyega omonene oyoisaine omoruoti agokora. Nabali nigo arenge nomochengo ase enkoro yaye ime, ekiagera konya otindire mono. Ase ayio Abigaeli tamotebetie gento kende, korende akaganya goika bogakia mambia.
english: When Abigail went to Nabal, he was in the house holding a banquet like that of a king. He was in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until daybreak.

ekegusii: Abimeleki agatebigwa ng’a abanto bonsi b’Omorobiri o Sekemu nigo bagasangererekanete amo.
english: When Abimelech heard that they had assembled there,

ekegusii: Ekero Abineri amo nabanto bande emerongo ebere baigete Heburoni ase Daudi, ere akabakorera omoyega.
english: When Abner, who had twenty men with him, came to David at Hebron, David prepared a feast for him and his men.

ekegusii: Ekero omosomba o Ibrahimu aigwete amang’ana abo, agatung’ama inse ase obosio bw’Omonene.
english: When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.

ekegusii: Ekero Aburamu asoete Misiri, Abamisiri bakarora omokungu oyio ng’a nigo arenge omonyakieni mono.
english: When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that she was a very beautiful woman.

ekegusii: Aburamu agachia koigwa ng’a oyomwabo osakoirwe na gwoswa, agatoma abamura baye abakong’u, abaiboire bwoye, abamanyire korwana esegi, babwatie ababisa goika Dani. Abarwani aba nigo barenge amagana atato, na ikomi na batano na batato.
english: When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and went in pursuit as far as Dan.

ekegusii: Ekero Aburamu abeire nemiaka emerongo kianda, na kianda (99). Omonene akamoorokera, akamotebia, “Inche ninche Nyasae Omobui; genderera ase obosio bwane, na obe omoikeranu.
english: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty; walk before me and be blameless.

ekegusii: Ekero abasomba b’Abisalomu bachete ase omokungu oria nyomba ime, bakamoboria, “Ng’ai Yonathani na Ahimasi bare?” Omokungu oria akabatebia, “Bambokire orooche orwo, bachiire.” Ekero abanto baria babarigetie tibabarora, bakairana Yerusalemu.
english: When Absalom's men came to the woman at the house, they asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman answered them, "They crossed over the brook." The men searched but found no one, so they returned to Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Inyora buna Akani, mosinto o Zera, amochete ase ebinto biria biatananetwe ase ogosirigwa; omoganda bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli nigo onyorete egesusuro ase engencho eyio, tari omonto oria bweka osirete ase ogosaria koria.”
english: When Achan son of Zerah acted unfaithfully regarding the devoted things, did not wrath come upon the whole community of Israel? He was not the only one who died for his sin.'"

ekegusii: Ekero Akisi arenge koboria Daudi, “Insemo ki gwachiete korwania rituko ria rero?” “Daudi aba okomoiraneria,” “Ense ya Irianyi ere ey’Abayuda,” gose “Ense ya Irianyi ere eya Yerameeli,” gose “Ense ya Irianyi ere ey’Abakeni,”
english: When Achish asked, "Where did you go raiding today?" David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah" or "Against the Negev of Jerahmeel" or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."

ekegusii: Ekero Adamu abeire nemiaka rigana erimo na emerongo etato (130), akaibora omwana omomura ase omogwekano oye, omogwekaine, akamoroka Seti.
english: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Seth.

ekegusii: Erio kegima, ekero Ahabu aigwete ng’a Naboti okure, akaimoka akagenda ase omogondo oria bw’emesabibu o Naboti Omoyesireeli, akayoira okaba oyoye.
english: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take possession of Naboth's vineyard.

ekegusii: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and went around meekly.
english: Ekero Ahabu aigwete amang’ana aria, agatandora chianga chiaye, na akeboyia chigunia, na kweng’ata. Akararera chigunia, akaba omokanyeku ore nomoichano.

ekegusii: Ekero Ahasi, mosinto o Yotamu mosinto o Usia, arenge omoruoti bw’Abayuda, Resini, omoruoti bw’Abasiiria, na Peka, omoruoti bw’Abaisraeli, mosinto o Remalia, abwo babere bagatiira gochia Yerusalemu koyorwania, korende tibanyarete koyobua.
english: When Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up to fight against Jerusalem, but they could not overpower it.

ekegusii: Ekero Ahasia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, aroche amang’ana aria, agatama gochia ase ensemo ya Beti‐Hagani. Yehu akamobwatia korwa nyuma, agateba, “Morase nere boigo!” Na ekero arenge ase egari yaye ime ogotiira gochia Guri, ang’e na Ibileamu, bakamorasa. Erio agatama goika Megido agakwera aroro.
english: When Ahaziah king of Judah saw what had happened, he fled up the road to Beth Haggan. Jehu chased him, shouting, "Kill him too!" They wounded him in his chariot on the way up to Gur near Ibleam, but he escaped to Megiddo and died there.

ekegusii: Ekero Ahitofeli aroche ng’a ogosemia kwaye kwangirwe, akariina etigere yaye, akagenda omochie oye, na karobeirie amang’ana ’enyomba yaye, akagenda agesunga, agakwa. Gakure agatindekwa ase oboina bwa ise.
english: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his house in order and then hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father's tomb.

ekegusii: Ekero enchara yariete abanto bonsi ba Misiri, barabwo bakamorera Farao abae endagera; na Farao agatebia Abamisiri bonsi, “Genda ase Yusufu, na rinde rionsi arabatebie, goika morikore.”
english: When all Egypt began to feel the famine, the people cried to Pharaoh for food. Then Pharaoh told all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph and do what he tells you."

ekegusii: ekero Abaisraeli bonsi bagocha ase obosio bw’Omonene, Nyasae oino, aase agwo arachore, osome amachiko onsi, erinde Abaisraeli bonsi bayaigwe.
english: when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before them in their hearing.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli bonsi bakaigwa chinkuma chi’ekina ekio omoruoti agambete; erio bakairoka omoruoti, ekiagera nigo baroche ng’a obong’aini bwa Nyasae nigo bwarenge ime yaye ase okogamba kw’oboronge.
