english: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell with her face to the ground to pay him honor, and she said, "Help me, O king!"

ekegusii: Korende ekero omokungu oria aroche Samweli, agakuura neriogi rinene agatebia Saulo, “Nase ki kwang’aina? Aye n’Saulo.”
english: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out at the top of her voice and said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

ekegusii: Omokungu agachia korora omote oria ng’a nomuya ore ase okoriegwa na okogwenera amaiso, na omote oria noyo bw’okoganigwa, ekiagera okobaa okomanya, agatwa amatunda aye, akaria. Erio akaa omosacha oye, nere akaria.
english: When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.

ekegusii: Ekero omwaka bw’Omochengo oraike ase Abaisraeli omwando obo nigo orarusigwe korwa ase omwando bw’egesaku keria keranyuome abaiseke abwo. Obwando obo nigo orarusigwe korwa ase omwando bw’egesaku giaito.”
english: When the Year of Jubilee for the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and their property will be taken from the tribal inheritance of our forefathers."

ekegusii: When the years are many, you are to increase the price, and when the years are few, you are to decrease the price, because what he is really selling you is the number of crops.
english: Onye emiaka ere emenge, nomente rigori, onye ere emeke, norikeeyie, ekiagera egento ekio agokooneria nomobaro bw’okwama kw’omogondo.

ekegusii: When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he had great wealth.
english: Ekero achia koigwa ring’ana riria, omomura oria akagenda nobororo, ekiagera arenge nenibo enyinge.

ekegusii: nanga nigo batomerete gatore moyo, ekiagera babete nendamwamu enene asetore;
english: when their anger flared against us, they would have swallowed us alive;

ekegusii: Na ekero abaise, gose abamura bamwabo, barache kobasoera asetore, intwe nigo torabatebie: Komoranche mobabatigere, ekiagera titwanyorerete kera omonto omokungu ekero gi’esegi, na ekiagera inwe abanyene timwababaete babe abakungu babo, timori nokomocha kw’ogosaria eira eria twatiananetie.”
english: When their fathers or brothers complain to us, we will say to them, 'Do us a kindness by helping them, because we did not get wives for them during the war, and you are innocent, since you did not give your daughters to them.'"

ekegusii: Ekero omoika orure ase omonto, ere nigo akoirana ase amaroba, ase arwete. Ase rituko erio erio emeroberio yaye nigo egosira.
english: When their spirit departs, they return to the ground; on that very day their plans come to nothing.

ekegusii: Inche nigo naiboretwe chindiba chitarabao, nonya ne chinsoko chi’amache.
english: When there were no oceans, I was given birth, when there were no springs abounding with water;

ekegusii: Amatuko ayio kaerire, akaroisia omoyega omonene ase abanto bonsi, abanene na abake, abarenge agwo Susa, omochie omonene. Omoyega oyio okabeera ase eraaro y’egeticha yagiteire, yarenge ase enyomba y’omoruoti, na okagenderera ase amatuko atano na abere.
english: When these days were over, the king gave a banquet, lasting seven days, in the enclosed garden of the king's palace, for all the people from the least to the greatest, who were in the citadel of Susa.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baria batano basoete nyomba mwa Mika na korusia omogwekano oria obaachire, na egesibao keria ki’obokuani, na ebinyasae biria, na omogwekano oria onyititoire na kobombwa, omokuani oria akababoria, “Inki eke mogokora?”
english: When these men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the other household gods and the cast idol, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

ekegusii: Nabo karachake koba ayio, rigereria igoro, ekiagera okoboorigwa kwaino gwaikire ang’e.”
english: When these things begin to take place, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."

ekegusii: Abana baboorigwe ekero bakoorire omotienyi oyomo, ne ching’iti boigo. Aye nobeke rigori ri’okobooria, ribe chisekeli isano chie chifeta, koreng’ana nesekeli egokorerwa ase Obomenyo Obochenu. (Esekeli eyemo nechigera ibere.)
english: When they are a month old, you must redeem them at the redemption price set at five shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs.

ekegusii: Ekero Saulo amo nomosomba oye baigete Gibea, ekeombe ekenene ki’ababani gekaumerana nere. Omoika o Nyasae ogacha igoro asare ne chinguru, nere agachaka kobaboka ase okobana ase egati y’ababani baria.
english: When they arrived at Gibeah, a procession of prophets met him; the Spirit of God came upon him in power, and he joined in their prophesying.

ekegusii: Bagaika Salami, bakarandia ring’ana ria Nyasae ase chisinagogi chi’Abayahudi, na barabwo nigo barenge na Yohana okobakonya.
english: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.

ekegusii: Na abateneneri bande be chiamate chiria ekero bachete ase enyomba y’Omonene agwo Yerusalemu, bakarua ebiegwa bi’ogwancha ase okoagachera enyomba ya Nyasae aase aye.
english: When they arrived at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the families gave freewill offerings toward the rebuilding of the house of God on its site.

ekegusii: Bagachia goika asare, akabatebia, “Inwe abanyene mwamanyire buna narenge egati yaino ekero gionsi korwa rituko rie ritang’ani nachagete gotacha aiga Asia,
english: When they arrived, he said to them: "You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I came into the province of Asia.

ekegusii: Ekero bachete agwo, Samweli akarigereria Eliabu, erio akarengereria, “Ekeene, omonto oyo oteneine aiga ase obosio bw’Omonene, nere omoakwa amaguta oye.”
english: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, "Surely the LORD's anointed stands here before the LORD."

ekegusii: Barabwo bagatirimboka, bakabasabera, erinde banyore Omoika Omochenu,
english: When they arrived, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit,

ekegusii: Ekero bachia gosoa, bakariina akanyomba ka irongo aase baikaransete: Petero na Yohana, Yakobo na Anderea, Filipo na Tomas, Baritholomayo na Matayo, Yakobo bw’Alufayo na Simion, oyomo bw’Abazelote, na Yuda o Yakobo.
english: When they arrived, they went upstairs to the room where they were staying. Those present were Peter, John, James and Andrew; Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew; James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

ekegusii: Ekero bamoboretie amente amatuko ande komenya amo nabarabwo, akaanga.
english: When they asked him to spend more time with them, he declined.

ekegusii: agwo ekero ebibe biria birabe biamanyekanire, omosangererekano orue eeri ensae ebe ekeng’wanso ki’ebibe na koyerenta agwo bosio bw’Eema y’Omosangererekano.
english: When they become aware of the sin they committed, the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the Tent of Meeting.

ekegusii: Bakarentera Yeso emori eria y’etigere, bakaara chianga igoro asero, na Yeso akayeriina.
english: When they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, he sat on it.

ekegusii: Bakairana korwa ase oboina, bagatebia baria ikomi nomo na baria abande bonsi amang’ana ayio onsi.
english: When they came back from the tomb, they told all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.

ekegusii: Ase igo ekero basangererekanete aiga, tintebaneti, korende rituko ria kabere ngaikaransa ase ekerogo kiane gi’ekegambero, ngachika omonto oyo arentwe.
english: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto abwo b’egesaku kia Reuben na ekia Dani amo nekeng’ese gi’ekia Manase baigete Yorodan mbarabare ase ensemo ya Kanani bakaagacha aroro egesasimero ekenene kiare kororekana korwa are.
english: When they came to Geliloth near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an imposing altar there by the Jordan.

ekegusii: Ekero baigete Yerusalemu bakaroisigwa nekanisa amo nabatomwa na abagaaka, bakaborokia amang’ana onsi aya Nyasae akorete nabarabwo.
english: When they came to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and elders, to whom they reported everything God had done through them.

ekegusii: Na barabwo bagachia goika ase Yeso, bakamosorora, bakabora, “Nagwenerete omokorere ring’ana eri,
english: When they came to Jesus, they pleaded earnestly with him, "This man deserves to have you do this,

ekegusii: Bagachiera Yeso, bakarora omonto oria obwatire nomoganda bw’ebirecha oikaransete, bweboyetie chianga, ore nebirengererio ebironge bakairoka.
english: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons, sitting there, dressed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

ekegusii: Erio bagaika aase are korokwa Mara, tibanyara konywa amache arengeo, ekiagera arenge amaroro mono. Nakio kiagerete aase aria akarokwa Mara.
english: When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. (That is why the place is called Marah.)

ekegusii: Ekero bachia goika kororia Misia, bagateema kogenda Bitinia, korende Omoika o Yeso tobaa ribaga.
english: When they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not allow them to.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia goika ase omoganda, omonto oyomo akamochiera agwo, akamotung’amera, akabora,
english: When they came to the crowd, a man approached Jesus and knelt before him.

ekegusii: Bagaika enyomba y’omonene oria bw’esinagogi; akarora riroroche, na abanto bakorera nokweumia okonge.
english: When they came to the home of the synagogue ruler, Jesus saw a commotion, with people crying and wailing loudly.

ekegusii: Kobaikire ase aborokigwa bande, bakarora omoganda omonene obaetanaine; aborokia b’amariko bakaengererania nabarabwo.
english: When they came to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and the teachers of the law arguing with them.

ekegusii: Bagachia goika aase akorokwa Ekeore, bakamobamba aroro, na baria abasaria, oyomo ensemo y’okoboko gw’okorio, na oyonde ensemo y’okoboko gw’okobee.
english: When they came to the place called the Skull, there they crucified him, along with the criminals-- one on his right, the other on his left.

ekegusii: Ekero baigete ase ekeooreri gia Kidoni, Usa akarambora okoboko kwaye gosiira Esanduku eria, ekiagera chiombe chiare kong’usa egari chiagochetwe.
english: When they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, because the oxen stumbled.

ekegusii: Ekero barabwo baikire ase ekeooreri kia Nakoni, chiombe chiarenge kong’usa egari eria chikarichanigwa. Ase igo Usa akarambora okoboko kwaye gosiira Esanduku eyio ya Nyasae.
english: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen stumbled.

ekegusii: Ekero baigete ase Yakobo ise, ase ense ya Kanani, bakamotebia ayio onsi abanyorete, bakabora,
english: When they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they told him all that had happened to them. They said,

ekegusii: Rigoro basangererekanete Galili, Yeso akabatebia, “Omwana‐o‐mwanyabanto ngochia are kobekwa ase amaboko ’abanto.
english: When they came together in Galilee, he said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be betrayed into the hands of men.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia korwa ase amache, Omoika bw’Omonene ogataboria Filipo; omogomba oria tamorora naende, korende nigo agendete enchera yaye ore nomogoko.
english: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him again, but went on his way rejoicing.

ekegusii: Barabwo bagachora chinyasae chinyia, erio chisegi chikaba ase ebiita biabo. Ase abanto chilifu emerongo ene ase Abaisraeli, inee, onde obo narorekanete ore nenguba gose ritimo?
english: When they chose new gods, war came to the city gates, and not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.

ekegusii: Naende kobakorwa echiiro, tibakoria batesibeti. Naende nchire chingencho chinde babwate buna ogosibia ebikombe ne chinyongo, na ebinto bie chitaai.)
english: When they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And they observe many other traditions, such as the washing of cups, pitchers and kettles.)

ekegusii: Ekiagera batanyorete ribaga ri’okomoira ime ase engencho y’omoganda oria bw’abanto, bakariina kerama igoro, bakamoikia korwa kerama noborere bwaye goika gati‐gati ase obosio bwa Yeso.
english: When they could not find a way to do this because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.

ekegusii: ekero chire ase amakuruma abo chieringanetie ase okoboera, gose gochiramaime agwo ase chiebisete?
english: when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in a thicket?

ekegusii: When they did not find him, they went back to Jerusalem to look for him.
english: Ekero batamonyorete, bakairana Yerusalemu, bakamorigia.

ekegusii: Barabwo banywe, batinde bataba‐tabe, babe buna chiosi, ase engencho y’esegi ndarente igoro asebare.”
english: When they drink it, they will stagger and go mad because of the sword I will send among them."

ekegusii: Ekero emechando eyio erabachere, abanto ba Nyasae nabanyore ogokonywa ogoke. Abanto abange mbabwatane nabarabwo ase obong’ainereria bw’okweansia.
english: When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many who are not sincere will join them.

ekegusii: Kobakoorire gokwana, Yakobo akairaneria, “Abaminto, ntegerera.
english: When they finished, James spoke up: "Brothers, listen to me.

ekegusii: Na ekaba ase omochakano obo bw’okomenya aroro tibamoirogete Omonene; ase ayio Omonene agatoma chindo ase egati yabo, chigaita abanto bande babo.
english: When they first lived there, they did not worship the LORD; so he sent lions among them and they killed some of the people.

ekegusii: Goika bagachia komorora ng’umbu y’enyancha bakamoboria, “Omworokia, indi gwachete aa?”
english: When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"

ekegusii: Ekero batarasoka gochia ase abanto bare ase eraaro ya isiko goika barusie chianga echio chi’obokoreri, bachitige agwo ase ebinyomba biria ebichenu, na babeke chianga ching’ao. Batakoreti bo, nigo barabaise gochena abanto ne chianga echio chiabo.
english: When they go out into the outer court where the people are, they are to take off the clothes they have been ministering in and are to leave them in the sacred rooms, and put on other clothes, so that they do not consecrate the people by means of their garments.

ekegusii: Mbaire amaicho e chitugo chiabo bagende korigia Omonene, korende tibakomonyora, ekiagera nabe bweatananirie korwa asebare.
english: When they go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, they will not find him; he has withdrawn himself from them.

ekegusii: Ekero barabe bakogendao, nindambore ekeonga kiane mbabwatere imeo buna chinyoni chikobwatwa. Nimbae egesusuro ase okobarongeyia, koreng’ana buna omosangererekano obo bworokererigwe.
english: When they go, I will throw my net over them; I will pull them down like birds of the air. When I hear them flocking together, I will catch them.

ekegusii: Mambia chuni, ekero baimogete na erioba rikaoroka rikabara ase amache, Abamoabu bakarora amache arenge bosio bwabo are amabariri buna amanyinga.
english: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water. To the Moabites across the way, the water looked red-- like blood.

ekegusii: When they grasped you with their hands, you splintered and you tore open their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and their backs were wrenched.
english: Ekero bakoboanetie namaboko abo, aye okabuneka, okabang’waroria amareko abo. Ekero bagwesiirerete okabuneka, ogatengechia ebibono biabo.

ekegusii: Kobachia koigota, agatebia aborokigwa baye, “Sangereria ebisamunye biatigaire, gento tigesira.”
english: When they had all had enough to eat, he said to his disciples, "Gather the pieces that are left over. Let nothing be wasted."

ekegusii: Abanto bagasangererekana agwo Misipa, bakabuucha amache, bakayaumora agwo ase obosio bw’Omonene, bakeng’ata ase rituko erio, bagakwana aroro agwo, “Twakorire ebibe ase Omonene.” Erio Samweli akaba okogambera Abaisraeli agwo Misipa.
english: When they had assembled at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. On that day they fasted and there they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel was leader of Israel at Mizpah.

ekegusii: Abalawi aba bagasangereria abanto bamwabo, erio bonsi bagechena, bagasoa ase enyomba y’Omonene bakayechena buna omoruoti konya arure ogochika koreng’ana ne ring’ana ri’Omonene.
english: When they had assembled their brothers and consecrated themselves, they went in to purify the temple of the LORD, as the king had ordered, following the word of the LORD.

ekegusii: Ekero abaruoti baria barentetwe ase Yoshua, ere akarangeria Abaisraeli bonsi amo, agatebia abatang’ani b’abarwani, abwo bagendete amo nere ase esegi, “Inchuo aiga ang’e, motache amagoti ’abaruoti aba.” Erio barabwo bagaika ang’e, bakabatacha.
english: When they had brought these kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had come with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and placed their feet on their necks.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia goikerania onsi ayarikire igoro yaye, bakamoikia korwa ase omote, bakamobeka ase oboina.
english: When they had carried out all that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

ekegusii: Ekero bambokire bagaika ense ya Genesareti, bakabeka ekerochi.
english: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and anchored there.

ekegusii: Ekero bambokire, bagaika ense ya Genesareti.
english: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.

ekegusii: Ekero bambokire ng’umbu, Elija agatebia Elisha, “Boria egento ndanyare kogokorera ritang’ani ntararusigwa asore.” Elisha agateba, “Nagosabire, ong’e omoika oo ara kabere.”
english: When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me, what can I do for you before I am taken from you?" "Let me inherit a double portion of your spirit," Elisha replied.

ekegusii: When they had crucified him, they divided up his clothes by casting lots.
english: Kobamobambire bagaatanana chianga chiaye, bagakora obomera.

ekegusii: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break.
english: Kobakorire iga, bakanyora chinswe chinyinge mono, na ekero ebionga biabo biachaka gotandoka,

ekegusii: Kobaigotire bakagusuyia emeeri ase ogotuguta engano ase enyancha ime.
english: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

ekegusii: Abaisraeli kobakoorire gwatanana ense eria ase chinsemo ao ao, bakaa Yoshua, mosinto o Nuni, ensemo ase egati yabo, ebe omwando oye.
english: When they had finished dividing the land into its allotted portions, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them,

ekegusii: Erio kobakoorire koragera, Yeso akaboria Simion Petero, “Simion mosinto o Yohana, nonyanchete kobua aba?” Akamoiraneria, “Ee, Omonene, aye nomanyete ng’a ningwanchete.” Akamotebia, “Risia chimanwa chie ching’ondi chiane.”
english: When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of John, do you truly love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."

ekegusii: Ekero emeremo eria yaerete chibesa chiria chiatigarete chikarentwa ase omoruoti na Yehoyada. Korwa ase chibesa echio chie chifeta na echie chitahabu ebikorero bi’enyomba y’Omonene bikaroisigwa, ebitaabo na ebinto binde bigokorerwa ase omosangererekano, na ebi’ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa, na ebi’ogosambera ubani. Abanto bakaba bakorua ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa ase enyomba y’Omonene kogenderera botambe ase obogima bwonsi bwa Yehoyada.
english: When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made articles for the LORD's temple: articles for the service and for the burnt offerings, and also dishes and other objects of gold and silver. As long as Jehoiada lived, burnt offerings were presented continually in the temple of the LORD.

ekegusii: Ekero bagendire egeka getari geke korwa ase enka ya Mika, bagaikeerwa nabagisangio ba Mika abarangeretigwe kobabwatia.
english: When they had gone some distance from Micah's house, the men who lived near Micah were called together and overtook the Danites.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baria bamanoire kogenda, rora, omomalaika bw’Omonene akaorokera Yusufu ase chindoto, akamotebia, “Imoka korwa aa, oire omwana na ng’ina, otame gochia Misiri, omenye aroro goika ngotebie, ekiagera Herode narigie omwana oyo anyare komoita.”
english: When they had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. "Get up," he said, "take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is going to search for the child to kill him."

ekegusii: Erio kobaetire egati y’Amfipoli na Apolonia, bagaika Tesaloniki aase esinagogi y’Abayahudi yarenge.
english: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

ekegusii: Nabo kabang’usire obwato chimaeli isato gose inye bakarora Yeso ogotaara ase enyancha igoro, ogoika ang’e ase obwato. Erio bakairoka,
english: When they had rowed three or three and a half miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the water; and they were terrified.

ekegusii: Bagachia komorora, bakaorokia ring’ana batebetigwe igoro y’omwana oyio.
english: When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child,

ekegusii: When they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli,
english: Erio bakanyenya eeri eria, na bakaa Eli omwana oria.

ekegusii: Ekero chingige chiria chiakoorire koria ebimeri bionsi bi’ense, inche ngasaba, ngateba, “Aye Omonene Nyasae, nagosoroire bwabere! Naki abanto b’ororeria rwa Yakobo baranyare koba moyo, ekero bare abake iga?”
english: When they had stripped the land clean, I cried out, "Sovereign LORD, forgive! How can Jacob survive? He is so small!"

ekegusii: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
english: Kobakoorire gotera Ogotera, bagasoka kogenda egetunwa ki’Emezeituni.

ekegusii: Erio kabaorokirie oborori na korandia ring’ana ri’Omonene, bakairana Yerusalemu, bakorandia amang’ana amaya ase ebichie ebinge bi’Abasamaria.
english: When they had testified and proclaimed the word of the Lord, Peter and John returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many Samaritan villages.

ekegusii: Nabo ekero bachia koigwa amang’ana ’okobokigwa kw’abakure abande bagasekereria, na abande bagateba, “Inatogotegerere naende ase amang’ana ayio.”
english: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some of them sneered, but others said, "We want to hear you again on this subject."

ekegusii: na Yerusalemu, na Idumea, na ng’umbu ya Yorodan, ne chinsemo chia Turo na Sidoni. Omoganda oyo omonene, ochia koigwa ebirage bi’amang’ana onsi arenge gokora, okamochiera.
english: When they heard all he was doing, many people came to him from Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, and the regions across the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon.

ekegusii: Ekero baigwete amang’ana ayio, bakaonchoka bakarigererania bare nobwoba, bagatebia Baruku, “Goika totebie omoruoti amang’ana aya.”
english: When they heard all these words, they looked at each other in fear and said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."

ekegusii: Na ekero bachia koigwa ng’a nigo agokwana nabarabwo ase omonwa bw’Ekeibirania, bakamenta gokira. Agakwana,
english: When they heard him speak to them in Aramaic, they became very quiet. Then Paul said:

ekegusii: When they heard that Jesus was alive and that she had seen him, they did not believe it.
english: Na barabwo, bagachia koigwa ng’a moyo are, na ororirwe nere, tibegena.

ekegusii: Ekero eriogi eri riaigwetwe, omoganda ogasangererekana amo, okaba nogokumia, ekiagera kera oyomo abaigwete bagokwana ase omonwa oye omonyene.
english: When they heard this sound, a crowd came together in bewilderment, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.

ekegusii: When they heard this, the crowd and the city officials were thrown into turmoil.
english: Omoganda oria na abanene b’omochie bagaichana ekero baigwete aya.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia koigwa amang’ana aya, bagakira‐kiri. Na barabwo bagatogia Nyasae, bagoteba, “Gaki, Nyasae oeire abanto b’Ebisaku boigo okoonchoka gokorenta obogima.”
english: When they heard this, they had no further objections and praised God, saying, "So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life."

ekegusii: Barabwo, ekero bachia koigwa, bagatogia Nyasae, bakamotebia, “Oyominto, kwarorire ng’a Abayahudi chilifu chinyinge begenire; na barabwo bonsi nigo bare nomokia ng’a amachiko abwatwe.
english: When they heard this, they praised God. Then they said to Paul: "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia koyaigwa, bagaakera Nyasae amariogi abo amo, bakobora, “Omogambi omonene, aye naye gwakorete igoro na ense, na enyancha, na ebinto bionsi ebire imeo.
english: When they heard this, they raised their voices together in prayer to God. "Sovereign Lord," they said, "you made the heaven and the earth and the sea, and everything in them.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia koigwa ring’ana riria, bagakumia; bakamotiga, bakagenda.
english: When they heard this, they were amazed. So they left him and went away.

ekegusii: When they heard this, they were furious and began shouting: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
english: Ekero bachia koigwa aya bagaichorwa nendamwamu, bagaaka eriogi, bagateba, “Aritemi y’Abaefeso nenene!”

ekegusii: Ekero bachia koigwa amang’ana aya, bakagechigwa ase chinkoro chiabo ime, bakamoromananeria amaino.
english: When they heard this, they were furious and gnashed their teeth at him.

ekegusii: When they heard this, they were furious and wanted to put them to death.
english: Ekero bachia koigwa aya bakagechigwa, bakarigia kobaita.

ekegusii: Ere ekero arenge koramwa tairaneretie okoramwa okwo, ekero arenge gochandwa tatogonyete, korende akebeka asare ere oyokogamba ase oboronge.
english: When they hurled their insults at him, he did not retaliate; when he suffered, he made no threats. Instead, he entrusted himself to him who judges justly.

ekegusii: Barabwo kobamentire komoboria, akagororoka, akabatebia, “Ere oyotari nebibe ase egati yaino abe oyo bwe ritang’ani komoruta rigena.”
english: When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, "If any one of you is without sin, let him be the first to throw a stone at her."

ekegusii: Erio kobachia goika engegu, bakarora omorero bw’amakara aroro, na enswe ebekire igoro yaye, na omogati.
english: When they landed, they saw a fire of burning coals there with fish on it, and some bread.

ekegusii: Ekero baare korua ase Farao, bakanyora Musa na Haroni agwo nchera babaganyete,
english: When they left Pharaoh, they found Moses and Aaron waiting to meet them,

ekegusii: Abanto baria bakagenda gochia ase ebitunwa, bakebisa aroro amatuko atato, goika baria bababwatetie bakairana Yeriko. Barabwo bakaba bakobarigia ase chinchera chionsi, tibabanyora.
english: When they left, they went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had searched all along the road and returned without finding them.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia koimokia amaiso abo, tibarora monto otatiga Yeso bweka.
english: When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.

ekegusii: Ekero barabwo babekire emeriibo yabo ya inse ang’e neyane, na emetobwa yabo ang’e neyane, batigire orwaki rwabo ase egati yabo na inche, nigo bakorire erieta riane richenu riabeire eritachenegeti, ekiagera bakorire ay’okogechia. Ase ayio nabasiririe inde nendamwamu.
english: When they placed their threshold next to my threshold and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by their detestable practices. So I destroyed them in my anger.

ekegusii: Ekero baigete ase ense ya Sufu, Saulo agatebia omosomba oria barenge komo, “Bono tiga toirane gochia nka. Ande nigo tata aratige korengereria igoro ye chitigere, ne ribaga ri’ayio abe ogotochandekera intwe.”
english: When they reached the district of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, "Come, let's go back, or my father will stop thinking about the donkeys and start worrying about us."

ekegusii: Kobaikire aase aria atebetigwe na Nyasae, Ibrahimu akaagacha egesasimero agwo, akaara chinko igoro yaye, agasiba Isaka omwana oye, akamwareria igoro ye chinko chiria.
english: When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.

ekegusii: Ekero baigete ase ekeooreri gi’Atadi ng’umbu y’orooche rwa Yorodan, bakaba bakorera ebirero ebinene mono. Agwo Yusufu akagenderera komoreera ise ase engaki y’amatuko atano na abere.
english: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan, they lamented loudly and bitterly; and there Joseph observed a seven-day period of mourning for his father.

ekegusii: Bagaika ase rikura ri’Esikoli, na aroro bakabutora orosagia rw’emesabibu rwabwate egesago ekenene mono, bagasomeka omwaro ase orosagia roria, na abanto babere bakarwambana. Naende bagatwa amakomomanga na amako.
english: When they reached the Valley of Eshcol, they cut off a branch bearing a single cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole between them, along with some pomegranates and figs.

ekegusii: Erio kabaeirwe, bakaba nkwemurungania bare ase omonyene enyomba,
english: When they received it, they began to grumble against the landowner.

ekegusii: Bakairana, bagacha asare aase aganyete agwo Yeriko. Ere akabatebia, “Tinabakanetie ng’a timobaisa kogenda?”
english: When they returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"

ekegusii: Barabwo bakairana ase Yoshua, bakamotebia, “Tobaisa gotoma abanto bonsi. Abanto koreng’ana chilifu ibere, gose isato, mbaisane babue Ai. Tobaisa gotiga bonsi bechande kogenda, ekiagera abanyene omochie oria nabake.”
english: When they returned to Joshua, they said, "Not all the people will have to go up against Ai. Send two or three thousand men to take it and do not weary all the people, for only a few men are there."

ekegusii: Ekero abanto baria batano bairanete ase abamwabo agwo Sora na Esitaoli, barabwo bakababoria, “Mang’ana ki mwanyora?”
english: When they returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, "How did you find things?"

ekegusii: Bagachia komorora korwa aare, tibanyara komomanya gose nere. Bagachaka goaka amariogi bakorera; bagatandora chianga chiabo, bagesiarera ebuse gochia igoro na ase emetwe yabo.
english: When they saw him from a distance, they could hardly recognize him; they began to weep aloud, and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads.

ekegusii: Ekero bachia komorora, bakamosasima; korende abande mbabete nogosiereria.
english: When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some doubted.

ekegusii: Bono ekero abanene baria bachia korora oboremu bwa Petero na Yohana, na bakamanya ng’a nigo bare buna banto bande bonsi, batari ne chisemi, bagakumia. Erio bakamanya ng’a Petero na Yohana nigo konya babeire amo na Yeso.
english: When they saw the courage of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they were astonished and they took note that these men had been with Jesus.

ekegusii: Ekero barora eng’enang’eni eria, bagaichorwa nomogoko omonene mono.
english: When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.

ekegusii: Ekero abana babo bararore emeremo y’amaboko aane, eye nakorete ase egati yabo, mbachene erieta riane ime yabo, naende banche ng’a inche n’Omochenu o Yakobo inde, mbabe bateneine banyirogete inche Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli.
english: When they see among them their children, the work of my hands, they will keep my name holy; they will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

ekegusii: when they see the purity and reverence of your lives.
english: kobakorora orogendo rwaino oruya rore nokoiroka.

ekegusii: bakorera mono ekero bachia korora erioki ri’okoyia kwaye, bagateba, “Omochie ki ogwekaine omochie oyio omonene?”
english: When they see the smoke of her burning, they will exclaim, 'Was there ever a city like this great city?'

ekegusii: Bagatoma chirooti gochia Beteli. Omochie oyio nigo orenge korokwa Lusu agwo ritang’ani.
english: When they sent men to spy out Bethel (formerly called Luz),

ekegusii: ekero egochaka goseboka mwarora na komanya ase emioyo yaino ng’a embura yaisire gotwa.
english: When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.

ekegusii: Sisera agatebigwa ng’a Baraki, mosinto bw’Abinoamu, otiirire gochia ase egetunwa gia Tabori.
english: When they told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,

ekegusii: When they went across the lake, the disciples forgot to take bread.
english: Ekero aborokigwa baika ng’umbu, konya beebire koirana emegati.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto abwo basoete ase omochie, Isumaeli, mosinto o Netania, amo nabanto bande barenge komo, bagaita abanto abwo, erio bakaruta emebere yabo ime ase engoro yakunyire.
english: When they went into the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men who were with him slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern.

ekegusii: Ekero basoete rinani erio bakarora ng’a riaichoire nobooke, onde taboriete, ekiagera nigo bairogete okoragereria koria gwa Saulo.
english: When they went into the woods, they saw the honey oozing out, yet no one put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

ekegusii: Ekero barabwo baigete ase ense ya Gileadi, ase abanto b’egesaku kia Reuben, na ekia Gadi, na ekeng’ese ki’egesaku kia Manase, bagakwana nabarabwo, bakabatebia,
english: When they went to Gilead-- to Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh-- they said to them:

ekegusii: Ase engaki eria nigo barenge abake ase omobaro, bakabarwa ng’a tibaisaini gento, nigo barenge abaeti ase ense eyio.
english: When they were but few in number, few indeed, and strangers in it,

ekegusii: Ase engaki eria nigo barenge abanto abake ase omobaro, bakabarwa ng’a tibaisaini gento; nigo barenge abaeti ase ense eyio.
english: When they were but few in number, few indeed, and strangers in it,

ekegusii: Naende nyomba ime aborokigwa bakamoboria engencho ye ring’ana erio.
english: When they were in the house again, the disciples asked Jesus about this.

ekegusii: Bagaika ensemo erochie Yebusi, na konya bwairire, omosomba agatebia omonene oye, “Inchuo, togobere gochia ase omochie oyo bw’Abayebusi, erio torare aroro ase obotuko obo.”
english: When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone, the servant said to his master, "Come, let's stop at this city of the Jebusites and spend the night."

ekegusii: Ekero barenge nyomba mwa Mika, bakaigwa na komanya eriogi ri’omosae oria Omolawi, bakamoira ensemo, bakamoboria, “Ning’o okorenta aiga? Ngento ki ogokora aa? Emeremo yao nereri?”
english: When they were near Micah's house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned in there and asked him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?"

ekegusii: Amang’ana aya akamanyekana ase Abayahudi na Abagiriki bonsi abamenyete Efeso; obwoba bokabasoa bonsi, na erieta ri’Omonene Yeso rikabakwa.
english: When this became known to the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, they were all seized with fear, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

ekegusii: Erio kararengereretie aya, agaika ase enyomba ya Mariamu ng’ina Yohana, oyokorokwa naende Mariko; na abanto abange nao basangererekanete gosaba.
english: When this had dawned on him, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered and were praying.

ekegusii: Ayio agachia gokoreka, abande ase egesinka keria, abarenge namarwaire, bagacha, bakagwenigwa.
english: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.

ekegusii: Oyio agachia koigwa ng’a Yeso ochire korwa Boyahundi goika Galili, akamochiera, akamosorora achiche agwenie omwana oye, ekiagera konya oisire gokwa.
english: When this man heard that Jesus had arrived in Galilee from Judea, he went to him and begged him to come and heal his son, who was close to death.

ekegusii: Abarisia bagachia korora ayio, bagatama, bakararia amang’ana ase omochie na ebichie.
english: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside,

ekegusii: Ekero abanto abwo babogoretie Esanduku eria y’Omonene bagendire ebitambokero bitano na ekemo, Daudi akanyenya eng’ombe eyemo, na emori eyemo enoru, chikaba ebing’wanso.
english: When those who were carrying the ark of the LORD had taken six steps, he sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.

ekegusii: Ekero amatuko ao are amaya kabe nomogoko, na ekero are amabe rengereria ng’a Nyasae nere okorire ayio onsi abere, erinde omonto tabaisa komanya erirache komobwatia korwa nyuma yaye.
english: When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, a man cannot discover anything about his future.

ekegusii: Tou, omoruoti o Hamati, agachia koigwa ng’a Daudi obuire abarwani bonsi ba Hadadeseri, omoruoti o Soba,
english: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

ekegusii: Toi, omoruoti o Hamati, agachia koigwa ng’a Daudi obuire abarwani bonsi ba Hadadeseri,
english: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,

ekegusii: When two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing by the Nile,
english: Nyuma y’emiaka ebere koyaetire Farao akarota chindoto. Akarora ng’a oteneine engegu y’orooche rwa Naili,

ekegusii: Korende emiaka ebere koyaerire, Porikio Festo agasoa obogambi ribaga ria Feliki; na Feliki akarigia gwekora omuya ase Abayahudi, agatiga Paulo osibire.
english: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.

ekegusii: Ekero Uria achete, Daudi akamoboria amang’ana igoro ya Yoabu buna are gokora, na amang’ana ’abanto, na buna esegi egendererete.
english: When Uriah came to him, David asked him how Joab was, how the soldiers were and how the war was going.

ekegusii: Ekero moka Uria aigwete ng’a omosacha oye okure, akaba okomoreera,
english: When Uriah's wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

ekegusii: Gatokogambigwa iga togosusurwa n’Omonene, titobaisa konacherwa ekina amo nense.
english: When we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.

ekegusii: ekero togokwanwa bobe, intwe twaebereria. Twakorirwe buna eogoto y’ense na eubi y’ebinto bionsi goika bono.
english: when we are slandered, we answer kindly. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.

ekegusii: Ekero twaigete Yerusalemu abaminto bagatoroisia ase omogoko.
english: When we arrived at Jerusalem, the brothers received us warmly.

ekegusii: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
english: Ekero twasoa Rumi, Paulo akaegwa ribaga komenya ere bweka, amo nomorendi ore komorenda.

ekegusii: Togaeta enyancha ensemo ya Kilikia na Pamfulia, togaika Mira, omochie o Likia.
english: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.

ekegusii: Ekero twaigwete ayio, tokerusia moyo ekiagera twaboboete; onde tari noboremu bonde, ekiagera Omonene, Nyasae oino, nere Nyasae o igoro na oyo bw’ense inse.
english: When we heard of it, our hearts melted and everyone's courage failed because of you, for the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.

ekegusii: Togachia koigwa aya, intwe na abanto baria tokamosorora tabaisa gotiira gochia Yerusalemu.
english: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

ekegusii: Onye tokobekera chibarasi ebinto emenwa, ebi’ogochiraa, erinde chitoigwere, nigo tokoraa emebere yabo yonsi.
english: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can turn the whole animal.

ekegusii: “Ekero twairanete ase tata, omosomba oo, tokamotebia amang’ana ao, omonene one.
english: When we went back to your servant my father, we told him what my lord had said.

ekegusii: Nonya ebibe biambuire aye nigo okwabera ogosaria okwo.
english: When we were overwhelmed by sins, you forgave our transgressions.

ekegusii: Ekero omokori amabe agocha, ogochaywa nigo kogocha boigo, na ogochaywa okwo nigo gokorenta obosooku.
english: When wickedness comes, so does contempt, and with shame comes disgrace.

ekegusii: Sanibalati, na Tobia, na Gesemu Omoarabu, amo nababisa bande baito, batebetigwe ng’a naagachire orwaki roria, naende ng’a konya naribirie aase onsi atagoretwe. (Nonya ase engaki eria konya tindabeka ebisieri ase ebiita.)
english: When word came to Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left in it-- though up to that time I had not set the doors in the gates--

ekegusii: Ekero Abamisiri baraigwe amang’ana ayio igoro ya Turo, nigo baraichane mono.
english: When word comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report from Tyre.

ekegusii: Omonto ogokwana amang’ana amange tari komocha korenta ogosaria, korende oyo orendete omonwa oye nigo are omong’aini.
english: When words are many, sin is not absent, but he who holds his tongue is wise.

ekegusii: Ekero mogoika ang’e naase esegi ekorwanera, omokuani agende bosio, akwane nabanto,
english: When you are about to go into battle, the priest shall come forward and address the army.

ekegusii: Ase erieta ri’Omonene Yeso, inwe ekero morasangererekane, na omoika one nao ore amo nokobua kw’Omonene oito Yeso,
english: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, and the power of our Lord Jesus is present,

ekegusii: “Ekero morabe mokogenda korwania ababisa baino, na momenyete ase egetwori, mwerende mono korwa ase kera egento getachenegeti.
english: When you are encamped against your enemies, keep away from everything impure.

ekegusii: “Ekero mokogesa chindagera chi’emegondo yaino, na mwebe omosaima bw’endagera mogondo, timobaisa koirana gochia koywoyia, korende moyotige obe oyo bw’omonto omomenyi omenyete asemore, gose oyo bwe chintakana, na ababoraka, erio nario Omonene, Nyasae oino, arasesenie emeremo yaino yonsi mogokora.
english: When you are harvesting in your field and you overlook a sheaf, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the alien, the fatherless and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

ekegusii: Ekero morabe nemechando, na ayio onsi arabanyore ase amatuko agochigocha, imomoiranere Omonene, Nyasae oino, naende moigwere eriogi riaye.
english: When you are in distress and all these things have happened to you, then in later days you will return to the LORD your God and obey him.

ekegusii: Ekero barabwo barabachande ase omochie oyomo, motame gochia ase oyonde; nekeene nabatebirie: Timogokoora emechie y’Abaisraeli Omwana‐o‐mwanyabanto ataracha.
english: When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. I tell you the truth, you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

ekegusii: Aye ogatiira gochia igoro ogoosa abasibwa, na okanyora ebiegwa ase egati ya mwanyabanto, ee, nonya nase egati y’abasaria, ng’a aye Omonene Nyasae onyare komenya aroro.
english: When you ascended on high, you led captives in your train; you received gifts from men, even from the rebellious-- that you, O LORD God, might dwell there.

ekegusii: Ngosaba more, ko timori koegwa, ekiagera nigo mogosaba bobe. Ayio mogosaba nigo moganetie gokorera ase okogania kwaino okobe.
english: When you ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may spend what you get on your pleasures.

ekegusii: Ekero mwatorire amazeituni aino, timoirana naende gosangereria ase chinsagia aya mwamochete gotora. Moyatigere abamenyi, ne chintakana, na ababoraka.
english: When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave what remains for the alien, the fatherless and the widow.

ekegusii: Inee! Ekero mokorua eng’iti eukorete koba ekeng’wanso, ayio tari bobe? Gose ekero mokorua eye eremarete, gose endwaire, ayio tari bobe? Moraisa korua eng’iti buna eyio ase omogavuna oino, Inee, nagokigwe nainwe, gose abanchere?” Nabo Omonene bw’Emeganda akoboria.
english: When you bring blind animals for sacrifice, is that not wrong? When you sacrifice crippled or diseased animals, is that not wrong? Try offering them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you?" says the LORD Almighty.

ekegusii: “Ekero okoagacha enyomba enyia, goika oagache egetango ase ekerama insinyo, erio nario omonto atagwe korwao akwe; okomocha kw’ogokwa kw’omonto oragwe korwao tigokobarerwa enyomba yao.
english: When you build a new house, make a parapet around your roof so that you may not bring the guilt of bloodshed on your house if someone falls from the roof.

ekegusii: Kweagacheire ebinyomba bi’emegwekano ogosasima ase amatabekania onsi e chinchera, na ase kera enchera kwaagachire aase aimokererete igoro ogosasimera. Nonya naboigo tikwarenge buna omokungu omotayayi onde bwensi, ekiagera nigo gwachayete ogoakanerwa gwe chibesa.
english: When you built your mounds at the head of every street and made your lofty shrines in every public square, you were unlike a prostitute, because you scorned payment.

ekegusii: Ning’o okobaboria ng’a morentane ebinto ebio bionsi ekero mogocha ase obosio bwane na gotaara‐taara ase chiraaro chiane?
english: When you come to appear before me, who has asked this of you, this trampling of my courts?

ekegusii: Ekero moraike ang’e nense y’Abaamori, abanto b’ororeria rwa Loti, timobaisa kobachegia gose kobarwania esegi, ekiagera tinkobaa inwe nonya nensemo eyemo y’orogongo orwo nabaeire barabwo.” (
english: When you come to the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them to war, for I will not give you possession of any land belonging to the Ammonites. I have given it as a possession to the descendants of Lot."

ekegusii: Ekero mogosangererekana amo, timori koria endagera y’Omonene;
english: When you come together, it is not the Lord's Supper you eat,

ekegusii: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
english: Ekero orache ondentanerie egetambaa gi’okwambara, eke natigerete Karipo aria Teroa. Naboigo kogocha ondentanerie chibuku, na kobua mono chiria chi’amasankwa.

ekegusii: Ekero orabe gokorera, tiga emegwekano ogosasima gwasangereirie egotoorie. Omwaga noyeire gochia aare, ee, embeo bosa neyeire. Korende oyo orantamere naire ense ebe omwando oye, ee, naire egetunwa kiane egechenu.”
english: When you cry out for help, let your collection [of idols] save you! The wind will carry all of them off, a mere breath will blow them away. But the man who makes me his refuge will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain."

ekegusii: Ekero moraike ase ense eria Omonene arabae, buna abarierete eira, erio namobe mokomoruera ekeng’wanso eke.
english: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as he promised, observe this ceremony.

ekegusii: “Ekero morabe mwaikire na komenya ase ense eyio Omonene, Nyasae oino, agochia kobaa ebe eyaino, aande moganie omoruoti abagambere, buna ebisaku biria bibaetanaine bibwate abaruoti babo bakobagambera.
english: When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you and have taken possession of it and settled in it, and you say, "Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,"

ekegusii: “Ekero moraike ase ense eria Omonene, Nyasae oino, agochia kobaa, timobaisa kweorokereria kobwatia chingencho chi’okogechia okwo ebisaku biria bimenyeteo binarete gokora.
english: When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to imitate the detestable ways of the nations there.

ekegusii: Na ekero gwakoorire gosoma ebuku eye, oyesiberanie rigena, oyerute ime ase orooche rw’Eufarati.
english: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.

ekegusii: Ekero oraike aroro origie Yehu, omwana omomura o Yehosafati, mosinto o Nimusi. Erio osoe ime, omotebie atenene atige abagisangio baye, omosoyie ase akanyomba ka ime.
english: When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi. Go to him, get him away from his companions and take him into an inner room.

ekegusii: Ekero moragende aroro nigo moranyore abanto tibebegeti ang’e korwana, na ense eria nengare. Ee, Nyasae obekire ense eria ase amaboko aino. Ense eria teremeiri gento kende gionsi gekorwa ase riroba.”
english: When you get there, you will find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land that God has put into your hands, a land that lacks nothing whatever."

ekegusii: Ekero kwabieire endagera, nigo bikoyesangereria; ekero kwaramboire okoboko kwao, nigo bigoisaneka nebinto bire ebiya.
english: When you give it to them, they gather it up; when you open your hand, they are satisfied with good things.

ekegusii: Ekero morabe mokorwana esegi nababisa baino abwo barache kobarwania ase ense yaino, mobe mokobugia ebirombeta ase eriogi ri’ogotabobora, erinde monyare koinyorwa ase obosio bw’Omonene, Nyasae oino, na inwe namotoorigwe korwa ase ababisa baino.
english: When you go into battle in your own land against an enemy who is oppressing you, sound a blast on the trumpets. Then you will be remembered by the LORD your God and rescued from your enemies.

ekegusii: “Ekero morabe mokogenda korwania ababisa baino esegi, na mokorora chibarasi, ne chigari, na abarwani babo bare abange kobua abaino, timobairoka, ekiagera Omonene, Nyasae oino, oria obarusetie korwa ase ense ya Misiri, nigo are amo nainwe.
english: When you go to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt, will be with you.

ekegusii: “Ekero mokogenda ase esegi korwania ababisa baino, na Omonene, Nyasae oino, ababeke ase amaboko aino, nainwe mobabue na moboosa,
english: When you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God delivers them into your hands and you take captives,

ekegusii: Ekero mwatorire amasabibu aino, timoirana naende gochia gosangereria ayatigaire, korende moyatigere abamenyi, ne chintakana, na ababoraka.
english: When you harvest the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines again. Leave what remains for the alien, the fatherless and the widow.

ekegusii: Aye nigo orasoigwe ase ogotacheneka ase amasio ’abanto b’ebisaku, erio omanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene.”
english: When you have been defiled in the eyes of the nations, you will know that I am the LORD.'"

ekegusii: Ase rituko riria moramboke gochia ng’umbu ya Yorodan, na ekero moraike ase ense eria. Omonene, Nyasae oino, agochia kobaa, motenenie amagena amanene, moyaoomeranie.
english: When you have crossed the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.

ekegusii: “Ekero morabe mwambokire gochia ng’umbu ya Yorodan, Abasimeoni, na Abalawi, na Abayuda, na Abaisakaru, na Abayusufu, na Ababenjamin, batenene igoro ase egetunwa kia Gerisimu, basesenie abanto.
english: When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

ekegusii: Namonyore endagera morie moisaneke. Erio motogie Omonene, Nyasae oino, ase engencho y’ense eyio engiya abaeire.”
english: When you have eaten and are satisfied, praise the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.

ekegusii: “Ekero morabe mwaikire ase ense eria Omonene, Nyasae oino, agochia kobaa ebe omwando oino, na komenyao,
english: When you have entered the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance and have taken possession of it and settled in it,

ekegusii: Ekero gwakoorire kogechena igo, orente eeri ensae na emingichi korwa ase riicho, chionsi ibere chibe chitari na kemocho ase emebere yabo.
english: When you have finished purifying it, you are to offer a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without defect.

ekegusii: “Ase omwaka o gatato orue ensemo ya ikomi y’okwama kwao gwe chindagera ase Abalawi, na abamenyi, ne chintakana, na ababoraka, erinde barabwo banyore chindagera chibaisaine barariere agwo ase emechie yaino.
english: When you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you shall give it to the Levite, the alien, the fatherless and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.

ekegusii: Ekero mwabwatire omochie goika moyosambe, buna Omonene achikire, Morigererie mono, mokore buna nabachikire.”
english: When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what the LORD has commanded. See to it; you have my orders."

ekegusii: Na inwe ekero moraigwe amang’ana ’esegi na eburu‐buru, timogoswa, ekiagera aya bori nache kooroka ritang’ani, korende omoerio toraba ang’e.”
english: When you hear of wars and revolutions, do not be frightened. These things must happen first, but the end will not come right away."

ekegusii: Naende komoraigwe esegi, na ebirage bi’esegi, timoichanigwa, ekiagera bori, aya onsi nabe, ko moerio toracha.
english: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. Such things must happen, but the end is still to come.

ekegusii: Ekero egetureri kerabugigwe eriogi ri’ekerondereria, na mokoigwa eriogi eri ri’omochengo, abanto bonsi baake eriogi rinene ri’esegi, erio agwo chindwaki chi’omochie nachigwe inse kegima. Erio abarwani bonsi bayoumokere, kera omonto agende bosio rimo rioka.”
english: When you hear them sound a long blast on the trumpets, have all the people give a loud shout; then the wall of the city will collapse and the people will go up, every man straight in."

ekegusii: “Ekero egetunwa keria kiagendererete gwoka omorero, mokaigwa eriogi korwa ase egati‐gati y’omosunte oria, nainwe mwensi, abamore abatang’ani na abagaaka ase ebisaku biaino, mogacha asende.
english: When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was ablaze with fire, all the leading men of your tribes and your elders came to me.

ekegusii: Ekero kwabisire obosio bwao, nigo bikoba nobwoba obonene; na ekero okobiura omoika obo, nigo bigokwa, biairana ase amaroba ime.
english: When you hide your face, they are terrified; when you take away their breath, they die and return to the dust.

ekegusii: “Ekero mwanaaririe omochie na koyoboera ase engaki entambe, na koyorwania esegi, erinde moyoire, timobaisa gosaria emete ereo. Monyare koria amatunda ’emete eyio, korende timoyegecha. Inee! Emete nero nabanto erinde moyesirie?
english: When you lay siege to a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by putting an ax to them, because you can eat their fruit. Do not cut them down. Are the trees of the field people, that you should besiege them?

ekegusii: Ekero okorua aa asende rero noumerane nabanto babere ang’e nembeera ya Raeli, ase orogongo rwa Benjamin ase Selisa. Barabwo nigo baragotebie ng’a chitigere chiria mwagendete korigia chiatokire. Iso otigire gochichandekera, na bono naye achandekerete, ogoteba: Naki ndakore indore omwana one?
english: When you leave me today, you will meet two men near Rachel's tomb, at Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, 'The donkeys you set out to look for have been found. And now your father has stopped thinking about them and is worried about you. He is asking, "What shall I do about my son?"'

ekegusii: when you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.
english: Ekero ogochia korara, toba nobwoba, koraire nonyore chitoro chingiya.

ekegusii: “Ekero okoa omogisangio oo egento kende gionsi singo, tobaisa gosoa ase enyomba yaye koira egento keria abekire kebe intenenera.
english: When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not go into his house to get what he is offering as a pledge.

ekegusii: Ekero kwarire eira ase Nyasae, tobaisa gotebana koyeikerania, ekiagera ere tari kogokigwa nabanto abariri. Ikerania eira kwariete.
english: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.

ekegusii: “Komogoika ang’e nomochie mogochia korwania esegi, ritang’ani morarie amang’ana ’omorembe ase abanto b’omochie oyio.
english: When you march up to attack a city, make its people an offer of peace.

ekegusii: Nonya ngoika rero iga, ekero mokorua ebiegwa biaino, na gosamba abana baino babe ebing’wanso, nigo mogwesoyia ase ogotacheneka ase ogosasima emegwekano yaino yonsi. Naende inwe Abaisraeli, Inee, ninyanchete momborie amang’ana? Ekeene buna inche inde moyo, tingwancha momborie. Ninche Omonene Nyasae natebire ayio.
english: When you offer your gifts-- the sacrifice of your sons in the fire-- you continue to defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. Am I to let you inquire of me, O house of Israel? As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, I will not let you inquire of me.

ekegusii: Ekero morabe mogoeta ase amache ime, nimbe amo nainwe; namoba mogoeta ase chindooche, tichikobamera. Namoete ase omorero, timogosambwa, gose omorero ekebemberi tokobasiria.
english: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you pass through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flames will not set you ablaze.

ekegusii: Ekero twachete aase aa, Sihoni omoruoti o Hesiboni, na Ogi, omoruoti o Basani, bagacha gotorwania esegi, korende tokababua.
english: When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight against us, but we defeated them.

ekegusii: Ekero okorora omoibi, nigo ogwancherana nere, boigo nigo okobwatana nabatomani.
english: When you see a thief, you join with him; you throw in your lot with adulterers.

ekegusii: Ekero morarore amang’ana ayio, mosasoke ase chinkoro chiaino; amauga ’emebere yaino nareerete buna obonyansi oborere; erio abanto mbamanye ng’a okoboko kw’Omonene nigo kore amo nabasomba baye, naende ng’a ekeririanda kiaye nigo kere igoro y’ababisa baye.
english: When you see this, your heart will rejoice and you will flourish like grass; the hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, but his fury will be shown to his foes.

ekegusii: Ekero ogotoma omoika oo, nigo bigotongwa, naende gwakora ense yaba enyia.
english: When you send your Spirit, they are created, and you renew the face of the earth.

ekegusii: Ase ayio, komorakorere abamino ebibe na goichania chinkoro chiria chikobugwa bwango, igo mwakoreire Kristo ebibe.
english: When you sin against your brothers in this way and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

ekegusii: Ekero ogoikaransa koria endagera amo nomogambi, orengererie mono ng’a ning’o ore ase obosio bwao.
english: When you sit to dine with a ruler, note well what is before you,

ekegusii: Neke ogosimeka, tori gosimeka egento keria kegocha koba, korende embusuro yoka; onye nengano gose mbusuru ende yonsi.
english: When you sow, you do not plant the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or of something else.

ekegusii: “Ekero morarambore amaboko aino ase ogosaba, inche nigo ndatube amaiso aane timbarora, na ekero morabe mogosaba mono, tinkobaigwa ekiagera amaboko aino nigo aichire amanyinga.
english: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide my eyes from you; even if you offer many prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood;

ekegusii: Ekero orabe kogotaara, ayio nakoraae; ekero orabe koraire, nakorende, na ekero orabe gokoboka, ayio nakwane naye.
english: When you walk, they will guide you; when you sleep, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you.

ekegusii: When you walk, your steps will not be hampered; when you run, you will not stumble.
english: Ekero orabe kogotaara, togotererigwa, na ekero orabe gokominyoka, tokogochwa.

ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, ekero gwatang’anete abanto bao na ogotaara ase erooro,
english: When you went out before your people, O God, when you marched through the wasteland, Selah

ekegusii: Na inwe abamwarenge mokwete ase ogosaria kwaino na ase ogotaroka kw’emebere yaino, Nyasae akabakora koba moyo amo nere, gaikire kobaabera ogosaria gwonsi.
english: When you were dead in your sins and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our sins,

ekegusii: Naki ekero mwarenge abasomba b’ebibe nigo mwarenge abasibore korwa ase oboronge.
english: When you were slaves to sin, you were free from the control of righteousness.

ekegusii: Barabwo tibamoirogete Nyasae. Ase ayio bagacha, bakabarwania na goita abanto abatigarete nyuma konya bagoyire na korosa.
english: When you were weary and worn out, they met you on your journey and cut off all who were lagging behind; they had no fear of God.

ekegusii: Ekero orabe gokorema riroba tirigokwamera endagera nonya ng’ake. Igo orabe omoomboganu na omoetanani ase ense.”
english: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."

ekegusii: ekero aye Nyasae gwatenenete konacha ekina na kobatooria abwo bonsi bagokorerwa bobe.
english: when you, O God, rose up to judge, to save all the afflicted of the land. Selah

ekegusii: Ekero endamwamu yaye erakee, na ere ebire aya kwamokorerete, erio nintome abanto bache gokorangeria oirane korwa aroro. Nase ki ndakwerwe nainwe mwensi babere ase rituko erimo.”
english: When your brother is no longer angry with you and forgets what you did to him, I'll send word for you to come back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"

ekegusii: Onye abana bao bakorete ebibe asare, ere obaeire egesusuro ase engencho y’okomocha kwabo.
english: When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin.

ekegusii: Ekero amatuko ao araikeranigwe na obe gokogenda korara ase chisokoro chiao chiararete, nimbeke oyomo bw’ororeria rwao, oyorarue ase oyomo bw’abamura bao, agambe; nainche ninkong’ie oboruoti bwaye.
english: When your days are over and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

ekegusii: Ekero amatuko ao ay’ogokwa araike, na orare ase chisokoro chiao, nimbeke oyomo bw’oroiboro rwao abe omoruoti, ninkore oboruoti bwaye bobe ne chinguru.
english: When your days are over and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.

ekegusii: Ekero ebinto biao bi’oboonchoreria biaruete ase chinyancha, nigo gwaisanegetie abanto abange; obotenenku bwao obonge, na oboonchoreria bwao, nigo bwatenengetie abaruoti b’ense.
english: When your merchandise went out on the seas, you satisfied many nations; with your great wealth and your wares you enriched the kings of the earth.

ekegusii: Ekero nanyorete amang’ana ao, ayio nigo abete endagera yane, ee, amang’ana ao agaichoria enkoro yane nomochengo, akangokia, ekiagera inche nigo nkorokwa ase erieta riao, aye Omonene, Nyasae bw’Emeganda.
english: When your words came, I ate them; they were my joy and my heart's delight, for I bear your name, O LORD God Almighty.

ekegusii: When Zebul the governor of the city heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, he was very angry.
english: Ekero Sebuli, omogambi bw’omochie oria, aigwete amang’ana a Gaali, mosinto bw’Ebedi, akaba nendamwamu enene.

ekegusii: Ere agaichana gachia komorora, na omoondoko okamobwata.
english: When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and was gripped with fear.

ekegusii: Ekero Zedekia, omoruoti bw’Abayuda, amo nabarwani baye bonsi, baroche abanene abwo bagatama botuko, bagasoka korwa ase omochie, bagaeta ase omogondo bw’omoruoti, bakagenda bagasokera egeita kiarenge gati‐gati ye chindwaki ibere. Bagatama gochia ase Ekerubo Ekiomo.
english: When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled; they left the city at night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.

ekegusii: Ekero Simuri aroche ng’a omochie obwatirwe, agasoa ase eburi y’enyomba y’omoruoti, agasamba enyomba y’omoruoti, na Simuri omonyene agesamberao.
english: When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the citadel of the royal palace and set the palace on fire around him. So he died,

ekegusii: Daudi akaba okorwania ense eyio na goita abanto bonsi pi, abasacha na abakungu; agasakora ching’ondi, ne chiombe, ne chitigere, ne chingamia, akaira ne chianga. Erio aba okoirana gochia ase Akisi.
english: Whenever David attacked an area, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but took sheep and cattle, donkeys and camels, and clothes. Then he returned to Achish.

ekegusii: Ekero aitete abanto abatigari nigo bamorigetie; nigo baonchogete, bakamorigia ase ekeene.
english: Whenever God slew them, they would seek him; they eagerly turned to him again.

ekegusii: Ere nigo arenge konacha etukia yaye omoerio o kera omwaka, ekiagera yare koba endito mono. Oborito bw’etukia yaye nigo bwarenge chikiro ibere na ekeng’ese, koreng’ana ekerengo kiare gokorerwa ase omoruoti.
english: Whenever he cut the hair of his head-- he used to cut his hair from time to time when it became too heavy for him-- he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.

ekegusii: Ekero nkwara amare igoro y’ense, na omokubinyongo nobe okororekana ase amare,
english: Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,

ekegusii: Ekero kende gionsi ngokwana, nigo nkorera, nigo ngoaka eriogi nteba, “Obotindi na ogosaria!” Botambe nigo ngochecherigwa na gosekererigwa ase engencho ye ring’ana riao, aye Omonene.
english: Whenever I speak, I cry out proclaiming violence and destruction. So the word of the LORD has brought me insult and reproach all day long.

ekegusii: Kera engaki barenge kogenda ase esegi, Omonene nigo arenge kobabeea na obarentera amabe, buna konya abatebirie na gotiana. Barabwo nigo barenge nemechando emenene.
english: Whenever Israel went out to fight, the hand of the LORD was against them to defeat them, just as he had sworn to them. They were in great distress.

ekegusii: Na ekero Esanduku eria yarenge goikigwa aase bagotimokera, Musa nigo arenge goteba, “Aye Omonene, bairanere Abaisraeli aba bare chilifu ne chilifu.”
english: Whenever it came to rest, he said, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."

ekegusii: ekero kiamobokire nigo gekomogaragaria inse, asokia risombogoku, na koriania amaino; ase ayio chinguru chiaye chisira. Ngakwana naborokigwa bao bageserie, tibanyara.”
english: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive out the spirit, but they could not."

ekegusii: Ekero Yehudi asomire chinsemo isato, gose inye, chi’amang’ana aria, omoruoti akabogoria omoyio, agachinachana, agachiruta riko ase omorero, chikayia. Omoruoti akagenderera kona‐gokora boigo goika ebuku eria yonsi ekayia ekaera ase omorero oria.
english: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns of the scroll, the king cut them off with a scribe's knife and threw them into the firepot, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire.

ekegusii: Onde bwensi ogocha kondora nigo agokwana amang’ana ’oborimo, enkoro yaye nigo egosangereria amabe, erio ogenda isiko oraria amang’ana ayio amabe.
english: Whenever one comes to see me, he speaks falsely, while his heart gathers slander; then he goes out and spreads it abroad.

ekegusii: Onye chinkoro chiaito chigotogambia, Nyasae nomonene kobua chinkoro chiaito, na ere nigo amanyete onsi.
english: whenever our hearts condemn us. For God is greater than our hearts, and he knows everything.

ekegusii: Ekero kende gionsi Esanduku eria yarenge gochaka kobogorigwa gotang’ana orogendo, Musa nigo arenge kobora, “Omonene, imoka, ababisa bao tiga baserigwe na goserebanigwa, na baria bakogechete tiga batame korwa ase obosio bwao.”
english: Whenever the ark set out, Moses said, "Rise up, O LORD! May your enemies be scattered; may your foes flee before you."

ekegusii: Engaki ende yonsi esanduku eria yare korentwa n’Abalawi ase abanto baria omoruoti achorete, na ekero barabwo baare korora ng’a chibesa chiabeire chinyinge, omoriki bw’omoruoti na omosomba bw’omokuani omonene nigo baare gocha barusia chibesa echio. Nyuma y’ayio bairania esanduku eria aase aye. Bakaba bagokora igo rituko ase rituko bagasangereria chibesa chinyinge.
english: Whenever the chest was brought in by the Levites to the king's officials and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the royal secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. They did this regularly and collected a great amount of money.

ekegusii: Ekero kende gionsi riire riria riarenge koimokerera igoro korwa ase Eema eria, erio Abaisraeli nigo barenge komanora, bachaka orogendo rwabo. Na aase riire riria riarenge gotenena, aroro agwo nao Abaisraeli barenge gotoora.
english: Whenever the cloud lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites set out; wherever the cloud settled, the Israelites encamped.

ekegusii: Kera engaki Elikana arenge korua ekeng’wanso, nigo arenge koa Penina amo nabana baye, abamura na abaiseke, kera oyomo egetari kiaye.
english: Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

ekegusii: Na ebirecha bi’eubi bigachia komorora, bikagwa ase obosio bwaye, bikarera bigateba, “Aye naye Omwana o Nyasae.”
english: Whenever the evil spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, "You are the Son of God."

ekegusii: Kero kende gionsi Abaisraeli barenge kobusura chimbusuro chiabo, Abamimidiani, na Abaameleki, na abanto ba moocha nigo baare gocha kobarwania esegi.
english: Whenever the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites and other eastern peoples invaded the country.

ekegusii: Botambe ekero omoruoti arenge gosoa ase enyomba y’Omonene, abarendi nigo barenge gochibogoria, naende bachiirania ase enyomba y’oborendi.
english: Whenever the king went to the LORD's temple, the guards bore the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.

ekegusii: Botambe ekero omoruoti abete ogosoa enyomba y’Omonene, abarendi nigo barenge gochibogoria, naende bachiirania ase enyomba y’oborendi.
english: Whenever the king went to the LORD's temple, the guards went with him, bearing the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.

ekegusii: Na engaki ende yonsi ching’iti chiria chire moyo chikomotogia ere oyoikaransete ase ekerogo ki’obonene, na komoa ogosika, na komoakera ng’a mbuya mono, ere oyore moyo goika kare na kare,
english: Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor and thanks to him who sits on the throne and who lives for ever and ever,

ekegusii: Ekero kende gionsi Omonene arenge kobaa omogambi nigo arenge koba amo nomogambi oria, naende aba ogotooria abanto korwa ase ababisa babo, ase engaki omogambi oria arenge moyo. Omonene nigo arenge kobarorera amabera ekero aigure okwerera kwabo inse y’abwo babamigete na kobachanda.
english: Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, he was with the judge and saved them out of the hands of their enemies as long as the judge lived; for the LORD had compassion on them as they groaned under those who oppressed and afflicted them.

ekegusii: Ekero abanto bonsi barorire riire riria rigotenena ase egesoero ki’Eema, baba bakoimoka na gotung’ama inse ase ogosasima, kera omonto ase egesoero ki’eema yaye.
english: Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they all stood and worshiped, each at the entrance to his tent.

ekegusii: Ekero omokubinyongo okoba ase amare, na inche nkoyorigereria, ning’inyore okobwatana kwane gwa kare na kare, okwo nakorire egati yane, inche Nyasae, na kera egetongwa kere moyo ase ense.”
english: Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and all living creatures of every kind on the earth."

ekegusii: Ase engaki ende yonsi omoika oria omobe okorwa ase Nyasae ore gocha igoro ase Saulo, Daudi igo are okobugia obokano. Erio omoika oria omobe oba okorua ase Saulo, nere oba ogokanyeka na kweigwa buya naende.
english: Whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would take his harp and play. Then relief would come to Saul; he would feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.

ekegusii: Kero kende gionsi chimbori gose ching’ondi echiare ne chinguru gochiaganirie amarieme, Yakobo nigo are kobeka ebite biria bosio bwe ching’iti ase chintuba chiria chinyare konyora amarieme gochikorigereria ebite ebio.
english: Whenever the stronger females were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs in front of the animals so they would mate near the branches,

ekegusii: Ekero Obomenyo obwo borabe bokong’anyigwa, Abalawi nabwo barabosimore, na ekero borabe bogotenenigwa naende, nabwo barabotenenie aase agwo. Omonto onde bwensi otachikiri aise goika ang’e n’Obomenyo obwo goika aitwe akwe.
english: Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites shall do it. Anyone else who goes near it shall be put to death.

ekegusii: Ekero bagosoa ase Eema y’Omosangererekano goika besibie ase amache ayio, tibabaisa gokwa; naboigo ekero bakogenda ase egesasimero ase okoruera Omonene ekeng’wanso ki’omorero
english: Whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water so that they will not die. Also, when they approach the altar to minister by presenting an offering made to the LORD by fire,

ekegusii: Ekero bomanire nigo bagocha asende, na inche nabagambera ebina biabo na kobamanyia emeroberio ya Nyasae na amachiko aye.”
english: Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me, and I decide between the parties and inform them of God's decrees and laws."

ekegusii: Engaki ende yonsi chibesa chiarenge koba chinyinge ime ase esanduku omoriki bw’omoruoti na omokuani omonene nigo barenge gocha kobara chibesa chiria chiare korentwa ase enyomba y’Omonene na gochibeka ime ase emebuko, naende bayeboa.
english: Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the royal secretary and the high priest came, counted the money that had been brought into the temple of the LORD and put it into bags.

ekegusii: Ekero bakobaira ase ekina, na kobabeka ase amaboko ’abanto, timochaka gwechanda korengereria ayamorigetie gokwana; korende rinde rionsi moraegwe ase ensa eria, morikwane, ekiagera tari inwe morakwane, korende n’Omoika Omochenu.
english: Whenever you are arrested and brought to trial, do not worry beforehand about what to say. Just say whatever is given you at the time, for it is not you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

ekegusii: Akabatebia, “Enyomba ende yonsi ase morasoe, mobeere aroro goika ekero moraimoke korwa aase aria.
english: Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that town.

ekegusii: aase amakonde abo atagokwa na omorero otakorimeka.
english: where "'their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.'

ekegusii: Ng’ai chinyasae chia Hamati na Aripadi chire? Ng’ai chinyasae chia Sefariwaimu na Hena, na Iwa chire? Inee! Chiatooririe Samaria korwa ase okoboko kwane?
english: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?

ekegusii: Ng’ai chinyasae chia Hamati na Aripadi chire? Inee! Chinyasae chia Sefariwaimu, ng’ai chire? Chiatooririe ense ya Samaria korwa ase okoboko kwane?
english: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?

ekegusii: Bono chisokoro chiaino ng’ai chire? Na ababani baino, ng’ai bare? Inee! Mbagendererete koba moyo botambe?
english: Where are your forefathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?

ekegusii: Ng’ai bare ababani baria bao bakobanerete bakogotebia ng’a, omoruoti o Babeli takonyara koirana gocha gokorwania na korwania ense eye?
english: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?

ekegusii: Ng’ai abanto bao abang’aini bare? Onye bareo, tiga bagotebie na gokomanyia aya Omonene bw’Emeganda arobeirie igoro ya Misiri.
english: Where are your wise men now? Let them show you and make known what the LORD Almighty has planned against Egypt.

ekegusii: Ng’ai nkorusia chinyama nkoa abanto aba bonsi? Barabwo nigo bakorera asende bagoteba: Toe chinyama torie!
english: Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep wailing to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'

ekegusii: Ng’ai ndagende, erinde ntigane n’Omoika oo? Gose ng’ai ndatame gochia, indue ase obosio bwao?
english: Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence?

ekegusii: “Nase ki toragende aroro? Abaminto batwoboirie, ekiagera batebire ng’a abanto bare ase ense eria nabanene naende nabatambe gotobua. Emechie yabo nemenene, naende nigo egiteire chindwaki chiigete igoro. Naende ntwarora amamonto, abanto b’ororeria rw’Anaki.”
english: Where can we go? Our brothers have made us lose heart. They say, 'The people are stronger and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the sky. We even saw the Anakites there.'"

ekegusii: agateemwa na Saitani ase engaki y’amatuko emerongo ene. Na amatuko aria tariete gento. Goika agachia koera, akaigwa enchara.
english: where for forty days he was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and at the end of them he was hungry.

ekegusii: Where has your lover gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your lover turn, that we may look for him with you?
english: Aye ore omoseera kobua abakungu bonsi, ng’ai omwanchi oo achiire? Omwanchi oyio oo, ng’ai aonchokire gochia? Togende amo naye tomorigie.

ekegusii: Akamenya aroro emetienyi etato. Ekiagera Abayahudi bamoboerete, konya omanoire kogenda ase enyancha gochia Siiria, agachora koiranera goetera Makedonia.
english: where he stayed three months. Because the Jews made a plot against him just as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

ekegusii: akamenya aroro goika Herode agakwa, erinde rinyare goikerana eriatebetwe n’Omonene ase omonwa bw’omobani, “Korwa Misiri nkarangeria omwana one.”
