ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Korwa Ase Capital FM, Parliament Grounds: Riberera ritindi ndiamentekana ase rituko ria rero, aaria ase Parliarment, igoro y' ogochia maguta motwe ase ebiiseke. Kobwatekana na Kitutu Chache North MP Hon Jimmy Angwenyi, ogochia maguta motwe nigo kore egento ekenene ase ebisaku ebinge, naende buna nigo ebewenerete gotigwe kogenderera. Parliament nigo yatebetigwe buna the Director of Public Prosecutions, nigo atagete gokora omokia gosiria FGM, ase chinsemo echio chire chintindi ase egekoro ekio echio chire buna ekobwatia: It is time to move on. Ching'ong'o chiria still chikwerekererete FGM ase obotindi, Kenya engima. Nyamira County Women's Representative, Mhe Alice Chae nigo agotosemia buna bono yaikire engaki ase intwe Abagusii to move on, korwa ase chinchera chiria chitatokonye gochia ase amatuko a motwe. "Inche tiindochi buna ninki gekogera eserikali etagete goetia amachiko ayio agoita ekemira, abwo ase ntwe totaraetia richiko rigokana obwanchani gati ya abasacha amo na abasacha bande, gose abakungu am na abakungu bande, ebio bire ebimira bie chinse chinde" Nabo Mhe Angwenyi atebete. "Egekoro kia Abagusii nigo kegoteba buna abaiseke nkonintwa bare aake" Nabo Mhe Angwenyi amentete naende. Bono abwo nario riberera riamentekanete ekero Mwingi North MP Mhe John Munuve, aboretie Mhe. Angwenyi gose ere onintirwe, naende gose n' ekeene buna abaiseke baye banintirwe. Abwo abwo bono nario Nyamira County Women's Representative Mhe Alice Chae aimogete na goteba buna ere nachiete magotwa motwe. Ase boigo, nigo Mhe Chae atebete buna ekemira eke nigo kere ekebe, naende giateire amatuko aye. "Nigo ngosaba buna nanga Mhe Angwenyi nigo are omosubati buna inche, oyio ochiete maguta motwe, korende ore moyo. Ase boigo, tiga Mhe Angwenyi atoenekerie buna abasacha bagototama, erinde bagenda konywoma abakungu korwa chinsemo chiria chitari kogenda maguta motwe" Nabo Mhe Chae amentete. Mhe. Angwenyi, oyio ogendererete gwekwania, nigo atugutetwe isiko ya Parliament. Ababunge nigo baboretie buna tiga richiko rikong'igwe, ase ogosiria egekoro eke, ekio kere mamincha y' richiko ria Kenya, Prohibition of FGM Act of 2011 and the The Children's Act of 2001.
english: These are the details: Event at Capital FM, Parliament Grounds: The situation is tense and uncertain near Parliament, there is a lot of commotion and excitement. It involves Kitutu Chache North MP Hon Jimmy Angwenyi, a lot of commotion and excitement is happening, and it seems they are planning something to help. Parliament has been adjourned while the Director of Public Prosecutions investigates cases related to FGM, and this issue is very serious and important because it affects our daughters: It is time to move forward. This practice which continues to perpetuate FGM and child marriage, shames Kenya. Nyamira County Women's Representative, Hon Alice Chae said that we should forget about the past and encourage the Abagusii people to move on, so that this harmful tradition does not continue. "We need to thank the government for taking action against those who commit these crimes, both current and former officials, including leaders and former leaders, and all those involved in this bad behavior," Hon Angwenyi added. “The future of the Abagusii people depends on ensuring our children are safe” Hon Angwenyi concluded. This matter also concerns Mwingi North MP Hon John Munuve, who supported Hon. Angwenyi and urged everyone to be careful, and emphasized that our children deserve protection. This was also echoed by Nyamira County Women's Representative Hon Alice Chae who agreed and stated she will continue to fight for their rights. And further, Hon Chae added that the law is already in place, and she respects the traditions of her people. "I urge Hon Angwenyi to continue speaking out, to protect our children, and to save lives. And I ask Hon Angwenyi to show compassion to the people, so they don't blame leaders for this harmful tradition,” Hon Chae concluded. Hon. Angwenyi, who is seeking re-election, was escorted out of Parliament. Members of Parliament have resolved that if the law is broken, and if it threatens the welfare of the country, then it undermines the laws of Kenya, the Prohibition of FGM Act of 2011 and the The Children's Act of 2001.

ekegusii: abanto 55 gotooka nebinyinyi bia Corona, ewizara yobochenu yatebire Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 25, 2022 Abanto 55 nigo baenegetigwe nebinyinyi bia Corona maega yabanto 1934 korengwa ase chinsa 24 chiaetete. Koreng’ana newizara yobochenu, 45 ase abwo nabakenya ase 10 bare abamaiko. 36 nabasacha na 19 nabasubati, omoke pi nonmwana bwemika 2, ase omogotu pi abwate emiaka 88. Ekaonty ya Nairobi eyatang’anete nabanto 39, Uasin Gishu 6, ekaonty ya Murang’a 4,Busia 2, Mombasa2, Kiambu amo na Kisumu oyomo oyomo. Omowaziri bwobochenu Mutahi Kagwe natebete abanto 153 babwenire korwa ase endwari eyio, ase 152 babwena ase chinka noyomo korwa ase enyagitari. Ase bono abanto 53 nigo batangire ase chinyagitari ao ao kobwatekana nendwari eyio ase abande 797 bagendererete konyora obogwenia korwa ase chiinka. Ase bono, morwaire taiyo ore ICU, onde taiyo obekeire mbeo na onde taiyo ore HDU.
english: Abanto 55 experienced several deaths due to Corona, the Ministry of Health has confirmed. Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 25, 2022 Abanto 55 is among those who died from Corona, bringing the total to 1934 since March 24th. According to the Ministry of Health, 45 were men and 10 were women. 36 were over the age of 60 and 19 were under the age of 30, including a two-year-old child and an 88-year-old man. Nairobi County recorded 39 cases, Uasin Gishu 6, Murang’a County 4, Busia 2, Mombasa 2, Kiambu and Kisumu each had one case. Minister of Health Mutahi Kagwe reported that 153 people tested positive for the disease, while 152 recovered from the illness. Also, 53 people are currently admitted to intensive care units, 797 are isolated at home with mild symptoms, and another 797 are awaiting test results. Furthermore, there are patients in general wards, some requiring oxygen support and others in High Dependency Units.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Eamate yaito ya Gusii.com, nigo togochengera omwaka omogeni buna Mosamba mwaye oiboirwe! Egesunte kia Masaba, kwaheri. Nigo twayokorire omwaka o 2012 na komotogia Omotongi oito buna mbuya mono ase obomoyo. Nntwe ntori baya, aba twaikire omwaka oyo omonyia 2013, omotienyi oyo bw' Engatiato. Bono rende ninki tosemereti? Inyora buna abakoro nigo batotebetie omobayeno oria ogoteba buna Bamanya kerumbe, mbateganda kerumbe. Bono ninki batagete gototebia gose? Nigo barenge gototebia buna toganya embura etwe, omaye kogenda gotenya! Toganya omwaka oike gati, omanye gochaka kobanga eki otagete gokora omwaka oyo omonyia. Omoyega o 2013 obwatire nse pi! Mbuya mono ase abana ba Mwayagetinge ase ogokinia ekebute eke kia Gusii.com. Ogochenga okuya, n' ebisio ebinge ase kera oyomo ase omwaka oyo omoyia o 2013. Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egesunte Kende - Egesunte Kia Masaba [ December] 31, 2012. Inyora omwaka oyo nari ense yaito ya Kenya egocha gotwara obochori obotang'ani ase richiko eri riyia riaetigwa bwango iga. Ekurate enene neri buna Borai mboora nguru, boe kiige bori bwomo! Eng'encho ende, rigia abarai bari bare n' obomanyi erinde ense yaito techa gotakaa. Mwanyagetinge, narorire buna omoyega oyo nigo obwatete inse pi, ebusa yayire, amandasi arosigwe, n' chimbori chianyenyirwe. Baminto ntonywa na koria bobe. Are mono, inyora buna Okobwatia egesingororo ko nambaba tori, chinswe chitagoseka gokonywa amache! Igo toisa kobwatia abanto otamanyeti ase bagochia oche gweitia naende. Nigo Gusii.com egoakera kera omosani oirete engaki yaye ya bene, gotarera ekebute eke na gosanga amange igoro y' Omogusii buna arenge engaki eria yaetire. Ogotara kwaino, nakwo kogererete ekebute eke gekagenderera. Onye tari inwe, ewebusaiti eye tekoba moyo. Twasabeire kera omwana o Mwanyagetinge, ebisio b' Omonene ase omwaka oyo o 2013. Amaiga y' omwaka omoyia ayio na Omonguru aseseni Abana ba Mwanyagetinge mwensi ase mwabeta kera aase. Happy New Year 2013!
english: These are the news: Welcome to Gusii.com, and happy new year to everyone, may you live long! Greetings to the people of Masaba, goodbye. We worked in the year 2012 and completed Omotongi village with good health. Now this time has come, we have entered the year 2013, which is called Engatiato. How are you all doing? May the children and adults be well, may they rejoice because Bamanya has arrived, let them celebrate. How will they manage to rejoice fully? They will rejoice because the rains have come, so they can farm! Let the year pass quickly, so that we can start working on the next year. The year 2013 started very well! Good health to all the children of Mwayagetinge who are interested in the website of Gusii.com. Happy new year, and many blessings to you throughout the year 2013. By Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Greetings Kende - Greetings from Masaba [December] 31, 2012. This year was a good year for Kenya because it received sufficient rainfall and the food situation improved greatly. The harvest was abundant, like Borai harvesting maize, and they were full! However, there are some people who don’t understand that a good year doesn’t last forever. Mwayagetinge, I remind you that this year started very well, it was peaceful, the economy improved, and businesses flourished. People rejoiced and worked hard. Also, remember that prosperity comes with responsibility, and wealth should not be wasted! It is important to help others so that they too can benefit. Gusii.com wants to thank everyone for their support, for visiting the website and sharing information about the Gusii people. Thank you very much, and we will continue improving the website. Anyone who wishes, the website is always available. We wish our child Mwanyagetinge success and blessings throughout the year 2013. The days of the past year passed with Omonguru leading the children of Mwanyagetinge towards progress. Happy New Year 2013!

ekegusii: Omong’ina oyomo bwe emiaka ya igatwa nigo agendererete gokendia ebitingiro biaye aaria echela ya Siaya nyuma y’ogotebekana goita oyomwabo goika ekerengo kio’gokwa, ase engencho egotebekana buna nigo nyagosiran oyio arenge bobwatania ebinto bia omoiti oyo nerideni erio ria chibesa chia kenya 1,500 erio asinyirwe goakana. oboiti obo bwatigire ekenyoro kia Asembo Boi Kasabong ime ye ekaonti ya Siaya ase amaisugusu amange nyuma ya ababwatani be ekeombe eke ki’abang’ina. Nyagosira, Philister Arega, oyokabeire omorai ase Tin-to-Ler Women Group nigo aumerana na amakweri ase enka ya Benter Akinyiase bachiete na abarai bande gotema koonia enibo ya Akinyi’ erio koirania chibesa echio. Koreng’ana na omonyakerogo bwe’keombe ekio omosubati Ester Odero, Akinyi Akinyi nigo asabete chibesa Sh2, 000 korwa ase ekeombe omotienyi bwe Rigwata (April) ase ariete eira yogoakana magega y’omotienyi oyomo. |John Omedo okoreera ng’ina Philister Arega nyagosira oyio oitwa na oyomo bw’ekeombe aaria Asembo Boi Kasabong’ ime ya Rarieda Constituency amagega y’okogenda kwoyia ridenii riabo. . [omobwekano na TITUS MUNALA/STANDARD]| echuma yaera nigo yarenge nemeremo emekong’u mono ekiagera abarai aba nigo babeire bagoetanana ase baria basabete ebitoki bakaanga goakana koirera koonia chinibo chia abasabi aba.Korende nigo egotebekana buna nyagosira Arega nigo abogoretie ekaraya akamobutoria omong’ina bw’ emiaka 55 akamora nse buna enchogu. abanyakeombe nigo batama magoro nyanche ebitingiro bikabaira gotoria amagima abo. Nigo egotebekana buna Omosacha oyorenge karaire nere ochete gokonya na gotoria ekero anyorete omong’ina oyio oraire bakabuga nigo embeo yamoerera korende bakanyora otwekire mo. Onyango oyo ogokora emeremo aaria Nandi Hills nigo acha inka ase omotimoko omoke na tamanyete buna omorugi oye konye osabire chibesa korwa ekeombe ekio. Akinyi bono nigo abwatire aaria Aram Police Station chingaki obotuki bwachakire. Rarieda OCPD omosike Johana Chebii oyoigete agwo nigo atebete buna abarai na omosacha omosoerwa nere bachikirwe korika oroboti Nigo omosike oyoo boigo agoteba buna abanyakenyoro batige kobogoria na koira richiko ase amaboko abo ekiagera onye baika koira ring’ana eri ase are,amakweri tare gocha kobao. {orina Ontiri korwa Texas}
english: The woman identified herself as having been involved in a road accident and reported stealing items from a house in the Chela area of Siaya County following a dispute with her husband which led to separation, she claimed the disagreement stemmed from her refusal to share property worth Ksh 1,500 which was given to her as dowry. The incident reportedly happened in the home of Asembo Boi Kasabong in Siaya County and involved several relatives. The suspect, Philister Arega, who claims to be a member of the Tin-to-Ler Women Group, denied the allegations leveled against her by Benter Akinyi's family, claiming they were falsely accusing Akinyi of theft and attempting to seize her property. Speaking to our correspondent, Esther Odero, Akinyi Akinyi stated that she lent Akinyi Sh2, 000 in April and is now demanding repayment along with interest on the loan. |John Omedo reports on Philister Arega, the suspect accused of theft in the home of Asembo Boi Kasabong in Rarieda Constituency, alleging she went to steal their belongings. . [reported by TITUS MUNALA/STANDARD]| The local administrator said he had received numerous complaints from people who claimed they had been defrauded by those who borrowed money from them and failed to repay it, leading to disputes. It is alleged that the suspect Arega confessed to being 55 years old and suffering from a mental illness. Residents lamented that thieves were becoming bolder and robbing them during the day. It is also alleged that Omosa, who is over 80 years old, refused to cooperate with police and declined to provide information about the incident, making it difficult for investigators to make arrests. This incident occurred in the Nandi Hills area and has caused anxiety among residents who fear that criminals may target them and steal their property. Akinyi, however, filed a report at the Aram Police Station regarding the attack. Rarieda OCPD Johana Chebii confirmed that suspects and Omosa will be arrested and charged with robbery. He added that residents should avoid confrontations and resolve issues peacefully instead of taking the law into their own hands, warning that such actions could lead to more problems. {story by Ontiri from Texas}

Abagaka baria babo Ongwae Mekenye na Filbert Misire mbaroche aya? On that note nevertheless, I still wish to take this opportunity to thank our ancestors wherever they are in their graves for preventing it from happening. May their souls reign forever. ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Omogaka sokoro ominto nabwate eng'ana. Nigo sokoro agoteba buna Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. "Bono ekio ninki omogaka?" Nche nigo natang'ang'a nkoboria. Omoremi nkogenda are gosamora chibando aaria Nyanguru Hill, Kisii County. Kang'wanigwa n' rise n' chinyanduri, omoremi oyo agaansa gokura, ogotumatuma na gochachana! Nyanguru Hill eyio. Ng'ai miino ere? : Picture na special correspondent, Gusii.com files. Nigo sokoro ominto antebia ng'a oyio n' omobayeno oito ntwe Abagusii korwa bokoro. Ase ogotosomia igoro y' omobayeno oyo oito, omogaka sokoro nigo antebia omogano. Nigo omogaka ateba ng'a abwo kare na kare, omoremi oyomo narengeo. Bono omoremi oyo akamanora gochia kogesa chibando chiaye korwa ase endemero yaye. Keri keri, kare nchera kwagachia, akaumerana n' omobisa oye nchera abwo mbarabare. Obe! Omobisa oyio n' rise n' chinyanduri! Bono ko baumerana n' omoremi oyo gochia korigereria ensemo iga, omobisa oyo akamong'wania ne rise n' chinyanduri! "Aaachie che che...bono ngaki ngokora?........." Omoremi oyo agaansa gokura, ogochachana na gotumatuma gaansa korurwa. Korwa abwo, omoyo okaamba gokwa nga tagenda mogondo, airane gochia bwoye. Nonya nabo igo, mbarabare abwo, omogaka oyomo narengeo oyatengerete amakore aya onsi. Tobwatekania omobisa. Aye manya ekerenga kiao. Bono omogaka oyo agatebia omoremi oyo takwa omoyo, korende agenderere ne esabari yaye y' okogenda mogondo kogesa chibando. Omogaka oyo akamosegeta buya. Bono omogaka sokoro nigo agoteba buna omobisa nigo agotaka gokobogeria korwa ase emeremo yao eri bwanchente gokora. Korende nebeterereti ng'a goika omanye ekerenga kio omobisa erinde bweatanane korwa ase are. Eng'ana eye nigo egosegeta omonto otware omokia erinde omobisa tanyora ribaga ri' okomokorekania, egere atige emeremo yaye. Eke nakio kiagerete Abagusii abakoro bagateba buna Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. Korwa ase omogaka sokoro ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week and thank you for listening.

Then he went to visit Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. “What is this thing about the old man?” He then started complaining bitterly. This reporter who goes to cover news around Nyanguru Hill, Kisii County. Troubled by heat and dust, this reporter refuses to rest, jumps around and gets excited! That Nyanguru Hill. What is happening today?: Picture and special correspondent, Gusii.com files. Then people noticed that this was how the Abagusii people were being treated. After thoroughly examining this treatment, the old man refused to accept it. And the old man realized this time and again, this reporter was persistent. Why does this reporter continue to chase news so that he can fulfill his duties? Quickly quickly, I almost forgot, he reconciled with the person he had previously disagreed with. Oh! This person is troubled by heat and dust! So when they reconcile with this reporter to discuss important matters, this person complains about the heat and dust! “Aah… what is going on?...” This reporter refuses to rest, gets excited and jumps around refusing to be calmed down. Because of this, this life seems like it won’t end, he continues chasing after it. Despite all this, those people, the old man who was persistent has been honored with all these years. Let us respect this person. Let everyone know their worth. Why did the old man notice this reporter wasn’t living well, so he encouraged him to continue pursuing news so he could fulfill his duties. The old man was very grateful. Why did the old man then realize that the person wanted to show them how they were being mistreated so they could address it? Continue investigating and find out what this person’s value is so that people don’t take advantage of them. Little money is enough to make someone forget everything and abandon their responsibilities, so that they can fulfill their desires. Indeed, let us remember the Abagusii elders who visited Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. Because of the old man and the people, this person will be our topic for this week and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Monunguno O Barema (February) 15, 2011. Aya amwabo aya: "Nintagete kogenda bware" Ebimura binde can't wait kogenda iburu. Iburu, maguta motwe no okwaroka na amarieta ye Ekegusii yo ogosara. Abaisia ki baikire emiaka ikomi mbaka ikomi ne ebere nigo bare goisanera kogenda iburu. Mara enyinge, iburu nigo yare gochiegwa ase engaki yo omotienyi bwe Egesunte kende (December) ase kera omwaka. Abaisia nigo bare kwearigania ase omoyega oyo buna ekobwatia. Nigo bare korigia chingoko bagochia konyenya ne ebitugi bio ogouta omorero ekero bare nyomba. Inyora inga morero bwo omware tonya korima. Omosari nigo arenge koba oyomo ase ekenyoro ekegima na abasae bataranywoma nabwo bare kobira abaisia ekero bare gochia iburu. Obotuko bwo ogokiera rituko rie enyangi ya iburu, aba be enyangi nigo bare korara na abamura barie bachiete iburu banyenya chingoko. Mambia maaambia, nigo abaisia aba bare koirwa roche gwesibia amache amakendu na korurwa ne chinyanduri ne risa egere beariganie ase enyangi eye. Abasegi nigo bare kobogoria amatimo na kweboyia amayo. Egetono nigo kiare korosigwa kiamanya koruma buna endo. Aaiga, nigo bare gotebigwa buna endo igo yare kobamera nande yabaroka. Ekero kio ogosarwa gwaikire nigo oyo ore kogenda iburu are gotarera omote gochia magega egere tarora amanyinga buna agoiteka. Korwa aiga amatera yo obware aterwa kwagachia ase omware are koirwa. Omorero nigo ore gosegeswa bwoka amatuko onsi pi omware are nyomba. Ki yare komochani orime, nigo yare koba chimuma naende yare kobetereria okorerane chisokoro. Omware nigo are gosoa saiga na korwa gesieri korende tare koirorera goeta gesieri eke. Korwa bono, nigo are gotumia etirisa. Omware nao agasokeire etirisa ochia gwota ensakia korende kera rituko nigo are kweyaka ribu. Mware tare korora gose gwesibia mache mpaka arwe nyomba. Abare nigo bare kobeka egesena. Abwo nyomba, nigo bare gokora emekubio ene. Engaki eyio ye emekubio ene kiyaerire, nigo yare gokagerwa buna omware obwenire na korwa nyomba. Ekero akorwa nyomba, mware tare gweeta gesierie keri asoerete. Nigo are kogenda roche bwesibia na kweboyia buya. Korwa aiga mware tare korara saiga aria ase arenge nyomba. Nigo are korara ase eamate amatuko abere omanya koirana sobo. Goansera aiga omware bono nigo are no obosiborwe bwo ogotumia gesieri kende gionsi gia saiga. Bono gochakera engaki eye, momura bwarogete tare gosoa ase abaibori bare korara. Echio ne chimuma. Inee rero enyangi eye nereo?
english: By Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. February 15, 2011. These are the words: "One who doesn't hurry won't get far." The elders say they can't wait to get old. Old age, wisdom comes with gray hair and experience in the Ekegusii language of our ancestors. People often live for many years, up to eighty or ninety years, before they prepare to become old. But nowadays, old age is celebrated during the month of December at the end of the year. People strive for good health so that it may benefit them. They build houses and acquire possessions and livestock so that their homes are beautiful. A home without wealth is not admirable. The community gathers to help those who are sick and the youth assist the elderly in preparing for old age. The tradition of honoring the months of old age, those months are when people and relatives visit the aged and share stories. Truly speaking, it is the elderly who remember past events and are reminded through songs and dances about the months of old age. The young ones respect traditions and appreciate gifts. Poverty is said to prevent someone from understanding things fully. Sometimes, they are given assistance so that they may recover and become strong. Before something valuable is lost, it is better to prepare to become old and strengthen oneself to gather knowledge so that it remains. Work done by women and men is carried out to improve the home. Wealth should be used wisely to ensure that everything is well within the home. If it is not managed properly, it will diminish and disappear quickly. A person should work hard and diligently, always striving to achieve success. Work alone, however, is not enough; one must also have blessings. A person who has blessings receives gifts and remembers the past. A home should be protected against thieves until it becomes established. People often save money. That savings, when used to rebuild the home, ensures that the home is secure and work continues. Before starting new work, a person should first assess their resources. They should then begin slowly and carefully. Work done by a person who plans ahead is successful because they know how to manage their time. Preparing for tomorrow requires a person to be diligent and work consistently, always striving to succeed. Work today, therefore, is important.

english: These are the words: The heart feels like a person who has been troubled and does not understand how to continue studying the matter of the elders and their customs. Let them cry, the heart remembers the elders and their time. So, people say that the elders have power and can cause harm: 19. Did he delay coming from Heaven, and when he came down, did he appear like a foolish child? What reason makes him sit quietly and listen to advice: A wise person who understands things well knows how to listen to advice from someone who speaks truthfully and wisely. Why? A wise person needs to learn things. And again, therefore he listens to advice carefully, a leader who knows what is good, knows how to choose good things over bad ones! It is very important. That is why: Tradition preserves the history of ancestors. And also this: The truth is that some people do not want others to live a righteous life. But what is the problem? They will be ashamed. The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times. [ righteousness ]. In ancient Kisii, a person truly respected those who were disciplined. Consider how a parent treats a child, teaching them respect. This is the strength of Kisii culture, which has endured through hardship. Picture and Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files. 21. The problem of old times always remains: Anyone who disrespects the ancestors [ righteousness ], a person who does not value tradition. Similarly, anyone who disrespects parents also does not value tradition. But what is the problem? The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times [ righteousness ]. 22. Remember this point: A wise person does not reveal secrets carelessly. Be careful, and let wisdom guide you. Also, a leader should not be careless, lest they regret it. Let everyone carry their own burden, Kisii people know how to bear it. 23. I finish speaking these important words: A person carries a heavy burden when they travel and find themselves in a difficult situation. Let them go slowly. Why? Because it is better to be cautious than reckless. This message brings comfort to the heart. He says that if they accept it, let them remember this thing. Drink these waters, and thank you for listening.

Ekero ore Gusii, nabo okorora buna omogaso ogoansa mambia naende buna risase rikorimera morogoba. Onye kore ase chinse chinde, goika oakane chibesa otarigwe impaka ase atambe erinde ororore buna risase rikorimera, onye kore ne bahati. Onye tori nka Gusii, tori korora buna risase rikorimera 2. Mache tari gwansa. Ekio nakio egento egetangani okorora. 3. Mabere tari gwansa. Nobeka amabere angana inaki ase echae, aye ne chinsa ogosaria. Egento amabere ye chinse chinde are, nigo abekire ebinto bigokobotia. 4. Onde bwensi mokoumerana nigo agokoboria inga, "Aye seino ingai" Korende ekero ore nka seino Gusii, nigo okoborigwa inga, "Aye tori mochokoro o Manoti......Manoti nomosani one....." 5. Nyoko koro tari gokobisera kende. Ekero okogenda gokwania nyokokoro, nigo agoikoinekera naende okobisera ebisukari. Onde takobikuna. Nyokorome nigo agokonyenyera engoko oteba inga ekebwato eke neki omoigwa....onde tasumbua omoigwa... 6. Nyoni tichiri kogoterera rimaambia echuni. Nyoni tichiyo. Nigo obwenerete gweterera aye bweka. 7. Nigo okona korenda inga ne chinsa irenga chire. Aye negetongu giensa. Ekero ore Gusii okona goaka oboche aaria etuka maate..... gose okona gosiswa etuki na abasani bao... ningo ore na acha n' chinsa? 8. Omogaso ekero ochire, oyio no omogaso. Obokendu ekero bwachire, obwo no obokendu. Obokendu na omogaso o Gusii tona goita onde. Ekero ore ase chinse chinde naende batebe inga ense neche ekende, wewe chunga sana. 9. Chinsaga. Tichiyo. Amabere amaroranu. Echio ne chindoto. Rinagu, risosa, ebisukari, erongori yobori, egesare, rikuneni.. ebio bionsi tibiyo. Goika origi obongaini bonde konyora ebinto ebio. 10. Ekerisimasi nerituko erimo rioka (inyora buna aye negetongu giensa - namba 7 igoro). Ekero ore nka Gusii, ekerisimasi nomotienyi omogima na gochi igoro. 11. Narotire kinde Gusii. Nankio nankio, nigo okona korota buna nao ore nka Gusii, kore amo na abasani bao. Gusii n' erwenyi y' omwando.
english: 1. A child who cries a lot causes trouble and also causes annoyance. In our Gusii culture, people cry a lot when they are happy and when they cry because of sadness. Anyone who doesn't know how to cry, let them learn how to cry so that when they cry because of sadness, they will be lucky. Anyone who is a true Gusii person, cries a lot when they are sad. 2. Rats don't have respect. This world is full of people who cause trouble. 3. Old men don't have respect. Sometimes old men say things that hurt others, and it is considered bad manners. Let old men speak only good things and avoid saying hurtful words. 4. A foolish person boasts and says, “Today is my day.” In our tradition as Gusii people, boasting is discouraged and said like, “I have finished working at Manoti… Manoti is very far away…”. 5. A lazy person does not succeed. Our ancestors said that laziness leads to poverty, and one should work hard to earn sugar. Don't be idle. Lazy people always complain about their lives like a boat without an oarsman…don’t bother the oarsman… 6. Birds chirp while pecking at grains in the field. These are small birds. It is appropriate to listen to them and watch them. 7. People boast as if they own everything. They speak carelessly. In Gusii culture, people brag about owning large farms…they boast about being wealthy and having many wives…what is the benefit of bragging? 8. A good custom is a good thing, and a bad custom is a bad thing. A bad custom and a good custom of the Gusii people can ruin someone. Be careful when dealing with people who behave strangely. 9. Greetings. Small birds. Old men who cry. This is a curse. Salt, soda, sugar, cooking fat, millet, sorghum…all those things are not free. Learn from wise people who understand life and appreciate valuable things. 10. Christmas has come with its joy (remember what was said in point 7 above). In our Gusii culture, Christmas is a time for eating meat and drinking beer. 11. I remember this Gusii land. Again and again, people boast as if they are Gusii people, associating themselves with the elders. Gusii is a land of abundance.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Amaoga a Thanksgiving korwa ase Aida Morgan Nigo barwete Bongeresa chitariki 6, omotienyi o Kianda (Tureti ya Kebaki), omwaka 1620. Bagatara ase enyancha ase emetienyi ebere. Bagaika Massachusetts omoerio bwo omotienyi o ikomi na rimo (Egesunte). Nonya nabo igo, ase tarenge aroro agiya ase obwato bwarenge kobekwa. Rakini ase chitariki 11 chio omotienyi o ikomi na kabere (Egesunte Kende), bakanyora ase agiya aaria Plymouth Rock. Nonya banyorete ase bakobeka obwato, emechando ya abanganyi aba 102 korwa Bongeresa konyora teraera. Amarwaire. Chisegi na Abaindi. Enchara. Nigo baigete Amerika engaki yo obokendu. Ekero omotienyi o Kane (Rigwata) omwaka 1607 ochiete goika, konyora enusu ya abanganyi aba 102 bakure. Buna Nyasae abangete, bagasimeka endagera engaki eyio ye Rigwata. Endagera ekama buya. Ase ogoakera Nyase inga imbuya mono, abanganyi aba amo na Abaindi bari barenge abasani bagateba inga tiga omoyega obe aroro bwo ogoakera Nyasae asante. Rituko rio ogoaka inga imbuya mono rikaiborwa. Omwaka o 1789, Omogambi George Washington agateba inga tiga rituko rio ogoaka imbuya mono ribekwe. Rakini nigo yairete impaka omwaka o 1941 ekero Bunge yaetetie inga kera Tichi Kane yo omoerio bwe Egesunte obe eholidei enene Amerika. Inche nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase obomoyo korwa ase Nyasae. Nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase ebisio nanyorire ase omwaka oyo. Akamoisia gaito, Barack Obama Ochwoga Nyaberi Orongo Manyange nigo kaiborwa omotienyi omotangani (Engatiato) omwaka oyo. Abachokoro bo omongina Kerubo no omogaka Nyaberi inkona komentekana bare. Ekio nakio ekeegwa ekenene sana ase inche korwa ase Nyasae ase omwaka o 2009. Eria Kabere, imbuya mono ase abasomi ba Gusii.com. Onye tari inwe nanga ewebusaiti eye teiyo. Ninwe mogotoa omokia kera rituko. Nigo ingoakera Nyasae inga imbuya mono ase okobaa ribaga rio ogosoma Ekegusii. Inee? Aye rende? Inkwaboka bono mambia? Nobwate ase okorara? Kwarire kende rero? Nobwate agachanchabe okona kobeka? Nobwate mosani onde? Moiri onde rende? Buya sana. Tebia Yeso inga imbuya mono. Omonguru bweka. Intobwati kende otatiga korwa ase Nyasae. Rituko rigiya ria Thanksgiving. Amerika Egenderere. Kenya Egenderere. Omogano o Thanksgiving korwa ase Christian Answers. Jared nyaberi, Omosomba bwe Ekegusii nao agotoka ase Abagusii at gmail dot com amo na Facebook dot com/abagusii
english: These are their stories: The first Thanksgiving was celebrated by Aida Morgan They wrote about it on November 6th, the pilgrims of England (United Kingdom), in the year 1620. They traveled from another country to a new land. They arrived in Massachusetts, a beautiful place of arrival and rest (America). After a few days, they built houses and prepared to plant. On November 11th, they landed on a rock (American shore), and they remembered their journey to this area called Plymouth Rock. After writing and building boats, the group of 102 passengers thanked God greatly. It was difficult. Sickness and Indians. Hunger. They came to America seeking freedom. In 1607, the colony of Jamestown (Virginia) almost failed, and only half of the 102 passengers survived. But God helped them, and they established a strong colony in Virginia. The colony thrived. And because of God's grace, those people and the Indians became friends and lived together peacefully, thanking God for his help. That tradition of giving thanks continued. In 1789, President George Washington declared that day as a national day of thanksgiving. Later, in 1941, Congress officially designated the fourth Thursday of November as a major American holiday. Today we celebrate that day of thanksgiving and remember God. We celebrate that day remembering the events of that year. Recently, Barack Obama, son of Nyaberi Orongo Manyange, was inaugurated president that year (America). The leaders of the church and the pastor Nyaberi were present. This event was widely publicized and celebrated as a blessing from God in 2009. Greetings, thanksgiving to the readers of Gusii.com. Anyone who has information should visit the website. Share this story with others. Let us thank God for the gift of speaking Ekegusii. What now? Are you there? Can you hear me clearly? What about resting? Is everything alright? What about building a boat? What about peace and prosperity? How is life going? Come back soon. Praise Jesus for his blessings. The preacher speaks. Let us pray diligently to God. Happy Thanksgiving Day. America celebrates. Kenya celebrates. The story of Thanksgiving from Christian Answers. Jared Nyaberi, Editor of Ekegusii and also reachable at Abagusii at gmail dot com and Facebook dot com/abagusii

ekegusii: Egesaku Omogati bw’amatunda ebwate ang’e chimbego 60 chi’emete machani ye chitropiki korwa ase omochia o Moraceae (omochie o mulberry gose chifigi). Nigo chigotoka ase Asia n’ebisinga bi’enyancha ya pacific. Omogati bw’amatunda nigo ore ang’e kobwakana chifigi. Omogati bwe ritunda osimekire mono nigo ore Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) amo amo na Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) chionsi echire ase omochie bw’omogati bwa amatunda. Parajubaea torallyi n’omote omuya korwa Amerika ya maate. Korende, tori gosimekwa mono isiko y’ase yachakerete na abaremi, Bolivia, esengencho y’echintetere chiaye chinene, eyio emoneti rigori rinene ase ogoetigwa enyancha. Oiboreire Bolivia, igo okwama ase aome naende are n’ebuse , emetaroekorakwa Inter-Andean chire n’oboigoro bwe chimita 2700–3400 igoro ya nyancha; aseigo, epamu eye nero eimogete igoro ase chikabira chionsi ense engima. Iberera ndiri goetania chidigiri 20 n’obokendu bwa botuko mbioyo. Reberera ngogenda rire inse gioka chidigiri 7 are emetienyi y’obokendu (omotienyi ogatano na kabere na omotienyi o gatano na gatato) n’embura egotwa omwaka omogima nigo ere chi mirimita 550 chioka. Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi. Ekemeri giepaini ya Khasi (Pinus kesiya) korwa Asia nigo gekwama bwago mono, naende nkeri gotoka raisi isiko ya sobo. Emete nigo egoika chimita 30–35 ase obotambe n’amatina agoika emita eyemo ase obonetu. Kera egesabo ekebwate amagwa amato akobeta atato, kera erimo rire chisentimita 15 goika 20 ase abotambe. Amatunda korwa aekemeri eke nigo are chisentimita 5 goika 9 ne chintetereechire chisentimita 1,5 goika 2,5 ase abotambe. Riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) rimanyire buna Kasturi srire rotunda rie chitripiki ang’e chimita 10–30 ase obotambe erigotoka ase asinine ase akorokwa Banjarmasin ase Borneo ya maate (Indonesia). Amatuko aya riasire gosira ekiagera rikonachwa mono. Korende, nabo rikonya gosimekwa aiga asengencho y’amatunda aye agwansa.
english: The black mulberry tree is a fruit tree belonging to the fig family (Moraceae). It originates from Asia and the islands of the Pacific Ocean. The black mulberry tree grows well in warm climates. The breadfruit tree is closely related to Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) and also Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) are all members of the breadfruit family. Parajubaea torallyi is a palm tree native to South America. Currently, it is mainly cultivated as an ornamental plant by collectors, Bolivia, where it has a significant economic importance due to its large seeds, which are used for oil extraction on the coast. Native to Bolivia, it grows in humid forests and montane forests of the Inter-Andean region at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level; however, it can also grow at lower altitudes in drier areas. It requires approximately 20 years to reach maturity and a trunk diameter of up to one meter. A mature tree can produce around 7 kilograms of seeds annually (approximately 500 seeds per kilogram) and requires about 550 millimeters of rainfall per year. Welwitschia (Welwitscha mirabilis) is a unique desert plant endemic to the Namib and Angolan deserts in southwestern Africa. Welwitschia plants are dioecious, meaning they have separate male and female individuals. The adult plant consists of a short stem with two continuously growing leaves that become twisted and shredded over time, forming a massive, tangled mass. Welwitschia reproduces sexually through cones. Khasi pine (Pinus kesiya) originates from Asia and grows well in mountainous regions, but it is also found in plantations. It reaches heights of 30–35 meters with a trunk diameter of up to one meter. It has small, needle-like leaves arranged in bundles of two, and its bark is reddish-brown. The cones of this pine tree are 5 to 9 centimeters long and 1.5 to 2.5 centimeters wide. Kalimantan mango (Mangifera casturi) is commonly known as Kasturi mango, a tropical fruit tree reaching heights of 10–30 meters, originating from lowland forests and cultivated near Banjarmasin in Borneo (Indonesia). This type of mango is known for its fragrant aroma. Currently, it is also being grown commercially for its delicious fruits.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Ase omokubio oyo oera, omogaka sokoro ominto natosemia igoro y' Omogusii oria orenge korokwa Omorominta. Ntwarora buna omorominta nigo are Omogusii oria oitete Omosigisi. Ase boigo, tokarora buna ogoitana gwaito ntwe Abagusii n' ebisaku binde nigo kwarengeo ase engencho ebisaku ebi binde biatoetanaine, biatagete gotoita. Ase rero, omongina magokoro ominto nigo atagete kobwatera abwo korwa ase sokoro atigerete. Tigwachiete nyangi? Rirorio tiyarenge konyarekana ogende ase ekeigoroigoro gi' okoremera ebiranya ase engaki eyio. Abangina nkoiririata bare aaria Keumbu. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files. Omongina baba ominto nigo agoteba buna ase chisegi chiato amo n' Abasigisi, ebiranya nkoremerwa biare. Bono okoremera ebiranya ninki? Nabo oraborie. Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa erinde Abasigisi aba ababisa baitwe ase obonge. Ase okoinyora, ntwaroche ase eganki y' omotienyi bw' Egetamo (March) omwaka oyo, buna ebiranya biaremeretwe mbaka Abasigisi abange bagaitwa ase Esegi Y' Osaosao amo na Kabianga. Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa nse. Biamanya koragererigwa n' abagaka abanene Bono baba nigo agoteba buna oyore gosicha ebiigoro igoro nere ore kogenda oremera ebiranya egere bing'use abasigisi. Bono ebiranya ninki? Kobwatekana n' baba ominto, eye n'emete yare gosunyuntwa baremera inse. Ko biaremeirwe nse, abagaka abakoro nigo bare koragereria Abasigisi. Bono Abasigisi bakonyagoka baete rioka, nigo biare kobasiekera, baitwa baera pi! Ebiigoro igoro n'omong'ina Omogusii ogasichire oba buna egosori yare gokorwa botuko korende torenge borogi. Komenta nayio, bari bare koyokora nigo bare koba getirianda! Mosacha tatakeire igaa! Ebiigoro igoro nigo biare gokorwa n' abakungu boka. Abaminto inyora buna aba n' abakungu boka bare koyokora. Oyo otamanyete, tare kogenda. Tari igo rioka, oyotachieti nyangi, taregochi aroro na torekoirwa nka. Chinyabubu nigo chiare gosicha, na aiga obosemi obonge nigo bware koregwa buna enyangi ye ebitinge, kera ekemo kie ebimira bio Omogusii na nigo yaregosicherwa orosana ime na abakorerani ao ao. Nabo omoyega bw' okoremera ebiranya orenge gokorwa igo. Until next time, omongina baba nigo ateba buna bwatera abwo and thank you for listening.
english: These are the things: It is said this day, the government is good, seeking help from people so that the Gusii nation may be remembered by the Government. We request that the government remember the Gusii nation who have helped the Kisii people. It is also said, we request that you bring gifts like the Gusii and their clans so that they can remember those clans which were forgotten, they will not fail to assist. Therefore, a person with a good heart should not fail to help them because they have assisted. Are we understanding correctly? The matter does not exceed showing respect and honoring the differences among the communities and their cultures. Those who understand well are found in Keumbu. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files. A person who loves people understands that there is a meeting with the Kisii people, differences are being honored greatly. Why honor the differences now? They are asking about it. Differences are greatly honored especially the Kisii people who show kindness to others and their generosity. Also concerning this, we request that you remember the culture of our ancestors during March of this year, so that differences are honored until the Kisii elders are called upon from Esegi Y' Osaosao and Kabianga. Differences are greatly honored indeed. They know how to cooperate with the leaders. Therefore, people understand that you should go and see the problems facing the people so that you can help them overcome those challenges. What about these differences? It is about uniting with the people, and they are happy when they are helped. Let it not be forgotten, the leaders should remind the Kisii people. Therefore, the Kisii people should rejoice and celebrate, they should sing songs of praise! These problems and the Gusii people who are suffering, it is said that they will be resolved quickly so that they don’t take too long. Comment on this, if they continue they will find solutions! The youth should not be left behind! These problems will be solved by the leaders. People say that those with the leaders should continue. This one you did not understand, go and learn. It is not a small matter, you will understand later and be rewarded accordingly. Gossip is spreading, and all the bad news has been heard that the community’s traditions, customs and values of the Gusii people have been preserved and shown to everyone and their collaborators. They also pray for assistance in resolving the differences and ensuring it doesn’t happen again. Until next time, people love and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abwo ase rinani ria Matieko, ogasusu narenge aroro amo n' ebimanu biaye. Bono Ogasusu gakonya gotara rinani eri ime, akaigwa enchara na gochaka korigia endagera. Buna Ogasusu akonya goeta ase rinani eri iime, akaumera omong'anyi okororekana omotambe gochia ime. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu amo n' ebimanu biaye bigasoa omong'anyi oyo ime. Omwango ase ogoaka esabu, Ogasusu nigo atebete buna "Ebimwana ebi rero goika toigote" Omwana oyomo ore kwaa, n' ebimwana biinde biikomotunyana koru magega, Ogasusu okare korigia endagera aaria ase orosana rwa Matieko. Omong'anyi oyo kumbe n' obwe Omansamu. Bono konyora Omansamu osokire isiko gochia koratara. Aaiga ase omong'anyi ime, Ogasusu tanyorete kende giokori korende nyuma ye chintunde chiinke igo, Omansamu akaba oiranire. Konyora atarasoa omong'anyi oye ime, konye Ogasusu okare korora Omansamu gakoirana. Ogasusu okare goaka esabu ase obwango Ogasusu akaba n' obwoba obonene, korende agaaka esabu ya bwango na korengereria eki arakore ekiagera Omansamu arenge gosoa omong'anyi oyo ime, nigo arenge gocha koria Ogasusu oyo amo n' ebimanu biaye bionsi pi. Obwango obwo obwo, Ogasusu okare goteba goteba buna "Abana bane tiga takwoboa. Bono nigo nkobaitera Omansamu oyo erinde monyare komoria" Omansamu koigwa aya, akaondoka kerage na gochaka gotama korwa ase omong'anyi oyo !! Keri keri, nario Omansamu aumerete Okabwe na komotebia buna omonto nare osoire omong'anyi oye ime na nigo atagete komoita erinde oyo n' abana baye banyore endagera bakoria. Obwango obwo, Okabwe agatebia Omansamu taoboa nonya, na komotebia amokobe gochia ase omong'anyi oye erinde arore oyo okomoseria korwa bwoye. "Abana bane, rero goika toigote" Okabwe agasibera ekemincha kiaye gochia ase Omansamu. Bono buna bare aang'e n' omong'anyi, bakaigwa eriogi rigosoka korwa ime rigoteba ibuna "Abana bane bono nari twareteirwe Omansamu n' omosani oye Okabwe. Rero goika toigote" Omansamu buna aigwete aya akaondoka mono na komanya buna Okabwe nigo among'ainete. Aaiga nario Omansamu atagete atame. Buna agasaine gotama, akanyora engori eye asiberetwe nigo yare komong'usa bobe, ekairera ekemincha gi' Okabwe kobutuka amo n' engori !! Omansamu akaminchori agatama kwagachia n' Ogasusu amo n' abana baye bakanyora ribaga bagatama korwa omong'anyi oyo.
english: These are the words: Long ago there was a child named Matieko, who greatly loved his mother and father. This child often went to the river to play, sometimes falling and getting hurt. But this child could also go to the river alone, avoiding dangers and carefully watching over himself. Because of this, this child and his parents were happy with that river. When this child grew up, this child said, “Children who are too young should not be sent.” The first child was small, and the other children followed him closely, and this child watched over himself near the river of Matieko. That river was also known as Omansamu. This famous Omansamu always had a way of helping people. When this child reached the river, this child quickly jumped across the water and then climbed a tall tree, and Omansamu was very surprised. He did not expect this child to cross the river like that, so this child made Omansamu laugh. This child then went to grow up. This child became very scared, and he went to grow up with fear and thought about what he had done to make Omansamu happy with that river, and he wanted to help this child and his parents. This fear caused this child to repeatedly say, “Four children have come and they will drown. That is why I will take this Omansamu and protect him from danger” Omansamu heard these words, and he ran away quickly and began to think about what happened with that river!! Finally, Omansamu met Okabwe and told him that the river had been causing problems for that river and that he needed to find a way to protect those children from harm. Because of this, Okabwe promised Omansamu to help him, and he vowed to use his power to prevent such things from happening again. “Four children, they should not be sent.” Okabwe remembered his kindness towards Omansamu. So when they came to the river, they fell down and started saying, “Four children, we have brought Omansamu and his family to Okabwe. They should not be sent.” But when Omansamu heard this, he ran away alone and realized that Okabwe was deceiving him. However, Omansamu didn't understand. When he looked around, he saw a shadow that had been cast upon him, which made Okabwe's tree shake violently!! Omansamu was frightened and ran back to Ogasusu and his children, and they all fled quickly from that river.

ekegusii: Kwaheri ase obotaka.Naende kwaheri ase abajumbe bari bakongaina Abananchi omwaka ase kera omwaka inga emasini ya amatoke neche erosigwe Gusii. Abajumbe bonsi ba Gusii. Obosoku sana. Twatwarire chimbuche toganyete emasini ya amatoke Gusii. Genda gochia aaria. Abasae ba Gusii bakanire inga tibari koganya amangana yo oborimo. Nyambega Gisesa nigo agoteba inga abasae ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Group baansire korosia chindagera ao ao korwa ase amatoke na gochionia ase efaida. ase omobwekano, nigo bakogora ritoke ase Ksh. 300. Bamanya koroisia chichip echio bakoonia ase rigori ria Ksh.1,680. Tari chips chioka bakoroisia. Korwa ase amatoke, nigo bakoroisia obosie,chikeki,ejamu,echuisi,amarwa,chingori,amajambe amo ne chogopia. Emasini eye ne chibesa irenga yaira? Ksh.chimillioni 6. Ase emiaka emenge sana, abaremi ba Gusii nigo bakoriegwa chibesa na abagori ba amatoke abwo bakoyaira ase emechie emenene ya Kenya na koyaonia ase efaida enene sana. Amatoke nigo akoonigwa aaria Kisumu, Kitale, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru na kera ase. Abasae aba ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Goup nigo bagokorera egasi yabo aaria ase omochie o Miriri. Omosike James Omiso nere omonyakerogo bwe ekeombe eke. Omochie o Miriri nigo ore chikilomita 23 korwa Bosongo. Ebara ye ramu nechiete impaka Miriri? Yaya. Amache nangusire? Nonya. Omorero rende? Hakuna. Ayio onsi taratanga abasae aba baito. Ekeombe eke nigo kebwate abasae ange 44. Bonsi nigo baigete fomu fo yoka. Banyorire ogokonywa korwa ase Farm Africa, Kenya Industrial Research Development Institute (Kirdi), International Service for Acquisition of Agri-biotechnology Application (Isaaa) na Kenya Gatsby Trust. Ekeombe kia Kirdi nakio kiabaete emasini. Kitutu Masaba CDF nero iyakora buya ase okobakomboera enyomba ase bakogacha amatoke. Buya sana. ekegusii: Rhapidophyllum hystrix Rhapidophyllum hystrix n’eyemo ye Chipamu chikoremerereia obokendu obonene ase chimbego chie chipamu. Embego n’eyemo yoka ere ase egesaku kia Rhapidophyllum. Igoogosimekwa ase akendu ase chinsemo chia USA ya maate- moino. Korene n’gesio ase okoremeriria kwaye kw’obokendu bore inse buna chidigiri 20 igo yaanchire monoe getich mono imeya Yuropu. Nigo ere embego y’epamu enkong’u, naende ekwama chimita 1–3 chioka ase obotambe n’amagwa amaya ase ritina. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix igo ere enke ekorusia chimbande raisi, amatina amange akorosia ekemeri ekegare mono. Ase engaki entambe, amatina ayio narosi orosana oronene. Epamu y’esindani teri korosi matina korende ekobi erakine goika chimita 1,2 ase obotambe goika 17,8 ase obogare. Amatina nigo abwate amato amakoro, amatwaro, n’amagwa amatanyerere amatambe. Nigo atirete buya , gose aarare inse ekiagere chikorwanerera oborabu gose ekiriri. Chintetere nigo chigosimekwa ase abwate amache. Ase amiaka 3 ametang’ani. Nigo etakeire chibe are n’obokendu. Epamu y’esindani igo egotaka ase are n’omoika bwa amache naende ebekwe ase omogaso gose ekiriri ementwe omogaso buna egokina. Eekororekana buya ekero chibekire ase ekiriri akeigo. Ekero chiamete ase omogaso omogima, ekobi ekobwatana n’amato asitia ekara machani. Ebimeri bietaneti emiaka 3 nabo bikogachwa isiko y’egeticha ase omwaka omogima onye komenyete ase riberera ritari goetania chidigiri 10. Buna enkendu, epamu ekoremereria obokendu nigo etakeire gosimekwa ase riroba rieteti amache buya naende ebekwemaate. Omobisa omonene bw’epamu eye tari bokendu korende riroba ribwate amache amange. Ribererea riainse mono amo n’eriroba ribwate amache amange nigo agosaria emerio. Epamu eye nabo ekonyara komenyera obokendu chidigiri –15 goika –20. Riberera ria inse mono rimanyire yamenyerete riarenge chidigiri –28.
english: Rhapidophyllum hystrix Rhapidophyllum hystrix is a plant from the large palm family of the palm tree. The leaf is a typical leaf of the genus Rhapidophyllum. It originates from the forests of the southeastern United States. The seed is collected and planted so that about 20 seeds can be transported to Europe each year. It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. On fertile soil, the roots become very large. The fan palm does not have climbing roots, but rather roots that reach a length of 1.2 m and a depth of 17.8 cm. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. Cold tolerance varies depending on the variety, but most varieties can tolerate temperatures down to -15 to -20 degrees Celsius. Extremely low temperatures below -28 degrees Celsius can cause damage.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abagambi Ba Abagusii Ekero Omosongo Aigete Nka Gusii Ase orogendo amo n' okong'anya gwaito, Abagusii ntwaigete ase tokwebaka amarieta y' ching'iti ao ao. Ase okoboria, ntoratebigwa buna ninki kiagerete tokeebaka iga. Ninki gose? Mbuya ki twaroche ase chingiti echi ekagera tokeebaka amarieta abo? Buna togotebigwa, Abagusii mbebagete amarieta ayio akobwatia: (I). Ababasi nigo bebagete, Enchage (Zebra ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, nigo togotebigwa buna Omobasi n' omongaini! Omobasi nere oorogeti Omogusii buna eng'ombe ekobaswa korwa ebigoti! Abagusii bande nigo barenge konyenya eng'ombe korwa omogongo! Nonya nabo igo, abande nigo bagoteba buna Ababasi nigo babasete eng'era korua omogong'o rika rie ritana, erio bakarokwa Ababasi! (II). Abagirango. Engo (leopard ase Ekenyamorero). Omogirango nigo agirete koria engo. Oyo nere naende omomura okabere ase Omogusii, naende okorokwa Omogirango Omosweta! (III). Abanyaribari. Aba nabwo naende bamanyire buna Abasweta ((Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, naende bamanyire buna Abanyaribari Amang'eng'a! Aba nabwo bagatangire esegi ko yatindiire korwa Bomanyi, buna togotebigwa. Tari igo rioka. Omonyaribari nere obarete, gose kobaga Omogusii bwensi ase abeta ritangani. Abagambi bari babarete Abagusii ritangani nao barwete Nyaribari. (IV). Abamachoge. Tari Abanyaribari boka barenge kweroka Abasweta. Abamachoge nabarabwo nigo bebagete Abasweta (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). (V). Abanchari. Engubo. Omonchari nere Engubo Y' Ndiba chia Bokendu! Engubo nigo yanchete komenya aase amache amakendu ime. Ntwe ntomanyeti gose eke nakio kiagerete Abanchari bakeeroka erieta eri. (VI). Abagetutu. Aba nabwo Abasweta abatang'ani (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Omogetutu nere omomura omonene. Oyo nere naende okorokwa Enda Y' Enchogu nyabana bange! Korwa ase omongina magokoro Kwamboka Mireri amo na abagaka chisokoro Samuel Omare Nyambisa amo n' Kenyanya Marube, mbuya mono and thank you for listening. english: These are their stories: The Clans of the Gusii People, the Council of Elders, they speak like the Gusii. They travel far and gather little things, the Gusii people don't understand how to save small amounts of money at all. They are wasteful, but traditions remain strong so they can save something. What is this? My mother tells us about the tradition of saving small amounts of money from time immemorial? But it is said, the Gusii people have forgotten those old ways of saving: (I). The Herdsmen, they save, Zebras and Wild Animals. Comment on this, it is said that the Herdsmen and the Farmers! The Herdsman who herds cattle is like a Gusii man whose cow has calves! The Gusii people today no longer bother to milk cows until their udders are full! Despite this, they say that the Herdsmen saved enough wealth to buy things: (II). The Hunters. Leopards and Wild Animals. The Hunter hunts for leopards. This one also goes to the forest to become a Gusii, and is feared by the Leopard Clan! (III). The Gatherers. These ones also know that the Baboons and Wild Animals. Comment on this, they also know that the Gatherers are skilled! These ones collect firewood to cook food for the elders, but it is said. It is not always easy. The Gatherer is respected, what does it mean to be a Gusii person among those who are knowledgeable? The clans were respected by the Gusii people and they fought against the Gatherers. (IV). The Machoge Clan. It is not the Gatherers who bother to fear the Baboons. The Machoge clan also respect the Baboons and Wild Animals. (V). The Chari Clan. The Shield. The Chari person is the Shield of the Bokendu family! The shield protects the entire Bokendu homestead. I don't know what makes them think that the Chari people will abandon their inheritance. (VI). The Getutu Clan. These ones are the Baboons who fight (Wild Animals). The Getutu person is a very large man. This one also fears the Land of the Enchogu people, his relatives! From the hearts of our ancestors Kwamboka Mireri and the elder Samuel Omare Nyambisa and Kenyanya Marube, my mother says and thank you for listening.
