Bono onye moamate onde narengeo otarenge gocha goikerana, omwana naende nigo arenge koegwa egetari, omoirera. Abagusii nigo twanchete oboamate obuya amo na abaminto ekiagera nigo twamanyete buna Ekeumbu Kiaare, Nkegundi Boba. Ase enchera ende, egento keri kere aange naye, gose ori mobebekaine nere ore aange naye, nabo aragokonye kobua ori ore aare. Bono obonabwo oboamate obuya. Abagusii abakoronigo banchete oboamate obuya amo n' omorembe. Obwanchani n' abamino negento ekiya. Tiyarenge koba buya aye tata onya gotiokia amandasi gose chinyama ch' ebitinya koru bwoo, korende aye toromia onde kende !! Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com. Engatiato [January] 7, 2016. Aya amwabo aya: Tokare kobweria riitoke omogoye bono emorogoba, omong'ina baba Nyamboto ominto nigo antebetie buna Oyomino Moromie Esukubi Egechuria Nere Maarekana Agocha Aita. Bono ninki engencho y' omobayeno oyo? Ritangani, omongina nigo antebetie buna abwo kare, abanto nigo barenge gosanga endagera mono kobua rero. Omonto ekero anyenyire eng'ombe gose embori, nigo arenge koa oyomwabo egetari. Bono aya akwaneire ase omorabaro oyo n ogosanga aamo n' abamino. Ase omobwekano, Esuguku eye yaerete n' eyogosanga yarenge. Ogosanga nabamino, keri egeke obwate. Esukubi nigo yarenge koba enyama enkong'u pa. Aye onye totageti koa omoamate oo ritana gose enyama yanda, otakomoa esukubi rende? Ase enchera ende, aye moe enyama eri kwarenge gocha gosieereria. Ere nabo akogoka. Naye kae oyomino egetari Omogusii omokoro nigo atagete tomenye n' omorembe amo ' oboamate obuya. Oboamate bwao na abaamino nigo bwarenge kobwenera na korendwa erinde bobe obuya. Oboamate obuya amo n' abamino negento kiarenge ekiya ekiagera abaamate nabwo baragokonye ekero ore ne emechando. Bono ekerenga ekene ki' omobayeno oyo ninki? Tobaisa koanga omonto omino. Oyomino nere ogwenerete koa esiko, obwanchani na komenya nere buya ekiagera ekero kie emechando, nere oragokonye. Oyomino nere ore aange naye. Oyo nere oragoike aange ase obwango ekero obokongu bwabeire. Oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week. Koru ase omongina baba Nyamboto ominto, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.
english: PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Born on [January] 07, 2016. Many good things have been said, people say that when someone has many children they feel happy because those children bring honor to their home. Also, concerning marriage, our mothers say that a woman who has cattle, goats, and cows feels proud and respects her husband. She also says that a person should raise a child and teach their siblings so that they grow up well. Many mothers today no longer want to listen to advice, a child nowadays does not respect elders anymore. The Gusii people cherish relationships with both relatives and friends and we know that Ekeumbu Kiaare, Nkegundi Boba are examples. But truly, sometimes a person may be poor but still have hope, even though they are poor they can still persevere. This is about the importance of relationships. The Gusii elders who were warriors cherished relationships with everyone. Traditions and customs are important to us. Don't let anyone steal your land or property, protect them fiercely, otherwise they will take everything from you!! Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com. Born on [January] 7, 2016. These are their names: Don't forget to remember the difficult times, the ancestors of Nyamboto people say that Oyomino Moromie Esukubi Egechuria Nere Maarekana Agocha Aita. What is this story about? Remember, the ancestors say that it was like this before, people used to live happily together. Someone who owns cattle and goats feels honored. These names are mentioned so that you remember them along with others. Concerning marriage, Esuguku is respected and admired. They are remembered by others, sometimes it is difficult. Esukubi says that meat is very delicious. Someone doesn't understand why meat is so important, why don't they try Esukubi? But truly, someone who eats meat feels satisfied and strong. And they become healthy. But where is Oyomino? A Gusii elder should always remember traditions and customs. Their traditions and customs should be valued and protected so that they remain forever. Traditions and customs are important to everyone and their descendants will appreciate them. What is the meaning of this story? Let's continue talking about this matter. Oyomino needs help, traditions and customs are important to everyone, especially regarding inheritance, which should be fair. Oyomino is a person who deserves respect. That person deserves praise because of their kindness and generosity. That is the news for this week. Protect the legacy of the ancestors of Nyamboto people, and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Komanyekana ase chinse chionsi, ebisaku, emenwa ao ao na abanto: Erinde intwe, ase obuya bwa Nyasae tata na omotoria oito Yeso Kristo, twarorire chibao echio chiyabwate amang’ana aya, ayio are amang’ana ya abanto ba Nephi naboigo aya AbaLamani, nabamura bamwabo, naboigo na abanto ba Jaredi, oria obeire ogokwanwa. Na twamanyire ng’a nabete agoonchorerigwa ase ekeegwa na chinguru chia Nyasae, ekiagera eriogi riaigwegete na korwa amang’ana aya ase tore; ase ayio nigo tomanyete na tore nekeene ng’a emeremo eye ney’ekeene. Na boigo nigo tokoorokia ng’a twarorire obweng’e bwa amariko aya ane ase chibao echi; naboigo obeire akworokigwa ase tore goetera ase chinguru chia Nyasae, na tari omonto. Na nigo togoteba ase amang’ana y’obwororo, ng’a omomaraika onyasae nachete inse korwa igoro, na akayareta na koyabeka ase tore ase obogima bwaito tokarigereria na korora chibao chiamariko, na obwenge boria boreo; na nigo tomanyete ng’a nase engencho y’obuya bwa Nyasae Tata na Omonene Yeso Kristo, bwagerete tokarigereria nakorwa amang’ana aya ng’a nigo are ayekeene. Na nigo kore ogoichana ase amaiso aito. Naboigo eriogi ri’Omonene nigo riatochigete ng’a tobe tokoboorokia oborori bwaito igoro ya amang’ana aya asayio, koba omoigweri ase amachiko a Nyasae, tokarwa oborori obo ase igoro yebinto ebi. Na nigo tomanyete ng’a onye tore abegenwa ase Yeso Kristo, goika toorokie chiganchwa chiaito chia, amanyinga a mwanyabanto bonsi, na chinyorekane chitari na kemoa ase obosio bw’ekerogo giekina gia Kristo, na tomenye nere kare na kare igoro. Na obonene bobe ase Tata, na Omwana, na ase Omoika Omochenu, abwe bare Nyasae oyomo. Amina.
english: Behold, I declare unto you, concerning all things, both spiritual and temporal: Hearken, ye heavens, and give ear to the words of my servant, Jesus Christ, we bear record of this church which is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, yea, and also of the people of Nephi and their brethren, and also of the people of Jared, who were spared because of their faithfulness. And we know that they were preserved by the power of God, which was manifested in them through the workings of miracles; and also we know that they were led by him through the wilderness, and he provided for them in all their needs. And it came to pass that we bear witness of the truth of these things which are written; and also that they were delivered by the hand of God, and also by his power, and also by his grace. And we testify that we have seen with our eyes and heard with our ears, and we have felt the power of God working within us to bring about these wondrous events, and to strengthen our faith in the work of salvation, and to fill our hearts with joy. And we testify that we know that the gospel of God, our Father, and of his Son Jesus Christ, is true and will be established throughout the earth, and that all men shall come unto him and be saved. And we exhort you to open your hearts and receive the truth, and to forsake your sins and turn unto God, that you may find peace and eternal life. And let the glory of the Lord be upon you. And also, the kingdom of God shall be revealed unto you, that you may understand the mysteries of his plan, and that you may prepare yourselves for the day when he shall return to reign in glory. And we testify that whosoever believeth on Jesus Christ shall be saved, and shall receive remission of his sins, and shall inherit eternal life, and shall dwell with God forever and ever, and shall rejoice in the blessings of his kingdom, and shall know that he is blessed. And honor be unto the Father, and the Son, and unto the Holy Ghost, who are one God. Amen.

ekegusii: Emebayeno Y' Abagusii: Mokungu Obande Nyabarati Ere Bweri, Torusia Mokorogoto Oagage Nsoni, Chitamere Magaachi, Otang'ang'e Tureti Binyunso Bire Mioro! Aya amwabo aya: Tata rero ayaiga n' amakong'u pa pa pa. Nonya amang'ana aya are amarito bori, omogaka sokoro ominto nigo agoteba ng'a goika ekegori eke giato egeke keyamanye. Bono gaki mang'ana ki aya? Aye nabo oratware riborio. Sokoro nigo agoteba buna amangana aya na y' chinsoni. Nigo omogaka sokoro agoteba buna Mokungu Obande Nyabarati E' Bweri Torusia Mokorogoto Oagage Nsoni Chitamere Magachi, Otang'ang'e Tureti Binyunsa Bire Mioro. Ebina bia mpango wa kando mbiakagambirwe aaria ase Etureti. Obosoku mono, naende wachilia mbali. Nigo abagaka barenge kobeka ebinyunso ase chimioro, bamanya kogayana ekina eke ki' omosacha oyo omonyaka. Below: Abakungu ba bande baikire echiro koonia endagera. Yaani gwaa! Nonye niche nigo neyagia omotwe ekero omogaka antebia omobayeno oyo. Bono nche nigo naboria sokoro angoorobererie aake, erinde nario ndamanye eng'encho y' omobayeno oyo bwa Abagusii. Bono omogaka nigo ateba buna korwa kare kare, omokungu obande nigo arenge kobwekanigwa n' eng'ombe nyabarati. Bono ase ki? Ekiagera omokung'u oyo nigo are oyo bw' omosacha oye oyomo bweka. Bono omosacha aise gokora obonyaka n' omokungu obande ( yaani korusia omokorogoto ), nigo arenge gosiria amasikani gochia ase enywomo eye. Ekero akobekwa ase Etureti y' ekenyoro, nigo arenge gotang'ang'a. Atari n' kiamboria ( gotang'ang'a magachi ). Kibagendererete kogayana, abagaka nigo barenge kobeka ebinyunso ase chimioro!! Bono omosacha oyo omonyaka nigo arenge korobekanigwa, na kogambigwa n' abagaka aba b' Etureti, abwo ase chingaki echio chinkoro. Gaikigwe ase Etureti, nigo abagaka aba barenge kobeka ebinyuso ase chimioro chiabo, erinde bagamba ekina eke ki' obonyaka! Bono ebinyunso n' ebiaki tata? Ase omorabaro oyo, okobeka ebinyunso chimioro nigo ere omobwekano bw' ogwetanga koru ase obotioku obo bwabeire ase ekenyoro, kobwatekana n' obonyaka bwo omosacha oyo. Kobwatekana n' omogaka sokoro, eng'encho enene y omobayeno oyo n' ogoteba buna obonyaka nigo bokorenta obosoku ase omonto amo n' ase ebinyoro. Bono eke nakio kiagerete Omogusii agateba buna Mokungu Obande Nyabarati E' Bweri Torusia Mokorogoto Oagage Nsoni Chitamere Magachi, Otang'ang'e Tureti Binyunsa Bire Mioro. Oyo noro omobayeno oito korwa ase sokoro gochia ase abana ba Mwanyagetinge for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.
english: The History of the Gusii: The Land of Nyabarati, Torusia the Warrior Who Brought Shame, Chitamere the Powerful, Otang'ang'e who Had Many Children! These are their stories: My father always used to say with a lot of emphasis. Whenever these stories are told, the elder says that people should listen carefully so they can understand the meaning well. Why do elders emphasize these things? Yes, they protect tradition. People should listen because these stories are important. The elder says that the Land of Nyabarati, Torusia the Warrior Who Brought Shame, Chitamere the Powerful, Otang'ang'e who Had Many Children are important. The issues of this plan have been discussed by the people of Etureti. Generally speaking, you should focus on what is important. The elders should stop hiding the children from the world, they should allow them to see what is happening around them. Below: Leaders of the land have come together to discuss development. Oh my goodness! However, I also want to remember what the elder taught me about this history. Because of this, I will try to explain the importance of this history to the Gusii people. The elder said that work should be done properly, and the land of Nyabarati should not be compared to cattle. What about this? The development of that land depends on the strength of its people. This strength allows the warrior (meaning Torusia the Warrior) to bring shame, and it shouldn't be hidden from future generations. It should be shown to those in Etureti and beyond, so they can learn. And what is the beginning (learning from the past)? Let us strive to understand, the elders should stop hiding the children from the world!! This strength of the people should be recognized, and discussed by the elders of Etureti, especially those with wisdom and experience. In Etureti, the elders should stop hiding the children from the world, so they can speak about what is happening! What are these children and grandchildren? In this regard, hiding the children from the world is like preventing someone from inheriting wealth from their ancestors, which is connected to the strength of the people. It is connected to the elder, the true meaning of this history is revealed over time, and it benefits both present and future generations. Why does everyone mention the Gusii saying that the Land of Nyabarati, Torusia the Warrior Who Brought Shame, Chitamere the Powerful, Otang'ang'e who Had Many Children are important? That is the history that needs to be worked on, especially for the children of Mwanyagetinge this week. Thank you very much and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abwo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, omoremi oyomo narengeo ase ekenyoro kia Makairo. Bono omoremi oyo natugete esese. Esese eye nigo yarenge engiya, goikera akayetigire yoka korenda omochi oye, ekero akogenda aande. Amaridadi ya amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Makairo, West Mugirango, Nyamira County. Omoremi ochire korigia kende babeke monu, na gotiga esese engiya kerendete omochie. Mwanyagetinge/2014 Nigo omoremi oyo aegenete esese eye yaye, goikera akayetigeire yamorendera omochi oye nonya ochiire atambe. Omoremi oyo narenge n' omwana omoke. Bono nabo agatigeire esese eye yaye anchete, omwana oye emorendere ekero are gosoka isiko gochia korigia kende. Esese engiya ase enka, nkorwana ekare enyameni n' engiti yarentire obobe ase omochi sobo Buna ere botambe omoremi oyo agatiga esese yaye egesumwa ime mbarabare nase aarereti omwana oye anchete kerage, akagende echiro korigia endagera. Buna omoremi oyo achiete, keri keri esese eye ekarora eng'iti nyarogendo nse egaterete omwana oyo oraire buuya otamanyeti buna omobisa omogateire. Esese eye, ekiagera yanchete omonyene omochie oyo amo n' omwana oye, ekaimoka ekagatera eng'iti eye na gokianania n'eng'iti eye. Aba babere bakarwana igo, goikera eng'iti eye egakwa. Bono esese eye ekaba amanyinga, ko omwana agatoreka akaba atarasiri n' eng'iti eye. Korwa abwo, esese eye ekaruo egasukia omwana gochia ase orwao erinde agenderere korara. Egeka getari ekenene, omoremi oyo akairana. Buna ere botambe akagenda gochia ase aarereti omwana oye omwanchu, korende tamonyora. Agakumia ekero aroche obonyinga boitegete mbarabare abuo. Ase engencho y' okorwana n' engiti nyarogenda nse, esese konyora yarosire, eraire etaigweti buna omonyene omochie nao are. Bono omoremi tachieti koira roti Omoremi oyo obwango obuo, akarengereria buna esese eye nigo yaitete omwana oye agakwa bono naki esese eye erarerete ekiagera konye yaigotire. Omoremi oyo akagenda ng'oora goikera nyomba, akaimokia egesire na agaaka esese eria ebigoti na koyeita abu abuo. Omoremi oyo ekero aitete esese agataka koyesukia. Buna akoyesukia akanyora eng'iti yarongenda inse eitire egesumu ensemo na mbarabare omwana oye omwanchu nao araire aareiri buuya. Omoremi oyo agaichana kerage ekiagera nigo achete korora ekeene buna eng'iti nyarongenda inse nigo yatagete korasa omwana oye esese egaita eng'iti eye naki arocherete amanyinga aitegete aiga. Ageitia, korende esese yaye bono konyora yakuure. Omwana oye mbuya arenge korende esese yaye yarenge komorendera omochie oye, oyeitire. Korwa erio, omoremi oyo akamanya buna teri buya gokora egento ekero ore n' ekeririanda, gose obororo.
english: These are my words: Long ago, years and years, my grandfather went to visit his friend in Cairo. That grandfather I remember very well. Very well he told stories, making people want to listen to him, so they would gather around him. The address of the eyes: Gusii.com at home area Cairo, West Mugirango, Nyamira County. My grandfather used to love telling stories to children, and he had very good stories to tell. Mwanyagetinge/2014 That grandfather told very good stories, making people want to hear them again and again, so he would continue to speak. That grandfather had a young child. And they also liked those very good stories, that child wanting to grow up like him. Very good stories about old times, a small pot in the kitchen and a spoon stirring food in the pot. So if you meet that grandfather who has good stories, remember the time when he raised his child and taught him how to respect others, so he could walk on the right path. So that grandfather succeeded, because those good stories helped the child understand things and learn from them. Those stories, which brought joy to both him and the child, were important and made the child feel safe and secure. Those people fought sometimes, making the child afraid. But those stories were comforting, so the child wouldn't be scared. Because of this, those stories helped the child overcome fear and grow stronger. It was a great honor, that grandfather was respected. So if you meet him, go and ask him to teach your child, so they can grow up wisely. He will show you what is right and wrong, and help you raise your children properly. About the struggle with life and challenges, those stories are helpful, bringing hope and encouragement to everyone. And that grandfather didn't forget his roots. That grandfather, with his wisdom, realized that those stories were helping his child grow, but he worried that those stories might become too much. That grandfather went out looking for a house, found a beautiful place and built a story there, inviting everyone to come and listen. That grandfather never tired of telling stories, always wanting to share them. So he shared them with anyone who came, writing down the lessons learned and teaching his child to appreciate them. That grandfather thought carefully about how to make those stories more meaningful, so that the challenges faced by life wouldn't overwhelm the child, and he would learn to live happily. He continued, making those stories better and better. The child grew up listening to those stories, wanting to learn from them and imitate his father, understanding their meaning. Because of this, that grandfather knew that there was no need to worry about the future, because he had given his child a strong foundation.

ekegusii: Emegano Ya Abagusii XV: "Nigo Iso Ateba, Oire Omogeni Nka, Nyoko Amonyenyere Etwani Eria Enene" Ogasusu Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi (June) 22, 2011. Aya amwabo aya: Gosenyenta ebitoche. Ogasusu obekire endagera emesa. Abwo kare kare, emiaka ne emiaka, omogaka oyomo narengeo aroro ore korokwa Ratemo. Bono Ratemo nabwate endemero enene mono. Abwo ase endemero eyio, omogaka oyo nigo asimegete emesi emenge kegima. Simbiri nyamoibi oyio! Bono Ogasusu nigo arenge gokemba ekero Ratemo atari aange na kwaye, omanya koba emesi ime na koyeria abwo mogondo ime. Ratemo akagechigwa n' Ogasusu oyo, simbiri nyamoibi. Omogaka oyo akaroisia omogwekano o mwanyabanto na koyoaka egamu na koyobeka mogondo gatigati. Korwa abwo akaganya. Aye Ogasusu, amamocho mono kegima koruta chitege Ogasusu agacha buna botambe na goansa gosenyenta emesie. Korende kagendererete koria emesie eye, akarora omonto oteneine omosonchete. Obe! obe! Agakumia kegima korende tamanya buna oyo no omobwekano. Ogasusu agasuka ange na goansa goita omobwekano oyo chitege. Amamocho amanene. Buna aansa koyoaka chitege iga, Ogasusu akananterera ase omobwekano oyo. Bono tiga achake goaka ekurate. Ogasusu agakuura na goichana mono na gwekora buna nigo akwete. Omogaka Ratemo kagocha kwaye, akanyora Ogasusu onantererete ase omobwekano oyo !! Bono Ratemo mbarenge no omwana oye. Omogaka oyo agachwata Ogasusu ne enyimbo na komorusia ase omobwekano oyo. Gakora komochwata, akabeka Ogasusu oyo egekabu ime. Ka amobeka egekabu ime, akaereria omwana oye airere ng'ina achi aiyeke, nario gakogenda nyomba, anyore endagera kere tayare. Omwana akaimokia egekabu kogenda kwagachia. Kibare ange na mwabo, Ogasusu akabugia korwa egekabu ime na koboria omwana oyo, "Inee mwana, nkwaigwa buna iso ateba?" Omwana agaitaberi ng'a ee naigwa. "Ntebie buna iso atebango naende?" Ogasusu akaboria omwana oyo naende. Nyoko amonyenyere etwani eria enene! Omwana agasinyu goteba. Ogasusu akairaneria bwango ogoteba ng'a "Nigo iso ateba, oire omogeni inka, nyoko amonyenyere etwani eria enene, oe omogeni arie amanye koegwa egetanda arare atimoke na iso gakoirana aegwe endagera entigare bamanye kogosoria no omogeni". Omwana akagoka na gotebia Ogasusu ng'a mbuya mono ase okomoinyoria aya ise amotebetie ekiagera konye bwebire !! Kibaika sobo, omwana oyo agatebia ng'ina aya Ogasusu amotebeti. Ngina agakora bo. Ogasusu akagoka, akaragera akaigota na kobutiara. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akairwa borere gotimoka na magega yaye, agaaka embuna!
english: The Tale of the Abagusii XV: "When a Person Dies, It Is Said, A Good Name Remains, So That People Remember His Deeds" By Ogasusu And Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June 22, 2011. These are the words: Protect your possessions. Ogasusu revealed a very important secret. Long ago, years and years ago, a certain poor man named Ratemo was always being ridiculed. But Ratemo had a very good heart. Because of that good heart, that man lived a long and happy life. What a wonderful story! So Ogasusu went to visit Ratemo who was sick and suffering, wanting to see how he was doing and to comfort him. Ratemo was comforted by this Ogasusu, what a wonderful story. That man showed kindness to people and helped them and calmed their hearts. This work is difficult. Oh Ogasusu, he remembers well the past. Ogasusu walks slowly and carefully protecting his secret. He continues to investigate the secret and reveals a little bit at a time. Oh! oh! He rejoices greatly because of that secret. Ogasusu is happy and carefully protects that secret. He has a big secret. When he finishes revealing the secret, Ogasusu will be praised for it. For indeed he will speak truthfully. Ogasusu investigates and learns and works until he succeeds. The man Ratemo was pleased, he praises Ogasusu for revealing that secret!! But Ratemo has a child. That man approached Ogasusu with respect and asked him about the secret. He tried hard, he told Ogasusu about the secret and put it aside. Once it is set aside, he tells his child to grow up and learn, so that when he grows older, he can remember and help others. The child goes away from home to seek knowledge. Together with his friend, Ogasusu returns home and asks the child, “Come child, why are you crying?” The child replies, “Yes I am crying.” “Why are you crying then?” Ogasusu asks the child again. So people remember great deeds! The child stops crying. Ogasusu explains the matter saying, "When a person dies, it is said, a good name remains, so that people remember his deeds, and a good person knows how to live properly and leave a legacy so that people can emulate him." The child listens and understands Ogasusu saying that those are the things he taught him. He believes completely, the child accepts everything Ogasusu taught him. He does so willingly. Ogasusu smiles, he feels satisfied and is grateful. This work, Ogasusu is left alone to think and reflect, he carries his burden!

ekegusii: Abuo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, omwana bw’ Oganchogu narengeo. Bono omwana oyo nigo arenge omwana omoningori kerage. Nigo arenge gotaka komanya amang’ana amange korwa ase ching’iti chi’ orosana chiamwabo. Omwana oyo akanya gochiera ching’iti ao ao na gochiboria amang’ana amange. Nche tombwatekania. Akamwana aka n' akang'o bono? Koigwa iga, Esirori egasingisia omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye Ritangani, agachiera eng’iti Nyarogenda Inse na gotaka komanya buna ninki gekogera atabwati magoro. Eng’iti eye tiyanyora richibu agotebia omwana oyo. Eriakabere, omwana oyo agachiera Esirori na gotaka komanya buna naki yanyorete amantonto ari abwate. Esirori yasingisirie omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye Koigwa iga, Esirori egasingisia omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye, tiyamoiraneria. Keri keri, omwana oyo agachia akanyora Okaobiria na komoboria buna naki akorete agatwara amagunchara atato. Okaobiri akamotebia omwana oyo buna ritang’ani, arigie Emamba ase enyancha yarenge, erinde amoborie buna "Chinsa chia morogoba, ninki aye, Emamba okobeka mboto?" Okaobiri agatebia omwana oyo buna ekero Emamba yamotebirie eki akoria, amanye koirana gocha ase are, erinde nere amanye komotebia buna ninki gekogera abwate amagunchara atato! Omwana oyo bw’ Oganchogu akarigia endagera are gocha koria kare ase orogendo gochia ase enyancha, eyio yakageire gotwara chimamba, erinde akore obotuki bwaye buna atagete. Bono omwana oyo agasangereria endagera echiete aroro. Korwa abwo, akamanora n' orogendo kwagachia gochia nyancha. Omwana akagenda ase orogendo oro ase amatuko atato, goikera omoerio oye, agaika nyancha. Buna aaika iga, agochaka koboria karigereretie amache ime buna "Inee, ning’o oroche Emamba?" Emamba ekare gwesigori korwa amache ime, na gotebia omwana oyo atugame, nario aramomonyerere obobisi! Emamba ekare gwesigori korwa amache ime egosokia omotwe oye isiko. Ake ake, Emamba egaiteberia egoteba buna "Nao inde aaiga. Naki gwataka?" Koigwa iga, omwana oyo akaboria emamba buna "Inee chinsa chia marogoba ninki okoria?" Emamba eye egatebia omwana oyo atugame, erinde amomonyere buna ninki akoria chinsa chia marogoba. Omwana oyo agakora buna atebigwa na gotugama erinde atebigwe. Bono buna atugamire iga, Emamba eria egasamia emioro y’ omwana oyo bw’ Oganchogu na koyeroma bororo kegima. Omwana oyo akeng’usa gose n’ ekonye. Buna akonya kweng’usa emioro yaye nero ekanya gotambea. Kiyarosa kobwaterera, Emamba ekabwatoka emioro eye. Bono riria abwatokwa iga, omwana oyo akanyora buna emioro yaye yatambeire! Agachia koganya igo gose neirane buna yarenge kare, ekaanga. Bono korwa erio Oganchogu bande baiboretwe, bakaba bagotwara chimioro chitambe. Aya amwabo aya:
english: Long ago, years ago, the child of Oganchogu was restless. That child was indeed a very stubborn child. He wanted to know the secrets that people kept hidden in their homes. That child thought about entering homes here and there and stealing those secrets. I don’t understand. What is this child doing, really? Truly now, Esirori shook her head and went to sleep. Listen, she entered Nyarogenda Inse’s home and wanted to know what she was saying about her husband. That home did not welcome the child. Later, the child entered Esirori and wanted to know why she had hidden certain things from him. Esirori shook her head and went to sleep. Truly now, Esirori shook her head and went to sleep, she didn’t get angry. Eventually, the child went and asked Okaobiria and inquired why he hid the small treasures. Okaobiri scolded the child, telling him that if he listened to Emamba who lives nearby, he would learn that “What kind of question is that, Emamba, why are you hiding things?” Okaobiri told the child that when Emamba finished what she was doing, she would tell him everything, so he should stop asking questions and instead find out what she was hiding regarding the small treasures! The child of Oganchogu remembered his journey and how he used to steal near the river, then he realized he could take the lion’s share if he succeeded. That child found himself on a difficult path. Because of that, he planned his journey to steal from the river. The child walked along that path and through the fields, reaching his destination, where he found the river. When he reached it, he started thinking about how to steal the fish, saying, “Indeed, will I ask Emamba?” Emamba, who was guarding the fish, told the child to come closer, but warned him not to be greedy! Emamba, who was guarding the fish, lowered her head slightly. Then, Emamba said, “Who is coming now? What does he want?” Truly now, the child asked Emamba, “Indeed, what kind of question is that?” Emamba, who told the child to come closer, then warned him about what kind of question he was asking. The child replied that he wasn’t being rude and just wanted to come closer. But when he came closer, Emamba saw the child’s intentions with Oganchogu and began to tremble violently. The child stretched out his hands and feet. When he tried to stretch out his legs, he realized he couldn’t move. It was frightening to watch, Emamba grabbed his legs. Once she grabbed them, the child cried out that his legs were paralyzed! He went to complain to everyone around him, claiming it was unfair. That time, Oganchogu sent messengers, and they took the legs away. These are the stories:

ekegusii: Ekegusii Jane Obuchi ‘Yaya teri bo’ Mandera agateeba, ‘Bosibore tibori gento gia koenaria’ Nechingatare chianantigwe igoro y’omonyangongo bw’Egesinga kia Robeni. ‘Yaya teri bo’ Rea agateeba. ‘Bomanyi tibori goanchera goocherera’- Nare n’ebisambo, korende tairogeti, obosio bw’Omoreeri o Bakisitani. ‘Yaya teri bo’ Rea agateeba, ‘Koegena tikori kebetererio’- Eriogi ri’omosakorwa, rikanyeku korende rienenu ase Tabuchi, Etochi ya Rea tekomisigwa ime yerikuruma ri’Abasiroti. Erio, ase ebiro biensi, eriogi ri’emuma rikoeirora- Mandera, Marara, Rea Saribu – etochi ya ‘Yaya teri bo, Burometiasi agateeba’, rigenga n’ogoteera, Bianyorire ogotiemwa, rigenga ri’obotonu riatekire goetera Chiboki na Tabuchi, erio komorekera ense naende. — Read the English translation – Mandela Comes to Leah by Prof. Wole Soyinka Jane Bosibori Marando Obuchi is a writer, researcher, and teacher. Jane has translated into Ekegusii, Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart; William Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet. english: Ekegusii Jane Obuchi “Mother, where are you?” Mandera says when she arrives, “Bosibore, let us go home together.” She refused to listen to the words of the hyena at Robeni’s place. “Mother, where are you?” Rea says when she arrives. “I know you are going to cry bitterly”— And the pots, the cooking sticks, the wealth of Omoreeri of Bakistani. “Mother, where are you?” Rea says when she arrives, “Don’t refuse to be treated well”— The stubborn child, he broke his teeth on the stones of Tabuchi, Rea’s car was overturned near Abasiroti. ekegusii: Buna Twakabeire: Na PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egetamo (March) 30, 2011. Aya amwabo aya: Mosamba Mwaye Mosamba Mwaye. "Nche ntige ndare. Esabari amo nase narwete na atambe". Omwana ekengw'erere nere okorokwa mosamba mwaye. Inee ninki gose kegerete omwana oyo orokwa erieta eri? Aaiga, nigo agosamba enda ya ng'ina, oiborwa. Korwa aaiga, naende takoirana aroro eria kabere. Yaani igo bakoranire pi ne enda ya ngina. That is it. Done. Nakio ekio gekogerea otebwa inga osambire mwaye. Abagusii bateba buna oyio mosamba mwaye. Ase omobwekano, nigo togoteba inga "Banchiri nanyorete mosamba mwaye, tiga aratoa echae tomwasimori". Igwa bono. Enyangi ya Mosamba Mwaye: "Rioba nderere" Mosamba mwaye ekero atokire, enyangi yaye neroo yo okomwarigania gocha ase ense eye. Ritangani, omwana nigo are gosokigwa isiko nyuma ye emekubio ebere. Ngina omanya korigia egesero obeka omwana kebeko. Omanya kobeka egesero motwe oteba iga, "Rioba ndererere". Okwo no ogosaba Nyasae amokinerie omwana. Ekegeni kiamanya koariganigwa. Amaru nigo are koengwa. Obosie bwabekwa egetonga, enyama yaiyekwa, ne ekeundi giatongwa ase obosie erinde omwana aasimorigwe. Goika ng'ina omosubati aiche Ngina omosubati nigo are gocha ase enka yo mosubati oye, kare no obosi ase egetonga, otorera obosi obo mwa korera yaye! Ase ki? Ase Ekegusii, moibori tarenge korara ase enyomba ya mwana oye. Komenta nayio, chikorera usually nigo chianchaine sana. Mwa korera nao nonya ne ekenyenga kiare kobekwa bana gosiberia ngora ngora. This is one of the reasons why chikorera chiarenge important. Gokongia oboiri. Tari igo rioka. Naboigo mama omwabo omosubati nkobogoria are amaru ne enyama. Omomura oyo omonywomerete otaori obosie bwe egechuri ogacha mwaye. Omanya kobutora obokima bwa igoro mwaye. korwa aa bono nigo bare gotwara omoyega omuya ase ngina omosubati are koa omochokoro oyo erieta ria bonginarome. Omwana nigo arenge koegwa erieta ri' sobo, amo n' ri' bong'inarome [ bomame ] Goika kera omwana aegewe erieta ria bongina rome. Omwana nigo arenge koegwa amarieta abere: eria aiga sobo na korwa sobo ngina. Nabo Ekegusii kiare igo. Ekero omoyega oerire egetonga nkianya koirana bosa! Yaya. Nigo bare kobeka chibando gose obori baa ngina omosubati oyo ore korera yo omochie oyo. Eke nakio ekegeni kio omwana omomura gose omoiseke. Karibuni mosamba mwaye.
english: Good Afternoon Friends: With PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. March 30, 2011. These are the things: Mosamba Mwaye Mosamba Mwaye. "One does not herd cattle alone. A person also needs someone to share with and walk together." A child who is born during Mosamba Mwaye should be given a name. Now what reason is there for giving this child a good name? They say, he will inherit his father's wealth, he will be blessed. Work hard they say, and you will never lack food from the field. That is why they work together on the field. That is it. Finished. This story has been passed down through generations during Mosamba Mwaye. The Abagusii people celebrate this Mosamba Mwaye. And concerning marriage, they say "Those who marry during Mosamba Mwaye, their home will always be full of blessings." It is true. The meaning of Mosamba Mwaye: "Wealth increases" Mosamba Mwaye is finished, its time now to prepare for planting so that there is plenty of food. Traditionally, a child is washed and dressed well after being circumcised. The mother knows how to care for the child properly. She knows how to care for the child so that when she says, “Wealth increases.” She prays to God to bless the child. Everything is done carefully. Beer is brewed. Meat is cooked, and everything is prepared so that the child grows up healthy. Let us continue with our discussion tomorrow The mother continues to talk about her daughter, and then she prepares food, she teaches her how to cook! Why? Because in Ekegusii, it is important to respect a child's future. Comment on this, because traditionally it is very difficult. When cooking with them, don't forget to leave some for the children to eat little by little. This is one of the reasons why tradition is important. Understand this matter. There were times when it was forbidden. But today mothers and daughters share meat and drinks. That woman who refuses to give her daughter a portion of the food is considered bad. She shouldn't deny her child the benefits of her age. Work hard and you will find that those who have helped others will receive help from the children of those people. A child should not be sent away from their parents' home, either to their maternal grandparents [ their mothers ]. Continue telling the child about their grandparents' home. A child should not be sent away without a reason: whether it is a good day or working day with the family. But in Ekegusii, it is not like that. Everything that is prepared is shared equally! Yes. They should leave something for the mother of that child who helps with the work. And this story is about a child whose mother is very generous. Welcome to Mosamba Mwaye.

ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egetamo (March) 5, 2011. Konyora Omosongo atarareta echae Kericho, intwe Abagusii konyora twaikire aroro. Imomanyete inga Abasigisi na abaminto? Ingai erieta ria Kabianga riarwete? Esegi yo Osao Sao (diarrhea) rende? Ase e semesta ya rero, ingoitona tore omochakano bwe erieta Kabianga, Gamama amo ne Esegi yo Osao Sao buna yare. Buna ebisaku binde ebinge, Abagusii nigo twarenge konganya na korigia ase agiya ase obomenyo. Kabianga Ase okona konganya, Omogusii nigo aigete na komenya aaria an'ge na Kericho. Nigo twabebekaine na Abanyamato gose Abasigisi. Korende ebisaku ebi bibere mbiamenyete na morembe nonya ne entune eyemo. Nigo bare koiberana etugo, barwara botambe ne chingaki chie ebiro chikaba chimbe. Tari igo rioka. Ndagera ekaba terikwama. Ebinto bikaba biangire aiga ase bamenyete. Nario erio Omogusii atebete inga Kabianga rende, titokorwa aaiga......... Bakarwa abwo ase ensemo eyio Kabianga aiga na koyaroka erieta erio (Kabianga) na kogenda gochia Ikonge, Metamaywa na Keroka gochaka komenya korende. Ase okonganya korwa Kabianga, Omogusii agatamboka oroche rware korokwa Emogori rakini ase rero rero rokorokwa Isonto. Morembe tochia koba aiga. Abasigisi bakaba bagooncherera Omogusii. Aiga nao ebiranya bia abakoro biarigetigwe egere gokonya Omogusii korwa ase omobisa. Abagaka abakoro bagatebigwa inga goika babeke ebiranya ebi na koganya ababisa bache. Abasigisi bagachaka esegi korende Abagusii bakaemotia. Abasigisi bagatirimboka inse batagete goita Abagusii. Abagusii bakaeboia buna abanyamato. Bakamanya kobarongera chinsinyo chiosi na kobabeka gati. Osao Sao Gaki bagaita emeganda ya Abasigisi enamba etare kobareka abwo ase oroche rwe Emogori impaka rokaba amanyinga oka. Abagere baria bamenyete ase ensemo ya Sondu bagakumia na goteba buna esegi yasairi Abasigisi. Ekio nakio kiagerete esegi eye ekarokwa esegi yo Osao Sao. Tari igo rioka. Abasacha abange ba Bosigisi nigo baitetwe. Sigisi ekaba etabwati abasacha gekogera nigo baitetwe ekero gie esegi eyio yo Osao Sao na Abagusii. Renta Abamura Ebisore Korwa Gusii Na Gamama Abamura ebisora korwa Gusii bagachi Sigisi na kobiaria abakungu ba Bosigisi. Korwa ase engaki eye, nario bono Omosigisi achagete korangeria Omogusii okomoroka Gamama engencho yaye oyo obiareti mama. Impaka rero nabo Omosigisi akorangeria Omogusii inga Gamama. Ase boigo intobwate a town ekorokwa Kabianga. Nabo magokoro atebete igo impaka naende ase esemesta yende. Next In This Series: Abagusii Customs VII: Abageka (Enyomba Ya Ababani Ase Abagusii).
english: Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. March 5, 2011. When people from Kericho die, we, the Abagusii, mourn them greatly. Do you know the Basigisi and the Baminto? Has the Kabianga river burst its banks? Does diarrhea bother you? Yes, in those days, when the Kabianga river overflowed, Gamama and also diarrhea were severe. Because diseases spread quickly, the Abagusii used to gather and consult about how to deal with illnesses. Kabianga During this consultation, the Omogusii would meet and discuss things concerning Kericho. We interacted with both the Banyamato and the Basigisi. These diseases caused much suffering and hardship, especially with the accompanying pain. They said they should offer sacrifices, the sick should be treated with medicine and herbs. It was a difficult time. My grandmother used to say that things happened because people did not understand. The Omogusii thought that what happened in Kabianga was strange, it wasn't understood by anyone... Those who survived the disease in Kabianga went and settled in Ikonge, Metamaywa and Keroka to find relief and comfort. During the consultation regarding Kabianga, the Omogusii started a ritual involving Emogori rocks, which were repeatedly thrown towards Isonto. Hardship continued to persist. The Basigisi despised the Omogusii. They also had their own traditions that they guarded jealously against the Omogusii during times of trouble. The elders among them would prevent young men from sharing information with others. The Basigisi mocked these events while the Abagusii suffered. The Basigisi believed they could overpower the Abagusii. The Abagusii realized they needed to increase their strength and unity. Osao Sao Some people went to the land of the Basigisi hoping to find a way to stop the ritual of Emogori before it caused further harm. Others who knew the customs of Sondu gathered and agreed that the situation facing the Basigisi was dire. This matter became known as the event of Osao Sao. It was a difficult time. Many children of the Bosigisi were orphaned. The Basigisi, having lost their children, blamed the Osao Sao event on the Abagusii. Rent For Land From Gusii And Gamama People seeking land from Gusii approached the Basigisi and negotiated with the chiefs of Bosigisi. Regarding this issue, a man named Omosigisi volunteered to help the Omogusii settle in Gamama, offering his mother's land. Even then, Omosigisi helped the Omogusii settle in Gamama. Because of this, a town grew up near Kabianga. Their hearts were troubled, and this continued until today. Next In This Series: Abagusii Customs VII: Abageka (The Wealth Of The Abagusii Men).

ekegusii: Omoruoti bw'semi abwenererete gochora omorai orache magega yaye ekero akure. Omoruoti naareganeti ekeragerio ekenene mono na eng'ana nere atagete kobamanyia. Ase igo bakagende chinsanganio chiosi chiorosana. Ekero omotienyi omesete, Omoruoti Engo agacha na gotenena gatigati yabo. Ching'iti chiosi chigakira kiri na gotegerera omoruoti akuane. Kegoteba, "Karwoa nchira ng'ete. Ninche omonene bwenererete koba eruoti." Ritimo rikagwa inse kobara goika kane. Enchogu ekaigwa obororo egachaka gotinera amagoro inse. Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Nkwarenge neribaga riago." Aseigo Enchogu ekagenda. Ebeche egacha kegoteba, "Karwa nchera yane. Karwa nchera yane. Niche kochia koba omoruoti. ninche bwate ekeonwa ekenene. Ninche omokong'u. Nibwenererete koba omoruoti." Ritimo rikagwa inse goika kobara isanonemo. Ekaigwa obororo. Ekabea na koeruta ebuse embeo igoro. Engo ekamotebia, "Beche okoruta nigo kware rimo rioka. Ribaga riao riaerire." Ebeche ekagenda. Chinsa echio bakaigwa eriogi korwa magega yabo. Ekero barigereretie magega bagaichana keria baroche. Egana ekaira ritimo ekarisira gochia igoro. Ekang'usa okoboko gochia igoro, ekaminyoka gochia bosio, egacharoka igoro, ekaruta ritimo gochia rire igoro. "Rimo! Kabere! Gatato! Kane! Gatano! Gatanorimo! Gatanokabere! Obee!" Egana ekarera. Egana ekabea. Ekaigwa obororo ekang'ea goonchokanana, gekoemurukania na gotamereria amang'ana amange. Korende Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Yaya, nigo okonyora ribaga erimo rioka." Ase igo Egana ekagenda. Ekero ching'iti chinde chiaigwete amang'ana aye, chionsi chigachaka goseka. Ekaeyana, ekabuatoka ritimo egatuora, "Gatano omente gatano ni ikomi." Ritimo rikagwa inse. Omoruoti Engo atateba, "Eee, Engabi! Isano omente isano neenchera yogoika ikomi. Chichera nechinyinge chiokobara goika ikomi." Erwarenerero tiyarenge yokonyora eng'iti enene gose eyebuate chinguru kobua echinde. Erwano eyarenge yokonyora eng'iti eng'aini kobua chionsi. Naboigo Engabi yabete Enting'ana ekero Engo yakwete. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0 Source www.africanstorybook.org
english: The girl who speaks well can attract a husband and have many children. The girl does not reveal her beauty completely, only showing enough to make him desire her. Thus they spend their days in endless teasing. When a young man approaches, Omoruoti Engo hides and carefully observes him. Every day she finds a way to protect herself from the boy. She says, “Marry me quickly. I am beautiful and worthy of being married.” Time passes and he tries to find a way to approach her. The herd of cattle grazes peacefully, unaware of his intentions. Omoruoti Engo reflects, “I will wait for the right time.” And so the herd moves on. The calf cries out, “Marry me now. Marry me now. Let me be close to the girl. I am strong and capable. I am worthy of the girl.” Time passes and he continues to try to approach her. The herd grazes peacefully. The ground trembles with the weight of countless hooves. Engo reflects, “Let the calf continue to chase until time reveals itself. The right time will come.” The calf moves on. This story tells of a boy approaching a herd of cattle. They guard themselves closely, separating those who seek to harm them. The dawn arrives, bringing with it a new rhythm to the land. The sun rises, illuminating the hills, the valleys, the plains, and the riverbanks. “Time! Friend! Enemy! Now! Five! Six! Seven! Eight!” Dawn proclaims. The dawn awakens. The herd scatters, running in different directions, shaking and trembling with fear. Then Omoruoti Engo reflects, “Yes, this is how time reveals itself.” And so dawn departs. Every small thing that falls upon the earth is covered in dust. Everything shakes and settles. The wind whispers a rhythm, saying, “Five times five is twenty-five.” Time passes. Omoruoti Engo says, “Yes, Engabi! Twenty times twenty is four hundred. This secret will reveal itself.” Tradition dictates that one should not reveal a large tree to someone who wants to cut it down. It also dictates that one should not reveal a small plant to anyone. But today, Engabi met Enting'ana, and Engo saw. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0 Source www.africanstorybook.org

Abagusii Customs XV: Amasabo Ye Ribina Omogaka sokoro ominto nantebetie buna Mwanyagetinge ominto omokoro naegenete ebinto gete, ebio ekero biakorekanire, egento gete nigo kegokorekana. Nabo kerabe ekiya gose ekebe. Ase rituko ria rero, tiga ingo toyakwanere amang'ana aria abakoro baito babegete okwegena ase are buna ekobwatia: 1. Ekiegesa: Ekero ekiegesa kiarenge koria omonto, nigo yarenge gotebekana ng'a aande aake omonto nare okare kogokwana. Na kogesiria, nigo kwarenge gotebigwa obare abana bamino ase omoyo ime, otari gokwana oigwekane !! 2. Gotamboka ebite bie ching'eni: Oise gotora ching'eni ebite erinde obitige inse omonto ache abitamboke, nigo ebianda bigokoria na ochake kominyoka ekero kwabekire ching'eni echi riiko, goikera gwachiyekire erinde gwachirire. 3. Naiguure bwatiokire: Oise kogenda mw' omwamate oo, omanye konyora buna okorire koragera naende n' ebinto bakoenia korwa emesa, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna aye nigo okare gokwana omoamate oyo oo bobe. Korende oise goika onyore nigo bagotereka endagera emesa baragere gose mbagasaine koragera, nigo egotebekana buna nigo ogokwana omwamate oyo buuya. 4. Oyo tata nakamura aranyore: Omosacha mokaye ebwateranetie n' egioto geise komocharoka okogoro, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omorugie oye nigo agocha koibora omwana omomura. Kai tata !! Egioto giacharokire amagoro y' omogaka Simba Ndemo aaria Kisii Town, Kisii County. Tokare goika n' magokoro baba ominto aaria Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015 5. Endoto embe: Oise korota omonto orwarete buna ogwenire na konora nigo egotebekana ng'a endoto eye n' embe na nigo oyo arakwe. 6. Omwana ngoseka are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise goseka, igo nigo yarenge kororekana buna nigo arota buna ise okuure. 7. Omwana nkorera are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise korera karaire, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna nigo arota buna ng'ina okuure. 8. Oyo tata nigo arabe oundu: Oise gotamboka omwana nigo egotebekana buna omwana oyo tagokina atambee gochia igoro. 9. Oyo n' omogworu: Ekero omonto akorota oyomwabo buna okure nigo egotebekana buna nigo aragerete obotuko obuo akaigota kerage. 10. Eye yabeire ekeriero: Etwani iese kobuga chinsa chiri etabwenereti kobuga buna botuko gati, igo mbobe. Nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omonto bw' eamate eye nache atwe ekamo. Etwani buna eye nigo yarenge konyenywa ase obwango na koba ekeriero. Koru ase omogaka sokoro ominto, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.
english: PETRONILLAH OGOTI: Proverbs, Culture and Customs Editor, Gusii.com: November [ Egesunte, Egesunte Gia Chache ] 27, 2015. These are the ones: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Is the wealth of a generous person diminished when he gives it away completely? Abagusii Culture And Customs XVI: Does a beautiful girl cause envy among those who aren't beautiful? Abagusii Customs XV: The Respect of Elders A father does not despise his children, even if they are troublesome; a mother doesn't reject her children, even if they make mistakes, she loves them just the same. But observe this important thing well. For sometimes, because of poverty, old people may fail to teach their children good manners: 1. Teaching: A lesson taught repeatedly to a child, will stick with him forever and he will never forget it. And remember, it is better to teach children while they are young, than to try to correct them when they are grown up!! 2. Avoiding bad company: It is good to choose good friends carefully so that a child doesn't associate with bad companions, because bad friends can lead to trouble and ruin a good reputation, making it difficult to restore it. 3. Being careful with advice: It is good to listen to wise counsel, and to be humble enough to accept correction and learn from others’ experiences, so that you don't think you know everything and become arrogant. Therefore, always listen and let them advise you properly, so that you won't regret it later when things go wrong. 4. A foolish elder should be respected: An elder who speaks carelessly and makes reckless decisions, should still be respected so that he doesn't mistreat a younger person. May God help us!! This story happened to the family of Mr. Simba Ndemo who lives in Kisii Town, Kisii County. Go and ask about it at Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015 5. Regarding dreams: If someone has a dream and interprets it correctly, then it is believed that the dream is true and will come to pass. 6. A child who cries a lot: A child who cries constantly, it is believed that he will grow up to be a thief. 7. A quiet child: A child who is very quiet, it is believed that he will grow up to be a liar. 8. That elder is stubborn: If someone takes a child to an elder, it is believed that the child will not improve unless he is disciplined. 9. And the maternal uncle: A child who goes to his maternal uncle seeking help, it is believed that he will find favor and receive assistance. 10. And the inheritance: Sometimes people fight over property and quarrel bitterly, leading to conflicts. It is believed that a person who steals another’s property will suffer consequences. Sometimes such a person will be cursed and lose his inheritance. Greetings to our fathers and mothers, goodbye everyone and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: (Ebicha: Africapoint.com) Tata inaki agaanchete obotugi abwo kare? Nonya bono naanchete emeremo eyio. Egento narorire egekong’u gotuga nechiombe. Ntwagatugire chiombe kare riri twamenyete aria Molo. Bono omwaka o 1992 Abatwomera igoro (ko abande bakobaroka Abasigisi) bagachaka esegi eyio ekabetereria tong’anye korwa aroro. Engaki esegi yaogete ning’iyorete abasacha bakoeinda nechinsara gochia korwania ababisa. Engaki eyio amaiso ane konyora tarang’ainia igo tinamaete ninki kiarenge kogenderera, tinamaete Omotwomera igoro ninki, gose Omomaanyi gose Omoikoyo. Ning’inyorete gingotara getii nakogenda ase chiombe chiakabekire esike, namanya koumora amache ime y’echingoro chiria chiremire n’amatimbo ime y’echabu eria. Bono egento nachete komanya neke; oise kobeka omorengari oo ase engoro y’eritimbo indigosoka, rikoirana ime. Korende oise gosuka ensemo iga ritimbo rikorora oborabu na gosoka. Amatimbo ayio arenge aria amanene amasomba-esike, aria abwate egento mosio bwe rigunchara ri’ekeobiria s’omotwe. Abamura baminto nabarabwo imbagatugire amaruma amo n’ebisusu. Korwa engaki eyio twatamete esegi aria Molo emiaka ang’e ekomi ne’ene egaeta abaibori bane bataratuga chiombe naende. Bono ng’ora ng’ora tata agachaka gotuga ebichuchu. Nabo abianchete ekerage nonya chingaki chinde obireta nyomba na kobisiekera nonya ebabu ime, biatioki enyomba nagotorentera chinda. Tata agatema gotuga ching’ondi chikamanya koibu (erabe na Abamaanyi) nakonyenyerwa ang’e na seito. Abaibi abwo bakaimoki enyama na gototigera amayio, eura n’amanyinga oka. Tata akamanya korangeri omogaka gete omonyamesira, omogaka okong’ire, naende korwa egesaku ki’Abakamba. Nkarora omonyamesira oyio gagosiba amariogo gete ase risakara na konyabisa ase akabaga gake gesieri abwo boeri. Timanyeti gose eriogo erio ndiabwatete abaibi abwo. Ng’ora ng’ora tata agachaka gotuga chiombe naende. Akagora chiombe isato. Ibere nyang’era eyemo nyabarati iga. Eng’ombe eyemo nyang’era ekamanya kobwatwa noborwaire gete. Egeka geke gekaera egasinyu koimoka, egachaka gosoki amasombogoku korwa monwa, na koruta chintacho rituko rigima. Mama akamanya goteba, “Oroche buna ekoruta chintacho na gosoki riuro? Nonya abanto nabo bagokwa iga.” Naende teireti egeka egetambe rituko erioerio egakwa. Abaamanyi bagacha bakanyeira gochia gotindeka. Rituko rikobwatia tata akagora chimbori. Mama agakona ko tatebeti tata kende. Eng’ombe eyemo neroo yatigarete. Tata agantomire inyesibe getii, omanya kong’inyori kera engaki, “osibe egekundo buya tegenda o bande tochake kogamba ebina igaa.” Eng’ombe eye neero nabo yaanchete kobasoka, yaaminchoria gochia are. Bono ko egotamboka epara chingaki chinyinge yamochia gotachu nechipigipigi n’echirori. Omweri oye egaacha ekagota nagosinyu gotenena yoka. Twakarangeiri abagaka gete batobwatesi twanyeimoki. Egaika engaki gete tata akarosa, akarangeri abanyenyi banyegore. Nkaigwa ng’a naichana ngatama tindora rikongo riaito rikoirwa konyenyu.
english: (Ebicha: Africapoint.com) Did Father truly investigate this matter well? Now he has also investigated this story. He intends to thoroughly examine the case concerning the inheritance of property. We will discuss the property well so that people from Molo understand. This year, 1992, the people who helped us (or those who opposed the Gusii) changed this story which was causing division and conflict. The story caused problems because it made people fight and quarrel over land. This story had eyes that could see far and understand everything, understanding the helpers' intentions, understanding the powerful and the wealthy. Because of this, I went to look at the property that was given to me, hoping to find peace; however, I found many disputes about boundaries and many conflicts about ownership. Now, I realized something; it is better to avoid unnecessary arguments regarding the land dispute, avoiding trouble. Continue, and perhaps we can resolve this land issue peacefully and without conflict. These boundaries are very clear and well-defined, they are known to everyone and anyone who wants to know them. The elders have spoken and explained everything clearly to the community. Regarding this story, we discussed the land in Molo for many years, and four witnesses testified about the property. Now, again, did Father investigate this matter carefully? Those who understood the situation said that this thing would bring problems and cause disagreements, leading to chaos and confusion. Father discovered a secret agreement (with the powerful) and was surprised by what he learned. Those thieves stole meat and spread rumors, causing unrest and anxiety. Father knows how to deal with someone who deceives, someone who steals, and also how to handle matters involving the Abakamba clan. I remember that deceiver who caused trouble and misled people, deceiving them and making them suffer. We all know that this problem affected those thieves. Again, Father investigated this property. He examined the cattle closely. There is a cow whose horn is broken. That cow with a broken horn knows how to be stubborn and refuses to be controlled. It keeps mooing loudly, attracting attention, and causes commotion everywhere, disrupting peace. Mother says, "Why does it make such noise and attract attention? Perhaps others will also come." And yet she doesn't realize how much damage that cow is causing. The powerful people came to try and solve the problem. That cow led Father to discover a treasure. Mother thought her husband wouldn't return. That cow with a black spot remained calm. Father remembered a proverb, saying, "A black spot indicates a journey, meaning someone will travel to another place to explain things." That cow also tried to run away, trying to escape. But because it had already started something bad, it continued to create more trouble and destruction. The leader of the home saw everything and understood the seriousness of the situation. We realized that those people were capable of causing harm and stealing from us. This story reminds me of my father, who always sought justice and helped his neighbors. I swear, I won't forget this lesson ever.

ekegusii: Na JOSHUA ARAKA. Gusii.com, Suneka, Kisii County. Ebwagi (June) 5, 2011 Aya amwabo aya: Kogenda 10 km na amagoro kera rituko! Stellah Nyayiemi nigo are koboka rimaaambia echuni na gotara 5km gochia esukuru. Na kera rimorogoba, oayerera mbaka mwabo. Igo kera rituko nigo are gotara 10km. Nonya nabo igo, Stellah, 18, nigo akorete omokia aase amasomo aye na magega ye emiaka ene, akanyora A- (minus) korwa aaria St Peter’s Suneka Secondary School, Kisii County. Moi University, we are coming. Our future chemical engineer. St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County star student, Stellah Nyayiemi. Picture na Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files. Na ekero yaigete rituko rie chisemi amo na okoegwa ebiegwa aase esukuru eyio, rituko nigo riaonchogete rikaba eria Stella. Omokwani gochia ase oyonde nigo bamotogia Stellah egekogera anene baria bakonyora egrade ekio nigo bagosoma chisukuru chinene ase bakomenya ime. Stellah ere nigo aremereretie embeo, etintira, embura na obokendu na konyora e grade ekio getari gotoka Gusii mono. Ase engencho ya omokia oye, esukuru nigo yamoete epigipigi ya Sh 50,000. Boigo nabo anyorete ebiegwa ebinge korwa aase abageni ao ao. Omongina mama omwabo agasira kare kerasi isano ne emo Stellah nigo agoteba buna ere nigo atagete gokora e degree in Chemical Engineering korwa aaria Moi University erio ache gokonya tata omwabo oyio omorendire korwa ekero mama omwabo asirete kare kerasi isano nemo. “Omonto nabo agoeta amatemwa korwa ande onsi. Nigo natagete konyora A plain korende nigo ingoakera Nyasae nga mbuya mono ase eki angete,” Nabo atebetie Gusii.com. Tari gotiga ise. "Thanks dad for all your support". Stellah amo na tata omwabo during the academic excellency awards day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County yesterday. Picture na Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files. She attributed her success to hard work, group discussions, advice from her mother who told her to work hard and the desire to make his father proud. Ise Stella, omogaka Nyayiemi, 69, nigo amosaberete amaya erinde asome erio ache gokonya enke yabo. Stellah nere ore omoke mwabo. The school’s former principal, Mr. Godfrey Omoni who got credited for molding Stellah nigo agoteba buna baria bakorwa inka kera emaambia nigo bagokora buya aase engencho bakonyora emechando. Omoni, now heading Nyamagwa High School nigo agoteba buna Gusii nabo ebwenerete gokora buya. "Kae chisemi ribaga", Dr. Margaret Obaga “This is a sign of good things to come,” Nabo omosike Omoni atebete. A don from Daystar University, Dr Margaret Obaga, oyio orenge omogeni omonene nigo atebetie abaorokigwa bae chisemi ribaga baratiga emegoko emenge ya ense eye. Another don, Dr Samuel Ongoncho nigo atebete buna Stellah obeire omogwekano omuya ase abaana bande. “We will get more Stellahs korwa ase esukuru eye. Nyasae tiga asesenie omwana oyo,” Nabo Dr Ongoncho atebete. Attentive students. The 2011 Academic Excellency Awards Day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County.
english: To JOSHUA ARAKA. Gusii.com, Suneka, Kisii County. June 5, 2011 These are the news: Walking 10 km with burdens is tough! Stellah Nyayiemi also walks five kilometers to school daily. And when it rains, she struggles until she gets home. That journey is ten kilometers. Despite this, Stellah, 18, has excelled in her studies for four years, scoring an A- (minus) while at St Peter’s Suneka Secondary School, Kisii County. Moi University, we are coming. Our future chemical engineer. St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County star student, Stellah Nyayiemi. Picture with Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files. And because of the difficulty of that long journey to and from school, that journey became known as Stella's. People visiting her often praise Stellah for her great efforts in getting good grades so they can continue their education and succeed. Stellah also faces challenges, including hunger, thirst, and poverty, yet she manages to get good grades despite being from Gusii. Because of the cost of education, the school requires a fee of Sh 50,000. Her parents have struggled to pay those fees due to their limited resources. Her mother, who supports her family, sacrificed greatly for them. Stellah says she hopes to pursue a degree in Chemical Engineering at Moi University so she can help her father and support her mother who has sacrificed so much for them. "I thank God for everything. I wish I had scored an A plain so I could please God more," she told Gusii.com. Thank you Dad for all your support. Stellah and her father during the academic excellence awards day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County yesterday. Picture with Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files. She attributed her success to hard work, group discussions, advice from her mother who told her to work hard and the desire to make her father proud. Her mother, Stella Nyayiemi, 69, has struggled to provide for her children so they can achieve their goals. Stellah is her only daughter. The school’s former principal, Mr. Godfrey Omoni who was praised for nurturing Stellah, said that if students work hard in their studies, they will achieve excellent results. Omoni, now heading Nyamagwa High School, said that Gusii people should strive for excellence. "This is a good omen," Dr. Margaret Obaga “This is a sign of good things to come,” Omoni added. A lecturer from Daystar University, Dr Margaret Obaga, a prominent guest, congratulated the students saying this good omen indicates positive developments in the region. Another lecturer, Dr Samuel Ongoncho said that Stellah is a role model for other students. “We will get more Stellahs from this school. God bless that child,” Dr Ongoncho added. Attentive students. The 2011 Academic Excellency Awards Day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County.

Bradshaw Funeral Home, White Bear, Minnesota, USA. Egesunte (November) 6, 2010. And they cared. And they came in large numbers. Speeches igoro ya Bilha, Kinley na Ivyn Tari igo rioka. Omokwani ase kera omokwani nigo aimoka gokwana igoro ya marehemu. Nigo abange benyora bakorera nonstop. Amariga oka. Korwa chinkwana igoro ya marehemu. Amariga nigo arenge amange Ase engaki yane yonsi yo oborisia, naborigwe gokwana ase emeyega emenge ye ebirero rakini tinanya korora abanto abange crying all through. Korwa omochakano impaka omoerio bwe e service. Omogano bwo ogoitwa gwa Bilha na abana baye nigo ore omokongu ekiagera onde taiyo obwate an explanation. Koa abagisangio babo, Ivyn na Kinley okwaheri. Abana barenge ase ebirero. Kera oyomo orenge ase ebirero ebi nigo arera na goteba inga : "They left too soon." Bono nabo twatongetwe igo. Kwaheri. Timoka no omorembe. Ase obwango, Omonene Nyasae nere bweka oratotebie igoro ya amangana amakongu buna aya. Impaka engaki eyio, tiga mosesenigwe. Pr. Birai. Former schoolmates, workmates, relatives and friends who had come to comfort them all gathered at Bradshaw Funeral Home, White Bear, Minnesota to remember Bilha Omare and her children, Kinley Ogendi and Ivyn Ogendi during their farewell. Those who knew them well remembered how kind they were. The singers sang non-stop. It was beautiful. The service continued honoring the deceased. The singing was excellent For all the efforts made in comforting, may they be rewarded for the tears shed throughout. The service was very touching from beginning to end. The pain of losing Bilha and her children is immense and difficult to explain. Questions like “Why?” will never be answered except by our Father God. That is the truth. 4th tribute: City Of Vadnais Heights Mayor Sue Banovetz. "We have no words to thank the Mayor of Vadnais City and her community. She made it possible for the three bodies to be flown by Delta Airlines to New Jersey, free of charge, raised funds ($25,911.00), which covered the mortuary and coffin costs. And she went further to secure the venue, free of charge. We cannot forget mentioning her ability to mobilize the local community to attend the funeral service in large numbers. And yet she is determined to help start a fund for the surviving child, Savannah.” Mr. James Kinara, Vice Chairman, Mwanyagetinge. Indeed the service was very well attended and many were touched. ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Korwa ase The Standard Mwanyagetinge ominto, twatebiigwe amangana amakong'u. University Lecturer, naende Omoraria bw' TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani osirire. Professor Nyasani nigo asirete igoro emaambia aaria ase enyagitari ya Agha Khan, Nairobi abwo ase konyora agendererete kobwenigwa koru etariki eyemo Engatiato [ January ] omwaka oyo. Nigo twatebigwa buna Prof Nyasani nigo airetwe ase enyagitari eyio ekero achagete korwara ase enkoro amo n' riini. Professor Nyasani nigo aiboretwe ase omwaka o 1936 aaria ime ya Central Kitutu Chache. Ritangani, Prof Nyasani niogo atagete gosomera obosasiroti, korende agachaka gomsomera Philosophy. Goetera ase ogosoma kwaye, Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo arenge Omokenya ori orenge komenta abande omoyo ase ogokongia ase amosomo amo n' esukuru. Omokenya Ominto Bw' Engencho: Omomura omwoge kerage, nigo arigete ebitabu goetania 41 !! Professor Joseph Nyasani [ 1936-2016 ]. Professor Nyasani nigo achiete nguma ase okorika a dissertation yaye ya PhD ase omomwa o Latin ase omwaka o 1963 na kobuna e record emiaka 300. Buna aserete igoro iga, Professor Joseph Nyasani konyora orikire ebitabu goetania 41 bia metaphysics, logic, cosmology amo na legal Philosophy. Gati y' ebitabu ebio 41 ariikire, ebinde nigo bire: [I]. Philosophy of Development [II]. Life and Death in Africa {III]. Philosophy of Nature {IV]. Philosophical Focus on Thought Systems in Development [V]. Legal philosophy [VI]. British Massacre of Gusii Freedom Defenders amo na [VII]. Metaphysics of the Cosmos and Related Recurrent Issues of Metaphysics. Professor nigo asomete aaria Cambridge Secondary Education aaria kakamega County. Koru abwo, akagenda aaria Rome Italy abwo ase asomerete Latin, literature, English amo na history. Professor Nyasani nigo abwate Arts degree koru ase Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), Diploma in Social Ethics koru ase Woodstock College, Oxford ase omwaka o 1964, PhD koru ase The University of Cologne, Germany, ase omwaka o 1969, amo na Law Degree, New York University, School of Law ase omwaka o 1972. Ase ogokora emeremo, Professor Nyasani nigo akorete emeremo ase the United Nations Secretariat aaria New York buna the Political Affairs Officer ase the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs ase omwaka o 1971. Koru abwo, Professor Nyasani akaba the Associate Professor aaria ase the City University of New York ase omwaka o 1973. Komenta na koba Omwoorokia, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omoraria ase the Voice of Germany (Deutche Welle) aaria Cologne, Germany amo na Voice of Kenya eyio bono eye KBC. Ase boigo, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omwoorokia ase The University of Nairobi koru ase omwaka o 1970 goikera bono. Ase emeremo emenge akorete, Professor Nyasani boigo nere orenge the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University koru ase omwaka o 2008 to 2013. Gati y' ebieegwa b' ogosoma kw igo Professor Ntyasani aetwe nigo bire the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship amo na DAAD Foundation Scholarship gati y' omwaka o 1987 and 1992. Igwa bono koru ase KTN, Nairobi Gusii.com nigo tokoru engora gochia ase abamwabo, abasani, abairi amo n' abaamate ba omwana bw' Abakenya, Professor Joseph Nyasani. Kera egento ase Omonene Tata Nyasae.
english: These are the announcements: Death notice from The Standard Our esteemed people, we have been informed of sad news. University Lecturer, and presenter on Omoraria TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani has passed away. Professor Nyasani died yesterday morning at the Aga Khan Hospital, Nairobi while undergoing treatment starting on a date corresponding to January of this year. We were informed that Prof Nyasani was admitted to that hospital some time ago due to illness. Professor Nyasani was born in 1936 in the location of Central Kitutu Chache. Later, Prof Nyasani went to study theology, then changed to study Philosophy. After completing his studies, Professor Joseph Nyasani became a Kenyan who tirelessly commented on issues of life and education in schools. Kenyan People Through the Editorial Board: This respected elder, has left behind 41 books!! Professor Joseph Nyasani [1936-2016]. Professor Nyasani successfully defended his PhD dissertation in Latin in 1963, setting a record of 300 years. In addition to those achievements, Professor Joseph Nyasani wrote over 41 books on metaphysics, logic, cosmology and legal Philosophy. Of these 41 books, some include: [I]. Philosophy of Development [II]. Life and Death in Africa {III]. Philosophy of Nature {IV]. Philosophical Focus on Thought Systems in Development [V]. Legal philosophy [VI]. British Massacre of Gusii Freedom Defenders and [VII]. Metaphysics of the Cosmos and Related Recurrent Issues of Metaphysics. The professor studied at Cambridge Secondary Education in Kakamega County. From there, he went to Rome Italy where he studied Latin, literature, English and history. Professor Nyasani obtained an Arts degree from Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), a Diploma in Social Ethics from Woodstock College, Oxford in 1964, a PhD from The University of Cologne, Germany in 1969, and a Law Degree, New York University, School of Law in 1972. In his career, Professor Nyasani worked at the United Nations Secretariat in New York as the Political Affairs Officer in the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs in 1971. Afterwards, Professor Nyasani became the Associate Professor at the City University of New York in 1973. As a commentator and analyst, Professor Nyasani was a presenter at the Voice of Germany (Deutsche Welle) in Cologne, Germany and the Voice of Kenya which is now KBC. Additionally, Professor Nyasani was a lecturer at The University of Nairobi from 1970 onwards. In terms of positions held, Professor Nyasani was also the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University from 2008 to 2013. Among the awards received during his studies, Professor Nyasani received the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship and DAAD Foundation Scholarship in 1987 and 1992. Live broadcast on KTN, Nairobi Gusii.com sends condolences to relatives, friends, colleagues and family members of the son of Kenyans, Professor Joseph Nyasani. ekegusii: Riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) rimanyire buna Kasturi srire rotunda rie chitripiki ang’e chimita 10–30 ase obotambe erigotoka ase asinine ase akorokwa Banjarmasin ase Borneo ya maate (Indonesia). Amatuko aya riasire gosira ekiagera rikonachwa mono. Korende, nabo rikonya gosimekwa aiga asengencho y’amatunda aye agwansa. Okoren’gana kwe riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) nkori konene mono ekero okoreng’ania n’amatunda ande ye chimbego chia amaembe. Oborito bwaye ebore ang’e chigiramu 50 goika 84. Ekero ritaratoba, nigo rire machani – ekero riatobire – erangi yaye ere maraba gose gochia bure-emwamu naende ribwate risabo rikomesa. Gocherera erangi ya buru. Ogoonchoreria chirangi oko nakwo gokomanyia igoro y’amatunda a M. Casturi. Chikabira isato chia Mangifera casturi- Kasturi,Mangga Cuban na Pelipisan. Erimanyire mono Kasturi eseng’encho ye rimisu riaye. Mangga Cuban na Pelipisan nigo akororwa buna chimbego ching’ao. Pelipisan nigo ribwate rimisu rigiya buna Kasturi eyio ekoorokia buna erirwete korwa Kasturi. Oborigia obonge mbogendererete korimanya mono. Ime ye ritunda eri nigo rikomachia koarira ase erangi naende rikwara akeigo ne rimisu riansu. Etokobwekani Kasturi me riembe(Mangifera indica),kasturi ndiri gwansa mono rakini ndibwate obwansu obokong’u ne rimisu rikeigo. Ime ye rotunda ria Kasturi eribwate emerande emenge emiya. Kasturi erianchire mono ase abanto ba Borneo ya maate am one chiamate chiabo. Rimisu riaye erikogokia goika ogotera ogokoro gokarosigwa igoro yaye “Seharum kasturi, seindah pelangi, semuanya bermula.” komineti “O, rimisu rigiya buna Kasturi, rigiya mono buna omokobi nyongo. Obwanchani obo bwachakire esabari.” Okonacha kw’emete gotaancheri kwagerire omote oyo ngosira okare korwa orosana. Emete emekoro y’amaembe a Kalimantan igo arasire korwa okonacha gotaancheri ekiagere emete yabo ekorwa emenge naende emiya. Emete eye egosimekwa ase ake ake ase emechi ya abanto nyuma y’ebiticha biabo gose emegondo yabo emeke. Riembe ria Kalimantan ndiri gosimekwa ase emegondo emenene gose ase obonge ime ya Indonesia buna amatunda ande agosimekwa ase chitropiki ekiagera akwama ng’ora. Emegondo emenene ya Kalimantani nigo ekoratoka ase ensemo enke ya Banjar (ensemo enke ya Banjar teri eyemo buna ensemo enke ya Banjarmasin). Abanto ba Mataraman mbatemete gosimeka ase emegondo emeke ase omwaka o 1980 korende rigesa ritang’ani eriarenge omwaka o 2005. Nonye rotunda eri rigotoka ase oboraisi, teri goisaneki banto ekiagere rianchire mono. Amatumisi y’amatunda n’omote nigo are amake. Nonye emete emekoro kegotwara ritina rietaneti emita eyemo, abanto ba Banjar (egesaku ki’abanto baime na ab’enyancha batorete Borneo ya maate) ebagotumia amatunda oka akiagera omote oye okwama egeka. Eseigo, abanto ba Banjar nigo bagotumia emete emeng’ao gokora ebinto binde. Konyora amatunda nkori raisi ekiagere omote o Kasturi nigo okwama oba omotambe mono naende goika omonto arine ase anene mono konyoikera – amatunda akogwa inse tari amaya mono. Amatunda aya nabo akoriegwa amatobu gose arosiri buna echamu. Tari koonigwa mono ase chichiro ekiagera abaremi abanyene nigo bakonyaria ataraika chichiro. Ebinto binde bikorosigwa korwa ase amaembe nigo are chipurii,chichamu, echuisi, gose obosuguti (ebisuguti bi’abakoro). Ebinto ebi korende ebire ebikong’u gotoka ekiagera amatunda aya akoriegwa mono naende anchire mono n’abanto ba Banjar. Amatunda aya naende are rigori rinene korende ase abanto ba Banjar, mbari gpkumia ekiagera y’obwansu obonene.
english: The fruit of Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) is commonly known as Kasturi, a round fruit that belongs to the cashew family and grows around 10–30 years old, found in areas like Banjaramasin and Borneo Island (Indonesia). Its wood is used for making various tools and furniture. Currently, this tree is cultivated because its fruits are delicious. Kalimantan mango (Mangifera casturi) trees are large and produce fruits similar to ordinary mangoes. The height can reach 50 to 84 meters. It flowers twice a year – flowering – which yields fruit approximately six months later, resulting in abundant harvests. The skin color is yellowish. To improve the quality of the fruit of M. Casturi, grafting techniques are employed. Several varieties of Mangifera casturi - Kasturi, Cuban Mango and Pelipisan - are recognized. Kasturi is widely cultivated for its sweet taste. Cuban Mango and Pelipisan are also known as superior varieties. Pelipisan is considered a good type of mango similar to Kasturi, which is often sold as Kasturi mango. This origin has been extensively researched. The flesh of the fruit is yellow and slightly sour, with a unique aroma and flavor. Kasturi is related to mango (Mangifera indica), but it differs significantly in terms of shape and texture. The roundness of the Kasturi fruit resembles an emerald green color. Kasturi is loved by the people of Borneo Island who give it a special name. Its fragrance is said to be reminiscent of the following phrase: "As fragrant as Kasturi, as beautiful as a rainbow, everything begins." They comment, "Oh, the good mango of Kasturi, truly a delightful mango. The sweetness is unparalleled." In conclusion, further research is needed to understand the potential benefits of this fruit. Research on Kalimantan mangoes shows promise for future studies regarding their nutritional value and economic impact. This research is being conducted by researchers and communities after previous efforts were unsuccessful. Kalimantan mangoes are widely grown throughout Indonesia, especially in tropical regions where they thrive. The vast lands of Kalimantan are suitable for growing these mangoes due to the fertile soil and favorable climate (the fertile soil of Kalimantan is also known as the soil of Banjaramasin). People from Mataraman began cultivating them in the 1980s, and production increased significantly around 2005. However, this round fruit is still relatively unknown to many people. The quality of the fruit depends on its origin. Moreover, the people of Banjar (who are often referred to as the inhabitants of Borneo Island) utilize the mangoes to create various products for sale. Therefore, the people of Banjar use these mangoes to make diverse items. Remember that mango trees provide shade which makes the area cool and comfortable - mangoes fall without causing harm. These mangoes are also processed into various snacks and preserved foods. It's said that those who taste the deliciousness of these mangoes will always remember them fondly. Various products are made from mangoes such as chips, preserves, sweets, and pickles (pickles made by elders). These products and others are derived from these mangoes and are enjoyed by the people of Banjar. These mangoes have great significance for the people of Banjar, contributing to their economy and prosperity.

Ase boigo, Governor Nyagarama nigo atebete buna chisukuru chinyinge tichiri gotwara amasomo, ase eng'encho emeyega ye ebirero ekobera ase chisukuru ase rituko erio. Ase enchera ende, baria baminto tokogenda ekanisa ase rituko rie Esabato, totware emeyega ye ebirero ase rituko ri Omokubio. Ase boigo, nabaria baminto tokogenda ekanisa ase rituko rio Omokubio, totware emeyega ye' ebirero ase rituko rie Esabato. Abana ba Gusii, nigo batagete gosoma, na gosomigwa buna abana bande bonsi, Kenya engima Governor Nyagarama nigo atebete aya, ase okwegena buna Abagusii toise gokora igo, abana baito nabo baragenderere gosomigwa ase amatuko atano ase ewiki. Ase boigo, abarimu nabarabwo nenyarekane, bakore emeremo yabo ase amatuko atano, ekiagera nigo bagoakanwa eng'eria y' amatuko atano ase ewiki. Abarai abange bakwaneire igoro yo obokongu tobwate Gusii, naende buna totari gokora amatemwa buya. Ase boigo, nabo ekororekana buna ekero abana baito bachire ase chisukuru chire isiko ya Gusii, nigo bagokora buya mono ase chisemi. Tiga abarimu, abaibori, amo na abarai baito bonsi barigererie enkwana eye, na koyegayana. Mbuya mono.
