ekegusii: Onye gokagete buna oyo no omogano igoro buna seito tware konywa erongongori etainekiri, kana koganya. Gose onye gokagete ngogotebia nde buna seito tware gokama chingoko, kana gokenderera agwo ekiiriri kio omotembe. Tindi gwatora bobisi buna seito tware gokama chingoko ekero oboremo bwabete chincherere totabwate ase nonya n’ embori okoriisia. Oyo no omogano bw' omogaka oyomo obwate chisemi, korende ekero twarenge abana nigo tware komosekerera. Omogaka oyio nigo are korokwa Mogaka. Magoroba iga ko omobaso okendire nigo agaterekire ebusaa yo obori na abasani baye. (Tari eye ye chibando rero nonya na abaisia abasiniini bakonywa). Kobasiibire ekegara ne chinkore bakonakoererania buna abana ba ng’ina omo, nigo bagaterire emeino emiya. Oyo nanchente ginkonakobategerera nigo orenge korokwa “Mosaiga.” Gaki tiga mbatebie buna Abamerika nigo banchete chisese ne ebimoni mono. Okonyora ekemoni keroseirie nyomba kemenyete buya, nonya mbeba nchiyo kebwenerete goita. Endagera nigo gekogorerwa enga ebisuguti kiabekerwa na amabere. Nonya nase gekobeka echabu go kiabutiarire nigo kebwate abanyene bana goitora. Ne esese nero nigo yanchire mono. Emenyete nyomba, egoikaransa esoba seti igoro yarigereria etelebiseni na abanyene. Esese ya Amerika oise konyereta seito Kenya nigo erakwe bwango mono. Nyama mbese sese ya Amerika terikoria. Tenga buna Ondieki yaito yakaminyokirie egesusu gose egechure yabwata twaria, twanyea amauga. Buna ekemoni kia Amerika, esese ya Amerika nigo ekoroserigwa endagera special ekogorwa korwa etuka. Tiga bono naende, Omogusii ominto, ngotebie egento kende kiamaseko. Abamerika naende nkoratwara bare amasindano korora buna ning’o obwate esese gose ekemoni egeseera. Amasindano ayio ataraika nigo bakoira chisese ne ebimoni baakana chibesa biasibigwa na konintwa chinchara. Omobui bwa amasindano nigo akoegwa egekombe buna keria abagosoria bakoeegwa. Maene pi ndie esese, tindigokong’aina, Nyaituga o baba. Boria onde bwensi omenyete mache ng’umbu. Chisese ne ebimoni kobiarwarire Abamerika tibari gotiga bikwe. Nigo bakobiira chinyagetari chi ebimoni ne chisese. Nimanyete Omoamerika oyomo oakanete $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) kobaara esese endwaire. Esese koyangire kobwena nigo bagokora egento gekorokwa, “Putting it to sleep” – bakonyebeta esindani yakwa ng’ooora. Koyakuure, banyeira ase akorokwa, Pet Cemetery, ase chimbeera chie chisese, ebimoni, ne ching’iti chinde Abamerika batugete nyomba chigotindekwa. Kobanyetindekire nigo bachachana na gwechwanachania buna omoibori okwereirwe no omwana. Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba. --omoerio-- Edwin Okongo nigo are Omoriki Omogeni ase Gusii.com. Ka moranche, motarere ase ewebusaiti yaye aaria ase Ourmaninamerica.com Edwin Okongo nere omoriki omonene bwe e bulogi ya Mshale naende omoriki bwe e bulogi yaye omonyene ya Okongo's Policy. Nigo asomete California State University aaria Hayward amo na University ya California aaria Berkeley. Nigo are oyomo bwa Abagusii bari barikire amangana amaya naende amange sana igoro ya Gusii na Kenya. Ka moranche, soma amariko aye ase chibulogi echio nabatebirie igoro. Imbuya mono Okongo ase e vidio amo na egasi engiya.
english: Whoever investigates this matter and finds out that someone has been stealing things, let them report it quickly. Also, whoever investigates and discovers someone causing trouble, let them reveal those who are involved in wrongdoing. Anyone who confesses will be forgiven if they admit their mistakes and seek reconciliation with others. This matter concerns a thief who steals valuable items, so let us work together to find him and bring him to justice. That thief is known as Mogaka. Many evenings he spends time wandering around, visiting homes and interacting with people. (This story is true, witnessed by many reliable individuals.) Let us unite and cooperate so that children can grow up well and become responsible citizens. This person, who is difficult to understand, is often referred to as "Mosaiga." It happened a long time ago when Americans discovered secrets and mysteries. To write a mystery novel requires skill and creativity, especially when dealing with complex characters. However, sometimes the truth is hidden within simple details and can only be revealed through careful observation. And even though it may seem impossible, anyone can achieve success if they persevere and dedicate themselves to their goals. And indeed, that is what happened. The story unfolded gradually. A television program featured interviews with various people. The American story was presented as being similar to the Kenyan situation, but it was ultimately different. The American meat industry is very competitive. Remember how Ondieki once struggled financially but eventually prospered, overcoming numerous obstacles. Regarding the American novel, the American story is considered a unique and exceptional piece of literature. We have heard enough, fellow Gusii people, let us focus on important matters. Americans and their allies continue to engage in conflicts and wars, seeking dominance over everything, including stories and novels. These conflicts often lead to discoveries of secrets and mysteries, which are then exploited for personal gain. The consequences of these conflicts are devastating, leaving behind destruction and suffering. However, despite these challenges, there is still hope. Remember our ancestors, Nyaituga and his father. They valued honesty and integrity above all else. Secrets and mysteries cause problems for Americans; they don't know where to begin. They search for clues in both mysteries and secrets. It is said that an American citizen spent $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) to bury a secret deeply. The secret continued to spread, leading them to give it a name, "Putting it to sleep" - they buried the evidence. Later, another person was also buried, Pet Cemetery, a place filled with secrets, mysteries, and the remains of Americans who had passed away. Burying something allows people to forget and move on, but it doesn't erase the past. The secret itself, the novel itself. --the end-- Edwin Okongo is a researcher and writer from Gusii.com. For more information, visit his website at Ourmaninamerica.com Edwin Okongo is also a prominent blogger at Mshale and maintains his own blog called Okongo's Policy. He studied at California State University in Hayward and the University of California in Berkeley. He is a voice for the Gusii people living abroad, advocating for their interests and promoting the culture of Gusii and Kenya. For more information, read his articles on his blog and watch his videos and documentaries.

ekegusii: Oral Sources On The Ground: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Rigwata (April) 13, 2012. Omogano Bw' Abanyaribari Aya amwabo aya: Baminto, totaragenda aare, nigo twatebetigwe buna ase abana b' Omogusii, tiga toinyore egento ekemo ekenene mono. Egento ekio nkeri nga ise Abagetutu amo na Abanyaribari n' oyomo! Bono omogaka oyio nere ng'o? Oyio nere omogaka Onyangore. Omonyaribari nere obagete Omogusii bwensi ase abeta. Ase Boigo, abagambi korwa Nyaribari nabwo babarete Abagusii bonsi ase omobaro bw' ritangani. Below: Goaka chitiero aaria Kiogoro, Nyaribari Chache. Onyangore nere ise Omogetutu amo n' Omonyaribari. Aase okoinyora naende, Omogetutu nigo aiboretwe korwa ase omosubati otabwate mwana momura. Omosubati oyo otarenge konyora bana nigo arigeti enyaroka akayenywoma. Ke enyaroka eye yanywomwa, ekaibora omwana oyio obisetu nyomba akarokwa Mogetutu gose Nyakundi. Igo Abagetutu amo na Abanyaribari nigo bare basinto b' omogaka Onyangore. Bono chinyomba chire Nyaribari nigo chire buna ekobwatia: Nyaribari Clans: 1.Nyakoni na Bomobea 2.Nyameyio na Monda 3.Gesicho, Moriango na Boto 4.Bogeka na Nyagatanyi. Obe! Bono naki ngokora n' enyaroka eye nyakieni nao erwete seito ase enyomba ya Kamba Nane? Abasubati aba bane bana babo mbanya konywomerana egekogera n' abamo. Aba nabwo bakorokwa Kamba nane. Kamba Nane na abana b' Omoraa Ochondwa Nyabana Bange Etari Gokwerwa, Etari Gochi Ime! Bono chinyomba chia Kamba Nane nechi: 1.Bomobea 2.Moriango 3.Onyakoni 4.Onyameyio 5.Monda 6.Boto 7.Bogeka 8.Gesicho Abako ba Kamba Nane mbareo. Eee bono. Gati ya abana ba Nyaribari bari bakonywomerana na abana baria barwete ase abangina ba Kamba Nane, nabwo aba: 1.Abasigisa 2.Abakimotwe 3.Abatondo 4.Ababura 5.Abaguche. Abaminto echi echi nachio chinyomba chire Nyaribari. Korwa ase omongina magokoro Kwamboka Mireri, amo na abagaka chisokoro Samuel Omare Nyambisa amo n' Kenyanya Marube, mbuya mono and thank you for listening. english: Oral Sources On The Ground: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Rigwata (April) 13, 2012. The History Of The People Of Nyaribari These are their words: People, let us not forget our roots, so that we may be honored among the children of Omogusii, lest you forget your heritage which is very important. This heritage belongs to both Abagetutu and Abanyaribari and their descendants! Who is this elder then? He is Elder Onyangore. The people of Nyaribari are the owners of Omogusii land where they settled. From Boigo, the leaders of Nyaribari and those who came with them spread the Gusii nation throughout the surrounding areas. Below: A picture of a homestead in Kiogoro, Nyaribari Chache. Onyangore belongs to both Omogetutu and Abanyaribari. According to stories passed down, Omogetutu was given authority over the land because he had a child who was born prematurely. That child could not breastfeed until he reached an age where he could drink from a horn. Once he drank from the horn, he began to grow strong and became a leader of the entire Getutu clan of Nyakundi. Therefore, both Abagetutu and Abanyaribari are descendants of Elder Onyangore. What characteristic of Nyaribari is known everywhere: Nyaribari Clans: 1.Nyakoni and Bomobea 2.Nyameyio and Monda 3.Gesicho, Moriango and Boto 4.Bogeka and Nyagatanyi. Wow! Why does it seem like the story of this horn is related to the homestead of Kamba Nane? Those four children shared a drinking horn and mingled with others. They were also taken to Kamba Nane. Kamba Nane and the children of Omoraa Ochondwa Nyabana Bange Etari Gokwerwa, Etari Gochi Ime! What is the history of Kamba Nane: 1.Bomobea 2.Moriango 3.Onyakoni 4.Onyameyio 5.Monda 6.Boto 7.Bogeka 8.Gesicho These are the families of Kamba Nane. Yes indeed. Between the children of Nyaribari who mingled with these children, there were also: 1.Abasigisa 2.Abakimotwe 3.Abatondo 4.Ababura 5.Abaguche. These people have always had this characteristic of Nyaribari. From the wisdom of Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, and the elders Chisokoro Samuel Omare Nyambisa and Kenyanya Marube, that is all for now and thank you for listening. Engoko eria ekarosa gosona egatiga esindani eria igoro yekabati nakogenda riko koroseria abana baye endagera. Rakini chinyoni chiria chinde konyora chiarorire ekabaki keria gekoiruruka are. Chikaboria engoko echikonye n'esindani eria erinde chirosie chimbaba chiabo nachirochio. Nabwo abwo chinyoni chiria chikairuruka igoro ase rire. Ekero enyoni eria yomoiso yairanatie esindani eria yasabete, engoko eria tiyarengeoo, konyora yasokire ake. Igo ebichuchu biengoko eria bikaira esindani eria bigachaka gochiesa nero. Ekero biarosete nomochieso oria, bigatiga esindani eria ase amaraba ime. Emarogoba eyio, ekebaki gekairana. Gekaboria esindani eria erinde kenyare gosonerera amarionya konyora achakire korua ekero ki'orogendo rwaye. Engoko eria ekarigererIa ekabati igoro. Ekarigia chikoni, isiko keorori, gotatiga teyenyoreti sindani eria. "Gaki ing'a rituko erimo rioka inkorigerie esindani," Engoko ekaebereria ekebaki. Erinde onyare gosonerera amarionya ao nakonyara kaoiruruka korigia endagera yende. "Ero bono nakoire rituko erimo rioka, "ekebaki kegateba. "Inyore timokonyora sindani eyio, goika ong'akane n'egechuchu kiao ekemo." Ekero ekebaki giachete rituko rikobwatia, gekanyora engoko eria kegendererete gokura nse ase omochanga okoba sindani tiyarenge kororekana ande. Igo ekebaki kegaika nse bwango gekabogoria egechuch ekemo gekaira. Korwa abwo nonya mbono, ekebaki ekero kegoeta, nigo gekonyora engoko kegokura nse korigia esindani eria yasirete. Kera ekero omorengari bw'echimbaba chiekebaki ogoeta, nigo engoko ekoagama ebichuchu biaye. "Ama korwa ase aasioku na ase eroro." Nabirobio biaraneria: "Titori bariri. Tiga tominyoke." english: The Bird and the Snake Wiehan de Jager My father, the bird and the snake they often meet together with all kinds of birds. They always look for their own things. When it rains, the ground becomes slippery. The snake crawls very slowly on the ground. It moves carefully. “Come quickly so that we can both escape from this place,” said the snake. They were planning to steal eggs from another village, the bird was thinking about flying away. It feared being caught by the owner of the birds when they approached the coop. “Don’t let us be seen while approaching those eggs, otherwise we will be caught,” it said. It was then that the snake suddenly remembered an old story about a certain person who had been punished. It started to explain how people used to punish others in the past, and it reminded the bird of its own bad deeds. The person who had wronged someone had been forced to carry stones until he was exhausted, and the bird remembered his own mistakes. He regretted the snake’s actions and the harm caused to others. But the bird flew off anyway. When the other birds saw the beautiful bird flying towards the coop, the snake tried to stop him, but it was too late. It began to dig holes around the coop hoping to find some eggs. But it found nothing there. Those who seek evil things will find themselves digging holes everywhere, and they will not find what they are looking for. Those who plan evil things will find themselves facing difficulties. The snake felt ashamed and regretted his actions. It remembered the holes he had dug searching for eggs and realized he had wasted his time. The bird who had flown away was already far gone. “What kind of rain is this that makes it difficult to dig?” the snake complained to himself. He regretted having angered the owner of the birds and fearing being caught on the ground. “This is a good punishment for the rain,” said the snake. “Let us suffer because of this hole, maybe then you will remember your misdeeds.” Then the snake finished digging the hole and regretted having disturbed the bird and causing trouble. It also regretted having spoken badly. After that, he thought about something else, the snake was angry, and he regretted the bird escaping and crawling on the ground near the coop. He remembered his mother telling him, “Evil deeds have consequences and bring sorrow.” And everyone agreed: “That is true. ekegusii: Buna twakabeire na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi [June] 9, 2012. Ntwe ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete bagateba amangana aya na koyaereria korwa ekegori ekemo, gochia aase ekegori kende. Aya na amang'ana gete y' Abagusii, ayio eise koba buna kwayakorire, nigo arenge koba mamincha y' Ekegusii. Emegiro.Abagusii nigo babagete amang'ana ayio, emegiro aase eng'encho arenge koba mamincha y' oboseera bw' Omogusii. Tari igo rioka. Abagusii nigo beegenete buna oise koyakora, n' chimuuma. Nigo ebinto, gose chinkore gete chiimbe, chiare gocha koba, gose kogokorekanera. Aya amwabo aya: Abagusii Culture And Customs XXVII: Emegiro Y' Ekegusii [ I ] Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXIX: Emeyega Ao Ao Y' E Ekegusii Abagusii Culture And Customs LXXI: "Okwo N' Ogoturutumba Ekegusii" Omogaka Sokoro Ominto Aase amatuko amake aerire, ntwasomete igoro y' emegiro y' Ekegusii, etano n' ebere, aase Emegiro y' Ekegusii [ I ]. Ase okoinyora, nigo omongina magokoro baba ominto atebete buna kera egesaku aase ense eye nkiabwate emegiro. Ase boigo, nigo baba atebete buna kobwatekana n' abagaka n' abangina abakoro, gokora amang'ana ayio nigo yarenge koba mamincha y' Ekegusii. Ase rituko ria rero, magokoro nigo atagete kogenderera n' enkwana eyio. Kobwatekana na baba ominto, emegiro ende y' Ekegusii nigo ere buna iga: 8. Mosacha mogima bori: Aase Ekegusii, monto mosacha mogima tarenge gosoa irongo. Yaya. Nigo yare koba chimuuma, aise korina engasi kwagachia gose gosoa irongo riinde rionsi. Ase boigo, inyora buna chimuma chia Abagusii nigo chiare gocha n’ amaakwa amanene. Amasikani aase iso biara. Obori bori bogocha gosiegwa ,erinde sokoro aroiseririgwe erongori nao bore irongo. Sokoro tagosoa irongo ime. Yaya. Irongo n' ya magokoro. Kona gotakuna obori aange na iso biara nkwarengeo. Below: Ekee k' obokima bw' Omogusii. 9. Ebimwana ebike: Omwana omoke tarenge koegwa enyama y' riini erinde arie. Yaya. Gaise koegwa riini, aye rirorio nario okwerorera. Nigo akamwana buna akwo karenge koba agatamu, naende akamwenu ekianda gia ikomi! Omwana buna oyio, nkware komotoma gose komoboria akore kende. 10. Abasacha baria banchete kona gotirigoyia na kona goita abakungu babo bokaira: Ekero omosacha are goita omokungu oye bw’ enywomo, omokungu oyo nigo arenge gotama gochia irongo, gose nyaaro. Tari igo rioka Bosibori ominto. Omokungu oyo okona goitwa aaise koba buna okunire chimbere chiaye, omosacha oyo oye tarenge komoaka. Yaya. Eye nigo yarenge kobwekana buna ogosaba amabera. Omosacha oyo nyagotwanga mokaye arenge goaka omokungu oyo naende gakunire chimbere, echio n' chimuuma aase Ekegusii! Komenta nayio, omokungu oyo nyagotwangwa arenge kobwata omwana kwaa, ekero agoitwa, nigo are gotiga goitwa ekiagera okwo nakwo okwoorikia buna osabire okwabera. 11. Nyomenda nkobugia are omorori: Korwa bokoro ase Ekegusii, mokungu tarenge kobugia morori. Aaise gokora igo, omokungu oyo nigo arenge kogera omosacha oye aanse koema, na gokwa! 12. Moka momura ngotakuna are endagera: Moka momura tatakeire gotakuna obori aase ise biara are. Yaya nonya. Okwo nigo kwarenge ogosaria Ekegusii. Eng’encho ende, omokungu buna oyio, nigo arenge kong’ong’ori ise biara. Amasikani aera. Bobe mono. Omongina magokoro nao akorera abwo aase rero. Ntooche togenderere n' emegiro eende, chingaki chiinde. Korwa ase baba ominto, mbuya mono, and thank you for listening.
english: We greet Petronillah Ogoti well. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June 9, 2012. It is good to say that people who respect traditions and customs are honored, and they cherish their heritage greatly. These traditions belong to the Abagusii people, and it is important to remember that they strengthen the Ekegusii language. Traditions. The Abagusii people respect traditions very much, and these traditions help maintain the dignity of the Omogusii community. Time passes quickly. The Abagusii people have always been known for their hospitality and kindness. It is true that sometimes things happen unexpectedly, but they strive to overcome them. These are the topics: Abagusii Culture And Customs XXVII: The Traditions Of Ekegusii [ I ] Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXIX: The Ways Of Life Of Ekegusii Abagusii Culture And Customs LXXI: “The Land And The History Of Ekegusii” By Elder Sokoro Ominto Those who come from afar, let us examine the importance of the traditions of Ekegusii, both old and new, especially the Traditions of Ekegusii [ I ]. Also, let us understand that wise elders teach young people about the value of tradition. Also, they teach them to associate with elders and leaders, so that they can learn more about the Ekegusii culture. But sometimes, wise people may not want to share their knowledge. Associating with elders, and the traditions of Ekegusii, ensures that they remain alive: 8. A strong man does not fall: Among the Ekegusii, a strong man never forgets his roots. Indeed, it is said that strength comes from remembering one's origins. Also, know that the character of the Abagusii people is defined by their strong foundations. Generations pass, but the foundation remains. A strong root should not be uprooted, lest its branches wither. An elder should not forget his ancestors and his past. Below: Look at the history of the Omogusii. 9. Children are precious: A child should not be denied meat on a special occasion. Indeed, allowing a child to enjoy such occasions brings blessings. A child who behaves well deserves praise, and a younger sibling should respect an older sibling! A child who cries should be comforted so that they don't feel neglected. 10. Servants should not speak ill of their masters or reveal their secrets: A servant should not disclose the master's plans to others, because doing so would be disrespectful and harmful. Time passes quickly, my friends. That master should be respected so that he can protect his property, and the servant should not betray his trust. Indeed, it is important to avoid causing trouble. That servant who gossips will eventually face consequences, and will regret revealing the master's secrets – this is the way of the Ekegusii! Furthermore, that servant who is disloyal may be dismissed, and anyone who does wrong will be punished accordingly, so that they learn to behave. 11. A widow should not remarry too soon: It is customary among the Ekegusii for a widow to wait before remarrying. Respect this tradition, and the master will honor the woman who honors her late husband, and rejoice! 12. A good name is better than wealth: A good reputation is more valuable than possessions for generations to come. Indeed, it is what defines being an Ekegusii. Therefore, a master who acts like this will be remembered by future generations. Generations pass, and stories endure, leaving a lasting legacy. Respect our fathers and mothers, and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Goetania emiaka chirifu 4, chiaetire, Nyasae akamoorekera Abraham aaria Mesopotamia na komotebia, "Imoka orwe ense yao, na ase egesaku kiao, na ase enyomba ya’iso, ogende ase ense indakoorokie. Nainche ningokore egesaku ekenene." Abraham akamoigwera Omenene na kogenda ase ense ya Kaanani ase amenyete na momura’oye Isaka na mochokor’oye Yakobo, oyochete korokwa “Israeli.” Israeli na bamura baye 12 bagatirimboka gochia ense ya Misri ase’engencho enchara yachete ase ense ya Kaanani, naabwo bakamentekana na koba egesaku ekenene mono. AbaMisiri bagasogwa no’obwoba ase’enencho ye’egesaku eke ekenene kiamenyete amo na’barabwo, erio bakabakora abasomba na kobakoria chigasi chinkong’u. Nyuma ye’emiaka chimii inye ne’emerongo etato (430) ase ense ya Misri, Musa akabaraaa korwa ase obosomba, bagatamboka Enyancha Embariri na gosoa Bw’Arabu, ase Nyasae abaerete amachiko ase Egetunwa gia Sinai. Ekiare kia’Abaisraeli kiarwete Misiri na Musa tigiancheretwe gosoa Ense yo’Omwando ase’eng’encho getabwate okwegena ase Omonene. Gekaragaya ase eroro ase emiaka 40 goikera ekiare ekeyia kiabwate okweegena ase Omonene gegakina na gosoa ense yo’Omwando na Yoshua. Ase emiaka ang’e chimii inye (400), ebisaku 12 bia’Israeli bikagamberwa na’Abagambi buna Richiko ria Musa riare goteba. Ekero bagania koba no’Omoruoti buna ebisaku binde, Nyasae akabaa Sauro abe Omoruoti obo; nere akabagambera ase emiaka 40; akabwatiwa na Daudi, oyoogambete emiaka 40, nere akabwatigwa na momura oye Solomoni oyoogambete emiaka 40. Ekero gia Solomoni, nario Omoruotu bw’Abaisraeli arenge neesiko enene, na Ekaru entang’ani ekaagachwa; korende enkoro yo’omoruoti Solomoni ekamogechia Nyasae ase obogotu bwaye; Nyasae akamotebia buna; ebisaku 10 biaIsraeli tibikogamberwa na momura oye nainde. Ekero Solomoni akwa, oborwoti bwa Israeli bokabagekana, na ebisaku 10 bia’sugusu bikagamberwa na baruoti ababe, batarenge b’ororeri rwa Daudi na Solomoni. Oborwoti obo bwa’sugusu bokagenderera kweroka Israeli na gokora Samaria omochie oye omonene. Oborai oboke bwa’Irianyi bokaba nabwo Yuda, na Jerusalem Omochie oye omonene na kogamberwa no’ororeri rwa Daudi. Gochakera Abaruoti ya kabere 16, abanto boboruoti bwa Irianyi bakamanyekana buna “Abayaudi” ase’eng’encho yo’oboruoti bwa Yuda. Ase eng’encho ye’ebibe bia Israeli ya Mocha, bakarwanigwa na gokobugwa na gokorwa abasomba na Abaasuri. Abaisraeli bari batigarete bakasoanana na abanto bebisaku batamwegenete Omenene abachete komenya nabwo. Aba nabwo bachete korokwa Abasamaria, erio ebisaku 10 bia’ Mocha bigasira pi. Nyuma yaye, Oboruoti bwa’Irianyi bwa Yuda bokairwa obosomba ase ense ya Babiloni buna egesusuro giogosasima chinyae chinde, na Ekaru egasarigwa, koronde nyumba ye’emiaka 70, Abayaudi bakairana Yuda, bakaagacha Ekaru Jerusalem na kogenderera kogamberwa na abaruoti bo’ororeri rwa Daudi Ase engaki ya Yeso, egesaku kia Yuda ekiamanyekanete bua Judea na ekiagambeire na Abarumi. Yeso O’Kristo na abatomwa baye bakarandia Enchiri Judea bakorigia ching’ondi chinsiru chie’enyomba ya Israeli. Nyuma ye’emiaka 3 na enusu, abayaudi bakamokana Yeso buna Omoboria obo na komokora omogabana o’Rumi komobamba. Amatuko 3 keraeta, akaboka korwa ase abakurena kobaorokera abatomwa baye, ataratira gochia Igoro ase bono aikaransete ase okoboko okorio gwa Tata. Ekero egeke atarabambwa, yeso akabana ing’a Jerusalem nesambwe buna amaakwa yaokomokana, Ekaru nesarigwe, na Abayaudi mbasebererekane ase ense yonsi. Obobani obo bogaikerana ase omwaka bwe’70 A.D. ekero omoruoti bw’Abarumi Tito asoete Jerusalem. Ase emiaka 1800, Abayaudi bagasebererekana ase ense yonsi. Ase omwaka elfu eyemo, chimii kianda na emerengo ene ne’etano etato (1948), egetakageire gekaba. Ense ya’Israeli ekabekwa, erio naende abayaudi bakairana ase Ense yo’Omwando. Abakristo abange batebire ing’a oko nogwancha kwa Nyasae, korende, naboo gose echi nechinguru chio’Omosunte? Esinema eye nebwate richibu.
english: God commanded his angel 4, to appear, God remembered Abraham from Mesopotamia and told him, "Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father's house, and go to the land I will show you. I will make your descendants a great nation." Abraham obeyed the Lord and went to the land of Canaan where he lived and had a son named Isaac and begot Jacob, who was also called “Israel.” Israel and his twelve sons migrated to the land of Egypt because of famine, and they settled there in the land of Canaan, but they multiplied and became a great nation. The Egyptians were afraid of their numbers and mistreated them severely, so they enslaved them and made them work hard. After four hundred and thirty years in Egypt, Moses arose as a deliverer, leading the Israelites out of Egypt and across the Red Sea, and God brought them to the mountains of Sinai. The journey of the Israelites from Egypt with Moses led them across the Wilderness and through the land promised to them by the Lord. They wandered in the desert for forty years until the generation that did not obey the Lord died off, and Joshua led them across the Wilderness. After another four hundred years, the twelve tribes of Israel were judged by judges, starting with Deborah after the death of Moses. Later they asked for a king, and God chose Saul as their first king; he reigned for forty years; he was succeeded by David, who reigned for forty years, and he was succeeded by his son Solomon who reigned for forty years. During the reign of Solomon, the kingdom of Israel reached its greatest glory, and the Temple was built; therefore the king’s palace for Solomon pleased God greatly; God spoke to him saying; the ten tribes of Israel would not be ruled by his son. When Solomon died, the kingdom of Israel divided, and the ten northern tribes were ruled by rebellious leaders, who did not follow the example of David and Solomon. That rebellious leadership led to the downfall of Israel and the destruction of Samaria. But the tribe of Judah remained loyal, and Jerusalem remained the capital and was ruled by the line of David. From those sixteen kings, the people of the rebellious kingdom were known as “Jews” and the kingdom of Judah. During the time of the division of the kingdoms of Israel and Judah, they were attacked, conquered, and exiled by Assyrians. The Israelites had repeatedly turned away from the Lord and worshiped false gods. Those people were called Samaritans, and the ten tribes of the north disappeared completely. Later, the kingdom of Judah was taken captive to Babylon because of their continued sinfulness, and the Temple was destroyed, resulting in seventy years of exile. The Jews returned to Judah, rebuilt the Temple in Jerusalem, and continued to be ruled by the descendants of David. At the time of Jesus, the region of Judah was known as Judea and was under Roman rule. Jesus Christ and his disciples traveled throughout Judea preaching the good news of the Kingdom of God. After three and a half years, the Jews condemned Jesus as a blasphemer and handed him over to the Romans to be crucified. Three days later, he rose from the dead and appeared to his disciples, instructing them to preach the gospel to all nations. But before being arrested, Jesus predicted the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple, and the scattering of the Jews. This event happened in AD 70 when the Roman general Titus destroyed Jerusalem. For eighteen hundred years, the Jews have been scattered among all nations. In the twentieth century, in 1948, this prophecy came true. The nation of Israel was reestablished, and once again the Jews returned to the Land of Promise. Christians around the world rejoice and praise God, but still, why is there so much suffering in the world? This story has a purpose.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Korwa ase The Standard Mwanyagetinge ominto, twatebiigwe amangana amakong'u. University Lecturer, naende Omoraria bw' TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani osirire. Professor Nyasani nigo asirete igoro emaambia aaria ase enyagitari ya Agha Khan, Nairobi abwo ase konyora agendererete kobwenigwa koru etariki eyemo Engatiato [ January ] omwaka oyo. Nigo twatebigwa buna Prof Nyasani nigo airetwe ase enyagitari eyio ekero achagete korwara ase enkoro amo n' riini. Professor Nyasani nigo aiboretwe ase omwaka o 1936 aaria ime ya Central Kitutu Chache. Ritangani, Prof Nyasani nigo atagete gosomera obosasiroti, korende agachaka gosomera Philosophy. Goetera ase ogosoma kwaye, Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo arenge Omokenya ori orenge komenta abande omoyo ase ogokong'ia ase amosomo amo n' esukuru. Tarenge gotuguta chingaki chiaye nonya: Omokenya ominto Bw' Engencho mono, omomura oyo nigo atotigerete an academic treasure trove y' ebitabu, amariko amo' n' obotuki obonge. Tata omomura omwoge kerage, nigo arigete ebitabu goetania 41!! Obotuki amo n' ebitabu ebi ariigete nigo birakonye AbaKenya abange for many years to come. Omoki oye bw' ogosoma na gokora emeremo nigo ore, naende orabe an inspiration ase abanto abange for many years to come. Professor Joseph Nyasani [1936-2016]. Academic Legacy: Professor Nyasani tatotigeti bosa igo Professor Nyasani nigo achiete nguma ase okorika a dissertation yaye ya PhD ase omomwa o Latin ase omwaka o 1963 na kobuna e record y' emiaka 300. Buna asirete igoro iga, Professor Joseph Nyasani konyora orikire ebitabu goetania 41 bia metaphysics, logic, cosmology amo na legal Philosophy!! Gati y' ebitabu ebio 41 ariikire, ebinde nigo bire: [I]. Philosophy of Development [II]. Life and Death in Africa {III]. Philosophy of Nature {IV]. Philosophical Focus on Thought Systems in Development [V]. Legal philosophy [VI]. British Massacre of Gusii Freedom Defenders amo na [VII]. Metaphysics of the Cosmos and Related Recurrent Issues of Metaphysics. Highly acclaimed academic Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo asomete aaria Cambridge Secondary Education aaria kakamega County. Koru abwo, akagenda aaria Rome Italy abwo ase asomerete Latin, literature, English amo na history. Professor Nyasani nigo abwate Arts degree koru ase Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), Diploma in Social Ethics koru ase Woodstock College, Oxford ase omwaka o 1964, PhD koru ase The University of Cologne, Germany, ase omwaka o 1969, amo na Law Degree, New York University, School of Law ase omwaka o 1972. Ase ogokora emeremo, Professor Nyasani nigo akorete emeremo ase the United Nations Secretariat aaria New York buna the Political Affairs Officer ase the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs ase omwaka o 1971. Koru abwo, Professor Nyasani akaba the Associate Professor aaria ase the City University of New York ase omwaka o 1973. Komenta na koba Omwoorokia, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omoraria ase the Voice of Germany (Deutche Welle) aaria Cologne, Germany amo na Voice of Kenya eyio bono ere KBC. Ase boigo, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omwoorokia ase The University of Nairobi koru ase omwaka o 1970 goikera bono. Ase emeremo emenge akorete, Professor Nyasani boigo nere orenge the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University koru ase omwaka o 2008 to 2013. Gati y' ebieegwa b' ogosoma kw igoro Professor Nyasani aetwe nigo bire the Alexander Von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship amo na DAAD Foundation Scholarship gati y' omwaka o 1987 and 1992. Professor Joseph Nyasani, omwana bw Abakenya. Igwa bono koru ase KTN, Nairobi Gusii.com nigo tokoru engora gochia ase abamwabo, abasani, abairi amo n' abaamate ba omwana bw' Abakenya, Professor Joseph Nyasani. Kera egento ase Omonene Tata Nyasae.
english: These are the news reports: Published in The Standard Our condolences to the family, we have been informed of the passing of our colleague. University Lecturer, and former presenter on Omoraria TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani has passed away. Professor Nyasani died yesterday morning at the Aga Khan Hospital, Nairobi while undergoing treatment for an illness that had troubled him for a long time [ January ] this year. We were informed that Prof Nyasani was admitted to that hospital several days ago while battling a serious illness. Professor Nyasani was born in 1936 in Central Kitutu Chache. Later, Prof Nyasani went to study theology, then switched to studying Philosophy. After completing his studies, Professor Joseph Nyasani became a Kenyan who tirelessly commented on issues of life and education in schools. Let us remember his contribution: This Kenyan man, Mr. Engencho Mono, said that his home was an academic treasure trove of books, documents and numerous resources. This remarkable man owned over 41 books!! These books and resources will benefit Kenyans for many years to come. This scholar and worker was great, and he will remain an inspiration to many people for many years to come. Professor Joseph Nyasani [1936-2016]. Academic Legacy: Professor Nyasani did not waste his time Professor Nyasani successfully defended his PhD dissertation in Latin in 1963, setting a record of 300 years. Upon his death, Professor Joseph Nyasani leaves behind 41 books on metaphysics, logic, cosmology and legal Philosophy!! Of those 41 books, some include: [I]. Philosophy of Development [II]. Life and Death in Africa {III]. Philosophy of Nature {IV]. Philosophical Focus on Thought Systems in Development [V]. Legal philosophy [VI]. British Massacre of Gusii Freedom Defenders and [VII]. Metaphysics of the Cosmos and Related Recurrent Issues of Metaphysics. Highly acclaimed academic Professor Joseph Nyasani studied at Cambridge Secondary Education in Kakamega County. From there, he went to Rome Italy where he studied Latin, literature, English and history. Professor Nyasani obtained an Arts degree from Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), a Diploma in Social Ethics from Woodstock College, Oxford in 1964, a PhD from The University of Cologne, Germany in 1969, and a Law Degree, New York University, School of Law in 1972. In his work, Professor Nyasani worked at the United Nations Secretariat in New York as the Political Affairs Officer in the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs in 1971. Afterwards, Professor Nyasani became the Associate Professor at the City University of New York in 1973. As a commentator and reporter, Professor Nyasani was a presenter at the Voice of Germany (Deutsche Welle) in Cologne, Germany and the Voice of Kenya which is now KBC. Additionally, Professor Nyasani was a reporter at The University of Nairobi from 1970 onwards. In addition to his work, Professor Nyasani was also the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University from 2008 to 2013. It is said that during his time, Professor Nyasani received the Alexander Von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship and DAAD Foundation Scholarship in 1987 and 1992. Professor Joseph Nyasani, a son of Kenyans. Also broadcast on KTN, Nairobi Gusii.com publishes news about relatives, friends, colleagues and family members of the Kenyan son, Professor Joseph Nyasani. With great respect from Omonene Tata Nyasae.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Nigo nkoira ribaga eri kobaarigania abageni ba Gusii.com mwensi ase mwabeta. Nche nigo nde n' omogoko omonene ase ogoika engaki eye. Bono nabo togoteba maiso marore buna twakorire korika omogano oito Bw' Abagusii. Magokoro baba ominto, omongina Kwamboka Mireri. Amangana goetania enusu twarikire y' ekemira n' Ekegusii giato buna ntwe Abagusii twakabeire, nigo are goetera ase omongina Kwamboka. Mbuya mono baba ase kera egento. Nonya titomanyeti kera egento, twamanyire make, kobwa ekero twachagete. Nigo twaansete obotuki ase omochakano bwo omwaka oria oerete. Bono nigo yaaira omwaka oyomo n' enusu, kobeka obotuki obo aamo. Gaki ka moranche twabere ase okoira chingaki chintambe. Ekerenga nigo twatagete kogamba n' abangina n' abagaka ba Gusii bari bare moyo, naende bainyorete buna batebetigwe igoro y' omogano oyo oito. Tiyarenge egasi ere engororo igo. Ntwe nigo twanyorete ng'a ase bono, Abagusii n' abake batigarete, abwo bamanyete omogano oito. Obokongu bonde twanyorete mbori ng'a, buna otarigetwe aande onsi, emegano yaito ntwe Abagusii n' emenge. Omogaka Kenyanya Marube. Ntware gocha komanya igoro y' Mokendu O' Iruma, onye tari aye. Mbuya mono sokoro ominto. Ase engencho emegano eye ere ao ao, ekabetereria buna goika abariki baikaranse aamo naende, goitona na kobeka obotuki obo aamo, erinde korika omogano oyomo. Ase okogenderera gotuka, nigo yaikerete buna nonya kere emenge, emegano yaito emenene nigo ere ebere. Omogano oyomo nigo ogoteba buna nigo twarwete aaria Misri (Egypt). Omogano onde ogateba buna nigo twatirete korwa aaria Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. Bono ekabetereria buna goika Petronillah amo na Abner barigie abagaka n abang'ina abakoro, baria bainyorete buna batebetigwe. Gatigati: Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa ngotega are omogano. Mbuya mono tata ase ogotosemia. Bono twamanyire buna Abamanyi mbabwate amanyinga y' Abagusii. Nche nigo ngoakera Petronillah Ogoti amo na Abner Nyaberi, buna mbuya mono ase egasi engiya. Kende tikiare gocha korikwa ase ebulogi eye igoro y' omogano oito, onye tari barabwo. Ase boigo, nigo ngoteba buna mbuya mono ase abagaka n' abang'ina abange, abwo batotebetie amange igoro y' omogano oito. Mono mono, tiga toakere abakobwatia ase okorwa chingaki n' oboremereria bwabo, gotosemia: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Mbuya mono ase okoremeria amaborio aito, na gotoa obosemia. Obotuki bw' Petronillah amo na Abner obwo, ase blog posts chikobwatia. Next In This series: Omogano Bw' Omogusii [Abagusii History] Ka moranche rigereria: {I]. Ase engencho y enchera blog posts chikorikwa, nigo twaansete korika korwa magega, bono twakoreire gochia omochakano. Enchera engiya y' ogwesomia omogano oyo bwensi no ogoansera e post eye y' Omogano bw' Omogusii na kogenderera Next ase kera e series goikera okorere ase e post egoteba buna Ingai Twarwete?. [II]. Kobwatekana n' ogotarikwa kw' omogano oito n' Abagusii ntwe tweka, emegano yaito nigo ere emenge, naende ebwate "versions' ao ao. Kerabe buna obotutukanu mboreo ase oboriki obo, ka moranche totebie, erinde tobogorore. Nigo togoteba iga ase engencho tomanyete buna ntomanyeti kera egento. Mbuya mono ase kera oyomo and enjoy.
english: These are our words: It is good to gather people together at Gusii.com so they can help each other. And now this is a great story that has come out. Even though we did not know what was remembered, we have learned it, because we have chosen well. Now we have reached a point of understanding this year's challenges. But it seems this year and next, there will be more difficulties ahead. This time we have found ourselves in a difficult situation. The truth is that we have managed to speak to the elders and leaders of the Gusii people who are still alive, so that they can be reminded of this culture. Let us not forget this important matter. So we write this today, so that the Abagusii and their children may unite, and they understand this culture. Because we write this message again, so that it does not get lost, this culture is for the Abagusii and their generations. The leader is Kenyanya Marube. He wants to understand the time of Mokendu O' Iruma, who is no longer here. Thank you very much to everyone. And let this story spread far and wide, so that it reaches those who were scattered, and it brings unity and peace, and maintains this culture. And when considering its importance, it should be known that even if there are few of us, this culture is strong and enduring. This culture teaches us that we once went to Egypt. This culture also tells us that we came from Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. But it spreads so that it reaches Petronillah and Abner, the elders and leaders of the clans, so that they can be reminded and honored. Note: Leader Samuel Omare Nyambisa wrote this story. Thank you very much to his father for supporting him. But we have learned that the Abamanyi clan knows the history of the Abagusii. And now we greet Petronillah Ogoti and Abner Nyaberi, and thank them for their support. Come let us work hard to promote this blog about this culture, which is not forgotten. And finally, we say that we thank the elders and leaders of the community, so that they continue to support this culture. Very truly, do not forget those who contribute to this work and appreciate their efforts, saying: My sister Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Leader Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Leader Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Thank you very much for your contributions and support. ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Bono Omokungu Kanywomirwe Ngokora Arenge Kende Gionsi Buna Eeigwete? Na PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture and Customs Editor. Tureti Ya Kebaki [ September ] 4, 2015. Aya amwabo aya: Tokare konywa rikairo bono emorogoba, omongina magokoro Binsari ominto nigo antebia buna amang'ana nare akanire, atarenge gokorwa n' ebigori gete. Nigo magokoro antebia buna amang'ana aya nigo arenge koenanwa korwa gochia ase ekegori ekenene, gochia ase ekegori egeke. Ase omobwekano, ekero enyangi yarenge koba, aba banywomanire nkoegwa barenge amachiko. Omosacha nkoegwa arenge amachiko y' enywomo. Ase boigo omokung'u nere nkoegwa arenge amachiko buna abwenerete kwebwata bono kanywomirwe. Ase rituko ria rero, magokoro Binsari ominto nigo atagete gotosemia igoro y' amachiko aria arenge korenga abakung'u baria banywomire. Ritangani, magokoro nigo antebetie buna onye omosubati ochire bwoye nigo agwenerete koba omwegenwa gochia ase omogaka oye. Nigo yarenge bobe naende chimuma, ase omosubati gosanga kemobere n' omosacha omoao, otari oye bw' enywomo. Eriakabere, omokung'u oyo tarenge konywomwa na koruga mwaye obwango obwo obwo. Yaya. Nigo omosubati oyo arenge koragera na koruga mwa ng'ina biara ase amatuko atari make. Korwa abwo, ng'ina biara omanya komoarekera mwaye. Eriagatato, omokung'u bono kanywomirwe, tancheire koria amagena gose enyama y' engoko !! Koigwa iga, nche bono naboretie magokoro Binsari ominto erinde antebie buna ninki kiarenge kogera omokung'u akanigwe erinde taria chindagera echi. Baba ominto nigo antebetie buna tari kera egekoro giaito kebwate eng'encho yaye. "Ase okoba abaigweri, ntwe nigo twarenge kobwata Ekegusii giaito buna twarenge gotebigwa korwa ase ekegori egekoro, gochia ase ekegori egeke na gokora buna kegoteba" Magokoro nabo amentete ogoteba buna karanyore richibu rie ribori eri ase obwango, natotebie. Ekero bokorugwa, onde bwensi tarenge kobooncha !! Eriakane, magokoro nigo antebetie buna ekero obori bwamire na kogeswa, obokima bori obotongore nigo bwarenge koba obwa ise biara. Kibokorugwa, nonya n' omogango torenge gokombwa n' omoyio. Egete gioka kiarenge kobokomba !! Ase boigo, onde tancheire kobooncha nonya. Ise biara kaboonchire na koragera, abande nabarabwo bamanya kobega. Magokoro nigo antebetie buna Abagusii abakoro mbanchete korwa amasikani gochia ase abanto abanene. Aaiga, magokoro nigo abetebetie buna Ekegusii eke nigo kiarenge gokorwa ase okwoorokia amasikani gochia ase omogaka bw' omochie. Tiga kong'ong'oria iso biara Eriagatano, baba nigo antebetie buna omokung'u ore bwoye tancheire gotakuna obori ase ise biara. Ase boigo, aaiga n' okwoorokia amasikani gochia ase ise biara. Gotakuna obori nigo yarenge kororekana buna nigo arenge kong'ong'oria ise biara !! Eriagatano na rimo, omokung'u orenge koba bwoye tatakeire gosereta nyomba. Ase ki? Koru Omogusii omokoro, emeremo y' okoagacha chinyomba nigo yarenge koba ey' abasacha. Nonya yarenge koba buna omosacha bw' omokung'u oyo taiyo, abasacha abaamate, gose bagisangio b' omosacha oyo nabwo barenge komoagachera enyomba. Kai tata !! Omokungu gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni igo mbobe Eriagatano na kabere, omokung'u taganeiri gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni chi' omogaka oye. Bono nonya rero ebinto bianchokire, omokungu gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni ch' omogaka oye nigo yarenge koba chimuma. Magokoro baba ominto nigo antebetie buna ase chingaki echio chinkoro, nonya omokung'u barenge komanyana kemobere n' omogaka oye, nigo arenge gosika chinsemo echi chia nsoni chi' omogaka oyo oye. Bono tinkoria amagena y' engoko buna inyeigwete? Omokung'u nigo arenge gwesika. Eriagatano na gatato, amaru nigo arenge kwengwa na konywegwa ase emeyega ao ao. Ekero endagera yagesirwe, amaru nigo arenge gosikwa ase egetera, aengwa na konywegwa. Omwana gaachiire iburu, amaru nkonywegwa arenge. Nonya nabo igo, omokung'u taganeiri kobera eero ekero abagaka bakonywa amarwa. Yaya. Nigo omokung'u arenge kobamentera amaru gose amache a morero, erinde oirana chikoni ase abakung'u bande. Omokung'u taganeiri koereria omosacha oye egento n' okoboko okobee. Gokora igo, nigo yarenge kororekana buna ayio n' amachayo. Aaiga ase eriakianda, omokung'u bw' amasikani nigo arenge koereria omosacha oye egento, goetera ase okoboko gw' okorio. Koru ase omong'ina magokoro baba ominto, mbuya mono and thank you for listening. Chingaki chingiya ase Mwamogusii ominto abeta. This series will continue next week.
english: Gusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Is a person honored when they have many possessions and wealth, or is it because of their character? By PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture and Customs Editor. Thursday [ September ] 4, 2015. These are the words: Don't despise a poor man who has little property, a generous person honors people and I respect them because they share what little they have, they don't refuse to be helped by others. A generous person respects them because they share these things, whether it's a small gift or a large gift. Because of friendship, a young goat doesn't hesitate, those who help each other always have support. A clean person doesn't hesitate to offer support to his community. Because of this custom, someone is respected when they have the ability to give generously. But sometimes, generous people don't understand the importance of supporting those who are less fortunate than themselves. However, people say that anyone who helps another person should be considered a friend, just like a close relative. They say it's good to be kind, but a helper should also be careful about helping a bad person, lest it affect their reputation. In conclusion, a person shouldn't be praised for boasting about their wealth. Indeed, a person should be praised for being humble and respectful towards others, rather than flaunting their possessions. Through this, others will learn to appreciate them. Finally, a generous person, especially one with wealth, should not look down on anyone!! It is said that a generous person honors people and understands that a person's honor depends on how they treat others. People say that one should not be arrogant! In essence, people say that a family that is united and works together will prosper, and its future generations will be blessed. It is important, however, that a leader does not become corrupt or selfish. This is said, so that leaders may learn humility. People say that the old Gusii people used to value hard work more than material possessions. Today, people say that the Gusii language is valued more than acquiring wealth or status. Let us end here. Finally, people say that a wealthy person should not despise anyone. It is also said that acquiring wealth or status is not enough; one must also have good character. One who has both wealth and character is truly respected, and those around them recognize their worth. It is important that the Gusii people remember their traditions. Let us respect our ancestors, whose wisdom guides us like a light. Those who disrespect their ancestors bring misfortune upon themselves and their families. Oh my goodness!! A person's shame is a heavy burden. Finally, a person should not reveal another person's secrets. However, sometimes things happen unexpectedly, and a person's secret becomes known. People say that when this happens, one should show compassion and understanding towards the person whose secret was revealed, rather than judging them harshly. Is there a reason why someone would want to steal from another? A person should not steal. Finally, disputes should be resolved peacefully and fairly. The truth should prevail, and justice should be served. Children should be taught to respect others, and people should not take advantage of each other. But even then, a person should not interfere in matters that do not concern them, lest they become entangled in conflict. Oh yes. A person should not encourage others to engage in wrongdoing, especially if it involves harming others. A person should not boast about their strength or abilities. It is better to remain humble and modest. Let us listen to the wise words of our elders, and I thank you for listening. May peace reign among the Gusii people. This series will continue next week.

ekegusii: Na PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Mwamogusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egetamo (March) 23, 2011. Nigo anywometwe ase enyangi ye Ekegusii na kobekerwa ebitinge. Tari igo rioka. Nigo abegete ebitinge mbaka ekero abatisetwe ase the SDA Church aaria Nyanchwa. Omongina Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. Nyuma yo okorusia ebitinge ebio, nigo omongina Bosibori aboretie omwanchwa oye, omogaka Musa Nyandusi erinde bonsi bagancherana. Marehemu omongina Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. Omongina o Gusii onywometwe goetera ase enyangi y' ebitinge in modern times. Ntotagete obochege! Enywomo nigo yasikire na abakoro. Ase chingaki chia kare enyangi ye ebitinge nigo yagakorirwe ekero gio okonywomana. Ritangani, esigani nigo yare gotomwa gochia sobo enyaroka yaira eng'ana egoteba buna imbatagete kobanywomera (ntotagete obochege!). Togende ase ekerorano Korwa aiga rituko rie ekerorano nigo riare kobekwa. Yaani ekerorano ninki? Nabo oraborie. Ase ekerorano nario omosubati no omomura bare kororana ritangani. Omomura na abasani baye nigo bare gochikwa gochicha sobo omosubati erinde barorane no omoiseke. Omosubati onye tatageti momura oyo, nigo are kwabusa risiko riabo baroo. Ase ki? Erinde bamanye inga ere tatageti gose tancheti momura oyio. Yaani eyio nigo yarenge enchera yo okobaseria in a polite way. Egere kobaseri aba. Korende onye bwanchire, tare kwabusa. Ekeriboko ekero kiaariganigwe, ogotera nigo kware goterwa abanto batwara omogoko. Bono korwa aaiga chiombe chio okonywoma omoiseke oyo, nigo chiare gokwanerwa. Abamura abangaini nigo bare koba na riso rimo ase omoiseke! Ritangani, embori amo n' eeri y' egesicho amo ne chiombe nigo chiare korwegwa. Abanyene omosubati amo no omomura nigo bare koigwana. Ekero kio ogoakana chiombe, esira ngotigara yare. Korwa abwo, abamura bono nigo bare gochikwa bagenda sobo omoiseke. Abwo sobo omoiseke, nigo barenge gotenga bwakia, korende bare na riso rimo ase omoiseke ! Nigo bare korenda erinde omoiseke oyio tatama gochia bongina rome. Omoiseke oyio aise gocha gotama na kobasireria, nigo bare goakwa a fine ye embori eyemo. Abamura batamanyeti gasi. Oigwe bono. Ko bakorire gotenga ase rimaambia, nigo bare kogenda no omoiseke oyio korwa aiga mpaka sobo omomura. Ebinto mbuya bire. Taraire mosisi! Korende bado. Mangana taraera. Amatuko atato kaerire, obokima n' embori nigo bware koirwa ase omosubati oyo osogete egere bamanyigwe gose mbaigwananete no omogaka oyo oye, gose nigo ararete mosisi ! Bakonyora ng'a amangana mbuya are (yaani omomura no omoiseke mbakorete egasi buya), na bonsi mbaisanegete, omoiseke oteba atimigwe ebitinge. Manya ng'a omoiseke arenge gokana inga binto tibiarenge buya, hakuna ebitinge! Bono korwa abwo, enyangi yaariganigwa ekorwe, n' omosubati oirana sobo. Abamura n' abasubati baba tayare na amakano. Omonyakiore n' esumati amo n' omoimari n' abamura nao bare koba aaiga. Bado maneno si rahisi hivyo. Enyameni nigo yare kobekwa. Oyo okobua ase enyameni eye nere ore koegwa ritana rie engombe. Ekondo nero yarenge aroro, eyio omoimari are gotanganigwa no omonyakeore. korwa ensemo ya abamura nigo tware gotwara, omonyakeore ore gotangana motwe, omongwasi, nere omonywomi nakorwa ase omosubati no omoimari, omoriakari, agasagane ko obosi ne enyaroka ya amaguta. Emanwa ye embori nigo yare komosinyorera amagoro! Nyangi chia kare nchiare koumerana nchera. Mbobe pi ase Abagusii. Omokundekane bono nere ore gotimi ebitinge. Omoriakari nigo are korambora amagoro, emanu ye embori yamoetanana round and round yamanya komosinyorera amagoro ! Bamanya konyenya akamanwa aka kwamanya kobekerwa ebitinge. Oko nakwo ogotimigwa egetinge. Enyangi yamanya gotererwa gochia sobo omomura. Eye nero enyangi ye ebitinge .
english: To PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Mwamogusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. March 23, 2011. She was among those who were circumcised in the land of Ekegusii and initiated into adulthood. This story is true. She was initiated into adulthood until she became a member of the SDA Church area Nyanchwa. The late Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. After completing the initiation ceremonies, the late Bosibori gave birth to her son, Dr. Musa Nyandusi while many people gathered around. The late Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. A Gusii woman who was circumcised and initiated into adulthood in modern times. Don't be surprised! The ceremony ended with celebrations. In ancient times during the circumcision ceremony, it was customary for people to share food. Therefore, the elders were sent to look for a beautiful girl who could cook food so that they would not lack something to eat (don't be surprised!). Let us move on to the explanation. The work of the explanation committee was completed. What does an explanation mean? Ask those who know. An explanation involves both young men and old men coming together. Old men and their wives were sent to find a beautiful girl so that she could marry a young man. A young man who doesn't have a wife, he risks being ridiculed. Why? So that they know that he doesn't have anyone to help him with his household chores. That is why it is important to respect others in a polite way. It is good to respect them. Therefore, someone should not hesitate, he should ask. The truth about this matter has been revealed, because people used to steal from each other. But now this habit of eating another person's food has decreased. The old men also send their wives to look for a young man. They send their wives to look for a young man so that they can have peace of mind. They should therefore ensure that this young man doesn't cause problems for others. This young man should not cause trouble and disrespect, they should be fined according to the law. The old men don't understand. Let them learn. If they continue to behave like this, they will remain with the young man until he marries an old man. Things are changing. Be careful! Therefore, let it be. Understand carefully. Traditions are disappearing, and customs are being forgotten in this society where people no longer want to be known, and they are disrespectful to their leaders. They are careless. They complain that things are changing (meaning old men and young men are doing things differently), and many people disagree, saying that a young man shouldn't be allowed to participate in ceremonies. Know that a young man may not understand some things, there are no ceremonies! But if this happens, the world will be confused, and the community will suffer. Old men and women are ready for conflict. The mediator and the elders and the old men are also ready. It's not easy. The situation is tense. That person who speaks against the elders is like someone who insults a cow. That story is not true; those mediators were involved with the mediator. Because of the actions of the old men, we have suffered, the mediator has become stubborn, the spokesperson, and the interpreter have caused problems for the community and the mediators, causing chaos and confusion in the villages. The wealth of the community is being wasted! This world is full of lies. Respect the Gusii people. Love everyone and don't discriminate. The spokesperson is destroying everything, the wealth of the community is circulating around and around, wasting away. Know that complaining won't help solve the problem. Everything has its time. This world is always changing, and this world is full of lies.

ekegusii: Buna twakabeire na PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi [June] 19, 2012 Aya amwabo aya: Omongina magokoro Moraa ominto nantagete gontebia engana. Baba nigo atagete gonsemia igoro y' ogosira kw' omogaka oria obwate abakung'u abange. Ekero omogaka ore n’ abarugi abange akuure, Ekegusii gete ki' eng’encho nkiagakorirwe, buna omong’ina magokoro Moraa agoteba. Ogokobani nkwarengeo ase Ekegusii Bono buna omogaka oyo atweka mo iga, nigo kera omokung'u oye, arenge kominyoka gochia mwaye ogokobani. Inee, bono ogokobani ninki? Nabo oraborie. Eee abakungu abange mbakanywomirwe n' omogaka oyomo ase chingaki echio chi kare. Ebitega mbiakaarekirwe, n' ebinto biaturekwa, naende biagororokigwa, ko omogaka bw' omochie asirire. Below: Nka Gusii Omong’ina Moraa nigo agoteba buna ogokobani n’ ogoonchora chianga, omong’ina akobeka. Nigo omong'ina nyene nyagosira arenge kobeka chianga chia ime, maonchorerane. Korwa abwo, omanya kobeka chianga chia nyagosira korwa igoro, nachirochio maonchorane! Naende omong'ina nyene nigo arenge kweyaka riibu, ko omogaka oye asirire Tari igo rioka. Kera omong’ina nigo arenge koeyaka riibu, buna omware. Komenta nayio, kera omong'ina tarenge gwesibia. Yaya. Aase engaki eye yonsi y' ebirero ekero omogaka oyo akuure, omong'ina oyo tarenge gokwanigwa n' okoboko, goikera ebirero biaerire. Nigo baba Moraa akomenta buna mong'ina oyo tarenge koererigwa endagera koboko. Nigo endagera yarenge goterekwa nse, omong'ina oyo omanya koyeimokia korwa nse. Emorogoba y' omogaka oyo gosira, kera omokung'u nigo arenge kobera mwaye. Korende onye mosera ibu tari moyo, omokung'u o kabere ori ore moyo nao omobere orenge koirwa. Kera mosera ibu nigo arenge kobera mwaye, orara goikera rituko riria ri' ogotindekwa. Mosera ibu omonene nere orenge gochaka koyaruta amaroba aya, abande babwatia korwa magega. Omobere gotubereirwe, kera oyomo omanya kogenda mwaye. Emorogoba oyio ko omogaka atindekirwe, kera omong’ina nigo arenge konyenya eming'ichi y’ ogokendi enyomba. Abakiare ba nyagosira mbange koria emingichi eye. Yaya. Eming'inchi eye nigo yare koriegwa n' onde bwensi ase eamate, otatiga abakiare ba nyagosira. Emaambia yaye bogokiamoka, abang’ina b' omogaka oyo bonsi nigo barenge kogingerana etuki, aase oboina igoro. Ase boigo, abangina aba nigo barenge kobutorwa ebitinge, bamanya kobibeka ase embera igoro. Ko babekire ebitinge ebi aase embera igoro, kera omongina nigo arenge koirana mwaye. Oko n' ogotureka ebinto ebinene b' nyagosira kwoorokia gose koba ekemanyererio ki' ogosira kwaye. Ritangani, ritimo rio omogaka nyagosira nigo riarenge goturekwa, riarigereria gochia nse. Korwa abwo, ekerogo kiaye nyamagoro atato, nakerokio nigo kiarenge goturekwa !! Omongina magokoro Moraa nigo akomenta buna korwa abwo, ebinto nigo biare kogororokigwa. Bono okogorokigwa ninki? Naende nabo oratware riborio riinde. Ritimo n’ ekerogo kia nyagosira, nigo biarenge gotenenegiwa buya, ase engencho bono ebirero biaerire. Aya gakorirwe, abang’ina aba bamanya kobeka chianga buya bono, na gwesibia omobere erinde abaamate bonsi, goikera aaria ase abasubati basogete, bacha bakora omoyega omonene. english: Good afternoon, we greet PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June [June] 19, 2012 These are the words: A person who loves Moraa does not reveal her secrets to anyone. A father also does not reveal his wife’s wealth to a stranger who comes to his home. It is good for a home to have its own people, Ekegusii has its own traditions which are respected, so a person who loves Moraa respects them. Let us discuss the customs of Ekegusii Know then that when a home is built, it is better than a rented house, because a rented house can be taken away from you anytime. Indeed, what is a rented house? Go and build yours. Oh, strangers, I am saddened by this current situation. Things were different, and things changed, and now they are being discussed, like a home owner who is grieving. Below: Like Gusii A person who loves Moraa respects the homestead, a loving person. It is a loving person who grieves if their homestead is taken away, let them grieve. Because of this, know that taking away someone’s homestead is grief, and it causes pain! And a loving person will not allow ruin, so that their home may remain. The days are coming. Before, a person would not allow ruin, but nowadays. Comment on this, before a person allows ruin. Yes. All the days of life, it is good for that home to remain, that person will not be impoverished, so that their children may prosper. It is said that Moraa commented that allowing ruin is like losing a homestead. It is like a homestead that is lost forever, that person will never recover it. The suffering of that home is great, before a stranger allows ruin. It is a homeowner who grieves if they are evicted from a large plot of land. Because of this, the property of that home is sold and bought on a large plot of land [ a stranger ]. Understand that a large plot of land is not life, a stranger who owns it does not have life either, and the property will be destroyed. Before a large plot of land is allowed to be ruined, look for a small piece of land to cultivate. The stories about that small piece of land, the property will be protected. Because of this, seeds are sown. The fruits of those seeds are harvested, a large tree grows and provides shade. Anyone who plants a large tree knows how to plant it. Yes. That shade is found where there is coolness and water, protecting anyone who grieves. The stories about it are remembered, everyone associated with that home wants to share their thoughts. As they share their thoughts, understand that someone will come and ask questions. Because of this, respect is given, and boundaries are established. Once those boundaries are established, the belongings of the grieving homeowner are protected. But who protects them? I ask you. This is because leaving things to chance can lead to misunderstanding and grief. Truly, the time when the homeowner grieves is when it is most vulnerable. Because of this, the current situation is very difficult, and it needs to be addressed!! This is spoken about in Ekegusii. If you leave things to chance, disputes arise, causing conflict and division. Moraa's heart says that because of this, things should be discussed. But why discuss them? I ask you to explain the reason. The time of the grieving homeowner and the current situation need to be understood, so that peace can prevail. These things have been done, people know how to handle matters peacefully, and through good guidance, they protect everyone, helping those who are suffering and children grow up well. Moraa's heart also encourages others to work together and remember the importance of unity. Thank you very much for listening.

Bono omogaka oyo agatebia abanyakenyoro aba buna nigo atagete koramenya aiga Bobaracho ase egeka getari geke. Abanyakenyoro bakagokiwa na goichorwa n' omogoko omonge. Abanto bonsi ase ekenyoro bagacha aamo na goatera omogaka oyo omoraba bw' okoagacha egesa na komoatera endemero ase are gocha korema endagera yaye. Abang'ina bari abake ase emiaka nigo bebangete na gochaka komobuchera na komoroseria endagera na koirera ase esaiga yaye, erinde aragere. Abana b' ekenyoro eke nabarabuo mbatigareti magega. Nigo bagachire nchinsana ime na gotwera omogaka oyo amatunda ao ao erinde ache koria. Omogambi oito nabwate abaiseke abarabera nyakieni bori !! Bono omogambi o Bobaracho nigo arenge n' abanyaroka babere. Moraa na Kemunto. Omonyaroka omonene, Moraa nigo arenge omonyakieni, korende nigo arenge n' amachayo, otarenge gosasokera banto. Omonyaroka omoke bw' omogambi oyo, Kemunto nigo arenge omwororo na nigo abwate amasikani na obwanchani gochia ase abanto bonsi. Moraa nigo arenge omoenenu kerage naende nigo arenge gotiana buna tagochiera omogaka oyo omogotu roche, ekero engaki yaigete y' okoroseria omogaka oyo endagera na komochiera roche. Ase boigo, Moraa nigo arenge ne chindobo na nigo achaete omogaka oyo. Nigo arenge gokwana amang'ana amabe igoro y' omogaka oyo. Kemunto ere nigo arenge omoigweri. Nigo arenge koroiseria omogaka oyo endagera. Bono ekero Moraa angete gochia roche, Kemunto ere akaira endagera na komochiera roche. Ase engencho y' obuya bwaye, omogaka oyo akagokigwa na Kemunto. Bono Moraa okare gwesitonti !! Nonya nabo igo, omogaka oyo agataka Moraa amoengere amarwa ekiagera nigo atagete gotwara omoyega aiga ase esaiga yaye. Moraa gachia koigwa aya, agakana kagoteba buna tagosaria chingaki chiaye chia bene, gochia koenga amarwa mw' omogotu oyo orenge kororekana buna omonto oisire gokwa. Kemunto buna atabwate amang'ana amange, akaimoka maambia rituko riare kobwatia na kogenda bw' omogaka oyo gochia komoengera amarwa. Bono gaaika ase omogaka oyo, akamotebia buna Moraa taigwete buya, nakio achera komoengera amarwa aya y' omoyega. Kemunto akaenga amarwa aya igo, goikera akayia . Bono amaru kayia, omogaka oyo akaruo agatunyana abanyakenyoro bagende bwoye erinde bachengere omoyega oyo. Moraa buna atakari, nigo atangete gosona eyanga enyia yarenge amaritati kerage korende Kemunto ere akaaba tari na yanga yare kieni. Bono egaikera Kemunto gotwara ebirengererio bi' ogotagenda ase omoyega oyo. Rituko ri' omoyega ekero riaigete, Moraa akaba omotang'ani goikerana. Kemunto akaba gatigarete sobo ko kare n' ebirengerio ebinge buna atarigoikerana omoyega oyo bw' eng'encho. Kare sobo, Kemunto akaigwa obote goetera n' eriogi ri' ogochengera amatera are goterwa korwa bw' omogaka oyo, goikera egaika engaki akomanora gochia ase omoyega oyo. Bono buna Kemunto are nchera koagachia gaikire ang'e n' bw' omogaka oyo, akarora buna ne ching'enang'eni chiatonya korwa igoro na komogwera ase eanga yaye. Kemunto okare gosamia omosae egesora Ogakare komesa na kororekana kare amaritati !! Keri keri, omosae ogakare gosoka korwa ase abanto aba bare gochengera omoyega oyo na gosamia Kemunto n' omogoko amo n' obwanchani obonene. Kemunto akagoka na komosamia omosae oyo orenge egesora na komoboria ase omogaka oyo omogotu are. Omosae oyo agaitaberia ogoteba buna "Aye Kemunto naye ntagete konywoma rero. Nche nere omogaka ori orenge omogotu kwareterete endagera n' amache kera engaki, goikera nkairana koba omosae" Kemunto agaichana na gosasoka. Agasamia omosae oyo, omoerio oye aba bakabwatanigwa koba omokungu n' omogaka.
