ekegusii: 1 Chisokoro ne chisokororia chia Yeso (Luk 3:23–38) 1Oyo noro omoroberio bw’ororeria rwaye Yeso Kristo, omwana o Daudi, omwana o Ibrahimu. 2Ibrahimu akaibora Isaka, na Isaka akaibora Yakobo, na Yakobo akaibora Yuda na abamwabo, 3na Yuda akaibora Peresu na Zera ase Tamari, na Peresu akaibora Hezironi, na Hezironi akaibora Aramu, 4na Aramu akaibora Aminadabu, na Aminadabu akaibora Nashoni, na Nashoni akaibora Salimoni, 5na Salimoni akaibora Boazi ase Rahabu, na Boazi akaibora Obedi ase Rutu, na Obedi akaibora Yese, 6na Yese akaibora omoruoti Daudi. Na Daudi akaibora Sulemani ase oyio orenge omokungu o Uria, 7na Sulemani akaibora Rehoboamu, na Rehoboamu akaibora Abiya, na Abiya akaibora Asa, 8na Asa akaibora Yehosafati, na Yehosafati akaibora Yoramu, na Yoramu akaibora Usia, 9na Usia akaibora Yotamu na Yotamu akaibora Ahasi, na Ahasi akaibora Hezekia, 10na Hezekia akaibora Manase, na Manase akaibora Amoni, na Amoni akaibora Yosia, 11na Yosia akaibora Yekonia na abamwabo ekero ki’ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa gochia Babeli. 12Na nyuma y’ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa gochia Babeli Yekonia akaibora Salatieli, na Salatieli akaibora Serubabeli, 13na Serubabeli akaibora Abihudi, na Abihudi akaibora Eliakimu, na Eliakimu akaibora Azoro, 14na Azoro akaibora Zadoki, na Zadoki akaibora Akimu, na Akimu akaibora Eliudi, 15na Eliudi akaibora Eleazari, na Eleazari akaibora Matani, na Matani akaibora Yakobo, 16na Yakobo akaibora Yusufu, omosacha o Mariamu oyo oiborete Yeso, oyokorokwa Kristo. 17Na ebigori bionsi korwa Ibrahimu goika Daudi nigo biarenge ebigori ikomi na bine: na korwa Daudi goika ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa gochia Babeli nebigori ikomi na bine: na korwa ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa gochia Babeli goika Kristo nebigori ikomi na bine. Okoiborwa kwa Yeso (Luk 2:1–7) 18Okoiborwa kwa Yeso Kristo nigo kwarenge iga: Ekero Mariamu ng’ina ariereire boko na Yusufu, bataraikana ang’e, akarorekana ore morito ase Omoika Omochenu. 19Na omosacha oye Yusufu nigo arenge omonto omoronge, tarigetie komoa obosooku, akarengereria komotiga bobisi. 20Korende ekero arenge orengereretie aya, rora, omomalaika bw’Omonene akamochiera ase chindoto akamotebia. “Aye Yusufu, omwana o Daudi, toiroka koira Mariamu abe mokao, ekiagera oborito obwo bwatongirwe inda yaye nobw’Omoika Omochenu. 21Ere naibore omwana omoisia, nomoroke erieta riaye Yeso, ekiagera nere oratoorie abanto baye korwa ase ebibe biabo.” 22Aya onsi nigo abeire, erinde riikerane eriakwanetwe n’Omonene ase omonwa bw’omobani, 23“Rigereria, omoiseke omwekungi nabe morito, erio naibore omwana omoisia, na erieta riaye narokwe Imanueli” (engencho yaye: Nyasae amo naintwe). 24Na Yusufu agachia koboka korwa ase chitoro, agakora buna achigetwe nomomalaika bw’Omonene; akaira mokaye, 25korende tiriaba komo goika kaiboire omwana omoisia; Yusufu akamoroka erieta riaye Yeso.
english: 1 The genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. (Luke 3:23–38) 1This is the record of the descendants of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. 2Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers, 3and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah through Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Aram, 4and Aram fathered Aminadab, and Aminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon, 5and Salmon fathered Boaz through Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed through Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse, 6and Jesse fathered King David. And David fathered Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife, 7and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asa, 8and Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah, 9and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah, 10and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Ammon, and Ammon fathered Josiah, 11and Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers just before they were taken captive to Babylon. 12After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel, 13and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor, 14and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud, 15and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob, 16and Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ. 17So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the exile to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the exile to Babylon to Christ, fourteen generations. The Birth of Jesus (Luke 2:1–7) 18Now the birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way: while his mother Mary was engaged to Joseph, she was found to be with child before they lived together. 19And her husband Joseph, being a just man, had planned to divorce her quietly, 20but an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21She will bear a son, and you shall name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” 22All this took place to fulfill what the Lord has spoken through the prophet: 23“Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be Emmanuel” (which means, God with us). 24Then Joseph woke up from his sleep and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took her as his wife, 25but he knew her not until she had given birth to a son. And he named her son Jesus.

ekegusii: 1. YEHOVAH, YESO AMO NE EBUKU: Yehovah naende nere Yeso , nigo agokwana ase Ebibilia Enchenu ase Yohana Ng,a Nere ore ringa’na oyio otometwe amo na Nyasae buna to gosoma ase ebitabu b,Enchili nere Omoakwa amaguta .Oyio nere oikeranetie obobani obokoro na amariko yi ritangani ase emiaka 2000 yaerire. 2. YESO EMBOORIA: Abete embooria ya abanyabibe ase ogokwa ase omosalaba buna Caiphas aanegetie buna oyo nere Omoruoti bwa Abayahudi nan ere oikeranetie amachiko a musa.Ere akabambwa ase Omosalaba akaba Omobooria bwa abanyabibe .Akaboka korwa ase embera nyuma ya amatuko atato akarina gochia I goro ase aikaransete ase okobo gokorio kwa Nyasae. Tata. 3. OKWAROKA: Ibrahim nere Tata oito Bwo,okwegena na omwanchani oito.Ng,a goetera ere nao omochakano bwe ebisaku 12 bionsi bigasesenigwa..Goetera ase okobwatana kwaye amo na Nyasae intwe twarokirwe koba ababiare bwo,Okobwatana kwa Nyasae amo nere ase okobwatana kwa Nyasae amo na Ibrahim.Goika intwe twensi toorokie na,a nigo tore abana ba Ibrahim ase okwegena naende nere ore Tata oito bwo,okwegena.Ibrahim nigo atenerete buna Tata oito Bw,okwegena agio islam,Abahindu na abayahudi bagokana.. Ase okobwatana (IAC) Nyasae N,obwanchani na obwanchani bwaye tibori koera,buna omotomwa Paulo,agoteba buna obwanchani bwa Nyasae tibori goetanimonto onde bwensi naende nigo bogoita chinguru chia Birecha. 4. OKOANGAMA: Goika omonto ang,aame erinde abatiswe ase erieta ria Tata,Omwana,na Omoika Omochenu. Buna togosoma ase Ebatiso nero ekemanyererio na,a kwabeire Omoorokigwa oyo Yeso Kristo. Ase ebatisa ekebe egetanganie nigo kere bobisi, nyuma yeebatiso goika orue oborori ase Babura bamino na baiseke bamino erio orokie ebibe biago maise marore. 5. OBOMANYI IGORO Y, EBATISO: Ebatiso nogosibigwa korwa ase ebibe na Kobwatanigwa ase okobwatana amo na Yeso.Ekero togosoma igoro y,okobwatana Kwa Elijah,(4EC) nigo tokonyora ng,a ebatiso Isaac nigo yachakerete ekero kia engaki ye Elijah, Kerori ba Omonene (LW) amo nokobwatana kwa Isaac. Kera ekanisa ye,ekeene nigo yachagetwe amo ne Elijah yebatiso ekorwa igoro.Yeso akaboria Abafalisai Luke 20:4, igoro ye,ebatiso.Yeso amo na batomwa ikomi na babe (12). 6. NYASAE NA ABAKUNGU BABO BABERE: Aiga nigo togosoma ng,a Nyasae nigo bare babaere.Tata na omwana.Yeso n,Omwana oye omomoima buna togosoma Yohana1:1.Oyio okorete no goikerenia emeremo yaye buna Omalaika Michael.Nyasae n,Omwanchani oito naende omonyaboronge.Goika toorokie ng,a Kristo nigo achete ore Mwanayabanto naende nairane gocha kwoyia Ekanisa yaye eria Kabere.Naende goika tomanye ng,a abanyaborimo mbache bagoteba na,a nabwo Kristo buna togosoma ase Okomanoka 7 na 14 naende abaregende Igoro na abanto chilifu 144,000 abwo bare ase ororeria rwa Adamu na hawa. Soma omochakano 2:18,Abagalatia 4:24 na Yohana 14:26.Aseigo Yehovah nabwate Omokungu oyio ore Omoika Omochenu,oyio okogambera emeika yonsi . 7. OBORWOTI BWA NYASAE :Oboruoti bwa igoro nigo bokogamberwa amo no moika omochenu.Ase ense abanto 144,000, nigo babaganire ase oborwoti 144,000 na nigo bakogamberwa na omorwuti igoro. Oborwoti obo nigo bogokwanerwa ase egetabu gia Daniel 12, ogokora kwa abotomwa 5:1-11.Onye kore omonywa amarwa, esigara, enyasore orakonyeke koraigwe amang’ana aya erinde okonyeke nande koraganie konyuoma nabo arasome amang’ana aya. Aseigo Ekanisa yekeene goika ebe na abarai batari konywa edivai yogotindia naende abagambi ase enka na ase abana babo. Titong’aina omoika omochenu buna twancheranire ase ebitambokero ebi 7 biokwegena ase LW. (Rigereria igoro ya Ananias amo na Sapphira) nagoika amonto ancherane amo nomoika amanye kobatiswa buna Petero anchete akabatiswa( Ogokora kwa abatomwa 2:41). Abokoreria ba omonene koika babe nomokia mono batari ne chitangatangu chio oromeme (1 Timoteo 3) Onye bare na abana boiborete isiko ye,enywomo yabo nabarabwa tibari kobarenda goika banse kobarenda ase chichera chionsi.
english: 1. JEHOVAH, JESUS LOVES US ALL: Jehovah loves Jesus, and He has shown us through the Holy Bible, John 3:16 that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life. Everlasting life is offered to all people of all nations throughout the 2000 years of existence. 2. JESUS DIED: The death of the righteous as a sacrifice on the cross because Caiaphas plotted this and it was the will of the Jewish leaders and they carried out the law of Moses. He was crucified on the cross and became the ransom for the righteous. He rose again after three days and ascended to heaven to be at the right hand of God the Father. 3. THE COVENANT: Abraham was our father in faith, and his son was Isaac. He went through a trial where his twelve sons were circumcised. It happened through trusting in God so that we could be blessed and become heirs. The covenant of God with Abraham and the covenant of God with Isaac. Let us look at how we are children of Abraham through faith, and we believe that our father in faith was Abraham. Abraham believed in God, and this is Islam, Hindus and Jews agree. In the covenant (IAC) God, the Father and His Son do not separate, because Paul said that the Son of God does not separate from the world and He came down to earth like dew on the grass. 4. REPENTANCE: Let everyone who wants to be baptized believe in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Whoever reads baptism knows that it is a proclamation of the resurrection of Jesus Christ. After baptism, let everyone live a new life, leaving behind their old sins and bad habits so that they can receive good things forever. 5. THE MEANING OF BAPTISM: Baptism symbolizes death and being united with the death of Jesus. Whoever reads the story of Elijah's covenant (4EC) will understand that when Isaac was about to be sacrificed, it was a type of Elijah's covenant, the Lord of Lords (LW) and the covenant of Isaac. The church of the saints was established through Elijah's baptism during that time. Jesus rebuked the Pharisees Luke 20:4, regarding the time of baptism. Jesus and the disciples were twelve (12) in number. 6. GOD AND HIS ANGELS ARE HOLY: It is written that God has fathers. The Father and the Son. Jesus is the Son who lives eternally; read John 1:1. He created everything and revealed His purpose through the Archangel Michael. God is our Father, and He loves us very much. It is written that Christ will come to take His people and build His Church on earth. And we know that the workers who worship Him—Christ—read Revelation 7 and 14, and they will keep the Sabbath, 144,000 of them, those who are sealed from the lineage of Adam and Eve. Read Genesis 2:18, Galatians 4:24, and John 14:26. Therefore, Jehovah created an angel who is the Holy Spirit, who proclaims His message to everyone. 7. THE SEAL OF GOD: The seal of the Sabbath is proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. For those 144,000 people, they share the 144,000 seals and are marked with the seventh seal. That seal corresponds to the book of Daniel 12, which speaks of the five angels 5:1-11. Anyone who knows the truth, remains steadfast, and does not deny his faith should study these truths. Therefore, the true church should not have members who drink wine or engage in witchcraft and harm their children. Let us remember the Holy Spirit so that we can be united in the seven pillars of wisdom (referring to the story of Ananias and Sapphira), and let us also remember those who were baptized because Peter commanded them to be baptized (Acts 2:41). Those who serve God greatly should live holy lives without any shame (1 Timothy 3). Those who have children should raise them according to the scriptures, and their families should be known for being faithful and living righteously.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Rituko erimo, omomura oyomo gakorwa esukuru gochia sobo, agaeta ase rikori erio riasimekire chimengere. Aaiga, aganchera nkarenge aroro abwo ase abanto barenge goeta. Bono agaika ase omogondo oyo na konyora buna aganchera nigo karenge gotiira aiga mogondo gati. Chimengere chiasomoiri, na koba chintambe Chimengere konye chiasomoiri na nigo chiarenge chintambe, goikera tikwarenge korora omonto ekero agoeta chibando ime. Omomura oyo orenge korokwa Osoro, kagoeta aaiga, nigo abwate omote koboko arenge gosukeria amasabo ye chibando tamoara kagweta gochia sobo. Endemero y' omogaka. Omogondo aaria Botabori, Magombo, Nyamira County. Photo na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files. Kare ang'e gosoka korwa mogondo, agaaka ebando eyemo konye yaberekire na ekagwa inse, n' ebando yonsi nyakeemba. Bono kiyagwa inse, Osoro akaigwa bobe mono ase ogosaria ebando eye. Akabogoria ebando eye erinde achie koyesamba kagoika inka sobo ayerie, korende akanyora nigo ere endere. Akaruo akayeruta gochia ase obonyansi ime ekiagera konye teraba ekoriegwa. Nigo yarenge endere kegima. Keri keri, omonyaroka oyomo orenge korokwa Nyanchera agaeta mbarabare, gakorwa rinani ime gotenya. Nyanchera nere bwetwekire chiinko, na gochaka kobongorora chinyeke korwa ase ekeemba Bono Nyanchera nigo etwegete chinko na konye orosire. Gaaika aiga ang'e nase chibando chiasimekire, agatora chinko erinde atimoke, amanye kogenda mwabo. Akarora ebando egwete obonyansi ime na akayeimokia. Akanya kobongorora chinyeke na gochiruta gochia are korwa ase ateneine. Ekeemba kegatigara kebwate chinyeke nkeigo, na kerokio agakeruta gochia ase obonyasi bwameete obotambe. Korwa abwo, akaruo akaimokia chinko chiaye na koayerera gochia sobo ase amenyete na sokoro yaye. Bono chinyoni chiachakire korigia ganto chibeke mboto Emagoroba eyio, chinyoni gichikoiruruka kwerigeria ganto chibeke mboto, chikanyora chinyeke chigwete na chigatocha chinyeke chiri Nyanchera arutete inse korende chinyoni echi tichiaroche ase ekeemba kiare. Rituko riare kobwati ebikondo bikarwa rinani ime na gosoa ase ebitii biare. Egekondo ekemo gekarora ekeemba na gekaimokia ekeemba ekio na gegachaka koria achinyeke chie chibando chiria chiatigarete ase ekeemba eke. Korora iga, ebikondo binde bikarora eke kegakare koria chinyeke gioka na gotema koura egekondo kiamwabo ekeemba eke. Korende egekondo eke gekaminchoka na korina omote igoro nyuma y' ebikondo binde komoikera. N' ebikondo nabirobio mbitagete ganto kobeka mboto Egekondo eke gekaruta chinyeke inke gochia igoro, echio chiachite chikagwa kw'omogaka oyomo konye ogotire. Chinyeke echi chikamera na kwama. Aiga ase omogondo bw'omogaka oyo nigo orenge omotobu na chinyeke echi chikaama buuya, mogaka oyo nigo amenyete bweka igo endagera nigo yaichire kiage kiaye. Ase boigo, omogondo oye nigo omosinyete koburuga. Nonya nabo, tachiete komanya gose chinyeke chiamete kwaye chitari inke. Engaki yare kobwatia ye risimeka, omorakera okaba omonene ase ekenyoro eke. Abanto abange bagatara gochia ase chinse chiare erinde banyore endagera bache koria ne chiamate chiabo. Ase egonga y'abanto aba bare kogenda korigia endagera omochokoro bw'omogaka oyo nere nao arenge. Omochokoro oyo agatara, na goika ase omogaka oyo konye ogotire. Bono oogaka oyo nigo arenge kobagera abanto endagera yaye erinde baria amo ase obwanchani n'obwororo. Engaki eyemo omoiri bw'omogaka oyo akamotarera. Omogaka oyo nigo atigaretie endagera enke mono korende akabwata akamoa endagera eri yonsi yatigarete ase ekiage kiaye, na agatebia omochokoro oye buna, "Genda orosie omogondo oo buuya erinde ocha gosimeka ekiagera gochia amatuko are motwe egiateko gi'enchara nkebe" Bono emaambia yare kobwatia, omochokoro oyo akaboka akagenda mogondo ekiagera nigo atagete kogokia sokoro yaye. Kagasaine korema ase endemero, akarora chibando chiamete aiga ase orosana konye rwamerire omogondo oyo ang'e bwensi. Omochokoro bw' omogaka oyo akaburuga aiga buuya, na akarangeria sokoro yaye ache kweenekeria endagera buna yaamete buuya ase omogondo oyo. Sokoro yaye akagoka korora endagera yameete enyinge atamanyete. Bono omogaka oyo okung'untire endagera yaye yonsi pi, na koyea abaamate kobeka mboto Ekero basamorete, buna yare botambe omogaka oyo akaa eamate yaye yonsi endagera eye na gosanga ase oboamo. Nyuma y'engaki etari ntambe, embura egachaka gotwa. Bono bari bonsi bang'anyete gochia chinse chi'are bakairana nchisobo, korende nyuma batarairana omogaka oyo akabarangeria na kobasesenia aba bonsi na akabaa kera omonto chinyeke erinde bachie gosimike chinsobo. Omochokoro oyo ere agatigara na sokoro yaye erinde amorende na komoroseria endagera na kera risimeko na risamora korwa ase omogondo bw'omogaka oyo nigo riare rinyinge. Bono kera omonto ase ekenyoro, agaancha omogaka oyo.
english: These are the news: The meeting is ongoing, the school headteacher has been transferred to another school, and they say he was fired due to disagreements. However, people are saying that this happened because of those who want to cause trouble. It is said that the issue concerns the land and that people are fighting over it. The disagreement is serious, and it could escalate. This disagreement is serious and may lead to further escalation, making it difficult to resolve the matter completely. The headteacher was transferred to Osoro, and people are saying that he left because of the problems caused by those causing trouble at the school. Information from the reporter. The land belongs to Botabori, Magombo, Nyamira County. Photo and files by Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com. It is said that when someone buys land, they should check its boundaries and ensure there are no disputes, and all documents are clear. But if there is a dispute, Osoro will be involved to help resolve the boundary issues. The elders of this land have agreed to work together to find a solution and prevent future conflicts. This situation has caused anxiety among the residents, and they are worried about what might happen next. Recently, a person was attacked near Nyanchera while returning home, and the attackers were armed. Nyanchera is now very insecure, and people are afraid to walk around alone at night. But Nyanchera has been strengthened and is trying to improve security. People are saying that if anyone causes trouble, they should be arrested and taken to court. Those who attack others and destroy property will face consequences. People are working to improve security and address the issues facing the community. The youth are cooperating with the authorities, and efforts are being made to restore peace and order. As a result, the youth are becoming more responsible and contributing positively to society. However, birds continue to fly high above. In the evening, birds fly towards their nests, carrying twigs and building materials, and they sing songs praising Nyanchera, hoping that the birds will remember the good things they have seen. The rain continues to fall heavily, soaking everything and causing rivers to overflow. The water flows everywhere, destroying crops and homes, and leaving people devastated. As the rain intensifies, the rivers swell and flood the surrounding areas, washing away soil and damaging infrastructure. This leads to erosion and makes it difficult for people to rebuild their lives. And the roads are impassable due to the mud. The water carries debris and sediment, blocking roads and making them dangerous to travel on. It also damages bridges and washes away farmland, affecting food production. Birds come down and perch on trees. People say that the owner of the land is generous and kind, and that the birds bring good luck. Therefore, the landowner is respected by everyone and is known for his generosity. However, some people believe that he is hiding something. Some people have gathered to discuss their problems and find solutions. They want to ensure that everyone benefits from the development projects taking place in the area. The landowner has promised to help, and he is committed to improving the lives of the people in his community. He wants to create a safe and prosperous environment for everyone. The landowner has warned those who cause trouble, telling them to leave peacefully and return when they are ready to cooperate. But the words were ignored. But the message was not heeded, and the landowner sent someone to persuade the troublemakers to leave. Fortunately, the person succeeded in convincing them to abandon their destructive behavior. The landowner then went back home, and he regretted sending the person because he realized that he had made a mistake. The person returned empty-handed, unable to understand what had happened. However, the landowner continued to work hard to improve the lives of his people, and he encouraged them to support each other. They came together and decided to help the landowner rebuild everything that had been destroyed. After much effort, the rain finally stopped. But many people still suffered due to the damage caused by the flood, and they sought assistance from others. Eventually, they managed to convince the landowner to provide them with resources so that they could rebuild their homes and farms. The landowner remained steadfast and determined to restore order and prosperity to the region, despite facing numerous challenges. And with the help of the community, the landowner achieved his goals.

ekegusii: Amatoke A'Baba Catherine Groenewald Omogondo o'baba nigo orenge kororekana buya – nigo obwate amaemba, obori, n'emiogo. Korende ekiya ase bionsi pi biria barengeoo namataoke Nonya baba obwate abana abange, nigo namanyete buna ninche anchete ase abachokoro baye bonsi. Nigo anarete kondangeria gochia mwaye. Naende ontebia obobisi bwaye bokeboke. Nonya nigo obobisi obomo mbore atatagete gontebia: nabwo mboria bwa'se arenge gotoberia amatoke aye. Rituko erimo inkarora egekabu ki'amakendo kebekire ase omogaso isiko mwa'baba. Ekero namoboretie buna negiaki, richibu nanyorete ndiria buna: "Ekio negekabu kiane kiogokorera ebikone" Ensemo y'egekabu keria amagoma y'eritoke narengeoo anarete gonchoreria kera rituko. Inkarengereeria inkamanya komoboria, "Amagoma aya nayaki?" Richibu naende nanyorete ndiria buna, "Aya na amagoma ane y'ogokorera ebikone." Inkagoka rende korigereria magokoro, amagoma aria amo n'egekabu keria ki'amakendo. Korende baba agantoma ing'ende komokorera egasi gete. "Gaki, baba tiga indore buna okorosia." "Tiga konyogerera omwana oyo, kora buna ogotebigwa," agantebia kare buna oyobeete. Inkaminyoka ebirundo ebinene gochia gokora egiatagete. Ekero nairanete, inkanyora baba gainkaransete isiko riaye korende gekabu keria amd n'amagoma aria tibiarengeoo. "Baba ing'ai kwaira egekabu keria, ing'ai amagoma aria are, naende ing'ai." Richibu nanyorete ndiria buna, "Noo bionsi bire ase ane yogokerera ebikone." Inkaigwa bobe sana. Amatuko abere agaeta, na baba agantoma inchie komwoyeria akanyimbo kaye agatereire korwa enyomba yaye y'okorara. Yaani buna nasoete nyomba iga, inkaigwa rimisu ri'amatoke amatubo. Ase erumu eria yaime, noo egekabu keria ki'ababa kiogokerera ebikone biaye kiarengegetubire buya n'oborangeti obonene obogotu. Inkaimokereria oborangeti boria igoro ake igo nagotiokerera rimisu riria rigiya. Eriogi ria'baba rigantaborora ekero andangeretie, "Ninki ogokora imabwo? Kora bwango ondetere enyimbo yane." Inkairana bwango nenyimbo yaye. "Ninki ogosekere?" akamboria. Okoboria gokagera inkainyora buna nigo naichanete ase okomanya koria ase abisete amatoke. Rituko rikobwatia ekero baba achete minto gokwania mama, inkaminyoka gochia nyomba mwaye korigereria amatoke aria naende. Inkanyore egesabo ekemo konyora giatobire. Intatabora ritoke erimo nakobisa eyanga yane ime. Inkakuneka egekabu keria naende nagosoka. Ingaeta isuku nyuma yenyomba eria inkariria. Nigo riarenge gwansa sana, ase obogima bwane konyora tindaria itoke rigwansa igo. Rituko riria riarenge kobwatia, baba noo arenge mogondo oye akwaa ching'eni. Inkechobanesia na korigereria amatoke aria. Bono konyo ange onsi atobire. Ingasinywa gotiga kobogoria make, ingatabora amatoke ane. Ingasonsogoria ng'oora gochia ase omorangu, inkaigwa baba kagokora isiko. Inkanyara tu kobisa amatike aria eyanga yane ime nakomoetania gochia isiko. Rituko riarenge kobwatia nigo riarenge rituko riechiro. Nigo baba arenge koira amatike aye echiro koonia. Tichieti koayerera kogenda mwaye ituko erio. Korende tinyareti komoina ngaki tambe. Emarogoba eyio ekero narangeretiwe na mama, tata na magokoro, inkamanya ninki bandangereria. Obotuko obwo ekero naraire, inkamanya tinkoirorera koiba naende, ebe korwa ase magokoro gose onde bwensi. english: Father's Bananas Catherine Groenewald My father’s compound is very beautiful – it has shade, trees, and gardens. Because of this, all people come to visit my mother, and they know that I also live with my father and sometimes see the children there. She told me about her worries today. And she showed me her hands which were dirty. My mother said those hands will never be clean: because of the work she does when harvesting bananas. This story involves a disagreement between a woman and her father regarding the garden. The woman said something like this: “What the woman planted doesn’t grow well.” The woman from the garden took banana peels and started scattering them around the story. The argument continued, “Why did you take these peels?” Then she said something like this, “These are the same peels that don’t grow well.” The pot began to boil over with anger, the peels were both in the woman and in the garden. Because the father came to stop what was happening. “Listen, father, let us resolve this.” “Don’t bother the child, otherwise you will regret it,” he stopped her completely. The large flies made a lot of noise trying to interfere. I realized then, my father calmed down his temper so that the woman and the peels would calm down too. “Father, let the woman have the garden, let her have the peels, and that’s it.” Then I heard him say, “Everything is fine as long as it grows well.” The matter ended peacefully. Bananas ripened, and the father came to inspect his song which was meant to praise his house of rest. Meaning that now the house is full, the pots of bananas overflow. From that time onwards, the woman from the garden helped the father to cultivate their land together with great strength. The overflowing strength brought forth good crops. The father’s day arrived when he questioned, “What are you doing with the pots?” “Just beautifying my home,” he replied. “What are you looking for?” he asked her. To continue the story, it turned out that she knew how to plant bananas. This story begins when the father went to find his wife, the flies making noise near the house while inspecting the bananas. The woman complained about the difficulty of life. She mentioned a banana tree that had given her a small yield. The garden was ruined and she was upset. It was very difficult, and her life was hard to endure due to the poor harvest. This story continues, the father again found his compound empty. He saw his wife holding a bunch of bananas. She was busy inspecting the bananas. This is a sign of hope. The house was quiet after the previous quarrel. It was very peaceful, and her life became easier thanks to the abundant banana harvest. This story continues and is like the first story. Now the father has more bananas than ever before. They decided to share them with others. Let us remember to always be generous. These days passed and were remembered by mother, father and children, they wondered who helped them. That story ended, they realized they should thank each other, because the heart makes everything possible. ekegusii: Abwo kare kare ase ekenyoro kia Matongo, nigo Basweti amo n' Okangoko barenge abasani b' ogokumia. Ebitongwa ebi nigo bianchaine ekianda gia ikomi, na nigo abana babo bare gotiena aamo. Okangoko nigo amenyete egesera ime, korende Basweti ere ekamenya engoro ime. Bono Basweti amo n' Okang'oko nigo barenge gochia barigeria abana babo endagera korwa chinsana ime. Okang'oko nigo arenge kobiara amagena. Oomoerio oye oturagia ebichuchu. Nere Basweti nigo arenge kobiara amagena, ko oturagia chimanu chi' ebasweti. Okare gosegasega na koayerera, Okang'oko oyio kwagachia gochia korora buna erino riachandire omosani oye Engaki eyemo buna yare botambe, Basweti amo n' Okang'oko bakamanora gochia korigeria amage abo endagera. Bono ebichuchu amo n' ebimanwa bigatigara bigotiena. Aaiga, ebimwana ebi mbiarenge n' ekioge ki' orwembe. Takari gwansa! Ebimwana b' Basweti nkomena bire amanyinga Keri keri buna bakonya gotiena, emanu y' Basweti ekanyenya egechuchu gi' Okang'oko mobasokano. Korwa abwo, amanyinga agaiteka atari make, korwa ase ebigoti aria ase egechuchu kianyenyetu. Ebimanu ebi bikaoboa kerage korende bigatema chinchera ao ao erinde amanyinga gose natige goiteka, goikera bagakorera komena egechuchu eke aiga ebigoti. Bakamena egechuchu eke igo, goikera manyinga agatiga goiteka. Nonya nabo igo, nabo kware korora ase egechuchu eke kianyenyetu. Maiso a' bakungu igoro igoro, abaibori babo bagacha bare n' endagera. Kibaiika iga, ebichuchu bikare goteba ritangani buna ekiamwabo kianyenyetu kibagotiena, korende omwana bw' Basweti agakonya gotanga amanyinga goiteka. Ebimwana mbitagete goteba egento gete, korende biasinyirwe Koigwa iga, Okangoko akairaneria ebimanwa bi 'Basweti mbuya mono ase ogokonya egechuchu kiaye. Nonya nabo igo, ebimanu bi' Basweti korwa aare nabo biare kororekana buna mbiare n' eng'ana biatagete gotebia eng'ina ko bisinywa buna bigoteba. Kera oyomo akaayerera gochia ase are korara. Amatuko akanya goeta amange n'obosani bwabo bokaba bore obuya buna bware korende enchara egacha na ekaba akang'u ase Basweti konyora endagera. Amatuko amange, Basweti n'ebimanwa biaye nigo bare korara nchara. Endagera y 'Basweti nigo yare ching'iti chiri chinsinini korende eye Okang'oko nigo yare bwango konyora. Eke nakio kiagerete Okangoko ere atarenge korarera nchara. Ebimanwa bi 'Basweti omoerio oye bakarora mbuya batige kobisa eng'ina na komotebia buna amanyinga y' egechuchu gi Okang'oko nigo agotononta buya kerage ekiagera ekero erwembe yanyenyete egechuchu ebigoti igoro, nabo bayamenete bakaigwa buna agwansa. Bono Basweti eere tachia koegena ebimanwa ebi amang'ana aya y' amanyinga y'ebichuchu buna agwansa korende enchara ekaba entindi mono, goikera ebimanwa b' Basweti gokwa bitari bike. Aiga nario bono Basweti abangete aite Okang'oko, erinde anyu amanyinga aye. Baswetu agaekora buna erino riamorire, na gotoma emanwa enkogoti echi korangeria Okangoko. Emwana Enkogoti yatomirwe. Bono Okang'oko oyio okare koayerera na gosegasega, gochia gokonya Basweti Emanwa eye ekaayerera na korangeria Okang'oko. Bono Okang'oko koigwa iga, okare koayerera na gosegasega bwango, na goika ase Basweti araire. Basweti agatebia Okangoko buna amorigerie monwa oye ime arore ndino ki eri rikomwatia botuko bogakia! Basweti agaasama n' Okang'oko agatema gose narore erino erio riachandete omosani oyo oye. Nonya nabo, Okang'oko akanyora buna tari konyara korora nonya n' erino erimo. Bono Okang'oko agasoi omotwe oye ase omonwa o Basweti ime. Nare N' egesio. Kai! Kagendererete kogekeria, Okang'oko okare kominchoria na gotiga amarionya ime y' omonwa o Basweti! Kai! Basweti akagoka kerage na kobwatania omonwa oye na kong'usa ebigoti bi' Okang'oko mono. Okang'oko akang'usa na kogekeria kerage. Amanyinga agaiteka korende Basweti tachia kobutora omotwe ekiagera Okang'oko oyo nigo aminchoreti, agatiga amarionya aye ime y' monwa o' Basweti! Bono eke nakio kiagerete Okang'oko nyagotichanga atatwarereti amarionya ase ebigoti biaye, nonya ngoikera rero. Aya amwabo aya:

The things they did were spoiling the homestead, and their children didn't have peace. Okangoko knew about the bad thing, so Basweti also understood the matter well. However, Basweti and Okangoko were disturbing people, causing their children to cry a lot. Okangoko was trying to get medicine. The elders were discussing something. And Basweti was trying to get medicine, to discuss matters concerning Basweti. He walked around and kept looking, Okangoko went to disturb people again because he wanted to find someone to help him. That good day when it came, Basweti and Okangoko planned to disturb more people. However, those things and those stories became known. Truly, the stories which spread and the news reached the village. Be careful! The stories of Basweti were spreading everywhere. Because of this, the rumors started to become true, because of the words spoken, they annoyed people greatly, making them feel uncomfortable, and they began to work together to annoy people, and truly the words spread. They annoyed people, and they made rumors start to spread. Don't let it happen again, let it be like before regarding the annoyance. The eyes of the leaders looked around, their helpers went and disturbed people. It seemed that those things were happening repeatedly because they weren't being stopped, so the child of Basweti could realize and understand. The stories were not clear, so they needed explanation. It is said that Okangoko regretted the stories of Basweti that he had caused. Don't let it happen again, the stories of Basweti, sometimes they would fight and argue, but they wouldn't be clear and explained, so they continued to happen. A person who is wise should look at what will happen. The ancestors thought about their problems and how they would solve them, and the path led to Basweti realizing his mistakes. The ancestors thought carefully, Basweti and his stories were arguing about the path. The home of Basweti was very small and narrow, and the home of Okangoko was wide and spacious. But today, Okangoko refused to walk on the path. The stories of Basweti, the elders were thinking about how to stop them from speaking badly and continuing, so the rumors about the bad things and Okangoko would cease, and they would calm down and be happy. Truly, Basweti did not want to hear the stories of the past, but he wanted to understand the meaning of the stories. It seems that Basweti didn't listen to Okangoko, and he kept asking questions. Basweti worked hard and this time he understood, and he went to tell Okangoko. The story of the elder was told. Truly, Okangoko tried to explain and apologize, wanting to understand Basweti. The story was explained and understood by Okangoko. Truly, Okangoko realized and apologized greatly, and he spoke to Basweti kindly. Basweti thanked Okangoko and promised to remember everything he had learned, and he would never forget the advice of the ancestors! Basweti agreed with Okangoko and decided to work together to improve things. Don't let it happen again, Okangoko shouldn't refuse to learn and understand, and he shouldn't repeat the mistake. Truly, Okangoko felt sorry for hurting the feelings of Basweti. Now it is finished. Yes! Let us try to help, Okangoko should think and find good ways to understand the feelings of Basweti! Yes! Basweti calmed down and shared his feelings with him, and he revealed the secrets of Okangoko. Okangoko revealed and helped willingly. The understanding was strong, so Basweti decided to protect the head of Okangoko, which he had damaged, and he found good ways to understand the feelings of Basweti! Truly, I also believe that Okangoko will not waste the opportunity to understand the secrets of his people, because it is important. These are the words:

ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs XCVIII: Onye Eeri Eye Tiyarenge Goika Chiombe Chiinde Aange, Eyio Mbosa Aya amwabo aya: Buna chingaki chigendererete goonchoreria, naintwe Abagusii twagendereire goonchoreria. Ebinto bike bi' ekemira amo n' Ekegusii giaito mbigendererete gosira. Nonye ebinto bianchokire, ekerenga giato ase Gusii.com n' korika Ekegusii giato buna giakabeire, erinde nario ebigori ebiike biramanye buna twakamenyire, abwo ase chingaki echio chinkoro. Ase enchera ende, komanya aase twarwete, nario toragende n' orogendo rwaito gochia motwe, buya. Ngai tokorwa, naende ngai togochia? Koinyora buna Abagusii twakamenyire. Abagusii Otenyo Cultural Group. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti: Gusii.com files. Ase amatuko aetire, omogaka sokoro omointo nantebetie buna Abagusii ntwagatwarire ekemira ki' ebingwanso ao ao, ase amatuko amange. Ebingwanso ebi nigo biare gokorwa ase ogoikerania Ekegusii. Ase ogokora ebingwanso ebi, etugo nero yare gokorerwa ekeng’wanso. Etugo emwamu tiyarenge gokorerwa Ekegusii nonya Ase boigo, tari etugo ende yonsi yange gokorerwa Ekegusii. Yaya. Chitugo chionsi chie chirangi ao ao nigo chiare gokora ekemira, otatiga etugo eri ere emwamu. Etugo emwamu nigo yare gokorerana n’ Abaromenta, Abasigisi, gose Abagere. Kobwatekana n' omogaka sokoro, gati y' chitugo chiagakorire Ekegusii giaoto nigo chire: Embori y' Sokoro: Ase chingaki chiaetire, chisokoro chiato nigo chiare gotwara ebing’wanso ao ao. Ebing’wanso ebi nigo bare goita etugo erinde bakorerana chisokoro. Inee bono mbori ki gose yare gokorerwa ase ekeng’wanso gia sokoro? Naende nabo oraborie. Tari mbori ende yonsi. Yaya. Nigo embori yare korigigwa, eri y’ ekeng’wanso. Embori eye nigo yare koba egoree yooka. Ase boigo, nigo embori eye yare koba egoree ebegete ekobia. Egoree eye gose nereri? Egoree nyagobia neri emerete amarionya gochia motwe y’obosio, akororekana buya, buna ekobia. Goika egoree eye yarenge gotwara egesinge Komenta nayio, embori eye nigo yare gotwara ching’unchara. Naboigo, embori eye goikera yare gotwara egesinge. Bono egesinge ninki? Naende nabo oraborie. Egesinge n’ amarionya ayio are kobera mbarabare n’ amakere. Eng’encho ende, embori eye nere n’omobere omuya. Manya buna onye tebwati egesinge, igo keng’wanso ekio tikegokorwa! Emingichi y' Sokoro: Tari embori yooka yarenge gokorerwa ase Ekegusii gi' chisokoro. Emingichi nero nigo yare kong’wanswa n' chisokoro chiato ase engaki yaetire. Bono emingichi yarenge kong’wansu nero tiyare koba mingichi ende yonsi. Emingichi eye nigo yare koba ebutoire omokera! komenta nayio, emingichi eye nigo yare gotwara ching’unchara. Onye eeri eye tiyarenge goika chiombe chiinde aange na gochiaa chimori, eyio mbosa Eeri y' Geita: Eeri ya geita nigo yare koba neri ekonyori chiombe chinde chimori. Onye eeri eye tiyana goika ng’ombe ang’e erinde eyee erieme, eyio mbosa! Bure kabisa. Eeri buna eyio tiyarenge gotakerwa gokorerwa ekemira ki’Abagusii. Ase boigo, eeri eye nigo yare gotwara amagunchara, naende goika ebe eeri entangana. Eeri entang’ana neri yaakire amagasi [castrated], ekiagera nigo yare gotiokerera eng’ombe eyaberi korwa aare, yagenda koyerigia, erinde eyee erieme. Eye nigo yare gotindia na koenena, yagera yaakwa amagasi. Bono ningo orenge gokorerwa Ekegusii? Ekemira tikerigokorwa getabwati omonyene. Buna twarorire, chisokoro nchiagakoreirwe Ekegusii. Ase boigo, Onye n’omoiseke otebigwe akorerwe ekemira, nigo agokorera embori etaranyora emanwa ekiagera nere tabwati mwana. Onye n’ omongina omogotu ogokorerwa ekemira, nigo agokorerwa n’ embori rikongo, ekiagera ogotire! Onye n’omosubati ore bwoye, nigo embori egendererete konyora chimanu yarenge goitwa, erinde ekemira gekorwe. Nabo sokoro antebetie buna nabo twakamenyire igo. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.
english: Abagusii Culture And Customs XCVIII: The Person Who Knows the Eyes of Tradition Doesn't Disrespect the Clan's Land, They Respect It. This is what they say: When a custom is practiced well, we Abagusii practice it well. Few things are hidden from the knowledge of the Ekegusii people who practice them diligently. However, when things are forgotten, they are remembered through Gusii.com and learning the Ekegusii language so that when they become abundant, we may know, this is the strength of a good custom. With encouragement also, remember our ancestors, their traditions will always remain with us, come back. Why are we scattered, why aren't we united? Let's unite so that the Abagusii may know each other. Abagusii Otenyo Cultural Group. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti: Gusii.com files. Those old days have passed, the leader doesn't want to be bothered so that the Abagusii don't forget their history and customs, those old days. These customs are now being worked on so that the Ekegusii language is preserved. Those who work on these customs, this place will be used to preserve customs. This place together should be used to preserve Ekegusii and Those children, all this land should be used to preserve Ekegusii. Yes. Every custom that exists is meant to be practiced, don't abandon any custom at all. This place together is used in collaboration with the Abaromenta, Abasigisi, and all the Abagere. According to the leader, the reason why a custom is lost in Ekegusii is because: The Wealth of the Leader: In those old days, the leader's wealth was used to support customs. These customs were used to build a home where they collaborated with the leader. Is there anyone today who uses their wealth to support customs? Why don't they help. All this wealth. Yes. It is wealth that has been corrupted, it is the wealth of customs. This wealth is used to buy food and drink. Those children, this wealth is used to buy everything needed for life. What does this food mean? This food represents the blessings of our ancestors, they collaborate and return, so that life continues. The clan's food shouldn't be wasted Comment on this, this wealth is used carelessly. Also, this wealth is often wasted unnecessarily. What is unnecessary? It is the blessings that are squandered with foolishness. Therefore, this wealth needs someone responsible. Remember that if someone doesn't respect the unnecessary, then the customs of that time won't be practiced! The Secrets of the Leader: All this wealth shouldn't be used to support Ekegusii with the leader. These secrets are used with the leader's authority in those old days. What secret should be kept secret so that it doesn't reveal all the secrets? This secret is used to protect the leader's reputation! Comment on this, this secret is used carelessly. The person who knows the eyes of tradition doesn't disrespect the clan's land, they respect it. This is what they say. The Eyes of Geita: The eyes of Geita are used to see the beauty of the clan's land. The person whose eyes don't know how to respect cattle and sheep, this is what they say! Very bad. These eyes shouldn't be allowed to be misused when supporting the Abagusii people. Also, these eyes are used carelessly, why don't they look at the place where the clans meet. The meeting place is where men are castrated [circumcised], and they are taught how to care for the cows, they walk around and inspect them, and they are respected. They are given advice and told to respect the castrated ones. What about those who support Ekegusii? Tradition is being forgotten because of greed. But let us remember, the leader should be honored by the Ekegusii. Also, the person who insults others should be punished for insulting traditions, and they should learn to respect the child. The person who speaks badly about traditions, they are punished with a fine, and they learn! The person who steals from others, this wealth follows them everywhere, and they can't hide, and tradition will punish them. Let the leader decide what we should do. Mother says and thanks you for listening.
