ekegusii: 1 Chisokoro ne chisokoororia chia Yeso (Luk 3:23-38) 1Oyo noro omoroberio bw’echisokoro chia Yeso Kristo korwa ase ororeria rwa Daudi, oyio orenge korwa ase ororeria rwa Aburaamu. 2Korwa ase Aburaamu goika omorwoti Daudi akaibora Isaka, na Isaka akaibora Yakobo, na Yakobo akaibora Yuda na abamwabo, 3na Yuda akaibora Peresu na Zera ase Tamari, na Peresu akaibora Hezironi, na Hezironi akaibora Aramu, 4na Aramu akaibora Aminadabu, na Aminadabu akaibora Nashoni, na Nashoni akaibora Salimoni, 5na Salimoni akaibora Boazi ase Rahabu, na Boazi akaibora Obedi ase Rutu, na Obedi akaibora Yese, 6#2 Abar 24:14,15; 2 Amg 36:10; Yer 27:20na Yese akaibora omorwoti Daudi. Na Daudi akaibora Sulemani ase oyio orenge omokungu o Uria, 7na Sulemani akaibora Rehoboamu, na Rehoboamu akaibora Abiya, na Abiya akaibora Asa, 8na Asa akaibora Yehosafati, na Yehosafati akaibora Yoramu, na Yoramu akaibora Usia, 9na Usia akaibora Yotamu na Yotamu akaibora Ahasi, na Ahasi akaibora Hezekia, 10na Hezekia akaibora Manase, na Manase akaibora Amoni, na Amoni akaibora Yosia, 11na Yosia akaibora Yekonia na abamwabo ase chingaki chiria Abaisraeli basakoretwe na kong’anyigwa gochia Babiloni. 12Na magega ko Abaisraeli basakoirwe na kong’anyigwa gochia Babiloni Yekonia akaibora Salatieli, na Salatieli akaibora Serubabeli, 13na Serubabeli akaibora Abihudi, na Abihudi akaibora Eliakimu, na Eliakimu akaibora Azoro, 14na Azoro akaibora Zadoki, na Zadoki akaibora Akimu, na Akimu akaibora Eliudi, 15na Eliudi akaibora Eleazari, na Eleazari akaibora Matani, na Matani akaibora Yakobo, 16na Yakobo akaibora Yusufu, omosacha o Mariamu oyo oiborete Yeso, oyio okorokwa Kristo. 17Na ebigori bionsi korwa Aburaamu goika Daudi nigo biarenge ebigori ikomi na bine: na korwa Daudi goika ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa kwa Abaisraeli gochia Babiloni, n’ebigori ikomi na bine: na korwa ogosakorwa na okong’anyigwa kwa Abaisraeli gochia Babiloni goika Kristo, nebigori ikomi na bine. Okoiborwa kwa Yeso (Luk 2:1-7) 18 # Luk 1:27 Okoiborwa kwa Yeso Kristo nigo kwarenge iga: Ekero Mariamu ng’ina konya ariereirwe boko na Yusufu, na konya bataramenyana buna omosacha n’omokuungu, Mariamu akarorekana ore morito ase chinguru chi’Omoika Omochenu. 19Yusufu nigo arenge omonto omooronge, na tarigetie komoa obosooku, maiso marore, ase igo akaroberia amotige bobisi. 20Korende ekero arenge orengereretie aya, rora, omomalaika bw’Omonene akamochiera ase chindoto akamoteebia. “Aye Yusufu, korwa ase ororeria rwa Daudi, toiroka koira Mariamu abe mokao, ekiagera nigo abeire morito ase okobua kw’Omoika Omochenu. 21#Luk 1:31Ere naibore omwana omoisia, nomoroke erieta riaye Yeso, ekiagera nere oratoorie abanto baye korwa ase ebibe biabo.” 22Aya onsi nigo abeire, erinde riikerane ring’ana riria riakwanetwe n’Omonene goetera ase omonwa bw’omobani: 23 # Isaya 7:14 “Rigereria, omoiseke omwekungi nabe morito, erio aibore omwana omoisia, na erieta riaye narokwe Imanueli” (engencho yaye: Nyasae nare naintwe). 24Na Yusufu agachia kobooka korwa ase chitoro, akanywoma Mariam buna omomalaika bw’Omonene konya amoteebirie akore. 25#Luk 2:21Korende konya tibaramanyana kemobere nyuma ataraibora omwana oye omoisia. Naende Yusufu akamoroka erieta riaye Yeso.
english: 1 The genealogy of Jesus Christ (Luke 3:23-38) 1This is the record of the ancestry of Jesus Christ, son of David, descendant of Abraham. 2From Abraham came Isaac, and from Isaac came Jacob, and from Jacob came Judah and his brothers, 3and from Judah came Perez and Zerah through Tamar, and from Perez came Hezron, and from Hezron came Aram, 4and from Aram came Aminadab, and from Aminadab came Nahshon, and from Nahshon came Salmon, 5and from Salmon came Boaz through Rahab, and from Boaz came Obed through Ruth, and from Obed came Jesse, 6#2 Bar 24:14,15; 2 Chr 36:10; Jer 27:20and from Jesse came King David. And David came Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife, 7and Solomon came Rehoboam, and Rehoboam came Abijah, and Abijah came Asa, 8and Asa came Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat came Joram, and Joram came Uzziah, 9and Uzziah came Jotham, and Jotham came Ahaz, and Ahaz came Hezekiah, 10and Hezekiah came Manasseh, and Manasseh came Ammon, and Ammon came Josiah, 11and Josiah came Jeconiah and his brothers at the time they were taken captive and sent to Babylon. 12After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel, 13and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor, 14and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Akim, and Akim fathered Eliud, 15and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Mattan, and Mattan fathered Jacob, 16and Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. 17Therefore the total number of generations from Abraham to David is fourteen, and from David to the exile to Babylon, fourteen, and from the exile to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen. The Birth of Jesus (Luke 2:1-7) 18 # Luke 1:27 The birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way: Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19Because Joseph was a righteous man, he did not want to expose her to public disgrace, so he had in mind to divorce her quietly. 20But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21#Luke 1:31She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.” 22All this took place to fulfill what the Lord has said through the prophet: 23 # Isaiah 7:14 “Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel” (which means, “God with us”). 24So Joseph woke up, and did what the angel of the Lord commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25#Luke 2:21But he had no relations with her until she gave birth to her firstborn son; and he named him Jesus.

ekegusii: Thank You !! Abaminto Naende Twairaneirie Omonene Tata Nyasae, Amo Nainwe Buna Mbuya Mono Ase Kera Egento Aya amwabo aya: Thank you !! Mbuya mono ase Omonene Tata Nyasae ase ebisio amo n' ogoikerania okoba gw' ebulogi eye. Ase boigo, nigo tokoira ribaga eri ase okoiraneria buna mbuya mono, ase bari mwensi mwasangire naintwe ase ekebute eke, na kogera ebulogi eye yaikeranire iga. Twaakire buna mbuya mono, ase amauko mogotorikera, erinde gotomenta obomanyi igoro y' chinchera amo n' egekoro giaito, na gotosegeta. Mbuya mono. Ase boigo, mbuya mono gochia ase Petronillah Ogoti, ase omokia akorete bw' obotuki bw' egekoro, emerabaro, ebitandawili, amo n' chinchera chinde chionsi chiaito ntwe Abagusii. Ase eng'encho y' omokia oye, goetera 88% y' ebulogi eye nigo yaikeranire, ase eng'encho y' obotuki akorire. Eye n' emeremo emekong'u eyio ntwe totarenge gocha goikerania onye ntwabwate obotuki bonga buna obo. Mbuya mono naende. Onye gokagete buna kera egento gwakorire nase eng'echo yao aye bweka, rirorio tata noraita !! Erongori eri y' obori omorugi oo akobekeire ase egesanda egotonontera nigo egoikerana, goetera ase enchera entambe mono. Ritang'ani, Omotongi Nyasae nere ontongire endemero, na kogera omogaso obare, n' embura gotwa. Korwa abwo, goika omomura arigigwe, na koegwa ekonda korema endemero eye. Gakorire korema, goika omong'ina Bitutu arigie abangina bande, erinde bamokonye kobusura. Bono ekero obori bogenderere kwama, goika naende magokoro arigie egesangio gi'okwaga enchagwa. Aaiga, obori obo kibwamire [ Inyora Mr. Ong'eng'o - "Epwee pwee" mogondo kwao, richore nario rigotanga kobeka monu !! ] naende bogeswe, goika bwomigwe, bobongororwe, bosunyuntwe, boerwe n' oroteru, bosiegwe, boinekwe obwanga, erongori egotonontera erosigwe: Ase enchera ende, abanto n' abange bagokora emeremo, erinde aye onywe erongori eng'ansu. Tokare koganyerera erongori eng'ansu aaria bomame, Bogichoncho, Bobasi Chache yaito, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014 Mbuya mono gochia ase abang'ina n' abagaka baito Abaminto ntokweba goakera mbuya mono na koinyora abagaka amo n' abang'ina baito abange korwa nka Gusii, ase ogotoa emegano, amo n' obosemia obonge igoro y chinchera chiaito. Tiga nainwe Omonene abainyore ase emeremo eye mwakorire. Onye tari goetera ase obosemia bwaino, nanga 88% y' obotuki obo bw' Petronillah, mbwarenge gocha goikerana. Nainwe tiga Omonene agenderere kobasesenia na kobaa amatuko amange ase ense eye. Ebulogi tegoikerana, onye chingero tichiiyo. Ntwe nigo tokoinyora abateri bonsi ba Gusii ase omokia mokorete ase ogotogokia. Mbuya mono gochia ase Mr. Ong'eng'o, Abana Sungusia, Abagosabusia, omosubati Sabby Okengo, Ebiosi PAG Church Choir, Rev Douglas Otiso, Bobasi Commandos, Metamaywa Camp Choir, Nyanchonori SDA Church Choir, Nyamache Geen, Bonyakoni Kirwanda, Embarambamba, Musa Omosomba, Borangi SDA Church, Joseph Siko, Miriri Songa, Marehemu Christoper Monyoncho amo na abateri bande baito abange [ gaki tekonyarekana korika amarieta onsi igaa ]. Tiga nainwe Omonene abamentere ase emeremo eye mogokora. Naintwe Egesa FM ngotokuna ere enkoro Nchera teiyo torebe Egesa FM ase emeremo emiya bakorire ase Gusii yaito. Mbuya mono gochia ase abarari bonsi ba Egesa FM ase ogokora emeremo emiya. Amatuko ande, naintwe nabo okonyora ekero totegererete Egesa FM, twamanya gotaboria aganto gete gakwanire na gotokuna enkoro. Bono gitwakunirwe enkoro, nabo tokorika e post igoro y' aya twaigwa. Ase enchera ende, ebulogi eye tegoikerana buya, onye ntori korika ari amaya abaminto bakwanire. Omonene asesenie abarari baito bonsi ase Egesa FM. Omwaka oyo nigo orenge omonene ase omonu bw' Ekegusii. Oyo noro omwaka naintwe Abagusii twanyora Endabaro [ Endabasia ], yaito. Endabasia eye nigo yairete emiaka 12 koyerika !! Mbuya mono naende gochia ase Kennedy Bosire, amo na Gladys Machogu ase ogotwara oboremereria obonge mono. Eye nigo ere e contribution enene mono gochia ase Omogusii, eyio eratokonye gochia ase amatuko amange gochia motwe. Abaminto nabange batokuna na gotokonya ase chinchera ao ao omwaka oyo. Onye twebire onde, gaaki twasabire okwabera. Ase boigo, onye kende nkeroo totaikerania omwaka oyo ase oboriki, kamoranche twabere. Goetera ase ogwancha kw' Nyasae, tweegenire buna ntoikeranie amange ase omwaka oyo ogocha. Bono omwaka oyo goikire aange koengekana, nigo tokobasabera amaya ase kera oyomo. Tiga nainwe Omonene Nyasae abainyore na kobasesenia. Chisokoro n' Omonene Tata Nyasae oyio. Oyomino, Jared Nyabuto Nyaberi.
english: Thank You !! Our ancestors and descendants praise the great God Nyasae, and we also thank Him greatly. These are the words: Thank you !! Great God Nyasae, may He bless this book and its author. May He help us so that this book helps others, and may it be remembered forever, and may this book be useful to everyone. We accept it from our ancestors, and may it bring good things, protect knowledge from loss and destruction, and provide guidance. Great God. May He also bless Petronillah Ogoti, who wrote about customs, traditions, problems, and everything concerning the Gusii people. The quality of her writing makes 88% of this book understandable, and the quality of her research is high. And the stories she tells are very interesting and make one want to learn more. Great God and descendants. Anyone who understands what they are doing should know that this is a good thing! This story of a brave man who overcame challenges and achieved success shows how hard work pays off. Listen, children of God, let us continue to strive for excellence, and may there be peace and prosperity. Therefore, honor those who have worked hard, and respect their efforts. Because of their efforts, honor Bitutu’s family and friends, and let them avoid misfortune. This matter concerns the entire community, so let us all come together with sincere hearts to achieve progress. Indeed, this story has inspired [Mr. Ong'eng'o - “Epwee pwee” his nickname, a beautiful song that encourages perseverance!!] and continues to motivate, inspire, encourage, comfort, strengthen, heal, and empower; it has been well received: May this message spread far and wide, and may people use it to improve their lives and build a better future. Let us not forget the importance of preserving our culture, Bogichoncho, Bobasi Chache area, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014 Great God bless our families and communities Our ancestors and descendants appreciate this gift from our families and communities who work like the Gusii people, and they offer advice and wisdom regarding everything concerning our culture. We thank the great authors for writing this book. Anyone who contributes to this wisdom, including the 88% contribution of Petronillah, deserves recognition. We pray that the great God will continue to guide and bless our heritage. This blog is informative, and it provides valuable insights. We should remember all the sons and daughters of Gusii who strive to maintain our traditions and customs. Great God bless Mr. Ong'eng'o, Abana Sungusia, Abagosabusia, musician Sabby Okengo, Ebiosi PAG Church Choir, Rev Douglas Otiso, Bobasi Commandos, Metamaywa Camp Choir, Nyanchonori SDA Church Choir, Nyamache Geen, Bonyakoni Kirwanda, Embarambamba, Musa Omosomba, Borangi SDA Church, Joseph Siko, Miriri Songa, the late Christopher Monyoncho and others too numerous to mention [whose names I cannot recall at this moment]. We thank the great God for inspiring them to write this book. We also praise Egesa FM for its dedication I commend Egesa FM for supporting the efforts of the Gusii people. Great God bless all the presenters at Egesa FM for promoting our culture. With your support, we believe that Egesa FM will continue to thrive and provide quality programming. This commitment has earned them respect, and we appreciate their contributions. May this message spread far and wide, and may this blog be remembered forever, so that no one forgets the important role played by dedicated individuals. May God bless all the presenters at Egesa FM. That year was a significant one for the Ekegusii language. It was the year we wrote Endabaro [Endabasie], indeed. This Endabasie took 12 years to compile!! Great God also bless Kennedy Bosire, and Gladys Machogu for their tireless efforts and immense contribution to the Gusii community, which greatly benefited our children. Many people came together and collaborated during that year. Let us remember, because we prayed for success. Therefore, let no one forget the challenges faced that year; we overcame them. Through the grace of God, we have been able to achieve much this year. This year has brought many changes, and we pray for continued progress. We thank the great God for hearing our prayers and answering them. Glory to the Almighty God. Sincerely, Jared Nyabuto Nyaberi.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abwo kare kare, ase ekenyoro kia Nyanchwa, ebigoro mbiarenge aroro. Bono ebigoro ebi nigo biagiteire ime y’emete emenge, eyio yameete naende yarenge kororekana buya. Abamenyi be ebigoro ebi nigo bamenyete n’ omogoko amo n’omorembe omonene. Emaambia eyemo, abanto be ekegoro ekemo bagakumia ase aya baroche. Ase ekegoro ekemo, omote norenge oyomo bwamete na koba omotambe kobua emete yonsi pi ase ebigoro ebi bionsi biabebekaine aaiga. Omote oyo ogakina okaba swanya Ebisabo bi’ omote oyo nigo biasabogete, goikera bikaama na koba ebitambe mono ase chinsemo chionsi pi. Chinsagi chi’ omote oyo nigo chiarenge buna emete ende, eri yamete aiga ase ekegoro eke gose ebigoro biri binde biabebekaine aiga. Ase boigo, amato y’ omote oyo akaama na koba amanene kegima, goikera agatanga omogaso togoika ase amaraba gose obonyansi. Omote oyo okairera ekiriri ekenene gocha aiga, goikera ekegoro ekegima omosunte okabwata omonene. Bono ebimeri ao ao bikaba mbiri komera na koama ase eng’encho mbiare konyora omogaso erinde obimente chinguru biame ase botoereru. Ebimeri ebinge bigakwa, goikera egeateko gi' enchara gekarorekana koba ang’e. Nonya nabo igo, ching’iti chi’ orosana chirochio nchibwate obosubore n’ omogoko ekiagera nigo chiare koria amato aya, ayio arenge gosaboka bogakia. Bono Abanto ba Nyanchwa bagatwara obwoba n’ omote oyo. Bakanya korigia chinchera ao ao barayogechere, ekiagera omote oyo konye obeire omonene kerage. Abamenyi aba bakaigwana bayogeche gose mbache gokonyeka, nyuma enchara etarabaita korwa ase ekegoro eke. Bono emaambia eyemo, bagaturana, na gochaka koyogecha. Bakayogecha bokaira na koirana riakagororoba chinsobo, ase baragerete na gotimoka korwa ase emeremo emekong’u bakorete rituko rigima. Kai! Mote oyo tori kororekana gose nogechetwe. Aankio yaye, bakairana kogenderera kogecha omote oyo korende bagakumia ekiagera banyorete omote oyo naende bwamire torikororekana gose nogechetwe rituko ria igoro yaye! Bagaichana korende bagachaka koyogecha. Abamenyi ba Nyanchwa Hill: Ntwe nigo totagete kobutora omote oyo, erinde toagache chinyomba ase tokomenya. Korigereria korwa Kisii Town gochia aaria beautiful Nyanchwa Hill. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files. Bono ekero bwairete aba bakairana chinsobo buna yarenge botambe, bakaboka rituko rinde na kogenda ase omote oyo na konyora naende bwamire anene kobua buna bayotigete! Bagakumia na goichana mono kerage. Aya akaba kagokorekana ase amatuko atari make, goikera engaki baruseti moyo buna omote oyo tobwenereti gokunwa. Bagateba buna nigo ogotigwa igo, bwame goikera kaa ase oratigere kwama. Bono buna babwatete amakere na gotenena bayosonchete, Okanyoni oyomo akairuruka goocha ase barenge. Okanyoni nabwate eng'ana Okanyoni oyo nigo arenge omosiniini mono batare koyemanya buna n' Oknyoni ki orenge. Okanyoni oyo akabakwanera korende as’ eng’encho aba barenge n’ obororo obonge, tibachia komokwanera ekiagera nigo bayechayete buna tayarenge n’amang’ana arabakonye nonya n’ asinini. Korende Okanyoni ere tachieti korusia moyo kobakwanera. Akagenderera kobatebia buna "Timoseka. Aya nkobatebia nigo are y’e ng’encho na nigo arabakonye ase anene kegima motaregokagera. Nche ninde n’ obokonyi n’ obobisi bw’ omote oyo obanchandire emiaka emenge" Bono abanto aba bagakumia na gokira erinde bategerere aya Okanyoni oyo abwate. "Okaobori nere obanchandire ase amatuko aya onsi. Ekero mogokora kogecha nigo Okaobiri arenge gocha, omena ase mware gwatia erinde omote oyo osaboka obotuko obogima! Nigo Okaobiri atagete omote oyo onyakoba aroro ekiagera nigo okomokonya kwebisera ababisa baye erinde obatwara na konyora endagera yaye yak era rituko" Okanyoni akagenderera okobatebia abamenyi b' Nyanchwa buna "Ekero mwainokire, nere buya mwatiga ebisire aroro na nigo mogwatia mwatiga aria ase atieriri arori igoro, erinde kogocha komena omote egesire kenyenye oromeme rwaye" Ekero Okanyoni akoora goteeba amangana aya, abanto ba Nyanchwa bakaigwa buya na koirana chinsobo. Kobwakia emaambia yaye, bagacha n’ ebisire bitieriri bigaika na bagachaka goatia omote oyo ong’ana swanya. Amamocho mono ase Okaobiri komena omote. Bono onyenyire oromeme rwaye rwensi pi! Ekero riagororobete, aba bagatiga ebisire ase omote naaria ase atieriri akaroria igoro erinde bakagenda chinsobo. Buna botambe ere, Okaobiri agacha na kong’ea komena omote oyo. Keri keri, Okaobiri agachacka komena buna botambe na konyenya oromeme rwaye na korobutora! Okaobiri akaigwa obororo, n' amanyinga agaiteka atari make. Okaobiri korora iga, agatiachoria n' chimbero chimbariri, tachia koirana rinde aiga. Korwa abwo, mote oyo tochieti gosaboka. Abamenyi b' Nyanchwa bakayogecha igo, goikera okagwa nse, n omogoko ogaichora ase abanto abwo bachagete gosimeka chindagera chikaama.
english: These are the words: Long ago, in the days of Nyanchwa, the hyenas were very numerous. These hyenas would often raid the interior of the homesteads, which caused great suffering and endless lamentation. Those who understood the ways of the hyenas knew their tricks and their immense power. In those times, people of the homesteads gathered together because of this matter. Because of the homesteads, they agreed that everyone should contribute something towards buying medicine to protect all the homesteads from harm. That thing was considered important. The expenses of that thing were met, through contributions from each family and by giving gifts from everything available. The reputation of that thing grew greatly, so that the homesteads and all the hyenas that had been causing harm were protected. And also, the strength of that thing increased and became very powerful, through offering respect and avoiding bad talk about all the homesteads. That thing brought great peace and prosperity, making the homesteads flourish abundantly. However, some things happened repeatedly and remained a concern, causing great hardship and bringing sorrow to the people. Other things were discovered, leading to investigations to find out what was happening. Nevertheless, despite all this, the secret of the ordeal remained hidden and its power continued to grow, so that these matters could be resolved and problems overcome. And the people of Nyanchwa feared that thing. They planned various strategies and discussed them extensively, hoping that this thing would bring lasting peace. Those knowledgeable individuals spoke truthfully, so that the truth about the homesteads would be revealed. However, in those times, they traveled and consulted widely. They spoke about going and returning during the evening, and they rejoiced and worked hard on the tasks they had undertaken. Indeed! That thing will continue to bring peace to all generations. Truly, they went around exploring this thing thoroughly, gathering information to understand how this thing works and why it continues to bring peace to future generations! They deliberated thoroughly and consulted widely. The people of Nyanchwa Hill said: We will not allow this thing to be lost, lest we lose our identity and knowledge. Let us return to Kisii Town to visit the beautiful Nyanchwa Hill. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files. And so, those who went around realized that they should not give up, but persevere and continue to explore this thing and ensure that it remains strong enough to last forever! They gathered and deliberated further. These words spread throughout the land, leading to respect and understanding, so that people would not underestimate the importance of preserving this thing. They believed that if it were forgotten, it would be like losing a precious treasure. But if they remembered and cherished it, birds would fly high above, rejoicing. Birds flew swiftly. That bird is known for its speed, but people don't know what makes it so fast. This bird helped those who needed assistance, offering support and encouragement, but some doubted its ability because of its small size. Therefore, the bird decided to demonstrate its strength and resilience. It declared, “I will show you. Today I will reveal my power and prove that I can overcome any obstacle. I am also capable of carrying heavy burdens across vast distances.” And so, the people gathered to witness the bird's demonstration. “This is a testament to the strength of our ancestors. The secret to success lies in perseverance, dedication, and unwavering commitment. If this bird can achieve such feats, then we too can overcome challenges and build a prosperous future!” The bird continued to proclaim to the people of Nyanchwa, “My friends, remember this lesson: always strive for excellence and never settle for mediocrity. Work diligently and tirelessly, and let your efforts bear fruit for generations to come.” And so, the bird completed its mission, leaving the people of Nyanchwa inspired and motivated. To commemorate this event, they held celebrations and shared stories, ensuring that the memory of this remarkable bird would endure. But Okaobiri alone remained focused on the task. And indeed, his wisdom shone brightly! After much deliberation, they began working on the task together, striving for excellence and achieving great results. But alas, Okaobiri stumbled and fell while attempting the task. However, he quickly recovered and persevered, refusing to give up! Okaobiri was exhausted, and his limbs were aching, but his spirit remained unbroken. Okaobiri rose again, strengthened by determination, and continued his journey with renewed vigor. From that moment forward, the task became easier. The people of Nyanchwa rejoiced, realizing that through unity and collaboration, they could accomplish anything, and their community flourished like never before.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Magokoro nigo agoteba nga konyora Omosongo ataraika Gusii, kera enyomba ase Abagusii yabwate omogambi. Nigo magokoro agoteba ng'a Omongeresa nigo aigete ase erwenyi ya seito Gusii ase omwaka 1893. Ekero ekio kio ogoika nka Gusii, abagambi ba Abagusii nigo barenge buna ekobwatia: 1.Bonchari: Omogaka Okongo nere orenge omorwoti aaria Bonchari yaito ekero Omosongo agoika Gusii. 2.Bogirango Irianyi (South Mugirango): Omogaka Kereu nere orenge kogamba Bogirango Irianyi yaito ko Omosongo agoika Gusii. 3.Bomachoge: Omogaka Nyamosi nere obete omorwoti o Bomachoge yaito ase engaki eyio. 4.Bobasi: Omogaka Nchore nere orenge kogamba aaria Bobasi yaito ase engaki eyio. 5.Nyaribari: Omogaka Nyamwamu nere orenge kogamba ase Nyaribari yaito ko Omosongo agoika Gusii. 6.Bogirango Sugusu (North Mugirango): Omogaka Ndubi nere orenge kogamba aaria Bogirango Sugusu yaito. 7.Bogetutu (Kitutu): Ase ekenyoro kie Enda y' Enchogu, omogaka Angwenyi ominto nere orenge omorwoti aaria Bogetutu yaito ko Omosongo agoika Gusii. Korende obogambi bwo omogaka Angwenyi aaria Bogetutu needs special attention. Ase ki? This is because at the time, omogaka Angwenyi nigo arenge kogamba in the entire area ya Getembe (Bosongo) eyio Omosongo arierete obote, naende atagete koira. Tari igo rioka, Baba nigo agoteba buna Omosongo nigo arierete Gusii yonsi obote. "Nigo Omosongo arierete Gusii yonsi obote" Magokoro baba ominto, Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, Ichuni, Kisii County: Picture na PETRONILLA OGOTI, Mwanyagetinge.com/2011 Ense ya Gusii entobu Omongeresa nigo aigete Getembe akanyora ense entobu, naende ebwate embeo engiya. Nonya nabo igo, akanyora nga tari ere Omosongo omotangani goika Gusii. Yaya. Konyora Omojeremani oikire Gusii before him. Bono, Omongeresa akanyora ng'a kumbe konyora Omojeremani otang'anire goika Bosongo (eyio naende ekorokwa Getembe). Ogosakora kwa Nyabitabo Buna baba agoteba, Omongeresa amo no Omojeremani bakarwana esegi. Korwa abwo, Omojeremani agatama gochia Tanzania (eyio yarenge korokwa Tanganyika at the time). Ekero eke, abanto bagasakora ebinto biokoriera endagera. Engaki eyio ekarokwa engaki ye Enyabitabo. Engaki eyio, omogaka narenge aroro ore korokwa Gasuko, oyio orenge Omosoba (Suba) naende omokirimani bwo Omongeresa. Gasuko agatebia Omongeresa buna omogaka Angwenyi nere ore kogamba ase ensemo eyio ya Getembe. Nche tinkogamba ne ritoto! Omongeresa agataka bagambe na Angwenyi korende Angwenyi akaanga buna takogamba ne ritoto! Gasuko akaebereria Angenywi ekero Omongeresa abegete eema yaye bweri gati! Omogambi Angwenyi agasoka na kogamba no Omongeresa ore korokwa Nyarigoti. Omogambi Angwenyi akabekerwa rirangeti ribariri buna a uniform. Nyuma ye emetienyi etano Angwenyi agateba nga natagete gotigera omwana oye obogambi bwa Getembe. Gati ya abana bo omogaka Angwenyi abamura mbarengeo babere. Abamura bo omogambi Angwenyi: Ooga no Onsongo Omomura omonene nere orenge korokwa Ooga. Omomura onde omokogoti nere ore korokwa Onsongo. Angwenyi nigo atagete Onsongo agambe, korende Gasuko nigo atagete Ooga. Gasuko agatebia Ooga buna ise ochorire Onsongo agambe, korende nabo bagoonchora obogambi obo magega yo okorwa chiombe emerengo ene. Abakungu emerongo ene: Chiombe emerongo ene. Ooga narenge na abakungu emeronge ene. Akarusia engombe eyemo korwa kera ase omokungu mpaka chigaisana akaa Gasuko. Ekero Nyarigoti are kobekera omogambi egutwa omosangererekano okarangerigwa na Angwenyi. Gasuko ongainire Nyarigoti Kera oyomo namanyete buna Onsongo nkobekerwa arenge egutwa. Nyarigoti ga koboria gose abanto mbanchete Ooga, abanto basungusia emetwe. Gasuko akamanya kongaina Nyarigoti buna ogosungusia omotwe nakwo ogwanchera Ooga agambe! Ooga akabekerwa ekerauni kio oborwoti. Angwenyi agaichana na koigwa bobe, korende egesaku kio Ooga gekaragererwa misi. Next In This series: How It all Started, Part I: Omogano Bwa Abagusii
english: These are their stories: The heart says that when Omosongo arrived in Gusii land, the people of Abagusii accepted his intentions. The heart also says that Omongeresa led him to the customs of the Gusii people in the year 1893. That event became known as Gusii, and the leaders of Abagusii agreed on four things: 1.Bonchari: Chief Okongo and others from the Bonchari region acknowledged that Omosongo had come to Gusii. 2.Bogirango Irianyi (South Mugirango): Chief Kereu and others from Bogirango Irianyi stated that Omosongo had come to Gusii. 3.Bomachoge: Chief Nyamosi and others from Bomachoge confirmed this matter. 4.Bobasi: Chief Nchore and others from the Bobasi region affirmed this matter. 5.Nyaribari: Chief Nyamwamu and others from Nyaribari stated that Omosongo had come to Gusii. 6.Bogirango Sugusu (North Mugirango): Chief Ndubi and others from Bogirango Sugusu confirmed this. 7.Bogetutu (Kitutu): From the council of elders of Enda and Enchogu, Chief Angwenyi and others from the Bogetutu region stated that Omosongo had come to Gusii. Therefore, the leadership of Chief Angwenyi in the Bogetutu area requires special attention. Why is this? This is because at that time, Chief Angwenyi was the leader throughout the entire Getembe (Bosongo) area where Omosongo first settled, yet he did not understand anything. It wasn't long before people said that Omosongo had conquered all of Gusii. “Omosongo conquered all of Gusii” – words of the elder Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, Ichuni, Kisii County: Photo by PETRONILLA OGOTI, Mwanyagetinge.com/2011 The history of Gusii begins Omongeresa led Getembe and wrote down the history, and it spread widely. However, some say that he didn't write about Omosongo coming to Gusii. Indeed, German administrators were present in Gusii before him. But, Omongeresa wrote so that it would be remembered that the Germans came to Bosongo (which is now called Getembe). The incident at Nyabitabo People say that Omongeresa and the German administrators fought a battle. After that, the Germans fled to Tanzania (which was then called Tanganyika). As a result, people began to tell different versions of events. This story is known as the story of Nyabitabo. In that story, the chief refused to allow anyone to settle in Gasuko, including the Suba people, and the followers of Omongeresa. Gasuko supported Omongeresa, but Chief Angwenyi refused to let them settle in the Getembe area. What will you say now?! Omongeresa asked them to speak with Angwenyi, but Angwenyi refused to speak with them! Gasuko pleaded with Angwenyi, but Omongeresa managed to get a piece of land there anyway! Chief Angwenyi eventually agreed to speak with Omongeresa regarding settling in Nyarigoti. Chief Angwenyi was arrested and imprisoned because of his uniform. Later, five days later, Angwenyi escaped while trying to reach his child concerning the matter of Getembe. Many of Chief Angwenyi’s children scattered and disappeared. Angwenyi’s children: Ooga and Onsongo The eldest son was from Ooga. The younger son was from Onsongo. Angwenyi sent Onsongo to speak, but Gasuko sent Ooga instead. Gasuko supported Ooga, but they also told Onsongo to speak, saying that they should investigate the matter thoroughly and find out what happened. The elders of that matter: What happened during that matter. Ooga had those elders with him. He chased away the cow that had been grazing near Gasuko’s territory until it reached a disagreement. Then Nyarigoti decided to arrest the chief who was causing trouble and was being influenced by Angwenyi. Gasuko wanted to help Nyarigoti Long ago, everyone knew that Onsongo was arrested. Nyarigoti gathered all the people except Ooga, people who lowered their heads. Gasuko realized that helping Nyarigoti meant lowering one’s head too, just like Ooga did! Ooga was arrested and taken to court. Angwenyi rejoiced and said that the situation with Ooga was resolved. Next In This series: How It all Started, Part I: The History of the Gusii People

ekegusii: Emegano Y' Abagusii XXXVI: Bakungu Mbatakeiri Koria Amabere Y’ Eng’ombe, Emori Etaramera Amaino A Igoro! Aya amwabo aya: Abwo kare kare, omogaka oyomo narengeo na mokaye, ase ekenyoro kia Bomariba. Bono omogaka oyo nigo arenge korokwa Mogire. Na mokaye nigo arenge korokwa Nyaboke. Mogire na mokaye, omongina Nyaboke nigo barenge n’ bana batano. Abamura babere ne chinyaroka isato. Ekero enyaroka enkogoti yarenge emiaka etano, enchara enene egaateka ase ekenyoro eke kia Bomariba. Embura ekaba engaki etambe etari gotwa, n' morakera ogacha omotindi kegima. Ase boigo, chindooche chionsi chikooma pi, n' emete ne ebimeri bikooma. Komenta nayio, etugo ekarea bobe mono mbaka ekang’ea gokwa mono. Abanto ba Bomariba bagachandeka kegima, ase enchara kobaita. Ase engaki eye, chingige nachirochio chigaacherera abamenyi aba ba Bomariba. Bono chingige echi nachirochio chikamenta emechando ase emechando ende. Ko obokongu bwaba obonge, ogosemeria gokaera ase abamenyi aba. Bono bakaganya ogokwa ekiagera baganyete embura ase amatuko amange goika bakarosa. Bono omogaka oyo Mogire agachandeka kerage ase eng’encho arenge n’ eamate enene, eyio arenge korageria. Bono egasi yaye nigo yarenge ogotimoka gwoka. Ase boigo, kera oyomo ase abanto baye, natageta aigote. Bono omogaka Mogire akarosa korigeria eamate yaye. Akaba tari kogenda gotwara erinde anyore kende arentere eamate yaye eche koria. Nyaboke agachia komosegeta agende buna abagaka bande bare kogenda korigeria chiaamate chiabo, Mogire ere akaanga pi, kagotimoka abwo ase enka yaye. Mogire akaba gakobera nyomba, na Nyaboke ogenda korigeria abana endagera. Bono abana aba ba Mogire nigo bare korora buna abaise ba abasani babo bare kogenda korigia endagera ya abana babo, babaretera baria. Abana aba nabarabwo bakagania ng'a ise omwabo nere agende kobarigeria endagera ekiagera ng’ina tare korenta endagera ekobaisana. Engaki eyemo, Nyaboke akaba kagosiria ogosemeria gw’ okorageria eamate eye yaye. Bono agatiana ng'a tarageria omogaka oyo oye Mogire otare korwa nyomba, oganyererete arenterwe endagera na Nyaboke, omanya goansa koinagera. Bono omogaka oyo Mogire nigo amenyete saiga mwaye. Bono ng'ai mwaira amabere n' obonyansi bwakabucha iga? Mabere tarengeo akonywegwa. Emete amo n' obonyansi biakinire aaria Bomariba. Picture na special correspondent, Bomariba. Gusii.com files. "Ndagera tiyarengeo, ekoriegwa" Nyaboke. Nyaboke agachaka korosia endagera, na koyebisa. Nigo arenge koria n’ abana baye, takoirera Mogire kende aaria saiga mwaye. Nyaboke akaba kagotoma omomura oye gochia ase ise amenyete saiga na komotebia ng'a ndagera yarenge ekoriegwa! Bono Mogire akaba gakorara nchara ase amatuko atari make. Mogire agachaka gotwara chitang’utang’u buna nigo bare komong’aina. Bono akagenda ase abagisangio baye na kobatebia aya y’ okoba n' nchara ase amatuko amange. Abagisangio baye koigwa igo, bakamotebia buna eamate yaye nigo ekomong’aina. Mogire akagechigwa kerage na gotiana gokora egesiomba gochia ase omorugi oyo oye. Engaki eye embura egachaka gotwa kemonyiriro. Korwa abwo, ekaba enyinge n’endagera egachaka gosaboka. Ase boigo, obonyasi bokaama. Bono chiombe chikanyora endagera chikori, n' amabere akabucha mono. Mogire bono nere akagoka ekero eng’ombe yaye yaiyeretie emori! "Ayie! Timosaria na goturutumba ekemira. Bakungu mbatakeiri koria amabere y’ eng’ombe, emori etaramera amaino a igoro!" Mogire. Koyaiyeria emori, Mogire agatebia omorugi oye buna ase ekemira kiabo, bakungu mbatakeiri koria amabere y’ eng’ombe, emori etaramera amaino a igoro! Akamotebia buna takoyariera, ase eng'encho araturutumbe ekemira. Obwango obo nabwo Nyaboke ainyorete buna are gokorera Mogire engaki eri enchara yabetete inse aaiga Bomariba. Kare n' amarimu, Nyaboke akaimoka rituko riare kobwati rimaambia echuni n’ abana baye bari bare abake na kogenda sobo boiborwa. Gaaika sobo boiborwa, agatebia ise aya Mogire atagete komokorera. Bono Nyaboke akarara abwo sobo kabere. Rituko ria gatato, ise n’ abasani baye bakaimoka kwagachia gochia o Nyaboke erinde bagayane aya Mogire atagete gokora. Mogire na Nyaboke oye baanchanire na komenya n' omorembe Mogire akagoka korora Nyaboke oiranire korende ageekora koigwa bobe buna Nyaboke achiete sobo. Bono abagaka bagaikaransa na koyakwanera aya are gocha goetani eamate eye ya Mogire na Nyaboke. Omoerio oye Mogire agaancherana gotiga mokaye tanywa amabere y’ eng’ombe na koaberana korwa ase onsi aria konyora aetire. Eeamate ya Mogire egatigara kemenyete n’ omogoko n’ omorembe korwa erio.
english: The Story of the Gusii XXXVI: The Herdsmen Who Milked the Cow, The Warrior Who Conquered the Land of Igoro! These are their stories: Long ago, a man named Oyomo had a wife, who lived near the place of Bomariba. This man was known as Mogire. And his wife was known as Nyaboke. Mogire and his wife, mother Nyaboke, had five children. The people were blessed with abundant harvests. This beautiful story lasted for five years, a large gathering took place near the place of Bomariba. The rain that fell was good and sufficient, and the millet grew well. Because of this, everyone was happy, and the food and drinks were plentiful. Comment on this, a house built beautifully until it reached completion. The people of Bomariba rejoiced greatly, because of the large harvest. And today, the celebration continues to attract visitors from Bomariba. But this celebration sometimes causes problems and conflicts. So when there is a disagreement, someone mediates among the visitors. But they agreed to share the harvest equally, so that no one would be left behind. And this man Mogire rejoiced greatly, because he had many possessions, which were being increased. But his last act was to become very generous. And because of this, long ago and the people of those days, he showed kindness. But this man Mogire decided to distribute his possessions. He could not bear to see anyone suffer while he had plenty. Nyaboke encouraged him to continue helping others, and Mogire agreed to do so, remembering his past. Mogire began to build houses, and Nyaboke went to distribute the children amongst them. And these children of Mogire decided to return to their mothers, so that their fathers could also distribute gifts to their children, sharing with them. These children then gathered together, saying that they should go and help distribute the gifts equally, so that no one feels neglected. Today, Nyaboke decided to oversee the distribution of her own possessions. But she wondered whether to tell this man, Mogire, not to build houses, but instead to share everything with Nyaboke, so that there would be unity. But this man Mogire understood her intentions. But why does milk and witchcraft cause trouble? Milk that has soured is wasted. Food and witchcraft have spread throughout Bomariba. Picture and special correspondent, Bomariba. Gusii.com files. “Harvests are not enough, they are stolen” Nyaboke. Nyaboke decided to protect the harvest, and she succeeded. She shared it with her children, leaving nothing for Mogire at all. Nyaboke was able to provide for her family, and she declared that harvests are not enough! But Mogire started to feel sorry for his relatives who were poor. Mogire decided to start working hard so that they could all benefit. But he went to his friends and asked them to help him with his work and his relatives. His friends agreed to help, promising that his possessions would increase. Mogire was surprised and happy to hear this from his friend. Today, rain fell and the land became fertile. When this happened, it was a sign that the harvest would be plentiful. Because of this, witchcraft disappeared. This tree grew tall, and its leaves provided shade. Mogire realized that he had made a mistake when he mistreated his cows! “Oh! We will celebrate and dance with joy. Let the elders milk the cows, and let the milk flow like a river!” Mogire. He continued to praise the cows, Mogire thanked his friend for helping him, and said that the elders should milk the cows, and let the milk flow like a river! He promised that he would not forget, and that he would always remember his friend. The respect that Nyaboke had for him increased, and she helped Mogire today with the work that had been left unfinished since the time of Bomariba. Now and forever, Nyaboke remembered the lesson about sharing with her children and going to visit her relatives. Going to visit her relatives, she reminded him of what Mogire had failed to do. But Nyaboke woke up that morning and remembered everything. The lesson of that day, she and her daughters remembered how Nyaboke protected them from Mogire’s neglect. Mogire and Nyaboke then reconciled and lived peacefully. Mogire decided to return Nyaboke’s kindness by doing whatever she wanted so that Nyaboke would be satisfied. But people gathered and wondered why they were unable to achieve the prosperity that Mogire and Nyaboke had achieved. Their secret was that Mogire always shared his milk with others and treated everyone fairly. Mogire’s wealth increased with peace and harmony because of this action.

ekegusii: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Amaumuntia (May) 26, 2012. Chinyomba chio Omogusii: Aya amwabo aya: Ntwaroche nga aaiga Egesumu (Kisumu), nao ng'ina Mogusii [ omongina Nyakomisaro oyio naende orenge korokwa Nyakomogendi ] asirerete. Ase boigo, ntwatebetigwe buna omwana o Mogusii okorokwa Orechi (Enswe ase Ekegere), nao anyoreretwe aaiga Egesumu. Ase okogenderera gotebigwa omogano oyo oito, temanyekanetie gose Orechi ere nigo atigarete aaiga Egesumu ase okonganya konde gwaito, na gotwara ororeri rwaye aroro, gose nigo asirerete aroro. Erieta "Kisumu" n' rie Ekegusii. Twaikire Downtown, City Of Kisumu [Egesumu]. Tiga tosike omochie o Kisumu. Aaaiga nao esokoro yaito enene, Mogusii asirerete. Ase boigo, aaiga nao ng'ina Mogusii, [ magokoro oito omonene Nyakomisaro, oyio naende ore korokwa Nyakomogendi ] asirerete. Ase okogenderera n' omogano oyo oito, nigo togotebigwa buna abamura ba Mogusii baria banganyete korwa Egesumu nigo barenge batano na babere. Orechi ere tari gokwanwa ase achiete. Bono nigo togotebigwa ng'a Mogusii narenge ne chinyomba isano na ibere buna ekobwatia. Chinyomba echio nigo chire: [I]. Mogusero: Mosinto Omogusii omomura omonene, nigo arenge korokwa Mogusero. Mogusero nigo aiboretwe n' omongina Mokeira Bwari, oyio orenge oyomo bw abangina batano b' Mogusii. Omomura oyo Mogusero nere otang'ete komena egesero mogondo! Komenta nayio, Mogusero nere naende togotebigwa orenge korokwa Sereti. Abana b' Mogusii nigo barenge buna ekobwatia: Ase okounenkia omogano oyo oito, temanyekanetie gose Mogusero ere nayorete enyomba yaye buna Monyaribari gose Mobasi, konyora atarasira gose nigo asirete bogesi. Nonya nabo igo, ekero tokobwatia abana ba Mogetutu, Abagusero mbareo. Omwana oyo o' Mogetutu okorokwa Mogusero nabo erabe ng'a nigo nigo aetwe erieta ria ise moke [ Mogusero oyio konyora osiriore magega ]. [II]. Omogetutu: Ase abana ba Mogusii baria baigete kwamboka korwa Egesumu gocha ase ebitunwa bia Gusii na gochia motwe, Mogetutu nere omomura omonene. Omogetutu gose Mogetutu Mw' Nyakundi ere nigo arogetwe iga korwa ase omongina Mogoisera oyio otamete. Bono Mogoisera nigo arenge otare konyora bamura. Ekabetereria ng'a omongina Mogoisera [ mosubati omwabo Gichana ] goika anywome omoiseke oyio oramonyorere omwana. Ekero omosubati oyo anyora omwana, akamonengeta ng'a " Na aganto g' Enkundi...Agatutu". Omwana oyio akarokwa Mogetutu Mwanyakundi. [III]. Mogirango: Mogirango ere nigo arogetwe iga ase engecho y' omongina Bwoisera ore koanga koria engo koyaitirwe. Omongina oyo ere nigo are kogira na gokana pi pi pi buna takoria engo. Gachia konyora omwana bakamoroka buna Gendabu Mw' Mogirango Okogira Engo. Bono aba bakarokwa Abagirango gose "Bakogira engo". [IV]. Monyaribari: Nyaribari amagenga rende barabuo ninki barokeretwe iga? Abamura ba Nyaribari abagaka na abana babo kibare kogenda esegi yo oroari rwa Sigisi na Gusii nigo bare gotanga Mosigisi taira chiombe chia Gusii bakarokwa Nyaribari Amangenga. [V]. Mobasi: Ababasi nigo baitete eng'era na koyebasa korwa omogongo rika bare koyenyenya korwa ritana. Bakarokwa Ababasi. [VI]. Momachoge: Abamachoge rende? Omwana omoiseke Bwoisera akagenda Bomachoge rinani ime. Buna togotebigwa, eng'oge ekamonyoria omwana akarokwa Machoge Osweta Ngoge. [VII]. Monchari: Bonchari na abana b' omosubati o Mogusii orenge korokwa Kebenchari. Omosubati oyo Kebenchari nigo asogete Bogere, korende magega yaye akairana nka Gusii. Ororeria rw' Kebenchari narwo rokorokwa Abanchari.
english: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Dated May 26, 2012. The story of Omogusii: These are the words: It happened that when he went to Kisumu, and there was a person from Gusii [ this Nyakomisaro who always likes being praised by Nyakomogendi ] he became angry. After that, he was asked to be circumcised like a child of Gusii in Orechi (the place near Ekegere), and he refused to go to Kisumu. And because of this matter which caused great trouble, it wasn’t understood by Orechi until he agreed to go to Kisumu and carry his belongings, and take his cattle with him, so that he could become angry again. “Kisumu” is also in the Gusii language. We arrived Downtown, City Of Kisumu [Kisumu]. There were many people in Kisumu. People went there in large numbers, Gusii became angry. After that, people and a person from Gusii, [ whose heart is very big Nyakomisaro, who always likes being praised by Nyakomogendi ] became angry. And because of this matter which caused great trouble, it wasn’t decided that the elders of Gusii should meet in Kisumu and discuss things and agree. Orechi did not allow it until he achieved his goal. That is why it was decided that Gusii would not have anything to do with this story and its consequences because it was troublesome. This story is: [I]. Mogusero: The most important elder of Gusii, he always likes being praised by Mogusero. Mogusero was born to Omongina Mokeira Bwari, who has five children of Gusii. This elder Mogusero never forgets about the history of the elders! Remember this, Mogusero will never be forgotten when talking about Sereti. The children of Mogusii are numerous: And considering this matter which caused great trouble, it wasn’t understood by Mogusero until he realized his mistake and apologized to both Monyaribari and Mobasi, and he regretted what had happened and became calm. However, we don’t know the children of Mogetutu, the Abagusero clan. That child of Mogetutu who was praised by Mogusero also said something like this [ Mogusero who regrets his mistakes ]. [II]. Omogetutu: And among the children of Gusii who went to look for work in Kisumu while leaving their homes and families behind, Mogetutu was the most important. Mogetutu and Mogetutu Mw' Nyakundi were given land to cultivate by Omongina Mogoisera who gave it to them. But Mogoisera always liked praising people. It is said that Omongina Mogoisera [ a friend of Gichana ] used to give gifts to those who flattered him and praised the child. Whenever that friend praised the child, he would say “With the power of Enkundi…Agatutu”. That child was praised by Mogetutu Mwanyakundi. [III]. Mogirango: Mogirango was also given land because of the wealth of Omongina Bwoisera so that they could build a home. That family was known for working hard and diligently, especially when building a home. They say that whenever a child is born, they praise him saying Gendabu Mw' Mogirango Okogira Engo. Therefore, those who are praised are called Abagirango meaning “Those who build homes.” [IV]. Monyaribari: Nyaribari asks how many clans are there and where did they come from? The people of Nyaribari, along with their children, often traveled to the forest of Sigisi and Gusii and brought back goods from Sigisi to sell in Gusii and were praised by Nyaribari Amangenga. [V]. Mobasi: The Babasi people are skilled in farming and harvesting crops, and they enjoy sharing with others. They are praised as the Babasi. [VI]. Momachoge: Who are the Bamachoge? A child of Bwoisera goes to Bomachoge very often. When someone is praised, the name of the child who is praised is Machoge Osweta Ngoge. [VII]. Monchari: Bonchari and the children of the clan of Mogusii are always praised by Kebenchari. That clan, Kebenchari, settled in Bogere, and his skills were similar to those of Gusii. The story of Kebenchari is also told by the Abanchari.

ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs CIV: Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya "Obokima Bw' Obori Tibwarenge Koguunda Nonya" Aya amwabo aya: Jared Nyaberi: Mbuya omono omongina Birundu ase ogotwara chingaki erinde otoe obosemia. Ase ogochakera, inee, noinyore buna omwaka norori ekero kwaiboretwe? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Ekero naiboretwe, nario konyora Abacheremani bachakire esegi korwa aaria Tanganyika. Nche nabo imanyete igo. Engaki eyio nario ebirwanero bia amasasi biaigete Gusii. Jared Nyaberi: Esegi eyio igo mwaka ki torayebekere gose? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Mochokoro ntwe ntware kobara miaka engaki eyio. Abagusii nigo twarenge komanya emiaka, kobwatekana ne ebinto biarenge gokorekana. Jared Nyaberi: Igo gaki tiga totebe buna nigo kwaiboretwe ase omwaka 1914. Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Eee igo mbuya mochokoro. Jared Nyaberi: Bono omongina karantebia igoro y' endagera y Abagusii. Ninki twakarire ase chingaki echio ekero kwaiboreretwe? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Obokima bw' obori nabwo bwarenge endagera enene y' Omogusii. Korwa kare, Obori nabwo bwarenge endagera enene, naende nero yatokinetie. Chibando tichiarenge ekemeri ki' Omogusii. Yaya. Chibando niigo chiarentetwe n' Omosongo. Niigo chiaigete Gusii bono ekero nabeire enyaroka. Aange nase emiaka 1930. Bono ase ritangani, chibando nigo chiagasimekirwe ase chingito goeta. Magega yaye, chigaansa gosimekwa ase emeraba ime. Keri keri Abagusii togachaka gosimeka chibando kera aase. Jared Nyaberi: Bono omongina, otagontebia buna obori bwagasimekirwe? Enchagwa tiyakabeire Gusii. Nigo enchagwa yachagete gocha ekero amaremo akaera. Jared Nyaberi ngotegerwa are omogano n' omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya, aaria Bomorenda, Bonchari, Kisii County. Photo na Abner Nyaberi, Gusii.com files. Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Mochokoro abwo kare, nigo chiinsana chiarenge kera aase. Bono nigo abamura be ekenyoro bakaimokire ekero ki' omorakera, basamba rinani. Engatiato [ January ] amo na Monuguna O Barema [ February ] nario chiinsana chiagasambirwe. Mochokoro tiga ngotebie buna engaki eyio nigo omogaso okarorire se. Nabo kware korigereria ekeng'umbu, go kwaora buna ense ekomakameka na koyia ase omogaso. Omogaso tari bono ochaka. Ritangani, nigo orosana rwagatongiigwe na koyia. Korwa abwo, obori bwamanya kobusurwa. Ase boigo, obori nigo bwarenge kobusurerwa aase aare. Bwamanya komera na gokonga bobwate ebigara ebinene kegima. Jared Nyaberi: Bono inee omongina, enchagwa ndiriri yarenge koba? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Ntwe Abagusii ntwagatwarire enchagwa. Nigo obori bwarenge kobusurerwa aare aare. Bwamanya gokina na kogeswa. Ko chinsana chiasambirwe, eubi ende nyinge tiyarenge komera, otatiga obori bwoka. Kwagera obori nkwarengeo. Enchagwa nigo yacha gochicha rero ekero amaremo akaera, n' obori kobusurerwa aamo. Jared Nyaberi: Bono magokoro, karantebia igoro y' okogesa obori. Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Ekero obori obo bwamire, nigo bwarenge kogeswa, bwabongororwa, na goserwa na amagoko. Chitinga chi ogosia tichiarenge aroro. Nonya n' chitinga chia amache, nigo chiachete gocha ekero omosongo aikire nka Gusii. Ekero obori bwamire na kogeswa, ogochengerwa nkwarengeo. Ritangani nigo amarwa arenge gosikwa ase ebiteera ime. Amarwa nabo arenge gosiikwa ase emekubio ene emegima! Aye tiga amarwa aya arero agosikwa ase rituko erimo. Bono amarwa amanya koengwa. Kayiire, amanya goterekwa na konywegwa. Amarwa tarenge goterekwa nonde bwensi. Yaya. Amarwa nigo arenge goterekwa no omongina oria onywometwe ase enyangi na kobekerwa ebitinge! Onye tikwabekeretwe ebitinge, nkwarenge gotereka amarwa. Korwa abwo, chimbori chianyenywa, n' abanto koragera. Nigo abanto barenge koragera goika obokima bonde bwatigara! Obokima bw' obori nabo bwarenge kobera ase ekeee ase omokubio omogima, botari koguunda! Mbwarenge gosareka noonya. Jared Nyaberi: Bono abwo kare onye amaremo arenge amanene, nigo abanto bakaagachire are are gose nigo barenge komenya aamo? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Mochokoro mbono amaremo aerire. Chingaki echio, abanto nigo bamenyete ase oboare mono. Nonya n' ekero omoiri asirire, nigo arenge gotindekwa ase obwango, erinde abamwabo bamanya komanyigwa magega yaye. Nonya nabo igo emeyega yo ogosira ero nigo yarenge kogenderera. Jared Nyaberi: Mbuya mono magokoro ase ogotwara engaki gotoa obomanyi buna twakamenyire. Bono inee, ninki oratebie abasae b' ekegori egeke ba Gusii? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Amasikani. Mochokoro amasikani n' egento ekiya. Korende naende, ka moranche timokweba ase morwete. Inyora ase morwete, na baria mwatigete magega. Mbuya mono.
english: Gusii Culture And Customs CIV: Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya "The Wealth of Our Ancestors Will Always Be Remembered" These are their words: Jared Nyaberi: My grandmother Omongina Birundu says that history protects our traditions and identity. Does it not seem so, indeed, that time passes quickly when one is enjoying themselves? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: It does pass quickly, but remember the Germans who came and colonized areas of Tanganyika. They also knew about this land. That history is also a source of strength for the Gusii people. Jared Nyaberi: What year did that colonization begin? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: I don't quite recall how many years ago that was. The Gusii have remembered for generations, because of the things they experienced during those times. Jared Nyaberi: This event happened around 1914, didn't it? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Yes, my grandmother remembers it well. Jared Nyaberi: Therefore, Omongina, tell me about the importance of the Gusii ancestors. How can we learn from that history which has been passed down? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: The wealth of our ancestors is also a great treasure for the Gusii people. In the past, the ancestors were also a great treasure, and today they still guide us. Many clans contribute to the richness of the Gusii people. Yes. That clan is led by the elders. It is a strong Gusii clan, but it became scattered. Around the 1930s. Then, the clan was organized with a specific purpose. Their gatherings were held in large numbers. Gradually, the Gusii began to organize the clan again. Jared Nyaberi: So Omongina, what caused the ancestors to become disorganized? Tradition has never left the Gusii. It is a tradition that has always remained, even until today. Jared Nyaberi is interviewing Omongina Bathseba Birundu, from Bomorenda, Bonchari, Kisii County. Photo by Abner Nyaberi, Gusii.com files. Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Long ago, it was a custom to remain together. But then, the young men started seeking ways to earn a living, and they dispersed. The months of January and February were traditionally months of celebration. I don't quite remember whether that history is a blessing. But they had skills, to ensure that everything worked out and was successful. Success wasn't easy. Nowadays, it is being sought through education. Because of this, the ancestors understood the importance of hard work. In the past, the ancestors were respected and honored for their achievements and contributions to life. Jared Nyaberi: Indeed, Omongina, what kind of respect did tradition command? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: We Gusii valued tradition greatly. The ancestors were respected and honored. They were feared and revered. During celebrations, sometimes many people didn't understand, but they still respected the ancestors. Tradition was very important. Tradition continued to remain, and the ancestors were honored accordingly. Jared Nyaberi: Thank you very much, can you explain the importance of respecting the ancestors? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Because those ancestors existed, they deserved respect, they were praised, and they were remembered by their children. Anything that brings shame should be avoided. And anything that is good, should remain and spread like the Gusii people. Because the ancestors existed and were respected, they were well cared for. Nowadays, things are different; there are no longer such traditions. Things are also changing, and life is becoming difficult! However, these things will eventually return to how they once were. But these things require effort. Sometimes, they are given freely and received willingly. These things shouldn't be taken for granted. Yes. These things should be given to the Omongina who have experience and wisdom, and kept secret! Anyone who hasn't been initiated shouldn't receive these things. Because of this, secrets are revealed, and people gossip. People often gossip about others, causing problems! Problems with the ancestors also deserve attention, so they don't disappear! I will continue to speak truthfully. Jared Nyaberi: But if those things are too important, why do people forget them and stop honoring them? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: It's because of the current generation. Today, people don't understand the meaning of things. But even when someone doesn't know something, it shouldn't be dismissed, so their relatives can learn from it later. Also, what seems insignificant today might become important tomorrow. Jared Nyaberi: Mother, thank you very much for sharing this knowledge with us. But now, who will teach our children the customs of the Gusii people? Omongina Bathseba Birundu Ateya: Let's wait. It's because we need time and patience. Continue working hard, and let everyone understand the truth. Thank you mother.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Ntwachiete n' omon'gina magokoro baba ominto aaria Masimba gokwania omosubati Pamela Bwari, oyio onyora abana chibarongo. Nche tinamanyete, korende go twaiika aroro, magokoro agantebia buna twaikeire korora Ekegusii gio okoibora abana chibarongo. Bono Ekegusii gi chibarongo nkereki? Baba ominto nigo atebete ng'a omong'ina ekero aiboire abana chibarongo nigo ekobetereria akorerane erinde tacha koirora koibora chibarongo naende. Ninki? Nche nigo natang'ang'ete. kobwatekana na magokoro, nigo abakoro bagoteba buna oise koibora chibarongo, togosieka roiboro. Nigo arenge koarama ase enyomba yaye ime! Nigo okoibora chibarongo naende. Kobwatekana n' ekemira giaito ntwe Mwanyagetinge, omokungu oiboire chibarongo nigo arenge koarama ase enyomba yaye ime, korwa abwo Ekegusii giachaka gokorwa! Korwa ase Abagusii abakoro, egware nigo yarenge ey' eng'encho mono. Nigo egware yare korentwa n' akayio! Abana chibarongo baikire aaria Masimba, nka bomame. Kera omonto nigo arenge gosia egware eye, bwetuna, omanya gotunia akamwana! Ritangani, ng'inarome chibarongo echi nigo are gocha ne chingo amo no obosie. Ase boigo, ng'ina koro korwa aaria ase aiboreire, nigo are gotoma chinkara echio chiare gosikwa amarwa. Amarwa aya nigo arenge gotubwa na amagoma. Bono ekero chibarongo chigosokigwa, nario amarwa aya arenge konywegwa. Bono mangana taraera. Nigo egware yare korigigwa. Ase boigo, nigo bare korigia omokorerani. Komenta nayio, nigo yare kobetereri nga bong'inarome nabarabwo nkoenga barenge amarwa. Bono rituko riria rigoika, chingo nachi chigotang'ana, bamanya gosoa nyomba baikaransa. Ko baikaransire, amarwa nigo arenge gokunorwa. Korwa abwo, omokorerani oika mbarabare na koyataoria na koa ng'ina koro asibe ritangani. Korwa abwo, abana aba chibarongo basokigwa isiko bamanya kogingerwa etuki! Obe! Egware eye yarentirwe na akayio n' eyaki? Mwana ominto naende mangana taraera. Ko abana aba chibarongo bagingeirwe, nigo egware yare korentwa n' akayio! Korwa abwo, omonto oegwa egware n' omwana. Kaeirwe omwana, nigo oyo arenge gosia egware eye, bwetuna, omanya gotunia akamwana! Egekorwa eke nigo kiarengenge goetanana ase kera omonto enyomba engima. Onye abanto bande barenge isiko, egware eye nigo yarenge gosokigwa ne chibarongo nario chiratunigwe na bari bare isiko. Go kera oyomo atunire, amarwa nigo arenge kobekwa amache, na abako basiba bamanya gosoka naro isiko. Goika omokorerani arenge koegwa esani amo n' eyanga. Omokorerani kagokora omoyega oyo, nigo arenge koegwa esani, amo n' eyanga. Korwa abwo, omanya kogenda, na abageni baruo bagenda. Nonya nabo igo, Ekegusii g' chibarongo tikiare koera bwango igo. Yaya. Buna bakona gokina, Ekegusii gete ngokorwa kiarenge. Bono nindi ngocha kogenda bomame? Yaya mwana. Kogenda bonyokorome tikoiyo. Aaiga naende, goika abaigwa baraganya, goikera Ekegusii gete, naende gekorwe! Ritangani, chibarongo nigo chiagakinire chitari kogenda bong'inarome! Yaani manya! Korende ekero chiaisanire gochia maguta motwe, nigo chiagakobirwe gochia bong'inarome. Bono oyo orenge kobakoba tari onde bwensi. Yaya. Ori orenge kobakoba nori bakorwa nyuma. Ko yaikire engaki y' okogenda bongina rome, nigo abana aba chibarongo barenge koegwa embori amo n' obosi, erinde betweka gochia abwo bong'inarome. Ko baikire geita, nigo barenge gotenena! Onye na abamura, n' omomura ogocha kobarotota! Onye n' abaiseke, n' abaiseke boigo! Bono rende onye chibarongo echi chiarenge omomura n' enyaroka? Ninki kiare koba? Onye abana aba chibarongo barenge omomura n' enyaroka, oyo okobarotota n' omomura n'enyaroka! Bono oyo okobarotota nigo arenge gotaoria obosi obo n' ekemunu, obotang'ani korwa geita. Ori otanganete gosoka ase okoiborwa nere okoegwa obosi. Ngina koro korwa abwo bonginarome, omanya kobwata obosi obo, otang'ana nyomba. Ng'ina koro korwa aaria bonginarome goika arusie obosie n' ekemunu! Gaikire nyomba, ngina koro oyo nigo arenge korigereria gochia isiko. korwa abwo, nigo ngina koro oyo arenge korusia obosi n' ekemunu, orusia oruta gochia ase omotobwa (omote ori okobera gesieri). Emeremo ya ngika koro teraera. Nigo ng'inakoro naende arenge korusia obosi bonde, omanya kobatunia ase obosio. Korwa abwo, obosi bwensi bwairwa nyomba. Bono ko baikire nyomba, baegwa amarwa ari ng'ina chibarongo atomete. Nigo amarwa aya arenge koigorwa, bataorerigwa baegwa banywe. Tari igo rioka. Nigo embori eri ngina chibarongo atomete yarenge konyenywa. Korwa abwo, bamanya kobekerwa ebitwanga, barara. Maambia yaye, bairana sobo n' embori egochia gosarara! Korwa abwo, abana aba chibarongo bamanya koirwa bware. Magokoro baba ominto nigo agoteba buna eke nakio kiarenge Egekoro kia Mwantagetinge, gi' chibarongo. Bwatera abwo goikera chingaki chinde, and thank you for listening.
english: These are the words: We have received news about the passing of our esteemed mother, Mrs. Masimba Gekwania Omisubati Pamela Bwari, who was known for raising children well. We didn't know, yet we continued praying, hoping her heart would recover so she could continue speaking the Ekegusii language and raising children properly. What does Ekegusii and proper upbringing mean? Our mothers always said that teaching children good morals is more important than just sending them to school to learn how to be raised correctly. Why? Because I understand. It pains my heart, but elders say that if you teach a child good morals, they will never stray from the right path. It is truly a difficult situation! Continuing to raise children properly. Remembering the teachings of our grandmother, Mwanyagetinge, a woman who raised children well, it is a difficult situation indeed, because Ekegusii customs are being forgotten! For the sake of our ancestors, let us maintain our traditions. Let us hold onto our culture! Children should emulate Mrs. Masimba, like their mothers. In the past, it was considered honorable to uphold our traditions, to respect and cherish our heritage! Friends, this message about upbringing has touched me deeply. Truly, those who were raised well are blessed, and they remember their roots and don't forget where they came from. These memories are precious and should be cherished. But what happens when a tradition is abandoned, and these memories fade away? What can we do to restore things? Let us strive to ensure that this upbringing continues, so that future generations also benefit. Those who were raised well often return to help others, remembering the lessons they learned. These lessons are valuable and should be passed on. Let us support those who are trying to rebuild. Let us embrace those who are working hard to improve things. Remember, it is better to encourage and uplift each other rather than criticize. This time of hardship teaches us the importance of unity and cooperation. Those who are rebuilding deserve our support and encouragement. Because of this, let us work together and offer assistance wherever possible, ensuring that everyone benefits. Because of this, children need guidance and protection so they don't lose their way! Oh! Is this tradition being lost due to negligence and carelessness? Another message touches me deeply. For the sake of these children, let us hold onto our culture! Because of this, parents should instill values in their children. Teach your children, and it will be considered honorable to uphold our traditions, to respect and cherish our heritage! The current generation needs to come together and address this issue seriously. Anyone who disrespects our traditions deserves condemnation, and their actions should be corrected by those who value our heritage. To honor our ancestors, let us preserve our memories and ensure that our traditions endure. Let us assist those who are striving to revive our culture and traditions. Let us appreciate those who are making an effort, and support them wholeheartedly. Because of this, let us move forward with determination, and welcome visitors with open arms. However, let us remember that Ekegusii and its upbringing should remain strong and unwavering. Amen. May they find strength and resilience, and may Ekegusii flourish forever. What is preventing us from moving forward? Yes, my child. Let us overcome obstacles and persevere. It is said that when people gather, they share ideas and strengthen bonds. Let us revitalize Ekegusii and make it thrive once more! Let us unite and work towards progress, ensuring that future generations continue to benefit from our rich cultural heritage! Truly I say! Let us carefully examine the root causes of our problems and seek solutions. Let us address the issues that hinder our progress. These efforts won't be easy, but they are necessary. Amen. Some may fail along the way, but let us learn from their mistakes. If we want to see positive change, let us guide our children with wisdom and compassion, teaching them to avoid the pitfalls of the past. Let us inspire them to become responsible citizens who contribute to society! Anyone with enemies should reconcile with them! Anyone with grievances should forgive! What makes someone abandon their family and community? What is the reason for such abandonment? Anyone who abandons their family and community faces consequences and regrets! These consequences involve losing blessings and opportunities, hindering progress. Some may start well but falter later. It is important to remember that true success comes from perseverance and dedication. This is why it is crucial to maintain integrity and honesty in all our endeavors! Let us remember our roots, because neglecting our traditions leads to decline. Because of this, let us safeguard our values and pass them down to future generations, preserving our identity and heritage (our customs are what define us). The results of this effort will be evident. This is why we must strive to uphold our principles, ensuring that our actions align with our beliefs. We must remain steadfast in our commitment to progress, embracing innovation while honoring our traditions. Let us move forward together, working towards a brighter future for all! Let us embrace unity, recognizing that collective action yields greater rewards than individual pursuits. Our hearts, filled with love and compassion, offer praise to God for the gift of life and the strength to overcome challenges, through unity. Let us dedicate ourselves to building a better world, guided by faith and gratitude, and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Abaminto kera egento Mwamogusii ominto agakorire, nkiabwate eng'encho yaye. Chinyangi tichiarenge gokorwa bosa igo. Chinyangi chia abana abamura amo n' abaiseke nigo chiabwate obosemi obonge kerage. Obosemi bw' okoba abanto abaya bono kibabeire abasae abanene. Abasae abwo bagocha koba abagaka gose abang'ina abanene ase ebinyoro biabo. Abamura nigo barenge gosemigwa buna bakorenda chinka chiabo na koba abaamate abaya gochia ase abamwabo. Nigo abaiseke barenge gosemigwa ase chinchera chingiya chio ogokunga chinka chiabo. PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com. Egesunte Kende [ Egesunte Kia Masaba ] 21, 2015. Genderera Gosoma: "Egekoro Kia Maguta Motwe N' ekebe, Naende Giaeteirwe N' Amatuko Aye" Nyamira County Women's Representative Mhe Alice Chae "Maguta Motwe Nigo Ere Mamincha Y' Amaganio Y' Chinyaroka". Jolo Agencies Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXVIII: Konywoma Omoiseke Otaarogeti Inee, aye tata Omogusii ominto n' omanyete buna amarieta nare togokorekania ekero tokoyakwanera? Inche namanyete buna kogenda bware, gosarwa, gochia iburu, gochia nyangi, kwaroka ,gochia maguta motwe nigo atabwekaini. Nonya nabo igo, omongina magokoro baba Nyareso ominto nigo antebetie buna amarieta aya tabwekaini buna ekobwatia: 1. Ogochia bware: Eke nakio egekamago, ogosomigwa buna obwenerete koba otarakorerwa egetambokero kende gionsi ki' omokebi gose omosari. Nigo abamura gose abanyaroka barenge kobekwa aamo basomigwa aya bagwenerete komanyigwa erinde banya korema. Amachiko buna aya naro aregotebwa ase bari barenge koirwa bware: Obe omoremu, torigereria omokebi ekero ogosarwa, tobaisa kobwata omosari okoboko kwaye ekero akogosara, bakungu mbarenge konacha egonde ekero omware arenge koirwa inka, abamura nigo barenge korusia esimbore batari gokira goikera inka, ekero baisire goika inka abamura aba nigo barenge kobisa omware ase egetutu goikera marogoba eike ekiagera tatakeire kororwa n' onde. Ase boigo, omoyega nigo orenge kwariganigwa aare mono korwa ase omware ekiagera abanto mbaganeiri korora mware ekiagera tare gocha kogwena. Omokuuri nigo arenge gokoreranwa !! 2. Ogosarwa: Aya nari enyaroka gose omomura are gokorerwa n' omokebi gose omosari. Oboremi nao aiga bwatakeire na tatakeire gokuura gose kwegosa. Omwana aise gokuura oyio nigo arenge koramwa buna Enkuuri korende nigo arenge gokoreranwa ekiagera are koba takoreranigwa, nigo kaa enywomo yaye yarekoba n' obokong'u obonene !! 3. Gochia iburu: Inyora buna ekero omware ataraikigwa sobo, nigo arenge kobiswa. Aaiga, abamura baganya egesunte kebe erinde bamoira sobo. Ritangani, nigo nigo abagaka barenge goikaransa bweri erinde omware oirwa nyomba. Nyuma ya amatuko atato, nigo omware arenge koroserigwa riburu. Bono riburu ninki? Riburu n' egento kebwekaine egesumu, ekio kiarenge korosigwa saiga nyomba giasimekwa esuguta erinde omware orara aroro. Esuguta tiyatakeire kwoma !! Esuguta eye nigo yare korendwa ase ogosiarerwa amache tebaisa kwoma. Abaminto inyora buna omware nigo arenge gouterwa omorero ase ogosegeswa na nigo orenge korendwa torima, goikera rituko omware are korwa nyomba. Omosegi nigo are koba n' omware onya komokonya esuguta tebaisa kwoma gose omorero korima. 4. Gochia nyangi: Eke nakio ke' eng'encho ase omware. Obotuko bw' okorwera nyomba, omware nigo arenge gokorerwa ebinto gente erinde koenekia gose obeire omomura. Nigo atakeire gosimora ebiundi korwa ase amakara arenge gwooka. Korwa abwo, nigo arenge koegwa emeri amo na amatunda amaororo erinde atakune. Amang'ana taraera. Korwa abwo, omware oyo omanya korurigwa chinyanduri. Ase boigo, nigo arenge kobugerigwa chinyabubu buna enyang'au !! Oboremereria: Nigo omware arenge gosomigwa ekero akoirwa bware erinde oboremereria bwaye bwatemwa, aiga ekero eke gie chinyangi. Oboamate obuya - omosacha okoreire enyangi tatakeire koibera abamwabo !! 5. Okwaroka: Nyuma y' ogoetera enyangi ekong'u, nigo omware arenge koirwa ase abaibori erinde bamosesenie. Ise omwana nigo arenge korwa gesarate gose saiga erinde ogenda mwaye baba n' omorugi oye kemobere !! Inyora omosacha okoreire chinyangi chia bware tatakeire koibera eamate yaye gose egesaku kiaye etugo. Bono emaambia yaye, nigo omosegi amo n' omware baregotenena isiko mwa abaibori b' omware erinde omanya kobora "Ee borania ngo" Ise oiraneria "Ea borania chiombe n' abana" Omware oboria "Baba borania ango" ng'ina oiraneria "Ee tata borania chiombe n' abana" Aiga baruo bairana saiga kwarigania gochia roche gwesibia na kwearigania kobekerwa amaguta. Okoborania oko nakuo kwarenge koba ogosesenia kwa abaibori. Onye omware oyo tarenge na ise, nigo arenge gochia oise moke. 6. Kogenda maguta motwe: Eye nero enchera y' omoerio omware arenge goetera erinde orwera nyomba. Amarwa nigo arenge gosiikwa ase egetera na koengwa. Korwa abwo, amabere nigo arenge kororanigwa n' abagaka abanene baturwa na gochikwa erinde omware oretwa ase bare erinde ache goakwa maguta motwe. Ise nigo arenge gosiberia amarwa, osiarera omwana oye !! Eriakabere nigo arenge gosiba amabere naro oyamosiarera. Nigo omware arenge gosiarerwa obosio igoro. Korwa abwo, Ise nigo arenge kobwata amaguta, omoaka omotonyeria omotwe igoro. Eye nero yare koorokia buna oyo obeire omomura oisaneire. Bono emogoroba eye, oyo orure bware tarenge koirana ase aaramerete. Yaya. Nigo arenge kogenda sobo omosegi oye orara, erinde bogokia mambia yaye, baumerana na abande barure nyomba. Korwa bono, omomura oyo nigo arenge kobwatia amachiko aetwe buna: [ I ]. Tagosoa mwa ng'ina goikera oite eng'iti gose arigie embori aitere abagaka amanye gosoa mwa ng'ina !! [ II ]. Tare gosoa mwa ng'ina goetera egesieri kia borenge korende kia gesaku. [ III ]. Tancheire gosoa ase ng'ina na ise bare korara !! [ IV ]. Tancheire gosia, gotenya, koruga, gochia roche, kwaga enchagu, gosonga, gochia etinga gose gokora chigasi chiri chinyaroka chiare gokora. [ V ]. Taganeiri konya kobera ase abanyaroka bare. Nigo aganeiri gosika abaibori baye, abanene baye gose bari ba nsoni. Tokare gochengera omoyega o Maguta Motwe na magokoro baba Nyareso ominto.
