english: People who have a good name in Mwamogusii people respect them, and they honor their mother. A person who doesn't work hard suffers greatly. A person with children and wives respects great wealth. Great wealth helps those poor people become rich. Those rich people can help their fellow poor people, and their small possessions increase. Those children should strive diligently so they can build their houses and help their parents. Their wives should strive diligently to maintain their homes well. PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com. Good Morning [Good Morning from Masaba] 21, 2015. Read More: "The Power of Unity and Peace, and the Importance of Tradition" Nyamira County Women's Representative Hon. Alice Chae "Unity and Peace Bring Development and Progress." Jolo Agencies Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXVIII: Remembering Our Ancestors Indeed, my fellow Gusii people, don't you think we have forgotten our traditions because of modernization? Know that when someone dies, gets sick, has problems, has bad dreams, steals, or has disputes, they seek the help of elders. Many people today, due to changing times, no longer believe that these things can be solved: 1. Dealing with Illness: This disease is widespread, and it is important to prevent it through proper hygiene for everyone. Both young and old should be vaccinated against diseases. A child who refuses medicine should be forced to take it, and treatment should be sought quickly so that the illness does not worsen!! 2. Preventing Theft: All thieves and robbers should be punished by the elders. The guilty and innocent should be investigated thoroughly. A child who steals something should be disciplined so that Enkuuri (traditional punishment) is carried out, and they should not repeat the offense, otherwise their family will face shame!! 3. Handling Disputes: If there is a disagreement, it should be resolved. Also, people should live peacefully and avoid conflict. Let the judges investigate the matter carefully and resolve the dispute fairly. What is a dispute? A dispute is a problem that arises from misunderstanding, which can lead to fighting and damage property. The fight should not continue!! The fight itself has caused much suffering and destruction. People say that when someone is wronged, they should seek justice and not retaliate, so that the dispute can be resolved peacefully. The mediator should help those involved find a solution and restore peace. 4. Respecting Elders: This applies to everyone regarding respect for elders. During times of hardship, elders should be given support and honored by everyone. It is not good to disrespect them or speak ill of them. By doing so, one shows respect and gratitude. Good manners are essential. By doing so, that person gains wisdom. Therefore, they should be treated with kindness and respect, especially during difficult times. Respectful behavior – an elder who is mistreated should not reveal it to others!! 5. Inheritance: After respecting the elders, the deceased should be mourned and remembered. A child should be raised properly so that they can carry on their parents' legacy. People say that a respectful child will never forget their roots. These words also apply to the mediator and the deceased, who should remember the teachings of their ancestors. These words, both the mediator and the deceased, agreed on a custom among the descendants of the deceased and were able to say “Yes, we agree.” And the others said, “Yes, we agree with the children.” The deceased said, “Father, we agree,” while the others said, “Yes, father, we agree with the children.” But they all disagreed about how to share the inheritance and how to distribute the wealth. Sharing inheritance is important for maintaining relationships with the descendants. Anyone who does not participate in this process should not interfere. 6. Going to Seek Help: Today, I will tell you about a situation where someone needs help and seeks assistance. They should look for trustworthy people and ask for guidance. By doing so, strong men will come forward and offer their support, helping the person overcome their challenges and achieve success. It is important to protect those seeking help, especially children!! One should also protect their own possessions. The person should be shown compassion and understanding. By doing so, today, they have found a way to express their gratitude to those who helped them. Today, they have realized the importance of kindness and generosity. These words also apply to the evening, when someone remembers past events. Yes. They decide to visit their friend and seek advice, sharing their concerns and discussing matters with their neighbors. Through this, the person finds solutions to their problems and gains strength from their community. Here are some guidelines for achieving success: [ I ]. Respect everyone and show humility, allowing wise people to guide you and teach you wisdom. [ II ]. Be humble and seek knowledge from those who possess it, striving for excellence. [ III ]. Be patient and persevere, working hard towards your goals. [ IV ]. Be diligent, honest, hardworking, resourceful, courageous, compassionate, and strive for perfection in everything you do. [ V ]. Be grateful for the blessings you receive and acknowledge the contributions of others. Show respect to your ancestors and honor their memory, remembering those who came before you. Please remember and cherish the lessons learned from Maguta Motwe and the spirit of Baba Nyareso Ominto. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015 Thank you for your attention, Baba Nyareso Ominto, my mother and thank you for listening.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abwo kare kare, ching’iti chi’orosana nchiarenge aroro. Bono chingiti echi nigo chiamenyete n’ oboamo amo n’ omorembe aaiga ase rinani ria Bondonya, Bomachoge. Chingingiti echi nigo chiarenge buna ebikondo, chinyang’au, ebiobiri, amo n' chingabi. Nchire chiare koria amato, nchire chiamenyete amache ime, na nchire chiamenyete ebiswa ime. Engaki eyemo, omorakera omotindi ogaateka ase rinani eri ime. Riberera rigaichora mono, goikera amache akaba botu boke. Endo nero yatenenerete ching’iti echi chionsi aiga Bondonya. Bono Endo ekarangeria omosangererekano bwe ching’iti echi chionsi. Ase omosangererekano oyo, ching’iti echi chikaigwana chireme egesima, erinde gose nchinyore amache chinywe. Obwango obwo obwo, ching’iti echi chikaigwana buna nigo chiare kobwaterana, erinde chireme egesima eke n' oboamo. Bono Ogasusu otameire buna onyorire orogendo gochia mache ng'umbu !! Ching’iti echi chigakunama gokunya egesima. Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu ere taikerana ekiagera nigo atebete buna nigo anyorete esabari ya mobasokano, kogenda mache ng’umbu. Obwango obwo, chingiti echi tichieegena Ogasusu nonya. Bono chigatebi Ogankuru akore obotuki bw’ Ogasusu erinde bamanye ase achiete. Ogankuru agatwara engaki enkong’u gokora obotuki bw’ okomanya ase Ogasusu arenge koreng’ana nase engaki eye ching’iti chinde chiare gokunya egesima gose mbanyore amache nonya n’ amasinini. Chingaki echi chionsi, Ogasusu nigo ebisete mbarabare nase egesima eke kiare gokunywa, korende Ogankuru tamanya. Ogankuru akairana agatebia ching’iti chinde buna taigeti konyora ase Ogasusu aberete. Bono ekero egiateko ekene giachicha aaria Bondonya, chingiti chinyinge chiagatwara erango y' amache enene na korea mono. Ebioto bionsi bikanyorera ribaga na gosoa amache aya ime na gochaka kwoga na goaka ontimbu. Endo ekaigwa bobe na gotogonya ase eriogi rinene. Ching’iti chionsi chikaondoka kerage ekiagera Endo nigo yagechetigwe mono. Ogakondo agaesokia na goteba buna tiga ateme nabo arabwate Ogasusu oyo obachandire ase a matuko atari make. Ogakondo agaancherwa korenda egesima eke kiabo erinde Ogasusu tabaisa goika konywa amache gose koyatumia gwesibia omobere oye naende. Ogakondo akarosia omobwekano bw’ omorabera omuuya omonyakieni kerage. Ching’iti chikagokigwa ne ekebwekane eke. Ogankondo akabeka ekenanti erinde onde aise koyebwata nigo kware konanterera. Omobwekano oyo okabekwa aang’e ne egesima n' Ogankuru akeebisa erinde tarorekana n' Ogasusu ase aberete. Bono Ogasusu okare kwerindori gocha buna botambe !! Ogasusu agacha buna botambe korende tarora onde orendete egesima eke. Kai !! Ogasusu akagenda rioka korende amaiso aye akagokigwa n’ omorabera oteneine aang’e n’ egesima eke korende otarenge gokwana na Ogasusu. Ogasusu akaruo agakuna omorabera oyo. Bono buna amokunete okoboko kwaye gokananta na akaira okoboko koria gwatigarete erinde ang’use oko konde. Naboigo oko gokananta na agasinywa buna are gokora !! Agachia gotema igo, ekaba akong’u. Chingaki echi chionsi, Ogakondo nigo amotengerete korwa egetutu kiare mbarabare ne egesima eke. Ake ake, Ogankondo akarangeria ching’iti chiamwabo. Chingiti echi chikaminyoka gocha na konyora Ogasusu nigo anantete ase ekebwekane eke ki’ omorabera. Bono ching’iti echi chigachaka koa Ogasusu ebinyerere. Ogasusu akarera igo, korende onde taiyo omorocherete amabera. Bono bagateba buna nigo bare gwokia omorero eriinde basambe Ogasusu oyo obachandete ase amatuko atari amake. Omorero okabekwa n' Endo ekanantoria Ogasusu na komobwata amorute riiko. Riria Endo yamobwata iga, Ogasusu akaminchoria na koniantoka ne chimbero chimbariri. Ching’iti echi chigachia komominyoki igo, tichiamoikera. Korwa erio, Ogasusu karorire ching’iti chi’ orosana, nigo agotama.

ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Abwo kare kare, Oganchogu narenge ase engegu y' oroche rwe Egucha aaria Ogembo. Abwo mbarabare, nigo arenge kogamba n' Okang'ubo, oyio ocheng'enaine amache igoro. Ase engaki eye, oroche oro nigo rwarenge orosinini na ndwarenge n' mache mange. "Inaki yaa Okangubo mbokiete abwo?" Oganchogu okare koboria, kagosiberia amache Ase eng'encho oroche oro rwarenge oroke mono Oganchogu nigo yare komobera aororo komorora Okang'ubo ekero are roche. Bono kibagendererete kogamba, Oganchogu agatebia Okang'ubo buna "Aaye n' omonene na nigo ore n' omobere omonene kerage. Nainche tindi moke. Igo nere buya aye obe omoruoti ase oroche, nainche imbe omoruoti bwe ense enkamoku" Okangubo akanya gocheng'enena ang'e n' ase Oganchogu ateneine mbarabare n' engegu y' oroche oro na goitaberia buna "Toise koba abaruoti nabo togokora kende gionsi toratake engaki ende yonsi onde atari gotokania na tokore ching'iti chiri chinsiniini chikore egasi torachitebie" Bono Ogasusu oyio oikaransete otengerete korwa egetutu ime, kagosiiba erongori rikairo !! Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu nao arenge mbarabare, ebisete egetutu kiarenge aange n' oroche oro. Bono Oganchogu n' Okangubo tibamanyete buna Ogasusu nao atengererete buna bare koroberia, erinde bachiche gochanda ching'iti chiri chi'orosana chinke engaki chiabeire chikogamba aiga. Ogasusu akaigwa bobe na gweteb ase omoyo oye ime buna goika atange Oganchogu n' Okangubo korwa ase ogotenenera ching'iti chi'orosana. Ase boigo, Ogasusu tatagete Oganchogu atenenere ching'iti chie ense. Ase ig,o akarigia chinchera chio ogocha gotangaOganchogu taira oboteneneri. "Gaki nkonye ase ogwancha kwao" Ogasusu okare koruta enduru Bono Ogasusu akarengereria korigia obong'ainereria erinde atange ching'iti echi ibere tichibaisa kogamba nonya nake. Ekero Oganchogu akora konywa amache agasuka korwa ase engegu eye y' oroche. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akarigia engori entaambe na kogenda goikera ase oroche oro rware na gochaka korangeria Okangubo okomoteba buna "Gaki nkonye ase ogwancha kwao" Okangubo akaboria buna "Nninki kiaba gose?" Abwo nario Ogasusu airanereretie ogoteba buna "Eng'ombe yane nigo yaratera etintira ime. Bono nasinyirwe koyekonya erwe etintira eye ime" Okangubo agaitaberia buna "Ninki oroche indagokonye ?" Koigwa iga, Ogasusu agateba buna, "Tiga insibe engori eye, erinde inyeranderere omobere oo bwensi na insibe eng'ombe eria ekare ensemo eri ya moino. Bono kinasibire engombe yane na kingoteba buna ng'usa, ong'use bokong'u ekiagera eng'ombe eye n' enene kerage" Okangubo agateba buna nabo akonyara kong'usa n' chinguru, atabwati mochando nonya. Bono Okangubo agatenena ase engegu igoro na gotenena aang'e n' Ogasusu. Ne engori egasibwa obogatigati bw' enda y' Okangubo. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akabogoria na kong'usa engori gochia ase Oganchogu arenge na komonyora. "Oganchogu gaaki inkonye" Ogasusu okare gokwana n' amabera. "Ninki ekebe?" Oganchogu akamoboria. Ogasusu agaitaberia ogoteba buna eng'ombe yaye nigo yaratera etintira ime, naende yasinyirwe kwerusia ime. "'Ninki otagete nkore bono?" Oganchogu akaboria. "Gaki tiga insibe engori ase omobere oo erinde insibe n' eng'ombe yane ase eraterete, erinde imanye kogotebia buna ng'usa na ong'use bokong'u ekiagera eng'ombe eye nigo ere enene kerage" Ogasusu akairaneria. Korora amabera, Oganchogu agateba buna ere nabo akongusa chiombe isato ase entunde eyemo, naende taigwa kende nonya !! Korora amabera, Oganchogu agateba buna ere tabwati bokong'u ekiagera nabo akong'usa chiombe isato ase entunda eyemo atari nabokong'u bonde bwensi !! Ogasusu agasiba engori na kogenda akeebisa ase egetutu kende kiarenge ang'e n' oroche oro. Korwa aaiga ase ebisete, nabo arenge korora ching'iti echi chionsi ibere buna chiare kong'usanana, chiarigerereti chisemo ao ao chitari kororana. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akababoria gose babeire aang'e kong'use engori. Oganchogu n' Okangubo bagaitaberia na gochaka kong'usa engori. Chikaigwa buna oborito bwarenge na kogasana kong'usa ne chinguru chinene kerage. Aba babere bakang'usa engori ase engaki entambe. Oganchogu akarosa. Omoerio, oye, Okangubo akamong'usa na komoiyeraia akagwa roche ime !! Bono gasoa ase oroche, akarora engori gesibire ase Okangubo na koigwa bobe. Oganchogu akaboria Okangubo buna ninki akorera eng'ombe ya Oasusu. Oganchogu akaba n' obororo obonge na gotaka komanya buna ninki Okangubo akorerete eng'ombe y' Ogasusu. Nere Okangubo akaigwa obororo na gotebia Oganchogu buna "Aye nigo okong'aina. Ingai eng'ombe y' Ogasusu ere ?" Ogasusu engaki eye ching'iti echi ibere chikonya koborania amaboria, nigo ebisete egetutu ime gekonya goseka ng'ora ng'ora. Ching'iti echi naende chigachaka kong'usa engori eye buya. Okangubo akarosa entunde eye n' Oganchogu akamong'usa na komorusia amache ime. Ogasusu obeire Matiebo, na gosaria emeroberio Obwango obwo obwo, engori ekabutoka na Oganchogu agaaka inse ne chinguru chinene. Ase boigo, Okangubo akairana na goaka inse amache ime. english: These are the words: Long ago, Oganchogu went to visit his father Egucha who lived in Ogembo. Later, he also went to talk to Okang'ubo, a very wealthy man who owned many cows. His homestead was beautiful, and his cows were numerous and he had many herdsmen. “What did Okangubo say to him?” Oganchogu asked curiously. His homestead was beautiful, and his cows were numerous, so Oganchogu decided to go and thoroughly investigate Okang'ubo’s wealth. This made him think, Oganchogu told Okang'ubo, “You are rich and yet you still carry things on your head. Don’t be ashamed of working hard. It is good to work like others, don’t despise work because it is considered lowly.” Okangubo listened attentively to what Oganchogu said and then replied, “Listen, people should not boast about their wealth; they should remember that everything they have can disappear quickly and they should avoid arrogance and pride.” But Ogasusu, who understood everything, warned them against greed!! Despite this, Ogasusu also went later, wanting to see the wealth that everyone was talking about. And Oganchogu and Okang'ubo didn’t realize that Ogasusu had come to find out whether they would share their wealth, lest their children suffer from poverty and hardship. Ogasusu arrived quietly and heard their conversation about life, realizing that they were discussing how to avoid greed. But unfortunately, Ogasusu failed to make Oganchogu understand his point. And again, he noticed something strange that made Oganchogu appear unwilling to listen. “I will give you some advice,” Ogasusu said loudly. Then Ogasusu began to explain how important it was to help those in need, reminding them that someday they too might face difficulties. And Oganchogu continued to drink beer while visiting his father’s homestead. Because of this, Ogasusu observed carefully and walked over to tell Okang'ubo, “I will give you some advice.” Okangubo asked, “Why are you saying that?” Then Ogasusu explained, “A cow today may stumble and fall. So, let me advise you to always have some reserve for emergencies.” Okangubo wondered, “What does this mean?” It happened that Ogasusu said, “Let us slaughter this cow, and distribute the meat among the poor, and let us also slaughter another cow which we shall save for times of famine. Let us therefore share this cow so that when there is drought, we will have something to eat.” Okangubo responded, saying he was afraid of losing his possessions, but he pretended to agree. And Okangubo went back to his homestead and secretly informed Ogasusu. With the cow that was slaughtered, they shared it with the needy people of Okangubo’s clan. Because of this, Ogasusu rejoiced and decided to share the remaining cow with Oganchogu and offer him guidance. “Oganchogu, I will give you some advice,” Ogasusu said with determination. “What is it?” Oganchogu inquired. Ogasusu explained that his cow had stumbled and fallen, and he needed to find a way to recover it. “What prevents you from doing so?” Oganchogu asked. “I say, let us slaughter this cow and distribute the meat among the poor, and let us also slaughter another cow which we shall save for times of famine, so that when there is drought, we will have something to eat,” Ogasusu reiterated. Again, Oganchogu replied that he was also afraid of losing his livestock due to hardship, and he feared being left with nothing!! Again, Oganchogu stated that he would rather hoard his wealth than share it with others, fearing future problems. Ogasusu took the cow and went to hide it near the riverbank, away from them. After a while, he returned and found everyone still arguing about sharing, constantly changing their minds. Because of this, Ogasusu questioned why they weren’t willing to share the cow. Oganchogu and Okangubo wondered and considered sharing the cow. It became clear that their reluctance stemmed from fear and selfishness. These people then shared the cow with the needy families. Oganchogu was upset. Suddenly, Okangubo began to milk the cow and carelessly spilled the milk everywhere!! This caused anger and frustration, and he quickly hid the cow from Okangubo and ran away. Oganchogu accused Okangubo of stealing Ogasusu’s cow. Oganchogu walked with a heavy heart and tried to understand why Okangubo had stolen Ogasusu’s cow. But Okangubo fell into a trap and confessed to Oganchogu, saying, “Yes, I did it. Is it really Ogasusu’s cow?” Ogasusu and the elders gathered, and because of their wisdom, they resolved the dispute and brought peace. The elders agreed that the cow should be returned to its owner. Okangubo was ashamed and apologized to Oganchogu and started milking the cow again. Ogasusu visited Matiebo and expressed his gratitude. During that time, the cow gave birth to a calf, and Oganchogu was overjoyed. Meanwhile, Okangubo continued to steal and hide the milk. Because of this, Oganchogu realized his mistake and sought forgiveness. Okangubo also admitted his wrongdoing and promised to stop. Ogasusu happily witnessed the reconciliation and praised them both for their honesty.

english: Parajubaea torallyi grows natively in the moist forests of South America. Currently, it is cultivated as an ornamental tree and in arboretums, Bolivia being its main center of interest due to its large population, which is threatened by deforestation. Found in Bolivia, it grows at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level in the Inter-Andean dry forest; however, some populations grow at lower altitudes in more humid environments. It flowers after about 20 years and has a trunk diameter of up to 1 meter. It can reach heights of up to 7 meters in cultivation (with a crown spread of 5 to 8 meters) and lives for approximately 550 years. It needs well-drained soil to thrive, prefers full sun, a trunk, and also requires adequate drainage to prevent root rot, benefiting people who want to plant it because it is easy to grow. Large trunks become hollow and those associated with old age are prone to decay, making them unsuitable for use as timber. It is said that in Europe, trunks can reach diameters of 3 meters. The palm thrives in areas where temperatures rarely drop below -8 degrees Celsius. Many birds feed on its fruits, but they remain mostly in the highlands, beautiful palms! In Bolivia, the palm grows to a height of 14 meters with a trunk diameter of 25–35 centimeters. The palm can live for 100 years and reach a height of 30 meters with a trunk diameter of 50 centimeters. Some individuals have been reported to reach heights of 20 meters! The trees are common in the cloud forests of Bolivia. It is a relatively fast-growing palm, but it does not grow as quickly as other species due to its size. This species is classified as P. torallyi var. microcarpa with smaller leaves and P. torallyi var. torallyi with larger leaves. However, there is confusion, var. microcarpa tends to grow more slowly, while those in drier and warmer climates grow faster. Its conservation status is considered vulnerable due to habitat loss. Nevertheless, its seeds germinate easily, provided they are fresh and kept moist, and planted shallowly. Well-maintained plants, with adequate watering and fertilization, benefit greatly from this care, especially during the first few years, and the seedlings will be strong and healthy. It needs regular care, including pruning, fertilizing, and protecting against pests and diseases, benefiting people who appreciate this native tree and also helping to conserve the species and its habitat. Parajubaea torallyi and its relatives are important ecologically and economically. In Ecuador and Colombia, Parajubaea cocoides grows at altitudes between 2500–3000 meters – the palm is found on slopes and is not very common. It is closely related to Parajubaea torallyi, and sometimes confused with other species of Parajubaea torali. Other populations were discovered in Peru in the 1990s, identified as Parajubaea sunkha which is similar and was described in 1996. It grows up to 8 meters tall and is found in the Andean foothills near Vallegrande in the Santa Cruz region of Bolivia at elevations between 1700–2200 meters. There has been some confusion about whether Parajubaea tirali is the same as Parajubaea sunkha. The seed of Parajubaea germinates easily. The fruit is used locally for food. Those interested should collect the fruits, but they need to be cleaned well and sown fresh, and they need moisture throughout the year. The seeds sprout readily when kept moist for several months. Old seeds may take longer to germinate. Flowering occurs annually, producing abundant flowers. The flowering period lasts for several months each year. Typically, the seeds collected from the fruit are approximately 20 mm long and 5–7 mm wide. The seeds are covered with a hard shell. The shells are often cracked during collection. The seeds also require stratification before sowing. To germinate the seeds, it's necessary to simulate the conditions of the rainy season (wet and dry periods), mimicking the environment where they grow (especially in Bolivia - areas with distinct wet and dry seasons). After cracking the shells, the seeds that have been collected should be soaked in water for several weeks, alternating between soaking and drying. Stop watering the seeds and let the soil dry out for few months. Take the seeds out of the soil, put them back into water for around a week and then sown them again. Don't delay planting the seeds and provide adequate moisture. Soak the seeds first, then place them in damp cloth and sow them. The seedlings take about a year to mature and produce leaves. Any damaged seedlings, discard them along with those that don't sprout after being watered. The germination rate of Parajubaea can reach 100%, producing strong sprouts, and the seeds are very resistant to damage. In some cases, there may be a small hole, which indicates good viability; otherwise, the seed will not germinate unless it's fully intact. A large hole indicates a better chance of sprouting. Parajubaea is native to isolated areas of eastern South America. A major reason for its decline is deforestation due to agriculture, leading to habitat loss and fragmentation. The palm tree that grows here is unique and rare. Larger seeds are more likely to survive. The growth of these seeds is affected by animals like the spectacled bear (Tremarctos ornatus), which disperse the seeds across wider areas. ««« Previous article: Welwitschia mirabilis - a plant from the Namib desert Next article: Omogati bw’amatunda Artocarpus odoratissimus, Marang »»»

ekegusii: 1 Omogano bw’ogotongwa g’wense 1Agwo omochakano Nyasae agatonga igoro na ense, 2Bono ense tiyarenge na kieni kende, gose kende gionsi tikiareengeo, n’omosunte ekerima nigo oyetubete, na Omoika o Nyasae ogatoeerera igoro y’amaache. 3 # 2 Abakr 4:6 Erio Nyasae agachiika: “Tiga oborabu bobeo,” erio kegima oborabu bokabao. 4Nyasae akagokigwa na keria aroche. Erio agaatanana oborabu korwa ase omosunte, 5akaroka oborabu boria omobaso, na omosunte akayoroka obotuko. Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bokaba maambia, rituko rie ritang’ani. 6 # 2 Petr 3:5 Erio Nyasae agachiika, “Tiga oboiko bobe egati‐gati y’amaache, erio bwatanane amaache korwa ase amaache ande.” 7Igo Nyasae agakora oboiko boria, bogaatanana amaache ayare inse y’eaanga korwa ase amaache ayare igoro y’oboiko; ayio akaba boigo. 8Akaroka oboiko boria igoro. Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria kabere. 9Naende Nyasae agachiika, “Tiga amaache ayare inse y’erioba asangererekane aase aamo, egere ense enyomo erorekane;” ayio akaba boigo. 10Akaroka aase aria aomo ense, na amaache aria asangererekanete amo akayaroka chinyancha. Nyasae akarora ayio ng’a namaya. 11Erio agachiika agateeba: “Tiga ense emere ebimeri bigokina, buna ebimeri bikorua na emete ekwama amatunda are ne chimbusuro chire imeo, kera oyomo ase egesaku kiaye ekenyene” ayio akaba boigo. 12Na ense ekamera ebimeri bionsi, na Nyasae akarora ng’a ayio namaya. 13Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria gatato. 14Erio Nyasae agachiika “Tiga emebaso ebe ase oboiko bw’aaria igoro, bwatanane omobaso korwa ase obotuko; erio ebe ebimanyererio bikworokia ebiro bi’amatuko, ne chingaki, n’emiaka, 15ebe emebaso ase oboiko aaria igoro, boyee ense omobaso na oborabu,” ayio onsi akaba boigo. 16Erio Nyasae agakora emebaso ebere emenene, Risase rigaambere ekero kia mobaso n’omotienyi ogaambere ekero kia botuko; agakora ne ching’enang’eni boigo. 17Akayebeka ase eanga aaria igoro, eyee ense oborabu, 18egaambere omobaso na obotuko, na gwatanana oborabu korwa ase omosunte. Nyasae akarora ayio ng’a namaya. 19Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria kane. 20Naende Nyasae agachiika, “Tiga amaache atware obonge bw’ebitongwa bire moyo, ne chinyoni chikoiruruka igoro ase ense, chigoetanana inse y’eaanga ya igoro.” 21Erio Nyasae agatonga ebitongwa ebinene bire ase amaache ime, amo n’ebitongwa binde bionsi bimenyete ase amache ime, boigo agatoonga chinyoni. Nyasae akarora ng’a ayio namaya. 22Erio akabisesenia bionsi, agateeba ebitoongwa biria bimenyete amaache ime bisaraare biichore ime ase chinyancha, naende agateebia chinyoni chisaraare ase ense. 23Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria gatano. 24Naende Nyasae agachiika, “Tiga ense etware ebitongwa bire moyo, kera egesaku n’engencho yaye. Ching’iti chigotugwa, n’echikwagura, ne ching’iti chi’orosana, kera egesaku nengencho yaye” ayio akaba boigo. 25Ase igo Nyasae agakora ching’iti chi’orosana, Nyasae akarora ng’a ayio namaya. 26 # 1 Abakr 11:7 Erio Nyasae agateeba: “Bono tiga tokore omonto; ase omogwekano oito, otobwekaine. Nigo arabe n’echinguru agaambere chinswe chia nyancha, ne chinyoni chikoiruruka igoro, ne ching’iti chigotugwa, ne ching’iti chionsi chi’orosana, na ense yonsi, ne ching’iti chionsi chinene n’echinke.” 27#Omoch 5:1,2#Mat 19:4; Mar 10:6Nabo Nyasae agatonga Mwanyabaanto ase omobwekano oye omonyene; ase omobwekano o Nyasae ere akamotonga. Agatonga omosacha na omokungu, 28akabasesenia, akabateebia: “Moibore, mosarare, moichore ase ense, na moyegaambere. Ngokobeeka inde ogaambere chinswe, ne chinyoni, n’echingiti chionsi chi’orosana. 29Nabaeire kera ekemeri gekwama chimbusuro, na kera omote okwama amatunda ebio nabio biraabe endagera yaino. 30Korende ching’iti chi’orosana ne chinyoni chionsi nachieire ebimeri ebibese bionsi bibe endagera yabo.” Ayio onsi akaba boigo. 31Nyasae akarora ebinto ebio bionsi akorete, na birobio nigo biareenge ebiya mono. english: 1 For when you are afflicted, remember God 1Hear this plea, Lord, judge and defend my cause, may my tears find favor with you, and the Holy One of God will vindicate me. 3 # 2 Chronicles 4:6 Thus says the Lord: “Strengthen your hands,” thus says the Lord to Zerubbabel. Thus says the Lord, and it will be done today, and they will rejoice, and they will be blessed. 6 # 2 Peter 3:5 Thus says the Lord: “Strengthen your faith among the nations, and let the nations come to know my name.” For the Lord strengthens his faith, and he brings the nations to know his name, and he makes them holy. 7He strengthens his faith forever. ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Amo na Joshua Araka: Gusii.com/2010, Manga Escarpment. Embeo nigo ekogusa korwa Enyancha ya Victoria yaaka Emanga. Nigo embeo egotengia emete ye emanga. Eye nero e Manga gose Manga Escarpment buna abande bakoyeroka. Emanga nigo ere ange chieka 100. Nigo ere ime ya Manga District ange na Kisii Town. Nigo E Manga ere ase orobebe rwa Kitutu Masaba na Kitutu Chache. Goteneine ase e Manga, nabo okorora Kisii Town, Bogere,Enyancha ya Victoria amo ne chinsemo chinde chia Nyamira District. Enyomba yo Omogusii nigo yarenge "round". Omosongo nere orentete chikona. Enyomba yaito Manga yaagachetwe ne Ritongo Cultural Group yagotire. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abangina na abagaka abakoro ba Gusii nigo bagoteba inga E Manga nigo yarenge ase Abagusii barenge koumerana gosaba, gokora ebingwanso ne emeyega yende yonsi emenene. Omogaka Omondi Onkundi, 70, nigo agoteba inga abakoloni nigo baagachete Ekoti (Ritongo) entangani ime ya Gusii aaiga ase E Manga.Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga ekero omokoloni arwete Gusii, Ritongo rikanganyigwa gochia Nyamira. Gopreserve omogaino oito. Gotaka komanya ase twarwete. Ribwago Cultural Group. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Engoro No Omosasa O' Kegancha Nigo omogaka Onkundi agoteba inga, otatiga ogotamanyekana ase chingaki echi chie ekerero, E Manga nigo yasikire sana ase amatuko amakoro. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga chisokoro na Nyasae (Engoro) nao bameneyete igaa. Omogaka Onkundi nigo akomenta inga erieta "Nyasae" nigo twasumete korwa Bogere. Nyasae tiriri rieta rie Ekegusii asiri. Erieta rironge ase Omogusii ribaga ria Nyasae nigo rire "Engoro". Buna ebisaku binde, Abagusii nigo bare gosuma amarieta goeta goeta kobwatekana buna barenge goetanana ase okonganya. Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga engaki ya botuko, nabo emerero yare kororekana egwoka ase chinsana chie E Manga. Nigo abanto bare kogenda maambia korotota banyora inga kende tikeyieti. Omogaka Samuel Ongeri nigo agoteba inga ekio ne ekeene rakini nigo akomenta inga omoika bwe Engoro nigo omenyete ase omote okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. Aaiga ase Omosasa O 'Kegancha nao Abagusii barenge gosaba ase Engoro na komoboria aramere ababisa, gosibia emechie na koyesesenia. "Goikera rero, Omosasa O'Kegancha nao oteneine ase E Manga. Onde takoyobutora gose atumie chinko chiaye. Echio ne chimuma." Nabo omogaka Ongeri amentete. Omosasa O' Kegancha. Oteneine korwa kare kare. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Ngoro Mwaga Tari igo rioka. Egento kende kere ase E Manga ne engoro ekorokwa "Ngoro Mwaga". Nigo engoro eye echakerete egetare igoro, egaeta gati na goika inse. Nigo gekoba inga engoro eye nigo ere eya amasikani ase Engoro. Onye gotagete goika ange, goika okore emeroberio gete erinde omanye koyerora. Engoro Ya Mwaga tegoichora. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 "Goika osibe obonyansi bore machani kabichi amo ne chinko. Basi omanye koruta obonyansi obwo amo ne chinko echio ase engoro eyio ime. Korwa abwo chisokoro nabo chikogwanchera origererie engoro eyio". Nabo omogaka Onkundi akomenta. Nonya nabo igo, engoro eyio tiyana goichora obonyansi ne chinko gesa na gesa. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga emioyo ye chisokoro nao yamenyete aaiga ase E Manga. Nigo bare gocha igaa korwa ebingwanso, gosaba na gokora emeyega ende yonsi emenene. Renta obonyansi ne chinko momanye korigereria Engoro Ya Mwaga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Enyancha Yo Okari Ange na Ngoro Mwaga, enyancha neroo etari kororekana ekorokwa Enyancha Yo Okari. Nigo Omogano Bwa Abagusii ogoteba inga omochie oyomo nomenyete igaa rakini enyomba yabo ekarimera gochia inse ne echancha ekamanya gotoka. Yaani enyomba eyio nigo yanywetwe ne enyancha. Enyancha eyio nigo erokire erieta rio omogaka bwe enka eyio yanywetwe, omogaka Okari. Igena Monto Ebinto bie E Manga ne ebinge. Eariganie koumera Igena Monto. Gati ye ebinto ebinge bie E Manga bire ne maana ase Omogusii ne rigena rikorokwa Igena Monto. Rigena eri nigo rikororekana buna omonto. Korwa aare, nigo rikororekana buna omonto oikaransete rakini ekero gwaikire ange, kwanyora inga ne rigena. Omogusii nigo anchete goaka oboche. Nigo togoteba igo ekiagera chingoro chio ogoakera oboche bwa Ajua nao chichongire ase egetare igoro ase E Manga. Nigo William Marianga and Andrew Okera bagoaka oboche rakini nigo batebete inga oboche obo nigo bwarosetigwe ne Engoro. Tari monto oboroisetie. Goaka oboche E Manga igoro. Aba imbamanyete go kill time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abamenyi be E Manga nigo batagete ogobago robekwe, chioteli chibekwe amo ne Museum ebwate Omogano o Gusii ne ebinto Abagusii bagatwarire. Ase amatuko aetire, ekeombe kia NGO kie Ritongo Cultural Group ingiatagete koagacha enyomba ye egetamaduni, babeke abateri bo obokano na abangina na abagaka bagototebia omogano bwo Omogusii. Kende tikeraba goikera bono ase engencho yo oboremerwa bwe chibesa. Togende gotara E Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Abanene be Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga Na George Morara nigo bagoteba inga enyomba yaagachetwe bono yagotire. Nigo enyomba eye yaagachire ase ekegambero kio omochifu omokoro, Zachary Angwenyi. Aaiga nao gekoba inga Omochifu Angwenyi nigo agambete na korwa ogochika kwo ogokeia enamba ye chiombe chie enyangi korwa 20 impaka 6! "Eke nakio kiagerete Abasacha abange ba Gusii bagaansa konywoma naende". Nabo Ezra abuga akomenta naende. Konyora abasacha abange batigire konywoma ase engencho yo ogotatwara chiombe 20 na gochia igoro. Gusii.com iyakorete obotuki na konyora inga eserikali iyatagete kobeka Manga Escarpment ebe e National Monument. Emepango eyio teraba. Nigo ensemo eye ere engiya ase obotari rakini tebwati batari bange. Ase okogamba no omowaziri bwe Egetamaduni naende omobunge o North Mugirango, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui, nigo egotebekana inga emeroberio neroo yo okorenda na koroisia E Manga. "Nigo E Manga ebwate ekieni sana naende nabo erarente amagenderero sana toise koyerenda". Nabo Mhe. Ombui amentete. Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Nigo Mhe. Ombui atebete inga naborie eserikali erwe ogokonya erinde Manga Cultura Center eagachwe. Ase boigo, nigo atebete inga netakeire orobago robekwe erinde emepaka yaye emanyekane.
english: These are the stories: Amo and Joshua Araka: Gusii.com/2010, Manga Escarpment. Long ago there was a person called Enyancha of Victoria who lived in Emanga. It was a person who owned land in Emanga. And now it is in Manga near Manga Escarpment where people gather. Emanga is about 100 years old. It is located in Manga District and Kisii Town. In Manga it borders Kitutu Masaba and Kitutu Chache. It has connections to Manga, also reaching Kisii Town, Bogore, Victoria Falls and even some parts of Nyamira District. The homesteads of the Gusii people were usually “round”. The fences were very short. This Manga homestead was built by the Ritongo Cultural Group and is well known. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Together with the elders of the Gusii people they say that Manga is where the Gusii people used to meet for consultations, perform ceremonies and resolve all important matters. Elder Omondi Onkundi, 70, says that the colonialists found the Ritongo (Cultural Center) already established within the territory of the Gusii people specifically at Manga. Elder Onkundi says that when the colonialists came to Gusii, Ritongo was moved to Nyamira. Let us preserve our traditions. Let us remember our history. Ribwago Cultural Group. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Wealth of the Clan of Kegancha Elder Onkundi says that it is not widely known that this area, Manga, was very significant to the ancestors. The Gusii people believed that their strength came from God (the Creator) and they respected tradition. Elder Onkundi comments that the name "God" was first heard in Bogore. God’s creation for the Gusii people is referred to as "Engoro". However, in ancient times, the Gusii people had many different ways of life but they always united to solve problems. Elder Onkundi says that because of tribal conflicts, things often deteriorated leading to chaos in Manga. People would travel far and wide spreading rumors causing anxiety. Elder Samuel Ongeri says that this place and its surroundings are sacred and he comments that the name Engoro originated from the ancestor Okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. The clan of Omosasa O 'Kegancha and the Gusii people worshipped Engoro and offered sacrifices, performed rituals and sought blessings. “Therefore, Omosasa O'Kegancha and his descendants are in Manga. He did not move anywhere during his lifetime. This is his home and burial ground.” Also said elder Ongeri. Omosasa O' Kegancha. Descendants live everywhere. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Name of the Year This year has passed. A celebration took place in Manga and the name given was “Ngoro Mwaga”. It was a unique name which attracted attention and caused excitement. It was agreed upon that this name represented the strength of Engoro. Anyone who understood its meaning knew how important it was to protect it. The Name of the Year is celebrated. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 “It is good to respect both the living and the dead. Therefore, let us protect this heritage both now and in the future so that this name continues to be remembered.” Also commented Elder Onkundi. However, this name does not celebrate the living and the dead equally. The Gusii people believe that their ancestors have power and they honor them in Manga. They offer gifts, worship and pray for prosperity and peace. Respect both the living and the dead to preserve the Name of the Year. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The Story of Okari Like Ngoro Mwaga, this story also happened in the past called the Story of Okari. It is said that the history of the Gusii people tells of a man named Oyomo who lived near a tree whose roots were deep and branches spread wide. That tree was associated with a story. This story is about what happened to the elder named Okari. A Certain Person There are things in Manga and elsewhere. Let us remember a certain person called Igena Monto. Both things from Manga and elsewhere have meaning to the Gusii people and are remembered as Igena Monto. This memory is about a person. In the past, it was about a person who was respected by everyone, and it is still remembered today. The Gusii people also have traditions. It is believed that there was a time when a young man named Ajua went looking for traditions in Manga. William Marianga and Andrew Okera also searched for traditions and found that those traditions were preserved by Engoro. There is much more to learn. Searching for Traditions in Manga. Sometimes we just want to pass the time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 The elders of Manga have realized that something needs to be done, a building should be built and a museum established to showcase the culture of the Gusii people and the items they used. For generations, organizations like the Ritongo Cultural Group have worked hard to preserve our heritage, bringing together leaders, experts and elders to promote the culture of the Gusii people. We need to support them in this endeavor. Let's continue to develop Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Leaders of the Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga and George Morara, have stated that the land allocated for this purpose is sufficient. It is land that belonged to a former leader, Zachary Angwenyi. People say that Chief Angwenyi gave permission for the construction of a house with twenty rooms and six bathrooms! “I urge all the clans of the Gusii people to come together.” Ezra said. They encourage the clans to contribute towards building twenty rooms and six bathrooms. Gusii.com reports that efforts are underway to persuade the government to declare Manga Escarpment a National Monument. These plans are progressing. And there is hope that future generations will benefit from this. According to the Minister for Culture and Member of Parliament for North Mugirango, Hon. Wilfred Ombui, he supports the idea of preserving and developing Manga. “Manga has a lot of history and it can attract tourists if developed properly,” Hon. Ombui added. Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Hon. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010 Hon. Ombui further stated that the government should help fund the construction of the Manga Cultural Center. Additionally, he mentioned that funds should be allocated to renovate the existing structures so that their importance is recognized.

ekegusii: |“Korende koramoorokie Yesu Kristo as'omonwa oo, nakomwancha as'omoyo oo, ng'a Nyasaye namobogetie korwa as'amakweri, nokonyeke: naki as'enkoro abanto igobakwegena baikera oboronge; nas'omonwa oorokia goika onyora ogotoreka. naki, onde bwonsi orarangerie erieta ri'Omonene nakonyeke.” Aba Rumi 10:9-10,13| Okoboka gwa Kristo-Okorigia engencho yaye Omotomwa Paulo nigo agotonenekeria ase rirube riaye ritangani ase Abakorintho: “Korende onye okobokigwa kw’abakure tikori, rirorio Kristo nere tobogetiwe, “(1 Abakorintho 15:13). Ase egesieri ekio nigo agoteba:” Naende Onye Kristo nere tabogetigwe, rirorio okorandia gwaito nokwa bosa, na okwegena kwaino nokwa bosa,” (Abakorintho 15:14) Engencho yakobokigwa gwa Kristo nigo ekororekana ase obonge na omogoko ase okorandia buna ekanisa ya ritangani egokina (omobwekano ogokora kwa Abatomwa (2:31, 4:33,17:18,26:23.) Ange kera kirori bwenchili nigo akoraga okobuka gwa Kristo koba ogosemeria ase baria baganetie ogotooreka. Amariko nigo agoteba, “Naki nkabaranderia amang'ana ayananyorete ritang'ani, ng'a Kristo igakwete as'engecho y'ebibe biaito, buna agoteba amariko; naende ng'a agatindekwa, naende akaboka, rituko ria gatato, buna agoteba amariko;” 1 Abakorintho 15:3-4. Aye’ngencho mono, Ebibilia nigo egotebereria naze ki ogokwa na okoboka kwa Yeso kogotoa egesoero kia igoro. Egesusuro kie’bibe namakweri. Nyasae agatonga mwanyabantho kare omoikeranu. Korende Adamu na Hawa bakamocha koigwera amachiko a Nyasae, nere akabaa egesusuro, Omogambi oyokwabera abakobuna amachiko, tari Omogambi omonyakeene Naboigo “Aba Naki eng'eria y'ebibe namakweri; korende ekeegwa kia Nyasaye nobogima bwa kare nakare ase Yesu Kristo Omonene oito.” (Aba Rumi 6:23). Nonya nogokora amaya takonyara korogeiya amabe ase Nyasae, onyore omochenu koreng’ania nobuya bwaye. “Oboronge bwaito bwonsi nigo bore buna amachanchabe are ne riko.” (isaya 64:6b). Korwa ase ekebe gia. Adamu, mwa nyabanto nigo are nokomocha kwogotaigwera amachiko ye’keene aya nyasae.“naki bonsi bakorire ebibe, barorire ng'a baremeirwe nobonene bwa Nyasaye;” (Aba Rumi 3:23). And even now it is through believing in the resurrection that we become followers who are saved. Mark writes, “And I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures;" 1 Corinthians 15:3-4. Therefore, the Bible teaches that belief and following Jesus leads to the fulfillment of life. The consequences of sin and transgression. God judges humanity because of disobedience. When Adam and Eve disobeyed God’s command, they fell into sin, The penalty for sin is death, but God’s plan to save people from sin is revealed in His Son Jesus Christ, "For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23). But despite knowing the truth about God, people still choose to disobey Him, rejecting His forgiveness. “All have turned aside, together they have become worthless; no one does good, no, not one.” (Isaiah 64:6b). Because of this. Adam’s descendants are all born with a sinful nature and are unable to please God. “for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God;” (Romans 3:23). Sin is not just big things like murder or blasphemy, but also includes love of money, hatred of enemies, and deceit of tongue and pride. Because of sin, everyone has deserved death – eternal separation from God in hell. Sin causes many problems in life, leading to broken relationships with God, others, and ourselves, resulting in guilt, shame, and emptiness. This condition of sin separates us from God and prevents us from experiencing true joy and peace. Eve also believed in the lie instead of the truth. However, God promised Adam and Eve hope through a descendant, who would crush the serpent’s head and restore their relationship with God. (Genesis 3:15)This promise pointed forward to God’s ultimate solution—His own Son (Jesus)—who would conquer sin and its effects on humanity. Jesus willingly went to the cross, suffering the punishment we deserve, and rose again triumphantly from the grave. The sacrifice of Jesus provides a way for us to be reconciled to God, and those who believe in Him receive forgiveness and new life; therefore, anyone who trusts in the life of Jesus will experience forgiveness and restoration. ekegusii: Amachiko nareo ao ao ase ense eye tomenyete agototang'ana naende boigo amachiko nareo ayagototang'ana gochia ase Nyasae. Richiko rie 1.OMONENE NYASAE NAGWANCHETE, NAENDE OKOEIRE OMOROBERIO BWOGOKUMIA ASE OBOGIMA BWAO. OBWANCHANI BWA NYASAE Naki Nyasae ayianchete ense, goika akarua Omwana oye omomoima, erinde monto onde bwensi oyomwegenlre tasira, korende abe nobogima bwa kare na kare. Yohana 3:16 OMOROBERIO O'NYASAE ASE AYE OMONYENE Omoibi tagocha, otatiga aibe, na konyenya, na gosaria; Inche nigo nachete erio babe nobogima, naende babe naborobwo obonge. Yohana 10:10 Inee inki gekogera abanto abange batabwati obogima obwo? Nase engencho... Richiko ria 2. MWANYABANTO NOMONYABIBE Ebibe biaye biagerire bweatananire korwa ase Nayasae, ase igo tamanyeti obwanchani na omoroberio O'Nayasae ase obogima bwaye. MWANYABANTO NOMONYABIBE Ekiagera bonsi bakorire ebibe, na baremeirwe nobonene bwa Nyasae. Abarumi 3:23 Mwanyabanto igo atongetwe abe omosani O'Nyasae, korende ere akarigia enchera yokogenda kobwaye na obosani bwaye na Nyasae bokabutoka. Eke nakio Ebibilia ekoroka ebibe. Ase omogwekano... - Ekero mwanyabanto akoba mamincha ya Nyasae. - Ekero mwanyabanto atari komosika Nyasae. - Ekero mwanyabanto atari komenya ime yechinchera ching'ikeranu chia Nyasae. MWANYABANTO OATANANIRWE KORWA ASE NYASAE Taibo, obobe bwaino nabwo bwabaatananire korwa ase Nyasae Oino. Ebibe biaino biagerire Omonene obisire obosio bwaye korwa asemore, ase igo tari koigwa ogosaba kwaino. Isaya 59:2 Nyasae nomochenu na mwanyabanto nomonyabibe. Mwanyabanto origirie chinchera chiokomoikera Nyasae ase chinchera ao ao: goetera ase Ekanisa, ogokora okuya, gokonya abanto bande, korende ase chinguru chiaye osinyirwe. |Richiko na 3. YESO KRISTO NERE ENCHERA YOKA YOKORUSIA EBIBE Yeso Kristo agakwa ase engencho y'ebibe biaito erio mwanyabanto anyare komanya obwanchani na omoroberio o Nyasae ase obogima bwaye. AGAKWA NAENDE AKABOKA: Ekiagera Kristo nere agakwa ara rimo ase engencho y'ebibe. Ere oyorenge omonyene oboronge agachandwa ase engencho yabatari abaronge, erinde atorente ase Nyasae. I Petero 3:18 YESO IMOYO ARE Nyuma y'ogochandwa kwaye akeorokia asebare ase ebiorokererio ebinge ng'a moyo are. Akaba okobaorokera ase engaki y'amatuko emerongo ene, na gokwana nabarabwo igoro y'oboruoti bwa Nyasae. Ogokora Kw'Abatomwa 1:3 YESO NERE ENCHERA YEKEENE YOKA Yeso akamoiraneria, Inche ninche enchera, na ekeene, na obogima; monto onde tagocha ase Tata otatiga goetera asencle. Yohana 14:6 Goetera ase ogokwa kwa Yeso Kristo ase omosaraba mwanyabanto onyarire goika ase Nyasae. Okomanya amachiko aya atato oka taisaini. Ogochika gwa kane nigo gogokomanyia buna oranyare komonyora Kristo ase obogima bwao... Richiko ria 4. NEKOGWENERETE KOMOMANYA YESO KRISTO BUNA OMOTORIA NA OMOKONYI BWOBOGIMA BWAO. Nario oramanye obwanchani na omoroberio o'Nyasae igoro yobogima bwao. GOIKA OMONYORE KRISTO GOETERA ASE OKWEGENA Korende bonsi abamwanchete, akabaa okobua babe abana ba Nyasae, nabwo bariegenire erieta riaye. Yohana 1:12 Naki mwatoorigwe ase obuya, ase enchera y'okwegena; ayio tarwete asemore abanyene, korende nekeegwa kia Nyasae gose tari ase ogokora, monto onde tacha gwetogia. Abaebeso 2:8,9 NIGO OKOMONYORA KRISTO GOETERA ASE OKOMWARIGANIA ASOE ASE ENKORO YAO Rigereria, ninteneine gesieri gotura; omonto karaigwe eriogi riane na koigora egesieri, ninsoe asare, nindagere amo nere, na ere amo nainche. Okomanoka 3:20 Komwanchera Yeso Kristo asoe ase enkoro yao nokomanya ng'a: - Goonchoka gochia ase Nyasae na gotiga ebibe - Komwegena Kristo asoe enkoro yao naende akwabere ebibe biao. - Omwanchere aonchore obogima bwao obe buna atagete ere. Inee bicha ki ere omoreng'anio oo? Inee bicha ki oganetie ebe omoreng'anio bwo obogima bwao? Ayakobwatia nomoroberio buna oramonyore Kristo ase obogima bwao. NABO ORAMONYORE KRISTO BONO IGA Morangerie Yesu asoe ime yobogima bwao. Mwegene Omonene anyare kogokorera kobwatekana na eira yaye. Ere Yesu bwanchire akwariganie naende naganetie komenya ime yenkoro yao. Nabo orasabe iga. Omonene Yeso Kristo, ninkoganetie. Naigoire egesieri kiobogima bwane naende nagwanchire obe omotoria naende omonene one ekiagera inche natigire ebibe. Imbuya mono ase okonyabera ebibe biane. Kabe omonyakerogo bwobogima bwane. Onkore omonto oria otagete imbe ase obosio bwao. AMINA Inee Ogosaba oko inkworokia kore okogania gwenkoro yao? Onye ogosaba oko kore okogania kwomoyo oo, bono saba onyare komwanchera Kristo asoe ime yobogirna bwao. BUNA ORAMANYE NG'A YESU OSOIRE IME YE ENKORO YAO Bono inee? Kwamwariganeirie Yeso ime yobogima bwao? Naki omanyete? Kobwatekana na Okomanoka 3:20 Ng'ai Kristo are bono iga? Kristo otebire buna nachiche ime yobogima bwao. Inee nang'ainererie gose? Naki oramanye ng'a Nyasae okoiraneirie ogosaba kwao? (Egekogera natebete ng'a onde bwensi oranyegene amo na amariko ane nakonyeke ekiagera ariegenire erieta ri'Omwana o Nyasae!) OYORE NA YESO NARE NOBOGIMA BWA KARE NA KARE Naki obo nabwo oborori, ng'a Nyasae otoeire obogima bwa kare na kare, na obogima obo nigo bore ime ase Omwana oye. Ere oyore n'omwana, nare nobogima; ere oyotari n'Omwana o Nyasae, tari nobogima. Nabarikeire inwe amang'ana aya, erinde momanye ng'a more nobogima bwa kare na kare, inwe abwo mwariegenire erieta ri'Omwana o'Nyasae. 1 Yohana 5:11-13 Mwaakere Nyasae imbuya mono kera rituko kiagera Kristo nare ime yobogima bwao. "Mokoborokereria kobwata aya onsi nabachigete; na rora, inche nigo inde amo nainwe amatuko onsi goika omoerio bw'ense" (Mathayo 28:20). Okoeire obogima bwa kare na kare. Abakristo nigo bagwenerete kwegena omonene Nyasae oito amo nering'ana riaye buna erikire ase ebibilia. Neba buna oranyare kweigwa aye omonyene, manya nga Kristo ere tari goonchoka ase obogima bwao. "Timoba abanchi chibesa, moisaneke nebi more nabio, ekiagera ere omonyene otebire, "Tinkogotiga nonya ng'ake, gose tingokoremera" (Abaiberania 13:5) Ebigicha eye yegari igo egotworokia obomaene bwe Ebibilia. Okwegena amo na okweigwa igo bigokora emeremo ase obogima two omoknisto. - Obomaene bwomonene igo bobwate chinguru chiogototang'ana - (Einchini) - Igo tobwateranetigwe nechinguru chiobomaene na okwegena - (Amaguta ye ebetironi) - Buna tokoigwera obomaene, ebirengererio biaito igo bikobwatia enchera endonge. - (Orotuba gose eturera) - Igo tokwegena Nyasae nobomaene bwaye korende tari okweigwa gwaito Ekero twakorire ebibe nigo egwenerete twangame nere natwabere. Ase go tonyara kwegena ebirengererio biao korende bwegene obomaene bwe ring'ana ria Nyasae. BONO KWAMONYORIRE KRISTO Ekero kwamonyorete Kristo ase enkoro yao ebinto ebinge igo biakoregete. - Kristo agasoa ime yenkoro yao (Okomanoka 3:20 na Abakorosai 1:27) - Ebibe biao bikaberwa (Abakorosai 1:14) - Okaba omwana o Nyasae (Yohana 1:12) - Kwanyarire konyora omoroberio omyuya noborai obuya bwa Nyasae ase obogima bwao (Yohana 10:10 na II Abakorinto 5:14, 15, 17). Inee nonyare korengereria igoro ya kende gionsi ekiya kebuete Kristo oyore ime yenkoro yao? Onye nabo mwaakere Nyasae imbuya mono ase ogosaba bono iga ase amaya agokoreire. Goakera Nyasae imbuya mono igo gokworokia okwegena. Tosabe bono tosibogete. Egento kende ninki? BUNA ORANYARE GOKINA ASE EKEMOIKA Buna omwana omoke agokina naboigo egwenerete omokristo nere akine ekemoika. Amang'ana akobwatia nabo aranyare kogokonya. EKANISA IGO ERE YENGENCHO ENENE MONO Ekero chinko chibekire amo, igo chikoyia noborabu obonene mono. Beka oroko rokoyia ase riraba rire nobokendu nomorero oye igo okorima naende obe ekegenga, chinko chinyinge nigo chigwoka buya. Ase omobwekano oyo: igo ere obogima obokong'u mono ekero ogotema komenya obogima bwegekristo aye bweka. Igo ere buya mono kegima ekero mokobwaterana nabakristo bande baria bamomanyete Yeso Kristo buna omotoria obo (Abaibirania 10:25) Goika ogende ekanisa eria abanto begenete buna Ebibilia nering'ana riobomaene ria Nyasae, naende ase Yeso Kristo agotogigwa buna nomwana O Nyasae.

ekegusii: Okobokigwa No’omochakano Engaki yo ogokwa no kobokigwa abanto abange ngochengera bare nakogokera okobokigwa kwo omotori oito omonene, Yeso Kirisito (Tito 2:13). Ase bare, eri nario rituko rinene rio amotimoko ase ekarenda yegekirisito.1 Amangana yo kobokigwa naro amangana yengencho mono ase obokeresito: Kobokigwa gotaiyo titobwati komanya ase ogotorigwa gwaito korwa ase ebibe biaito (1 Abakorinto 15:12–18). Ebimanyererio ebitangani Okobokigwa nigo kore ase ringana, naboigo ase ebimanyire mono, mbiri bioka gose ebimanyererio ebitanganitobwate bia abakeresito biokorikwa igoro you okobokigwa. Ebio esiko ekogenda gochi 1 Abathesaloniki; ekemo kiomochakano bwo amarube a Paulo, ayio arigetwe AD 50.2 Emiaka chirifu ibere nyuma yogokwa kwa kirisito. Omoganda norengeo bwabanto abwo bare koiranerania nga ere nabogetigwe korwa ase amakweri, naboigo akaagacha oboroso obuya ase amangana aya; naboigo amangana buna aya tari koba botuko. Korende enchiri ngoteba ere. Nonya ne miaka chiribu nyuma yebikoro ebio bigotebererwa (sirika AD 30–33), genda magega ase amangana a kare gose ase ogobwatia ogokoro.3 Naboigo amangana aya a kare tabwati amangana amange ayio are rirube riengencho ria Paulo. Ekio naki gekogera twateba nga ngogenda ere magega mono ogochaka ogotangani okuo kwabwatetu nakogachwa.4 “Ringana rio okobokigwa gwa kristo ne ringana rie engencho mono gochi ase abakeresito:Kobokigwa gotaiyo,Nto bwati gosemeria gwo okoborigwa kwe ebibe biaito (1 Abakorinto 15:12–18)”. Ekanisa entangani Okobokigwa ngoteberera kore ase chinchera inye (gwachagete AD 67–855) ngotebwa bire buna nigo bire ebiogotantania, korende ebinge bioogatantani mbirio ao nainde buna torakagere ase chingencho echi inye chingao chie egento emaiaka emenge nyuma yo okoba. Nigo bire ne binto ebinge buna nongo orosetie omoganda bwa abakungu abwo bachiete ase rikuruma, nga amaraika na abere arenge ao gose nerimo nakogenderera. Ebinge bie ebi mbiri bio ogotantani, buna bitamentiri aroro, ase ekio orokererio; ekemo ngetebe rimo nga riraika riakwanete, naboigo ekeorokererio ekende getebe nga’ amaraika nonsi akwanete. Nebe ogotantania onye ekeo rokererio gegoteba riraika erimo rioka. Nkorenta ere engencho nga abasacha baarigete baarigete amangana aya nabo barainyore amangana amangao nonya gakororekana amangana amange ase otebia kwabo kwe ebinto biakorekanete. Teri korenta engencho goteba nga’ ase engencho ya abakungu bare ase erisiti, Kobokigwa ngokorekaneti bi.6 Naboigo, okobokigwa kwo obobui ngaange kware koba ase enchera etakageire ase emeganda emetangani ya abayaudi bare gocha goteba rikuruma ritabwati kende. Abayaudi abatangani mbaegenete mono igoro yo obogima nyuma yobonde, abande mbaegenete okobokigwa, nabende tibaegenete (buna abasadusesi (Mathayo 22:23). Nabande mbaegenete nga mbande babo bara bokigwe; korende onde tari ase abayuda baegenete nga’omonto oyomo narenge gochi kobokigwa nyuma ya onde bwensi. Eke nakio kiagerete abaorokigwa batabwate bomanyi bonde bwenshi igoro yeki yeso are goteba ekero abanete ogokwa kwaye naboigo nokobokig. Ebimanyererio bio okobokigwa gwa kristo gochia ase aba orokigwa baye Ebimanyererio mbireo nga,krwa omochakano bwe orogendo rwa abakristo, Okobokigwa gwa kristo ngwatumegete gosomia keria abaorokigwa baye baraetere ase okobokigwa. Ase 1 Abathesaloniki 4:13–18, Paulo nkorwa are ekemanyererio igoro yo okobokigwa; Ntwegenete nga yeso nakwete naboigo akaboka naende naboigo ntwegenete nga nyasae narente na yeso baria bakwete amo nere. Igo okobokigwa kwa yeso nkoba kore engencho yo okobokigwa kwa abakeresto ekero arache. Ase abaibiribi Philippians 3:20–21, nkomanya tore nga okobokigwa kwe emebere yaito nebe buna oria o yeso kristo. english: While we wait for the blessed hope—the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ (Titus 2:13)—let us also be eager, with a great expectation, for the fulfillment of the Christian faith.1 The basis for this waiting is the promise of resurrection, which is central to Christianity: Resurrection guarantees that we will not experience permanent death because of our sins (1 Corinthians 15:12–18). Important background information This waiting is based on certainty, and it involves understanding certain things, namely, how the beliefs of Christians were established during the time of this waiting. This matter is discussed in 1 Thessalonians; specifically, Paul's account of his visit, which occurred around AD 50.2 Several years after the crucifixion of Christ. The purpose was to encourage believers who were being persecuted and to remind them of the promises; and also to ensure that those promises remain valid. Continue reading this chapter to understand more. After about three years following these events (approximately AD 30–33), there began to spread the teachings of the earlier apostles.3 However, these earlier teachings did not contradict the later teachings of Paul. This is why we can confidently say that they both convey the same message regarding the essential truths.4 “The foundation of the hope of Christ and the foundation of everything else for Christians: Resurrection guarantees that we will not experience permanent death because of our sins (1 Corinthians 15:12–18).” The early church This waiting was understood by the leaders (who lived from approximately AD 67–855) to mean that some things would happen, while others would not occur until much later, and these latter matters were often misunderstood. These things included the persecution of rulers, along with angels and messengers who claimed to have revelations. Some of these claims were true, but most were false; and the false revelations often lacked credibility. Nevertheless, the truth remained clear despite these distortions. Therefore, let us diligently examine what the teachers teach, ensuring that their teachings align with the fundamental principles and do not introduce innovations that contradict established doctrines. There should be no teaching that contradicts the teachings of the apostles, for the resurrection is at the heart of our faith.6 Moreover, this waiting has been likened to a man who entrusted his property to servants while he traveled abroad, expecting them to manage it responsibly during his absence. The Jewish leaders questioned John the Baptist about his identity and authority, seeking confirmation that he was indeed the expected messenger. They also debated whether they should believe in Jesus, questioning whether He had come to fulfill their expectations (as suggested by the Sadducees – Matthew 22:23). And they questioned whether they should accept Him based on His own merits, because the Jews did not recognize Him as the Messiah until after the events unfolded. But now, let those who are resurrected testify to the abundance of life that Jesus offers, and let this testimony lead others to believe in Him. The beliefs surrounding Christ's return concern those who are awaiting it. These beliefs include the hope of reunion with loved ones who have passed away, and the expectation that Christ's return will bring comfort and joy to believers. As Paul wrote in 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18, he shared his understanding of the resurrection; explaining that when Jesus returns, those who have died in Christ will rise first, and then those who are still alive will join them in the air to meet the Lord. Therefore, the resurrection of Jesus is the foundation of the Christian hope, surpassing all earthly expectations. In Philippians 3:20–21, we find assurance that our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await the coming of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ. [Ed.: This translation is incomplete. Omongina Clemencia Mokeira Emegano y' ororeri rwaito ntwe Abagusii n' emenge. Nigo togotebigwa buna ntwe Abagusii twensi nigo twarwete aaria Misri. Kobwatekana n' omogano oyomo, ororeri rwaito nigo rore iga: Omonto akaibora Enonko. Enonko akaibora Ribiaka. Ribiaka akaibora Magoma. Magoma akaibora Osogo. Bono Osogo nere akaibora Mogusii. Bono sokoro yaito Mogusii, akamanya koibora Mogusero, Mochorwa, Mobasi, Nyaribari, Mogirango, Mogetutu, Monchari, na Momachoge. Okonywoma n' okonywomwa gochia ase ebisaku binde nkare gwaansete: Aaiga Transmara nao omosubati oyomo o Gusii orenge korokwa Koinania anywometwe n' Omomanyi na gotigara. Gatigara oo, ntwe tokagenderera n' orogendo rwaito gochia Botende. Ase igo, twensi n' abamo n' Abamanyi egekogera mbabwate amanyinga aito. Abangina b' omogaka Mogusii Mogusii nanywomete abakungu batano buna ekobwatia: 1. Moguche Ibu ore korokwa Kemunto akaegwa erieta rie ebitinge akarokwa Bonareri. 2. Nyamisanchu ore korokwa Kwamboka oetwe Nyaboke, koba erieta rie ebitinge. 3. Bosibori nere obwate omomura okorokwa Mocharwa. 4. Bwari nere oiborete omomura okorokwa Omache, o Monchari. Omache nere naende orogetwe Onchari Omache, Chindiba Chia Bokendu. 5. Mokeira, oyio oiborete Sereti ore Omogusero. Emegano yo ogocha n' okonganya kwa Abagusii nigo ere emenge. Ase boigo, emegano eye tiyarigetwe aande. Ntwe nigo tokoyerika bono buna togotebigwa. Ase boigo, nigo togotebigwa buna ase chingaki echio chionsi , eganga ya Abagusii nigo yarenge konganya ase okorigia ense entobu ase ebimeri. Gotenena nkwarengeo. Onye ememiso gose mesabakwa tiyarengeo, abagaka nigo barenge goteba nga "Togenderere gochia motwe". Ase okonganya kwabo, nigo barenge korigia ase ememiso amo n' emesabakwa ere emenge. Ebi nabio biare kobaorokia buna ase ayio natobu. Omogano omotangani nigo ore iga: Omogano oyo nigo ogoteba buna Omogusii nigo arwete korwa chinsemo chia Irianyi gose ensemo ya Mombasa, mbaka agacha goika aiga nka Gusii. Ase Abagusii, Mombasa eyio, nigo naende yare yare korokwa Mokendo o' Iruma. Nigo togotebigwa buna Mogusii narenge na momura omwabo ore korokwa Otere oyio onaende ore korokwa Mogikoyo. Abamura aba babere nabwo batirete korwa Irianyi ya Mokendo o Iruma (Mombasa) na gocha gatigati ya Kenya. Aiga gatigati ya Kenya, Otere nao atigarete. Mogusii amo na basubati bamwabo bakanyora buna ememiso amo n' emesabakwa tiyarenge aaiga gatigati ya kenya. Korende Mogusii, kare na abasubati bamwabo bakagenderera ase okong'anya ko batiga Otere aaira gatigati ya Kenya. Omosubati oyomo ore korokwa Moragori, nigo atigarete aaria aange na Mt Elgon (Boruya) ase okonganya, akaba ngina Abamaragoli. Omosubati onde, Mosoba agatigarera igaaria Suba. Ase boigo, omosubati onde omwabo Mogusii, ore korokwa Mokogoti, naende gose Mokoro, nigo achiete agatigara aaria Botende (kuria). Korwa gatigati ya Kenya, Mogusii nigo atorete aaria Boruya. Nonya nabo igo, nigo banganyete naende korwa Boruya na komotiga Moragori aroro. Korwa abwo, bagatirimboka gochia chinsemo chia Irianyi ya Boruya na goika Egesumu (kisumu). Below: Beautiful Mokendo O' Iruma: Omogano onde bw' Abagusii nigo ogoteba buna Mogusii amo na abamura babwabo abwo barenge Otere [Mogikoyo], Momeru, Mokamba, Moragori amo na Moembu nigo baimogete ase orogendo korwa aaria Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. Ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete Mogikoyo, Momeru Mokamba, amo na Moembu bagatigarera aaria Central kenya, korende Moragori amo na Mogusii barabwo bakagenderera n' orogendo. Aaiga ase ensemo ya Egesumu, bakaagacha egesarate gio okomenya (ebisumu) abwo Egesumu (Kisumu), korende chimori chikaagacherwa ebisumu ebinge. Mogusii akaroka asaya, Egesumu (Kisumu) korwa ase ebisumu ebi baroseti. Buna togotebigwa, aaiga Kisumu nao omomura oyomo orenge korokwa Orechi [Enswe ase Ekegere] aiboreretwe. Ase boigo, aaiga nao omoiseke orenge korokwa Kemunto (gulf ase Ekenyamorero) aiboreretwe. Mogusii tachieti komenya abwo Kisumu ase amatuko amange. Ogocha kwa Abagere amo n' riroba gotaba riitobu gokagera Abagusii naende bakanganya korwa Egesumu kogenda ase akorokwa Gwasi. Aaiga Gwasi, riroba itobu ndiarenge aroro nonya. Ase engencho eyio, Abagusii amo na abande naende bakanganya na gotiga Mosoba (Abasuba) aroro. Aaiga Bosoba nao omwana omomura orenge korokwa Mosoba aiboreretwe. Korwa Kisumu, Mogusii bagaeta na gotamboka ase Ekemunto (gulf) na kwamboka gochia ase ebitunwa bia Gusii. Ko baika Gusii, bagaatanekana. Mokoro akagenda Botende (kuria) na Mosoba akamboka kogenda Bosoba (Suba). Nonya nabo igo, Mogusii ere agatigara Gusii na mbaka rero nao are Gusii. Oyo noro omogano bw' okonganya gwaito omotangani. Aba bonsi n' abaminto. Omokamba, Omoragori, Omogikoyo, Omoembu, Omomeru, Omotende, Omosoba: Nigo tokona goitana bosa. Aba mbamura n' baiseke baminto. Omogano onde bw' omochakano bwo Omogusii nigo ogoteba buna Abagusii nigo barwete Misri (Egypt ase rero). Ritangani, nigo togotebigwa ng'a Mogusii, oyio ore ise bw' Abagusii bonsi, narenge amo na bamura babwabo abwo barenge Moragori, Mokamba, Mogikoyo, Moembu, amo na Momeru. Baminto ng'ai twarwete? Nigo togotebigwa buna Mogusii, kare na bamura bamwabo, nigo atirimbogete ase chingegu chi' oroche rwa River Nile na goeta gati gati y ense ya Ethiopia. Korwa abwo, akagenda Sudan na gosokera aaria Uganda. Korwa Uganda (Boganda), Mogusii nigo agendererete n' orogendo mbaka agaika aange na Mt. Elgon. Nigo togototebigwa aaiga Mt. Elgon, nao Mogusii aatananakenate amo na abamwabo, na kogenda kobwaye. Moragori ere agatigara aaria ange na Mt Elgon, na koba ase egesaku kia Abaluhya. Gatiga abamwabo, Mogusii akang'anya na kogenda komenya aaria aange na Siaya, eyio ere Bogere ase rero. Ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete Mogusii agatiga abawabo ase okonganya oko. Ase engencho y' chisegi korwa ase Abagere be ense eyio ya Siaya, Mogusii akang'anya naende, korwa abwo na kogenda komenya aaria Egesumu (Kisumu). Erieta "Kisumu" n' rie Ekegusii Aaiga, Egesumu, nigo Abagusii baagachete ebisumu ebinge bie chiombe, ekagera bakayaroka (Gesumu) Kisumu. Nigo togotebigwa buna aaiga Gesumu nao Mogusii amo na ng'ina, oyio ore korokwa Nyakomogendi basirerete na gotindekwa. Nonya nabo igo, chiombe chigaansa gokwa n' enchara enene ekaba abwo Egesumu. Ge enchara yaba, abana ba Mogusii tibachieti komenya igaa ase amatuko amange. Ase engencho y enchara eye, abagaka abanene b' egesaku giaito ase engaki eyio, abwo barenge Mobasi, Oibabe, Mochorwa na Mogusero bakaroberia okonganya kwa Abagusii korwa Egesumu, kogenda gochia ase ebitunwa bia Gusii ya rero. Ke emeroberio eye y' okonganya yaera, bagatamboka ase ekemunto (gulf) na goika ase ebitunwa bia Gusii ya rero. Korwa ase ebitunwa bia Gusii, bakagenderera konganya mbaka bagaika Kericho [eye nero naende ekorokwa Kabianga]. Ko baika Kabianga, obokongu bokaba. Ndagera tiyare kwama. Tari igo rioka. Esegi korwa ase Abamanyi amo no Abasigisi ekaba entindi. Komenta nayio, oborwaire obonge ase etugo amo na abanto bokabucha. Bono emechando eye yonsi ekagera Abagusii bakaroka ase aya, Kabianga. Ke emechando emenge yaba aaiga Kabianga, Abagusii bakanganya naende na koirana bagotirimboka gochia Sotik, Gelegele, Ikorongo, Trans Mara [ Emara gose Transmara, Mara Motobo, Igena ria Gamba]. Naende nigo tokona goitana bosa. Abamanyi mbabwate amanyinga aito ntwe Abagusii. Aaiga Emara Motobo nao omosubati oyomo bwa Abagusii orenge korokwa Nyakoinania anywometwe amo na Abamanyi na gotigara Bomanyi. Korwa abwo, Abagusii bakagenderera ase okonganya gochia Migori (Botende), Nyangarora, Nyakoe, Getembe [ ange na Marani], Manga Isecha (Emanga y' Ogeto, na Monyerero) ime ya Central kitutu, amo na aaria Emanga nse ya Ikuruma. Egesaku getabwati abarai nigo kegotagoka. Abarai mbakabeiroo korwa kare Abwo ase obomenyi n' okonganya gwaito gwensi korwa Egesumu, Abagusii ntwabwate abagaka abanene abwo barenge korwa oborai amo n' obosemia. Gati y' abagaka abwo ase chingaki echio nigo barenge koraa chinyomba chia Abagusii nigo barenge buna ekobwatia: [I]. Abanchari [Omogaka Oisukia nere orenge omorai]. [II]. Ababasi [Mogichoncho, oyio orenge omomura omonene o Mobasi nere orenge omorai]. [II]. Abasweta [ Omogaka Manyanta nere orenge omorai]. Ka moranche inyora buna Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge nabwo Abasweta. Abagusii mbebagete amarieta gete ye chingiti ao ao, amarieta ayio akabwata. Omogaka Manyanta nigo arenge koraaa Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge bonsi. [IV]. Abagetutu [ Omobani Sakawa nere orenge omorai]. Ase okoinyora naende, Omobani Sakawa nigo arwete ase enyomba ya Abageka aaria Bogetutu. Abageka nabwo barenge enyomba enchorwa ya ababani ase Abagusii. Tochiesera Abageka.
