english: Good afternoon, we greet you together with Petronillah Ogoti Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Greetings also to Abner Nyaberi, Kenyatta University. The Legend Of The Gusii People: Oral Sources On The Ground: Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba; Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache; Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache; Recorded on May 26, 2012. These are the topics: The Gusii: Where Did We Come From? The First Gusii.com Blog Post On February 22, 2009. "Is It Good To Abandon Old Customs And Traditions?" By Clemencia Mokeira The history of our ancestors among the Gusii people. It is said that the Gusii people originally came from Egypt. According to this legend, our ancestry goes like this: This man gave birth to Enonko. Enonko gave birth to Ribiaka. Ribiaka gave birth to Magoma. Magoma gave birth to Osogo. This Osogo then gave birth to Mogusii. This lineage of Mogusii knows his descendants, namely Mogusero, Mochorwa, Mobasi, Nyaribari, Mogirango, Mogetutu, Monchari, and Momachoge. Visiting and being visited brings great joy to those who have wealth: The people of Transmara and their fellow Gusii people often visit Koinania and are honored by the elders and respected. Because of this respect, they travel along our paths to Botende. Today, there are also those among us who live with the elders and learn good manners from them. Ancestors of the Mogusii clan Mogusii had five sons when he settled down: 1. Moguche Ibu, who was born to Kemunto and raised in a homestead near Bonareri. 2. Nyamisanchu, who was born to Kwamboka and Nyaboke, also in a homestead. 3. Bosibori, who inherited property from Mocharwa. 4. Bwari, who inherited property from Omache, of Monchari. Omache was named after Onchari Omache, a descendant of Bokendu. 5. Mokeira, who inherited secrets from Omogusero. The traditions and unity of the Gusii people are very strong. However, this tradition has not been fully documented. That is why we remember what was said. However, it is said that once upon a time, when the land was full of peace, the Gusii people lived in harmony and shared everything equally. Let us be careful. Anyone whose eyes are closed does not see, so the elders say, “Look carefully.” During their gatherings, they always share stories and discuss important matters. Those who are present often boast about their wealth. The story that is told goes like this: This story says that the Gusii people migrated from a place called Irianyi, all the way to Mombasa, until they reached a point where they recognized the land as Gusii. The Gusii people, at Mombasa, were later led by Mokendo of Iruma. It is said that the Gusii people did not travel alone; they were accompanied by Otere, who also led Mogikoyo. These leaders brought people from Irianyi of Mokendo and Iruma (Mombasa) and settled in the central region of Kenya. In the central region of Kenya, Otere also settled. The Gusii people and their companions agreed that their stories and discussions should not be forgotten in the central region of Kenya. Therefore, the Gusii people, along with their companions, decided to send Otere to settle in the central region of Kenya. One companion, born to Moragori, settled near Mount Elgon (Boruya) during their travels, associating with the Abamaragoli. Another companion, Mosoba, settled in the area of Suba. Also, another companion of the Gusii people, born to Mokogoti, went to Mokoro and finally settled in Botende (Kurian). From the central region of Kenya, the Gusii people moved to Boruya. But despite this, they continued to visit Boruya and consult Moragori. From there, they migrated to Irianyi of Boruya and settled in Egesumu (Kisumu). Below: Beautiful Mokendo O' Iruma: It is said that the Gusii people and their fellow tribesmen traveled together, including Otere [Mogikoyo], Momeru, Mokamba, Moragori, and Moembu, on their journey to Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. It is known that Mogikoyo, Momeru, Mokamba, and Moembu settled in Central Kenya, while Moragori and the Gusii people continued their journey. From the shores of Lake Kisumu, they began to explore and discover (fish) around Egesumu (Kisumu), and this became a common practice. The Gusii people sought sustenance, and Egesumu (Kisumu) provided them with abundant fish. As it is said, the shores of Kisumu and the surrounding areas near Orechi [the banks of River Ekegere] were discovered. Furthermore, the shores and surroundings near Kemunto (the Gulf of Ekenyamorero) were also discovered. The Gusii people started exploring around Kisumu and its environs. The people of Abagere and their traditions helped the Gusii people navigate towards Egesumu, heading towards Gwasi. In Gwasi, the tradition was very strong. During those times, the Gusii people and others associated with Mosoba (the Basuba) also mingled. The people of Bosoba and their children near Mosoba were also discovered. From Kisumu, the Gusii people returned and camped near Ekemunto (the gulf) and collected resources from the land of Gusii. When they left Gusii, they dispersed. One group went to Botende (Kuria), and another moved towards Bosoba (Suba). Over time, the Gusii people remained in Gusii, and their descendants are still Gusii today. This is the story of our ancestors and origins. These are all clans. Omokamba, Omoragori, Omogikoyo, Omoembu, Omomeru, Omotende, Omosoba: These are the names of the clans. These tribesmen and their families are numerous. It is said that the history of the Gusii people tells us that the Gusii people came from Egypt. Traditionally, it is said about the Gusii people, that they, along with their fellow tribesmen like Moragori, Mokamba, Mogikoyo, Moembu, and Momeru, migrated together. Where did these people come from? It is said that the Gusii people, along with their fellow tribesmen, crossed the great river Nile and reached the lands of Ethiopia. From there, they traveled to Sudan and settled in the area of Uganda. From Uganda (Boganda), the Gusii people continued their journey until they arrived near Mount Elgon. It is said that near Mount Elgon, the Gusii people separated from their companions and continued onward. Moragori settled in his own area near Mount Elgon, and interacted with the people of Abaluhya. Following his companions, the Gusii people continued to explore the area near Siaya, which is now called Bogere. I understand that this is where Mogusii settled with his people during their migration. In the region of Siaya, among the people of Abagere, Mogusii continued on, and then proceeded to explore the area of Egesumu (Kisumu). The name “Kisumu” comes from Ekegusii. From there, in Egesumu, the Gusii people found abundant resources including livestock, and the land was fertile (Gesumu) Kisumu. It is said that in Gesumu, Mogusii and his people prospered, and were blessed with plenty. Over time, the livestock increased greatly, and there was a large settlement in Egesumu. Because of this settlement, the children of Mogusii did not need to search for food from distant places. In the vicinity of this settlement, prominent leaders emerged from various areas, such as Mobasi, Oibabe, Mochorwa, and Mogusero, who organized the affairs of the Gusii people in Egesumu, working to protect the wealth of Gusii. Through this organization, they began to move from the gulf and settle in the territories of Gusii. From the territories of Gusii, they continued to organize themselves until they reached Kericho [which is also known as Kabianga]. When they arrived at Kabianga, there was conflict. The ground was very swampy. The weather was hot. The land was difficult due to the presence of the Abamanyi and Abasigisi people. However, despite these challenges, the elders and warriors persevered. All this hardship led the Gusii people to settle here, in Kabianga. As more settlements developed around Kabianga, the Gusii people moved further and established settlements in Sotik, Gelegele, Ikorongo, Trans Mara [Transmara, Mara Motobo, the ridge of Gamba]. And then they started to spread out. The Abamanyi people understood their ways just like the Gusii people. From Mara Motobo and its surroundings, the Gusii people extended their territory towards Nyakoinania, interacting with both the Abamanyi and the Bomanyi people. From there, the Gusii people continued to organize themselves and expand towards Migori (Botende), Nyangarora, Nyakoe, Getembe [including Marani], Manga Isecha (the plains of Ogeto, and Monyerero) in the central highlands, and also the plains of Ikuruma. The land became increasingly populated. People built homes everywhere. Because of this extensive migration from Egesumu, the Gusii people remembered the prominent leaders who came from different regions. The stories of these leaders and their deeds have been passed down through generations, becoming part of the history of the Gusii people: [I]. The warriors [The leader Oisukia who was also a warrior]. [II]. The priests [Mogichoncho, who was also a great healer of Mobasi and a warrior]. [III]. The diviners [The leader Manyanta who was also a warrior]. They say that the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge were also diviners. The Gusii people remember them fondly, remembering their wisdom and knowledge. The leader Manyanta was particularly skilled in dealing with the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge. [IV]. The rainmakers [The leader Sakawa who was also a warrior]. It is said that Omobani Sakawa possessed the power to control the weather for the people of Bogetutu. These people also had the power to influence events among the Abagusii. Honor the rainmakers. english: |Colossians To the Colossians 1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy his brother, 2 to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. 3 We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you, 4 having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the saints, 5 because of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you have heard about through the word of truth, the gospel 6 which has come to you, just as it also does throughout the whole world, and is bearing fruit and increasing—just as it has done among you since the day you heard it and understood the grace of God in truth, 7 just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf, 8 who has told us of your love in the Spirit. 9 And so, from the day we heard this, we have not ceased praying for you, asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, 10 so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge of God, 11 strengthened with all power according to His glorious might, for all perseverance and patience with joy, 12 giving thanks to the Father who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in light, 13 who delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of His beloved Son, 14 in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. 15 He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation. 16 For by Him all things were created, both in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through Him and for Him. 17 And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together. 18 He is the head of the body, the church, He who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that He might be supreme in everything. 19 For in Him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of His cross. 20 And though you were once alienated from God and hostile in your mind because of your evil deeds, 21 yet He has now reconciled you in His flesh through death, in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before Him. 22 But you, being made alive in Christ, were raised up together with Him and seated with Him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus, 23 to demonstrate His surpassing greatness in generations to come, so that with eternal glory He might show the wealth of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. 24 To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. 25 Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of His body, which is the church. 26 I have become its servant according to God’s plan entrusted to me for your benefit. 27 To them God willed to make known how great are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ living in you, the hope of glory. 28 We proclaim Him, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone mature in Christ. 29 For this reason I also suffer, striving according to His power that works within me. 1 So then, just as we have received from the Lord and taught you, you must live in love with one another, as you learned from God. 2 And further, we instruct you to live a life worthy of the calling you have received. 3 Be eager to maintain unity in the Spirit, binding yourselves together with peace. 4 There is one body, one Spirit—just as you were called to one hope when you were called— 5 one Lord, one faith, one baptism, 6 one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all. 7 But to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of Christ’s gift. 8 Therefore it says: “When He ascended on high, He led captivity captive and gave gifts to men.” 9 What does this mean? That He descended to the regions below. This is the One who ascended far above all heaven, so that He might fill everything.) 10 Now to Him who is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us, 11 to Him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen. 12 For we write to you, brothers and sisters, encouraging you to recognize and acknowledge God’s grace toward you, which was shown to you through our ministry. 13 Therefore, we urge you not to become discouraged because of the suffering of our fellow believers. It is God’s will that you endure hardship for His name. 14 For just as we told you earlier, we tell you again: The kingdom of God is not about eating and drinking, but about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. 15 For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on earthly things, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on spiritual things. 16 But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Him. 17 However, if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Him. 18 But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; and He has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the strong. 19 For God’s wisdom seems foolish to this world, but God knows that its wisdom is true. And the world’s wisdom seems wise, but God knows that it is foolishness. 20 So let us not boast about what we can do, but rather rejoice in what God has done for us. 21 We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in worldly terms. 22 Let others think we are crazy, but you know that we are sane when we speak of God. 23 We are weak, but you are strong. You dishonor us, but we honor you. 24 We appear foolish, but you are respected. We are hungry and thirsty, while you are well-fed. We are poorly dressed, while you are clothed in fine garments. 25 We are treated like the scum of the earth, but you are esteemed by the world. 1 Now those who are believers should live according to the example of Christ, who gave himself up for us, so that we might have eternal life with God. 2 Those who are not believers should not judge those who are. 3 For our lives are hidden with Christ in God. 4 Christ will reveal his glory in us, and we will share in his splendor. 5 Let us not be proud or arrogant, but humble ourselves before God. 6 Let us not seek our own interests, but the interests of others. 7 Let us not think highly of ourselves, but instead look to God for guidance. 8 Let us not compare ourselves to others, but focus on pleasing God. 9 Let us not be lazy or idle, but work hard to serve God. 10 Let us not be selfish or greedy, but generous and compassionate. 11 There is no difference between Jew and Gentile, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian and Scythian, slave and free—for Christ is all, and in all. 12 Therefore, as God’s chosen people, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. 13 Bear with each other and forgive one another, just as the Lord forgave you. And above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins. 14 Let peace reign in your hearts, and let the peace of Christ control you. 15 Be thankful in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus. 16 Let the message of Christ dwell among you richly, teaching and admonishing one another with all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God. 17 And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. 18 Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. 19 Husbands, love your wives and do not mistreat them. 20 Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord. 21 Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord. 22 Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, as though serving Christ. 23 Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters. 24 Remember that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord, for you are serving the Lord Christ. 25 So whoever practices deceit, let him know that he will reap what he sows. 1 Now we who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not to please ourselves. 2 Each of us should please our neighbors for their good, to build them up. 3 For even Christ did not please himself, but took on the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. 4 And being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by obeying to death—even death on a cross! 5 Therefore God exalted him to the highest position and gave him the name above all names. 6 This is why, at the mention of the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth. 7 And every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. 8 Now about Philemon, our dear brother, and Archippus, our fellow prisoner: 9 I send greetings to you, along with the church that meets in your home. 10 Greetings to Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. 11 To Mark, who ministered with Barnabas and Paul. 12 And to Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner. Instructions to you: give comfort to my friend Onesimus. 13 Also greet those who meet in the house of Nympha and to all the churches. 14 Greet Luke, Demas, and the others. 15 Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters at Laodicea, and to Nymphas and the church in his home. 16 After you have read this letter, see that it is also read in the church at Laodicea, and that you exchange letters with them. 17 Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.” 18 I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember me!

ekegusii: Edwin Okong'o, Omwana Oito Mache Ng'umbu okarangire chibando. Yaani nere bweka okona koria chibando saiga mwaye. igwa bono Omoriki ne Edwin bw’ Okong’o, Omwana Oito o Mache Ng’umbu Kero kende konde Nairobi togaikaransa emesa koragera no omosani one okorokwa Motanya na momura oye Mogeni. Omong’ina oye Nyakerario konye ominire obokima bw’ obori ne enyama ye embori, chinsaga na amabere amaruranu amaroro se abwate amakombi amanene ndagoake bwateke erogoma. Tokaigatera bono obokima egesamaro, no omong’ina Nyakerario okona gototiotereria. Omong’ina agatotebia, “Bobege moigote kegima. Ninwe abamura mogokiina.” Motanya akamotebia, “Omwanchi, gaki inche no omogaka omogotu tari bono ngokina. Nche nigo nkoria bosiniini.” Intwe abamura tokagenderera. Tokabosimbaga buna abana be esekenderi enchara eitete ekero abarimu barire chibesa chibwenerete kogorera abana endagera eisaine. Nainche buna konye narure Mache Ng’umbu ase ntari konyora bosie bwa bori, nkaigatera. Mbwata obokima, mbobata ekegusii, mbwaterania enyama ne chinsaga, mbeka gochia monwa. Kobogotirimboka, ng’iyereria na amabere amaruranu. Ekero twakoora bwonsi korwa ekee omong’ina akarangeria omosubati ore komokonya koruga arete obonde. Nkamokania, “Yaya, Mami, inche naigotire.” Omong’ina agatebia omosubati, “Retera Mogeni bono Omoamerika ere tiga ange onarire ebitoche bia Mache Ng’umbu.” Mogeni nere agakana, “Mami, yaya. Nabeire buna riria nabete.” Ngachia koigwa igo, ngaseka, ngaseka, ngaseka, mbaka ngaturungana. Naende ngaseka, ngaseka mbaka nkarera. Naende ngaseka, ngaseka, yaani ngaseka mbaka bagakaga nabeire richara. Chimbaru chikang’atia. Konakora goseka kamoboria, “Mogeni, ng’ai omanyerete omogano oyio?” Mogeni akaboria, “Mogano ki?” O Motanya na Abanyaribari, no omogano oyio no oyoseito, aria Nyamira, Bogirango Bosongo. Seito Makairo omogaka oyomo narenge ore korokwa Gesokera Nyandagesera bwanchete enyama mono. Rituko erimo omogaka onde ore korokwa Nyakundi akamochiika ekegeni komana chiombe. Ekero baika aroro, Gesokera agasokera endagera mbaka agasinywa koimoka. Endagera eyio aigaterete egachaka komobeta korwa nda. Agachaka gokema na kwana buna emori yarire chibando chinyinge ekooreka. Abamura makamobogoria gochia sukunyoma bakamwengera esabuni aroka endagera abanto batano bararie baigote. Abagaka ba seito bagasoka ase ogochika omonto okobasareria obogeni. Kobairana nka Makairo bagatiana buna onde tabase gochika omogaka Gesokera gochia kegeni kende. Naende rinde bono Makairo gekirete tokoigwa buna omogaka onde okorokwa Ndemo nere orangerigwe ekegeni. Agaetia abagaka bande tachiika Gesokera. Korende buna seito Makairo totari gokiria ng’ana, omonto akamonyerera Gesokera. Gesokera akagenda bw’ omogaka Ndemo akanyora abande no bare bakobanga esabaria. Akababoria gose mbamoire obogeni nere. Ndemo kamokania, “Yaya, Gesokera, nkwaretete obosoku obonene o mosubati o Nyakundi. Aye ne esese embe etari bogeni.” Gesokera agachaka gosorora buna omwana obwatirwe na amamocho ogosorora taitwa, “Yaya, gaki Tingonkora bo kabere, Ndemo.” Ndemo akanga pi, “Yaya! Orabaise gochia gokwera aria oboko otoreterere.” Gesokera agatugama nse na gosorora mono, “Gaki, gaki, gaki, abagaka baminto timontiga.” Seito Gusii monto mosacha gocha gotugama nse na gosorora buna omwana nabo ogokaga buna na amaene agoteba. Abagaka bagancherana komoira oboko bwa Ndemo aaria Nyamusi Etari Bitutu, Bigirango Irianyi. Ekero baigete ekegeni endagera ekarosigwa enyinge. Kobakona koragera botuko rende seito Gusii sitima etaiyo mono ne ebibeya togwokia. Bakaragera igo onde tachia korora Gesokera gagosokera naende. Akaigatera bono naende mbaka enda ekaba buna omonyocho. Ekero yachaka komoresania Gesokera akaimoka korwa nyomba akagenda gochia gesona. Agetoora ebwobi okonagokema. Omosae oyomo bw’ ekenyoro ekio okorokwa Momanyi akamorora. Akamoboria, “Omogaka, naki imbuya okare bori?” Gesokera akamotebia, ogotogota but ekeragita, “Nabeire buna riria nabete.” Momanyi akamoboria, “Naki kwabete?” “Nabeire buna riria nabete.” Momanyi agakaga Gesokera no oborwaire akabwate. Akaminyoka gochia eero ase abanto bare kona gosiba ekegara na gotengera chisani chia Christopher Monyoncho omwana bw’ Araka, riyo ri ebasweti. Momanyi gateba, “Mochumbe, kararimia ekenada.” “Yaa, Momanyi bono ne ebirecha bikoriete? Ndimie ekenanda abageni bagotenga? Tiga esani eye eraera.” “Yaya, yaa, Mochumbe, oMogeni orwarire.” Mochumbe akarimia ekenanda. Momanyi akaboria, “OMogeni orwarire aa ogoteba buna obeire buna riria abete. Ng’o obwate eriogo riaye?” Omogaka Ndemo akaminyoka gochia isiko ogoteba, “Obe! Obe! Obe! Oyio eriogo riaye ntomanyete. Mwengere esabuni Omo.” Bakengera Gesokera esabuni. Bakamobetereria keero buna omwana ekengwerere bwangire konya erongori. Akaroka chinyama echinde chingima atatakuneti akamanya gocha koba buya. Korwa erio onde tachia komochika Gesokera gochia bogeni bonde. Ekero seito Makairo twaigwete omogano oyio, togaseka. Gatwarageire twaigotire togachaka togoteba, “Nabeire buna riria nabete.” Tomanya goseka bono buna amachore arorire chibando. “Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! Nabeire buna riria nabete.” Na seito Gusii bono buna tonarete goakaakania amang’ana buna embori ekonia egesero, ani amang’ana aikire Nyaribari sobo Mogeni. Edwin bw’ Okong’o, Omosani omonene bwe Ekegusii nere omoriki bwo Omwana Oito o Mache Ng’umbu Chimbera chie chisese, Cambria Cemetery, California. Nigo akamorangeirie na amasikani. “Aye, baba yane, mosubati on Bosire,” Mogaka arangeria. “Ee!” “Gaki tomentere a mache a morero.” Mong’ina nere okonyora erio konye orasiibire ekemite na abang’ina abaamate kobakona kogosoria na goteera. Rero ndero, toe Echae ya morero toe “Mosubati o Bosire naye gaki,” Mogaka omotebia kagoseka. “Ntomanyete buna tari chae ya morero mokonywa agwo chikoni.” “Nyakerario,” Mong’ina arangeria mosubati oye. “Ereria iso amache gose natotigane tonywe echae eye Kemuma arosia.” Abang’ina na abagaka bonsi baseka mono mbaka baturungana. Mong’ina nigo arenge omong’ina bwamaseko mono. Nyakerario kabamenteire amache, abagaka basiiba ake igo. Nabo rinde kware konyoora abasae bande buna oyomo ore korokwa Mong’are bakonywa bwango, bwango ne endamwamu. “Aye omoisia oyo Ratemo gwatindire,” omogaka onde ore korokwa Nyambati amotebia. “Ee, tiga agende,” abagaka bonsi bancherana. Mong’are o Ratemo gachiire bachaka kogamba buna are omonywa bobe. “Mbuya twamoseria,” Mogaka ateba. “Mwaigwa bono buna rinde anywa akooga bogakia?” “Ayio na amake,” Nyambati ateba. “Rinde momura one Momanyi taigwa ‘esagasaga’ botuko agachia gosoka akamonyora araire omochachaku ime?” “Naki amokorete?” omogaka onde akaboria. “Gaki Momanyi one ne emechando. Nigo amokururete akamobeka as konye arorire chinsanako magoroba.” Bonsi, abagaka, abang’ina, na abana bagaseka mbaka bagaturungana. Omomura oyomo ekegara gekamotokeria. Tamanyete buna ka abagaka bakogamba nigo okoratiga konywa gwategerera. “Yaa naye karwe aa tonara egento eke kia abagaka,” Nyambati akamotebia. “Tiga bagende bonsi,” Mogaka ateba. “Ee, tiga Mochumbe ache atwaterie chinko botaraira,” Mong’ina akabatebia. “Yaya,” Mogaka agakana. “Tumia ebiemba. Egento eke Mochumbe asiiba kiamokorire richara arabaise gweaka egesire.” Mochumbe na bagisangio baye bakagenda gochia saiga gotegerera eretio “BPC Swaeri Sabesi” (BBC Swahili Service). Abagaka bakorora buna abasae bachiire bagatoma Nyakerario gochia kiage abaretere ebuga. Bagatiera na konywa. Mogaka agaansa go kwana amang’ana onde ataare komanya engencho yaye. “Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba! Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba!” Inche erio nigo narenge omwana omosiniini. Tinamanyete eng’encho ye, “Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba.” Korende ngakina, ngakora esekenderi ngacha mache ng’umbu, Amerika. Gaki tiga mbatebie buna Abamerika nigo banchete chisese ne ebimoni mono. Okonyora ekemoni keroseirie nyomba kemenyete buya, nonya mbeba nchiyo kebwenerete goita. Endagera nigo gekogorerwa enga ebisuguti kiabekerwa na amabere. Nonya nase gekobeka echabu go kiabutiarire nigo kebwate abanyene bana goitora. Ne esese nero nigo yanchire mono. Emenyete nyomba, egoikaransa esoba seti igoro yarigereria etelebiseni na abanyene. Esese ya Amerika oise konyereta seito Kenya nigo erakwe bwango mono. Nyama mbese sese ya Amerika terikoria. Tenga buna Ondieki yaito yakaminyokirie egesusu gose egechure yabwata twaria, twanyea amauga. Buna ekemoni kia Amerika, esese ya Amerika nigo ekoroserigwa endagera special ekogorwa korwa etuka. Tiga bono naende, Omogusii ominto, ngotebie egento kende kiamaseko. Abamerika naende nkoratwara bare amasindano korora buna ning’o obwate esese gose ekemoni egeseera. Amasindano ayio ataraika nigo bakoira chisese ne ebimoni baakana chibesa biasibigwa na konintwa chinchara. Omobui bwa amasindano nigo akoegwa egekombe buna keria abagosoria bakoeegwa. Nimanyete ngoteba ore buna, “Etwini gaki naye! Esese eegwe egekombe kiamaminyoko?” Maene pi ndie esese, tindigokong’aina, Nyaituga o baba. Boria onde bwensi omenyete mache ng’umbu. Chisese ne ebimoni kobiarwarire Abamerika tibari gotiga bikwe. Nigo bakobiira chinyagetari chi ebimoni ne chisese. Nimanyete Omoamerika oyomo oakanete $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) kobaara esese endwaire. Esese koyangire kobwena nigo bagokora egento gekorokwa, “Putting it to sleep” – bakonyebeta esindani yakwa ng’ooora. Koyakuure, banyeira ase akorokwa, Pet Cemetery, ase chimbeera chie chisese, ebimoni, ne ching’iti chinde Abamerika batugete nyomba chigotindekwa. Kobanyetindekire nigo bachachana na gwechwanachania buna omoibori okwereirwe no omwana. Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba. --omoerio-- Edwin Okongo nigo are Omoriki Omogeni ase Gusii.com. Ka moranche, motarere ase ewebusaiti yaye aaria ase Ourmaninamerica.com Edwin Okongo nere omoriki omonene bwe e bulogi ya Mshale naende omoriki bwe e bulogi yaye omonyene ya Okongo's Policy. Nigo asomete California State University aaria Hayward amo na University ya California aaria Berkeley. Nigo are oyomo bwa Abagusii bari barikire amangana amaya naende amange sana igoro ya Gusii na Kenya. Ka moranche, soma amariko aye ase chibulogi echio nabatebirie igoro. Imbuya mono Okongo ase e vidio amo na egasi engiya.

I laughed and laughed and laughed until we were reconciled. And I kept laughing and laughing until I grew up. And I kept laughing and laughing, meaning I laughed until my friends came back. The pot was boiling. He asked while laughing, "Mogeni, do you remember that story?" Mogeni answered, "What story?" It was about Motanya and the Banyaribari, and the story of those people from Nyamira, Bogirango Bosongo. Makairo the elder was a man who was known for helping people with their problems. A time came when an elder named Nyakundi fell ill and needed help with his livestock. Then everyone gathered, and Gesokera helped them until he was exhausted. That day he received a gift of gratitude for his efforts. The gift was a cow, but it died due to illness. The people blamed him, accusing him of witchcraft. Five men came to investigate. The relatives of the elder gathered to discuss how to avenge themselves. They agreed that they would not allow anyone to help Gesokera again. Later, Makairo learned that the elder named Ndemo had been accused of witchcraft. He called the relatives together and told them that they should not accuse Gesokera. Gesokera went to the elder Ndemo and apologized to him and his people. He explained everything to them. Ndemo said, "Yes, Gesokera, I forgive you for the great offense against Nyakundi. But this matter will not be forgotten." Gesokera replied sadly, saying, "Yes, father Tingonkora, Ndemo." Ndemo continued, "Yes! You have caused trouble for our community." Gesokera begged him and pleaded, "Father, father, father, please don't let us suffer." The people of Gusii also gathered and pleaded, saying that the child should not be punished because of what happened. The relatives consulted each other about how to deal with Ndemo and the people of Nyamusi Etari Bitutu, Bigirango Irianyi. Then they took the livestock to a place where there was plenty of grass. They drove the cattle and goats to a pasture near Gesokera, where he was still suffering. That evening, they walked until they reached a dark place. Then they began to plan how to punish Gesokera and make him regret his actions. They decided to take revenge on him. An old woman named Momanyi approached him and started asking questions. She asked, "Elder, why are you so sad?" Gesokera replied, trembling slightly, "Because I am afraid of being beaten." Momanyi asked, "Why are you afraid?" "Because I am afraid of being beaten." Momanyi grabbed Gesokera and beat him severely. She then sent him to Christopher Monyoncho's house, the son of Araka, which was a place of worship. Momanyi said, "Mochumbe, confess your sins." "Yes, Momanyi, but what about those who have wronged me? Should I tell them my sins too? Let everyone speak their truth." "Yes, yes, Mochumbe, the elder has forgiven you." Mochumbe confessed his sins. Momanyi said, "The elder has forgiven you because you are afraid of being beaten. Is that why you came here?" The elder Ndemo sent someone to ask, "Is it true? Is it true? Is it true? This story is unbelievable. Bring me Omo soap!" They brought Gesokera the soap. They washed the child thoroughly, hoping to cleanse him of his wrongdoing. He slaughtered a young goat and cooked it, knowing that something bad would happen. After that incident, they went back to planning how to punish Gesokera further. It is said that the people of Makairo heard about this event and were saddened. They gathered together and discussed it, saying, "Because I am afraid of being beaten." Everyone laughed at this, saying, "Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! Because I am afraid of being beaten." And the people of Gusii always say that when someone speaks foolishly or makes empty promises, they are like Nyaribari, the wife of Mogeni. Edwin son of Okong’o, a prominent person in the Gusii language and the author of the book "The Child of Eight," Mache Ng’umbu. Photograph taken at Cambria Cemetery, California. Flikr/Wonderlane The author and Edwin son of Okong’o, the child of eight, Mache Ng’umbu. People. Storytellers. Ancestors, children of the past. Remember this lesson well! Once upon a time, when the land was still new, the elder from Makairo, a man who understood the Gusii customs, went to Kebirigo to learn more about the Gusii traditions. Anyone who wants to know about our history should listen carefully to the stories told by our ancestors, or seek guidance. Anyone who wants to understand our culture should respect the wisdom of the elders and honor their teachings. It is important to remember that our ancestors faced many challenges, but they persevered through hard work and determination. That is the story of the elder who lived a long life, and how he taught his children and grandchildren to live in harmony with nature and with each other. The elder was known as Mogaka. Every evening, he would gather his family around the fire and share stories of the past. (This is a good example of how to teach children about their heritage.) Our ancestors worked tirelessly to ensure that future generations would inherit a rich cultural legacy, and we must continue to uphold those values. Siberia is cold, oh Siberia is cold, Mosaiga Ayeee, ayee Mosaiga Give me strength, Mosaiga give me strength to persevere Ayeee, ayee Mosaiga Our ancestors also say that Mogaka named his clan "Mong’ina". He then went to conquer Mong’ina. He did so with courage and determination. “Yes, my father, I will obey Bosire,” Mogaka declared. “Good!” “I will bring you the head of an enemy.” Mong’ina refused to accept this offer and instead chose to reconcile with his enemies and make peace. Therefore, let us remember, let us… The shield of the warrior, let us… “I will obey Bosire, but first,” Mogaka said thoughtfully. “Let me see what this shield can do.” “Nyakerario,” Mong’ina replied respectfully. “It has the power to protect us from harm and to guide us on our journey.” Everyone laughed until they were breathless. Mong’ina then became the leader of his people. Nyakerario skillfully crafted shields, and the elders cherished them greatly. They also remembered the day when the people of Mong’are gathered together to celebrate their victory, singing and dancing joyfully. “Yes, that Ratemo was very brave,” the elder from Nyambati remarked. “Yes, let him go,” everyone agreed. Mong’are and Ratemo set out on a mission to prove their worth. “My friends, let us pray,” Mogaka began. “What shall we offer to appease the spirits?” “Bring some honey,” Nyambati suggested. “And some tobacco, so that Momanyi may find ‘esagasaga’ and discover the secrets of the forest.” “Why does she ask for that?” the elder inquired curiously. “Because Momanyi is wise and knowledgeable. She knows how to interpret dreams and visions, and she can use her powers to help us overcome obstacles.” Everyone laughed again until they could laugh no more. “Yes, let us allow them to pass,” Nyambati concluded. “Let them go,” Mogaka agreed. “Yes, let Mochumbe go and bring back news of the outside world,” Mong’ina added. “Alright,” Mogaka conceded. “Let us send messengers. Mochumbe is skilled at gathering information and reporting accurately.” Mochumbe and his companions traveled far and wide, listening to the BBC Swahili Service. The elders decided that the people should accompany Nyakerario on a visit to the market. They went with gifts. Mogaka refused to sleep, staying awake all night to contemplate his thoughts. “This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity! This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity!” That is when the young boy was born. We know his name, "This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity." He grew up quickly, becoming strong and healthy like an American. First, he told stories about how Americans had destroyed everything with weapons. To make a prosperous home, one needs a cow, a goat, and a hen. The land was fertile and abundant, providing plenty of food. And because of this abundance, people were able to raise children and prosper. But this story is just beginning. A prosperous home, a beautiful garden, and a television set where people gather to watch. The American way of life has spread throughout Kenya, bringing both benefits and challenges. Meat is expensive, but American meat is readily available. Remember that Ondieki once lamented the loss of traditional foods, saying that they were healthier and more satisfying. But the American way of life, the American dream, is being promoted through special programs and events. We continue onward, people of Gusii, remembering our traditions. Americans are now involved in politics, claiming that they can bring progress and development. These politicians often use empty promises and lies to deceive people, causing confusion and chaos. The consequences of their actions are felt by everyone, especially the poor and vulnerable. I remember hearing someone say, “What will happen next? Will this dream ever come true?” Many years later, my mother, Nyaituga, passed away. She left behind a legacy of strength and resilience. Americans' obsession with wealth prevents them from finding happiness. They accumulate possessions and money endlessly. I heard that an American spent $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) to bury his pet. When a pet dies, they perform a ritual called "Putting it to sleep" - they take the animal to a special place. It is said that there is a place called Pet Cemetery, where Americans bury their pets, along with their toys and belongings. They then grieve and mourn, comparing their grief to losing a child. This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity. --end of article-- Edwin Okongo is a researcher and writer from Gusii.com. ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya: Bagoteba ng'a "Rero mochokoro goika tokoire e field trip", sokoro amo na magokoro nigo bangira aaria ase The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, nigo narutete chintacho, korende ki naika aroro, nigo nabete no omogoko ase ogosomigwa na kwoorokigwa buna Abagusii twakabeire, ne ebinto twagatumiire. Unless twaagachire e museum yaito ekogacha our artifacts amo no omogano oito bwa Abagusii, eye nero the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online buna eye. It is possible nga artifacts chio Omogusii ne chinyinge, and they are scattered in many places. Korende we have no central repository. We hope that things will change in the next few years with the establishment of the Omogusii Museum and Cultural Center. Ase boigo, mbuya mono to the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Troupe ase efforts babwate to preserve the few artifacts that are left with us. In addition, the Otenyo Troupe has been instrumental in teaching us our history and traditions which are being forgotten fast. Thank you for your selfless efforts. And to our readers, thank you for visiting and our cultural feature follows. Enjoy. Ebitinge Enywomo yo Omogusii tiyare koera onye bitinge tibiyo. Without ebitinge, igo nywomo teraba. Omosubati o Gusii nigo arenge gotimigwa ebitinge ase ekero kie enyangi. Ebitinge nabio biare koba buna chibeta echi chie ekerero. Inaki ebitinge biare koroisigwa? Chintere chie etarimbo nigo chiare kobutorwa ebing'ese ebingese. Omosubati obwate okogoro okogare nigo are konacherwa ebing'ese bitano na kemo. Oyo obwate okogoro ogosiniini nigo are are konachera ebing'ese bitano. Kwamanya korambora okogoro, bia bekwa. Korwa abwo, risangwa rie eng'ombe rianachwa. Barietanani ase okogoro ime. Onye ebibao bigotigara, nigo bare kobeka emurwa yaticha. Mangana taraera. Korwa abwo, bamanya koyeaka egetinya egere kiororobe. Ase omoerio, nigo bare goaka etago kiamanya koba egetinge na koba ekieni. Below, egetinge kio Omogusii buna kiarenge kororekana. Ebibekerero Ao Ao Omogusii nigo arenge koroisia ebibekero ebinge kobwatekana buna okogania ne egasi yabo. Let us see a few, starting with the picture below. Gochakera ase okobee motwe: Oroteru. Oroteru narwo rware koirura obori, amaemba, ching'ende gose chibando. Komenta nayio, oroteru nabo rware gotumeka ase okogachera endagera temporarily. Ime yo oroteru oro nigo toroche ensio. Ekero obori gose amaemba arenge gosiegwa, ensio, together with orogena nabio biare gotumeka ase ogosia. Orogena amo ne ensio nigo are koiywa korwa ase egetare gose rigena ritari koburoka riamanya goturwa. Abasacha nabwo bare gokora aya. Onye aye ki bwanchete ributi, manya ng'a orogena narwo rware gosia obori ne ememera, yamanya koroisia ributi rigwansa. Behind oroteru to the left ne egekabu. Egekabu nakio kiare kobeka endagera buna chinyeni ekero chikwau korwa mogondo. Komenta nayio, egekabu nabo kiarenge gotumeka kobeka kende gionsi kiarenge koirwa ase obogeni gose echiro. Riroba rie ebundo Magega ye egekabu on the left ne enyongo. Enyongo nigo yare koroisigwa korwa ase riroba rie ebundo, riamanya gosambwa. Enyongo nigo yare gotumeka kogacha amache, amarwa, ributi.... Immediately behind oroteru nigo tobwate ekebari. Emeremo ye ekebari no okogacha endagera. Buna bono ekero endagera yagesirwe, nigo yare kobekwa ekebari ime korwa mogondo. Ekebari amo ne egetonga (not pictured) nabio biare korusia endagera mogondo. Right behind ekebari gochia center left ,ne ebirandi. E discussion ye ebirandi is further down in this article. Magega ye ebirandi, we have chinyakaruga. Enyakaruga nero yarenge gokora egasi yo okoiyeka endagera. Endagera eng'asu buna enyama ya nda, obokima bwo obori, erongori yo obori..... ebitoche ebi bionsi nigo biakaiyekeirwe ime ye enyakaruga. There is more discussion ye enyakaruga further down. Ase okorigereria, nabo okorora nga, abamagokoro amo ne chisokoro chiato nabo chiaroisetie ebinto bio okwerenda buya egere togaika igaa. Orogena Ne Ensio ya Mwamogusii Obokima bwo obori, ememera ya amarwa, obosie bwe erongori.....Ebi bionsi tibiare koba without orogena ne ensio. Eye nero etinga entangani naende original yo Omogusii. Abasubati nabwo bagasire obosie. It was backbreaking work korende at the time, abasubati tibare gokumia. Below, orogena amo ne ensio yo Omogusii buna biare kororekana. Obokano Bwo Omogusii Nabwo bakairirwe ase kera enyangi. Kera ase omoyega omuya bwo Omogusii. Abana nkogenda bare iburu gose kobekerwa maguta motwe? Renta obokano. Enyaroka Sarange nkoywomwa ekare? Sokoro renta obokano. Ntwaigwete ng'a omogeni natogete aaria bwo omogaka Obinge? Tata ominto tera omoino na kobugia obokano. Nigo bwakaroserigwe korwa ase omote bwo omotembe, risangwa amo no obongori botano na botato. Why obongori botano na botato? Ntoranyora ichibu korende nkoririgia tore. Below, Obokano bwo Omogusii buna bwakabeire. On the right, omosubati Gesare nkonyegeria are amareko. Abande ntwanyorete e chance yo okoiyekerwa enyama ya nda ase enyakaruga. Ase boigo, tokaiyekerwa engoko no omosori. Baminto gento tikeri ekiya buna ogosenyenta endagera eiyekire ime ye enyakaruga! Onye gotagete koragera buya pi, you should try it some time. Enyakaruga nero yakinetie Abagusii abakoro ekagera togaika igaa. Below, buna yakarorekanire, enyakaruga yo Omogusii amo ne ekeburugo, biganyete enyama ya nda ebekwe ime. Ko obori gose amaemba amire na kwoma, goika arenge korusigwa echafu yonsi magega yo ogosiegwa. Ase okorusia obori gose amaemba echafu, nigo Abagusii barenge gotumia ekonu. Nigo obori bwakabekirwe ekonu ime, bwamanya gosunyuntwa. Korwa abwo, bwamanya koirurwa no oroteru. Ekonu nigo yare koroisigwa na abasacha. Ase okoroisia ekonu, abasacha nigo barenge gotumia omote bwo omotembe. Timanyeti gose emetembe netigarete Gusii. Right nse ye ekonu, nigo toroche egesero. Bono egesero ninki? Egesero ne risangwa rie embori, engombe gose engondi. Ge etugo yanyenyirwe, kende gionsi tikiare gotugutwa. This includes risankwa. Risangwa nabo riarenge gotumeka buna oboraro, kobekerera endagera ase ekeoreri ekero ekwoma gose teiteka gochia riroba nse. Below, ekonu eyio on top of egesero to the left. Ekero endagera yarosigwe ne ekonu, nigo yare koirurwa no oroteru erinde yamanya kogachwa irongo. Konyora etarairwa irongo, endagera nigo yare kobekwa ime yo omonyoncho ime yamanya kogachwa. Bono rende omonyoncho ninki? Omonyoncho nigo orenge koroisigwa buna ekebari korende nigo orenge omonene. Ebirundu nabio biare gokorekanigwa, mbaka omonyoncho omanya koba. Ningo orenge koroisia omonyoncho? Abasacha nabwo bakarosirie emenyoncho. Ko oroisirie buya, omonyoncho nigo orenge kogacha obori ase amatuko amange. Enduruche y' Mwamogusii Because Abagusii twabebekaine ne ebisaku binde ebitindi, naende biatagete gotoita, goika twarenge koroisia ebibekerero bio okorwana. Titware gokira igo. Omogusii nigo abwate amatimo, chinsara, chinguba, chinungu, amo ne ebinde buna chinduruche. Enduruche nigo yarenge gotumeka koruta ebinto buna amagena gochia ase ababisa. Kende gionsi kiare korutwa ne enduruche nigo kiarenge kominyoka ne chimbero chimbariri! Below, enduruche yo Omogusii buna yarenge kororekana. Obokombe It is hard to imagine how ororeri rwo Omogusii survived ase emiaka eye yonsi kobwatekana ne ebibekeroro twabwate. Temanyekaneti nga Abagusii twabeire abaremi ase emiaka erenga. Korende nonya nabo igo, nao tore igaa ase engencho abangina na abagaka abakoro barigetie chinchera chio ogotorageria. Omogusii no omong'aini. Ase oboremi, Omogusii nigo aroisetie obokombe bwe rigena. Amakombe aya naro arenge gotumeka ase oboremi bwe chibando, amatoke, obori, amaemba, chinsaga....kera egento. Below, obokombe bwo Omogusii buna bwakabeire. Nigo Mwanyagetinge twarenge surrounded by enemies. Nigo twabwate abanto bande babebekaine naintwe buna Abamanyi, Abagere, Abamansae amo na Abasigisi. Abanto aba be ebisaku ebi binde bionsi nigo barenge gotorwania ntwe, erinde baire etugo gose amaremo aito. Ntwarenge kwegembera. Together with ebirwanero binde, this is where enguba y' Mwanyagetinge came in. Abamura ebisora korwa Gusii nigo bagatumiire chinguba ase esegi. Nigo enguba yare korosigwa korwa ase risangu rie engombe. Below, enguba ya abamura ebisore korwa Gusii. Abagaka amo na abangina abakoro tibare kobekerwa bokima ande onsi otatiga ase ekee. Kobeka obokima ase ekebekerero kende gionsi nigo yare koba amachayo. Ekee nakio kiare gotumeka ase okobeka obokima, especially obokima bwo obori. Nigo ekeee gekorosigwa korwa ase chimboba chio obori ne emegoye. Abasubati nabwo bare koroisia ebiee. Go keroisirie buya, ekee tikiare gokendia ndagera. Yaya. Ekee nigo kiare kogacha riberera rio obokima bwo obori for a long time. Below, ekee kio Omogusii buna kiare kororekana. Ekerandi Kio Omogusii Omogusii nigo anchete amabere. Eee bono. Amabere ye eng'ombe amaroranu abekire ekerandi ime Mose ominto. Ekerenadi nigo kiare korosigwa korwa ase risosa rie ekerandi. Ge ekerandi giakong'ire, nigo kiare kogeswa. Giatigwa kioma na gosatwa amo na abasubati. Nigo abakungu bare gotumia ekebeya gosata ekerandi erinde kiaba amaridadi bori. Below, ekerandi kio Omogusii with ekemumeko gie ekeemba. Eee gaki amache ang'usirwe in some places. Chigari nchiroo. Komenta nayio, ntobwate chibodaboda amo na mkokoteni. Korende, it was not always this way. Nigo Omogusii arenge kobogira kera egento gagokebeka motwe! Amache nigo arenge kobuchwa korwa rooche abekwa omotwe igoro. Chinko, amatoke, obori...ndagera ende yonsi. Nonya nabo igo, Omogusii deviced a way to lessen pain yo okobogoria ebinto ase omotwe. Engata. Engata nero yare kobekwa gati yo omotwe oo amo ne egento keri obogoretie. Engata eye nero yare kobekwa motwe ekero ogwetweka. Nigo engata yare korosigwa korwa ase emegombo ya amatoke. Below. engata yo Omogusii buna yakabeire. Ntwarora above buna abasubati bare kobeka ebitinge ase enyangi ye enywomo. Enyangi yo Omogusii omokoro tiyare koba onye amaino ye embeche taratoka erinde omoywomi abekerwe motwe. Ntoramanya exactly the purpose chisokoro amo na abamagokoro baito bateberete nga goika omonywomi abeke amaino ye embeche motwe oye. Buna tokona koboria chisokoro amo na abamagokoro baria baito batigarete, we will know more. Kabekire aamo iga, amaino aya nigo arenge korokwa ebibaga. Below, amaino ye embeche (ebibaga) yo omonywomi buna arenge kororekana. Ekiore Kia Mwanyagetinge In addition yo okobeka amaino ye embeche (ebibaga) ase omotwe oye, Omogusii omoywomi o kare nigo atakeire kobeka ekiore motwe oye. Ekiore nigo kiarenge koroisigwa korwa ase risankwa. Below, ekiore kio Omogusii buna giakarorekanire. Ritimo Rio Omogusii Buna twarorire, segi tiyare koba onye birwanero tibiyo. Ntwarora buna Omogusii abwate chinguba, chinsara amo na amatimo. Ase baria mogokina bono, tiga mbamanyie n'ga kera omogaka bwo omochie nigo abwate ritimo riaye. This is in addition to chinsara, enguba etc. Kera omogaka o Gusii amo na abamura be emechie bonsi, were standing armies. Baganyete ekero ekurate ekoba. Below, omomura egesora oyomo o Gusii kare ne ritimo riaye. Behind him is the Assistant Minister for Culture and MP for North Mugirango Borabu, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui and others aaria Keroka Cooperative Union Grounds recently during the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival. Ekerangesa gia Sokoro Onye gokoigwa ekero sokoro agoasimora rimaambia, there is a reason why. Ekerangesa. Abagaka abanene ba kare nigo barenge konywa etumbato ye ekerangesa. Etumbato nigo yare kobekwa ase ekerangesa ime na gosunyuntwa. Korwa abwo, abagaka bamanya kobeka etumbato eyio ase chimioro. Basi bono tiga ogoasimora goanse. What followed from there was ogoasimora kore successive. Amato ye etumbato arenge kobekwa ase ekerangesa ime nigo arenge koba amabese. Ogoasimora okonene nigo kwaminetie buna etumbato eyio n' engiya !! Ekerangesa nigo kiare koroisugwa korwa ase omote bwo omotembe. As you can see, omotembe nigo orenge important ase carpentry amo na arts and crafts yo Omogusii. Below, ekerangesa kio Omogusii buna giakarorekanire. Omogusii tarenge gokira igo ka amarwaire achire. Ase ki? Omogusii nigo arenge omonyagitari. Abarwaria mbarengeo. Komenta nayio, abarwaria abwo mbabwate ebinto barenge gotumia ase okorwaria abarwaire. Ekemo kie ebibekerero bia abarwaria ba Gusii ne ekebwe. Bono ekebwe ninki? Onye amanyinga akwereire emeki ime, gose omonto nigo aagetwe ase gete akabimba na amanyinga gokwera ime, abarwaria nigo barenge gotumia ekebwe koyang'usa. Ko omonto ang'usirwe amanyina ayio ne ekebwe, ensemo eyio yarwarete nigo yarenge gosusana. Korwa abwo, omonto obwena. Ekebwe nigo kiare koroisigwa korwa ase orogunchara. Abaminto, below ne ekebwe buna giakarorekanire. Bono Mwanyagetinge ominto, e field trip nao yaereire igaa. Ntobatebie when the next trip comes. For now, magokoro nigo ateba ng'a enyama ya nda netigarete enyakaruga ime aaria nka. Bono tiga toraayerera gochia ase enka. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.
english: These are the words: They celebrated with the saying “A good seed grows well during a field trip”, so with joy and enthusiasm they visited the area of The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, I was hesitant, but when I saw it, I liked it, and I felt proud of our culture and heritage because the Abagusii people were represented, and things were done well. Unless we visit the museum which displays our artifacts and our customs of the Abagusii people, and this is the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online too. It is possible that artifacts of Omogusii are elsewhere, and they are scattered in many places. Therefore we have no central repository. We hope that things will change in the next few years with the establishment of the Omogusii Museum and Cultural Center. Also, praise to the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Troupe for their efforts to preserve the few artifacts that are left with us. In addition, the Otenyo Troupe has been instrumental in teaching us our history and traditions which are being forgotten fast. Thank you for your selfless efforts. And to our readers, thank you for visiting and our cultural feature follows. Enjoy. Stories The life of the Omogusii person is incomplete without stories. Without stories, life is empty. The ancestors of Gusii greatly valued stories and their importance. Stories also served as a way of entertainment. Why are stories disappearing? This issue is becoming increasingly difficult to address. Ancestors used to tell stories at night and in the evenings. People who had time would gather in the evening and listen. Those who had time in the afternoon would also gather and listen. To understand properly, be careful. Do this, a bull is slaughtered. Share among yourselves the meat. Whoever steals, let them be taken to the river to be cleansed. Be mindful. Do this, people know how to respect a beautiful calf that doesn't wander off. And nowadays, people want to know whether a story is true or false. Below, some stories of Omogusii and their meanings are presented. Ceremonies Ao Ao The Omogusii people greatly value ceremonies that are performed and celebrations with their peers. Let us see a few, starting with the picture below. Look and remember: Oroteru. Oroteru was a special container for storing millet, beans, and other grains. Comment further, Oroteru also was used to display items temporarily. The lid of Oroteru was strong. The grain and beans were carefully stored, the lid, together with its handle were also made to last. The handle and the lid were made from wood and skillfully carved so that the container wouldn't fall and break. The elders also used to say this. Anyone who didn't appreciate it, knew that the handle was made to protect the container and its contents, knowing how important it was. Behind Oroteru to the left is Egekabu. Egekabu was a place to put items temporarily, like a shelf where things could be placed. Comment further, Egekabu also was made to last and serve generations, being used to store various items. The seat of Ebundo Next to Egekabu on the left is Enyongo. Enyongo was used for grinding, especially during the preparation of Ebundo. Enyongo was also made to display tools, knives... Immediately behind Oroteru is Ekebari. The opening of Ekebari is for displaying items. But if the shelf was full, it was used to hold Ekebari itself. Ekebari and its surroundings (not pictured) were also used to display items. Right behind Ekebari towards the center left are Ebirandi. A discussion about Ebirandi is further down in this article. Next to Ebirandi, we have Chinyakaruga. Chinyakaruga was used to store various items for safekeeping. These included medicine, animal hides, clothing… all sorts of things were kept inside Chinyakaruga. There is more discussion about Chinyakaruga further down. For remembrance, and for future generations, let those with knowledge and wisdom also teach others what they have learned. The Handle And Lid Of Mwamogusii Animal hides, knife sheaths, containers… everything needs a handle and lid. This is how things were originally done by the Gusii people. Our ancestors also valued tradition. It was backbreaking work making them at the time, our ancestors did not give up. Below, the handle and lid of Omogusii can be seen. The Customs Of The Gusii People They were respected in ancient times. Ancient customs of the Gusii people. Children today, will they be able to inherit the wealth of their ancestors? Preserve the customs. Was Sarange remembered in the past? Remember to preserve the customs. Did Ogosi’s father get land from Obinge? Don’t let people forget the importance of preserving customs. It was crafted using materials from the forest, including wood and bamboo. Why wood and bamboo? Because they were readily available. Below, the customs of the Gusii people are displayed. On the right, old men like Gesare are shown demonstrating. People were given a chance to showcase their skills with animal hides at Chinyakaruga. Also, they were allowed to display their crafts and artistry. People shouldn’t think that only important items are stored inside Chinyakaruga! Anyone who wants to learn should try it sometime. Chinyakaruga greatly helped the Gusii people secure their possessions. Below, showing how it was used, Chinyakaruga of the Gusii and its contents, containing animal hides inside. When hides become dirty and worn out, they are taken to be cleaned thoroughly. And when cleaning the hides, the Gusii people use special stones. Once the hides have been cleaned with the stones, they become smooth. After this process, they are dried and polished. Stones are used to polish them by skilled artisans. They say that everything about Gusii culture is unique. To the right of the stone, there is a grinding stone. What is a grinding stone? A grinding stone is made from wood, and used for grinding grains. It is strong and durable, and everything is ground using it. This includes millet. It is also used to grind maize so that it can be stored for future use. Below, that stone on top of the grinding stone to the left. Once the grain has been ground with the stone, it is dried and polished so that it doesn’t spoil. Grind the grain well, then store it inside a container so that it doesn’t spoil. What is a container? A container is made from bark and is very large. Its sides are decorated, until the container is finished. How do you make a container? Artisans also create containers. After polishing it, the container is used to store hides and other valuables. The history of Mwamogusii Because the Gusii people were surrounded by many enemies, and they didn’t understand each other, they decided to create defenses to protect themselves. We won’t give up. The Gusii people had weapons like spears, shields, clubs, arrows, and others. History is used to remember events and teach future generations. Everything is remembered through history and passed down! Below, the history of the Gusii people will be explained. Traditions It is difficult to imagine how the customs of the Gusii people survived throughout all those years while facing challenges. We shouldn’t forget that the Gusii people were brave for many years. But now, we still have our traditions, which connect us to our ancestors who lived long ago. The Gusii and their neighbors. In ancient times, the Gusii people defended their traditions fiercely. These traditions included things like ceremonies, dances, hides, clothing, songs…and more. Below, the traditions of the Gusii people will be described. We were surrounded by enemies. We had many neighbors who fought against us, such as the Abamanyi, Abagere, Abamansae, and Abasigisi. These neighbors caused us a lot of trouble and tried to take our land and property. We refused to surrender. Along with the warriors, this is where the shield of Mwanyagetinge came in. The elders used the shield to defend the Gusii community. The shield was made from cowhide. Below, the shield of the elders defending the Gusii community. The youth and their neighbors did not allow anyone to steal their livestock. Stealing livestock was considered a serious offense, and the thief would face consequences. Livestock, especially cattle, were very important. Livestock were protected using traps made from cattle tails and intestines. The thieves also stole livestock. In the past, it wasn’t easy to recover stolen livestock. Yes. Livestock were able to graze peacefully for a long time. Below, the livestock of the Gusii people will be discussed. Circumcision among the Gusii The Gusii people practice circumcision. It is true. The male genitals of cattle are cut during circumcision, just like humans. Circumcision is done using a special knife. Once the circumcision is complete, it is celebrated. It is performed by traditionalists and young men. The leaders use a special stick to assist during circumcision so that it doesn’t hurt too much. Below, the circumcision of the Gusii people with its accompanying rituals. Sometimes, it is done differently in some places. It is very painful. However, nowadays, we use medicine and vehicles. But, it wasn’t always this way. The Gusii people were once strong enough to endure hardship! Pain was relieved by applying herbs to the wound. Spears, shields, cattle…and everything else. Now, the Gusii people devised a way to reduce the pain of removing items from the head. Finally. This method was used to relieve pain on the head and even on parts of the body that had been injured. This method was applied to the head until it healed completely. It was created using the husks of bananas. Below. the final method of the Gusii people has been explained. I remember that previously, young men would apply bandages to the forehead and temples. The forehead of the Gusii person should not have any scars because they affect the beauty of the head. I don’t understand exactly the purpose of the gourds and horns that people carry when offering drinks to heal the head. But if we continue researching the gourds and horns that people carry, we will learn more. Let us investigate further; these things were never hidden. Below, the healing of the head (bandages) of the drink has been discussed. The Ceremony of Mwanyagetinge In addition to applying bandages to the head, the Gusii people of old also practiced performing a ceremony on the head. The ceremony was usually carried out through divination. Below, the ceremony of the Gusii people will be described. The Rituals of the Gusii As we have seen, there was no peace without war. I remember that the Gusii people had spears, shields, and clubs. And those who were brave enough, especially the elders and warriors, had their own rituals. This is in addition to shields, spears, etc. In the past, the Gusii people and their ancestors had standing armies. They prepared well for battle. Below, the ancestral warriors of the Gusii people had their rituals. Behind him is the Assistant Minister for Culture and MP for North Mugirango Borabu, Hon. Wilfred Ombui and others at Keroka Cooperative Union Grounds recently during the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival. The Importance of Gourds Anyone who sees a gourd being used for brewing, there is a reason why. Its importance. The great chiefs of old used to drink beer from gourds. The beer was poured into the gourd and then stirred. Because of this, the chiefs knew how to pour the beer into containers. But today, this is rarely done. What followed from there was continuous brewing. The contents of the gourd were poured into the gourd and were considered sacred. Continuous brewing led to prosperity and wealth!! The gourd was often made beautifully and carefully. As you can see, carpentry and arts and crafts of the Gusii people greatly depend on it. Below, the gourd of the Gusii people will be described. The Gusii people did not lack knowledge when faced with challenges. So what? The Gusii people were very skilled. They worked hard. Commenting on this, they worked hard and used tools to overcome challenges. Therefore, the skills of the Gusii people were praised. But who praised them? Anyone who understands well about medicine, knows that herbs are gathered and ground with medicine, the doctors use those skills to heal. If the herbs are mixed with medicine and the disease is cured, the cure is considered effective. Because of this, medicine is good. The skills are often developed through practice. People, below, have skills which will be described. This Mwanyagetinge person, his field trip was successful. Let us wait for the next trip. ekegusii: Ekegusii Jane Bosibori Obuchi Abwo kare kare, mwanyabanto nigo arenge gotaarera amagoro na’maboko, buna getongwa kende gionsi eke-nyamagoro ane. Mwanyabanto nigo arenge omwango kobua egesusu, endo, gose ekeobiria. Amagoro na’maoko nigo arenge aang’e mono ne’bimo binde: abwate chinenko chibwekaine: amareko ne’menyuma; ebigokoro na’maru; embaratero ne’nsanyi; egetinkiro no’koboko. Kera okoboko na kera okogoro nigo kwabwate ebiara bitano ne’bichara bitano, egechara ekemo ase kera ekiara gio’kogoro ne’giokoboko. Ebiara bionsi bitano bia’maboko na’magoro, korwa ekiara ekenene goika egeke, nigo biarobeirie enchera ebwekaine. Ase amatuko aria, ekiara ekeneene gio’koboko nigo kiarenge ang’e ne’biara binde bio’koboko buna ekiara ekeneene gio’kogoro kiarenge ang’e ne’biara binde bio’kogoro. Amagoro na’maboko nigo arenge korokana bwamwabo. Amagoro na’maboko nigo arenge gokonyana ase okobogoria omobere gochia ande onsi ore gotaka kogenda; echiro, chituka, korina na goika omote gose ebitunwa, ande onsi ase ogotaara kwaganeirie. Nonya na’se amache ime, nigo arenge kobwaterana buya mono gokonya omobere gocheng’enena, goaka ontimbu gose gotibogeria. Nigo asibogete na koigwana ase obwaamate bwabo. Nigo arenge gosaba obokonyi korwa ase ebimo binde buna; eriogi korwa ase omonwa, okoigwa korwa ase ogoto, okonyonka korwa ase emioro, amo no’korora korwa ase amaiso. Okoigwana na okobwaterana kwabo gokareta emoko ase ebimo binde. Ebimo ebi binde bikaanga korwa ogosemia na obokonyi gochia ase bwamwabo aba babere. Endamwamu ekabatuba gotarora buna amagoro na’maboko naro arenge kobaira ande onsi batagete. Ebimo binde bigachaka koroberia amabe ase amaboko na’magoro. Oromeme rogasaba ekerengererio korwa ase obongo na rokageikerania abwo abwo. Rogachaka gokumia, ‘maiso marore, igoro ye’chinguru ne’siko ya’maboko na’magoro. Rokarigia komanya ng’a ning’o obwate ekieni ne’siko enene kobua oyonde. Abwo ritang’ani, ’bimo ebi bibere, amaboko na’magoro, tibiarenge gokumia igoro ye’kioyonde abwate gose are gokora korende bono bigachaka gosaba eriogi korwa ase omonwa nabo igo bigachaka goteeba buna nigo bire ebie’ngencho mono ase omobere kobua ebimo binde. Keri keri, ekerengererio eke kegaonchoreria na koba; ning’o ochongororogete kobua oyonde; amaboko akerora ng’a aro na’re ne’ebiara ebinyerere, nabo igo agachaka gokwana na’machaya igoro ye’biara bia’magoro buna bire ebieng’e na ebinetu ebimigi. Biara bia’magoro tibigokirie na ‘nkwana eye. Na birobio bikairaneria ase amachaya igoro yo’bonyerere bwe’biara bia’maboko. Bakaba, bamwabo bachayaine, baankaine! Egento eke gekagenderera ase amatuko amange, goika kero kende kegasaria ogokora emereme ase obomo no’boikeranu. Omoerio oye egaikera ase riborio rie’chinguru: Bikaboria ebimo binde kogayana ring’ana eri. Oromeme rokarua ekerengererio ng’a babe no’kwamererania. Bonsi bagaancherana buna eke ne’kerengererio ekiya. Korende, obokong’u obomo no’bo: okoamererania oko inkoroki? Ebimo bigachaka korua ogosemia; ebinde bigateeba ng’a bamwabo aba bakinane enyameni. Ebinde bigateeba barwane ne’meyio, gose gotinkana chimbero, korende kera ekemo kie’birengererio ebi gekaangwa ng’a ne’gekong’u goikerania ase ebimo ebi bibere; okogoro gose okoboko. Ase entunde ya kabere, oromeme rogasaba ekerengererio korwa ase obongo, igoro yerichibu ria bwango. Ase amagoro na’maboko, nigo kera ekemo kie’bimo ebi kiarenge koreta okoamererania kwaye. Bwamwabo bagaancherana ne’kerengererio eke. Okoamererania oko nigo gwakorekanete ase arabirie ime ye rinani, ang’e na rooche. Ebimo bionsi bikebeka ang’e ase kende gionsi gose mobasokano onde bwonsi orachere omobere, ekiagera bono ebimo bio’mobere nigo biarenge kong’usanana. Amaiso agachina are na’ng’e korora kende kebe kerache, korwa ‘nsinyo ende yonsi. Amato agategesia koigwa kariogi kande gonsi korwa ande onsi, emioro ekemiria buya erinde erio etiokerere gotioka kwa gento kende kebe maiso atarore, gose amato ataigwe; oromeme rokaba ang’e gokura na korangeria onye kende kebe kegocha. Ekerambauti gekararia amang’ana aya yo’koamererania goika chinsinyo inye chie’rinani, ase amache na’se ‘mbeo. Ching’iti chi-nyamagoro ane chikaba chintang’ani gosankererekana, chinyinge chiria chinene chikabogoria ebisabo ebibese kwoorokia ng’a nigo chiacheire omorembe. Ekaba obwaari bwe chirangi chie’ngo, endo, ekeobiria, enyang’au, rigwari, eng’ombe nyamagunchara ‘matambe, enchogu, engamia, egechure, egesusu, eunko, ne’mbeba. Ching’iti chia rooche, buna enswe, emamba, enkwe, chikaanekera emetwe yabo ase engegu yo’rooche, emegongo egatigara amache ime. Naye Elija? Akabora, Inche tari ere. Aye naye omobani oria? Akairaneria, Yaya. 22 Nabo bakamotebia, Naye ng'o, tobae okoiraneria abatotomete. Naki ogweteba? 23 Akabora, Inche neriogi ri'omonto okoaka eriogi eroro ime, Rongeyia enchera y'Omonene, buna atebete omobani Isaya, 24 Nabarabwo abatometwe baruete as'Abafarisai. 25 Bakamoboria, bakamotebia, Naki rende okobatisa, onye aye tori Kristo, gose Elija, gose omobani oria? 26 Yohana akabairaneria akabora, Inche iga nkobatisa as'amache: egati yaino otenenire oyomotamanyeti inwe. 27 Nere ogocha nyuma yane, oyorenge ritang'ani asende, gose inche tingwenereti nyesibore enuga y'egekoroto kiaye. 28 Aya iga akoregete Bethania ng'umbu ya Yorodan, nao arenge Yohana okobatisa. 29 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana akamorora Yesu ogocha asare, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye, oyobogoretie ebibe bi'ense! 30 Oyo nere nare goteba amang'ana aye, Ngochare omonto nyuma yane, oyore ritang'ani asende, ekiagera arenge ritang'ani asende. 31 Nainche tinamomanyete; korende aorokigwe as'Abaisiraeli, nabo as'ayio ngacha nakobatisa as'amache. 32 Yohana agakwana, akabora, Nayororire Omoika ogoika korwa igoro buna riruma, rigaikaransa igoro asare. 33 Nainche tinamomanya: korende ere oyontomete kobatisa as'amache, oyio agantchia, Ere oyoranyare korora Omoika ogoika nagoikaransa igoro asere, oyio nere okobatisa n'Omoika Omochenu. 34 Nainche narorire, naende natebire ng'a oyo n'Omwana o Nyasaye. 35 Naende rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana igarenge otene ne nababere b'aborokigwa baye. 36 Akamorigereria Yesu ogotara, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye! 37 Baria aborokigwa babere bakamoigwa ogoteba, bakamotunyana Yesu. 38 Yesu ageonchora, akabarora bakomotunyana, akabatebia, Ninki mokorigia? Bakamotebia, Rabii (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Omworokia), ng'ai omenyete? 39 Akabatebia, inchuo morore. Bagacha, bakarora aas'amenyete; bakamenya asare rituko riria: iga yarenge ang'e chinsa ikomi. 40 Anderea, momura omwabo Simon Petero, igarenge oyomo bwa baria babere bamoigwete Yohana nakomotunyana. 41 Oyo akamonyora ritang'ani Simon momura omwabo omonyene, akamotebia, Twamonyorire Masihi, (ogoonchorwa kwaye Kristo). 42 Akamoira ase Yesu. Yesu akamorigere ria, akabora, Aye Simon, omwana o Yona, norokwe Kefa (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Petero). 43 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yesu akarigia koimoka kogenda Galili, akamonyora Filipo: akamotebia, Ntunyana. 44 Nere Filipo igarenge omonto o Bethisaida, omonto bw'omochie bw'Anderea na Petero. 45 Filipo akamonyora Nathaniel, akamotebia, Twamonyorire ere oyorikeretwe na Musa as'amachiko, nababani, Yesu omwana o Yusufu, omonto o Nazareti. 46 Nathaniel akamotebia, Nakenyare egento ekiya korua Nazareti? Filipo akamotebia, Inchuo orore. 47 Yesu akamorora Nathaniel ogocha asare, agakwana asare, Rora, oyo n'Omoisiraeli ekeene ekeene, otari nobong'ainereria ime yaye. 48 Nathaniel akamotebia, Ing'ai kwamanyera? Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ritang'ani Filipo atarakorangeria, ekero kwarenge inse as'omoko, nakoroche. 49 Nathaniel akamoiraneria, akamotebia, Rabii, naye Omwana o Nyasaye, naye omoruoti bw'Abaisiraeli. 50 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ekiagera nagotebia, nakoroche inse as'omoko, gwanchire? Norore amang'ana amanene kobua aya. 51 Akamotebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, namoyerore igoro ekoigoka, namalaika a Nyasaye akorina, agoika igoro as'Omwana-o-mwanyabanto. 1 Naende rituko ria gatato yarenge enyangi ase Kana ya Galili; na ng'ina Yesu nao arenge. 2 Yesu nere akarangerigwa amo naborokigwa baye as'enyangi. 3 Goika edivai egachia kobaremera, ng'ina Yesu akamotebia, Tibari nedivai. 4 Yesu akamotebia, Omokungu inki nde inche naye? Ensa yane teraika. 5 Ng'ina akabatebia abasomba, Rinde rionsi arabatebie, rikore. 6 Nchiarenge aroro chinsiongo isano nemo chi'amagena, chiabekire aroro as'engecho y'ogwesibia kwabo Abayahudi, ker'eyemo iga yarenge ang'e ekerengo kia chigallon emerongo ebere. 7 Yesu akabatebia, Ichoria chinsiongo namache. Bagachichoria goika igoro. 8 Akabatebia, bono taa, moirere omonene bw'omoyega. Bakaira. 9 Omonene bw'omoyega agachia koyaigwa amache akoregete koba edivai, tamanya ase yarua, (korende abasomba mbamanyete ababuchete amache), omonene bw'omoyega akamorangeria omonene bw'enyangi, 10 akamotebia, Kera omonto ritang'ani iga agochaka edivai ere engiya, goika abanto kobatiekire konywa mono, erio oreta eyetari engiya: aye kwagachire edivai engiya goika bono, 11 Oyio noro omochako bw'ebikone Yesu akorete Kana ya Galili, akaorokia obonene bwaye; aborokigwa baye bakamwancha. 12 Nyuma as'aya akagenda goika Kaperinaum, ere, na ng'ina, nabamwabo, naborokigwa baye: bakamenya aroro amatuko amake. 13 Naende epasaka y'Abayahudi iga yarenge ang'e, Yesu akarina goika Yerusalemu. 14 Akarora hekalu ime abanto barenge gotonda chiombe neching'ondi namaruma, nabanyene koonchora chifetha, baikaransete: 15 agakora orokini ase chingori, akabasokia bonsi korwa ase hekalu, neching'ondi nechiombe; agaitera chifetha chiabo abanyene goonchora chifetha,agachionchora chimesa chiabo; 16 akabatebia baria barenge gotonda amaruma, Yatigerie aya; timokora enyomba ya Tata one koba enyomba y'ebiasara. 17 Aborokigwa baye bakainyora ng'a nerikire, Risemi ri'enyomba yao riandire. 18 Nabo Abayahudi bakairaneria bakamotebia, Ngekone ki ogotworokia, ekiagera ogokora aya? 19 Yesu akairaneria, akabatebia, Yetagore hekalu eye, nainche as'amatuko atato ninyetenenie. 20 Abayahudi bakabora, Hekalu eye yaagachetwe as'engaki y'emiaka emerongo ene netano nomo, naye oyetenenie as'amatuko atato? 21 Korende ere igare kobora amang'ana ase hekalu y'omobere oye. 22 Nabo agachia kobokigwa as'amakweri aborokigwa baye bakainyora ng'a igatebete ring'ana eri, bakariancha riria ririko nariria ring'ana atebete Yesu. 23 Goika agachia kobao Yerusalemu ekero ki'epasaka ase rituko rinene, abanto abange bakariancha erieta riaye, kobarora ebikone arenge gokora. 24 Korende Yesu tegenete asebare, naki abamanyete bonsi, 25 naende ekiagera tarenge nokorigia as'abanto goteba amang'ana igoro ase mwanyabanto; naki ere omonyene amanyete ayare ime as'abanto. 1 Narenge omonto oyomo bw'Abafarisai, erieta riaye Nikodemo, omonene bw'Abayahudi: 2 oyo agacha ase Yesu botuko, akamotebia, Rabii, twamanyire ng'a nomworokia ore, kwarure ase Nyasaye: naki omonto onde tari oranyare kobikora ebikone ebi ogokora, tatiga Nyasaye abe amo nere. 3 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Omonto ataiboiri eria kabere, takonyara koborora obonda bwa Nyasaye. 4 Nikodemo akamotebia, Naki aranyare omonto koiborwa kare omogaka? nanyare gosoa enda ya ng'ina eria kabere aiborwe? 5 Yesu akairaneria, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Omonto ataiboiri as'amache n'Omoika, takonyara gosoa obonda bwa Nyasaye. 6 Ekeiboire as'omobere nomobere; nekeiboire as'Omoika nomoika. 7 Tokumia ekiagera nagotebia, Nogwenerete koiborwa naende. 8 Embeo iga ekogenda as'erigetie, negeturi kiaye iga ogokeigwa, korende tomanyeti as'ekorua gose as'ekogenda: naboigo na ker'omonto oiboirwe as'Omoika. 9 Nikodemo akamoiraneria, akamotebia, Naki aranyare koba aya? 10 Yesu akairaneria akamotebia, Inee! Aye nomworokia as'Isiraeli, naya toyainyoreti? 11 Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Eritomanyete nario togokwana, neri toroche twariteba; noborori bwaito timorigwancha. 12 Kerabe nkobatebia amang'ana ense, nainwe timogwancha, naki moranche, kondabatebie amang'ana a igoro? 13 Naende omonto onde tari orinire igoro, tatiga ere oyoikire korwa igoro Omwana-o-mwanyabanto ore igoro. 14 Naende buna Musa aimogetie eng'iti eroro ime, naboigo Omwana-o-mwanyabanto agwenerete aimokererigwe: 15 erinde tasira omonto onde bwonsi oyomwanchire, korende abe nobogima bwa kare nakare. 16 Naki Nyasaye ayianchete ense, goika akarua Omwana oye omomoima, erinde 'monto onde bwonsi oyomwanchire tasira, korende anyore obogima bwa kare nakare. 17 Naki Nyasaye tamotomete as'ense Omwana oye agambie ense; korende ense ekonywe nere. 18 Oyomwanchire takogambigwa; oyotancheti otiekire kogambigwa, ekiagera atariancheti erieta ria Omwana oyomo bweka o Nyasaye. 19 Neke nakio ekina, ekiagera omobaso ochire ense, abanto bagancha omosunte kobua omobaso; naki ogokora kwabo kwarenge okobe. 20 Naki kera oyogokora amabe igagechete omobaso, gose tagocha as'omobaso, ogokora kwaye tikobaisa gokanigwa. 21 Korende oyogokora ekeene igagocha as'omobaso, ogokora kwaye kororekane ng'a iga gwakorirwe ase Nyasaye. 22 Nyuma as'aya Yesu naborokigwa baye bakagenda goika ense ya Boyahudi, akabera aroro amo nabarabwo okobatisa, 23 Yohana nere igarenge kobatisa aria Ainon, ang'e na Salim, ekiagera narenge amache amange: abanto bakomochiera bakobatiswa. 24 Naki Yohana konya tarabekwa echela. 25 Nabo, gokaoroka okoamererania as'aborokigwa ba Yohana n'Abayahudi as'amang'ana ogwesibia. 26 Bakamochiera Yohana, bakamotebia, Rabii, ere oyorenge amo naye ng'umbu ya Yorodan, oyio kwaorogetie aye, oyio nere nkobatisare, nabanto bonsi nkomochierabare. 27 Yohana akairaneria, akabora, Takonyara omonto konyora ring'ana rinde rionsi tatiga aegwe korwa igoro. 28 Inwe abanyene mwabaire kirori ng'a natebete, Inche tari Kristo, korende natomirwe gotang'ana asare. 29 Oyore nere omoriakari bw'enyangi nere omonene, korende omosani oye bw'omonene bw'enyangi iga agotenena nakomoigwa, origokera eriogi riaye omonene bw'enyangi: nabo oyo omogoko one oikeranire. 30 Ere nagwenerete amenteke, korende inche nkee. 31 Oyochire korwa igoro oyio igare igoro as'onsi: oyore bw'ense, noyo bw'ense, iga agokwana amang'ana ense: ere oyochire korwa igoro oyio igare igoro as'onsi. 32 Ayaroche nakoyaigwa, naro abereire kirori: gose onde tari oyobwanchire oborori bwaye. 33 Oyobwanchire oborori bwaye obekire ekemanyererio kiaye ng'a Nyasaye nekeene, 34 Naki ere oyotometwe na Nyasaye igakoyakwana amang'ana a Nyasaye: naki Nyasaye tari komoa Omoika as'ekerengo. 35 Tata omwanchire Omwana, omoeire bionsi as'amaboko aye. 36 Oyoramwanche Omwana nare nobogima bwa kare nakare; noyotamoigwereti Omwana takorora obogima, korende nendamwainu ya Nyasaye eramoikaransere. 1 Nabo Omonene agachia komanya ng'a Abafarisai baigure ng'a Yesu okorire aborokigwa abange kobua Yohana, nakobatisa, 2 (Yesu omonyene tare kobatisa, korende naborokigwa baye), 3 akarua Boyahudi akagenda Galili eria kabere. 4 Naende nagwenerete goeta gati ya Samaria. 5 Nabo agaika omochie o Samaria, okorokwa Sukar, ang'e nomogondo oria Yakobo amoete Yusufu omwana oye: 6 naende agwo yarenge ensoko ya Yakobo.
