Erio aborokigwa bakagoka kobachia komorora Omonene. 21 Yesu akabatebia eria kabere, Omorembe obe asemore: buna Tata antomete, naboigo nabatomire inwe. 22 Gakwanire aya, akabautera omoika akabatebia, Monyore Omoika Omochenu: 23 bande bonsi morarusie ebibe barusigwe; naende bande bonsi morasiekere, basiekeirwe. 24 Ko Thomas, oyomo bw'ikomi nababere okorokwa Didumo, tarengeo amo nabarabwo ekero achete Yesu. 25 Erio aborokigwa bande bakamotebia, Twamororire Omonene. Korende ere akabatebia, Ntarochi amaboko aye nebimanyererio bi'emesumari, nakobeka ekiara as'ebiorokererio bi'emesumari, nakobeka okoboko kwane rikere riaye ime, tingwancha nonya ng'ake. 26 Nyuma y'amatuko atano natato aborokigwa baye mbarenge aroro ime eria kabere, na Thomas amo nabarabwo. Yesu agacha, ebisieri bisiekire, agatenena gati gati, akabora, Omorembe obe asemore. 27 Erio akamotebia Thomas, Reta aiga ekiara kiao, orore amaboko ane; korete okoboko kwao, obeka ase rikere riane: toba oyotancheti, korende oyo bwegenete. 28 Thomas akairaneria, akamotebia, Omonene one, na Nyasaye one. 29 Yesu akamotebia, Ekiagera kwandora, gwanchire: mbare negesio abataroche ko begenire, 30 Nabo mbire ebikone binde ebinge akorete Yesu as'amasio aborokigwa baye, bitarikiri as'ebuku eye: 31 korende ebi biarikirwe monyare gwancha ng'a Yesu nere Kristo, Omwana o Nyasaye; naende as'ogwancha mobe nobogima as'erieta riaye. 1 Nyuma as'aya Yesu akeorokia naende as'aborokigwa baye, as'enyancha ya Tiberia; nere iga eorogetie iga. 2 Simon Petero, na Thomas okorokwa Didumo, na Nathaniel o Kana ya Galili, nabana na Zebedi, nabanto bande babere as'aborokigwa baye, barenge amo. 3 Simon Petero akabatebia, Nkogendande koruba chinswe. Bakamotebia, Naintwe natogende amo naye. Bagasoka, bakarina obwato ime; nobotuko boria tibanyora gento. 4 Goika bogachia goikia mambia, Yesu agatenena engegu: korende aborokigwa tibamanya gose ng'a Yesu. 5 Erio Yesu akabatebia, Abana, more neki mokoria? Bakamoiraneria,Yaya. 6 Akabatebia, Kerute ekeonga ensemo y'okorio y'obwato, nainwe namonyore. Erio bakaruta, korende tibanyara gokeng'usa as'engecho y'obonge bwe chinswe. 7 Omworokigwa oria Yesu anchete akamotebia Petero, Nere Omonene. Erio Simon Petero, agachia koigwa ng'a n'Omonene, akeboyia eanga yaye (ekiagera arenge getirianda), akeruta enyancha ime. 8 Aborokigwa bande bagacha as'obwato (naki tibarenge are as'ense enyomo, ang'e chifuti chimia isato), bakagekurura ekeonga geichire nechinswe. 9 Erio kobachia goika engegu, bakarora omorero bw'amakara aroro, naende enswe ebekire igoro yaye, nomogati. 10 Yesu akabatebia, Reta aiga ensemo ye chinswe echimwarubire bono, 11 Erio Simon Petero akarina obwato ime, agakeng'usa ekeonga goika engegu, geichire chinswe chinene, emia namerongo etano naisato: nonya chiarenge chinyinge buna iga, ekeonga tigiatandogete. 12 Yesu akabatebia, Inchuo morie. Korende omonto onde ase baria aborokigwa tarenge oyorigetie komoboria, Aye ning'o? mbamanyete ng'a n'Omonene. 13 Yesu akagenda akayobogoria omogati, akabaa, nechinswe boigo. 14 Eke nekero kia gatato Yesu arorekanete naborokigwa baye nyuma y'okoboka korwa as'amakweri. 15 Erio kobakorire okoragera, Yesu akamotebia Simon Petero, Simon o Yohana, nonyanchete kobua aba? Akamotebia, Ee, Omonene, aye kwamanyire ng'a ningwanchete. Akamotebia, Risia chimanwa chie ching'ondi chiane. 16 Akamotebia, eria kabere, Simon o Yohana, nonyanchete? Akamotebia, Ee, Omonene aye kwamanyire ng'a ningwanchete, Akamotebia, Risia ching'ondi chiane. 17 Akamotebia eria gatato Simon o Yohana, Nonyanchete inche? Akamotebia, Omonene aye kwamanyire onsi; kwamanyire ng'a ningwanchete. Yesu akamotebia, Risia ching'ondi chiane. 18 Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Gakwarenge omosae, iga kwarenge kweboyia, kwagenda aase origetie; korende korabe omogaka, norambore amaboko ao, noyonde nagosibe, akoire as'otarigeti. 19 Agakwana eri as'okworokia amakweri ki aramotogie Nyasaye. Erio gakorire gokwana aya, akamotebia, Ntunyana. 20 Petero ogweonchora, akamorora omworokigwa oria bwanchetwe na Yesu ogotunya; nere oria bweegegete gekuba kiaye ekero ki'okoria endagera ya mogoroba, nagokwana, Omonene ning'o orakorue? 21 Petero ochia komorora oyio, akamotebia Yesu, Omonene, noyo rende? 22 Yesu akamotebia, Kondarigie oyo aikaranse goika nchiche ninki erakogwenere? Aye ontunye inche. 23 Erio ring'ana eri rigasarera as'abamwabo ng'a omworokigwa oria tagokwa: korende Yesu tamotebetie, tagokwa; korende, Kondarigie aikaranse goika inchiche nki erakogwenere? 24 Oyo noria omworokigwa oyaroche aya, naende origete aya; naende twamanyire ng'a oborori bwaye nobw'ekeene. 25 Nare naende ayande amange ayakorete Yesu, naro kararikwe erimo erimo, iga ngokaga ng'a nonya nense yonsi tegoisana chibuku echiranyare korikwa.
english: |Kisii from Kenya John John 1 1 The beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2 This beginning was with God. 3 All things were made through him; without him nothing was made that has been made. 4 In him was life, and the life was the light of men. 5 The light shines in darkness, and darkness did not overcome it. 6 There came a man named John, sent from God, so that he might testify about the light. 7 He came to testify, to bear witness to the light, so that everyone who believes might have eternal life. 8 He was not the light, but bore witness to the light. 9 The true light which gives light to every man was coming into the world. 10 He was in the world, and the world was made through him, yet the world did not know him. 11 He came to his own people, and they did not receive him. 12 But to all who received him, he gave them the right to become children of God, to those who believe in his name: 13 who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. 14 And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15 John testified concerning him, and cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me ranks higher than I,’ because he existed before me.” 16 From his fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace. 17 For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18 No one has ever seen God; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him. 19 And this is the testimony of John when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” 20 He confessed, and did not deny, but said, “I am not the Christ.” 21 They asked him, “Then what are you? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.” 22 So they said to him, “Then who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us?” 23 He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet wrote.” 24 Now the Pharisees also had come and questioned him, asking, 25 “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26 John answered them, saying, “I baptize with water, but there stands One among you whom you do not know. 27 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal strap.” 28 These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. 29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” 30 This is he about whom I said, ‘After me comes one who is preferred over me, for he existed before me.’ 31 And I did not know him, but so that he might be revealed to Israel, therefore I came baptizing with water.” 32 John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven and resting upon him. 33 And I have borne witness that he is the Son of God.” 34 I have seen and testified that this is the Chosen One of God.” 35 The next day again John stood with his disciples, and looked at Jesus as he walked by. 36 And he said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him speak, and followed Jesus. 38 Then Jesus turned, and seeing them following, said to them, “What do you seek?” They said, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are you staying?” 39 He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day, for it was about the tenth hour. 40 Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of those who heard him, and he told his brother Simon, 41 He first found his own brother Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated, Christ). 42 And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of John, you shall be called Cephas” (which is translated, Peter). 43 The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee, and he found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.” 44 Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. 45 Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found him about whom Moses in the Law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” 46 Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.” 47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no deceit!” 48 Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip told you, I saw you under the fig tree.” 49 Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” 50 Jesus answered him, “Because I have told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.” 51 And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.” 1 On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. 2 Jesus himself and his disciples were also invited to the wedding. 3 When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” 4 Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with me? My hour has not yet come.” 5 His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.” 6 Now there were six stone water jars there for Jewish ceremonial washing, each containing twenty to thirty gallons. 7 Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them up to the brim. 8 Then he told them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so, 9 and when the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine, he did not know where it came from. But the servants who had drawn the water knew, and they testified, “This wine is from Cana in Galilee.” 10 Jesus said to her, “Every host serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, then the poor wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 11 This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him. 12 After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother and brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there for a few days. 13 During the Jewish festival, Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 14 In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money changers sitting there. 15 He made a whip out of cords, and drove all the animals and people out of the temple courts. He scattered the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables. 16 To those who were selling doves he said, “Get these out of here! Do not make my Father’s house a den of thieves!” 17 His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.” 18 The Jews demanded, “What sign can you show us to prove your authority to do this?” 19 Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and I will raise it again in three days.” 20 The Jews replied, “It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and you are going to raise it in three days?” 21 But he was speaking about the temple of his body. 22 After he was raised from the dead, his disciples recalled that he had said this, and they understood that he was talking about the temple of his body. 23 As he was going to Jerusalem, many people believed in him because they saw the miracles he performed. 24 But Jesus would not entrust himself to them, for he knew all people. 25 He did not need anyone to testify about mankind, for he knew what was in their hearts. 1 Now there was a Pharisee named Nicodemus, a member of the Jewish ruling council. 2 He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him.” 3 Jesus replied, “Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.” 4 “How can someone be born when they are old?” Nicodemus asked. “Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother’s womb to be reborn?” 5 Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. 6 Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit. 7 You should not be surprised that I said, ‘You must be born again.’ 8 The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” 9 “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked. 10 Jesus replied, “Are you Israel’s teacher, yet you do not understand these things? 11 Very truly I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony. 12 I have told you earthly things and you do not believe; how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? 13 No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came down from heaven—the Son of Man. 14 Just as Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, 15 that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.” 16 For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. 17 For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it, but to save it. 18 Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already because they have not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son. 19 This is the verdict: Light has come into the world, but people loved darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil. 20 Everyone who does evil hates the light, and will not come into the light for fear that their deeds will be exposed. 21 But those who live by the truth come into the light, so that it may be seen plainly that what they have done has been done in the sight of God. 22 After this, Jesus and his disciples went out into the countryside of Judea. He spent some time there with them, and baptized. 23 John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there; people were coming and being baptized. 24 This happened because John had not yet been thrown into prison. 25 Now a discussion arose between John’s disciples and a Jew about purification. 26 They came to John and asked, “Rabbi, why are you baptizing here if you aren’t the Messiah?” 27 John replied, “I baptize with water, but among you stands one you do not know. 28 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie the sandals on his feet.” 29 The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! 30 This is the one I meant when I said, ‘After me will come one who ranks higher than I.’ 31 The one who goes ahead of me has already gone, and I am coming after him.” 32 And John testified: “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and remain on him. 33 I have seen and I testify that this is the Son of God.” 34 The next day John again stood with his disciples and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 35 The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples. 36 When Jesus walked by, John looked at him and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus. 1 Now when the Pharisees learned that Jesus had been baptizing people and gaining more disciples than John— 2 though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did— 3 he left Judea and went back to Galilee. 4 As he traveled, he went through Samaria. 5 So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph. 6 Jacob’s well was there, and Jesus, tired from his journey, sat down beside the well. It was about noon. 7 A Samaritan woman came to draw water, so Jesus said to her, “Will you give me a drink?” 8 His disciples had gone to the town to buy food. 9 The Samaritan woman said to him, “You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?” (Jews do not associate with Samaritans.) 10 Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that asks you for a drink, you would have asked him for living water.” 11 “Sir,” the woman said, “you don’t have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water? 12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did also his sons and his livestock?” 13 Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, 14 but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.” 15 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water so that I won’t have to come here and draw water anymore.” 16 He told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.” 17 “I have no husband,” she replied. Jesus said to her, “You are right to say you have no husband. 18 For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. At this you spoke the truth.” 19 The woman said, “Sir, I can see that you are a prophet. 20 Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews claim that the place to worship is in Jerusalem.” 21 Jesus said, “Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. 22 You Samaritans worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. 23 Yet a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, for they are the kind of worshipers the Father seeks. 24 God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.” 25 The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.” 26 Jesus declared, “I, the one speaking to you, am he.” 27 Just then his disciples returned and were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But no one asked him, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her.” 28 Then the woman left her water jar and went back to the town. “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did,” she said to the women. “Could this be the Messiah?” 29 They came out of the town and made their way toward him. 30 Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, “Rabbi, eat something.” 31 But he said to them, “I have food you cannot comprehend.” 32 “Surely not the food someone brought him to eat?” the disciples asked each other. 33 Jesus told them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work. 34 Don’t you have a saying, ‘Four months until harvest’? I tell you, look around and see that the fields are already ripe for harvest. 35 The reaper’s wages are substantial, and he gathers in fruit for eternal life. So that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 36 For in this case, the saying holds true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’ 37 And I tell you that the person who harvests will receive a reward too, and the harvest yields an abundant crop. 38 I sent you to reap what you haven’t worked for. Others have done the hard work, and you have come to enjoy their efforts.” 39 Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the testimony of the woman who said, “He told me everything I ever did.” 40 So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there for two days, 41 and many more became believers because of his message. 42 They said to the woman, “We no longer believe just because of what you told us; we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he really is the Savior of the world.” 43 After the two days he left for Galilee. 44 Now Jesus himself had pointed out that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. 45 So when he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all that he did in Jerusalem at the Passover festival. 46 Once again he visited Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official whose son lay sick in Capernaum. 47 When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son. 48 “Sir,” he said, “come down before my child dies.” 49 Jesus replied, “Go home. Do you believe this?” 25 She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who has come into the world.” 26 And when she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside, whispering to her, “Jesus is calling for you.” 27 When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him. 28 Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, and Martha met him on the road. 29 When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 30 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was once again deeply moved in spirit. 31 So he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.” 32 Then Mary went to where Jesus was and knelt at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 33 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was greatly disturbed in spirit and testified, “See how much he loves him!” 34 Then someone said, “Rabbi, look!” And they began to weep loudly. 35 Jesus wept again. 36 The Jews said, “See how much he loved him!” 37 But some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?” 38 Jesus, once more deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it. 39 Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a bad odor, for he has been dead four days.” 40 Jesus answered, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” 41 So they took away the stone. Then Jesus looked up and said, “Father, I thank you that you have heard me. 42 I knew that you always hear me, but I say this so that the people will believe that you sent me.” 43 After he had said this, Jesus called out, “Lazarus, come out!” 44 The dead man came out, wrapped in grave clothes, and his hands and feet were tied with strips of linen. 45 Jesus said to them, “Untie him and let him go.” 46 So those who had stood there with Mary and seen what happened were amazed. 47 Some of the Pharisees said, “See how nothing gets us anywhere! Here we are, trying to destroy him.” 48 But even then many of the Jews came to Jesus and put their faith in him. 50 Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the Sanhedrin, also came forward and asked Pilate for Jesus’ body. 51 He received permission, and he took the body down and wrapped it in fine linen with spices—in keeping with Jewish burial customs. 52 Now there was a garden near the place of crucifixion, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid. 53 So they laid Jesus in this tomb, because it was nearby and the Sabbath was approaching. 54 As evening approached, a rich man named Joseph of Arimathea arrived. 55 He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him. 56 Joseph took the body, wrapped it in clean linen cloth, 57 and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. He rolled a large stone over the entrance of the tomb and went away.

Joseph, who was also known as Barnabas by the apostles (which means "son of encouragement"), a Levite from Cyprus, sold a field and brought the money to the apostles. 7. They questioned him, asking why he did this. 8. Then Peter said, “Ananias, why did you lie to the Holy Spirit and hold back some of the money for yourself? 9. You had the opportunity to sell your land. Wouldn’t you have kept the price for yourself? Why did you plan this deception in your heart? 10. But instead, you lied to God and stole from the fund. You have condemned yourself.” 11. When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. Everyone who heard it was deeply shocked. 12. His wife, Sapphira, came in shortly afterward, unaware of what had happened. She asked Peter, “Why did you sell your property?” 13. Peter replied, “Tell me, how much did you sell it for?” Sapphira answered, “Three hundred silver coins.” 14. Peter said to her, “How could you two agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look! At your feet are the bodies of those who lied to the Holy Spirit. And they will fall down and die right here!” 15. Immediately, she fell down at his feet and died. When the young men came in and found her dead, they carried her out and buried her beside her husband. 16. Great fear gripped the entire church and all who heard about these events. 17. The high priest and all his associates—that is, the Sadducees—were very disturbed because they were hindering the apostles from preaching about Jesus and his resurrection. 18. So they arrested the apostles and put them in jail. 19. But during the night, an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and released them. 20. He instructed them, “Go and stand in the temple courts and tell the people everything about this new life.” 21. So they went to the temple at dawn and began to teach. As the high priest arrived with his officials and the Sadducee council, 22. they summoned the apostles and brought them before the Sanhedrin. 23. The high priest questioned them, saying, “We gave you strict orders not to teach about this man, yet here you are filling Jerusalem with your teaching about him.” 24. Peter and John replied, “We must obey God rather than human beings! For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.” 25. The high priest and the others were amazed when they saw the boldness and confidence of Peter and John, for they could see that they were unschooled commoners. 26. They recognized that these men had been with Jesus. 27. After observing their courage, they warned them not to speak publicly about Jesus anymore. 28. Then they let them go. 29. But Peter and John responded, “Which is right in God’s eyes: to obey you or to obey God? We cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.” 30. And so, after warning them further, the Sanhedrin dismissed them. The people praised God for his miraculous power. 31. Many signs and wonders were performed among the people through the apostles. All the believers continued together in prayer. 32. They shared everything they owned and distributed the proceeds to anyone who was in need. 33. There was no one among them who lacked anything, for those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money to the apostles, and it was distributed to each person according to their need. 34. Now Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles called Barnabas—which means "son of encouragement"—sold a field he had owned and brought the money to the apostles. 35. Then they laid the money at the feet of the apostles, and it was distributed to each person according to their need. Acts 4:37 They sold property and possessions and gave the money to the apostles. ekegusii: Abwo kare omomura narenge ororo orenge korokwa Demane. Nigo abwate esare yambwabo orenge korokwa Demazana. Ekero abaibori babo bakwete nigo bachiete komenya na ise moke. Korende nigo bachandetwe mono. Nigo barenge goitwa nebiranya ebitambe, naboigo bakaba bakoegwa erongori yoka naende rimo rioka kera rituko. Igo bagatama.
kiswahili: Hapo zamani za kale paliondokea mvulana mmoja aliyeitwa Demane. Alikuwa na pacha mwenzake aliyeitwa Demazane. Wazazi wao walipofariki, Demane na Demazane walienda kuishi na mjomba wao. Huko kwa mjomba wao, walitendewa mabaya. Walichapwa kwa vibiko virefu, na walipewa uji mwepesi mara moja tu kwa siku. Kwa sababu hiyo, walitoroka.

ekegusii: Bakanyora ekerongo bakamenya ime. Nigo baoboete mono ekiagera nigo barenge koigwa buna abanto mbare barenge koria abande. Na abanto aba nigo bamenyete ase ebitunwa. Igo bakarosia omorangu omokongu gokuneka egesoerio, nechingoro ibere chioka ase ensemo eyemo yekerong keria erinde embeo noborabu binyare gosoa. Demane akamoonya mosubati omwabo, “Bera igaiga ase ekerongo eke erinde nche ing’ende koinda, naende tobaisa koiyeka nyama ende yonsi. Abanto baria bakoria abanto nigo banchete ogotioka kwe’nyama.
kiswahili: Hawakuwa na nyumba ya kuishi. Waliona pango wakaamua kuishi ndani mwake. Waliogopa kwa sababu walisikia kwamba majitu yaliyokula watu yaliishi karibu. Kwa hivyo waliunda mlango wenye nguvu. Wakafunga kiingilio na kuacha mashimo mawili ya kupitisha hewa na mwangaza. Kisha Demane akamwambia dadake, “Baki humu pangoni nikatafute chakula. Na usipike nyama kamwe. Majitu hupenda sana harufu ya nyama."

ekegusii: Kera emarorogoba Demane akaba gakorenta kende gionsi konyora aitire – buna egesusu amo neng’uko. Kero arenge koirana, nigo arenge gotera: "Demazana, Demazana,?Omwana o mama, ing’igorere ekerongo eke, chinyoni nabo chirasoe. Naende nigo kebwate chingoro ibere.”
kiswahili: Kila jioni Demane alirudi na nyama aliyowinda – sungura, ndege au paa. Kila aliporudi pangoni aliimba: "Demazane, Demazane, nimefika kwenye pango, nifungulie mlango, ndiye mimi si uongo, nimewinda na korongo, tupike kwa kikaango, ufungue kwa mpango, asiingie muongo.”

ekegusii: Demazane akarosa kobera ere bweka ase ekerongo keria kera rituko. Igo rituko erimo, ekero momura omwabo asogete isiko gochia koinda na gotega emenyama, agasoka nere korora. Akanyora oroche agasoa ime gochiesa, na korina emete igoro. Akaigwa buya koba isiko ye’kerongo keria. “Oranyore,” banto tibaiyo bakoria abande. Gose onyore buna tata moke nigo arenge gototebia igo erinde tooboe.”
kiswahili: Demazane alichoka sana kukaa pangoni peke yake. Basi siku moja kakake alipoondoka, naye Demazane alitoka na kwenda matembezi. Aliona mto mdogo akaogelea kwa furaha sana. Pia alipanda miti akaendelea kustarehe. Alifurahia uhuru wa kucheza. “Labda hakuna majitu,” aliwaza. “Pengine mjomba alisema kuna majitu ili kututisha tu.”

ekegusii: Rituko riria riarenge kobwatia akaba omoremu mono gouta omorero erinde anyare koigwa riberera. Gotatiga rende anyuotete ime yekerongo keria omorangu oria gosiekire – erio anyare koba tu ase omorembe. “Ninde nobomaene buna kende tikeiyo kerakorekane ing’ise gosamba akanyama gake igo. Nigo erabe buya koria endagera eiyekire.”
kiswahili: Kesho yake alipata ukakamavu, akawasha moto ili kuondoa baridi. Lakini aliwasha moto huo ndani ya pango kwa kuogopa majitu. Aliufunga mlango kabisa. “Nina hakika hakuna hatari nikichoma nyama kwa moto huu. Chakula cha kuchomwa ni kitamu.”

ekegusii: Ekero momura omwabo airanete agatera buna yarenge ekawaida, "Demazana, Demazana,?Omwana o mama, Igora ing’igorere ekerongo eke. Ebinyoni nabo bigosoa. Naende nigo kebwate chingoro ibere.” Akaigora omorangu oria erinde asoe. Ekero aroche enyama eria eiyekire, Demane akamoboria, “Inaki gwakora iga otabwate omorero?” “Nigo naanekera enyama eye ase omogaso isiko” Demazane akairaneria bwango. Demane buna arosete tachia koamererania nere, igo bagaikaransa nse koragera amo.
kiswahili: Demane aliporudi nyumbani aliimba kama kawaida: "Demazane, Demazane, nimefika kwenye pango, nifungulie mlango, ndiye mimi si uongo, nimewinda na korongo, tupike kwa kikaango, ufungue kwa mpango, asiingie muongo.” Alimfungulia mlango akaingia. Alipoona nyama iliyochomwa. Demane aliuliza, “Ulichomaje nyama bila moto?” “Nilichoma nyama hii kwenye jua nje ya pango,” Demazane alijibu upesi. Kwa vile Demane alikuwa amechoka hakuuliza swali tena. Waliketi wakendelea kufurahia chakula.

ekegusii: Rituko riria riarenge kobwatia, agauta omorero naende nakoiyeka enyama yende. Riria are ange’ gokora koiyeka akaigwa ogotera isiko yegesieri kiabo, "Demazana, Demazana,?Omwana o mama, Ing’igorere ekerongo eke. Ebinyoni nabo bigosoa. Naende nigo kebwate chingoro ibere.” Gotatiga riogi riria tiriarenge buna eria momura omwabo. Demazana agateba: “Yaya, aye tori oyominto, riogi riao tiriri buna eriaye.” Akarema koba ime yekerongo keria.
kiswahili: Siku iliyofuata Demazane aliwasha moto na akachoma nyama tena. Alpomaliza kutayarisha ile nyama alisikia sauti ikiimba kwenye mlango wa pango. "Demazane, Demazane, nimefika kwenye pango, nifungulie mlango, ndiye mimi si uongo, nimewinda na korongo, tupike kwa kikaango, ufungue kwa mpango, asiingie muongo.” Lakini sauti hiyo haikuwa kama ya kakake. Basi akasema: "Hapana, wewe si kakangu. sauti hiyo si yake."

ekegusii: Ake igo akaigwa naende omonto kagotera isiko yekerongo keria, “Tiga insoe mosubati ominto.” Ing’igorere omwana ominto. Omwana o mama, Ing’igorere ekerongo eke. Ebinyoni nabo bigosoa. Naende nigo kebwate chingoro ibere.” Eriogi riria nigo riarenge buna eriamomura omwabo, igo akamoigorera.
kiswahili: Baada ya muda mfupi alisikia sauti tena ikiimba: "Demazane Demazane, nimefika kwenye pango, nifungulie mlango, ndiye mimi si uongo, nimewinda na korongo, tupike kwa kikaango, ufungue kwa mpango, asiingie muongo.” Sauti hiyo ilifanana na ya kakake. Kwa hivyo alifungua mlango.

ekegusii: Omosacha oyomo omoneene omerete etukia omobere bwensi agaichora ekerongo keria ime. Akamong’usa Demazane atarachi gotama. Demazane akanyaro kobogoria ribu ike. Riria buna abogoirie kogenda, akanyakoruta ribu riria nchera kogenda.
kiswahili: Jitu kubwa lenye nywele mwili mzima lilijaa mlangoni. Likamchukua Demazane haraka. Hangeweza kutoka. Lakini Demazane aliokota jivu la jikoni akabeba. Alipokuwa akibebwa alimimina jivu lile njiani walikopitia.

ekegusii: Rituko riria egento gioka Demane anyarete gotega nekonu yenchinchoke – nigo ayebogoretie ime yegunia abwate mogongo oye. Ekero airanete, akanyora egesieri kegoire na mosubati omwabo taiyo...gotatiga rende aroche ribu risiareire nchera goeta gochia emete ime. Akabwatia ribu riria nchera kogenda baka akarora omorero bosio bwaye.
kiswahili: Demane aliporudi alipata mlango ukiwa wazi na Demazane hakuwa ndani ... Lakini aliona jivu lililomwagwa kulekea msituni. Alifuata jivu hilo mpaka alipoona moto mbali.

ekegusii: Ang’e nomorero oria omosacha omoneene omerete etukia omobere bwensi naikaransete aroro negunia eneene kere ensemo. Demane agatara mbaka as’are kagosogora buna oria oumiete.. “Gaki tata one, nonkonye? Naumiire okogoro kwane. Inkonye amache yokonywa.” Omosacha oria akairaneria, “Nigo indakoretere amache rioka ekero orang’eneki na kong’a oboene buna togokuna gunia yane.” akagacha egunia eria buuya nyomba mwaye.
kiswahili: Demane aliona jitu lililojaa nywele limeketi karibu na moto. Mfuko mkubwa ulikuwa karibu naye. Alisongea karibu na jitu hilo akijifanya anachechemea kama mtu aliyeumia mguu. “Tafadhali baba,” Demane alisema, “naomba unisaidie. Nimeumia mguu. Naomba maji ya kunywa.” Jitu likasema, “Ngoja nikuletee maji lakini usiguse mfuko wangu." Jitu lilisema huku likiweka mfuko ule vizuri ndani ya nyumba.

ekegusii: Riria buna achire iga, Demane akabutora engori yasibete egunia eria na mosubati omwabo agasoka. Demane akairania egunia eria yaye yabwate chinchoke ribaga yeria yabwate mosubati omwabo nakoganya korora ninki kerabe.
kiswahili: Lakini jitu lilipoondoka kwenda mtoni, Demane alikata kamba ya mfuko. Ulifunguka na dadake akatoka. Demane alibadilisha mfuko huo na mfuko wake uliojaa nyuki. Kisha yeye na dadake wakajificha na kungoja kuona kile ambacho kingetokea.

ekegusii: Ekero omosacha oria airanete namache, momura na mosubati baye bagacha nere. Agatebia omosubati oye, “Egento ekiya nkere ase egunia eria ere nyomba. Genda!onyerente igaa!” akaigora egunia eria ake igo korora ninki kiarenge ime yaye, gotatiga chinchoke chiria chikamoroma okoboko. Akarangeria kagoteba, “Nigo gekoroma.” Agatebia momura omwabo “Genda omokonye korenta!” Korende amachibu akaba boo naende.
kiswahili: Jitu lilirudi na maji pamoja na watoto wake wawili – msichana na mvulana. Likamwambia msichana, "Kuna mlo mtamu ndani ya mfuko. Nenda ukaulete!" Msichana alifungua mfuko kuona kilichokuwa ndani. Nyuki walimwuma mkono akalia akisema kwa sauti, “Inauma, inauma...” “Nenda ukamsaidie,” jitu lilimwambia mvulana kwa sauti. Pia mvulana aliumwa akalia kwa uchungu.

ekegusii: “Tiga gonkora omochinga,’ akoga nagosoa nyomba ime. Agasieka omorangu nagosibora egunia eria ere bweka. Chinchoke chiria chigasoka chikamoroma omotwe, emioro, namaiso aye. Agatuma tuma na gokura, gatubetwe amaiso nechinchoke chiria.
kiswahili: “Msinifanye mjinga,” jitu lilisema kwa sauti likajitoma ndani ya nyumba. Lilifunga mlango na kufungua ule mfuko. Nyuki wale walichomoka kwa wingi na kumwuma kichwani, masikioni, na hata kwenye macho. Alishindwa kuona akarukaruka na kulia kwa uchungu mwingi.

ekegusii: Akaminyoka na kogwa nomotwe ime yamache, omotwe oye okananta ase esike. Agaonchokera omote orenge ang’e naende akanyora nekonu yechinchoke. Korwa abuo ase engaki etambe, Demane na Demazane bakaria oboke obwansu korwa ase ekonu eria.
kiswahili: Jitu lilikimbia kuelekea kwenye bwawa la maji. Lilichopeka kichwa kwenye matope likakwama huko. Liligeuka na kuwa kisiki cha mti uliokatwa. Nyuki walijenga nyumba yao kwenye kisiki hicho. Baadaye, Demane na Demazane walifurahia asali tamu kutoka kwa mzinga huo wa nyuki.
